In the vocative, the final vowel is elided. He citta, he cittā, cittāni. In the accusative, the ni ending optionally becomes e. Cittaṃ, citte, cittāni. The rest is the same as the word purisa.

Evamaññānipi –

Similarly, other words are declined as follows:

Puñña pāpa phala rūpa sādhanaṃ,

Sota ghāna sukha dukkha kāraṇaṃ;

Dāna sīla dhana jhāna locanaṃ,

Mūla kūla bala jālamaṅgalaṃ.

Merit, demerit, fruit, form, means; ear, nose, pleasure, pain, cause; generosity, virtue, wealth, jhāna, eye; root, bank, strength, net, blessing.

Naḷina [M 0.0093] liṅga mukha’ṅga jala’mbujaṃ,

Pulina dhañña hirañña padā’mataṃ;

Paduma vaṇṇa susāna vanā’yudhaṃ,

Hadaya cīvara vattha kuli’ndriyaṃ.

Lotus, sign, face, limb, water, lotus; sandbank, grain, gold, foot, nectar; lotus, color, charnel ground, forest, weapon; heart, robe, cloth, family, faculty.

Nayana vadana yāno’dāna sopāna pānaṃ,

Bhavana bhuvana lohā’lāta tuṇḍa’ṇḍa pīṭhaṃ;

Karaṇa maraṇa ñāṇā’rammaṇā’rañña tāṇaṃ,

Caraṇa nagara tīracchatta chiddo’dakāni –

Eye, face, vehicle, solemn utterance, staircase, drink; dwelling, world, iron, firebrand, beak, egg, seat; instrument, death, knowledge, object, forest, protection; foot, city, bank, parasol, hole, water –

Iccādīni.

And so on.

Kammasaddassa tatiyekavacanādīsu rūpabhedo.

The variations in form of the word kamma in the instrumental singular and other cases.

Kammaṃ, kammā kammāni, he kamma, he kammā kammāni, kammaṃ, kamme kammāni.

Kammaṃ, kammā, kammāni; he kamma, he kammā, kammāni; kammaṃ, kamme, kammāni.

“Vā, u, nāmhi, cā”ti ca vattate.

And the rule “Vā, u, nāmhi, ca” (Optionally, u, in the nā-group of cases, and ca) applies.

197. A kammantassa ca.

197. And “A kammantassa ca” (And 'a' for the ending of kamma).

Kammasaddantassa ukāra akārādesā honti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi. Antaggahaṇena thāmaddhādīnamantassapi uttaṃ. Casaddaggahaṇena yuva maghavānamantassa ā hoti kvaci nā suiccetesu. Kammunā kammanā kammena vā, kammehi kammebhi.

For the ending of the word kamma, the substitutions u and a optionally occur in the nā-group of case endings. By the inclusion of anta, it is also stated for the endings of words like thāma, addhā, etc. By the inclusion of ca, the ā occurs sometimes for the endings of yuva and maghavā in the nā and su case endings, etc. Kammunā, kammanā, kammena optionally; kammehi, kammebhi.

Sasmāsu “u nāmhi cā”ti ettha casaddena puma kammathāmantassa cukāro vā sasmāsūti uttaṃ. Kammuno kammassa, kammānaṃ, kammunā kammā kammamhā kammasmā, kammehi kammebhi, kammuno kammassa, kammānaṃ.

In the sa, smā, and su case endings, by the word ca in “u nāmhi ca,” it is stated that the u suffix optionally occurs for the masculine kamma and thāma endings in the sa, smā, and su case endings. Kammuno, kammassa; kammānaṃ; kammunā, kammā, kammamhā, kammasmā; kammehi, kammebhi; kammuno, kammassa, kammānaṃ.

Smiṃvacane “brahmato tu smiṃnī”ti ettha tusaddena kvaci ni hoti. Kammani kamme kammamhi kammasmiṃ, kammesu.

In the smiṃ case ending, by the word tu in “Brahmato tu smiṃnī,” ni sometimes occurs. Kammani, kamme, kammamhi, kammasmiṃ; kammesu.

Evaṃ [M 0.0094] thāmunā thāmena thāmasā vā, thāmuno thāmassa, thāmunā thāmā. Addhunā, addhuno iccādi purimasamaṃ.

Similarly, thāmunā, thāmena, thāmasā optionally; thāmuno, thāmassa; thāmunā, thāmā. Addhunā, addhuno, etc., are similar to the preceding examples.

Guṇavantu si, “savibhattissa, ntussa, simhī”ti ca vattate.

(Guṇavantu + si). And the rules “Savibhattissa” (Of the word with case ending), “Ntussa” (Of ntu), and “Simhi” (In the si case ending) apply.

198. Aṃ napuṃsake.

198. Aṃ napuṃsake (Aṃ in the neuter).

Napuṃsake vattamānassa liṅgassa sambandhino ntuppaccayassa savibhattissa aṃ hoti simhi vibhattimhi. Guṇavaṃ cittaṃ.

For a neuter noun, the ntu suffix, when connected to a word with a case ending, becomes aṃ in the si case ending. The result is guṇavaṃ cittaṃ.

Yomhi “ntussanto yosu cā”ti attaṃ, ikāro ca. Guṇavanti, guṇavantāni, sesaṃ ñeyyaṃ.

In the yo case ending, by the rule “Ntussanto yosu ca,” attaṃ and ikāro occur. The results are guṇavanti, guṇavantāni. The rest should be understood.

Gacchanta si, “simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo a”miti aṃ. Gacchaṃ gacchantaṃ, gacchantā gacchantāni.

Gacchanta + si. By the rule, 'simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo aṃ,' the nta suffix of words such as gacchanta becomes aṃ when followed by the si case ending. Gacchaṃ, gacchantaṃ; gacchantā, gacchantāni.

Akārantaṃ.

Ending in -a.

Ākāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo assaddhāsaddo.

The neuter word assaddhā ends in -ā.

“Assaddhā”iti ṭhite –

When 'assaddhā' stands thus:

“Samāsassā”ti adhikicca “saro rasso napuṃsake”ti samāsantassa rassattaṃ, samāsattā nāmabyapadeso, syādyuppatti. Sesaṃ cittasamaṃ.

With reference to the rule 'Samāsassa,' by the rule 'saro rasso napuṃsake,' the final vowel of the compound is shortened. Because it is a compound, it receives the designation of a noun, and the case endings are generated. The rest is similar to citta.

Assaddhaṃ kulaṃ, assaddhā assaddhāni kulāni iccādi.

Assaddhaṃ kulaṃ; assaddhā, assaddhāni kulāni, and so forth.

Tathā mukhanāsikāsaddo. Tassa dvandekattā sabbatthekavacanameva. Mukhanāsikaṃ, he mukhanāsika, mukhanāsikaṃ, mukhanāsikena iccādi.

Likewise, the word mukhanāsika. Because it is a singular dvandva compound, it is always in the singular number. Mukhanāsikaṃ, he mukhanāsika, mukhanāsikaṃ, mukhanāsikena, and so forth.

Ākārantaṃ.

Ending in -ā.

Ikāranto [M 0.0095] napuṃsakaliṅgo aṭṭhisaddo.

The neuter word aṭṭhi ends in -i.

Syādyuppatti, silopo, aṭṭhi.

Generation of the case endings, elision of si, resulting in aṭṭhi.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' is carried forward.

199. Yonaṃ ni napuṃsakehi.

199. Yonaṃ ni napuṃsakehi.

Napuṃsakaliṅgehi paresaṃ sabbesaṃ yonaṃ ni hoti vā.

After neuter gender words, for all 'yo' case endings, 'ni' is optionally the substitute.

Aṭṭhīni, aññattha niccaṃ yolopo, dīgho ca, aṭṭhī, tathā he aṭṭhi, he aṭṭhī aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhiṃ, aṭṭhī aṭṭhīni, aṭṭhinā iccādi aggisaddasamaṃ.

Aṭṭhīni. In the other case, there is always elision of yo and lengthening, resulting in aṭṭhī. Likewise: he aṭṭhi, he aṭṭhī, he aṭṭhīni; aṭṭhiṃ, aṭṭhī, aṭṭhīni; aṭṭhinā, and so forth, are similar to the word aggi.

Evaṃ satthi dadhi vāri akkhi acchi acci iccādīni.

Likewise: satthi, dadhi, vāri, akkhi, acchi, acci, and other such words.

Ikārantaṃ.

Ending in -i.

Īkāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo sukhakārīsaddo.

The neuter word sukhakārī ends in -ī.

“Sukhabhārī si” itīdha anapuṃsakattābhāvā sismimpi “agho rassa”miccādinā rassattaṃ, silopo. Sukhakāri dānaṃ, sukhakārī sukhakārīni, he sukhakāri, he sukhakārī he sukhakārīni, sukhakārinaṃ sukhakāriṃ, sukhakārī sukhakārīni.

Here, in the case of 'sukhakārī + si', because it is neuter, the vowel is shortened even when followed by the si case ending, by the rule 'agho rassaṃ,' and so forth, and si is elided. Sukhakāri dānaṃ; sukhakārī, sukhakārīni; he sukhakāri, he sukhakārī, he sukhakārīni; sukhakārinaṃ, sukhakāriṃ; sukhakārī, sukhakārīni.

Sesaṃ daṇḍīsaddasamaṃ. Evaṃ sīghayāyīādīni.

The rest is similar to the word daṇḍī. Likewise, sīghayāyī and other such words.

Īkārantaṃ.

Ending in -ī.

Ukāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo āyusaddo. Tassa aṭṭhisaddasseva rūpanayo.

The neuter word āyu ends in -u. Its declension is the same as that of the word aṭṭhi.

Āyu, āyū āyūni, he āyu, he āyū he āyūni, āyuṃ, āyū āyūni, āyunā āyusāti [M 0.0096] manogaṇādittā siddhaṃ. Āyūhi āyūbhi, āyuno āyussa, āyūnamiccādi.

Āyu, āyū, āyūni; he āyu, he āyū, he āyūni; āyuṃ, āyū, āyūni. The forms āyunā and āyusā are established because the word belongs to the manogaṇa group. Āyūhi, āyūbhi; āyuno, āyussa; āyūnaṃ, and so forth.

Evaṃ cakkhu vasu dhanu dāru tipu madhu hiṅgu siggu vatthu matthu jatu ambu assuādīni.

Likewise: cakkhu, vasu, dhanu, dāru, tipu, madhu, hiṅgu, siggu, vatthu, matthu, jatu, ambu, assu, and other such words.

Ukārantaṃ.

Ending in -u.

Ūkāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo gotrabhūsaddo.

The neuter word gotrabhū ends in -ū.

Gotrabhū si, napuṃsakattā rassattaṃ, silopo. Gotrabhu cittaṃ, gotrabhū gotrabhūni, he gotrabhu, he gotrabhū he gotrabhūni, gotrabhuṃ, gotrabhū gotrabhūni, gotrabhunā iccādi pulliṅge abhibhūsaddasamaṃ.

Gotrabhū + si. Because it is neuter, the vowel is shortened, and si is elided. Gotrabhu cittaṃ; gotrabhū, gotrabhūni; he gotrabhu, he gotrabhū, he gotrabhūni; gotrabhuṃ, gotrabhū, gotrabhūni; gotrabhunā, and so forth, are similar to the masculine word abhibhū.

Evaṃ abhibhū sayambhū dhammaññūādīni.

Likewise: abhibhū, sayambhū, dhammaññū, and other such words.

Ūkārantaṃ.

Ending in -ū.

Okāranto napuṃsakaliṅgo cittagosaddo.

The neuter word cittago ends in -o.

“Cittā gāvo assa kulassā”ti atthe bahubbīhisamāse kate “saro rasso napuṃsake”ti okārassa ṭhānappayatanāsannattā rassattamukāro, syādyuppatti, silopo. Cittagu kulaṃ, cittagū cittagūni iccādi āyusaddasamaṃ.

In the sense of 'a family that has dappled cows,' when a bahubbīhi compound is formed, by the rule 'saro rasso napuṃsake,' the vowel o is shortened to u due to proximity in place and effort of articulation. The case endings are generated, and si is elided. Cittagu kulaṃ; cittagū, cittagūni, and so forth, are similar to the word āyu.

Okārantaṃ.

Ending in -o.

Cittaṃ kammañca assaddha-mathaṭṭhi sukhakāri ca;

Āyu gotrabhū dhammaññū, cittagūti napuṃsake.

Citta, kamma, assaddha, aṭṭhi, and sukhakāri; āyu, gotrabhū, dhammaññū, and cittagū—these are in the neuter gender.

Napuṃsakaliṅgaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Neuter Gender is Concluded.

Sabbanāma

Pronouns

Atha [M 0.0097] sabbanāmāni vuccante.

Now the pronouns will be explained.

Sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya, itara, añña, aññatara, aññatama, pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara, ya, ta, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ, eka, ubha, dvi, ti, catu, tumha, amha iti sattavīsati sabbanāmāni, tāni sabbanāmattā tiliṅgāni.

Sabba, katara, katama, ubhaya, itara, añña, aññatara, aññatama, pubba, para, apara, dakkhiṇa, uttara, adhara, ya, ta, eta, ima, amu, kiṃ, eka, ubha, dvi, ti, catu, tumha, and amha—these twenty-seven are pronouns; being pronouns, they exist in the three genders.

Tattha sabbasaddo niravasesattho, so yadā pulliṅgavisiṭṭhatthābhidhāyī, tadā rūpanayo. Pure viya syādyuppatti, “so”ti sissa okāro, saralopaparanayanāni. Sabbo jano.

Herein, the word `sabba` has the meaning of 'all'. When it expresses a meaning specified as masculine, the method of forming its declensions is as follows. As before, the case endings, `si` and so on, are generated. The `si` ending becomes `o`, and then vowel elision and combination with the subsequent consonant are applied. For example: `Sabbo jano`.

Bahuvacane “sabba yo” itīdha “parasamaññā payoge”ti sabbādīnaṃ sabbanāmasaññā.

In the plural, in the case of `sabba yo`, by the rule `parasamaññā payoge`, words such as `sabba` receive the designation 'pronoun'.

“Yo”ti vattate.

The word `Yo` is continued.

200. Sabbanāmakārate paṭhamo.

200. The first [plural ending] after the `-a` of a pronoun.

Sabbesaṃ itthipumanapuṃsakānaṃ nāmāni sabbanāmāni, tesaṃ sabbesaṃ sabbanāmasaññānaṃ liṅgānaṃ akārato paro paṭhamo yo ettamāpajjate. Sabbe purisā.

Pronouns are the names for all things, whether feminine, masculine, or neuter. For all of these that have the designation 'pronoun', the first plural ending `yo` following an `-a` becomes `e`. For example: `Sabbe purisā`.

Akāratoti kiṃ? Sabbā amū.

Why is 'from an `-a`' stated? For example: `Sabbā amū`.

He sabba sabbā, he sabbe, sabbaṃ, sabbe, sabbena, sabbehi sabbebhi.

He sabba, he sabbā, he sabbe; sabbaṃ, sabbe; sabbena, sabbehi, sabbebhi.

Catutthekavacane āyādese sampatte –

When, in the dative singular, the substitution `āya` is to be applied—

“Ato, ā e, smāsmiṃnaṃ, āya catutthekavacanassā”ti ca vattate.

The rules concerning 'Ato' (from `-a`), the substitutions 'ā' and 'e' for 'smā' and 'smiṃ', and 'āya' for the dative singular are also continued.

201. Tayo [M 0.0098] neva ca sabbanāmehi.

201. And these three substitutions do not occur after pronouns.

Akārantehi sabbanāmehi paresaṃ smā smiṃ iccetesaṃ, catutthekavacanassa ca ā e āyaiccete ādesā neva hontīti āyādesābhāvo. Caggahaṇaṃ katthaci paṭisedhanivattanatthaṃ, tena pubbādīhi smā smiṃnaṃ ā e ca honti. Sabbassa.

After pronouns ending in `-a`, for the following `smā` and `smiṃ`, and for the dative singular, these substitutions `ā`, `e`, and `āya` do not occur; thus, there is no substitution of `āya`. The inclusion of `ca` is for the purpose of negating this prohibition in certain cases; thereby, after `pubba` and other such words, `ā` and `e` do occur for `smā` and `smiṃ`. For example: `Sabbassa`.

“Akāro, e”ti ca vattate.

The words `Akāro` and `e` are also continued.

202. Sabbanāmānaṃ naṃmhi ca.

202. And for pronouns, when `naṃ` follows.

Sabbesaṃ sabbanāmānaṃ akāro ettamāpajjate naṃmhi vibhattimhi.

For all pronouns, the final `a` becomes `e` when the case ending `naṃ` follows.

“Sabbanāmato”ti ca vattate.

The phrase 'from a pronoun' is also continued.

203. Sabbato naṃ saṃsānaṃ.

203. After `sabba`, `naṃ` becomes `saṃ` and `sānaṃ`.

Sabbato sabbanāmato parassa naṃvacanassa saṃ sānaṃiccete ādesā honti.

After the pronoun `sabba`, the ending `naṃ` becomes `saṃ` or `sānaṃ`.

Sabbesaṃ sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmā sabbamhā, sabbehi sabbebhi, sabbassa, sabbesaṃ sabbesānaṃ, sabbasmiṃ sabbamhi, sabbesu.

Sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ; sabbasmā, sabbamhā; sabbehi, sabbebhi; sabbassa; sabbesaṃ, sabbesānaṃ; sabbasmiṃ, sabbamhi; sabbesu.

Itthiyaṃ “itthiyamato āppaccayo”ti āppaccayo. Aññaṃ kaññāsaddasamaṃ aññatra sa naṃ smiṃvacanehi. Sabbā pajā, sabbā sabbāyo, he sabbe, he sabbā sabbāyo, sabbaṃ, sabbā sabbāyo, sabbāya, sabbāhi sabbābhi.

In the feminine, by the rule 'itthiyamato āppaccayo', the `ā` suffix is applied. The declension is otherwise like the word `kaññā` (maiden), except in the case of the `sa`, `naṃ`, and `smiṃ` endings. Sabbā pajā; sabbā, sabbāyo; he sabbe; he sabbā, sabbāyo; sabbaṃ; sabbā, sabbāyo; sabbāya; sabbāhi, sabbābhi.

Catutthekavacane “sabbanāmato vā”, sabbato koti ito “sabbato”ti ca vattate.

In the dative singular, the rules 'sabbanāmato vā' and 'sabbato' are continued.

204. Ghapato [M 0.0099] smiṃsānaṃ saṃsā.

204. After a `gha`-stem, `smiṃ` and `sa` become `saṃ` and `sā`.

Sabbato sabbanāmato ghapasaññato smiṃ saiccetesaṃ yathākkamaṃ saṃsāādesā honti vā.

After the pronoun `sabba` and after a stem designated `gha`, the endings `smiṃ` and `sa` optionally become `saṃ` and `sā` respectively.

“Saṃsāsvekavacanesu cā”ti vattate.

The phrase 'and in the singular endings `saṃ` and `sā`' is continued.

205. Gho rassaṃ.

205. A `gha`-stem is shortened.

Ghasañño ākāro rassamāpajjate saṃsāsvekavacanesu vibhattādesesu paresu.

The `ā` vowel designated `gha` becomes short when followed by the singular case-ending substitutions `saṃ` and `sā`.

“Sāgamo”ti vattate.

'The augment `sa`' is carried forward.

206. Saṃsāsvekavacanesu ca.

206. And when the singular case-endings `saṃ` and `sā` follow.

Saṃ sāiccetesu ekavacanaṭṭhānasambhūtesu vibhattādesesu paresu liṅgamhā sakārāgamo hoti.

When followed by these singular case-ending substitutions `saṃ` and `sā`, the augment `sa` is inserted after the stem.

Sabbassā sabbāya, sabbāsaṃ sabbāsānaṃ, sabbāya, sabbāhi sabbābhi, sabbassā sabbāya, sabbāsaṃ sabbāsānaṃ.

sabbassā, sabbāya; sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ; sabbāya; sabbāhi, sabbābhi; sabbassā, sabbāya; sabbāsaṃ, sabbāsānaṃ.

Smiṃmhi “sabbanāmato, ghapato”ti ca vattate.

In the case of the `smiṃ` ending, the rules 'from a pronoun' and 'from a `gha` stem' are carried forward.

207. Netāhi smimāyayā.

207. From these, the substitutions `āya` and `yā` do not replace `smiṃ`.

Etehi sabbanāmehi ghapasaññehi parassa smiṃvacanassa neva āya yādesā hontīti āyābhāvo. Vādhikārato kvaci hoti dakkhiṇāya uttarāyāti ādi.

After these pronouns designated `gha`, the substitutions `āya` and `yā` for the following `smiṃ` ending do not occur; thus, there is an absence of the `āya` and `yā` substitutions. Due to the governing rule of option, it sometimes occurs, as in `dakkhiṇāya`, `uttarāya`, and so forth.

Saṃyamādesā, sabbassaṃ sabbāyaṃ, sabbāsu.

The substitutions `saṃ` and `yaṃ`: sabbassaṃ, sabbāyaṃ; sabbāsu.

Napuṃsake sabbaṃ cittaṃ, sabbāni, he sabba, he sabbāni, sabbaṃ, sabbāni. Sesaṃ pulliṅge viya ñeyyaṃ.

In the neuter: `sabbaṃ cittaṃ`; `sabbāni`; O `sabba`; O `sabbāni`; `sabbaṃ`; `sabbāni`. The remaining forms should be understood to be like the masculine.

Evaṃ [M 0.0100] katarādīnaṃ aññatamasaddapariyantānaṃ tīsupi liṅgesu rūpanayo.

Thus, for the words beginning with `katara` and ending with `aññatama`, the method of declension is the same in all three genders.

Tattha katarakatamasaddā pucchanatthā.

Among these, the words `katara` and `katama` have an interrogative sense.

Ubhayasaddo dviavayavasamudāyavacano.

The word `ubhaya` denotes a collection of two components.

Itarasaddo vuttappaṭiyogavacano.

The word `itara` denotes the counterpart of that which has been stated.

Aññasaddo adhikatāparavacano.

The word `añña` denotes that which is additional or other.

Aññatara aññatamasaddā aniyamatthā.

The words `aññatara` and `aññatama` have an indefinite sense.

“Yo, sabbanāmakārate paṭhamo”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'yo' and 'the first case-ending in the declension of pronouns' are carried forward.

208. Dvandaṭṭhā vā.

208. Optionally, when situated in a dvanda compound.

Dvandasamāsaṭṭhā sabbanāmakārato paro paṭhamo yo ettamāpajjate vā. Kataro ca katamo cāti katarakatame, katarakatamā vā iccādi.

When situated in a dvanda compound, the nominative plural ending `yo` after a pronoun optionally becomes `e`. For example, `kataro ca katamo ca` becomes `katarakatame` or `katarakatamā`, and so forth.

Pubbādayo disādivavatthānavacanā.

The words `pubba` and so forth denote the determination of direction and other such categories.

Pubbo kālo. Bahuvacane “dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā”ti ettha parāti niddesato pubbādīhi yovacanassa vikappenekāro.

`Pubbo kālo` (former time). In the plural, based on the directive `parā` in the rule `dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā` (suffixes come after roots and stems), the `yo` ending after `pubba` and so forth optionally becomes `e`.

Pubbe pubbā, he pubba, he pubbe he pubbā, pubbaṃ, pubbe, pubbena, pubbehi pubbebhi, pubbassa, pubbesaṃ pubbesānaṃ. “Smāsmiṃnaṃ vā”ti vikappenākārekārā. Pubbā pubbasmā pubbamhā, pubbehi pubbebhi, pubbassa, pubbesaṃ pubbesānaṃ, pubbe pubbasmiṃ pubbamhi, pubbesu.

pubbe, pubbā; O pubba, O pubbe, O pubbā; pubbaṃ; pubbe; pubbena; pubbehi, pubbebhi; pubbassa; pubbesaṃ, pubbesānaṃ. By the rule `smāsmiṃnaṃ vā`, the optional forms with `ā` and `e` occur. pubbā, pubbasmā, pubbamhā; pubbehi, pubbebhi; pubbassa; pubbesaṃ, pubbesānaṃ; pubbe, pubbasmiṃ, pubbamhi; pubbesu.

Itthiyaṃ pubbā disā, pubbā pubbāyo iccādi sabbāsaddasamaṃ.

In the feminine: `pubbā disā`; `pubbā`, `pubbāyo`, and so forth, are declined like the word `sabbā`.

Napuṃsake [M 0.0101] pubbaṃ ṭhānaṃ, pubbāni, he pubba, he pubbāni, pubbaṃ, pubbāni, sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ. Evaṃ parāparadakkhiṇuttarādharasaddā.

In the neuter: `pubbaṃ ṭhānaṃ`; `pubbāni`; O `pubba`; O `pubbāni`; `pubbaṃ`; `pubbāni`. The remaining forms are like the masculine. The words `para`, `apara`, `dakkhiṇa`, `uttara`, and `adhara` are declined similarly.

“Sabbanāmato, dvandaṭṭhā”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'from a pronoun' and 'when situated in a dvanda compound' are carried forward.

209. Nāññaṃ sabbanāmikaṃ.

209. No other pronominal operation applies.

Dvandaṭṭhā sabbanāmato parassa yovacanassa ṭhapetvā ettaṃ aññaṃ sabbanāmikaṃ kāriyaṃ na hotīti saṃsānamādesābhāvo. Pubbāparānaṃ, pubbuttarānaṃ adharuttarānaṃ, “nāññaṃ sabbanāmika”nti vinādhikārena yogena tatiyāsamāsepi. Māsapubbāya, māsapubbānaṃ.

For the `yo` ending that follows a pronoun situated in a dvanda compound, no other pronominal operation occurs apart from the substitution of `e`; thus, there is no substitution of `saṃ` or `sānaṃ`. For example: `pubbāparānaṃ`, `pubbuttarānaṃ`, `adharuttarānaṃ`. By applying the rule `nāññaṃ sabbanāmikaṃ` independently of its governing context, this also applies in an instrumental compound: `māsapubbāya`, `māsapubbānaṃ`.

“Nāññaṃ sabbanāmika”nti ca vattate.

The rule 'no other pronominal operation applies' is also carried forward.

210. Bahubbīhimhi ca.

210. And in a bahubbīhi compound.

Bahubbīhimhi ca samāse sabbanāmikavidhānaṃ nāññaṃ hoti. Piyapubbāya, piyapubbānaṃ, piyapubbe.

And in a bahubbīhi compound, no other pronominal rule applies. For example: `piyapubbāya`, `piyapubbānaṃ`, `piyapubbe`.

Casaddaggahaṇena disatthasabbanāmānaṃ bahubbīhimhi sabbanāmikavidhānaṃva hoti.

By the inclusion of the word 'ca', the rule for pronouns applies to pronouns denoting direction in a bahubbīhi compound.

Dakkhiṇassā ca pubbassā ca yadantarāḷanti atthe bahubbīhi, dakkhiṇapubbassaṃ, dakkhiṇapubbassā, evaṃ uttarapubbassaṃ, uttarapubbassā iccādi.

In the sense of 'what lies between the south and the east,' a bahubbīhi compound is formed: dakkhiṇapubbassaṃ, dakkhiṇapubbassā; similarly, uttarapubbassaṃ, uttarapubbassā, etc.

Yatetasaddādīnamālapane rūpaṃ na sambhavati. Yasaddo aniyamattho.

For words such as 'ya', 'ta', and 'eta', a vocative form does not occur. The word 'ya' has a relative meaning.

Yo puriso, ye purisā, yaṃ, ye. Yā kaññā, yā yāyo, yaṃ, yā yāyo. Yaṃ cittaṃ, yāni, yaṃ, yāni. Sesaṃ sabbattha sabbasaddasamaṃ.

Yo puriso, ye purisā, yaṃ, ye. Yā kaññā, yā, yāyo, yaṃ, yā, yāyo. Yaṃ cittaṃ, yāni, yaṃ, yāni. The rest is like the word 'sabba' in all cases.

Ta [M 0.0102] eta ima amu kiṃiccete parammukha samīpa accantasamīpadūra pucchanatthavacanā.

'Ta', 'eta', 'ima', 'amu', and 'kiṃ'—these are words denoting, respectively, what is out of sight, near, very near, distant, and for the purpose of questioning.

Tasaddassa bhedo. “Ta si” itīdha –

The variations of the word 'ta'. Here, in the case of 'ta si'—

“Anapuṃsakassāyaṃ simhīti, sa”miti ca vattate.

The rules 'for the non-neuter' and 'sa' are carried forward.

211. Etatesaṃ to.

211. Of 'eta' and 'ta', the 't'.

Eta taiccetesaṃ anapuṃsakānaṃ takāro sakāramāpajjate simhi vibhattimhi. So puriso.

Of the non-neuter pronouns 'eta' and 'ta', the letter 't' becomes 's' when the 'si' case ending follows. So puriso.

Sabbanāmaggahaṇañca, ito taggahaṇañca vattate.

And the mention of 'pronoun' and the mention of 'ta' are carried forward from here.

212. Tassa vā nattaṃ sabbattha.

212. Optionally, the 't' of 'ta' becomes 'n' in all cases.

Taiccetassa sabbanāmassa takārassa nattaṃ hoti vā sabbattha liṅgesu. Ne te, naṃ taṃ, ne te, nena tena, nehi nebhi tehi tebhi.

Of this pronoun 'ta', the letter 't' optionally becomes 'n' in all genders. Ne, te; naṃ, taṃ; ne, te; nena, tena; nehi, nebhi, tehi, tebhi.

“Sabbassa, tassa vā sabbatthā”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'of the whole stem' and 'or of 'ta' everywhere' are carried forward.

213. Sasmāsmiṃsaṃsāsvattaṃ.

213. When 'sa', 'smā', 'smiṃ', 'saṃ', and 'sā' follow, 'atta' is the substitute.

Taiccetassa sabbanāmassa sabbasseva attaṃ hoti vā sa smā smiṃ saṃ sāiccetesu vacanesu sabbattha liṅgesu. Assa nassa tassa, nesaṃ tesaṃ nesānaṃ tesānaṃ.

For the pronoun 'ta', the whole stem optionally becomes 'atta' when the endings 'sa', 'smā', 'smiṃ', 'saṃ', 'sā' follow, in all genders. Assa, nassa, tassa; nesaṃ, tesaṃ; nesānaṃ, tesānaṃ.

“Smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi vā”ti ito “smāsmiṃnaṃ, mhāmhī”ti ca vattate.

From the rule 'Smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi vā', the terms 'smā, smiṃ, naṃ' and 'mhā, mhi' are carried forward.

214. Na timehi katākārehi.

214. Not after 'ta' and 'ima' when their form has been changed.

Ta imaiccetehi katākārehi paresaṃ smāsmiṃnaṃ mhā mhiiccete ādesā na honti.

After 'ta' and 'ima' when they have been altered, the substitutions 'mhā' for 'smā' and 'mhi' for 'smiṃ' do not occur.

Pakatisandhividhāna

The Rule of Natural Form in Sandhi

Atha [M 0.0022] sarānameva sandhikāriye sampatte pakatibhāvo vuccate.

Now, when the operation of sandhi concerning vowels is applicable, their remaining in a natural state is explained.

“Sarā, pakatī”ti ca vattate.

And the terms 'vowels' and 'natural' are carried forward.

35. Sare kvaci.

35. Sometimes, when a vowel follows.

Sarā kho sare pare kvaci chandabhedāsukhuccāraṇaṭṭhāne, sandhicchārahitaṭṭhāne ca pakatirūpāni honti, na lopādesavikāramāpajjanteti attho.

Indeed, vowels, when another vowel follows, sometimes remain in their natural form in places where there is a metrical break or difficulty of pronunciation, and in places where sandhi is not desired. The meaning is that they do not undergo elision, substitution, or modification.

Tattha pakatiṭṭhānaṃ nāma ālapanantā anitismiṃ acchandānurakkhaṇe asamāse padantadīghā ca ikārukārā ca nāmapadantātītakriyādimhīti evamādi.

Therein, the 'natural position' refers to: the end of vocatives not followed by 'iti'; when not for the sake of preserving meter; in non-compounds; long 'i' and 'u' at the end of a word; at the end of a noun or past tense verb, and so forth.

Ālapanantesu tāva – katamā cānanda aniccasaññā, katamā cānanda ādīnavasaññā, sāriputta idhekacco, ehi sivika uṭṭhehi, upāsakā idhekacco, bhoti ayye, bhikkhu arogaṃ tava sīlaṃ, siñca bhikkhu imaṃ nāvaṃ, bhikkhave evaṃ vadāmi, pañcime gahapatayo ānisaṃsā iccevamādīsu pakatibhāvo, pubbassaralopayavādesādayo na honti.

First, in vocative endings – 'What, Ananda, is the perception of impermanence? And what, Ananda, is the perception of danger?', 'Sariputta, here a certain one', 'Come, Sivika, arise!', 'Lay followers, here a certain one', 'Madam, venerable lady!', 'Monk, your virtue is free from disease', 'Monk, bail out this boat!', 'Monks, thus I say', 'These five advantages, householders' – in these and similar cases, the natural state prevails; elision of the preceding vowel, substitutions of 'y' and 'v', and so forth, do not occur.

Kvaciggahaṇena itismiṃ chandānurakkhaṇe sandhi hoti, yathā – sakkā devīti, namo te buddha vīratthu.

By the inclusion of 'kvaci', sandhi sometimes occurs in the context of 'iti' and for metrical preservation, as in: 'sakkā devīti', and 'namo te buddha vīratthu'.

Sareti kiṃ? Sādhu mahārājāti, evaṃ kira bhikkhūti.

Why the condition 'sare' (when a vowel follows)? For example: 'Sādhu mahārājāti', 'evaṃ kira bhikkhūti'.

Asamāse padantadīghesu – āyasmā ānando gāthā ajjhabhāsi, devā ābhassarā yathā, tevijjā iddhippattā [M 0.0023] ca, bhagavā uṭṭhāyāsanā, bhagavā etadavoca, abhivādetvā ekamantaṃ aṭṭhāsi, gantvā olokento, bhūtavādī atthavādī, yaṃ itthī arahā assa, sāmāvatī āha, pāpakārī ubhayattha tappati, nadī ottharati, ye te bhikkhū appicchā, bhikkhū āmantesi, bhikkhūujjhāyiṃsu, bhikkhū evamāhaṃsu, imasmiṃ gāme ārakkhakā, sabbe ime, katame ekādasa, gambhīre odakantike, appamādo amatapadaṃ, saṅgho āgacchatu, ko imaṃ pathaviṃ viccessati, āloko udapādi, eko ekāya, cattāro oghā.

In non-compounds with long word-final vowels – 'Venerable Ānanda recited a verse', 'the Abhassara gods, just as', 'those with threefold knowledge and who have attained psychic power', 'the Blessed One rose from his seat', 'the Blessed One said this', 'having paid homage, he stood to one side', 'going and looking', 'a speaker of truth, a speaker of meaning', 'if a woman should be an arahant', 'Sāmāvatī said', 'the wrongdoer suffers in both existences', 'the river crosses over', 'those monks who are of few desires', 'he addressed the monks', 'the monks complained', 'the monks said this', 'in this village there are protectors', 'all these', 'which are the eleven', 'at the edge of deep water', 'heedfulness is the path to the Deathless', 'may the Saṅgha come', 'who will conquer this earth?', 'light arose', 'one by one', 'the four floods'.

Nipātesupi – are ahampi, sace imassa kāyassa, no abhikkamo, aho acchariyo, atho anto ca, atha kho āyasmā, atho oṭṭhavacittakā, tato āmantayī satthā.

Also in particles – 'Are, I also', 'if of this body', 'no advance', 'Oh, wonderful!', 'and also inside', 'then the Venerable One', 'and also with painted lips', 'then the Teacher addressed'.

Kvaciggahaṇena akāra itīvevetthādīsu sandhipi. Yathā – āgatattha, āgatamhā, katamāssu cattāro, appassutāyaṃ puriso, itthīti, ca marīva, sabbeva, sveva, eseva nayo, parisuddhetthāyasmanto, nettha, taṃ kutettha labbhā, sacesa brāhmaṇa, tathūpamaṃ, yathāha.

By the inclusion of 'kvaci', sandhi also occurs in cases involving 'iti', 'iva', 'eva', 'ettha', and so forth. For example: 'āgatattha', 'āgatamhā', 'katamāssu cattāro', 'appassutāyaṃ puriso', 'itthīti', 'ca marīva', 'sabbeva', 'sveva', 'eseva nayo', 'parisuddhetthāyasmanto', 'nettha', 'taṃ kutettha labbhā', 'sacesa brāhmaṇa', 'tathūpamaṃ', 'yathāha'.

Asamāseti kiṃ? Jivhāyatanaṃ, avijjogho, itthindriyaṃ, abhibhāyatanaṃ, bhayatupaṭṭhānaṃ. Acchandānurakkhaṇeti [M 0.0024] kiṃ? Saddhīdha vittaṃ purisassa seṭṭhaṃ, yo missaro.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'asamāse'? [Examples of elision in compounds:] the tongue sense-sphere, the flood of ignorance, the faculty of womanhood, the sphere of mastery, the arising from fear. What is the purpose of [the word] 'acchandānurakkhaṇe'? [Examples of elision for metrical preservation:] 'Faith in this world is the highest wealth for a person,' 'who is my lord.'

Nāmapadantaikārukāresu – gāthāhi ajjhabhāsi, pupphāni āhariṃsu, satthu adāsi.

In the case of the final 'i' and 'u' of nouns: 'he addressed them with verses,' 'they brought flowers,' 'he gave to the Teacher.'

Kvacīti kiṃ? Manasākāsi.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'kvaci'? An example is: `Manasākāsi`.

36. Sarā pakati byañjane.

36. Vowels are unchanged before a consonant.

Sarā kho byañjane pare pakatirūpā hontīti yebhuyyena dīgharassalopehi vikārābhāvo. Yathā – accayo, paccayo, bhāsati vā karoti vā, vedanākkhandho, bhāgyavā, bhadro kasāmiva, dīyati, tuṇhībhūto, so dhammaṃ deseti.

Indeed, vowels, when a consonant follows, mostly remain in their natural form; that is, there is an absence of modification through lengthening, shortening, or elision. For example: `accayo`, `paccayo`, `bhāsati vā karoti vā`, `vedanākkhandho`, `bhāgyavā`, `bhadro kasāmiva`, `dīyati`, `tuṇhībhūto`, `so dhammaṃ deseti`.

Iti pakatisandhividhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

Thus, the section on natural sandhi is concluded.

Byañjanasandhividhāna

The Section on Consonant Sandhi

Atha byañjanasandhi vuccate.

Now, consonant sandhi is explained.

“Byañjane”ti adhikāro, “sarā, kvacī”ti ca vattate.

The heading 'byañjane' (before a consonant) is the governing rule, and 'sarā' (vowels) and 'kvaci' (sometimes) also carry over.

37. Dīghaṃ.

37. Lengthening.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci dīghaṃ pappontīti suttasukhuccāraṇachandānurakkhaṇaṭṭhānesu dīgho.

Indeed, vowels, when a consonant follows, sometimes attain length; thus, lengthening occurs in places for the sake of easy pronunciation of the Sutta and for metrical preservation.

Tyassa pahīnā tyāssa pahīnā, svassa svāssa, madhuva maññati bālo madhuvā maññatī bālo, tathā evaṃ gāme munī [M 0.0025] care, khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā, na maṅkū bhavissāmi, svākkhāto, yvāhaṃ, kāmato jāyatī soko, kāmato jāyatī bhayaṃ, sakko ujū ca suhujū ca, anūpaghāto, dūrakkhaṃ, dūramaṃ, sūrakkhaṃ, dūharatā.

`Tyassa pahīnā` becomes `tyāssa pahīnā`; `svassa` becomes `svāssa`; `madhuva maññati bālo` becomes `madhuvā maññatī bālo`; `tathā evaṃ gāme muni care`; `khantī paramaṃ tapo titikkhā`; `na maṅkū bhavissāmi`; `svākkhāto`; `yvāhaṃ`; `kāmato jāyatī soko`; `kāmato jāyatī bhayaṃ`; `sakko ujū ca suhujū ca`; `anūpaghāto`; `dūrakkhaṃ`; `dūramaṃ`; `sūrakkhaṃ`; `dūharatā`.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Tyajja, svassa, patiliyyati.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'kvaci'? [Examples where lengthening does not occur:] `Tyajja`, `svassa`, `patiliyyati`.

Yiṭṭhaṃ vā hutaṃ vā loke, yadi vā sāvake, puggalā dhammadasā te, bhovādī nāma so hoti, yathābhāvī guṇena so itīdha –

'Whatever is offered or sacrificed in the world,' 'or to disciples,' 'those persons are seers of the Dhamma,' 'he is by name one who says "bho",' 'he is of such a nature by his quality' – thus here:

Pubbasmiṃyevādhikāre –

In that very same governing rule:

38. Rassaṃ.

38. Shortening.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci rassaṃ pappontīti chandānurakkhaṇe, āgame, saṃyoge ca rassattaṃ.

Indeed, vowels, when a consonant follows, sometimes attain shortness; thus, shortening occurs for metrical preservation, in the case of an augment, and in the case of a conjunct consonant.

Chandānurakkhaṇe tāva yiṭṭhaṃva hutaṃva loke, yadiva sāvake, puggala dhammadasā te, bhovādi nāma so hoti, yathābhāvi guṇena so.

First, for metrical preservation: 'yiṭṭhaṃva hutaṃva loke', 'yadiva sāvake', 'puggala dhammadasā te', 'bhovādi nāma so hoti', 'yathābhāvi guṇena so'.

Āgame yathayidaṃ, sammadakkhāto.

In the case of an augment: `yathayidaṃ`, `sammadakkhāto`.

Saṃyoge parākamo parakkamo, āsādo assādo, evaṃ taṇhakkhayo, jhānassa lābhimhi, vasimhi, thullaccayo.

In the case of a conjunct consonant: `parākamo` becomes `parakkamo`; `āsādo` becomes `assādo`; similarly, `taṇhakkhayo`, `lābhimhi` (from `lābhī` + `amhi`), `vasimhi` (from `vasī` + `amhi`), `thullaccayo`.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Māyidaṃ, manasā daññā vimuttānaṃ, yathākkamaṃ, ākhyātikaṃ, dīyyati, sūyyati.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'kvaci'? [Examples where shortening does not occur:] `Māyidaṃ`, `manasā daññā vimuttānaṃ`, `yathākkamaṃ`, `ākhyātikaṃ`, `dīyyati`, `sūyyati`.

Eso kho byantiṃ kāhiti, so gacchaṃ na nivattati iccatra –

'He indeed will make an end; going, he does not turn back' – in this context:

Tasmiṃyevādhikāre –

In that very same governing rule:

39. Lopañca [M 0.0026] tatrākāro.

39. And elision, and the vowel 'a' in that place.

Sarā kho byañjane pare kvaci lopaṃ papponti, tatra lutte ṭhāne akārāgamo ca hoti. Etatasaddantokārassevāyaṃ lopo.

Indeed, vowels, when a consonant follows, sometimes undergo elision, and in that elided place, the insertion of the vowel 'a' also occurs. This elision applies to the final 'o' of the word 'eta'.

Esa kho byantiṃ kāhiti, sa gacchaṃ na nivattati, evaṃ esa dhammo, esa pattosi, sa muni, sa sīlavā.

`Esa kho byantiṃ kāhiti`, `sa gacchaṃ na nivattati`, `evaṃ esa dhammo`, `esa pattosi`, `sa muni`, `sa sīlavā`.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Eso dhammo, so muni, so sīlavā.

What is the purpose of [the word] 'kvaci'? [Examples where elision does not occur:] `Eso dhammo`, `so muni`, `so sīlavā`.

Casaddena etasaddantassa sarepi kvaci lopo. Yathā – esa attho, esa ābhogo, esa idāni.

By the word 'ca', elision of the final vowel of the word 'eta' also occurs sometimes even before a vowel. For example: `esa attho`, `esa ābhogo`, `esa idāni`.

Vipariṇāmena “saramhā, byañjanassā”ti ca vattate.

By transformation of case, 'saramhā' (from a vowel) and 'byañjanassa' (of a consonant) also carry over.

40. Paradvebhāvo ṭhāne.

40. Doubling of the following consonant in certain cases.

Saramhā parassa byañjanassa dvebhāvo hoti ṭhāne. Dvinnaṃ bhāvo dvibhāvo, so eva dvebhāvo.

The doubling of a consonant following a vowel occurs in specific cases. The state of two is dvibhāva, and that itself is dvebhāva.

Ettha ca ṭhānaṃ nāma rassākārato paraṃ pa pati paṭikamukusa kudha kī gaha juta ñāsi su sambhū sara sasādīnamādibyañjanānaṃ dvebhāvaṃ, tika taya tiṃsa vatādīnamādi ca, vatu vaṭudisādīnamantañca, u du ni-upasagga ta catu cha santasaddādesādiparañca, apadantā nākāradīghato yakārādi ca,

Here, the term 'ṭhāna' refers to the doubling of the initial consonants of 'pa', 'pati', 'paṭi', 'kama', 'kusa', 'kudha', 'kī', 'gaha', 'juta', 'ñāsi', 'su', 'sambhū', 'sara', 'sasa', and so forth, when they follow a short 'a' vowel. It also includes the initial consonants of 'tika', 'taya', 'tiṃsa', 'vata', and so forth, and the final consonants of 'vatu', 'vaṭu', 'disa', and so forth. Furthermore, it applies to a consonant following the prefixes 'u', 'du', 'ni', or following words like 'ta', 'catu', 'cha', 'santa', 'sadda', their substitutes, and so forth. Lastly, it involves the initial 'y' and so forth, when not at the end of a word, following a long vowel (excluding the letter 'na').

Yavataṃ talanādīna-mādeso ca sayādinaṃ;

Saha dhātvantassādeso, sīsakāro tapādito.

And the substitution of 't', 'l', 'n', and so forth for 'y', 'v', and so forth, and for 'sa' and so forth; together with the substitution for the final consonant of a root; and the sibilant sound arising from 'ta', 'pa', and so forth.

Chandānurakkhaṇe ca – ghara jhe dhaṃsu bhamādīnamādi ca, rassākārato vaggānaṃ catutthadutiyā ca iccevamādi.

And for the preservation of meter: the initial consonants of 'ghara', 'jhe', 'dhaṃsu', 'bhama', and so forth; and the fourth and second letters of the consonant classes after a short 'a' vowel, and so forth.

Tattha [M 0.0027] pa pati paṭīsu tāva – idha pamādo idhappamādo, evaṃ appamādo, vippayutto, suppasanno, sammā padhānaṃ sammappadhānaṃ, rassattaṃ, appativattiyo, adhipatippaccayo, suppatiṭṭhito, appaṭipuggalo, vippaṭisāro, suppaṭipanno, suppaṭipatti.

Therein, first regarding 'pa', 'pati', and 'paṭi': 'idha pamādo' becomes 'idhappamādo'; similarly, 'appamādo', 'vippayutto', 'suppasanno'; 'sammā padhānaṃ' becomes 'sammappadhānaṃ', with shortening of the vowel; 'appativattiyo', 'adhipatippaccayo', 'suppatiṭṭhito', 'appaṭipuggalo', 'vippaṭisāro', 'suppaṭipanno', 'suppaṭipatti'.

Kamādidhātūsu – pakkamo, paṭikkamo, hetukkamo, ākamati akkamati, evaṃ parakkamati, yathākkamaṃ.

In roots beginning with 'kama', and so forth: 'pakkamo', 'paṭikkamo', 'hetukkamo'; 'ākamati' becomes 'akkamati'; similarly, 'parakkamati', 'yathākkamaṃ'.

Pakkosati, paṭikkosati, anukkosati, ākosati, akkosati.

Pakkosati, paṭikkosati, anukkosati, ākosati, akkosati.

Akkuddho, atikkodho.

Akkuddho, atikkodho.

Dhanakkīto, vikkayo, anukkayo.

Dhanakkīto, vikkayo, anukkayo.

Paggaho, viggaho, anuggaho, niggaho, candaggaho, diṭṭhiggāho.

Paggaho, viggaho, anuggaho, niggaho, candaggaho, diṭṭhiggāho.

Pajjoto, vijjotati, ujjoto.

Pajjoto, vijjotati, ujjoto.

Kataññū, viññū, paññāṇaṃ, viññāṇaṃ, anuññā, manuññā, samaññā.

Kataññū, viññū, paññāṇaṃ, viññāṇaṃ, anuññā, manuññā, samaññā.

Avassayo, nissayo, samussayo.

Avassayo, nissayo, samussayo.

Appassuto, vissuto, bahussuto, āsavā assavā.

Appassuto, vissuto, bahussuto, āsavā assavā.

Passambhanto, vissambhati.

Passambhanto, vissambhati.

Aṭṭassaro, vissarati, anussarati.

Aṭṭassaro, vissarati, anussarati.

Passasanto, vissasanto, mahussasanto, āsāso assāso.

Passasanto, vissasanto, mahussasanto, āsāso assāso.

Avissajjento, vissajjento, pariccajanto, upaddavo, upakkiliṭṭho, mittaddu, āyabbayo, udabbahi iccādi.

Avissajjento, vissajjento, pariccajanto, upaddavo, upakkiliṭṭho, mittaddu, āyabbayo, udabbahi, and so forth.

Saramhāti [M 0.0028] kiṃ? Sampayutto, sampatijāto, sampaṭicchannaṃ, saṅkamanto, saṅgaho.

Why is 'saramhā' stated? For cases such as: 'Sampayutto', 'sampatijāto', 'sampaṭicchannaṃ', 'saṅkamanto', 'saṅgaho'.

Ṭhāneti kiṃ? Mā ca pamādo, patigayhati, vacīpakopaṃ rakkheyya, ye pamattā yathā matā, manopakopaṃ rakkheyya, idha modati, pecca modati.

Why is 'ṭhāne' stated? For cases such as: 'Mā ca pamādo', 'patigayhati', 'vacīpakopaṃ rakkheyya', 'ye pamattā yathā matā', 'manopakopaṃ rakkheyya', 'idha modati', 'pecca modati'.

Tikādīsu – kusalattikaṃ, pītittikaṃ, hetuttikaṃ, vedanāttikaṃ, lokattayaṃ, bodhittayaṃ, vatthuttayaṃ. Ekattiṃsa, dvattiṃsa, catuttiṃsa. Sīlabbataṃ, subbato, sappītiko, samannāgato, punappunaṃ iccādi.

In 'tika' and so forth: 'kusalattikaṃ', 'pītittikaṃ', 'hetuttikaṃ', 'vedanāttikaṃ', 'lokattayaṃ', 'bodhittayaṃ', 'vatthuttayaṃ'; 'Ekattiṃsa', 'dvattiṃsa', 'catuttiṃsa'; 'Sīlabbataṃ', 'subbato', 'sappītiko', 'samannāgato', 'punappunaṃ', and so forth.

Vatu vaṭu disādīnamante yathā – vattati, vaṭṭati, dassanaṃ, phasso iccādi.

Regarding the final consonant of 'vatu', 'vaṭu', 'disa', and so forth, for example: 'vattati', 'vaṭṭati', 'dassanaṃ', 'phasso', and so forth.

U du ni upasaggādiparesu – ukaṃso ukkaṃso. Dukaraṃ dukkaraṃ, nikaṅkho nikkaṅkhe.

When following the prefixes 'u', 'du', 'ni', and so forth: 'ukaṃso' becomes 'ukkaṃso'; 'dukaraṃ' becomes 'dukkaraṃ'; 'nikaṅkho' becomes 'nikkaṅkho'.

Evaṃ uggataṃ, duccaritaṃ, nijjaṭaṃ, uññātaṃ, unnati, uttaro, dukkaro, niddaro, unnato, duppañño, dubbalo, nimmalo, uyyutto, dullabho, nibbatto, ussāho, dussaho, nissāro.

Similarly: 'uggataṃ', 'duccaritaṃ', 'nijjaṭaṃ', 'uññātaṃ', 'unnati', 'uttaro', 'dukkaro', 'niddaro', 'unnato', 'duppañño', 'dubbalo', 'nimmalo', 'uyyutto', 'dullabho', 'nibbatto', 'ussāho', 'dussaho', 'nissāro'.

Tathā takkaro, tajjo, tanninno, tappabhavo, tammayo.

Likewise: 'takkaro', 'tajjo', 'tanninno', 'tappabhavo', 'tammayo'.

Catukkaṃ, catuddisaṃ, catuppādo, catubbidhaṃ, catussālaṃ.

'Catukkaṃ', 'catuddisaṃ', 'catuppādo', 'catubbidhaṃ', 'catussālaṃ'.

Chakkaṃ, channavuti, chappadikā, chabbassāni.

'Chakkaṃ', 'channavuti', 'chappadikā', 'chabbassāni'.

Sakkāro, sakkato, saddiṭṭhi, sappuriso, mahabbalo.

'Sakkāro', 'sakkato', 'saddiṭṭhi', 'sappuriso', 'mahabbalo'.

Ṭhāneti kiṃ? Nikāyo, nidānaṃ, nivāso, nivāto, tato, catuvīsati, chasaṭṭhi.

Why is 'ṭhāne' stated? For cases such as: 'Nikāyo', 'nidānaṃ', 'nivāso', 'nivāto', 'tato', 'catuvīsati', 'chasaṭṭhi'.

Yakārādimhi [M 0.0029] – nīyyati, sūyyati, abhibhūyya, viceyya, vineyya, dheyyaṃ, neyyaṃ, seyyo, jeyyo, veyyākaraṇo.

In the case of an initial 'ya': 'nīyyati', 'sūyyati', 'abhibhūyya', 'viceyya', 'vineyya', 'dheyyaṃ', 'neyyaṃ', 'seyyo', 'jeyyo', 'veyyākaraṇo'.

Ādisaddena etto, ettāvatā.

By the term 'ādi'—from here, thus far.

Anākāraggahaṇaṃ kiṃ? Mālāya, dolāya, samādāya.

Why the non-inclusion of the form? For a garland, for a swing, having undertaken.

Ṭhāneti kiṃ? Upanīyati, sūyati, toyaṃ.

Why 'ṭhāne'? It is brought near, it is heard, water.

Yavatamādese – jāti andho, vipali āso, ani āyo, yadi evaṃ, api ekacce, api ekadā iccatra, ikārassa “ivaṇṇo yaṃ navā”ti yakāre kate –

Regarding the substitutions for ya, va, ta, ma—in 'jāti andho' (blind from birth), 'vipali āso' (perverted aspiration), 'ani āyo' (without gain), 'yadi evaṃ' (if so), 'api ekacce' (even some), 'api ekadā' (even once)—here, for the vowel 'i', when 'ya' is formed by the rule 'the i-sound optionally becomes ya'—

“Sabbassa so dāmhi vā”ti ito maṇḍūkagatiyā vāti vattate.

From the rule 'Sabbassa so dāmhi vā', the word 'vā' carries forward by the frog's leap method.

41. Yavataṃ talanadakārānaṃ byañjanāni calañajakārattaṃ.

41. For the consonants ya, va, ta, la, na, da, there is the change to ca, la, ña, ja, ka.

Yakāravantānaṃ talanadakārānaṃ saṃyogabyañjanāni yathākkamaṃ calañajakārattamāpajjante vā.

The consonants ta, la, na, and da, when followed by ya in a conjunct, optionally become ca, la, ña, and ja respectively.

Kāraggahaṇaṃ yavataṃ sakāra ka ca ṭa pavaggānaṃ sakārakacaṭapavaggādesatthaṃ, tathā yavataṃ ta dha ṇakārānaṃ cha jhañakārādesatthañca, tato yavatamādesassa anena dvibhāvo.

The inclusion of 'kāra' is for the purpose of substituting the sa, ka, ca, ṭa, and pa groups for ya, va, ta; and likewise, for substituting cha, jha, ña for ta, dha, ṇa. Thus, by this, the substitution for ya, va, ta, ma becomes twofold.

Jaccandho, vipallāso, aññāyo, yajjevaṃ, appekacce appekadā.

Blind from birth, perversion, misfortune, just so, some, at times.

Vāti kiṃ? Paṭisanthāravutyassa, bālyaṃ, ālasyaṃ.

Why 'vā'? Of one whose conduct is hospitality, folly, laziness.

Saramhāti kiṃ? Añāyo, ākāsānañcāyatanaṃ.

Why 'saramhā'? Misfortune, the sphere of the infinitude of space.

Tapādito simhi – tapassī, yasassī.

From 'tapa' and so on, when the 'si' suffix follows: ascetic, glorious.

Chandānurakkhaṇe [M 0.0030] – nappajjahe vaṇṇabalaṃ purāṇaṃ, ujjugatesu seyyo, gacchanti suggatinti.

In preserving the meter—one should not abandon the ancient strength of sound; among the upright, it is better; they go to a good bourn.

Vaggacatutthadutiyesu pana tasmiṃyevādhikāre “paradvebhāvo ṭhāne”ti ca vattate.

However, concerning the fourth and second letters of a class, in that very same section, the rule 'doubling of the subsequent in its place' also applies.

Vaggacatutthadutiyānaṃ sadisavasena dvibhāve sampatte niyamatthamāha.

When doubling is obtained for the fourth and second letters of a class by way of similarity, it states a restrictive rule.

42. Vagge ghosāghosānaṃ tatiyapaṭhamā.

42. In a class, for voiced and unvoiced sounds, the third and first letters.

Saramhā parabhūtānaṃ vagge ghosāghosānaṃ byañjanānaṃ yathākkamaṃ vaggatatiya paṭhamakkharā dvibhāvaṃ gacchanti ṭhāneti ṭhānāsannavasena tabbagge tatiyapaṭhamāva honti.

Subsequent to a vowel, the voiced and unvoiced consonants in a class, respectively, undergo doubling, becoming the third and first letters of their class by proximity of articulation.

Ettha ca sampatte niyamattā ghosāghosaggahaṇena catutthadutiyāva adhippetā, itarathā aniṭṭhappasaṅgosiyā. Tena “kataññū, tannayo, tammayo”tiādīsu vaggapañcamānaṃ satipi ghosatte tatiyappasaṅgona hoti, ṭhānādhikārato vā.

And here, this being a restrictive rule, only the fourth and second letters are intended by the inclusion of 'voiced' and 'unvoiced'; otherwise, an undesired consequence would arise. Therefore, in cases like 'kataññū', 'tannayo', 'tammayo', etc., even though the fifth letters of a class are voiced, the consequence of the third letter does not occur, or it is due to the governing rule concerning the place of articulation.

Gharādīsu pa u du niādiparacatutthesu tāva – pagharati paggharati, evaṃ uggharati, ugghāṭeti, dugghoso, nigghoso, eseva cajjhānaphalo, paṭhamajjhānaṃ, abhijjhāyati, ujjhāyati, viddhaṃseti, uddhaṃsito, uddhāro, niddhāro, niddhano, niddhuto, vibbhanto, ubbhato, dubbhikkhaṃ, nibbhayaṃ, tabbhāvo, catuddhā, cabhubbhi, chaddhā, saddhammo, sabbhūto, mahaddhano, mahabbhayaṃ.

First, in words like 'ghara' and so on, with fourth-class consonants preceded by 'pa', 'u', 'du', 'ni', etc.—'pagharati, paggharati'; similarly 'uggharati, ugghāṭeti, dugghoso, nigghoso, eseva cajjhānaphalo, paṭhamajjhānaṃ, abhijjhāyati, ujjhāyati, viddhaṃseti, uddhaṃsito, uddhāro, niddhāro, niddhano, niddhuto, vibbhanto, ubbhato, dubbhikkhaṃ, nibbhayaṃ, tabbhāvo, catuddhā, cabhubbhi, chaddhā, saddhammo, sabbhūto, mahaddhano, mahabbhayaṃ'.

Yavata mādesādīsu – bojjhaṅgā, āsabbhaṃ, bujjhitabbaṃ, bujjhati.

In the substitutions for ya, va, ta, ma, and so on—'bojjhaṅgā, āsabbhaṃ, bujjhitabbaṃ, bujjhati'.

Ṭhāneti [M 0.0031] kiṃ? Sīlavantassa jhāyino, ye jhānappasutā dhīrā, nidhānaṃ, mahādhanaṃ.

Why 'ṭhāne'? "Of the virtuous meditator, those wise ones devoted to meditation, a treasure, great wealth."

Rassākāratoparaṃ vaggadutiyesu – pañca khandhā pañcakkhandhā, evaṃrūpakkhandho, akkhamo, abhikkhaṇaṃ, avikkhepo, jātikkhettaṃ, dhātukkhobho, āyukkhayo. Setachattaṃ setacchattaṃ, evaṃ sabbacchannaṃ, vicchinnaṃ, bodhicchāyā, jambucchāyā, samucchedo. Tatra ṭhito tatraṭṭhito, evaṃ thalaṭṭhaṃ, jalaṭṭhaṃ, adhiṭṭhitaṃ, niṭṭhitaṃ, cattāriṭṭhānāni, garuṭṭhāniyo, samuṭṭhito, suppaṭṭhāno. Yasatthero, yattha, tattha, pattharati, vitthāro, abhitthuto, vitthambhito, anutthunaṃ, catuttho, kuttha. Papphoṭeti, mahapphalaṃ, nipphalaṃ, vipphāro, paripphuseyya, madhupphāṇitaṃ.

After a short vowel, concerning the second letters of a class—'pañca khandhā' becomes 'pañcakkhandhā'; similarly 'rūpakkhandho', 'akkhamo', 'abhikkhaṇaṃ', 'avikkhepo', 'jātikkhettaṃ', 'dhātukkhobho', 'āyukkhayo'. 'Setachattaṃ' becomes 'setacchattaṃ'; similarly 'sabbacchannaṃ', 'vicchinnaṃ', 'bodhicchāyā', 'jambucchāyā', 'samucchedo'. 'Tatra ṭhito' becomes 'tatraṭṭhito'; similarly 'thalaṭṭhaṃ', 'jalaṭṭhaṃ', 'adhiṭṭhitaṃ', 'niṭṭhitaṃ', 'cattāriṭṭhānāni', 'garuṭṭhāniyo', 'samuṭṭhito', 'suppaṭṭhāno'. 'Yasatthero', 'yattha', 'tattha', 'pattharati', 'vitthāro', 'abhitthuto', 'vitthambhito', 'anutthunaṃ', 'catuttho', 'kuttha'. 'Papphoṭeti', 'mahapphalaṃ', 'nipphalaṃ', 'vipphāro', 'paripphuseyya', 'madhupphāṇitaṃ'.

Ākārato – ākhāto ākkhāto, evaṃ taṇhākkhayo, āṇākkhettaṃ, saññākkhandho, āchādayati, ācchādayati, evaṃ ācchindati, nāvāṭṭhaṃ, āttharati, āpphoṭeti.

From the vowel 'ā'—'ākhāto' becomes 'ākkhāto'; similarly 'taṇhākkhayo', 'āṇākkhettaṃ', 'saññākkhandho'. 'āchādayati' becomes 'ācchādayati'; similarly 'ācchindati', 'nāvāṭṭhaṃ', 'āttharati', 'āpphoṭeti'.

Saramhāti kiṃ? Saṅkhāro, taṅkhaṇe, sañchannaṃ, taṇṭhānaṃ, santhuto, tamphalaṃ.

Why 'saramhā'? 'Saṅkhāro', 'taṅkhaṇe', 'sañchannaṃ', 'taṇṭhānaṃ', 'santhuto', 'tamphalaṃ'.

Ṭhāneti kiṃ? Pūvakhajjakaṃ, tassa chaviyādīni chinditvā, yathā ṭhitaṃ, kathaṃ, kammaphalaṃ.

Why 'ṭhāne'? A cake and edibles, having cut away its skin and so on, as it stands, how, the result of kamma.

Nikamati, nipatti, nicayo, nicarati, nitaraṇaṃ iccatra – “do dhassa cā”ti ettha caggahaṇassa bahulatthattā tena caggahaṇena yathāpayogaṃ bahudhā ādeso siyā.

In 'nikamati', 'nipatti', 'nicayo', 'nicarati', 'nitaraṇaṃ'—here, in the rule 'do dhassa ca', because the inclusion of 'ca' has the meaning of 'variously', by that 'ca', various substitutions may occur according to usage.

Yathā – ni upasaggato kamu pada ci cara tarānaṃ paṭhamassa vaggadutiyo iminā dvittaṃ, nikkhamati, nipphatti, nicchayo, niccharati, nittharaṇaṃ.

For example—from the prefix 'ni', for the roots 'kamu', 'pada', 'ci', 'cara', 'tara', the first consonant becomes the second of its class and is doubled by this rule, thus: 'nikkhamati,' 'nipphatti,' 'nicchayo,' 'niccharati,' 'nittharaṇaṃ'.

Tathā [M 0.0032] bo vassa kuva diva siva vajādīnaṃ dvirūpassāti vakāradvayassa bakāradvayaṃ, yathā – kubbanto, evaṃ kubbāno, kubbanti, sadhātvantayādesassa dvittaṃ. Divati dibbati, evaṃ dibbanto, sibbati, sibbanto, pavajati pabbajati, pabbajanto, nivānaṃ nibbānaṃ, nibbuto, nibbindati, udabbayaṃ iccādi.

Similarly, for 'bho', 'vas', 'kru', 'div', 'siv', 'vraj' and so on, a double 'v' becomes a double 'b', as in 'kubbanto'; similarly 'kubbāno', 'kubbanti'; there is doubling of the substitution at the end of the root. 'Divati' becomes 'dibbati'; similarly 'dibbanto'. 'Sibbati', 'sibbanto'. 'Pavajati' becomes 'pabbajati', 'pabbajanto'. 'Nivānaṃ' becomes 'nibbānaṃ'. 'Nibbuto'. 'Nibbindati'. 'Udabbayaṃ', etc.

Lo rassa pari taruṇādīnaṃ kvaci. Paripanno palipanno, evaṃ palibodho, pallaṅkaṃ, taruṇo taluno, mahāsālo, māluto, sukhumālo.

Sometimes 'l' is substituted for 'r' in 'pari', 'taruṇa' and so on. 'Paripanno' becomes 'palipanno'; similarly 'palibodho', 'pallaṅkaṃ'. 'Taruṇo' becomes 'taluno'. 'Mahāsālo', 'māluto', 'sukhumālo'.

Ṭo tassa dukkatādīnaṃ kvaci. Yathā – dukkataṃ dukkaṭaṃ, evaṃ sukaṭaṃ, pahaṭo, patthaṭo, uddhaṭo, visaṭo iccādi.

Sometimes 'ṭ' is substituted for 't' in 'dukkata' and so on. For example, 'dukkataṃ' becomes 'dukkaṭaṃ'; likewise 'sukaṭaṃ', 'pahaṭo', 'patthaṭo', 'uddhaṭo', 'visaṭo', etc.

Ko tassa niyatādīnaṃ kvaci. Niyato niyako.

Sometimes 'k' is substituted for 't' in 'niyata' and so on. 'Niyato' becomes 'niyako'.

Yo jassa nijādissa vā, nijaṃputtaṃ niyaṃputtaṃ.

Sometimes 'y' is substituted for 'j' in 'nija' and so on, optionally. 'Nijaṃputtaṃ' becomes 'niyaṃputtaṃ'.

Ko gassa kulūpagādīnaṃ, kulūpago kulūpako.

Sometimes 'k' is substituted for 'g' in 'kulūpaga' and so on. 'Kulūpago' becomes 'kulūpako'.

Tathā ṇo nassa pa pariādito. Panidhānaṃ paṇidhānaṃ, evaṃ paṇipāto, paṇāmo, paṇītaṃ, pariṇato, pariṇāmo, ninnayo niṇṇayo, evaṃ uṇṇato, oṇato iccādi.

Similarly, 'ṇ' is substituted for 'n' after 'pa', 'pari', and so on. 'Panidhānaṃ' becomes 'paṇidhānaṃ'; likewise 'paṇipāto', 'paṇāmo', 'paṇītaṃ', 'pariṇato', 'pariṇāmo'. 'Ninnayo' becomes 'niṇṇayo'; likewise 'uṇṇato', 'oṇato', etc.

Patiaggi, patihaññati itīdha –

In the case of 'Patiaggi', 'patihaññati', etc.—

43. Kvaci paṭi patissa.

43. Sometimes 'paṭi' is substituted for 'pati'.

Patiiccetassa upasaggassa sare vā byañjane vā pare kvaci paṭiādeso hoti pubbassaralopo. Paṭaggi, paṭihaññati.

For this prefix 'pati', when a vowel or consonant follows, there is sometimes the substitution of 'paṭi', and elision of the preceding vowel. 'Paṭaggi', 'paṭihaññati'.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Paccattaṃ, patilīyati.

Why is 'sometimes' stated? 'Paccattaṃ', 'patilīyati'.

Puthajano puthabhūtaṃ itīdha “anto”ti vattate.

In the case of 'Puthajano' and 'puthabhūtaṃ', here the term 'anto' (the final part) is carried forward.

44. Puthassu [M 0.0033] byañjane.

44. 'U' is substituted for the final vowel of 'putha' before a consonant.

Puthaiccetassa anto saro ukāro hoti byañjane pare, dvittaṃ. Puthujjano, puthubhūtaṃ.

For this 'putha', the final vowel becomes 'u' when a consonant follows, and there is doubling. 'Puthujjano', 'puthubhūtaṃ'.

Byañjaneti kiṃ? Putha ayaṃ. “Puthassa a putha”iti samāseneva siddhe puna antaggahaṇādhikārena kvaci aputhantassāpi uttaṃ sare.

Why is 'before a consonant' stated? For 'Putha ayaṃ'. Although established simply by compounding, by the governing rule concerning the final part, 'u' is sometimes substituted even for a stem not ending in 'putha' when a vowel follows.

Mano aññaṃ manuññaṃ, evaṃ imaṃ evumaṃ, paralopo, iti evaṃ itvevaṃ, ukārassa vakāro.

'Mano aññaṃ' becomes 'manuññaṃ'; similarly, 'imaṃ' becomes 'evumaṃ', with elision of the following vowel; 'iti evaṃ' becomes 'itvevaṃ', with the 'u' becoming 'v'.

Avakāso, avanaddho, avavadati, avasānamitīdha –

In 'Avakāso', 'avanaddho', 'avavadati', 'avasānaṃ'—in these cases—

“Kvaci byañjane”ti ca vattate.

And the rule 'sometimes before a consonant' is also carried forward.

45. O avassa.

45. 'O' is substituted for 'ava'.

Avaiccetassa upasaggassa okāro hoti kvaci byañjane pare. Okāso, onaddho, ovadati, osānaṃ.

For this prefix 'ava', the sound 'o' is sometimes substituted when a consonant follows. 'Okāso', 'onaddho', 'ovadati', 'osānaṃ'.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Avasānaṃ, avasussatu.

Why is 'sometimes' stated? 'Avasānaṃ', 'avasussatu'.

Byañjaneti kiṃ? Avayāgamanaṃ, avekkhati.

Why is 'before a consonant' stated? 'Avayāgamanaṃ', 'avekkhati'.

Avagate sūriye, avagacchati, avagahetvā itīdha –

In 'avagate sūriye', 'avagacchati', 'avagahetvā'—in these cases—

“Avasse”ti vattate oggahaṇañca.

The rule 'for ava' is carried forward, and also the mention of 'o'.

46. Tabbiparītūpapade byañjane ca.

46. And when the prefix has the opposite meaning, also before a consonant.

Avasaddassa upapade tiṭṭhamānassa tassokārassa viparīto ca hoti byañjane pare.

For the word 'ava' standing as a prefix, the opposite of the sound 'o' is also substituted for it when a consonant follows.

Tassa viparīto tabbiparīto, upoccāritaṃ padaṃ upapadaṃ, okāraviparītoti ukārassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ. Casaddo katthaci [M 0.0034] nivattanattho, dvittaṃ. Uggate sūriye, uggacchati, uggahetvā.

'Tabbiparīto' means 'its opposite'; 'upapadaṃ' is a word placed before, a prefix; 'the opposite of the sound o' is a designation for the sound 'u'. The word 'ca' sometimes has the meaning of preclusion. There is doubling. 'Uggate sūriye', 'uggacchati', 'uggahetvā'.

Atippakho tāva, parasataṃ, parasahassaṃ itīdha –

In 'Atippakho tāva', 'parasataṃ', 'parasahassaṃ'—in these cases—

“Āgamo”ti vattate.

The rule concerning 'āgama' (augment) is carried forward.

47. Kvaci o byañjane.

47. Sometimes 'o' is the augment before a consonant.

Byañjane pare kvaci okārāgamo hotīti atippa parasaddehi okārāgamo “yavamada”iccādisutte casaddena atippato gakārāgamo ca.

When a consonant follows, the augment 'o' sometimes occurs; thus, for the words 'atippa' and 'para', there is the augment 'o'. And, by the word 'ca' in the rule beginning 'yavamada', for 'atippa' there is also the augment 'g'.

Atippago kho tāva, parosataṃ, parosahassaṃ, ettha “sarā sare lopa”nti pubbassaralopo.

'Atippago kho tāva', 'parosataṃ', 'parosahassaṃ'. Here, by the rule 'sarā sare lopa', there is elision of the preceding vowel.

Manamayaṃ, ayamayaṃ itīdha “manogaṇādīna”nti vattate.

In the case of 'Manamayaṃ' and 'ayamayaṃ', the rule concerning 'the mano group and so on' is carried forward.

48. Etesamo lope.

48. Of these, 'o' is substituted upon elision.

Etesaṃ manogaṇādīnamanto ottamāpajjate vibhattilope kate.

Of these, namely the `manas` group and so forth, the final letter becomes 'o' when the case ending is elided.

Manomayaṃ, ayomayaṃ, evaṃ manoseṭṭhā, ayopatto, tapodhano, tamonudo, siroruho, tejokasiṇaṃ, rajojallaṃ, ahorattaṃ, rahogato.

Examples are: `manomayaṃ`, `ayomayaṃ`; similarly, `manoseṭṭhā`, `ayopatto`, `tapodhano`, `tamonudo`, `siroruho`, `tejokasiṇaṃ`, `rajojallaṃ`, `ahorattaṃ`, `rahogato`.

Ādisaddena āpodhātu, vāyodhātu.

By the word 'ādi' (etc.), `āpodhātu` (water element) and `vāyodhātu` (wind element) are included.

Sīhagatiyā vādhikārato idha na bhavati, manamattena manacchaṭṭhānaṃ, ayakapallaṃ, tamavinodano, manaāyatanaṃ.

Here, by the principle of the lion's gait or by the governing rule, it does not occur in: `manamattena`, `manacchaṭṭhānaṃ`, `ayakapallaṃ`, `tamavinodano`, `manaāyatanaṃ`.

Iti byañjanasandhividhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

Thus, the exposition of the rules for consonant sandhi is completed.

Niggahītasandhividhāna

Rules for Niggahīta Sandhi

Atha [M 0.0035] niggahītasandhi vuccate.

Now, the euphonic combination of the niggahīta is explained.

Taṇhaṃ karo, raṇaṃ jaho, saṃ ṭhito, jutiṃ dharo, saṃ mato itīdha “niggahīta”nti adhikāro, “byañjane”ti vattate.

`Taṇhaṃ karo`, `raṇaṃ jaho`, `saṃ ṭhito`, `jutiṃ dharo`, `saṃ mato`—thus here, the topic is 'niggahīta', and 'byañjane' is understood.

49. Vaggantaṃ vā vagge.

49. Optionally, the class-final consonant before a class consonant.

Vaggabhūte byañjane pare niggahītaṃ kho vaggantaṃ vā pappotīti nimittānusvarānaṃ ṭhānāsannavasena tabbaggapañcamo hoti. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Tena “taṇhaṅkaro, raṇañjaho, saṇṭhito, jutindharo, sammato”tiādīsu niccaṃ.

When a class consonant follows, the niggahīta optionally becomes the class-final consonant; that is, it becomes the fifth letter of that class due to the proximity of their places of articulation. Here, the word 'vā' signifies a fixed option. Therefore, in examples such as 'taṇhaṅkaro', 'raṇañjaho', 'saṇṭhito', 'jutindharo', and 'sammato', it is always so.

Taṅkaroti taṃ karoti, taṅkhaṇaṃ taṃkhaṇaṃ, saṅgaho saṃgaho, taṅghataṃ taṃ ghataṃ. Dhammañcare dhammaṃ care, tañchannaṃ taṃ channaṃ, tañjātaṃ taṃ jātaṃ, taññāṇaṃ taṃ ñāṇaṃ. Taṇṭhānaṃ taṃ ṭhānaṃ, taṇḍahati bhaṃ ḍahati. Tantanoti taṃ tanoti, tanthiraṃ taṃ thiraṃ, tandānaṃ taṃ dānaṃ, tandhanaṃ taṃ dhanaṃ, tanniccutaṃ taṃ niccutaṃ. Tampatto taṃ patto, tamphalaṃ taṃ phalaṃ, tesambodho tesaṃ bodho, sambhūto saṃbhūto, tammittaṃ taṃ mittaṃ. Kiṅkato kiṃ kato, dātuṅgato dātuṃ gatoti evamādīsu vikappena.

Examples are: `taṅkaroti` (`taṃ karoti`), `taṅkhaṇaṃ` (`taṃ khaṇaṃ`), `saṅgaho` (`saṃgaho`), `taṅghataṃ` (`taṃ ghataṃ`); `dhammañcare` (`dhammaṃ care`), `tañchannaṃ` (`taṃ channaṃ`), `tañjātaṃ` (`taṃ jātaṃ`), `taññāṇaṃ` (`taṃ ñāṇaṃ`); `taṇṭhānaṃ` (`taṃ ṭhānaṃ`), `taṇḍahati` (`taṃ ḍahati`); `tantanoti` (`taṃ tanoti`), `tanthiraṃ` (`taṃ thiraṃ`), `tandānaṃ` (`taṃ dānaṃ`), `tandhanaṃ` (`taṃ dhanaṃ`), `tanniccutaṃ` (`taṃ niccutaṃ`); `tampatto` (`taṃ patto`), `tamphalaṃ` (`taṃ phalaṃ`), `tesambodho` (`tesaṃ bodho`), `sambhūto` (`saṃbhūto`), `tammittaṃ` (`taṃ mittaṃ`); `kiṅkato` (`kiṃ kato`), `dātuṅgato` (`dātuṃ gato`)—thus, in such cases, it is optional.

Idha na bhavati, na taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu, saraṇaṃ gacchāmi.

Here it does not occur, as in 'na taṃ kammaṃ kataṃ sādhu' (that action was not well done) and 'saraṇaṃ gacchāmi' (I go for refuge).

Sati copari vāggahaṇe vijjhantare vā idha vāggahaṇakaraṇamatthantaraviññāpanatthaṃ, tena niggahītassa saṃupasaggapumantassa le lakāro. Yathā – paṭisaṃlīno paṭisallīno, evaṃ paṭisallāṇo, sallakkhaṇā, sallekho, sallāpo, puṃliṅgaṃ pulliṅgaṃ.

Even though 'vā' (or) is mentioned above or in an intervening rule, its inclusion here is to indicate a different meaning. Therefore, a niggahīta, when followed by 'l' and forming part of the prefix 'saṃ' or the word 'puṃ' (masculine), becomes 'l'. For example: `paṭisaṃlīno` becomes `paṭisallīno`; similarly, `paṭisallāṇo`, `sallakkhaṇā`, `sallekho`, `sallāpo`, `puṃliṅgaṃ` becomes `pulliṅgaṃ`.

Paccattaṃ eva, taṃ eva, tañhi tassa, evañhi vo itīdha “vā”ti adhikāro.

In examples such as `paccattaṃ eva`, `taṃ eva`, `tañhi tassa`, `evaṃ hi vo`, here the word 'vā' (or) is the governing rule.

50. Ehe [M 0.0036] ñaṃ.

50. Before 'e' and 'h', it becomes 'ñ'.

Ekārahakāre pare niggahītaṃ kho ñakāraṃ pappoti vā, ekāre ñādesassa dvibhāvo.

When 'e' or 'h' follows, the niggahīta optionally becomes 'ñ'. When 'e' follows, the substituted 'ñ' is doubled.

Paccattaññevapaccattaṃ eva, taññeva taṃ eva, tañhi tassa tañhi tassa, evañhi vo evañhi vo.

`Paccattaññeva` (`paccattaṃ eva`), `taññeva` (`taṃ eva`), `tañhi tassa` (`taṃ hi tassa`), `evañhi vo` (`evaṃ hi vo`).

Vavatthitavibhāsattā vāsaddassa evahinipātato aññattha na hoti, yathā – evametaṃ, evaṃ hoti.

Due to the fixed optionality of the word 'vā', this does not occur elsewhere than before the particles 'eva' or 'hi'. For example: `evametaṃ`, `evaṃ hoti`.

Saṃyogo, saṃyojanaṃ, saṃyato, saṃyācikāya, yaṃ yadeva, ānantarikaṃ yamāhu itīdha “ña”miti vattate.

In `saṃyogo`, `saṃyojanaṃ`, `saṃyato`, `saṃyācikāya`, `yaṃ yadeva`, `ānantarikaṃ yamāhu`—thus here, 'ña' is understood.

51. Sa ye ca.

51. And with 'y'.

Niggahītaṃ kho yakāre pare saha yakārena ñakāraṃ pappoti vā, ñādesassa dvittaṃ.

When 'y' follows, the niggahīta optionally becomes 'ñ' along with 'y', and the substituted 'ñ' is doubled.

Saññogo saṃyogo, saññojanaṃ saṃyojanaṃ, saññato saṃyato, saññācikāya saṃyācikāya, yaññadeva yaṃ yadeva, ānantarikaññamāhu ānantarikaṃ yamāhu.

`Saññogo` (`saṃyogo`), `saññojanaṃ` (`saṃyojanaṃ`), `saññato` (`saṃyato`), `saññācikāya` (`saṃyācikāya`), `yaññadeva` (`yaṃ yadeva`), `ānantarikaññamāhu` (`ānantarikaṃ yamāhu`).

Vāsaddassa vavatthitavibhāsattāva saṃpadantato ca sabbanāmayakāraparato ca niggahītā aññattha na hoti. Yathā – etaṃ yojanaṃ, taṃ yānaṃ, saraṇaṃ yanti.

Due to the fixed optionality of the word 'vā', this change applies only to the niggahīta of the prefix 'saṃ' or of a pronoun followed by 'y', and not elsewhere. For example: `etaṃ yojanaṃ`, `taṃ yānaṃ`, `saraṇaṃ yanti`.

Ettha ca “saha ye cā”ti vattabbe “sa ye cā”ti vacanato suttantesu sukhuccāraṇatthamakkharalopopīti daṭṭhabbaṃ, tena paṭisaṅkhāya yoniso paṭisaṅkhā yoniso, sayaṃ abhiññāya sacchikatvā sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā, pariyesanāya pariyesanātiādi sijjhati.

And here, it should be understood that even though 'saha ye ca' should be said, the expression 'sa ye ca' in the suttas indicates that letter elision occurs for ease of pronunciation. Therefore, forms like `paṭisaṅkhāya yoniso` (`paṭisaṅkhā yoniso`), `sayaṃ abhiññāya sacchikatvā` (`sayaṃ abhiññā sacchikatvā`), and `pariyesanāya` (`pariyesanā`), and so on, are established.

Taṃ [M 0.0037] ahaṃ brūmi, yaṃ āhu, dhanaṃ eva, kiṃ etaṃ, nindituṃ arahati, yaṃ aniccaṃ, taṃ anattā, etaṃ avoca, etaṃ eva iccatra –

In `taṃ ahaṃ brūmi`, `yaṃ āhu`, `dhanaṃ eva`, `kiṃ etaṃ`, `nindituṃ arahati`, `yaṃ aniccaṃ`, `taṃ anattā`, `etaṃ avoca`, `etaṃ eva`—

52. Madā sare.

52. Before a vowel, 'm' and 'd' are the substitutes.

Niggahītassa kho sare pare makāradakārādesā honti vā. Ettha ca vāsaddādhikārassa vavatthitavibhāsattā dakāro yatetasaddato parasseva.

When a vowel follows a niggahīta, the substitutions of 'm' or 'd' optionally occur. And here, due to the fixed optionality of the governing word 'vā', the 'd' substitution occurs only after the words 'ya' or 'eta'.

Tamahaṃ brūmi, yamāhu, dhanameva, kimetaṃ, ninditumarahati, yadaniccaṃ, tadanattā, etadavoca, etadeva.

`Tamahaṃ brūmi`, `yamāhu`, `dhanameva`, `kimetaṃ`, `ninditumarahati`, `yadaniccaṃ`, `tadanattā`, `etadavoca`, `etadeva`.

Vāti kiṃ? Taṃ ahaṃ, etaṃ eva, akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ.

What is 'vā' (for)? `Taṃ ahaṃ`, `etaṃ eva`, `akkocchi maṃ avadhi maṃ`.

Ettha ca madāti yogavibhāgena byañjanepi vā makāro. Tena “buddhama saraṇama gacchāmī”tiādi sijjhati.

And here, by the division of the rule 'ma-dā', the letter 'm' optionally occurs even before a consonant. Therefore, expressions such as 'buddhama saraṇama gacchāmi' are established.

Tāsaṃ ahaṃ santike, vidūnaṃ aggaṃ, tassa adāsiṃ ahaṃ itīdha “sare”ti vattate.

In 'tāsaṃ ahaṃ santike', 'vidūnaṃ aggaṃ', 'tassa adāsiṃ ahaṃ'—thus here, 'sare' (before a vowel) is understood to continue.

53. Kvaci lopaṃ.

53. Sometimes, elision.

Niggahītaṃ kho sare pare lopaṃ pappoti kvaci chandānurakkhaṇe sukhuccāraṇaṭṭhāne. Pubbassaralopo, parassa asaṃyogantassa dīgho.

The niggahīta, when a vowel follows, sometimes undergoes elision for the preservation of meter or for ease of pronunciation. There is elision of the preceding vowel, and lengthening of the following vowel that is not followed by a conjunct consonant.

Tāsāhaṃ santike, vidūnaggaṃ, tassa adāsāhaṃ, tathāgatāhaṃ, evāhaṃ, kyāhaṃ.

'Tāsāhaṃ santike', 'vidūnaggaṃ', 'tassa adāsāhaṃ', 'tathāgatāhaṃ', 'evāhaṃ', 'kyāhaṃ'.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Evamassa, kimahaṃ.

Why 'sometimes'? 'Evamassa', 'kimahaṃ'.

Ariyasaccānaṃ dassanaṃ, etaṃ buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ, saṃratto, saṃrāgo, saṃrambho, avisaṃhāro, ciraṃ pavāsiṃ, gantuṃ kāmo, gantuṃ mano itīdha “kvaci lopa”nti vattate.

In 'ariyasaccānaṃ dassanaṃ', 'etaṃ buddhānaṃ sāsanaṃ', 'saṃratto', 'saṃrāgo', 'saṃrambho', 'avisaṃhāro', 'ciraṃ pavāsiṃ', 'gantuṃ kāmo', 'gantuṃ mano'—thus here, 'kvaci lopaṃ' (sometimes elision) is understood to continue.

54. Byañjane [M 0.0038] ca.

54. And before a consonant.

Niggahītaṃ kho byañjane ca pare lopaṃ pappoti kvaci chandānurakkhaṇādimhi. Rakārahakāresu upasaggantassa dīgho.

The niggahīta, when a consonant follows, also sometimes undergoes elision for the preservation of meter and so forth. Before the letters 'r' and 'h', the final vowel of a prefix is lengthened.

Ariyasaccāna dassanaṃ, etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ, sāratto, sārāgo, sārambho, avisāhāro, cirappavāsiṃ, dvittaṃ, gantukāmo, gantumano.

'Ariyasaccāna dassanaṃ', 'etaṃ buddhāna sāsanaṃ', 'sāratto', 'sārāgo', 'sārambho', 'avisāhāro', 'cirappavāsiṃ', 'dvittaṃ', 'gantukāmo', 'gantumano'.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ.

Why 'sometimes'? 'Etaṃ maṅgalamuttamaṃ'.

Kataṃ iti, kiṃ iti, abhinanduṃ iti, uttattaṃ iva, cakkaṃ iva, kaliṃ idāni, kiṃ idāni, tvaṃ asi, idaṃ api, uttariṃ api, dātuṃ api, sadisaṃ eva itīdha “niggahītamhā, lopa”nti ca vattate.

In 'kataṃ iti', 'kiṃ iti', 'abhinanduṃ iti', 'uttattaṃ iva', 'cakkaṃ iva', 'kaliṃ idāni', 'kiṃ idāni', 'tvaṃ asi', 'idaṃ api', 'uttariṃ api', 'dātuṃ api', 'sadisaṃ eva'—thus here, 'niggahītamhā' (after the niggahīta) and 'lopaṃ' (elision) are understood to continue.

55. Paro vā saro.

55. Or the following vowel.

Niggahītamhā paro saro lopaṃ pappoti vā. Niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ.

After a niggahīta, a following vowel optionally undergoes elision. The niggahīta becomes a class-nasal.

Katanti, kinti, abhinandunti, uttattaṃva, cakkaṃva, kalindāni, kindāni, tvaṃsi, idampi, uttarimpi, dātumpi, sadisaṃva.

'Katanti', 'kinti', 'abhinandunti', 'uttattaṃva', 'cakkaṃva', 'kalindāni', 'kindāni', 'tvaṃsi', 'idampi', 'uttarimpi', 'dātumpi', 'sadisaṃva'.

Vāti kiṃ? Kataṃ iti, kimiti, dātumapi, sāmaṃ eva.

Why 'optionally'? 'Kataṃ iti', 'kimiti', 'dātumapi', 'sāmaṃ eva'.

Ayampi vāsaddassa vavatthitavibhāsattā itīvīdānisīpevādito aññattha na hoti. Yathā – ahaṃ ettha, etaṃ ahosi.

This also, due to the restricted optionality of the word 'vā', does not occur elsewhere than before 'iti', 'iva', 'idāni', 'si', 'eva', and so forth. For example: 'ahaṃ ettha', 'etaṃ ahosi'.

Evaṃ assa te āsavā, pupphaṃ assā uppajjati itīdha sare pare lutte vipariṇāmena “parasmiṃ, sare, lutte”ti ca vattate.

In 'evaṃ assa te āsavā' and 'pupphaṃ assā uppajjati'—thus here, when a following vowel is elided by transformation, 'parasmiṃ' (when the following...), 'sare' (...vowel), and 'lutte' (...is elided) are understood to continue.

56. Byañjano [M 0.0039] ca visaññogo.

56. And a consonant is disjoined.

Niggahītamhā parasmiṃ sare lutte byañjano saññogo ce, visaññogova hotīti saṃyogekadesassa purimabyañjanassa lopo.

When a following vowel is elided after a niggahīta, if the consonant is conjunct, it becomes disjoined; that is, there is elision of the first consonant of the conjunct.

Dvinnaṃ byañjanānamekatra ṭhiti saññogo, idha pana saṃyujjatīti saññogo, purimo vaṇṇo, vigato saññogo assāti visaññogo, paro.

A conjunction is the standing of two consonants in one place. Here, however, the preceding letter is the conjunct, as it is conjoined. The following letter is the disjunct, as its conjunction has departed.

Evaṃ sa te āsavā, pupphaṃsā uppajjati.

'Evaṃ sa te āsavā', 'pupphaṃsā uppajjati'.

Lutteti kiṃ? Evamassa.

Why 'when elided'? 'Evamassa'.

Casaddena tiṇṇaṃ byañjanānaṃ sarūpasaṃyogopi visaññogo hoti. Yathā – agyāgāraṃ, vutyassa.

By the word 'ca', even the conjunction of three identical consonants becomes disjoined. For example: 'agyāgāraṃ', 'vutyassa'.

Cakkhu udapādi, ava siro, yāvacidha bhikkhave, aṇuthūlāni, ta sampayuttā ibhīdha “sare, āgamo, kvaci, byañjane”ti ca vattate.

In 'cakkhu udapādi', 'ava siro', 'yāvacidha bhikkhave', 'aṇuthūlāni', 'ta sampayuttā'—thus here, 'sare' (before a vowel), 'āgamo' (augment), 'kvaci' (sometimes), and 'byañjane' (before a consonant) are understood to continue.

57. Niggahitañca.

57. And the niggahīta.

Niggahītañca āgamo hoti sare vā byañjane vā kvaci sukhuccāraṇaṭṭhāne. Niggahītassa rassānugatattā rassatoyevāyaṃ.

The niggahīta is also inserted as an augment, optionally before a vowel or a consonant, sometimes for ease of pronunciation. Since the niggahīta follows a short vowel, this augment only occurs after a short vowel.

Cakkhuṃ udapādi, avaṃsiro, yāvañcidha bhikkhave, aṇuṃthūlāni, taṃsampayuttā, evaṃ taṅkhaṇe, taṃsabhāvo.

'Cakkhuṃ udapādi', 'avaṃsiro', 'yāvañcidha bhikkhave', 'aṇuṃthūlāni', 'taṃsampayuttā', 'evaṃ taṅkhaṇe', 'taṃsabhāvo'.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Na hi etehi, idha ceva.

Why 'sometimes'? 'Na hi etehi', 'idha ceva'.

Evaṃ vutte, taṃ sādhu, ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā, aggiṃva sanamaṃ itīdha lopādesakāriye sampatte yebhuyyena tadapavādatthamāha.

In 'evaṃ vutte', 'taṃ sādhu', 'ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā', 'aggiṃva sanamaṃ'—thus here, when the operations of elision and substitution are applicable, he spoke for the general purpose of precluding them.

58. Aṃ [M 0.0040] byañjane niggahītaṃ.

58. The niggahīta becomes 'aṃ' before a consonant.

Niggahītaṃ kho byañjane pare aṃiti hoti.

When a consonant follows, the niggahīta indeed becomes 'aṃ'.

Akāro uccāraṇattho, “saralopo”tiādinā pubbassaralopo vā.

The letter 'a' is for the purpose of pronunciation; or, by the rule 'saralopo' and so forth, there is optional elision of the preceding vowel.

Evaṃ vutte, taṃ sādhu, ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā, aggiṃva sandhamaṃ.

Evaṃ vutte, taṃ sādhu, ekaṃ samayaṃ bhagavā, aggiṃva sandhamaṃ.

Idha avuttavisesānampi vuttanayātidesatthamatidesamāha.

Here, he states an extension for the purpose of applying the stated method even to unspecified distinctions.

59. Anupadiṭṭhānaṃ vuttayogato.

59. Of the uninstructed, by the application of what has been stated.

Ye idha amhehi visesato na upadiṭṭhā upasagganipātādayo, tesaṃ vuttayogato vuttanayena sarasandhādīsu vuttanayānusārena rūpasiddhi veditabbā.

The formation of those prefixes, particles, and so forth, not specifically instructed by us here, should be understood by the application of what has been stated, following the stated method in vowel sandhi and so forth.

Tena “do dhassa cā”ti sutte casaddena pariyādīnaṃ rahanādivaṇṇassa vipariyayo yavādīhi, yathā – pariyudāhāsi payirudāhāsi, ariyassa ayirassa, bahvābādho bavhābādho, na abhineyya anabhineyya.

Therefore, in the rule ‘do dhassa ca,’ by the word ‘ca,’ there is a metathesis of letters such as ‘r’ and ‘h’ with letters such as ‘y’ and ‘v’ in words such as ‘pariya.’ For example: ‘pariyudāhāsi’ becomes ‘payirudāhāsi’; ‘ariyassa’ becomes ‘ayirassa’; ‘bahvābādho’ becomes ‘bavhābādho’; ‘na abhineyya’ becomes ‘anabhineyya’.

“Taṃ imināpi jānāthā”ti ettha “paro vā saro”ti sare lutte “tatrākāro”ti yogavibhāgena akāro niggahītassa dakāro, tadamināpi jānātha iccādi.

In the phrase ‘taṃ imināpi jānāthā,’ when the following vowel is elided by the rule ‘paro vā saro,’ then by splitting the rule ‘tatrākāro,’ the niggahīta is replaced by ‘da’, resulting in ‘tadamināpi jānātha,’ etc.

Iti niggahītasandhividhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

Thus ends the section on the rules of niggahīta sandhi.

Saññāvidhānaṃ sarasandhi sandhi,

Nisedhanaṃ byañjanasandhi sandhi;

Yo niggahītassa ca sandhikappe,

Sunicchayo sopi mayettha vutto.

The section on terminology, vowel sandhi, the section on prohibitions, and consonant sandhi; and that definite conclusion on the chapter of niggahīta sandhi, that too has been stated here by me.

Iti rūpasiddhiyaṃ sandhikaṇḍo

Thus, in the Rūpasiddhi, the Chapter on Sandhi.

Paṭhamo.

The First.

2. Nāmakaṇḍa

2. The Section on Nouns

Atha [M 0.0041] nāmikavibhatyāvatāro vuccate.

Now the introduction to nominal inflections is stated.

Atthābhimukhaṃ namanato, attani catthassa nāmanato nāmaṃ, dabbābhidhānaṃ.

A noun (nāma) is so called because it inclines towards a meaning and because it names a meaning in itself; it is the designation of a substance.

Taṃ pana duvidhaṃ anvattharuḷhīvasena, tividhaṃ pumitthinapuṃsakaliṅgavasena. Yathā – rukkho, mālā, dhanaṃ.

It is twofold, by way of etymological meaning and conventional usage; and threefold, by way of masculine, feminine, and neuter gender. For example: rukkho (tree), mālā (garland), dhanaṃ (wealth).

Catubbidhaṃ sāmaññaguṇakriyāyadicchāvasena, yathā – rukkho, nīlo, pācako, sirivaḍḍhotiādi.

It is fourfold, by way of common noun, quality, action, and proper name. For example: rukkho (tree), nīlo (blue), pācako (cook), Sirivaḍḍha, etc.

Aṭṭhavidhaṃ avaṇṇivaṇṇuvaṇṇokāraniggahītantapakatibhedena.

It is eightfold, by the distinction of stems ending in the a-vowel group, the i-vowel group, the u-vowel group, the letter o, and the niggahīta.

Pulliṅga

Masculine Gender

Tattha paṭhamaṃ akārantamhā pulliṅgā jātinimittā purisasaddā syādivibhattiyo parā yojīyante.

Therein, first, the inflections beginning with 'si' are applied after the masculine noun 'purisa,' which ends in 'a' and signifies a class.

60. Jinavacanayuttañhi.

60. Indeed, in accordance with the Victor's word.

Adhikāroyaṃ. Tattha pañca māre jitavāti jino, buddho. Jinassa vacanaṃ jinavacanaṃ, tassa jinavacanassa yuttaṃ jinavacanayuttaṃ, tepiṭakassa buddhavacanassa māgadhikāya sabhāvaniruttiyā yuttaṃ anurūpamevāti idaṃ adhikāratthaṃ veditabbaṃ.

This is a governing rule. Herein, 'Jina' (Victor) means the Buddha, because he has conquered the five Māras. The Victor's word is 'jinavacanaṃ.' 'Jinavacanayuttaṃ' means that which is in accordance with the Victor's word. The Tipiṭaka, the Buddha's word, is in accordance with the natural language of Māgadhī, being indeed suitable. This should be understood as the meaning of this governing rule.

Sā māgadhī mūlabhāsā, narā yāyādikappikā;

Brahmāno ca’ssutālāpā, sambuddhā cāpi bhāsare.

That Māgadhī is the root language, which primeval human beings spoke; which the Brahmās, who had not heard other speech, also uttered, and which the Perfectly Enlightened Ones also speak.

Adhikāro pana tividho sīhagatikamaṇḍūkagatikayathānupubbikavasena, ayaṃ pana sīhagatiko pubbāparavilokanato, yathānupubbikoyeva vā.

A governing rule, moreover, is threefold: by way of the lion's gait, the frog's leap, and serial order. This one, however, is of the lion's gait type, because it looks to what precedes and what follows; or it is simply of the serial order type.

Sakkatavisadisaṃ [M 0.0042] katvā jinavacanānurūpavasena pakatiṭṭhapanatthaṃ paribhāsamāha.

Having made it dissimilar to Sanskrit, for the purpose of establishing the base form in accordance with the Victor's word, he states a meta-rule:

61. Liṅgañca nipaccate.

61. And the stem is formed.

Liṅgaṃpāṭipadikaṃ, yathā yathā jinavacanayuttañhi liṅgaṃ, tathā tathā idha liṅgaṃ nipaccate ṭhapīyati. Casaddena dhātavo cāti jinavacanānurūpato “purisa”iti liṅge ṭhapite tato tassa dhātuppaccayavibhattivajjitassa atthavato saddassa “parasamaññā payoge”ti paribhāsato liṅgasaññāyaṃ –

The stem (liṅga) is the nominal base (pāṭipadika). Just as the stem is in accordance with the Victor's word, so here the stem is formed and established. By the word 'ca,' roots are also included. In accordance with the Victor's word, when the stem 'purisa' is established, then that meaningful word-form, devoid of root, suffix, and inflection, is termed a 'stem' by the meta-rule 'parasamaññā payoge'.

Ito paraṃ vibhattippaccayādividhāne sabbattha liṅgaggahaṇamanuvattate.

Henceforth, in the rules concerning inflections, suffixes, etc., the term 'stem' is carried forward throughout.

62. Tato ca vibhattiyo.

62. And after that, the inflections.

Tato jinavacanayuttehi liṅgehi parā vibhattiyo honti. Casaddaggahaṇena tavetunādipaccayantanipātatopi. Kammādivasena, ekattādivasena ca liṅgatthaṃ vibhajantīti vibhattiyo.

After those stems that are in accordance with the Victor's word, inflections occur. By the inclusion of the word 'ca,' they also occur after indeclinables ending in suffixes such as 'tave,' 'tuna,' etc. They are called 'inflections' (vibhattiyo) because they analyze the meaning of the stem by way of case-function, such as object, and by way of number, such as singularity.

Kā ca pana tā vibhattiyo? “Vibhattiyo”ti adhikāro.

And what, then, are those inflections? 'Inflections' is the governing rule.

63. Siyo, aṃyo, nāhi, sanaṃ, smāhi, sanaṃ, smiṃsu.

63. Si, yo; aṃ, yo; nā, hi; sa, naṃ; smā, hi; sa, naṃ; smiṃ, su.

Syādayo dvisatta vibhattiyo nāma honti. Tattha si, yo iti paṭhamā, aṃ, yo iti dutiyā, nā, hi iti tatiyā, sa, naṃ iti catutthī, smā, hi iti pañcamī, sa, naṃ iti chaṭṭhī, smiṃ, su iti sattamī.

The inflections beginning with 'si' are fourteen in number. Therein, 'si' and 'yo' are the first (nominative); 'aṃ' and 'yo' are the second (accusative); 'nā' and 'hi' are the third (instrumental); 'sa' and 'naṃ' are the fourth (dative); 'smā' and 'hi' are the fifth (ablative); 'sa' and 'naṃ' are the sixth (genitive); 'smiṃ' and 'su' are the seventh (locative).

Idaṃ [M 0.0043] pana saññādhikāraparibhāsāvidhisuttesu saññāsuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ, vuttañhi vuttiyaṃ “vibhattiiccanena kvattho, amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se”ti, itarathā purimasuttena ekayogo kattabboti. Ettha ca paṭhamādivohāro, ekavacanādivohāro ca anvatthavasena, parasamaññāvasena vā siddhoti veditabbo.

This, however, should be seen as a terminological rule (saññāsutta) among the rules of terminology, governance, meta-rules, and prescription. For it is said in the commentary: 'What is the purpose of the term 'vibhatti'? It is for an operation in a rule such as 'amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se'.' Otherwise, it would have to be formulated as a single rule with the preceding one. And here, the usage of 'first,' etc., and the usage of 'singular,' etc., should be understood as established either by their etymological meaning or by conventional terminology.

Ekassa vacanaṃ ekavacanaṃ, bahūnaṃ vacanaṃ bahuvacanaṃ, dvinnaṃ pūraṇī dutiyātiādi, itarathā purimasutte casaddena saññākaraṇe appakataniratthakavidhippasaṅgo siyā.

'Ekavacana' is the expression of one; 'bahuvacana' is the expression of many; 'dutiyā' (second) is that which completes two, and so on. Otherwise, if the terminology were established by the word 'ca' in the previous rule, there would be the unwanted consequence of a redundant and useless prescription.

“Jinavacanayuttañhi, liṅgañca nipaccate”ti ca vattate. Idha pana padanipphādanampi jinavacanassāvirodhenāti ñāpetuṃ paribhāsantaramāha.

The rules 'Jinavacanayuttañhi' and 'liṅgañca nipaccate' are also carried forward. Here, however, to show that the formation of words also proceeds without contradicting the Victor's word, another meta-rule is stated:

64. Tadanuparodhena.

64. Without contradicting that.

Yathā yathā tesaṃ jinavacanānaṃ uparodho na hoti, tathā tathā idha liṅgaṃ, casaddenākhyātañca nipaccate, nipphādīyatīti attho. Teneva idha ca ākhyāte ca dvivacanāggahaṇaṃ, sakkatavisadisato vibhattippaccayādividhānañca katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

The meaning is: in whatever way there is no contradiction to those words of the Victor, in that way the stem, and by the word 'ca' the verb also, is formed or derived. For that very reason, it should be seen that here and in the verbal system, the dual number is not included, and the rules for inflections, suffixes, etc., are made dissimilar to Sanskrit.
