Tattha avisesena sabbasyādivibhattippasaṅge “vatticchānupubbikā saddappavattī”ti vatticchāvasā –

Therein, when there is the potential for all inflections beginning with 'si' to apply without distinction, then by the power of the speaker's intention, based on the principle 'the application of words follows the speaker's intention,' it is said:

65. Liṅgatthe paṭhamā.

65. The first case is in the sense of the stem's meaning.

Liṅgatthābhidhānamatte paṭhamāvibhatti hotīti paṭhamā. Tatthāpi aniyamenekavacanabahuvacanappasaṅge “ekamhī vattabbe ekavacana”nti paribhāsato liṅgatthassekattavacanicchāyaṃ paṭhamekavacanaṃ si.

The first inflection occurs merely in the expression of the stem's meaning. Even there, when there is the potential for the singular or plural to apply without restriction, then by the meta-rule 'when one is to be expressed, the singular is used,' the first case singular inflection 'si' is used when there is a wish to express the singularity of the stem's meaning.

“Ato nenā”ti ito “ato”ti vattate, liṅgaggahaṇañca.

From the rule 'Ato nenā,' the word 'ato' is carried forward, as is the term 'liṅga' (stem).

66. So[M 0.0044].

66. So.

Si, oiti dvipadamidaṃ. Liṅgassa akārato parassa sivacanassa okāro hoti.

This is a two-word rule: 'si' and 'o.' For the inflection 'si' that comes after the 'a' of a stem, there is the substitution 'o'.

Suttesu hi paṭhamāniddiṭṭhassa kāriyino chaṭṭhīvipariṇāmena vivaraṇaṃ ādesāpekkhanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

For in the rules, it should be understood that the operand, which is stated in the first case, is explained by transforming it into the sixth case, as it relates to the substitute.

Ettha ca sīti vibhatti gayhate vibhattikāriyavidhippakaraṇato, “tato ca vibhattiyo”ti ito vibhattiggahaṇānuvattanato vā, evaṃ sabbattha syādīnaṃ kāriyavidhāne vibhattiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Here, 'si' is taken as the inflection, because this is the section on rules for operations on inflections, or because the term 'vibhatti' is carried forward from 'tato ca vibhattiyo.' Thus, it should be understood that everywhere in the rules for operations on 'si,' etc., it is the inflection itself that is meant.

“Vā paro asarūpā”ti paralope sampatte tadapavādena pubbalopamāha.

When the elision of the following vowel would be applicable by the rule 'Vā paro asarūpā,' he states the elision of the preceding vowel as an exception to that:

67. Saralopo’mādesappaccayādimhi saralope tu pakati.

67. Elision of a preceding vowel occurs when 'aṃ' or a substitute, suffix, etc., that begins with a vowel follows. But when a vowel has been elided, the following vowel remains in its natural state.

Pubbassarassa lopo hoti aṃvacane, ādesappaccayādibhūte ca sare pare, saralope kate tu parasarassa pakatibhāvo hoti. Ettha ca “saralope”ti punaggahaṇaṃ imināva katasaralopanimitteyeva parassa vikāre sampatte pakatibhāvatthaṃ. Parasarassa pakatibhāvavidhānasāmatthiyato amādesappaccayādibhūte sare paretipi siddhaṃ.

There is elision of the preceding vowel when the inflection 'aṃ' follows, or when a vowel that is a substitute, a suffix, etc., follows. But when the vowel elision has been done, the following vowel remains in its natural state. Here, the repetition of 'saralope' is to show that the following vowel remains in its natural state only when a modification would occur on account of the vowel elision performed by this very rule. By the force of the prescription that the following vowel remains in its natural state, it is established that this applies even when a vowel that is a substitute, a suffix, etc., follows.

Tyādivibhattiyo cettha, paccayattena gayhare;

Ādiggahaṇamākhyāta-kitakesvāgamatthidaṃ.

Herein, the verbal inflections beginning with 'ti' are taken as suffixes. The inclusion of 'ādi' (etc.) is for the purpose of augments in verbs and kṛt-suffixes.

Paccayasāhacariyā, cādeso pakatīparo;

Padantassaralopo na, tena’bbhāhādike pare.

By association with a suffix, a substitute is also taken as a suffix, but not a following base form. Therefore, the elision of a vowel at the end of a word does not occur when 'abbhāha,' etc., follows.

Tuggahaṇaṃ [M 0.0045] bhikkhunīādīsu saralopanivattanatthaṃ, “naye paraṃ yutte”ti paraṃ netabbaṃ. Puriso tiṭṭhati.

The inclusion of 'tu' in the rule is for preventing vowel elision in words like 'bhikkhunī.' What follows should be connected according to the maxim 'naye paraṃ yutte.' Example: Puriso tiṭṭhati (A man stands).

Puriso ca puriso cāti purisa purisaiti vattabbe –

When one wishes to say 'puriso ca puriso ca' (a man and a man), which becomes 'purisa purisa,' then:

68. Sarūpānamekasesvasakiṃ.

68. Of identical forms, when used more than once, a single one remains.

Sarūpānaṃ samānarūpānaṃ padabyañjanānaṃ majjhe ekova sissate, aññe lopamāpajjante asakinti ekaseso. Ettha ca “sarūpāna”nti vuttattāva siddhe asakimpayoge punāsakiṃgahaṇaṃ ekavibhattivisayānamevāsakimpayoge evāyanti dassanatthaṃ, na ca vicchāpayoge’tippasaṅgo. “Vaggā pañcapañcaso mantā”ti ettha “pañcapañcaso”ti niddeseneva vicchāpayogasiddhiyā ñāpitattā, atha vā sahavacanicchāya’maya’mekaseso.

Among identical forms—that is, words and consonants with the same form—only one remains, while the others are elided; this is 'ekaseso' (single remainder), which applies when a word is used more than once (asakiṃ). Here, since this is already established by the word 'sarūpānaṃ' when used more than once, the inclusion of 'asakiṃ' again is to show that this rule applies only to words with the same inflection when used more than once, and does not over-apply to distributive usage. This is known from the very instruction 'pañcapañcaso' in the phrase 'vaggā pañcapañcaso mantā' (hymns in groups of five each), which establishes the distributive usage. Alternatively, this 'ekaseso' is due to the desire for co-expression.

Yogavibhāgato cettha, ekasesvasakiṃ iti;

Virūpekaseso hoti, vā “pitūna”ntiādisu.

And here, by splitting the rule 'ekaseso asakiṃ,' there is optionally a single remainder even of dissimilar forms, as in 'pitūnaṃ,' etc.

Tattheva liṅgatthassa bahuttavacanicchāyaṃ “bahumhi vattabbe bahuvacana”nti paṭhamābahuvacanaṃ yo, purisa yo itīdha “ato, vā”ti ca vattate.

In that same context, when there is a wish to express the plurality of the stem's meaning, the first case plural inflection 'yo' is used, according to the rule 'when many are to be expressed, the plural is used.' In the state 'purisa yo,' the terms 'ato' and 'vā' are carried forward.

69. Sabbayonīnamāe.

69. For all 'yo' inflections, 'ā' and 'e'.

Akārantato liṅgamhā paresaṃ sabbesaṃ paṭhamāyonīnaṃ, dutiyāyonīnañca yayākkamaṃ ākārekārādesā honti vāti ākāro, sabbaggahaṇaṃ sabbādesatthaṃ, saralopādi purimasadisameva, purisā tiṭṭhanti.

After a stem ending in 'a,' for all 'yo' inflections of the first and second cases, the substitutes 'ā' and 'e' respectively occur optionally. The word 'sabba' (all) is for the purpose of a complete substitution. Vowel elision, etc., is the same as before. Example: purisā tiṭṭhanti (men stand).

Vā icceva rūpā rūpāni, aggayo, munayo.

Because of the word 'vā', the forms are: rūpā or rūpāni; aggayo; munayo.

Vāsaddoyaṃ vavatthitapibhāsattho, tena cettha –

This word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option. Therefore, in this context:

Niccameva [M 0.0046] ca pulliṅge, aniccañca napuṃsake;

Asantaṃ jhe katatte tu, vidhiṃ dīpeti vāsuti.

The word 'vā' indicates the rule: it is obligatory in the masculine and optional in the neuter; but it is not applied to the root 'as' when 'jhi' is made 'te'.

Tatthevālapanavacanicchāyaṃ “liṅgatthe paṭhamā”ti vattate.

In that same context, when there is a wish to express the vocative, the rule 'liṅgatthe paṭhamā' is carried forward.

70. Ālapane ca.

70. And in the vocative.

Abhimukhaṃ katvā lapanaṃ ālapanaṃ, sambodhanaṃ. Tasmiṃ ālapanatthādhike liṅgatthābhidhānamatte ca paṭhamāvibhatti hoti. Pure viya ekavacanādi.

Addressing, that is, making someone face one and speaking, is 'ālapana' or 'sambodhana.' The first inflection occurs when the meaning of the stem is expressed with the additional sense of the vocative. The singular and other numbers apply as before.

Purisa si iccatra –

In the case of 'purisa si':

71. Ālapane si gasañño.

71. In the vocative, 'si' has the designation 'ga'.

Ālapanatthe vihito si gasañño hotīti gasaññāyaṃ “bho ge tū”ti ito “ge”ti vattate.

The 'si' ending prescribed for the vocative case receives the designation 'ga'. Thus, when it has the designation 'ga', 'ge' is carried forward from the rule 'bho ge tū'.

72. Akārapitādyantānamā.

72. Of stems ending in 'a' and of stems such as 'pitu', the final vowel becomes 'ā'.

Liṅgassa sambandhī akāro ca pitusatthuiccevamādīnamanto ca ākārattamāpajjate ge pare.

The 'a' belonging to the stem, and the final vowel of stems such as 'pitu' and 'satthu', become 'ā' when 'ge' follows.

“Ge, rassa”miti ca vattate.

And 'ge' and 'rassaṃ' (short) are carried forward.

73. Ākāro vā.

73. Of 'ā', optionally.

Liṅgassa sambandhī ākāro rassamāpajjate ge pare vikappena, adūraṭṭhassālapanevāyaṃ.

The 'ā' belonging to the stem optionally becomes short when 'ge' follows. This applies only in the vocative of that which is not distant.

74. Sesato lopaṃ gasipi.

74. After the remainder, there is elision of 'ga' and 'si'.

“Siṃ, so, syā ca, sakhato gasse vā, ghate cā”ti evamādīhi niddiṭṭhehi añño seso nāma, tato sesato liṅgamhā gasiiccete lopamāpajjante. Apiggahaṇaṃ [M 0.0047] dutiyatthasampiṇḍanatthaṃ, ettha ca satipi siggahaṇe vaiti vacanameva ñāpakamaññatthāpi siggahaṇe ālapanāggahaṇassa. Keci ālapanābhibyattiyā bhavantasaddaṃ vā hesaddaṃ vā payujjante. Bho purisa tiṭṭha, he purisā vā.

The 'remainder' is that which is other than those specified by rules such as 'siṃ, so, syā ca', 'sakhato gasse vā', and 'ghate cā'. After that remainder stem, 'ga' and 'si' undergo elision. The inclusion of 'api' is for the purpose of combining a second meaning. And here, even with the mention of 'si', the word 'vā' itself is an indicator that the vocative is to be understood even in other places where 'si' is mentioned. Some, for expressing the vocative, use the word 'bhavanta' or 'he'. For example: 'Bho purisa tiṭṭha' (O man, stand!), or 'he purisā' (O men!).

Bahuvacane na viseso, bhavanto purisā tiṭṭhatha.

In the plural, there is no special rule. For example: 'Bhavanto purisā tiṭṭhatha' (O venerable men, stand!).

Tattheva kammatthavacanicchāyaṃ “va,”ti vattate.

In that very context, with the intention of expressing the meaning of the object, 'va' is carried forward.

75. Yaṃ karoti taṃ kammaṃ.

75. What one does, that is the object.

Yaṃ vā karoti, yaṃ vā vikaroti, yaṃ vā pāpuṇāti, taṃ kārakaṃ kriyānimittaṃ kammasaññaṃ hoti.

What one does, or what one modifies, or what one obtains—that factor, the basis for the action, is designated as the object (kamma).

76. Kammatthe dutiyā.

76. In the sense of the object, the second inflection is used.

Kammatthe dutiyāvibhatti hoti. Pure viya dutiyekavacanaṃ aṃ, “saralopo”tiādinā sare lutte “dīgha”nti dīghe sampatte pakatibhāvo ca, purisaṃ passa.

The second case ending is used in the sense of the object. As before, the second case singular is 'aṃ'. When a vowel is elided by a rule such as 'saralopo', and lengthening by the rule 'dīghaṃ' would be obtained, there is instead a retention of the natural form. For example: 'purisaṃ passa' (see the man).

Bahuvacane “sabbayonīnamāe”ti yovacanassekāro, purise passa.

In the plural, by the rule 'sabbayonīnamāe', the 'yo' ending becomes 'e'. For example: 'purise passa' (see the men).

Tattheva kattuvacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the wish to express the agent (kattu)—

77. Yo karoti sa kattā.

77. The one who acts is the agent.

Yo attappadhāno kriyaṃ karoti, so kattusañño hoti.

One who, being independent, performs an action, is designated as the agent.

“Tatiyā”ti vattate.

'Tatiyā' (the third case) is carried forward.

78. Kattari ca.

78. And in the agent.

Kattari ca kārake tatiyāvibhatti hotīti tatiyekavacanaṃ nā.

The third case ending occurs in the agent as a grammatical factor. Thus, the third case singular is 'nā'.

79. Ato [M 0.0048] nena.

79. After 'a', 'nā' becomes 'ena'.

Enāti avibhattikaniddeso. Akārantato liṅgamhā parassa nāvacanassa enādeso hoti, saralopādi, purisena kataṃ.

'Ena' is a designation without a case ending. After a stem ending in 'a', the case ending 'nā' becomes 'ena', with vowel elision and other operations. For example: 'purisena kataṃ' (done by the man).

Bahuvacanamhi –

In the plural—

80. Suhisvakāro e.

80. When 'su' and 'hi' follow, the 'a' becomes 'e'.

Su, hiiccetesu vibhattirūpesu paresu liṅgassa sambandhī akāro ettamāpajjate.

When the case forms 'su' and 'hi' follow, the 'a' connected with the stem becomes 'e'.

81. Smāhismiṃnaṃ mhābhimhi vā.

81. 'Smā', 'hi', and 'smiṃ' optionally become 'mhā', 'bhi', and 'mhi' respectively.

Sabbato liṅgamhā smā hi smiṃiccetesaṃ yathākkamaṃ mhā, bhi, mhiiccete ādesā honti vā, purisehi, purisebhi kataṃ.

After any stem, 'smā', 'hi', and 'smiṃ' are optionally replaced, in order, by 'mhā', 'bhi', and 'mhi'. For example: 'purisehi' (by the men), 'purisebhi kataṃ' (done by the men).

Tattheva karaṇavacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the desire to express the instrumental (karaṇa)—

82. Yena vā kayirate taṃ karaṇaṃ.

82. That by which something is done is the instrument.

Yena vā kayirate, yena vā passati, yena vā suṇāti, taṃ kārakaṃ karaṇasaññaṃ hoti.

That by which something is done, that by which one sees, or that by which one hears—that grammatical factor is designated as the instrument.

83. Karaṇe tatiyā.

83. The third case is used for the instrument.

Karaṇakārake tatiyāvibhatti hoti, sesaṃ kattusamaṃ, āviṭṭhena purisena so puññaṃ karoti, purisehi, purisebhi.

The third case ending occurs for the instrumental grammatical factor. The rest is the same as for the agent. For example: 'āviṭṭhena purisena so puññaṃ karoti' (by the possessed man, he performs merit), 'purisehi' (by the men), 'purisebhi' (by the men).

Tattheva sampadānavacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the desire to express the dative (sampadāna)—

84. Yassa [M 0.0049] dātukāmo rocate dhārayate vā taṃ sampadānaṃ.

84. To whom one wishes to give, to whom something is pleasing, or to whom one owes something—that is the dative.

Yassa vā dātukāmo, yassa vā rocate, yassa vā dhārayate, taṃ kārakaṃ sampadānasaññaṃ hoti.

To whom one wishes to give, to whom something is pleasing, or to whom one owes something—that grammatical factor is designated as the dative.

85. Sampadāne catutthī.

85. The fourth case is used for the dative.

Sampadānakārake catutthīvibhatti hotīti catutthiyā ekavacanaṃ sa.

The fourth case ending occurs for the dative grammatical factor. Thus, the singular of the fourth case is 'sa'.

86. Sāgamo se.

86. The augment 'sa' is prefixed when 'se' follows.

Sabbato liṅgamhā sakārāgamo hoti se vibhattimhi pare. Purisassa dhanaṃ dadāti.

After any stem, the augment 'sa' occurs when the case ending 'se' follows. For example: 'Purisassa dhanaṃ dadāti' (He gives wealth to the man).

Bahuvacanamhi “dīgha”nti vattate.

In the plural, 'dīgha' (lengthening) is carried forward.

87. Sunaṃhisu ca.

87. And when 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi' follow.

Su naṃ hiiccetesu paresu liṅgassa antabhūtā sabbe rassasarā dīghamāpajjante, caggahaṇamikārukārānaṃ kvaci nivattanatthaṃ. Purisānaṃ.

When 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi' follow, all short vowels at the end of the stem become long. The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of occasionally preventing the lengthening of the vowels 'i' and 'u'. For example: 'Purisānaṃ' (of the men).

Tatthevāpādānavacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the desire to express the ablative (apādāna)—

88. Yasmā dapeti bhayamādatte vā tadapādānaṃ.

88. From whom one causes to give, or from whom one takes fear—that is the ablative.

Yasmā vā avadhibhūtā apeti, yasmā vā bhayaṃ, yasmā vā ādatte, taṃ kārakaṃ apādānasaññaṃ hoti.

From which, being a fixed point, something departs; from which there is fear; or from which one takes—that grammatical factor is designated as the ablative.

89. Apādāne [M 0.0050] pañcamī.

89. The fifth case is used for the ablative.

Apādānakārake pañcamīvibhatti hotīti pañcamiyā ekavacanaṃ smā.

The fifth case ending occurs for the ablative grammatical factor. Thus, the singular of the fifth case is 'smā'.

“Ato, sabbesaṃ, ā e”ti ca vattate.

And 'Ato' (from an 'a'-ending stem), 'sabbesaṃ' (of all), and 'ā e' (become 'ā' or 'e') are carried forward.

90. Smāsmiṃna vā.

90. 'Smā' and 'smiṃ' optionally.

Akārantato liṅgamhā sabbesaṃ smā smiṃiccetesaṃ yathākkamaṃ ākārekārādesā honti vā, aññattha mhādeso. Purisā apeti, purisamhā, purisasmā.

After a stem ending in 'a', for 'smā' and 'smiṃ', the substitutions 'ā' and 'e' occur respectively, optionally; otherwise, the substitution 'mhā' occurs. For example: 'Purisā apeti' (He departs from the man), 'purisamhā' (from the man), 'purisasmā' (from the man).

Bahuvacane sabbattha tatiyāsamaṃ, hissa bhiādeso hoti. Purisehi, purisebhi apeti.

In the plural, it is everywhere the same as the third case; for 'hi', the substitution 'bhi' occurs. For example: 'Purisehi apeti' (He departs from the men), 'purisebhi apeti' (He departs from the men).

Tattheva sāmivacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the desire to express the possessor (sāmi)—

91. Yassa vā pariggaho taṃ sāmi.

91. Whose possession it is, that is the possessor.

Yassa vā pariggaho, taṃ sāmisaññaṃ hoti.

Whose possession it is, that is designated as the possessor.

92. Sāmismiṃ chaṭṭhī.

92. The sixth case (genitive) is used for the possessor.

Sāmismiṃ chaṭṭhīvibhatti hoti. Ṭhapetvā āyādesaṃ sabbattha catutthīchaṭṭhīnaṃ samānaṃ rūpaṃ. Purisassa etaṃ dhanaṃ, purisānaṃ.

The sixth case ending occurs in the possessor. Except for the substitution 'āya', the forms of the fourth and sixth cases are the same everywhere. For example: 'Purisassa etaṃ dhanaṃ' (This wealth is of the man), 'purisānaṃ' (of the men).

Tattheva okāsavacanicchāyaṃ –

In that very context, with the desire to express the locative (okāsa)—

93. Yodhāro tamokāsaṃ.

93. That which is the basis (support), that is the locative.

Yo kattukammānaṃ kriyāya ādhāro, taṃ kārakaṃ okāsasaññaṃ hoti.

That which serves as the basis for the action of the agent and object—that grammatical factor is designated as the locative.

94. Okāse [M 0.0051] sattamī.

94. The seventh case (locative) is used for the locative.

Okāsakārake sattamīvibhatti hotīti sattamiyā ekavacanaṃ smiṃ, tassa “smāsmiṃnaṃ vā”ti ekāro, mhiādeso ca, purise patiṭṭhitaṃ, purisamhi, purisasmiṃ.

The seventh case ending occurs in the locative grammatical factor. Thus, the singular of the seventh case is 'smiṃ'. For that 'smiṃ', 'e' (ekāro) occurs by the rule 'smāsmiṃnaṃ vā', and also the substitution 'mhi'. For example: 'purise patiṭṭhitaṃ' (established in the man), 'purisamhi' (in the man), 'purisasmiṃ' (in the man).

Bahuvacane “suhisvakāro e”ti ekāro, purisesu.

In the plural, by the rule 'suhisvakāro e', the preceding 'a' becomes 'e'. For example: 'purisesu' (in the men).

Puriso, purisā, bho purisa bho purisā vā, bhavanto purisā, purisaṃ, purise, purisena, purisehi purisebhi, purisassa, purisānaṃ, purisā purisasmā purisamhā, purisehi purisebhi, purisassa, purisānaṃ, purise purisasmiṃ purisamhi, purisesu.

Puriso (Nom. sg.: a man), purisā (Nom. pl.: men), bho purisa (Voc. sg.: O man), bho purisā vā (Voc. pl.: O men), bhavanto purisā (Voc. pl.: venerable sirs, men), purisaṃ (Acc. sg.: a man), purise (Acc. pl.: men), purisena (Inst. sg.: by a man), purisehi purisebhi (Inst. pl.: by men), purisassa (Dat. sg.: to a man), purisānaṃ (Dat. pl.: to men), purisā purisasmā purisamhā (Abl. sg.: from a man), purisehi purisebhi (Abl. pl.: from men), purisassa (Gen. sg.: of a man), purisānaṃ (Gen. pl.: of men), purise purisasmiṃ purisamhi (Loc. sg.: in a man), purisesu (Loc. pl.: in men).

Tathā sugato, sugatā, bho sugata bho sugatā vā, bhavanto sugatā, sugataṃ, sugate, sugatena, sugatehi sugatebhi, sugatassa, sugatānaṃ, sugatā sugatasmā sugatamhā, sugatehi sugatebhi, sugatassa, sugatānaṃ, sugate sugatasmiṃ sugatamhi, sugatesu.

Likewise: sugato (Nom. sg.: the Well-Gone One), sugatā (Nom. pl.: Well-Gone Ones), bho sugata (Voc. sg.: O Well-Gone One), bho sugatā vā (Voc. pl.: O Well-Gone Ones), bhavanto sugatā (Voc. pl.: venerable Well-Gone Ones), sugataṃ (Acc. sg.: the Well-Gone One), sugate (Acc. pl.: Well-Gone Ones), sugatena (Inst. sg.: by the Well-Gone One), sugatehi sugatebhi (Inst. pl.: by the Well-Gone Ones), sugatassa (Dat. sg.: to the Well-Gone One), sugatānaṃ (Dat. pl.: to the Well-Gone Ones), sugatā sugatasmā sugatamhā (Abl. sg.: from the Well-Gone One), sugatehi sugatebhi (Abl. pl.: from the Well-Gone Ones), sugatassa (Gen. sg.: of the Well-Gone One), sugatānaṃ (Gen. pl.: of the Well-Gone Ones), sugate sugatasmiṃ sugatamhi (Loc. sg.: in the Well-Gone One), sugatesu (Loc. pl.: in the Well-Gone Ones).

Evaṃ surā’sura naro’raga nāga yakkhā,

Gandhabba kinnara manussa pisāca petā;

Mātaṅga jaṅgama turaṅga varāha sīhā,

Byaggha’ccha kacchapa taraccha miga’ssa soṇā.

Thus: gods, demons, men, serpents, nāgas, yakkhas, gandhabbas, kinnaras, humans, pisācas, ghosts; elephants, moving creatures, horses, boars, lions, tigers, bears, tortoises, hyenas, deer, horses, and dogs.

Āloka loka nilayā’nila cāga yogā, vāyāma gāma

Nigamā’gama dhamma kāmā;

Saṅgho’gha ghosa paṭighā’sava kodha lobhā,

Sārambha thambha mada māna pamāda makkhā.

Light, world, habitations, wind, relinquishment, yoga, effort, villages, market towns, tradition, Dhamma, desires; the Sangha, floods, sounds, repulsion, taints, anger, greed, rivalry, obstinacy, intoxication, conceit, negligence, and disparagement.

Punnāga [M 0.0052] pūga panasā’sana campaka’mbā,

Hintāla tāla bakula’jjuna kiṃsukā ca;

Mandāra kunda pucimanda karañja rukkhā,

Ñeyyā mayūra sakunaṇḍaja koñca haṃsā –

Punnāga trees, areca palms, jackfruit trees, asana trees, champak trees, mango trees, hintāla palms, palmyra palms, bakula trees, arjuna trees, and kiṃsuka trees; mandāra trees, jasmine, neem trees, karañja trees, and trees in general. To be known are: peacocks, birds, egg-born creatures, cranes, and swans—

Iccādayopi.

And so forth.

Manogaṇādissa tu nāsasmāsmiṃsu viseso. Aññattha purisasamaṃ.

But for the 'mano' group and so forth, there is a special rule regarding 'nā', 'smā', and 'smiṃ'. Elsewhere, it is like 'purisa'.

Mano, manā, he mana he manā vā, bhavanto manā, manaṃ, mane.

Mano (Nom. sg.: mind), manā (Nom. pl.: minds), he mana (Voc. sg.: O mind), he manā vā (Voc. pl.: O minds), bhavanto manā (Voc. pl.: venerable minds), manaṃ (Acc. sg.: the mind), mane (Acc. pl.: minds).

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' (optionally) is carried forward.

95. Manogaṇādito smiṃnānamiā.

95. After the 'mano' group and so forth, 'smiṃ' and 'nā' become 'i' and 'ā'.

Manopabhuti gaṇo manogaṇo, manogaṇādito smiṃ, nāiccetesaṃ yathākkamaṃ ikārākārādesā honti vā. Ādiggahaṇena bilapadāditopi.

The group beginning with 'mano' is the 'manogaṇa'. After the 'manogaṇa' and so forth, for 'smiṃ' and 'nā', the substitutions 'i' and 'ā' occur respectively, optionally. By the inclusion of 'ādi' (and so forth), this also applies to words beginning with 'bilapada' and so on.

“Manogaṇādito”ti vattate.

The phrase 'Manogaṇādito' (after the 'mano' group and so forth) is carried forward.

96. Sa sare vāgamo.

96. The augment 'sa' optionally occurs when a vowel follows.

Eteheva manogaṇādīhi sare pare sāgamo hoti vā. Manasā, manena.

After these very words of the 'mano' group and so forth, when a vowel follows, the 'sa' augment optionally occurs. For example: 'Manasā' (by the mind), 'manena' (by the mind).

Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, tena “mano manā manaṃ mane manaāyatana”ntiādīsu na hoti. “Mānasikaṃ, cetasika”ntiādīsu niccaṃ. Manehi, manebhi.

This word 'vā' (optionally) indicates a restricted option. Therefore, it does not apply in instances like 'mano, manā, manaṃ, mane, manāyatana', and so forth. It is always applied in instances like 'mānasikaṃ, cetasikaṃ', and so forth. For example: 'Manehi' (by the minds), 'manebhi' (by the minds).

“Manogaṇādito, vā”ti ca vattate.

And 'Manogaṇādito' (after the 'mano' group and so forth) and 'vā' (optionally) are carried forward.

97. Sassa [M 0.0053] co.

97. And 'sassa' becomes 'so'.

Manogaṇādito parassa sassa vibhattissa okāro hoti vā. Sāgamo.

After the 'mano' group and so forth, the case ending 'sa' optionally becomes 'o'. This occurs with the 'sa' augment.

Manaso manassa, manānaṃ, manā manasmā manamhā, manehi manebhi, manaso manassa, manānaṃ, manasi mane manasmiṃ manamhi, manesu.

Manaso (Dat. sg.: to the mind), manassa (Dat. sg.: to the mind), manānaṃ (Dat. pl.: to the minds), manā (Abl. sg.: from the mind), manasmā (Abl. sg.: from the mind), manamhā (Abl. sg.: from the mind), manehi (Abl. pl.: from the minds), manebhi (Abl. pl.: from the minds), manaso (Gen. sg.: of the mind), manassa (Gen. sg.: of the mind), manānaṃ (Gen. pl.: of the minds), manasi (Loc. sg.: in the mind), mane (Loc. sg.: in the mind), manasmiṃ (Loc. sg.: in the mind), manamhi (Loc. sg.: in the mind), manesu (Loc. pl.: in the minds).

Evaṃ vaco vayo tejo,

Tapo ceto tamo yaso;

Ayo payo siro chando,

Saro uro raho aho –

Likewise: vaco (speech), vayo (age), tejo (energy), tapo (austerity), ceto (mind), tamo (darkness), yaso (fame), ayo (iron), payo (milk), siro (head), chando (desire), saro (sound), uro (chest), raho (solitude), aho (day)—

Iccādi manogaṇo.

Thus is the 'mano' group, and so forth.

Guṇavantusaddassa bhedo. Guṇavantu si itīdha –

The declension of the word 'guṇavantu'. Here, in the case of 'guṇavantu' with 'si'—

“Savibhattissa, ntussā”ti ca adhikāro.

And 'savibhattissa' (of that with its ending) and 'ntussa' (of 'ntu') are governing rules.

98. Ā simhi.

98. 'Ā' occurs when 'si' follows.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa āādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi. Guṇavā.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, the substitution 'ā' occurs when the 'si' inflection follows. For example: 'Guṇavā'.

“Yomhi, paṭhame”sīhagatiyā “vā”ti ca vattate.

And 'Yomhi' (when 'yo' follows), 'paṭhame' (in the first case), and 'vā' (optionally) are carried forward by the 'lion's gait' method.

99. Ntussa nto.

99. 'Ntu' becomes 'nto'.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa ntoādeso hoti vā yomhi paṭhame, guṇavanto tiṭṭhanti.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, the substitution 'nto' optionally occurs when 'yo' of the first case follows. For example: 'Guṇavanto tiṭṭhanti' (The virtuous ones stand).

“Sunaṃhisu, atta”nti ca vattate.

And 'Sunaṃhisu' (in 'su', 'naṃ', 'hi') and 'attaṃ' (becomes 'a') are carried forward.

100. Ntussanto [M 0.0054] yosu ca.

100. And the final vowel of 'ntu' becomes 'a' when the endings 'yo' and 'su' follow.

Ntupaccayassa anto ukāro attamāpajjate sunaṃhi yoiccetesu, caggahaṇena aññesu aṃ nā smāsmiṃsu ca. Guṇavantā, chaṭṭhiyā siddhepi antādese puna antaggahaṇakaraṇato yonaṃ ikāro ca kvaci. Guṇavanti.

The final vowel 'u' of the 'ntu' suffix becomes 'a' before 'su', 'naṃ', 'hi', and 'yo'. By the inclusion of 'ca', this also applies to other endings such as 'aṃ', 'nā', 'smā', and 'smiṃ'. For example: 'Guṇavantā'. Although the substitution to 'anta' is already established for the genitive plural, by the repetition of 'anta' in the rule, the vowel 'i' also sometimes occurs for the endings 'yo' and 'naṃ'. For example: 'Guṇavanti'.

“A”miti vattate.

'Aṃ' is carried forward.

101. Avaṇṇā ca ge.

101. And the vowel 'a' occurs before 'ge'.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa aṃ avaṇṇaiccete ādesā honti ge pare.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, the substitutes 'aṃ' and 'avaṇṇa' (the vowel 'a') occur when 'ge' follows. For example: guṇava.

Bho guṇavaṃ bho guṇava bho guṇavā, bhavanto guṇavanto guṇavantā, guṇavantaṃ, guṇavante.

Bho guṇavaṃ, bho guṇava, bho guṇavā; bhavanto, guṇavanto, guṇavantā; guṇavantaṃ; guṇavante.

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' is carried forward.

102. Totitā sasmiṃnāsu.

102. 'To' and 'tā' are substituted before 'sasmiṃ' and 'nā'.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa toti tāādesā honti vā sasmiṃnāiccetesu yathāsaṅkhyaṃ. Guṇavatā guṇavantena, guṇavantehi guṇavantebhi.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, the substitutes 'to' and 'tā' occur optionally before 'sasmiṃ' and 'nā' respectively. The forms are: guṇavatā, guṇavantena; guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi.

103. Ntassa se vā.

103. 'Ntassa' is the optional substitute when 'se' follows.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa ntassaiccayamādeso hoti vā se vibhattimhi. Guṇavantassa guṇavato.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, this substitute 'ntassa' occurs optionally when the case ending 'se' follows. For example: Guṇavantassa, guṇavato.

104. Naṃmhi taṃ vā.

104. 'Taṃ' is the optional substitute when 'naṃ' follows.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa savibhattissa taṃādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Guṇavataṃ guṇavantānaṃ.

For the entire 'ntu' suffix with its inflection, the substitute 'taṃ' optionally occurs when the case ending 'naṃ' follows. The forms are: guṇavataṃ, guṇavantānaṃ.

“Amha [M 0.0055] tumha ntu”iccādinā smāvacanassa nābyapadeso.

By the rule beginning 'Amha tumha ntu', the ending 'smā' is not treated as 'nā'.

Guṇavatā guṇavantā guṇavantasmā guṇavantamhā, guṇavantehi guṇavantebhi, guṇavantassa guṇavato, guṇavataṃ guṇavantānaṃ, guṇavati guṇavante guṇavantasmiṃ guṇavantamhī, guṇavantesu.

Guṇavatā, guṇavantā, guṇavantasmā, guṇavantamhā; guṇavantehi, guṇavantebhi; guṇavantassa, guṇavato; guṇavataṃ, guṇavantānaṃ; guṇavati, guṇavante, guṇavantasmiṃ, guṇavantamhī; guṇavantesu.

Evaṃ gaṇavā kulavā balavā yasavā dhanavā sutavā bhagavā himavā phalavā sīlavā paññavā iccādayo.

Similarly, gaṇavā, kulavā, balavā, yasavā, dhanavā, sutavā, bhagavā, himavā, phalavā, sīlavā, paññavā, and so forth.

Himavantusaddato simhi kate –

From the word 'Himavantu', when 'si' is applied—

“Attaṃ, ntussa’nto”ti ca vattamāne –

And when 'attaṃ' and 'ntussa anto' (the end of 'ntu') are carried forward—

105. Simhī vā.

105. Optionally, when 'si' follows.

Ntupaccayassa anto attaṃ hoti vā simhi vibhattimhi. Himavanto, himavā, sesaṃ samaṃ.

The final part of the 'ntu' suffix becomes 'a' optionally when the case ending 'si' follows. For example: Himavanto, himavā. The rest is the same.

Puna vāggahaṇakaraṇaṃ himavantusaddato aññatra attanisedhanatthaṃ, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Tena guṇavantādīsu nātippasaṅgo.

Again, the inclusion of 'vā' is for the purpose of prohibiting the substitution of 'atta' in words other than 'himavantu'. This word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option. Therefore, there is no over-application to words such as 'guṇavantu'.

Evaṃ satimā dhitimā gatimā matimā mutimā muttimā jutimā sirimā hirimā thutimā ratimā yatimā sucimā kalimā balimā kasimā rucimā buddhimā cakkhumā bandhumā hetumā setumā ketumā rāhumā bhāṇumā khāṇumā vijjumā iccādayo.

Similarly, satimā, dhitimā, gatimā, matimā, mutimā, muttimā, jutimā, sirimā, hirimā, thutimā, ratimā, yatimā, sucimā, kalimā, balimā, kasimā, rucimā, buddhimā, cakkhumā, bandhumā, hetumā, setumā, ketumā, rāhumā, bhāṇumā, khāṇumā, vijjumā, and so forth.

Tattha satimantu bandhumantusaddānaṃ aṃsesu rūpabhedo. “Attaṃ, ntussā”ti ca vattate.

Therein, for the words 'satimantu' and 'bandhumantu', there is a difference of form in certain cases. And 'attaṃ, ntussa' is carried forward.

106. Sabbassa vā aṃsesu.

106. Of all, optionally in certain cases.

Sabbasseva ntupaccayassa attaṃ hoti vā aṃsaiccetesu. Idhāpi vāsaddassa vavatthitavibhāsattā nātippasaṅgo[M 0.0056]. Satimaṃ satimantaṃ, bandhumaṃ bandhumantaṃ, satimassa satimato satimantassa, bandhumassa bandhumato bandhumantassa, sesaṃ samaṃ.

Of the entire 'ntu' suffix, there is the substitution of 'attaṃ' optionally in these cases. Here too, because the word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option, there is no over-application. Satimaṃ, satimantaṃ; bandhumaṃ, bandhumantaṃ; satimassa, satimato, satimantassa; bandhumassa, bandhumato, bandhumantassa; the rest is the same.

Gacchantasaddassa bhedo, gacchanta si,

A distinction for the word 'gacchanta': gacchanta, si.

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' is carried forward.

107. Simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo aṃ.

107. When 'si' follows, the 'nta' of 'gacchanta' and so forth becomes 'aṃ'.

Gacchanticcevamādīnaṃ antappaccayantānaṃ ntasaddo aṃrūpaṃ āpajjate vā simhi vibhattimhi. Saralopasilopā, so gacchaṃ, gacchanto vā gaṇhāti.

Of 'gacchanta' and so forth, which end in the 'anta' suffix, the 'nta' optionally takes the form 'aṃ' when the 'si' case-ending follows. After elision of the vowel and of 'si', one has: so gacchaṃ, or gacchanto vā gaṇhāti.

“Gacchantādīnaṃ, ntasaddo”ti ca vattamāne –

When 'gacchantādīnaṃ' and 'ntasaddo' are carried forward—

108. Sesesu ntuva.

108. In the remaining cases, it is like 'ntu'.

Gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo ntupaccayova daṭṭhabbo sesesu vibhattippaccayesu, asmimhi kāriyātidesoyaṃ. Sesaṃ guṇavantusamaṃ.

For 'gacchanta' and so forth, the 'nta' is to be regarded as the 'ntu' suffix itself in the remaining case-endings. This is an extension of function. The rest is like 'guṇavantu'.

Te gacchanto gacchantā, bho gacchaṃ bho gaccha bho gacchā, bhavanto gacchanto gacchantā, [gacchaṃ] gacchantaṃ, gacchante, gacchatā gacchantena, gacchantehi gacchantebhi, gacchato gacchantassa, gacchataṃ gacchantānaṃ, gacchatā gacchantasmā gacchantamhā, gacchantehi gacchantebhi, gacchato gacchantassa, gacchataṃ gacchantānaṃ, gacchati gacchante gacchantasmiṃ gacchantamhī, gacchantesu.

Te gacchanto, gacchantā; bho gacchaṃ, bho gaccha, bho gacchā; bhavanto gacchanto, gacchantā; [gacchaṃ] gacchantaṃ; gacchante; gacchatā, gacchantena; gacchantehi, gacchantebhi; gacchato, gacchantassa; gacchataṃ, gacchantānaṃ; gacchatā, gacchantasmā, gacchantamhā; gacchantehi, gacchantebhi; gacchato, gacchantassa; gacchataṃ, gacchantānaṃ; gacchati, gacchante, gacchantasmiṃ, gacchantamhī; gacchantesu.

Evaṃ mahaṃ caraṃ tiṭṭhaṃ, dadaṃ bhuñjaṃ suṇaṃ pacaṃ;

Jayaṃ jīraṃ cavaṃ mīyaṃ, saraṃ kubbaṃ japaṃ vajaṃ –

Similarly: mahaṃ, caraṃ, tiṭṭhaṃ, dadaṃ, bhuñjaṃ, suṇaṃ, pacaṃ; jayaṃ, jīraṃ, cavaṃ, mīyaṃ, saraṃ, kubbaṃ, japaṃ, vajaṃ—

Iccādayo.

And so forth.

Bhavantasaddassa [M 0.0057] ga yo nā savacanesu viseso. So bhavaṃ.

For the word 'bhavanta', there is a special rule in the 'ga', 'yo', and 'nā' case-endings. So bhavaṃ.

“Bhavato”ti vattate.

'Bhavato' is carried forward.

109. Obhāvo kvaci yosu vakārassa.

109. Of the letter 'va', there is the substitution of 'o' sometimes when 'yo' follows.

Bhavantaiccetassa vakārassa obhāvo hoti kvaci yoiccetesu. Te bhonto bhavanto bhavantā.

Of this word 'bhavanta', the letter 'va' sometimes becomes 'o' when these 'yo' case-endings follow. Te bhonto, bhavanto, bhavantā.

“Bhavato”ti vattate.

'Bhavato' is carried forward.

110. Bho ge tu.

110. Bho when 'ga' follows; and 'tu'.

Sabbasseva bhavantasaddassa bho hoti ge pare. Tusaddena bhante, bhontādi ca, galopo, bho bhante bhonta bhontā, bhonto bhavanto bhavantā, bhavantaṃ, bhonte bhavante.

Of the entire word 'bhavanta', 'bho' is the substitute when 'ga' follows. By the word 'tu', the forms 'bhante', 'bhonta', etc. also occur, and there is elision of 'ga'. Thus: bho, bhante, bhonta, bhontā; bhonto, bhavanto, bhavantā; bhavantaṃ; bhonte, bhavante.

Nāsesu “obhāvo kvacī”ti yogavibhāgena obhāvo.

In the 'nā' and 'sa' cases, the change to 'o' occurs by means of splitting the rule 'obhāvo kvaci'.

Bhotā bhavatā bhavantena, bhoto bhavato bhavantassa iccādi.

Bhotā, bhavatā, bhavantena; bhoto, bhavato, bhavantassa; and so forth.

111. Bhadantassa bhaddanta bhante.

111. For 'bhadanta', the substitutes are 'bhaddanta' and 'bhante'.

Sabbasseva bhadantasaddassa bhaddanta bhanteiccete ādesā honti kvaci ge pare yosu ca. Bho bhaddanta bhante, bhadanta bhadantā vā iccādi purisasaddasamaṃ.

Of the entire word 'bhadanta', these substitutes 'bhaddanta' and 'bhante' occur sometimes when 'ga' follows and also in the 'yo' case-endings. Bho bhaddanta, bhante; bhadanta or bhadantā, etc. The rest is like the word 'purisa'.

112. Santasaddassa so bhe bo cante.

112. Of the word 'santa', 'sa' is the substitute when an ending beginning with 'bh' follows, and 'ba' is at the end.

Sabbasseva santasaddassa sasaddādeso hoti bhakāre pare, ante ca bakārāgamo hoti.

Of the entire word 'santa', the substitute 'sa' occurs when the letter 'bha' follows, and at the end, there is the augment 'ba'.

Casaddaggahaṇena [M 0.0058] abhakārepi samāse kvaci sakārādeso. Sabbhi.

By the inclusion of the word 'ca', even when not followed by the letter 'bha', the substitute 'sa' sometimes occurs in compounds. Sabbhi.

Bheti kiṃ? Santehi, sesaṃ gacchantasaddasamaṃ.

Why is 'bhe' stated? For the sake of the form 'Santehi'. The rest is like the word 'gacchanta'.

Atthi rāja brahma atta sakhasaddādīnaṃ bhedo, tatheva syādyuppatti, “rāja si”iti ṭhite –

There is a special rule for the words 'rāja', 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', and so forth; and similarly for the derivation beginning with 'si', as when 'rāja si' stands –

“Brahmattasakharājādito”ti adhikāro.

The governing rule is 'brahmattasakharājādito'.

113. Syā ca.

113. And 'si' becomes 'ā'.

Brahma atta sakha rājaiccevamādito sivacanassa ākāro hoti. Ādisaddena ātumādisaddato ca. Saralopādi. Rājā tiṭṭhati.

After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so forth, the 'si' case ending becomes 'ā'. By the word 'ādi', this also applies to words like 'attumā'. The process involves elision of a vowel, and so forth. For example: Rājā tiṭṭhati.

114. Yonamāno.

114. 'Yo' becomes 'āno'.

Brahmattasakharājādito yonaṃ ānoādeso hoti. Rājāno tiṭṭhanti, bho rāja bho rājā, bhavanto rājāno.

After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so forth, the substitute 'āno' occurs for 'yo'. For example: Rājāno tiṭṭhanti; bho rāja, bho rājā; bhavanto rājāno.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' is carried forward.

115. Brahmattasakharājādito amānaṃ.

115. After 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'rāja', and so forth, 'aṃ' becomes 'ānaṃ'.

Brahmādīhi parassa aṃvacanassa ānaṃ hoti vā. Rājānaṃ passa rājaṃ vā, rājāno.

After words such as 'brahma', the 'aṃ' case ending optionally becomes 'ānaṃ'. For example: Rājānaṃ passa, or rājaṃ; rājāno.

“Savibhattissa, rājassā”ti ca vattate.

And 'savibhattissa' and 'rājassa' are carried forward.

116. Nāmhi raññā vā.

116. In the 'nā' case, 'raññā' is substituted optionally.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññāādeso hoti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi. Raññā kataṃ rājena vā.

For the entire word 'rāja' with its case ending, the substitute 'raññā' occurs optionally in the 'nā' case ending. For example: Raññā kataṃ, or rājena.

117. Rājassa [M 0.0059] rāju sunaṃhisu ca.

117. For 'rāja', 'rāju' is substituted in 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'.

Sabbassa rājasaddassa rājuādeso hoti su naṃ hiiccetesu vacanesu. Casaddo vikappanattho, “sunaṃhisu cā”ti dīgho, rājūhi rājūbhi, rājehi rājebhi vā.

For the entire word 'rāja', the substitute 'rāju' occurs in these case endings: 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'. The word 'ca' indicates optionality. The long vowel is in 'sunaṃhisu cā'. For example: rājūhi, rājūbhi, or optionally rājehi, rājebhi.

“Savibhattissā”ti adhikāro.

The governing rule is 'savibhattissa'.

118. Rājassa raññorājino se.

118. For 'rāja', 'rañño' and 'rājino' are substituted in the 'se' case.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa rañño rājinoiccete ādesā honti se vibhattimhi. Rañño, rājino deti.

For the entire word 'rāja' with its case ending, these substitutes 'rañño' and 'rājino' occur in the 'se' case ending. For example: Rañño deti, rājino deti.

“Rājassā”ti vattate.

The word 'rājassa' is carried forward.

119. Raññaṃ naṃ mhī vā.

119. 'Raññaṃ' is substituted in 'naṃ' and 'mhī' optionally.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññaṃādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Raññaṃ rājūnaṃ rājānaṃ.

For the entire word 'rāja' with its case ending, the substitute 'raññaṃ' occurs optionally in the 'naṃ' case ending. For example: Raññaṃ, rājūnaṃ, rājānaṃ.

Pañcamiyaṃ –

In the fifth case –

120. Amhatumhanturājabrahmattasakhasatthupitādīhi smā nāva.

120. After 'amha', 'tumha', 'ntu', 'rāja', 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'satthu', 'pitu', and so forth, 'smā' becomes 'nā' optionally.

Amhatumhanturājabrahmattasakhasatthupituiccevamādīhi smāvacanaṃ nāva daṭṭhabbanti smāvacanassa nābhāvātideso. Atideso pana chabbidho.

After 'amha', 'tumha', 'ntu', 'rāja', 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', 'satthu', 'pitu', and so forth, the 'smā' case ending should be understood as 'nā' optionally; thus, this is an application of 'nā' for the 'smā' case ending. This application by analogy (atidesa) is sixfold.

Vuttañca –

And it is said –

“Byapadeso nimittañca, taṃrūpaṃ taṃsabhāvatā;

Suttañceva tathā kāri-yātidesoti chabbidho”ti.

"Designation and cause, that form, that nature; the rule and likewise the function—thus application by analogy is sixfold."

Tatrāyaṃ [M 0.0060] brahmattasakhādīsu pāṭhasāmatthiyato rūpātideso. Sesaṃ tatiyāsamaṃ.

Here, for 'brahma', 'atta', 'sakha', and so forth, by the force of their inclusion in the rule, it is an application of form. The rest is like the third case.

Raññā apeti, rājūhi rājūbhi, rājehi rājebhi, rañño, rājino santakaṃ, raññaṃ rājūnaṃ rājānaṃ.

Raññā apeti; rājūhi, rājūbhi; rājehi, rājebhi; rañño santakaṃ, rājino santakaṃ; raññaṃ, rājūnaṃ, rājānaṃ.

“Rājassā”ti vattate.

The word 'rājassa' is carried forward.

121. Smiṃmhi raññe rājini.

121. In 'smiṃ' and 'mhi', 'raññe' and 'rājini' are substituted.

Sabbasseva rājasaddassa savibhattissa raññerājiniiccete ādesā honti smiṃmhi vibhattimhi. Raññe, rājini patiṭṭhitaṃ, rājūsu rājesu.

For the entire word 'rāja' with its case ending, these substitutes 'raññe' and 'rājini' occur in the 'smiṃ' and 'mhi' case endings. For example: Raññe patiṭṭhitaṃ, rājini patiṭṭhitaṃ; rājūsu, rājesu.

Brahmasaddassa ca ga nā sa smiṃsu viseso. Brahmā, brahmāno.

And for the word 'brahma', there is a specific modification regarding the endings 'ga', 'nā', 'sa', and 'smiṃ'. Brahmā, brahmāno.

Ālapane ca “e”ti vattate.

And in the vocative, the rule for 'e' continues to apply.

122. Brahmato gassa ca.

122. After 'brahma', and for 'ga'.

Brahmasaddato gassa ca ekāro hoti, caggahaṇaṃ eggahaṇānukaḍḍhanatthaṃ, bho brahme, bhavanto brahmāno, brahmānaṃ brahmaṃ, brahmāno.

For the ending 'ga' after the word 'brahma', the letter 'e' occurs. The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of carrying forward the mention of 'e'. O brahme, venerable brahmās, brahmānaṃ, brahmaṃ, brahmāno.

Vipariṇāmena “brahmassa, anto”ti ca vattate.

By modification, 'brahmassa' and 'anto' also continue to apply.

123. Uttaṃ sanāsu.

123. The letter 'u' for 'sa' and 'nā'.

Brahmasaddassa anto uttamāpajjate sa nāiccetesu vacanesu. Uttamiti bhāvaniddeso katthaci abhāvadassanattho. Brahmunā, brahmehi brahmebhi.

The final part of the word 'brahma' becomes 'u' with respect to these endings, 'sa' and 'nā'. The term 'uttam' is a designation of a process, sometimes for the purpose of indicating non-occurrence. Brahmunā, brahmehi, brahmebhi.

Sasmiṃ utte kate “ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā”ti lasaññāyaṃ –

When 'u' has been made with respect to 'sa', in the designation 'la' by the rule 'ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā'—

124. Jhalato [M 0.0061] sassa no vā.

124. After a 'jhala', 'no' is optionally substituted for 'sa'.

Jhalasaññehi ivaṇṇuvaṇṇehi parassa saiccetassa vacanassa noiccādeso hoti vā. Brahmuno brahmassa, brahmānaṃ brahmūnaṃ vā, uttamiti yogavibhāgena aññatthāpi uttaṃ.

For the ending 'sa' that follows the i-vowels and u-vowels designated as 'jhala', the substitute 'no' optionally occurs. Brahmuno, brahmassa; brahmānaṃ or brahmūnaṃ. By splitting the rule 'uttam', the letter 'u' also occurs elsewhere.

Pañcamiyaṃ nābhāvātideso. Brahmunā, brahmehi brahmebhi, brahmuno brahmassa, brahmānaṃ brahmūnaṃ vā.

In the fifth case, there is an extension of the rule for the substitution 'nā'. Brahmunā, brahmehi, brahmebhi; brahmuno, brahmassa; brahmānaṃ or brahmūnaṃ.

125. Brahmato tu smiṃ ni.

125. But after 'brahma', 'ni' is substituted for 'smiṃ'.

Brahmasaddato smiṃvacanassa ni hoti. Tusaddena kammacammamuddhādito ca kvaci. Brahmani, brahmesu.

After the word 'brahma', 'ni' is substituted for the ending 'smiṃ'. And by the word 'tu', this also occurs sometimes after stems such as 'kamma', 'camma', and 'muddhan'. Brahmani, brahmesu.

Attasaddassa tatiyādīsveva viseso.

For the word 'attan', there is a special rule only in the third case and those that follow.

Attā, attāno, bho atta bho attā, bhavanto attāno, attānaṃ attaṃ, attāno.

Attā, attāno; O atta, O attā; venerable attāno; attānaṃ, attaṃ; attāno.

Nāmhi “akammantassa cā”ti ettha casaddena attantassa attaṃ vā. Attanā attena vā.

When 'nā' follows, in the rule 'akammantassa cā', by the word 'ca', the stem 'attan' optionally becomes 'atta'. Attanā or attena.

126. Attanto hismimanattaṃ.

126. The final part of 'attan' becomes 'anatta' when 'hi' and 'smiṃ' follow.

Attasaddassa anto anattamāpajjate hismiṃ pare. Attanehi attanebhi.

The final part of the word 'attan' becomes 'anatta' when 'hi' or 'smiṃ' follow. Attanehi, attanebhi.

“Tato, attato”ti ca vattate.

'Tato' and 'attato' also continue to apply.

127. Sassa no.

127. For 'sa', 'no' is substituted.

Tato attasaddato sassa vibhattissa no hoti. Attano, attānaṃ.

Therefore, after the word 'attan', 'no' is substituted for the case ending 'sa'. Attano, attānaṃ.

128. Smā [M 0.0062] nā.

128. For 'smā', 'nā' is substituted.

Tato attasaddato smāvacanassa nā hoti. Attanā apeti.

Therefore, after the word 'attan', 'nā' is substituted for the ending 'smā'. For example: Attanā apeti.

Nābhāvātideseneva siddhepi uttarasuttena ekayogamakatvā bhinnayogakaraṇaṃ atthantaraviññāpanatthaṃ, tena attantatakārassa rakāro jakāre kvaci. Atrajo attajo vā. Attanehi attanebhi, attano, attānaṃ.

Although this is established by the extension of the rule for 'nā', the formulation of a separate rule, instead of a single rule with the subsequent sutta, is for the purpose of indicating another meaning. By this, for the letter 't' of the stem 'attan', 'r' or 'j' is sometimes substituted. For example: Atrajo or attajo. Attanehi, attanebhi; attano, attānaṃ.

“Attato”ti vattate.

'Attato' continues to apply.

129. Tato smiṃ ni.

129. After that, 'ni' is substituted for 'smiṃ'.

Tato attasaddato smiṃvacanassa ni hoti. Attani, attesu.

Therefore, after the word 'attan', 'ni' is substituted for the ending 'smiṃ'. Attani, attesu.

Sakhasaddassa bhedo. Sakhā, sakhāno.

Variations of the word 'sakhi'. Sakhā, sakhāno.

“Yona”miti vattate.

'Yonaṃ' continues to apply.

130. Sakhato cāyono.

130. After 'sakhi', also 'āyo' and 'no'.

Sakhasaddato yonaṃ āyo noādesā ca honti. Sakhāyo.

From the word 'sakha', 'āyo' and 'no' are substituted for the 'yo' endings. Example: Sakhāyo.

131. Sakhantassi nonānaṃsesu.

131. For the end of 'sakha', 'i' is substituted when 'no', 'nā', 'naṃ', 'sa', 'i', and 'su' follow.

Sakhasaddantassa ikārādeso hoti nonānaṃsaiccetesu paresu. Sakhino tiṭṭhanti.

For the end of the word 'sakha', the vowel 'i' is substituted when 'no', 'nā', 'naṃ', 'sa', 'i', and 'su' follow. Example: Sakhino tiṭṭhanti.

Ālapane gasaññāyaṃ –

In the vocative, for the term 'ga' –

132. Sakhato [M 0.0063] gasse vā.

132. From 'sakha', for 'ga', 'e' is optionally substituted.

Sakhato gassa akāra ākāra ikāra īkāraekārādesā honti. Vāsaddena aññasmāpi kvaci ekāro. Yathā – bhaddante ise iti.

From 'sakha', for 'ga', the vowels 'a', 'ā', 'i', 'ī', and 'e' are substituted. By the word 'vā', 'e' also occurs sometimes for other words. For example: bhaddante, ise.

A ca ā ca i ca ī ca e cātipi e, pubbassarānaṃ kamena lopo.

'A', 'ā', 'i', 'ī', 'e', and also 'e' are substituted, with sequential elision of the preceding vowels.

Bho sakha bho sakhā bho sakhi bho sakhī bho sakhe, bhavanto sakhāno sakhāyo sakhino.

O friend, O friends! Examples: bho sakha, bho sakhā, bho sakhi, bho sakhī, bho sakhe; bhavanto sakhāno, sakhāyo, sakhino.

“Sakhantassa, āro cā”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'Sakhantassa' and 'āro ca' are also carried forward.

133. Sunamaṃsu vā.

133. Optionally, when 'su', 'naṃ', and 'aṃ' follow.

Sakhantassa āro bhoti vā sunaṃ aṃiccetesu paresu. Sakhāraṃ sakhānaṃ sakhaṃ, sakhāno sakhāyo sakhino, sakhinā.

For the end of 'sakha', 'āro' is optionally substituted when 'su', 'naṃ', and 'aṃ' follow. Examples: Sakhāraṃ, sakhānaṃ, sakhaṃ; sakhāno, sakhāyo, sakhino; sakhinā.

“Sakhantassā”ti vattate.

The rule 'Sakhantassa' is carried forward.

134. Āro himhi vā.

134. Optionally, 'āro' is substituted when the endings 'hi' and 'mhi' follow.

Sakhantassa āro hoti vā himhi vibhattimhi. Sakhārehi sakhārebhi, sakhehi sakhebhi.

For the end of 'sakha', 'āro' is optionally substituted when the endings are 'hi' and 'mhi'. Examples: Sakhārehi, sakhārebhi; sakhehi, sakhebhi.

Ikārādese “jhalato sassa no vā”ti no. Sakhino sakhissa, sakhārānaṃ sakhīnaṃ.

When the 'i' substitution has been made, 'no' is substituted for 'sa' by the rule 'jhalato sassa no vā'. Examples: Sakhino, sakhissa; sakhārānaṃ, sakhīnaṃ.

Smāvacanassa nābhāvo. Sakhinā, sakhārehi sakhārebhi sakhehi sakhebhi, sakhino sakhissa, sakhārānaṃ sakhīnaṃ.

The substitution of 'nā' for the ending 'smā' does not occur. Examples: Sakhinā; sakhārehi, sakhārebhi, sakhehi, sakhebhi; sakhino, sakhissa; sakhārānaṃ, sakhīnaṃ.

“Sakhato”ti ca vattate.

The rule 'Sakhato' is also carried forward.

135. Smime[M 0.0064].

135. For 'smiṃ', 'e' is substituted.

Sakhato smiṃvacanassa ekāro hoti. Niccatthoyamārambho. Sakhe, sakhāresu sakhesu.

From 'sakha', 'e' is substituted for the 'smiṃ' ending. This rule is stated to make the substitution obligatory. Examples: Sakhe; sakhāresu, sakhesu.

Ātumasaddassa paṭhamādutiyāsu attasaddasseva rūpanayo. Ātumā, ātumāno, bho ātuma bho ātumā, bhavanto ātumāno, ātumānaṃ ātumaṃ, ātumāno, ātumena iccādi purisasamaṃ.

For the word 'ātuma', the formation in the first and second cases is like that of the word 'atta'. Examples: Ātumā, ātumāno; bho ātuma, bho ātumā; bhavanto ātumāno; ātumānaṃ, ātumaṃ; ātumāno. From 'ātumena' onwards, it is like 'purisa'.

Pumasaddassa bhedo. Puma si,

Variations of the word 'puma'. Rule: Puma si,

“Savibhattissā”ti adhikāro.

'Savibhattissa' is the governing rule.

136. Pumantassā simhi.

136. For the end of 'puma', 'ā' is substituted when 'si' and 'mhi' follow.

Pumasaddassa savibhattissa ākārādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi. Antaggahaṇena maghavayuvādīnamantassa ca. Pumā.

For the word 'puma' with its case ending, the substitution of 'ā' occurs for the 'si' and 'mhi' endings. By the inclusion of 'anta', this also applies to the end of 'maghavā', 'yuvā', and other such words. Example: Pumā.

“Pumantassā”ti adhikāro.

'Pumantassa' is the governing rule.

137. Yosvāno.

137. For the 'yo' endings, 'āno' is substituted.

Pumantassa savibhattissa ānoādeso hoti yosu vibhattīsu. Pumāno.

For 'puma' with its case ending, the substitution 'āno' occurs for the 'yo' endings. Example: Pumāno.

138. Amālapanekavacane.

138. 'Aṃ' is substituted in the vocative singular.

Pumantassa savibhattissa aṃ hoti ālapanekavacane pare. He pumaṃ, he pumāno, pumaṃ, pumāno.

For 'puma' with its case ending, 'aṃ' is substituted when the vocative singular follows. Examples: He pumaṃ, he pumāno; pumaṃ, pumāno.

“Ā, vā”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'ā' and 'vā' are also carried forward.

139. U [M 0.0065] nāmhi ca.

139. And 'u' in the case of the 'nā' and 'mhi' endings.

Pumantassa āuādesā honti vā nāmhi vibhattimhi. Casaddena pumakammathāmantassa cu’kāro vā sasmāsu. Pumānā pumunā pumena vā.

For the final vowel of 'puma', the substitutions 'ā' and 'u' occur optionally in the case of the 'nā' and 'mhi' case endings. And by the word 'ca', the vowel 'u' is optionally substituted for the final vowel of 'pumakammatha' in the case of the 'sa' and 'smā' endings. Examples: Pumānā, pumunā, or pumena.

“Āne”ti vattate.

'Āne' is carried forward.

140. Hivibhattimhi ca.

140. And in the case of the 'hi' case ending.

Pumantassa hivibhattimhī ca āneādeso hoti. Vibhattiggahaṇaṃ savibhattiggahaṇanivattanatthaṃ. Pumānehi pumānebhi.

For the final vowel of 'puma', the substitution 'āne' also occurs in the case of the 'hi' case ending. The specification of 'vibhatti' is for the purpose of preventing the inclusion of the stem with its ending. Examples: Pumānehi, pumānebhi.

Casaddena yuvamaghavādīnamantassa vā ānādeso hoti sabbavibhattīsu. “U nāmhi cā”ti ettha casaddena pumantassukāro vā sasmāsu vibhattīsu. “Jhalato sassa no vā”ti no. Pumuno pumassa, pumānaṃ.

By the word 'ca', the substitution 'āna' optionally occurs for the final vowel of 'yuva', 'maghava', and so on, in all case endings. In the rule 'U nāmhi cā', by the word 'ca' therein, the vowel 'u' is optionally substituted for the final vowel of 'puma' in the 'sa' and 'smā' case endings. By the rule 'Jhalato sassa no vā', 'no' is substituted. Examples: Pumuno, pumassa; pumānaṃ.

“Smā, nā”ti vattate.

'Smā' and 'nā' are carried forward.

141. Jhalato ca.

141. And after a 'jhala' consonant.

Jhalaiccetehi smāvacanassa nā hoti. Caggahaṇaṃ kvaci nivattanatthaṃ. Pumānā pumunā pumā pumasmā pumamhā, pumānehi pumānebhi pumehi pumebhi, pumuno pumassa, pumānaṃ.

After these, which are 'jhala' consonants, 'nā' is substituted for the ending 'smā'. The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of preventing this in some cases. Examples: Pumānā, pumunā, pumā, pumasmā, pumamhā; pumānehi, pumānebhi, pumehi, pumebhi; pumuno, pumassa; pumānaṃ.

142. Āne smiṃmhi vā.

142. Optionally 'āne' for the 'smiṃ' and 'mhi' endings.

Pumantassa savibhattissa āneādeso hoti vā smiṃmhi vibhattimhi. Pumāne pume pumasmiṃ pumamhi.

For the stem 'puma' together with its case ending, the substitution 'āne' occurs optionally in the case of the 'smiṃ' and 'mhi' case endings. Examples: Pumāne, pume, pumasmiṃ, pumamhi.

143. Susmimā [M 0.0066] vā.

143. Optionally 'ā' before the 'su' and 'smiṃ' endings.

Pumantassa suiccetasmiṃ pare āādeso hoti vā. Pumāsu pumesu.

For the final vowel of 'puma', the substitution 'ā' occurs optionally when 'su' follows. Examples: Pumāsu, pumesu.

Yuvādīsu “yuva si” itīdha –

In the case of 'yuva' and so on, here from 'yuva si' –

“Pumantassā simhī”ti ettha antaggahaṇena ākāro, “hivibhattimhi cā”ti sutte casaddena ānādeso ca.

In the rule 'Pumantassā simhī', by the inclusion of 'anta' therein, the vowel 'ā' is substituted; and in the sutta 'Hivibhattimhi cā', by the word 'ca', the substitution 'āna' also occurs.

Yuvā yuvāno, yuvānā yuvā, he yuva he yuvā he yuvāna he yuvānā, bhavanto yuvānā, yuvānaṃ yuvaṃ, yuvāne yuve.

Yuvā, yuvāno; yuvānā, yuvā; O yuva, O yuvā, O yuvāna, O yuvānā; bhavanto yuvānā; yuvānaṃ, yuvaṃ; yuvāne, yuve.

“Akammantassa cā”ti ettha casaddena yuvamaghavādīnamantassa ā hoti vā nāsuiccetesūti āttaṃ.

In the rule 'Akammantassa cā', by the word 'ca' therein, the final vowel of 'yuva', 'maghava', and so on, optionally becomes 'ā' in the case of the endings 'nā', 'su', and so forth; hence the lengthening to 'ā'.

Yuvānā yuvena yuvānena vā, yuvānehi yuvānebhi yuvehi yuvebhi, yuvānassa yuvassa, yuvānānaṃ yuvānaṃ, yuvānā yuvānasmā yuvānamhā, yuvānehi yuvānebhi yuvehi yuvebhi, yuvānassa yuvassa, yuvānānaṃ yuvānaṃ, yuvāne yuvānasmiṃ yuvānamhi yuve yuvamhi yuvasmiṃ, yuvānesu yuvāsu yuvesu.

Yuvānā, yuvena, or yuvānena; yuvānehi, yuvānebhi, yuvehi, yuvebhi; yuvānassa, yuvassa; yuvānānaṃ, yuvānaṃ; yuvānā, yuvānasmā, yuvānamhā; yuvānehi, yuvānebhi, yuvehi, yuvebhi; yuvānassa, yuvassa; yuvānānaṃ, yuvānaṃ; yuvāne, yuvānasmiṃ, yuvānamhi, yuve, yuvamhi, yuvasmiṃ; yuvānesu, yuvāsu, yuvesu.

Evaṃ maghavā maghavāno, maghavānā iccādi yuvasaddasamaṃ.

Similarly, maghavā, maghavāno, maghavānā, and so on, are declined like the word 'yuva'.

Akārantaṃ.

End of the section on stems ending in 'a'.

Ākāranto pulliṅgo sāsaddo.

The word 'sā' is masculine and ends in 'ā'.

Sā si, silopo, sā sunakho.

Sā + si; elision of 'si'; yields sā. Example: sā sunakho, the dog.

Bahuvacane –

In the plural:

144. Agho [M 0.0067] rassamekavacanayosvapi ca.

144. A final vowel not designated 'gha' is also shortened in the singular and before the 'yo' ending.

Ghasaññakaākāravajjito liṅgassanto saro rassamāpajjate ekavacanesu yosu ca paresūti rassattaṃ. Apiggahaṇaṃ simhi nivattanatthaṃ. Sesaṃ neyyaṃ.

The final vowel of a nominal stem, excluding those designated 'gha' and the vowel 'ā', becomes short in the singular endings and when 'yo' follows; this is the shortening. The inclusion of 'api' is for the purpose of preventing this in the case of 'si'. The rest is to be inferred.

Sā tiṭṭhanti, he sa he sā, he sā, saṃ, se, sena, sāhi sābhi, sassa sāya, sānaṃ, sā sasmā samhā, sāhi sābhi, sassa, sānaṃ, se sasmiṃ samhi, sāsu.

Sā tiṭṭhanti; O sa, O sā; O sā; saṃ, se; sena; sāhi, sābhi; sassa, sāya; sānaṃ; sā, sasmā, samhā; sāhi, sābhi; sassa; sānaṃ; se, sasmiṃ, samhi; sāsu.

Evaṃ paccakkhadhammā gāṇḍīvadhanvāpabhutayo.

Similarly, words such as paccakkhadhammā, gāṇḍīvadhanvā, and so forth.

Ākārantaṃ.

End of the section on stems ending in 'ā'.

Ikāranto pulliṅgo aggisaddo. Syādyuppatti, aggi si,

The word 'aggi' is masculine and ends in 'i'. The derivation with 'si', etc., is as follows: aggi + si,

“Anto, simhi, vā”ti ca vattate.

'Anto', 'simhi', and 'vā' are also carried forward.

145. Aggissini.

145. For aggi, ini is substituted before si.

Aggissa anto ini hoti vā simhi vibhattimhi. “Sesato lopaṃ gasipī”ti silopo. Aggini aggi.

For the end of aggi, ini occurs optionally in the si ending. By the rule, “Sesato lopaṃ gasipī,” the elision of si occurs. Examples: Aggini, aggi.

Bahuvacane “ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā”ti jhalasaññāyaṃ –

In the plural, by the rule “ivaṇṇuvaṇṇā jhalā,” in the designation jhala—

“Jhalato, vā”ti ca vattate.

“Jhalato” and “vā” are also carried forward.

146. Ghapato ca yonaṃ lopo.

146. And elision of the yo endings after ghapa.

Ghapasaññehi itthivācakehi ākārivaṇṇuvaṇṇehi, jhalasaññehi ca paresaṃ yovacanānaṃ lopo hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsāyaṃ.

After those designated ghapa—feminine words ending in ā, i, and u—and after those designated jhala, elision of the following yo endings occurs optionally. This is a fixed option.

147. Yosu [M 0.0068] katanikāralopesu dīghaṃ.

147. Before yo endings where there has been elision of the case ending, there is lengthening.

Liṅgassantabhūtā sabbe rassasarā yosu katanikāralopesu dīghamāpajjante. Katā nikāralopā yesaṃ te katanikāralopā. Aggī.

All short vowels at the end of a stem are lengthened before yo endings where the case ending has been elided. Katanikāralopā are those where the case ending has been elided. Example: Aggī.

“Pañcādīnamatta”nti ito “atta”miti vattate.

From “Pañcādīnamatta,” the word “atta” is carried forward.

148. Yosvakatarasso jho.

148. Before yo, jha which is not shortened.

Yosu paresu akatarasso jho attamāpajjate. Aggayo.

When yo follows, jha, when not shortened, becomes atta. Example: Aggayo.

Jhoti kiṃ? Rattiyo.

Why is jha mentioned? Example: Rattiyo.

Ālapanepevaṃ. He aggi, he aggī he aggayo.

Similarly in the vocative. Examples: He aggi, he aggī, he aggayo.

Dutiyekavacane pubbassaralope sampatte –

In the accusative singular, when elision of the preceding vowel is applicable—

149. Aṃ mo niggahītaṃ jhalapehi.

149. After jhala and pa, niggahīta is substituted for aṃ and ma.

Jhalapaiccetehi parassa aṃvacanassa, makārassa ca niggahītaṃ ādeso hoti. Aggiṃ.

After jhala and pa, the substitution of niggahīta occurs for the following aṃ ending and for the letter ma. Example: Aggiṃ.

Aggī aggayo, agginā, aggīhi aggībhi, “sunaṃhisu cā”ti ettha caggahaṇena katthaci dīghābhāvo. Aggihi aggibhi.

Aggī, aggayo; agginā; aggīhi, aggībhi. In the rule “sunaṃhisu cā,” by the inclusion of ca, there is sometimes an absence of lengthening. Examples: Aggihi, aggibhi.

“Jhalato sassa no vā”ti no. Aggino aggissa, aggīnaṃ.

By the rule “Jhalato sassa no vā,” no is substituted. Examples: Aggino, aggissa; aggīnaṃ.

“Smā nā”ti vattamāne “jhalato cā”ti vikappena nā. Agginā aggismā aggimhā, aggīhi aggībhi aggihi aggibhi, aggino aggissa, aggīnaṃ agginaṃ, aggimhi aggismiṃ, aggīsu aggisu.

When “Smā nā” is carried forward, by the rule “jhalato ca,” nā is optionally substituted. Examples: Agginā, aggismā, aggimhā; aggīhi, aggībhi, aggihi, aggibhi; aggino, aggissa; aggīnaṃ, agginaṃ; aggimhi, aggismiṃ; aggīsu, aggisu.

Evamaññepi –

Similarly, others also—

Joti pāṇi gaṇṭhi muṭṭhi, kucchi vatthi sāli vīhi;

Byādhi odhi bodhi sandhi, rāsi kesi sāti dīpi.

Joti, pāṇi, gaṇṭhi, muṭṭhi; kucchi, vatthi, sāli, vīhi; byādhi, odhi, bodhi, sandhi; rāsi, kesi, sāti, dīpi.

Isi [M 0.0069] muni maṇi dhani yati giri ravi kavi,

Kapi asi masi nidhi vidhi ahi kimi pati;

Hari ari timi kali bali jaladhi gahapati,

Urudhiti varamati nirupadhi adhipati.

Isi, muni, maṇi, dhani, yati, giri, ravi, kavi; kapi, asi, masi, nidhi, vidhi, ahi, kimi, pati; hari, ari, timi, kali, bali, jaladhi, gahapati; urudhiti, varamati, nirupadhi, adhipati.

Añjali sārathi atithi samādhi udadhippabhutayo.

Añjali, sārathi, atithi, samādhi, udadhi, and others.

Ikārantaṃ.

Ending in i.

Īkāranto pulliṅgo daṇḍīsaddo.

The masculine word daṇḍī ends in ī.

“Daṇḍī si” itīdha –

Here, in the form “Daṇḍī si”—

“Agho rassamekavacanayosvapi cā”ti rassatte sampatte etthevāpiggahaṇena sismiṃ tadabhāve siddhe niyamatthamāha.

When shortening is applicable by the rule “Agho rassamekavacanayosvapi cā,” a restrictive rule is stated, since by the very inclusion of api here, the absence of shortening in the case of si is already established.

“Rassa”nti vattamāne –

When “rassa” is carried forward—

150. Na sismimanapuṃsakāni.

150. Not for non-neuter stems before si.

Sismiṃ napuṃsakavajjitāni liṅgāni na rassamāpajjanteti rassattābhāvo, silopo. Daṇḍī tiṭṭhati.

Before si, stems other than neuter do not undergo shortening; hence there is no shortening, and si is elided. Daṇḍī tiṭṭhati.

Anapuṃsakānīti kiṃ? Sukhakāri dānaṃ.

Why [the word] ‘non-neuter’? [Consider] ‘Sukhakāri dānaṃ’.

Ettha ca –

And here—

Visadāvisadākāra-vohārobhayamuttakā;

Pumādijānane hetu-bhāvato liṅgamīritā.

Clear and unclear forms, and expressions both conventional and unconventional, are called gender because they are the cause for knowing masculine and so forth.

Yolope daṇḍī tiṭṭhanti.

With the elision of 'yo': 'daṇḍī tiṭṭhanti'.

Itaratra “agho rassa”miccādinā rassatte kate –

Elsewhere, when shortening is done by “agho rassa” and so forth—

“Jhato, katarassā”ti ca vattate.

“Jhato, katarassā” is also in force.

151. Yonaṃ [M 0.0070] no.

151. 'No' for 'yo'.

Sabbesaṃ yonaṃ sālapanānaṃ jhato katarassā paresaṃ noiccādeso hoti. Daṇḍino tiṭṭhanti.

For all vocative 'yo' endings following a short vowel that has not been shortened, the substitution 'no' occurs. For example: 'Daṇḍino tiṭṭhanti'.

Katarassāti kiṃ? Aggayo.

Why [the word] ‘not shortened’? [Consider] ‘Aggayo’.

Adhikāraṃ vinā “yonaṃ,

No”ti yogavibhāgato;

Kvaci akatarassāpi,

No sāramatino yathā.

By splitting the rule 'yonaṃ no', without the governing rule, 'no' is sometimes substituted even for a stem that has been shortened, as in 'sāramatino'.

Ālapane “ge”ti vattate.

In the vocative, “ge” is in force.

152. Jhalapā rassaṃ.

152. Jhalapā [undergo] shortening.

Jhalapaiccete rassamāpajjante ge pare. Bho daṇḍi.

These ‘Jhalapa’ words undergo shortening when ‘ge’ follows. [E.g.,] ‘Bho daṇḍi’.

“Agho rassa”ntiādināva siddhepi rassatte punārambho niyamattho, tena “bho go”tiādīsu na bhavati. Daṇḍī daṇḍino.

Though shortening is established by “agho rassa” and the like, the repetition of the rule is for the purpose of restriction; hence, it does not occur in instances like “bho go.” [E.g.,] Daṇḍī, daṇḍino.

Dutiyāyaṃ rassatte kate “a”miti vattate, “ghapato smiṃ yaṃ vā”ti ito maṇḍūkagatiyā “vā”ti vattate.

When shortening is done in the second case, “aṃ” is in force; from “ghapato smiṃ yaṃ vā,” by frog-leap progression, “vā” is in force.

153. Naṃ jhato katarassā.

153. 'Naṃ' after a short vowel of an unshortened stem.

Jhato katarassā parassa aṃvacanassa naṃ hoti vā. Daṇḍinaṃ daṇḍiṃ, daṇḍī daṇḍino, daṇḍinā, daṇḍīhi daṇḍībhi, daṇḍino daṇḍissa, daṇḍīnaṃ.

For the ending 'aṃ' following a short vowel of a stem that has not been shortened, 'naṃ' is optionally substituted. [E.g.,] Daṇḍinaṃ, daṇḍiṃ; daṇḍī, daṇḍino; daṇḍinā; daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi; daṇḍino, daṇḍissa; daṇḍīnaṃ.

“Jhalato cā”ti nā. Daṇḍinā daṇḍismā daṇḍimhā, daṇḍīhi daṇḍībhi, daṇḍino daṇḍissa, daṇḍīnaṃ.

By “Jhalato ca,” ‘nā’ [is substituted]. [E.g.,] Daṇḍinā, daṇḍismā, daṇḍimhā; daṇḍīhi, daṇḍībhi; daṇḍino, daṇḍissa; daṇḍīnaṃ.

“Jhato, katarassā”ti ca vattate, pure viya “vā”ti ca.

“Jhato, katarassā” is also in force, and “vā” too, as before.

154. Smiṃ [M 0.0071] ni.

154. 'Ni' for 'smiṃ'.

Jhato katarassā parassa smiṃvacanassa niiccādeso hoti vā. Daṇḍini daṇḍismiṃ daṇḍimhi, daṇḍīsu.

For the ending 'smiṃ' following a short vowel of a stem that has not been shortened, the substitution 'ni' optionally occurs. [E.g.,] Daṇḍini, daṇḍismiṃ, daṇḍimhi; daṇḍīsu.

Evamaññānipi –

Thus also for others—

Dhammī saṅghī ñāṇī hatthī, cakkī pakkhī dāṭhī raṭṭhī;

Chattī mālī vammī yogī, bhāgī bhogī kāmī sāmī.

Dhammī, saṅghī, ñāṇī, hatthī; cakkī, pakkhī, dāṭhī, raṭṭhī; Chattī, mālī, vammī, yogī; bhāgī, bhogī, kāmī, sāmī.

Dhajī gaṇī sasī kuṭṭhī, jaṭī yānī sukhī sikhī;

Dantī mantī karī cāgī, kusalī musalī balī.

Dhajī, gaṇī, sasī, kuṭṭhī, jaṭī, yānī, sukhī, sikhī; Dantī, mantī, karī, cāgī, kusalī, musalī, balī.

Pāpakārī sattughātī, mālyakārī dīghajīvī;

Dhammacārī sīghayāyī, sīhanādī bhūmisāyī –

Pāpakārī, sattughātī; mālyakārī, dīghajīvī; Dhammacārī, sīghayāyī; sīhanādī, bhūmisāyī—

Iccādīni īkārantanāmāni.

And so forth are the nouns ending in 'ī'.

Gāmaṇīsaddassa tu sattamiyaṃ bhedo.

But for the word “gāmaṇī,” there is a difference in the seventh case.

Gāmaṇī, gāmaṇī gāmaṇino, bho gāmaṇi, bhonto gāmaṇī bhonto gāmaṇino, gāmaṇinaṃ gāmaṇiṃ, gāmaṇī gāmaṇino.

Gāmaṇī; gāmaṇī, gāmaṇino; bho gāmaṇi; bhonto gāmaṇī, bhonto gāmaṇino; gāmaṇinaṃ, gāmaṇiṃ; gāmaṇī, gāmaṇino.

Sesaṃ daṇḍīsamaṃ. Niādesābhāvova viseso. Evaṃ senānī sudhīppabhutayo.

The rest is like ‘daṇḍī.’ The absence of the ‘ni’ substitution is the difference. So too ‘senānī,’ ‘sudhī,’ and the like.

Īkārantaṃ.

Ending in 'ī'.

Ukāranto pulliṅgo bhikkhusaddo.

The masculine noun ‘bhikkhu’ ends in ‘u’.

Tatheva bhikkhusaddato si, silopo. So bhikkhu.

Similarly, from the word ‘bhikkhu,’ the suffix ‘si’ is elided, resulting in ‘So bhikkhu’.

Bahuvacane “ghapato ca yonaṃ lopo”ti yolopo, “yosu kata”iccādinā dīgho. Te bhikkhū.

In the plural, by the rule “ghapato ca yonaṃ lopo,” there is elision of ‘yo’; by “yosu kata” and so forth, there is lengthening, as in ‘Te bhikkhū’.

Lopābhāve “vā, yona”nti ca vattate.

In the absence of elision, the rules “vā” and “yona” are also in force.

155. Lato [M 0.0072] vokāro ca.

155. And from a stem designated ‘la,’ the substitution ‘vo’.

Lasaññato paresaṃ yovacanānaṃ vokārādeso hoti vā. Kāraggahaṇena yonaṃ no ca hoti. Casaddaggahaṇaṃ katthaci nivattanatthaṃ. Atha vā caggahaṇaṃ noggahaṇānuvattanatthaṃ, tena jantusabbaññūādito yonaṃ no ca hoti. Vāsaddo vavatthitavibhāsattho. Tena –

After a stem designated ‘la,’ for the following ‘yo’ endings, the substitution ‘vo’ optionally occurs. By the inclusion of ‘kāra’ in ‘vokāro,’ ‘no’ also occurs for ‘yo.’ The inclusion of the word ‘ca’ is to prevent this in some instances. Alternatively, the inclusion of ‘ca’ is for the purpose of carrying forward the substitution of ‘no’; therefore, from ‘jantu,’ ‘sabbaññū,’ and similar words, ‘no’ also occurs for ‘yo.’ The word ‘vā’ indicates a restricted option. Hence:

Bhikkhuppabhutito niccaṃ, vo yonaṃ hetuādito;

Vibhāsā na ca vo no ca, amuppabhutito bhave.

From ‘bhikkhu’ and so forth, ‘vo’ for ‘yo’ is always substituted; from ‘hetu’ and so forth, it is optional; and from ‘amu’ and so forth, neither ‘vo’ nor ‘no’ occurs.

“Attaṃ, akatarasso”ti ca vattate.

The rules “Attaṃ” and “akatarasso” are also in force.

156. Vevosu lo ca.

156. And when ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ follow, a change occurs to a stem designated ‘lo’.

Ve voiccetesu ca paresu akatarasso lo attamāpajjate. Bhikkhavo, bho bhikkhu, bhavanto bhikkhū.

And when ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ follow, the final vowel of a stem designated ‘lo’ which has not been shortened becomes ‘a’. For example: Bhikkhavo; O bhikkhu; you bhikkhus.

Lopābhāve –

In the absence of elision:

157. Akatarassā lato yvālapanassa vevo.

157. For the vocative ‘yo’ after a stem designated ‘la’ which has not been shortened, ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ are substituted.

Akatarassā lato parassa ālapane vihitassa yoiccetassa ve voādesā honti. Attaṃ. Bhavanto bhikkhave bhikkhavo. “Aṃ mo niggahītaṃ jhalapehī”ti niggahītaṃ.

For the ‘yo’ ending prescribed in the vocative, following a stem designated ‘la’ which has not been shortened, the substitutions ‘ve’ and ‘vo’ occur. The stem vowel becomes ‘a’. For example: Bhavanto bhikkhave, bhikkhavo. By the rule “Aṃ mo niggahītaṃ jhalapehī,” the niggahīta is formed.

Bhikkhuṃ, bhikkhū bhikkhavo, bhikkhunā, bhikkhūhi bhikkhūbhi bhikkhuhi bhikkhubhi, bhikkhuno bhikkhussa, bhikkhūnaṃ [M 0.0073] bhikkhunaṃ, bhikkhunā bhikkhusmā bhikkhumhā, bhikkhūhi bhikkhūbhi bhikkhuhi bhikkhubhi, bhikkhuno bhikkhussa, bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunaṃ, bhikkhumhi bhikkhusmiṃ, bhikkhūsu bhikkhusu.

Bhikkhuṃ; bhikkhū, bhikkhavo; bhikkhunā; bhikkhūhi, bhikkhūbhi, bhikkhuhi, bhikkhubhi; bhikkhuno, bhikkhussa; bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhunaṃ; bhikkhunā, bhikkhusmā, bhikkhumhā; bhikkhūhi, bhikkhūbhi, bhikkhuhi, bhikkhubhi; bhikkhuno, bhikkhussa; bhikkhūnaṃ, bhikkhunaṃ; bhikkhumhi, bhikkhusmiṃ; bhikkhūsu, bhikkhusu.

Evaṃ setu ketu rāhu bhānu paṅgu ucchu veḷu maccu sindhu bandhu neru meru sattu kāru hetu jantu ruru paṭu iccādayo.

Similarly for ‘setu,’ ‘ketu,’ ‘rāhu,’ ‘bhānu,’ ‘paṅgu,’ ‘ucchu,’ ‘veḷu,’ ‘maccu,’ ‘sindhu,’ ‘bandhu,’ ‘neru,’ ‘meru,’ ‘sattu,’ ‘kāru,’ ‘hetu,’ ‘jantu,’ ‘ruru,’ ‘paṭu,’ and so forth.

Hetujantusaddānaṃ paṭhamādutiyāsu viseso.

For the words ‘hetu’ and ‘jantu,’ there is a special rule in the nominative and accusative cases.

Hetu, hetū hetavo hetuyo, bho hetu, bhonto hetū hetave hetavo, hetuṃ, hetū hetavo hetuyo. Sesaṃ bhikkhusamaṃ.

Hetu; hetū, hetavo, hetuyo; O hetu; O hetus (bhonto hetū, hetave, hetavo); hetuṃ; hetū, hetavo, hetuyo. The rest is like ‘bhikkhu’.

Jantu, jantū jantavo. Kāraggahaṇena yonaṃ no ca hoti. Jantuno jantuyo, bho jantu, jantū jantave jantavo, jantuṃ, jantū jantavo jantuno jantuyo iccādi.

Jantu; jantū, jantavo. By the inclusion of ‘kāra,’ ‘no’ also occurs for ‘yo.’ For example: Jantuno, jantuyo; O jantu; O jantus (jantū, jantave, jantavo); jantuṃ; jantū, jantavo, jantuno, jantuyo, and so forth.

Satthusaddassa bhedo. “Satthu si”itīdha –

The declension of the word ‘satthu.’ Here, for ‘satthu + si’:

“Anto”ti vattate.

The rule “Anto” (the final vowel) is in force.

158. Satthupitādīnamā sismiṃ silopo ca.

158. For ‘satthu,’ ‘pitu,’ and so on, the final vowel is substituted by ‘ā’ in the ‘si’ case, and ‘si’ is elided.

Satthu pitu mātu bhātu dhītu kattuiccevamādīnamanto āttamāpajjate sismiṃ, silopo ca hoti. Satthā.

For ‘satthu,’ ‘pitu,’ ‘mātu,’ ‘bhātu,’ ‘dhītu,’ ‘kattu,’ and similar words, the final vowel becomes ‘ā’ in the ‘si’ case, and ‘si’ is elided. For example: Satthā.

“Satthu pitādīna”nti adhikāro.

“Satthu pitādīnaṃ” is the governing rule.

159. Aññesvārattaṃ[M 0.0074].

159. In other cases, ‘āra’ is substituted.

Satthu pitādīnamanto sivacanato aññesu vacanesu ārattamāpajjate. Ārattamitibhāvaniddesena katthaci aniyamaṃ dasseti.

The final vowel of ‘satthu,’ ‘pitu,’ and so on, becomes ‘āra’ in cases other than the ‘si’ case. By indicating this as a process of ‘becoming āra,’ it shows that the rule is not universal.

Āraggahaṇamanuvattate.

The inclusion of ‘āra’ is in force.

160. Tato yonamo tu.

160. After that, ‘o’ is substituted for ‘yo’; the particle ‘tu’ indicates a further application.

Tato ārādesato sabbesaṃ yonaṃ okārādeso hoti.

After that substitution ‘āra,’ for all ‘yo’ endings, the substitution ‘o’ occurs.

Tuggahaṇena aññehipi catuubhanadīgavādīhi yonamokāro hoti, saralopādi. Satthāro.

By the inclusion of ‘tu,’ for others like ‘catu,’ ‘ubhana,’ ‘dīgha,’ and ‘vādī,’ ‘o’ is also substituted for ‘yo,’ with vowel elision, etc. For example: Satthāro.

Ālapane “akārapitādyantānamā”ti āttaṃ. “Ge rassa”nti adhikicca “ākāro vā”ti vikappena rassattaṃ, valopo. Bho sattha bho satthā, bhavanto satthāro, satthāraṃ, satthāre satthāro.

In the vocative, by the rule “akārapitādyantānamā,” the final vowel is substituted by ‘ā’. Under the governing rule “Ge rassa,” by the specific rule “ākāro vā,” shortening optionally occurs, and the case ending is elided. For example: Bho sattha, bho satthā; bhavanto satthāro; satthāraṃ; satthāre, satthāro.

“Tato”ti ca vattate.

“Tato” (from that) is also in force.

161. Nā ā.

161. ‘Ā’ is substituted for ‘nā’.

Tato ārādesato nāvacanassa ākārādeso hoti. Satthārā, satthunāti ārattamitibhāvaniddesena siddhaṃ. Satthārehi satthārebhi.

From that, after the substitution `ārā`, the substitution `ā` occurs for the ending `nā`. The forms `satthārā` and `satthunā` are thus established by the indication of the state as `ārā`. For example: `Satthārehi`, `satthārebhi`.

“Vā naṃmhī”ti ito “vā”ti vattate.

From the rule “Vā naṃmhī,” “vā” is in force.

162. U [M 0.0075] sasmiṃ salopo ca.

162. When `sa` or `smiṃ` follow, `u` is substituted, and `sa` is elided.

Satthu pituiccevamādīnamantassa uttaṃ hoti vā sasmiṃ, salopo ca hoti. Ārādesāpavādoyaṃ. Satthu, aññattha bhāvaniddesenārābhāvo. Satthussa satthuno.

For the final vowel of `satthu`, `pitu`, and so on, the substitution `u` optionally occurs when `sa` or `smiṃ` follow, and `sa` is elided. This is an exception to the substitution `ārā`. In the case of `satthu`, elsewhere the absence of `ārā` is due to the indication of state. For example: `Satthussa`, `satthuno`.

“Āratta”nti vattate.

“Ārattaṃ” is in force.

163. Vā naṃmhi.

163. Optionally, when `naṃ` follows.

Satthu pituādīnamanto ārattamāpajjate vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Satthārānaṃ.

The final vowel of `satthu`, `pitu`, and so on, optionally becomes `ārā` when the case ending `naṃ` follows. For example: `Satthārānaṃ`.

Ārābhāve “vā naṃmhī”ti vattate.

In the absence of `ārā`, the rule “vā naṃmhī” is in force.

164. Satthunattañca.

164. And for `satthu`, the substitution `a`.

Satthusaddantassa, pitādīnamantassa ca attaṃ hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi, puna satthuggahaṇaṃ satthuno niccavidhānatthaṃ. Satthānaṃ.

For the final vowel of the word `satthu`, and for the final vowel of `pitu` and so on, the substitution `a` optionally occurs when the `naṃ` case ending follows. The repeated mention of `satthu` is for the purpose of making the rule obligatory for `satthu`. For example: `Satthānaṃ`.

“Amhatumhanturājabrahmattasakhasatthupitādīhi smā nāvā”ti smāvacanassanābhāvo. Satthārā, satthārehi satthārebhi, satthu satthuno satthussa, satthārānaṃ satthānaṃ.

By the rule “Amhatumhanturājabrahmattasakhasatthupitādīhi smā nāvā,” the ending `smā` becomes `nā`. For example: `Satthārā`; `satthārehi`, `satthārebhi`; `satthu`, `satthuno`, `satthussa`; `satthārānaṃ`, `satthānaṃ`.

“Ārato”ti vattate.

The rule “Ārato” is in force.

165. Tato smimi.

165. From that, `i` is substituted for `smiṃ`.

Tato ārādesato smiṃvacanassa ikārādeso hoti. Puna tatoggahaṇena aññasmāpi smiṃvacanassa ikāro. Yathā – bhuvi, divi.

From that, after the substitution `ārā`, the substitution `i` occurs for the ending `smiṃ`. Furthermore, by the inclusion of the word `tato`, `i` is also substituted for the ending `smiṃ` in other cases. For example: `bhuvi`, `divi`.

166. Āro [M 0.0076] rassamikāre.

166. `Ārā` becomes short when `i` follows.

Ārādeso rassamāpajjate ikāre pare, satthari, satthāresu.

The substitution `ārā` becomes short when `i` follows. For example: `satthari`, `satthāresu`.

Evaṃ kattā, kattāro, bho katta bho kattā, bhavanto kattāro, kattāraṃ, kattāre kattāro, kattārā, kattārehi kattārebhi. “U sasmiṃ salopo cā”ti uttaṃ, salopo ca. Kattu kattuno kattussa, kattārānaṃ kattānaṃ kattūnaṃ kattunaṃ, kattārā, kattārehi kattārebhi, kattu kattuno kattussa, kattārānaṃ kattānaṃ kattūnaṃ kattunaṃ, kattari, kattāresu, ārābhāve kattūsu kattusu.

Thus: `kattā`; `kattāro`; `bho katta`, `bho kattā`; `bhavanto kattāro`; `kattāraṃ`; `kattāre`, `kattāro`; `kattārā`; `kattārehi`, `kattārebhi`. By the rule “U sasmiṃ salopo cā,” `u` is substituted, and `sa` is elided. For example: `kattu`, `kattuno`, `kattussa`; `kattārānaṃ`, `kattānaṃ`, `kattūnaṃ`, `kattunaṃ`; `kattārā`; `kattārehi`, `kattārebhi`; `kattu`, `kattuno`, `kattussa`; `kattārānaṃ`, `kattānaṃ`, `kattūnaṃ`, `kattunaṃ`; `kattari`; `kattāresu`. In the absence of `ārā`: `kattūsu`, `kattusu`.

Evaṃ –

Similarly:

Bhattu vattu netu sotu, ñātu jetu chettu bhettu. Dātu dhātu nattu boddhu, viññāpetu ādayopi.

`Bhattu`, `vattu`, `netu`, `sotu`; `ñātu`, `jetu`, `chettu`, `bhettu`; `dātu`, `dhātu`, `nattu`, `boddhu`; `viññāpetu`, and others.

“U sasmiṃ salopo cā”ti vattate.

The rule “U sasmiṃ salopo cā” is in force.

167. Sakamandhātādīnañca.

167. And for `Sakamandhātu` and others.

Sakamandhātuiccevamādīnamanto ca uttamāpajjate sasmiṃ, salopo ca, niccaṃ punabbidhānā. Sakamandhātu viya assa rājino vibhavo, sesaṃ samaṃ. Evaṃ mahāmandhātuppabhutayo.

And for `Sakamandhātu` and so on, the final vowel becomes `u` when `sa` or `smiṃ` follow, and `sa` is elided; this is obligatory because the rule is stated again. For example, `Sakamandhātu viya assa rājino vibhavo` (the wealth of this king is like that of Sakamandhātu). The rest is the same. Thus also for `Mahāmandhātu` and so on.

Pitusaddassa bhedo. Simhi āttaṃ, silopo, pitā.

The declension of the word `pitu`. When `si` follows, the substitution `ā` occurs, and `si` is elided, resulting in `pitā`.

Yomhi “āro, rassa”nti ca vattate.

When `yo` follows, the rules for `ārā` and `rassa` are also in force.

168. Pitādīnamasimhi[M 0.0077].

168. For `pitu` and others, when the ending is not `si`.

Pitādīnamārādeso rassamāpajjate asimhi vibhattimhi. Sismiṃ ārādesābhāvepi asimhīti adhikavacanamatthantaraviññāpanatthaṃ, tena toādimhi pitādīnamikāro ca. Yathā – pitito, mātito, bhātito, dhītito, pitipakkho, mātipakkhoti.

For `pitu` and similar words, the `ārā` substitution becomes short when the case ending is not `si`. Even though there is no `ārā` substitution when `si` follows, the additional word `asimhi` is for the purpose of indicating another meaning. By this, when an ending beginning with `to` follows, `i` also occurs for `pitu` and similar words. For example: `pitito`, `mātito`, `bhātito`, `dhītito`, `pitipakkho`, `mātipakkho`.

Pitaro, sesaṃ kattusamaṃ. Bho pita bho pitā, bhavanto pitaro, pitaraṃ, pitare pitaro, pitarā pitunā, pitarehi pitarebhi. Bhāvaniddesena ārādesābhāve pitūhi pitūbhi pituhi pitubhi, pitu pituno pitussa, pitarānaṃ pitānaṃ pitūnaṃ, dīghābhāve pitunaṃ vā, pitarā, pitarehi pitarebhi pitūhi pitūbhi pituhi pitubhi, pitu pituno pitussa, pitarānaṃ pitānaṃ pitūnaṃ pitunaṃ, pitari, pitaresu pitūsu pitusu.

`Pitaro`. The rest is the same as for `kattu`. `Bho pita`, `bho pitā`; `bhavanto pitaro`; `pitaraṃ`; `pitare`, `pitaro`; `pitarā`, `pitunā`; `pitarehi`, `pitarebhi`. In the absence of the `ārā` substitution due to the indication of state: `pitūhi`, `pitūbhi`, `pituhi`, `pitubhi`; `pitu`, `pituno`, `pitussa`; `pitarānaṃ`, `pitānaṃ`, `pitūnaṃ`; or optionally `pitunaṃ` in the absence of the long vowel; `pitarā`; `pitarehi`, `pitarebhi`, `pitūhi`, `pitūbhi`, `pituhi`, `pitubhi`; `pitu`, `pituno`, `pitussa`; `pitarānaṃ`, `pitānaṃ`, `pitūnaṃ`, `pitunaṃ`; `pitari`; `pitaresu`, `pitūsu`, `pitusu`.

Evaṃ bhātā, bhātaro iccādi.

Similarly, `bhātā`, `bhātaro`, and so on.

Ukārantaṃ.

Words ending in '-u'.

Ūkāranto pulliṅgo abhibhūsaddo.

The masculine word 'abhibhū,' ending in '-ū'.

Tatheva syādyuppatti, silopo. So abhibhū, yolope kate te abhibhū.
