Similarly, the arising of 'si' and other endings, with the elision of 'si.' So abhibhū, and when 'yo' is elided, te abhibhū.

“Agho rassa”ntiādinā rassattaṃ, vokāro. Katarassattā attābhāvo. Abhibhuvo, bho abhibhu, bhavanto abhibhū abhibhuvo.

By the rule 'Agho rassa,' etc., there is shortening and the letter 'vo'. Due to which shortening is there no 'atta' substitution? Abhibhuvo, bho abhibhu, bhavanto abhibhū, abhibhuvo.

Katarassattā veādeso na hoti. Sesaṃ bhikkhusaddasamaṃ, rassattameva viseso. Abhibhuṃ, abhibhū abhibhuvo[M 0.0078], abhibhunā, abhibhūhi abhibhūbhi, abhibhuno abhibhussa, abhibhūnaṃ iccādi.

Due to which shortening does the 've' substitution not occur? The rest is similar to the word 'bhikkhu,' only the shortness is the distinction. Abhibhuṃ, abhibhū, abhibhuvo; abhibhunā; abhibhūhi, abhibhūbhi; abhibhuno, abhibhussa; abhibhūnaṃ, etc.

Evaṃ sayambhū, vessabhū, parābhibhū, sahabhūādayo. Sahabhūsaddassa yonaṃ noādesova viseso. Sahabhū, sahabhū sahabhuvo sahabhuno iccādi.

Thus, 'sayambhū,' 'vessabhū,' 'parābhibhū,' 'sahabhū,' etc. For the word 'sahabhū,' the substitution of 'no' for 'yo' is the only distinction. Sahabhū, sahabhū, sahabhuvo, sahabhuno, etc.

Tathā sabbaññūsaddassa yosveva viseso. So sabbaññū te sabbaññū, yolopābhāve rassattaṃ, “lato vokāro cā”ti ettha kāraggahaṇena yonaṃ noādeso. Vādhikārassa vavatthitavibhāsattā na ca vokāro. Sabbaññuno, bho sabbaññu, bhonto sabbaññū sabbaññuno, sabbaññuṃ, sabbaññū sabbaññuno iccādi.

Similarly, for the word 'sabbaññū,' the distinction is only in the 'yo' case. So sabbaññū, te sabbaññū. In the absence of 'yo' elision, there is shortening. By the rule 'lato vokāro cā,' here, by the inclusion of 'kāra,' the 'no' substitution for 'yo' occurs. Due to the established optionality of the 'vā' rule, the 'vo' sound does not occur. Sabbaññuno, bho sabbaññu, bhonto sabbaññū, sabbaññuno; sabbaññuṃ; sabbaññū, sabbaññuno, etc.

Evaṃ maggaññū dhammaññū atthaññū kālaññū rattaññū mattaññū kataññū tathaññū viññū vidū vedagū pāragū iccādayo.

Thus, 'maggaññū,' 'dhammaññū,' 'atthaññū,' 'kālaññū,' 'rattaññū,' 'mattaññū,' 'kataññū,' 'tathaññū,' 'viññū,' 'vidū,' 'vedagū,' 'pāragū,' etc.

Ūkārantaṃ.

Words ending in '-ū'.

Ekāranto appasiddho.

Words ending in '-e' are rare.

Okāranto pulliṅgo gosaddo.

The masculine word 'go,' ending in '-o'.

Tato syādyuppatti, silopo, go gacchati.

From that, the arising of 'si' and other endings, with the elision of 'si.' Go gacchati.

“Gāva se”ti ito “go”ti adhikāro, “āvā”ti ca vattate.

From the rule 'Gāva se,' the governing word is 'go,' and 'āvā' is also stated.

169. Yosu ca.

169. And in the 'yo' case.

Goiccetassa okārassa āvādeso hoti yosu. Casaddena nā smā smiṃsuiccetesu ca. “Tato yonamo tū”ti ettha tuggahaṇena yonamokāro, saralopādi. Gāvo tiṭṭhanti.

For the 'o' vowel of the word 'go,' the 'āvā' substitution occurs in the 'yo' case. And by the word 'ca,' also in 'nā,' 'smā,' and 'smiṃsu'. Here, in the rule 'Tato yonamo tū,' by the inclusion of 'tu', 'yo' becomes 'namokāra,' and vowel elision, etc. Gāvo tiṭṭhanti.

170. Avaṃmhi [M 0.0079] ca.

170. And 'ava' in the 'aṃ' case.

Goiccetassa okārassa āva avaiccete ādesā honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Seddena yo nā sa smāsmiṃsuiccetesu ca avādeso hoti. Gavo gacchanti, he go, he gāvo he gavo.

For the 'o' vowel of the word 'go,' the substitutions 'āva' and 'ava' occur in the 'aṃ' case ending. And by the word 'ca,' the 'ava' substitution also occurs in 'yo,' 'nā,' 'sa,' 'smā,' and 'smiṃsu'. Gavo gacchanti, he go, he gāvo, he gavo.

Dutiyāyaṃ “aṃmhī”ti vattate.

In the second case, 'aṃmhi' is stated.

171. Āvassu vā.

171. For 'āva', 'u' optionally.

Āvaiccetassa gāvādesassa antasarassa ukārādeso hoti vā aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Āvassa a āva, tassa āvasaddantassa. “Aṃmo”tiādinā niggahītaṃ. Gāvuṃ gāvaṃ gavaṃ, gāvo gavo.

For the final vowel of the 'āva' substitution for 'go', the substitution of 'u' occurs optionally in the 'aṃ' case ending. This refers to the 'a' of 'āva', of that word ending in 'āva'. By the rule 'Aṃmo,' etc., a niggahīta is added. Gāvuṃ, gāvaṃ, gavaṃ; gāvo, gavo.

“Goṇa, vā”ti vattate.

'Goṇa,' optionally, is stated.

172. Suhināsu ca.

172. And in 'su,' 'hi,' and 'nā' cases.

Su hi nāiccetesu sabbassa gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā. Casaddena sesesu ca. Goṇo, goṇā, he goṇa he goṇā, goṇaṃ, goṇe, goṇena, goṇehi goṇebhi, goṇassa.

In 'su,' 'hi,' and 'nā,' the 'goṇa' substitution occurs optionally for the entire word 'go.' And by the word 'ca,' also in the remaining cases. Goṇo, goṇā; he goṇa, he goṇā; goṇaṃ; goṇe; goṇena; goṇehi, goṇebhi; goṇassa.

173. Goṇa naṃmhi vā.

173. 'Goṇa' in the 'naṃ' case, optionally.

Sabbassa gosaddassa goṇādeso hoti vā naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Goṇānaṃ, goṇā goṇasmā goṇamhā, goṇehi goṇebhi, goṇassa, goṇānaṃ, goṇe goṇasmiṃ goṇamhi, goṇesu.

The 'goṇa' substitution occurs optionally for the entire word 'go' in the 'naṃ' case ending. Goṇānaṃ; goṇā, goṇasmā, goṇamhā; goṇehi, goṇebhi; goṇassa; goṇānaṃ; goṇe, goṇasmiṃ, goṇamhi; goṇesu.

Goṇādesābhāve gāvena gavena, gohi gobhi.

In the absence of the 'goṇa' substitution: gāvena, gavena; gohi, gobhi.

174. Gāva [M 0.0080] se.

174. Gāva se.

“Go āva se”iti tipadamidaṃ. Gossa o go, gosaddokārassa āvādeso hoti se vibhattimhi. Gāvassa gavassa.

'Go āva se'—this is a three-word rule. For the 'o' of 'go', that is, for the 'o' vowel of the word 'go,' the 'āvā' substitution occurs in the 'se' case ending. Gāvassa, gavassa.

Naṃmhi “go, avā”ti ca vattate.

In the 'naṃ' case, 'go' and 'avā' are also stated.

175. Tato namaṃ patimhālutte ca samāse.

175. From that, in the 'naṃ' case, and in compounds where 'pati' is not elided.

Tato gosaddato parassa naṃvacanassa aṃādeso hoti, gosaddokārassa avādeso ca patimhi pare alutte ca samāse. Casaddena asamāsepi aṃ avādesā. Gavaṃpatissa therassa, gavaṃ.

Following the word 'go', the substitution 'aṃ' occurs for the ending 'naṃ', and the substitution 'ava' occurs for the vowel 'o' of the word 'go' when 'pati' follows and in an unelided compound. By the word 'ca', the 'aṃ' and 'ava' substitutions also occur in a non-compound. Gavaṃpatissa therassa, gavaṃ.

“Suhināsu cā”ti ettha casaddena naṃmhi guādeso. “No ca dvādito naṃmhī”ti sutte casaddena nakārāgamo ca. Gunnaṃgonaṃ vā.

Here, in 'Suhināsu cā,' by the word 'ca,' the substitution 'gu' occurs for 'naṃ'. And in the rule 'No ca dvādito naṃmhī,' by the word 'ca,' the augment 'na' also occurs. Gunnaṃ, gonaṃ, optionally.

Gāvā gāvamhā gāvasmā gavā gavamhā gavasmā, gohi gobhi, gāvassa gavassa, gavaṃ gunnaṃ gonaṃ, gāve gāvamhi gāvasmiṃ gave gavamhi gavasmiṃ, gāvesu gavesu gosu.

Gāvā, gāvamhā, gāvasmā, gavā, gavamhā, gavasmā; gohi, gobhi; gāvassa, gavassa; gavaṃ, gunnaṃ, gonaṃ; gāve, gāvamhi, gāvasmiṃ, gave, gavamhi, gavasmiṃ; gāvesu, gavesu, gosu.

Okārantaṃ.

The section on words ending in 'o' is concluded.

Puriso guṇavā rājā, sā’ggi daṇḍī ca bhikkhu ca;

Satthā’bhibhū ca sabbaññū, goti pulliṅgasaṅgaho.

Man, virtuous one, king, one with fire, staff-bearer, and monk; Teacher, overcomer, and all-knowing one, and 'go'—this is the collection of masculine nouns.

Pulliṅgaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The masculine gender is concluded.

Asmā [M 0.0103] nasmā tasmā namhā tamhā, nehi nebhi tehi tebhi, assa nassa tassa, nesaṃ tesaṃ nesānaṃ tesānaṃ, asmiṃ nasmiṃ tasmiṃ namhi tamhi, nesu tesu.

Asmā, nasmā, tasmā, namhā, tamhā; nehi, nebhi, tehi, tebhi; assa, nassa, tassa; nesaṃ, tesaṃ, nesānaṃ, tesānaṃ; asmiṃ, nasmiṃ, tasmiṃ, namhi, tamhi; nesu, tesu.

Itthiyaṃ “tā si” itīdha sādesasilopā. Sā kaññā, nattaṃ. Nā tā nāyo tāyo, naṃ taṃ, nā tā nāyo tāyo, nāya tāya, nāhi tāhi nābhi tābhi.

In the feminine, for 'tā si', here the substitution 'sā' and the elision of 'si' occur. Sā kaññā, nattaṃ. Nā, tā, nāyo, tāyo; naṃ, taṃ; nā, tā, nāyo, tāyo; nāya, tāya; nāhi, tāhi, nābhi, tābhi.

“Etimāsamī”ti ito etimāggahaṇañca “tassā vā”ti ito taggahaṇañca pañcamiyantavasena vattate “vā”ti ca.

From 'Etimāsamī,' the taking of 'etimā,' and from 'tassā vā,' the taking of 'ta,' continues with the force of an ablative ending, and 'vā' (optionally) also continues.

215. Tato sassa ssāya.

215. Following that, 'sa' becomes 'ssāya'.

Tato tā etā imāto parassa sassa vibhattissa ssāyādeso hoti vā.

Following that, for the case ending 'sa' which comes after 'tā,' 'etā,' or 'imā,' the substitution 'ssāya' occurs optionally.

“Saṃsāsvekavacanesu ca, i”iti ca vattate.

And 'i' also applies in the singular 'saṃ,' 'sā,' and 'su' cases.

216. Tassā vā.

216. Tassā, optionally.

Tāiccetassa itthiyaṃ vattamānassa antassa ikāro hoti vā saṃ sāsvekavacanesu vibhattādesesu. Tissāya tassāya assāya nassāya assā nassā tissā tassā nāya tāya, nāsaṃ tāsaṃ.

For this word 'tā' occurring in the feminine, its final vowel optionally becomes 'i' before the singular case substitutions 'saṃ', 'sā', and 'su'. Tissāya, tassāya, assāya, nassāya; assā, nassā, tissā, tassā; nāya, tāya; nāsaṃ, tāsaṃ.

Pañcamīchaṭṭhīsu tatiyācatutthīsamaṃ. Sattamiyaṃ assaṃ nassaṃ tissaṃ tassaṃ nāyaṃ tāyaṃ, nāsu tāsu.

In the fifth and sixth cases, it is like the third and fourth. In the seventh case: assaṃ, nassaṃ, tissaṃ, tassaṃ, nāyaṃ, tāyaṃ; nāsu, tāsu.

Napuṃsake simhisādesābhāvā nattaṃ. Naṃ taṃ, nāni tāni, naṃ taṃ, nāni tāni, nena tena iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the neuter, due to the absence of the 'sā' substitution for 'si', the form is 'nattaṃ'. Naṃ, taṃ; nāni, tāni; naṃ, taṃ; nāni, tāni; nena, tena, etc., are the same as in the masculine.

Eta si, “etatesaṃ to”ti sakārādeso. Eso puriso, ete, etaṃ, ete iccādi sabbasaddasamaṃ.

For 'eta si,' by the rule 'etatesaṃ to,' the substitution of 's' for 't' occurs. Eso puriso, ete; etaṃ, ete, etc., are the same as for the word 'sabba'.

Itthiyaṃ [M 0.0104] etā si, sādeso. Esā kaññā, etā etāyo, etaṃ, etā etāyo, etāya, etāhi etābhi.

In the feminine, for 'etā si,' the 'sā' substitution occurs. Esā kaññā; etā, etāyo; etaṃ; etā, etāyo; etāya; etāhi, etābhi.

Sa smiṃsu pana “saṃsāsvekavacanesu cā”ti vattate.

But for the 'sa' and 'smiṃ' cases, the rule 'and in the singular 'saṃ,' 'sā,' and 'su' cases' continues to apply.

217. Etimāsami.

217. Etimāsami.

Antāpekkhāyaṃ chaṭṭhī, etā imāiccetesamanto saro ikāro hoti saṃsāsvekavacanesu vibhattādesesu. Sādesagatikattā ssāyādesepi. Casaddādhikārato aññekāsaddādīnamantassa ca.

The genitive case is used in expectation of 'anta' (end). For 'etā' and 'imā,' the final vowel becomes 'i' before the singular case substitutions 'saṃ', 'sā', and 'su'. Because it follows the logic of the 'sā' substitution, this also applies before the 'ssāya' substitution. And from the governing influence of the word 'ca,' it also applies to the final vowel of words such as 'añña,' 'eka,' etc.

Etissāya etissā etāya, etāsaṃ etāsānaṃ, etāya, etāhi etābhi, etissāya etissā etāya, etāsaṃ etāsānaṃ, etissaṃ etāyaṃ, etāsu.

Etissāya, etissā, etāya; etāsaṃ, etāsānaṃ; etāya; etāhi, etābhi; etissāya, etissā, etāya; etāsaṃ, etāsānaṃ; etissaṃ, etāyaṃ; etāsu.

Casaddato aññissā aññāya, aññissaṃ aññāyaṃ. Ekissā ekāya, ekissaṃ ekāyaṃ. Itarissā itarāya, itarissaṃ itarāyaṃ iccādi.

From the word 'ca': aññissā, aññāya; aññissaṃ, aññāyaṃ. Ekissā, ekāya; ekissaṃ, ekāyaṃ. Itarissā, itarāya; itarissaṃ, itarāyaṃ, etc.

Napuṃsake etaṃ, etāni, etaṃ, etāni, sesaṃ ñeyyaṃ.

In the neuter: etaṃ, etāni; etaṃ, etāni. The rest should be understood.

Imasaddassa bhedo. Ima si –

The declension of the word 'ima.' Ima si –

“Sabbassimassā”ti vattate.

The rule 'Sabbassimassā' is carried forward.

218. Anapuṃsakassāyaṃ simhi.

218. This substitution, 'ayaṃ', for the non-neuter, in the 'si' case.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva anapuṃsakassa ayaṃādeso hoti simhi vibhattimhi, silopo. Ayaṃ puriso, ime, imaṃ, ime.

For the entire word 'ima' when it is non-neuter, the substitution 'ayaṃ' occurs for the case ending 'si', and 'si' is elided. Ayaṃ puriso, ime, imaṃ, ime.

219. Animi [M 0.0105] nāmhi ca.

219. And 'ana' and 'imi' in the 'nā' case.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva ana imiādesā honti nāmhi vibhattimhi. Anitthiliṅgassevetaṃ gahaṇaṃ. Anena iminā.

For the entire word 'ima,' the substitutions 'ana' and 'imi' occur for the case ending 'nā'. This rule applies only to the non-feminine gender. Anena, iminā.

“Sunaṃhisū”ti vattate.

‘Sunaṃhisū’ is carried over.

220. Sabbassimasse vā.

220. For the entire stem 'ima', 'e' is substituted optionally.

Sabbassa imasaddassa ekāro hoti vā su naṃ hiiccetesu vacanesu.

For the entire stem 'ima', the letter 'e' optionally occurs before the case endings 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'.

Āppaccayantāniddesā, sabbatthāti avuttato;

Anitthiliṅgassevettha, gahaṇañhi imassiti.

Due to the non-mention of stems ending with the suffix 'ā', and because 'sabbattha' (in all genders) is not stated, here the stem 'ima' is taken only for the non-feminine gender.

Ehi ebhi imehi imebhi.

Ehi, ebhi, imehi, imebhi.

“Sabbassa, vā, sabbattha, sasmāsmiṃsaṃsāsvatta”nti ca vattate.

The rules ‘Sabbassa’, ‘vā’, ‘sabbattha’, and ‘sasmāsmiṃsaṃsāsvatta’ are also carried over.

221. Imasaddassa ca.

221. And of 'ima'.

Imasaddassa ca sabbasseva attaṃ hoti vā sa smā smiṃsaṃ sāiccetesu vacanesu sabbattha liṅgesu.

And for the entire stem 'ima', 'atta' is optionally substituted before the case endings 'sa', 'smā', 'smiṃ', 'saṃ', and 'sā', in all genders.

Assa imassa, esaṃ esānaṃ imesaṃ imesānaṃ, asmā imasmā imamhā, ehi ebhi imehi imebhi, assa imassa, esaṃ esānaṃ imesaṃ imesānaṃ, asmiṃ imasmiṃ imamhi, esu imesu.

Of this, of these, from this, by these, of this, of these, in this, in these.

Itthiyaṃ imā si, ayamādesasilopā.

In the feminine, from `ima` + `si`, there is the substitution of `ayaṃ` and the elision of `si`.

Ayaṃ kaññā, imā imāyo, imaṃ, imā imāyo, imāya, imāhi imābhi. Catutthiyaṃ attaṃ, ikāra- ssāyādesā [M 0.0106] ca, assāya imissāya assā imissā imāya, imāsaṃ imāsānaṃ. Sattamiyaṃ assaṃ imissaṃ imissā vā, “tesu vuddhilopā”dinā smiṃvacanassa vā sādeso. Imāyaṃ, imāsu. Sesaṃ ñeyyaṃ.

‘Ayaṃ kaññā’ (this maiden); ‘imā, imāyo’ (these); ‘imaṃ’ (this); ‘imā, imāyo’ (these); ‘imāya’ (by this); ‘imāhi, imābhi’ (by these). In the fourth case [dative], there is the substitution of ‘atta’ and the substitution of ‘āy’ for the letter ‘i’, [yielding the forms] ‘assāya, imissāya, assā, imissā, imāya’; [and in the plural] ‘imāsaṃ, imāsānaṃ’. In the seventh case [locative], the forms are ‘assaṃ, imissaṃ’, or optionally ‘imissā’. Alternatively, by the rule beginning ‘tesu vuddhilopā’, there is the substitution of ‘sā’ for the case ending ‘smiṃ’. [Other forms are] ‘imāyaṃ’; ‘imāsu’. The rest should be understood.

Napuṃsake ima si, “savibhattissa, vā”ti ca vattate.

In the neuter gender, from `ima` + `si`; and the rule ‘savibhattissa, vā’ (optionally for the whole word with its inflection) is also carried over.

222. Imassidamaṃsisu na puṃsake.

222. For 'ima' in the neuter, 'idaṃ' and 'aṃ' are substituted before the 'si' and 'su' endings.

Napuṃsake vattamānassa sabbasseva imasaddassa savibhattissa idaṃ hoti vā aṃ sisu paresu.

For the entire stem 'ima' with its inflection, when occurring in the neuter, 'idaṃ' and 'aṃ' are optionally substituted when the endings 'si' and 'su' follow.

Idaṃ cittaṃ virocati, imaṃ, imāni, idaṃ pupphaṃ passasi, imaṃ, imāni, anena iminā, ehi ebhi imehi imebhi iccādi pulliṅge viya ñeyyaṃ.

‘Idaṃ cittaṃ virocati’ (this mind shines); ‘imaṃ’ (this), ‘imāni’ (these). ‘Idaṃ pupphaṃ passasi’ (you see this flower); ‘imaṃ’ (this), ‘imāni’ (these). ‘Anena, iminā’ (by this); ‘ehi, ebhi, imehi, imebhi’ (by these), and so forth, should be understood as in the masculine.

Amusaddassa bhedo. Amu si –

The declension of the word 'amu'. From 'amu' + 'si' –

“Vā, anapuṃsakassa, simhī”ti ca vattate.

And the rules ‘vā’ (optionally), ‘anapuṃsakassa’ (for the non-neuter), and ‘simhī’ (before the ‘si’ and ‘hi’ endings) are also carried over.

223. Amussa mo saṃ.

223. For 'amu', 'm' becomes 's'.

Anapuṃsakassa amusaddassa makāro sakāramāpajjate vā simhi pare. Asu rājā.

For the word 'amu', when it is non-neuter, the letter 'm' optionally becomes the letter 's' when 'si' or 'hi' follows. For example: ‘Asu rājā’ (that king).

“Sabbanāmato, vā”ti ca vattate.

The rule ‘Sabbanāmato vā’ is also carried over.

224. Sabbato ko.

224. From all [pronouns], 'ka' [is suffixed].

Sabbato sabbanāmato paro kaiccayamāgamo hoti vā. Puna sabbatoggahaṇena hīnāditopi ko. “Amussa mo sa”nti vinādhikārena yogena kakārepi sādeso.

After every pronoun, the augment 'ka' optionally occurs. Furthermore, by the inclusion of 'sabbato' (from all), the 'ka' augment also follows words such as 'hīna' (inferior), etc. By the application of the rule ‘Amussa mo saṃ’, even without a direct governing rule, the substitution of 's' [for 'm'] also occurs when 'ka' follows.

Asuko[M 0.0107], asukā, asukaṃ. Sādesābhāve amuko, amukā, amukaṃ iccādi.

‘Asuko’ (masc.), ‘asukā’ (fem.), ‘asukaṃ’ (neut.). In the absence of the 's'-substitution: ‘amuko’, ‘amukā’, ‘amukaṃ’, and so forth.

Bahuvacane “lato vokāro cā”ti sutte anuvattamānavāggahaṇena vokāro na hoti, niccaṃ yolopo, dīgho ca.

In the plural, due to the word 'vā' (optionally) being carried over into the sutta ‘lato vokāro cā’, the substitution of 'vo' does not occur. Instead, there is always elision of 'yo' and lengthening of the preceding vowel.

Amū purisā, amuṃ, amū, amunā, amūhi amūbhi amuhi amubhi, amussa. “Amussādu”nti vinādhikārena yogena aduṃādeso, adussa, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ amusaṃ amusānaṃ, amusmā amumhā, amūhi amūbhi amuhi amubhi, amussa adussa, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ amusaṃ amusānaṃ, amusmiṃ amumhi, amūsu amusu.

‘Amū purisā’ (those men); ‘amuṃ’ (that); ‘amū’ (those); ‘amunā’ (by that); ‘amūhi, amūbhi, amuhi, amubhi’ (by those); ‘amussa’ (of that). By application of the rule ‘Amussāduṃ’, even without a direct governing rule, there is the substitution of ‘aduṃ’, yielding ‘adussa’ (of that). [Other forms are:] Gen. Pl.: ‘amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amusaṃ, amusānaṃ’; Abl. Sg.: ‘amusmā, amumhā’; Ins. Pl.: ‘amūhi, amūbhi, amuhi, amubhi’; Dat. Sg.: ‘amussa, adussa’; Dat. Pl.: ‘amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ, amusaṃ, amusānaṃ’; Loc. Sg.: ‘amusmiṃ, amumhi’; Loc. Pl.: ‘amūsu, amusu’.

Itthiyaṃ simhi sādesādi.

In the feminine, when 'si' or 'hi' follows, the 's'-substitution and so forth occur.

Asu kaññā asukā amukā vā, amū amuyo, amuṃ, amū amuyo, amuyā, amūhi amūbhi, amussā amuyā, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ, amuyā, amūhi amūbhi, amussā amuyā, amūsaṃ amūsānaṃ, amussaṃ amuyaṃ amuyā, amūsu.

‘Asu kaññā’ (that maiden), or ‘asukā’, ‘amukā’. [Other forms are:] ‘amū, amuyo’; ‘amuṃ’; ‘amū, amuyo’; ‘amuyā’; ‘amūhi, amūbhi’; ‘amussā, amuyā’; ‘amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ’; ‘amuyā’; ‘amūhi, amūbhi’; ‘amussā, amuyā’; ‘amūsaṃ, amūsānaṃ’; ‘amussaṃ, amuyaṃ, amuyā’; ‘amūsu’.

Napuṃsake amusi. “Savibhattissa”, imassidamiccādito “aṃsisu napuṃsake”ti ca vattate.

In the neuter: from `amu` + `si`. The rules ‘Savibhattissa’ and ‘aṃsisu napuṃsake’ (from the rule beginning ‘Imassidamaṃsisu’) are also carried over.

225. Amussāduṃ.

225. For 'amu', 'aduṃ' [is substituted].

Napuṃsake vattamānassa sabbasseva amusaddassa savibhattissa aduṃ hoti aṃsisu paresu. Aduṃ pupphaṃ, amū amūni, aduṃ, amū amūni, amunā iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

For the entire word 'amu' with its inflection, when occurring in the neuter, 'aduṃ' is substituted when the endings 'aṃ', 'si', or 'su' follow. For example: ‘Aduṃ pupphaṃ’ (that flower); ‘amū, amūni’; ‘aduṃ’; ‘amū, amūni’; ‘amunā’, and so forth, are the same as in the masculine.

Kiṃsaddassa bhedo. “Kiṃ si” itīdha –

The declension of the word 'kiṃ'. Here, in the case of 'kiṃ si' –

“Kissa [M 0.0108] ka ve cā”ti ito “kissa, ka”iti ca vattate.

From the rule 'Kissa ka ve ca', 'kissa' and 'ka' are also carried forward.

226. Sesesu ca.

226. And in the remaining cases.

Kimiccetassa kasaddo ādeso hoti vappaccayato sesesu vibhattibhedesu. Ettha ca “kissa ka ve cā”ti sutte casaddena vappaccayāvasiṭṭha thamādippaccayānaṃ gahitattā sesaggahaṇena vibhattiyova gayhante. Caggahaṇaṃ katthaci nivattanatthaṃ, tena “kissa, kismi”ntiādi ca sijjhati. “So”ti sissa o, saralopādi.

For this 'kiṃ', the word 'ka' is the substitute in the remaining types of inflections after the 'va' suffix. And here, in the rule 'kissa ka ve ca', since the word 'ca' includes the suffixes beginning with 'tha' that remain after the 'va' suffix, by the term 'sesa', only the inflections are to be understood. The inclusion of 'ca' is for preventing the substitution in some cases; thereby, forms such as 'kissa' and 'kismiṃ' are also accomplished. 'So' is formed by the substitution of 'o' for 'si', vowel elision, and so forth.

Ko eso, ke, kaṃ, ke, kena, kehi kebhi, kassa kissa, niggahītalopādi, kesaṃ kesānaṃ, kasmā kamhā, kehi kebhi, kassa kissa, kesaṃ kesānaṃ, kasmiṃ kismiṃ kamhi kimhi, kesu.

Ko eso, ke, kaṃ, ke, kena, kehi, kebhi, kassa, kissa (with elision of the niggahīta, etc.), kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kasmā, kamhā, kehi, kebhi, kassa, kissa, kesaṃ, kesānaṃ, kasmiṃ, kismiṃ, kamhi, kimhi, kesu.

Itthiyaṃ “kiṃ si”itīdha “sesesu cā”ti vibhattiyaṃ parāyaṃ kādese kate “itthiyamato āppaccayo”ti majjhe āppaccayo, silopo.

In the feminine, here in the case of 'kiṃ si', when the substitution 'ka' is made for the following inflection by 'sesesu ca', the 'āp' suffix is inserted in the middle by the rule 'itthiyamato āppaccayo', and 'si' is elided.

Kā esā kaññā, kā kāyo, kaṃ, kā kāyo iccādi sabbāsaddasamaṃ.

Kā esā kaññā; kā, kāyo; kaṃ; kā, kāyo; and so on, similar to the word 'sabbā'.

Napuṃsake kiṃ si, lopavidhissa balavatarattā paṭhamaṃ silope kate puna vibhattiparattābhāvā, “tadanuparodhenā”ti paribhāsato vā kādesābhāvo. Kiṃ etaṃ, kāni.

In the neuter gender, for 'kiṃ si', because the rule of elision is stronger, 'si' is first elided. Then, due to the absence of a following inflection, or alternatively, due to the maxim 'tadanuparodhena', there is no 'ka' substitution. Kiṃ etaṃ, kāni.

Dutiyekavacane “kvaci lopa”nti niggahītalope kate “aṃmo niggahītaṃ jhalapehī”ti niggahītaṃ. Kiṃ, kāni iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the accusative singular, when the elision of the niggahīta has been done according to 'kvaci lopa', the niggahīta is formed according to 'aṃmo niggahītaṃ jhalapehī'. Kiṃ, kāni; the remaining cases are similar to the masculine.

Ekasaddo [M 0.0109] saṅkhyātulyāsahāyaññavacano. Yadā saṅkhyāvacano, tadā sabbatthekavacanantova, aññattha bahuvacanantopi. Eko, ekā, ekaṃ iccādi sabbattha sabbasaddasamaṃ. Saṃsāsveva viseso.

The word 'eka' denotes number, similarity, solitude, and otherness. When it denotes number, it is always in the singular; elsewhere, it can also be in the plural. 'Eko', 'ekā', 'ekaṃ', etc., are in all respects similar to the word 'sabba'. The difference is only in certain cases.

Ubhasaddo dvisaddapariyāyo, sadā bahuvacanantova.

The word 'ubha' is a synonym for the word 'dvi', and is always in the plural.

“Ubha yo” itīdha “tato yonamo tū”ti ettha tuggahaṇena kvaci yonamokāro. Ubho purisāubhe vā, ubho purise ubhe. Su hisu “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā kvaci ekārassokāro. Ubhohi ubhobhi ubhehi ubhebhi.

Here, in the case of 'ubha yo', by the inclusion of 'tu' in the rule 'tato yonamo tū', the substitution for 'yo' and 'naṃ' optionally becomes 'o'. Ubho purisā or ubhe; ubho purise, ubhe. Before 'su' and 'hi', by 'tesu vuddhī' and so on, 'e' optionally becomes 'o'. Ubhohi, ubhobhi, ubhehi, ubhebhi.

227. Ubhādito naminnaṃ.

227. After 'ubha' and so on, 'innaṃ' for 'naṃ'.

Ubhaiccevamādito naṃvacanassa innaṃ hoti.

After 'ubha' and so on, the 'naṃ' ending becomes 'innaṃ'.

Ubhinnaṃ, ubhohi ubhobhi ubhehi ubhebhi, ubhinnaṃ, ubhosu ubhesu.

Ubhinnaṃ, ubhohi, ubhobhi, ubhehi, ubhebhi, ubhinnaṃ, ubhosu, ubhesu.

Dviādayo saṅkhyāsaṅkhyeyyavacanā, bahūnaṃ vācitattā sadā bahuvacanantāva.

The words 'dvi' and so on denote number and the numbered; and because they denote a multitude, they are always in the plural.

“Dvi yo”itīdha “savibhattissa, itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhya”nti ca adhikāro.

Here, in the case of 'dvi yo', the governing rules 'savibhattissa' and 'itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhya' also apply.

228. Yosu dvinnaṃ dve ca.

228. Before 'yo' suffixes, for 'dvi', 'dve' and...

Dviiccetassa saṅkhyāsaddassa itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānassa savibhattissa dveiccādeso hoti yosu paresu. Casaddena duve ca, kvaci duvi ca naṃmhi. Bahuvacanuccāraṇaṃ dvisaddato [M 0.0110] bahuvacanameva hotīti ñāpanatthaṃ. Dve dhammā, dve itthiyo, dve rūpāni, duve vā, evaṃ dutiyāyampi, dvīhi dvībhi.

For this numeral word 'dvi', existing in feminine, masculine, and neuter, together with its inflection, the substitute 'dve' occurs when the 'yo' suffixes follow. By the word 'ca', 'duve' also occurs, and sometimes 'duvi' before 'naṃ'. The utterance of the plural is to make known that from the word 'dvi' only the plural occurs. Dve dhammā, dve itthiyo, dve rūpāni, or duve; similarly in the accusative also; dvīhi, dvībhi.

Naṃmhi dīghe sampatte –

When lengthening is due before the 'naṃ' suffix –

229. No ca dvādito naṃmhi.

229. And for 'dvi' and so on, there is no lengthening before 'naṃ'.

Dviiccevamādito saṅkhyāto nakārāgamo hoti naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Casaddaggahaṇena itthiyaṃ ti ca tusaddato ssañcāgamo naṃmhi vibhattimhi. Dvinnaṃ duvinnaṃ vā, dvīhi dvībhi, dvinnaṃ duvinnaṃ, dvīsu.

From the numeral 'dvi' and so on, the 'na' augment occurs before the 'naṃ' inflection. By the inclusion of the word 'ca', and for 'ti' in the feminine, and from the word 'tu', the 'ssa' augment also occurs before the 'naṃ' inflection. Dvinnaṃ or duvinnaṃ; dvīhi, dvībhi; dvinnaṃ, duvinnaṃ; dvīsu.

Tisaddassa bhedo. “Ti yo”itīdha

The declension of the word 'ti'. Here, in the case of 'ti yo' –

Yolope sampatte

When the elision of 'yo' is due –

“Yosū”ti vattate.

The rule 'yosu' applies.

230. Ti catunnaṃ tisso catasso tayocattārotīṇi cattāri.

230. For 'ti' and 'catu', the substitutes are 'tisso', 'catasso', 'tayo', 'cattāro', 'tīṇi', and 'cattāri'.

Ti catunnaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ tisso catasso tayo cattārotīṇi cattāriiccete ādesā honti yosu paresu. Tayo purisā, tayo purise passa, tīhi tībhi.

For the numerals 'ti' and 'catu', existing in feminine, masculine, and neuter, together with their inflections, the substitutes 'tisso', 'catasso', 'tayo', 'cattāro', 'tīṇi', and 'cattāri' occur respectively when the 'yo' suffixes follow. Tayo purisā; tayo purise passa; tīhi, tībhi.

“Na”miti vattate.

The rule concerning 'naṃ' applies.

231. Iṇṇamiṇṇannaṃ tīhi saṅkhyāhi.

231. After the numeral 'ti', 'iṇṇaṃ' and 'iṇṇannaṃ' for 'naṃ'.

Tiiccetasmā saṅkhyāsaddā parassa naṃvacanassa iṇṇaṃ iṇṇannaṃiccete ādesā honti, saralopādi. Tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ, tīhi tībhi, tiṇṇaṃ tiṇṇannaṃ, tīsu.

After this numeral 'ti', for the following 'naṃ' ending, the substitutions are 'iṇṇaṃ' and 'iṇṇannaṃ', with vowel elision and so on. Tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ; tīhi, tībhi; tiṇṇaṃ, tiṇṇannaṃ; tīsu.

Itthiyaṃ [M 0.0111] tisso itthiyo, tisso, tīhi tībhi, naṃmhi ssañcāgamo, tissannaṃ, ssaṃbyavadhānato iṇṇābhāvo, sesaṃ samaṃ.

In the feminine: tisso itthiyo, tisso; tīhi, tībhi. Before the suffix naṃ, the augment ssañ is inserted, forming tissannaṃ. Due to the intervention of ssaṃ, the substitution of iṇṇa does not occur. The rest is the same.

Napuṃsake tīṇi, tīṇi. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the neuter: tīṇi, tīṇi. The rest is the same as in the masculine.

Tathā catusaddassapi yosu “ticatunna”ntiādinā yathāvuttādeso, “tato yonamo tū”ti ettha tusaddena kvaci okāro ca. Cattāro caturo vā, cattāro caturo, catūhi catūbhi catubbhi, catunnaṃ, nakārāgamo. Catūhi catūbhi catubbhi, catunnaṃ, catūsu.

Likewise, for the word catu before the yo suffixes, the substitution stated in the rule beginning ticatunnaṃ occurs. And here, in the rule tato yonamo tū, by the word tu, the vowel o also optionally occurs. The forms are: cattāro or caturo; cattāro, caturo; catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi; catunnaṃ, with the augment na; catūhi, catūbhi, catubbhi; catunnaṃ; catūsu.

Itthiyaṃ catasso, catasso, naṃmhi ssañcāgamo, “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā caturukārassa akāro. Catassannaṃ. Sesaṃ samaṃ.

In the feminine: catasso, catasso. Before the suffix naṃ, the augment ssañ is inserted. By the rule beginning tesu vuddhī, the u of catu becomes a, forming catassannaṃ. The rest is the same.

Napuṃsake cattāri, cattāri. Sesaṃ pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the neuter: cattāri, cattāri. The rest is the same as in the masculine.

Tathā –

Likewise –

Nīlādiguṇanāmañca, bahubbīhi ca taddhitaṃ;

Sāmaññavutyatītādi-kitantaṃ vāccaliṅgikaṃ.

A name of a quality such as 'blue'; a bahubbīhi compound; a taddhita derivative; a word ending in a kita suffix, such as a common noun or a past participle—these are adjectival in gender.

Etthedaṃ vuccate –

Herein, it is said:

Ese’so etamiti ca,

Pasiddhi atthesu yesu lokassa;

Thīpunnapuṃsakāniti,

Vuccante tāni nāmāni.

Those names which are established in the world with certain meanings, such as ese, eso, and etaṃ, are designated as feminine, masculine, and neuter.

Tiliṅgaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The section on the three genders is concluded.

Aliṅganāma

Nouns without Gender

Athāliṅgesu [M 0.0112] nāmesu tumhamhasaddā vuccante.

Now, among the nouns without gender, the words tumha and amha will be explained.

Tesaṃ panāliṅgattā tīsu liṅgesu samānarūpaṃ. “Tumhamha”iti ṭhite syādyuppatti.

However, due to their being without gender, their form is the same in all three genders. When tumha and amha stand as the bases, the case endings, beginning with si, are generated.

“Savibhattīnaṃ, tumhamhāka”nti adhikāro.

The governing rule is: savibhattīnaṃ tumhamhākaṃ.

232. Tvamahaṃ simhi ca.

232. When si follows, tvaṃ and ahaṃ are substituted; and also...

Sabbesaṃ tumhaamhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ tvaṃahaṃiccete ādesā honti simhi vibhattimhi. Casaddena tumhassa tuvañca hoti. Tvaṃ pumā, tvaṃ itthī, tvaṃ napuṃsakaṃ, tuvaṃ satthā vā. Ahaṃ pumā, ahaṃ itthī, ahaṃ napuṃsakaṃ.

For the entire words tumha and amha together with their case endings, the substitutes tvaṃ and ahaṃ respectively occur when the case ending si follows. By the word ca, tuvaṃ also occurs as a substitute for tumha. For example: tvaṃ pumā (you, a man), tvaṃ itthī (you, a woman), tvaṃ napuṃsakaṃ (you, a neuter being), or tuvaṃ satthā (you, the teacher). Ahaṃ pumā (I, a man), ahaṃ itthī (I, a woman), ahaṃ napuṃsakaṃ (I, a neuter being).

Bahuvacane “sabbanāmakārate paṭhamo”ti ekāro. Tumhe tiṭṭhatha, bhiyyo amhe mahemase.

In the plural, by the rule sabbanāmakārate paṭhamo, the vowel e is substituted for the case ending. For example: tumhe tiṭṭhatha (you stand); bhiyyo amhe mahemase (may we further honor us).

“Amhassā”ti vattate.

The rule amhassa is carried forward.

233. Mayaṃ yomhi paṭhame.

233. Mayaṃ is substituted when the nominative plural yo follows.

Sabbassa amhasaddassa savibhattissa mayaṃādeso hoti yomhi paṭhame. Mayaṃ gacchāma.

For the entire word amha together with its case ending, the substitute mayaṃ occurs when the nominative plural yo follows. For example: mayaṃ gacchāma (we go).

Ettha ca ekasmimpi gāravabahumānena bahuttasamāropā bahuvacanaṃ hoti.

And here, the plural is used even for a single individual by superimposing plurality out of respect and high regard.

“Aṃmhī”ti vattate.

The rule aṃmhi is carried forward.

234. Tavaṃ mamañca navā.

234. Tavaṃ and mamaṃ are substituted, optionally.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tavaṃ mamaṃiccete ādesā honti navā yathākkamaṃ aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Tavaṃ, mamaṃ passa.

For the entire words tumha and amha together with their case endings, the substitutes tavaṃ and mamaṃ occur optionally and respectively when the case ending aṃ follows. For example: tavaṃ passa (see you), mamaṃ passa (see me).

235. Taṃ [M 0.0113] mamaṃmhi.

235. Taṃ and maṃ are substituted when aṃ follows.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ taṃ maṃiccete ādesā honti yathākkamaṃ aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Taṃ, maṃ.

For the entire words tumha and amha together with their case endings, the substitutes taṃ and maṃ occur respectively when the case ending aṃ follows. The forms are: taṃ, maṃ.

236. Tumhassa tuvaṃ tvamaṃmhi.

236. For tumha, the substitutes are tuvaṃ and tvaṃ when aṃ follows.

Sabbassa tumhasaddassa savibhattissa tuvaṃtvaṃiccete ādesā honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Tuvaṃ tvaṃ.

For the entire word tumha together with its case ending, the substitutes tuvaṃ and tvaṃ occur when the case ending aṃ follows. The forms are: tuvaṃ, tvaṃ.

Bahuvacane “tumhamhehi, āka”nti ca vattate.

In the plural, the rule tumhamhehi ākaṃ is also carried forward.

237. Vā yvappaṭhamo.

237. Optionally, when the accusative plural yo follows.

Tumhamhehi paro appaṭhamo yo ākaṃ hoti vā. Tumhākaṃ passāmi, tumhe passāmi, amhākaṃ passasi, amhe passasi.

After `tumha` and `amha`, for the non-nominative plural ending `yo`, the substitute `ākaṃ` optionally occurs. Examples: `Tumhākaṃ passāmi` or `tumhe passāmi` (I see you all); `amhākaṃ passasi` or `amhe passasi` (you see us).

238. Nāmhi tayā mayā.

238. When the inflection `nā` follows, the substitutes are `tayā` and `mayā`.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tayā mayāiccete ādesā honti yathākkamaṃ nāmhi vibhattimhi.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, these substitutes `tayā` and `mayā` occur respectively when the inflection `nā` follows.

239. Tayātayīnaṃ takāro tvattaṃ vā.

239. Of `tayā` and `tayi`, the letter `t` optionally becomes `tva`.

Tayā tayiiccetesaṃ takāro tvattamāpajjate vā. Tvayā tayā, mayā, tumhehi tumhebhi, amhehi amhebhi.

Of these, `tayā` and `tayi`, the letter `t` optionally becomes `tva`. Examples: `tvayā`, `tayā`; `mayā`; `tumhehi`, `tumhebhi`; `amhehi`, `amhebhi`.

“Sasmiṃ, vā”ti vattate.

The terms `sa`, `smiṃ`, and `vā` are carried forward.

240. Sassaṃ.

240. For `sa`, `aṃ`.

Tumhamhehi sassa vibhattissa amādeso hoti vā. Tumhaṃ, amhaṃ dīyate.

After `tumha` and `amha`, for the inflection `sa`, the substitute `aṃ` optionally occurs. Examples: `Tumhaṃ dīyate`, `amhaṃ dīyate` (it is given to you, it is given to us).

241. Tava [M 0.0114] mama se.

241. `Tava` and `mama` when `sa` follows.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ tavamamaiccete ādesā honti se vibhattimhi, vikappenāyaṃ vijjhantarassa vijjamānattā.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, these substitutes `tava` and `mama` occur respectively when the inflection `sa` follows. This is by option, due to the existence of another rule.

“Se”ti vattate.

The term `se` is carried forward.

242. Tuyhaṃ mayhañca.

242. And also `tuyhaṃ` and `mayhaṃ`.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ yathākkamaṃ tuyhaṃmayhaṃiccete ādesā ca honti se vibhattimhi. Tava, mama tuyhaṃ, mayhaṃ vā dīyate.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, these substitutes `tuyhaṃ` and `mayhaṃ` also occur respectively when the inflection `sa` follows. Example: `Tava, mama, tuyhaṃ, or mayhaṃ dīyate` (it is given to you/me).

243. Amhassa mamaṃ savibhattissa se.

243. For `amha` with its inflection, `mamaṃ` is the substitute when `sa` follows.

Sabbasseva amhasaddassa savibhattissa mamaṃādeso hoti se vibhattimhi. Mamaṃ dīyate.

For the entire word `amha` with its inflection, the substitute `mamaṃ` occurs when the inflection `sa` follows. Example: `Mamaṃ dīyate` (it is given to me).

“Sassa”nti ito sīhagatiyā “a”miti vattate.

From the rule `sassaṃ`, the term `aṃ` is carried forward by the 'lion's leap' method.

244. Tumhamhehi namākaṃ.

244. After `tumha` and `amha`, for `naṃ`, `ākaṃ`.

Tumhamhehi parassa naṃvacanassa ākamiccādeso hoti, añca. “Tesu vuddhī”tiādinā amhassa kvaci asmādeso. Tumhaṃ tumhākaṃ, amhaṃ amhākaṃ asmākaṃ vā.

For the ending `naṃ` that follows `tumha` and `amha`, the substitute `ākaṃ` occurs, and also `aṃ`. By the rule `tesu vuddhī`, etc., the substitute `asmā` sometimes occurs for `amha`. Thus, optionally: `tumhaṃ`, `tumhākaṃ`; `amhaṃ`, `amhākaṃ`, `asmākaṃ`.

Pañcamiyaṃ “amhatumhanturāja”iccādinā smāvacanassa nābhāvātideso. Tayā, mayā apeti, tumhehi, amhehi tumhebhi amhebhi, tumhaṃ amhaṃ tava mama, tuyhaṃ, mayhaṃ mamaṃ pariggaho, tumhaṃ tumhākaṃ, amhaṃ amhākaṃ asmākaṃ dhammatā.

In the ablative, by the rule `amhatumhanturāja`, etc., there is an extended application of the substitution for `nā` to the ending `smā`. Examples: `Tayā, mayā apeti` (departs from you, from me); (instrumental) `tumhehi, amhehi, tumhebhi, amhebhi`; (genitive) `tumhaṃ, amhaṃ, tava, mama, tuyhaṃ, mayhaṃ, mamaṃ pariggaho` (your/my possession); `tumhaṃ, tumhākaṃ, amhaṃ, amhākaṃ, asmākaṃ dhammatā` (your/our nature).

“Smiṃmhī”ti vattate.

The term `smiṃmhi` is carried forward.

245. Tumhamhākaṃ [M 0.0115] tayi mayi.

245. For `tumha` and `amha`, `tayi` and `mayi`.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ tayi mayiiccete ādesā honti yathākkamaṃ smiṃmhi vibhattimhi. Takārassa tvattaṃ. Tvayi tayi mayi, tumhesu amhesu.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, these substitutes `tayi` and `mayi` occur respectively when the inflections `smiṃ` or `mhi` follow. The `t` of `tayi` can become `tva`. Examples: `tvayi`, `tayi`, `mayi`; (plural) `tumhesu`, `amhesu`.

Tesaṃ eva tumha amhasaddānaṃ padato paresaṃ kvaci ādesantaravidhāne rūpabhedo.

For these same words `tumha` and `amha`, when they follow another word, a difference of form occurs in certain cases due to the prescription of other substitutes.

“Navā”ti adhikāro.

`Na vā` (optionally) is the governing rule.

246. Padato dutiyācatutthīchaṭṭhīsu vo no.

246. After a word, in the accusative, dative, and genitive cases, the substitutes are `vo` and `no`.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ padasmā paresaṃ vo noādesā honti yathākkamaṃ dutiyācatutthīchaṭṭhīsu bahuvacanesu navā. Ettha ca “ekavacanesū”ti vakkhamānattā “bahuvacanesū”ti laddhaṃ. Pahāya vo gamissāmi, mā no ajja vikantiṃsu, dhammaṃ vo bhikkhave desissāmi, saṃvibhajetha no rajjena, tuṭṭhosmi vo pakatiyā, satthā no bhagavā anuppatto.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, when they follow another word, the substitutes `vo` and `no` occur optionally and respectively in the accusative, dative, and genitive plurals. And here, because 'in the singulars' will be stated later, 'in the plurals' is understood. Examples: `Pahāya vo gamissāmi` (I will go, having left you); `mā no ajja vikantiṃsu` (let them not harm us today); `dhammaṃ vo bhikkhave desissāmi` (I will teach you the Dhamma, O monks); `saṃvibhajetha no rajjena` (share the kingdom with us); `tuṭṭhosmi vo pakatiyā` (I am pleased with your nature); `satthā no bhagavā anuppatto` (the Blessed One, our Teacher, has arrived).

Navāti kiṃ? Bhayaṃ tumhāka no siyā, eso amhākaṃ satthā.

Why `na vā`? Examples: `Bhayaṃ tumhākaṃ no siyā` (May there be no fear for you); `eso amhākaṃ satthā` (this is our teacher).

“Padato, catutthīchaṭṭhīsū”ti vattate.

The terms `padato` and `catutthīchaṭṭhīsu` are carried forward.

247. Temekavacanesu ca.

247. And `te` and `me` in the singulars.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ padasmā paresaṃ te meādesā honti yathākkamaṃ catutthīchaṭṭhīsu ekavacanesu [M 0.0116] navā. Dadāmi te gāmavarāni pañca, dadāhi me gāmavaraṃ, idaṃ te raṭṭhaṃ, ayaṃ me putto.

For all the words `tumha` and `amha` with their inflections, when they follow another word, the substitutes `te` and `me` occur optionally and respectively in the dative and genitive singulars. Examples: `Dadāmi te gāmavarāni pañca` (I give you five excellent villages); `dadāhi me gāmavaraṃ` (give me an excellent village); `idaṃ te raṭṭhaṃ` (this is your kingdom); `ayaṃ me putto` (this is my son).

Navāti kiṃ? Idaṃ cīvaraṃ tuyhaṃ vikappanatthāya dammi, suṇātha vacanaṃ mama.

Why the word 'navā'? 'I give this robe to you for the purpose of assignment; listen to my word.'

Navādhikārato cettha,

Vo no te meti ye ime;

Pādādo ca ca vā evā-

Diyoge ca na honti te.

And here, from the governing rule 'navā', these substitutes 'vo, no, te, me' do not occur at the beginning of a line of verse, nor in conjunction with particles such as 'ca', 'vā', and 'eva'.

Yathā –

For example:

Na socāmi na rodāmi, tava sutvāna māṇava;

Tuyhañcāpi mahārāja, mayhañca raṭṭhavaḍḍhana.

I do not grieve, nor do I weep, having heard from you, O young man; and for you too, O great king, and for me, O promoter of the kingdom.

Evamidaṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ sandhāvitaṃ saṃsaritaṃ mamañceva tumhākañcāti.

Thus for a long time has this running on and transmigrating occurred for me as well as for you.

Padatoti kiṃ? Tava ñāti, mama ñāti.

Why the specification 'after a word'? 'Your kinsman'; 'my kinsman'.

“Te me”ti vattate.

'Te me' is carried forward.

248. Na aṃmhi.

248. Not when 'aṃ' follows.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ padasmā paresaṃ te meādesā na honti aṃmhi vibhattimhi. Passeyya taṃ vassasataṃ ārogyaṃ. So mamabravīti.

For all the words 'tumha' and 'amha' with their inflections, when they follow another word, the substitutes 'te' and 'me' do not occur when the accusative singular inflection 'aṃ' follows. For example: 'May he see you healthy for a hundred years'; 'He said to me'.

“Temekavacane”ti vattate.

'Te, me, in the singular' is carried forward.

249. Vā tatiye ca.

249. And optionally in the instrumental.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ padasmā paresaṃ te me ādesā honti vā yathākkamaṃ tatiyekavacane pare[M 0.0117]. Kataṃ te pāpaṃ, kataṃ tayā pāpaṃ, kataṃ me puññaṃ, kataṃ mayā puññaṃ.

For all the words 'tumha' and 'amha' with their inflections, when they follow another word, the substitutes 'te' and 'me' occur optionally and respectively when the instrumental singular follows. For example: 'kataṃ te pāpaṃ' or 'kataṃ tayā pāpaṃ' (evil was done by you); 'kataṃ me puññaṃ' or 'kataṃ mayā puññaṃ' (merit was done by me).

“Vā, tatiye”ti ca vattate.

And 'vā' and 'tatiye' are carried forward.

250. Bahuvacanesu vo no.

250. In the plurals, 'vo' and 'no'.

Sabbesaṃ tumha amhasaddānaṃ savibhattīnaṃ padasmā paresaṃ vo noādesā honti vā yathākkamaṃ tatiyābahuvacane pare. Kataṃ vo kammaṃ, kataṃ no kammaṃ.

For all the words 'tumha' and 'amha' with their inflections, when they follow another word, the substitutes 'vo' and 'no' occur optionally and respectively when the instrumental plural follows. For example: 'kataṃ vo kammaṃ' (work done by you); 'kataṃ no kammaṃ' (work done by us).

Bahuvacananiddesena kvaci yomhi paṭhame ca vo no honti. Gāmaṃ vo gaccheyyātha, gāmaṃ no gaccheyyāma.

By the specification 'in the plurals', 'vo' and 'no' sometimes also occur in the nominative plural. For example: 'gāmaṃ vo gaccheyyātha' (You should go to the village); 'gāmaṃ no gaccheyyāma' (we should go to the village).

Tathā pañcādīnamaṭṭhārasantānaṃ, katisaddassa cāliṅgattā tiliṅgepi samānarūpaṃ, aliṅgattā eva pañcādito itthippaccayābhāvo.

Similarly, for the numbers from five to eighteen and for the word 'kati', because they are without gender, the form is the same in all three genders. It is precisely because they are without gender that from five onwards there is no feminine suffix.

“Pañca yo”itīdha –

Here, in the case of 'pañca' + 'yo':

“Yosu dvinnaṃ dve cā”ti ito “yosū”ti vattate, “itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhya”nti ca.

From the rule 'yosu dvinnaṃ dve ca', the term 'yosu' is carried forward, and also 'itthipumanapuṃsakasaṅkhyaṃ'.

251. Pañcādīnamakāro.

251. For the numbers from five onwards, the final vowel becomes 'a'.

Antāpekkhāyaṃ chaṭṭhī, pañcādīnaṃ aṭṭhārasantānaṃ saṅkhyānaṃ itthipumanapuṃsake vattamānānamantassa savibhattissa akāro hoti yosu paresu. Ā eādesāpavādoyaṃ, pañcakkhandhā, pañca gatiyo, pañca indriyāni. Evaṃ dutiyāyañca.

The genitive case is used with reference to the end of the word. For the numbers from five to eighteen, when referring to the feminine, masculine, or neuter, the end of the word together with its inflection becomes 'a' when the plural ending 'yo' follows. This is an exception to the substitutions 'ā' and 'e'. For example: 'pañcakkhandhā' (five aggregates), 'pañca gatiyo' (five destinies), 'pañca indriyāni' (five faculties). And similarly in the accusative.

“Sunaṃhisū”ti vattate.

'Su, naṃ, hi, su' is carried forward.

252. Pañcādīnamattaṃ.

252. For the numbers from five onwards, the final vowel becomes short 'a'.

Pañcādīnamaṭṭhārasantānaṃ saṅkhyānamanto attamāpajjate su naṃ hiiccetesu paresu. Ettadīghāpavādoyaṃ. Pañcahi pañcabhi[M 0.0118], pañcannaṃ, pañcahi pañcabhi, pañcannaṃ, pañcasu. Evaṃ cha sa tta aṭṭhanava dasasaddā.

The final vowel of the numbers from five to eighteen becomes short 'a' when these endings follow: 'su', 'naṃ', and 'hi'. This is an exception to the lengthening to 'e'. For example: 'pañcahi' or 'pañcabhi' (by/from five); 'pañcannaṃ' (of five); 'pañcasu' (in/among five). Similarly for the words six, seven, eight, nine, and ten.

“Ekañca dasa cā”ti atthe dvandasamāse, “ekena adhikā dasā”ti atthe tappurise vā kate

When a dvanda compound is formed in the sense 'one and ten', or when a tatpurisa compound is formed in the sense 'ten increased by one':

“Saṅkhyāne”ti vattate.

'Saṅkhyāne' is carried forward.

253. Dvekaṭṭhānamākāro vā.

253. For 'dvi', 'eka', and 'aṭṭha', the final vowel optionally becomes 'ā'.

Dviekaaṭṭhaiccetesamanto ākāro hoti vā saṅkhyāne uttarapade pare. Vavatthitavibhāsāyaṃ. Ekādasa, dvādasa, aṭṭhārasa.

The final vowel of these words—'dvi', 'eka', and 'aṭṭha'—optionally becomes 'ā' when a subsequent member of a numerical compound follows. This is a restricted option. For example: 'ekādasa' (eleven), 'dvādasa' (twelve), 'aṭṭhārasa' (eighteen).

Saṅkhyāneti kimatthaṃ? Ekadanto, dvidanto, aṭṭhatthambho.

Why the specification 'in a numerical compound'? For example: 'ekadanto' (one-tusked), 'dvidanto' (two-tusked), 'aṭṭhatthambho' (eight-pillared).

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' is carried forward.

254. Ekādito dassa ra saṅkhyāne.

254. In counting, after eka, etc., the d of dasa becomes r.

Ekādito saṅkhyāto parassa dasassa ādissa dassa rakāro hoti vā saṅkhyāne. Sesaṃ samaṃ. Ekārasa, ekādasa.

After a number from eka onwards, the initial d of dasa is optionally replaced by r in a numerical compound. The rest is the same. Ekārasa, ekādasa.

Dve ca dasa ca, dvīhi vā adhikā dasāti dvidasa itīdha –

In the case of dvidasa, meaning 'two and ten' or 'ten increased by two':

“Vā”ti vattate.

Vā is carried forward.

255. Vīsatidasesu bā dvissa tu.

255. But for dvi, bā is substituted when vīsati or dasa follow.

Vīsati dasaiccetesu paresu dvisaddassa bā hoti vā. Tusaddena tiṃsāyampi. Rakāro, āttañca. Bārasa, dvādasa.

For the word dvi, bā is optionally substituted when vīsati or dasa follow. By the word tu, this also applies when tiṃsā follows. The substitution of r and the lengthening to ā also apply. Bārasa, dvādasa.

Tayo ca dasa ca, tīhi vā adhikā dasāti terasa. Ettha “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā tisaddassa teādeso ānavutiyā.

Three and ten, or ten plus three, thus terasa. Here, by the rule “tesu vuddhī” and so forth, for the word ti, te is the substitute up to ninety.

Cattāro [M 0.0119] ca dasa ca, catūhi vā adhikā dasāti catuddasa iccatra –

Four and ten, or ten with four added, thus in the case of catuddasa—

“Gaṇane, dasassā”ti ca vattate.

The words “gaṇane” (in counting) and “dasassa” (of dasa) are carried forward.

256 . Catūpapadassa lopo tuttarapadādi cassa cu copi navā.

256. Of the prefix catu, the tu is elided; and the remaining ca optionally becomes cu or co.

Gaṇane dasassādimhi ṭhitassa catuiccetassa upapadassa tusaddo lopo hoti, uttarapadādimhi ṭhitassa catūpapadassa cakārassa cu coādesā honti navā. Cuddasa, coddasa, catuddasa.

In counting, the sound tu of the prefix catu standing before dasa and so forth is elided; and the ca of the prefix catu, which is initial to the subsequent member, optionally becomes cu or co. Examples: Cuddasa, coddasa, catuddasa.

Apiggahaṇena anupapadassāpi gaṇane padādicakārassa lopo, cu co honti navā. Yathā – tālīsaṃ, cuttālīsaṃ, cottālīsaṃ, cattālīsaṃ.

By the inclusion of api in the rule, even for a word not used as a prefix, in counting, the initial ca of the word is elided, or it optionally becomes cu or co. For example: tālīsaṃ, cuttālīsaṃ, cottālīsaṃ, cattālīsaṃ.

Pañca ca dasa ca, pañcahi vā adhikā dasāti atthe pañcadasa. “Tesu vuddhī”tiādinā pañcasaddassa dasa vīsatīsu kvaci pannapaṇṇaādesā. Pannarasa, paṇṇarasa.

Five and ten, or ten plus five, thus pañcadasa. By the rule “tesu vuddhī” and so forth, for the word pañca, panna or paṇṇa are sometimes the substitutes when followed by dasa or vīsati. Examples: Pannarasa, paṇṇarasa.

Cha ca dasa ca, chahi vā adhikā dasāti atthe chadasa itīdha –

Six and ten, or ten with six added, thus in the case of chadasa—

“Chassā”ti vattate.

“Chassa” is carried forward.

257. Dase so niccañca.

257. And so is always substituted when dasa follows.

Chaiccetassa saṅkhyāsaddassa niccaṃ so hoti dase pare.

For the numeral cha, so is always the substitute when dasa follows.

“Saṅkhyānaṃ, vā”ti ca vattate.

“Saṅkhyānaṃ” (of numerals) and “vā” (optionally) are also carried forward.

258. La darānaṃ.

258. La is substituted for da and ra.

Saṅkhyānaṃ dakārarakārānaṃ lakārādeso hoti vā.

For numerals, la is optionally the substitute for the letters da and ra.

Laḷānamaviseso[M 0.0120]. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, tena “soḷasa” iti niccaṃ, “teḷasa, terasa, cattālīsaṃ, cattārīsa”miti vibhāsā, dasa pannarasādīsu na ca hoti.

There is no distinction between la and ḷa. This word vā indicates a fixed option. Therefore, soḷasa is constant, while teḷasa, terasa, cattālīsaṃ, cattārīsaṃ are optional. And it does not occur in dasa, pannarasa, and so forth.

Satta ca dasa ca, sattahi vā adhikā dasāti atthe sattarasa, sattadasa.

Seven and ten, or ten plus seven, thus in this sense, sattarasa, sattadasa.

Aṭṭha ca dasa ca, aṭṭhahi vā adhikā dasāti atthe aṭṭhadasa itīdha ātte kate –

Eight and ten, or ten with eight added, thus in the sense of aṭṭhadasa, here, when the lengthening has been made—

“Vā, dassa, ra, saṅkhyāne”ti ca vattate.

“Vā” (optionally), “dassa” (of dasa), “ra”, and “saṅkhyāne” (in counting) are also carried forward.

259. Aṭṭhādito ca.

259. And from aṭṭha onwards.

Aṭṭhādito ca dasasaddassa dakārassa rakāro hoti vā saṅkhyāne. Aṭṭhārasa, aṭṭhādasa.

And from aṭṭha onwards, the da of the word dasa optionally becomes ra in counting. Examples: Aṭṭhārasa, aṭṭhādasa.

Aṭṭhāditoti kiṃ? Catuddasa.

Why “from aṭṭha onwards”? For catuddasa.

Katisaddo bahuvacanantova, “kati yo” itīdha

The word kati is always plural-ending, as in the case of “kati yo”—

Niccaṃ yolopādi, rassattaṃ, kati tiṭṭhanti, kati passasi, katihi katibhi, katinaṃ, katihi katibhi, katinaṃ, katisu.

There is always elision of yo and so forth, and shortening. Examples: kati tiṭṭhanti (how many stand?), kati passasi (how many do you see?), katihi or katibhi (by how many), katinaṃ (of/to how many), katihi or katibhi (from how many), katinaṃ (of/to how many), katisu (among how many).

Aliṅganāmaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Indeclinable Nouns is concluded.

Vibhattippaccayavidhāna

The Exposition of Case-Endings and Suffixes

Atha vibhattippaccayantā vuccante.

Now, those ending in case-endings and suffixes are explained.

Tesaṃ panāliṅgattā, nipātattā ca tiliṅge, vacanadvaye ca samānaṃ rūpaṃ.

Among them, due to being indeclinable and particles, the form is the same in the three genders and in both numbers.

Purisasmā, purisehi vāti atthe –

In the sense of 'purisasmā' (from a man) or 'purisehi' (from men)—

260. Kvaci [M 0.0121] to pañcamyatthe.

260. Sometimes 'to' is used in the sense of the fifth case.

Sabbasmā suddhanāmato, sabbanāmato ca liṅgamhā kvaci topaccayo hoti pañcamyatthe.

After every pure noun and pronoun, the suffix 'to' sometimes occurs in the sense of the fifth case.

261. Tvādayo vibhattisaññā.

261. The suffixes beginning with 'tvā' have the designation of case ending.

Toādi yesaṃ dānipariyantānaṃ paccayānaṃ te honti paccayā tvādayo, te paccayā vibhattisaññā honti. Tena tadantānampi vibhatyantapadattaṃ siddhaṃ hoti.

Those suffixes which have 'to' as their beginning and 'dāni' as their end are the `tvādayo`. These suffixes are designated as case endings. Therefore, words ending in them are also established as words ending in case endings.

Purisato, evaṃ rājato vā, corato vā, aggito vā, gahapatito vā, hatthito, hetuto, sabbaññuto, kaññato, yuttito, itthito, bhikkhunito, ettha ca “kvacādimajjhuttarānaṃ dīgharassāpaccayesu cā”ti topaccaye rassattaṃ. Yāguto, jambuto, cittato, āyuto iccādi.

From a man; likewise from a king, or from a thief, or from fire, or from a householder, or from an elephant, from a cause, from the Omniscient One, from a maiden, from justice, from a woman, from a nun. And here, by the rule “kvacādimajjhuttarānaṃ dīgharassāpaccayesu cā”, there is shortening of the vowel when the suffix 'to' follows. Examples: 'yāguto' (from gruel), 'jambuto' (from a rose-apple tree), 'cittato' (from the mind), 'āyuto' (from life), and so forth.

Sabbanāmato sabbasmā, sabbehīti vā atthe sabbato, evaṃ yato, tato, katarato, katamato, itarato, aññato, ekato, ubhayato, pubbato, parato, aparato, dakkhiṇato, uttarato, amuto.

From pronouns: in the sense of 'sabbasmā' (from all) or 'sabbehi' (from all), thus 'sabbato'; likewise 'yato', 'tato', 'katarato', 'katamato', 'itarato', 'aññato', 'ekato', 'ubhayato', 'pubbato', 'parato', 'aparato', 'dakkhiṇato', 'uttarato', 'amuto'.

“Kissa, ku”iti ca vattate.

The rule beginning “Kissa ku” is also carried forward.

262. Tratothesu ca.

262. And when 'tra' and 'tha' follow.

Kimiccetassa ku hoti trato thaiccetesu ca paresu. Kasmā, kehīti vā kuto.

For the word 'kiṃ', 'ku' is substituted when 'tra', 'to', 'tha', and other such suffixes follow. In the sense of 'kasmā' or 'kehi': 'kuto'.

“Tothesū”ti vattate.

The phrase “tothesu” (when 'to' and 'tha' follow) is carried forward.

263. Sabbassetassākāro [M 0.0122] vā.

263. For `sabba` and `eta`, `a` is optionally substituted.

Sabbassa etasaddassa akāro hoti vā tothaiccetesu. Etasmā, etehīti vā ato.

For `sabba` and `eta`, `a` is optionally substituted when `to`, `tha`, and other such suffixes follow. In the sense of 'etasmā' or 'etehi': 'ato'.

“Sabbassetassā”ti ca vattate.

And “Sabbassa etassa” (for 'sabba' and 'eta') is carried forward.

264. E tothesu ca.

264. And 'e' is substituted when 'to' and 'tha' follow.

Sabbassa etasaddassa ekāro hoti vā tothaiccetesu. Dvittaṃ, etto.

For `sabba` and `eta`, `e` is optionally substituted when `to`, `tha`, and other such suffixes follow. Doubling occurs, as in 'etto'.

“Sabbassā”ti vattate.

“Sabbassa” (for 'sabba') is carried forward.

265. Imassi thaṃdānihatodhesu ca.

265. For `ima`, `i` is substituted; and when `thaṃ`, `dāni`, `ha`, `to`, and `dha` follow.

Imasaddassa sabbasseva ikāro hoti thaṃdānihatodhaiccetesu ca. Imasmāti ito.

For the entire word 'ima', 'i' is substituted when 'thaṃ', 'dāni', 'ha', 'to', 'dha', and other such suffixes follow. In the sense of 'imasmā': 'ito'.

“Kvaci to”ti yogavibhāgena ādippabhutīhi to sattamiyatthe. Aniccādīhi tatiyatthe ca. Yathā – ādimhībhi atthe ādito. Evaṃ majjhato, ekato, purato, pacchato, passato, piṭṭhito, pādato, sīsato, aggato, mūlato, parato iccādayo.

By division of the rule “Kvaci to”, the suffix 'to' is used in the sense of the seventh case after words such as 'ādi' (beginning), and in the sense of the third case after words such as 'anicca' (impermanent). For example, in the sense of 'ādimhi' (in the beginning): 'ādito'. Likewise: 'majjhato' (in the middle), 'ekato' (in one place), 'purato' (in front), 'pacchato' (behind), 'passato' (at the side), 'piṭṭhito' (at the back), 'pādato' (at the foot), 'sīsato' (at the head), 'aggato' (at the top), 'mūlato' (at the root), 'parato' (beyond), and so forth.

Tatiyatthe aniccenāti aniccato, aniccato sammasati. Evaṃ dukkhato, rogato, gaṇḍato iccādayo.

In the sense of the third case, 'aniccenā' (by impermanence) becomes 'aniccato'. Example: 'aniccato sammasati' (he contemplates by way of impermanence). Likewise: 'dukkhato' (by way of suffering), 'rogato' (by way of disease), 'gaṇḍato' (by way of a boil), and so forth.

“Atthe, kvacī”ti ca vattate.

“Atthe” (in the sense) and “kvaci” (sometimes) are also carried forward.

266. Tratha sattamiyā sabbanāmehi.

266. After pronouns, 'tra' and 'tha' are used in the sense of the seventh case.

Sabbanāmehi parā tra thaiccete paccayā honti kvaci sattamyatthe. Sabbasmiṃ, sabbesu cāti sabbatra sabbattha. Evaṃ [M 0.0123] yatra yattha, tatra tattha, itaratra itarattha, aññatra aññattha, ubhayatra ubhayattha, paratra parattha, kutra kuttha, “tratothesu cā”ti kuttaṃ. “Kissa ka ve cā”ti sutte casaddena kādeso. Kattha, amutra amuttha.

The suffixes 'tra' and 'tha' sometimes occur after pronouns in the sense of the seventh case. In the sense of 'sabbasmiṃ' (in all) or 'sabbesu' (among all), thus 'sabbatra', 'sabbattha' (everywhere). Likewise: 'yatra', 'yattha' (where); 'tatra', 'tattha' (there); 'itaratra', 'itarattha' (elsewhere); 'aññatra', 'aññattha' (in another place); 'ubhayatra', 'ubhayattha' (in both places); 'paratra', 'parattha' (beyond). 'Kutra', 'kuttha' (where). By “tratothesu ca”, 'ku' is substituted. By the word 'ca' in the rule “Kissa ka ve ca”, 'ka' is substituted, giving 'kattha'. 'amutra', 'amuttha' (yonder).

“Sabbassetassākāro”ti vattate.

The rule “Sabbassetassākāro vā” is carried forward.

267. Tre niccaṃ.

267. Invariably when 'tra' follows.

Sabbasseva etasaddassa akāro hoti niccaṃ tre pare. Atra. “Sabbassetassākāro vā”ti attaṃ, “e tothesu cā”ti ekāro, attha, ettha.

For both `sabba` and `eta`, `a` is invariably substituted when `tra` follows, as in `atra`. By the rule “Sabbassetassākāro vā”, the form is `attha`; by the rule “e tothesu cā”, `e` is substituted, resulting in `ettha`.

“Kvaci, atthe, sattamiyā”ti ca adhikāro, sabbasminti atthe –

And the governing rule 'Kvaci' (sometimes), 'atthe' (in the sense of), 'sattamiyā' (the seventh case) is carried forward. In the sense of 'sabbasmiṃ' (in all)—

268. Sabbato dhi.

268. From 'sabba', 'dhi' is added.

Sabbaiccetasmā dhippaccayo hoti kvaci sattamyatthe. Sabbadhi.

From the word 'sabba', the suffix 'dhi' sometimes occurs in the sense of the seventh case. Example: 'sabbadhi' (everywhere).

269. Kismā vo.

269. From 'kiṃ', 'va' is added.

Kimiccetasmā vappaccayo hoti kvaci sattamyatthe.

From the word 'kiṃ', the suffix 'va' sometimes occurs in the sense of the seventh case.

270. Kissa ka ve ca.

270. For 'kiṃ', 'ka' is substituted when 'va' follows, and also.

Kimiccetassa kasaddo ādeso hoti vappaccayepare. Caggahaṇena thahamādiavappaccayepi. “Tesu vuddhī”tiādinā kakāre akārassa lopo ca vamhi. Kva gatosi tvaṃ.

For the word 'kiṃ', the word 'ka' is substituted when the suffix 'va' follows. By the inclusion of 'ca', this also applies when suffixes such as 'tha', 'ha', and 'ma' follow. And by 'Tesu vuddhī', etc., the 'a' of 'ka' is elided when 'va' follows. Example: 'Kva gatosi tvaṃ?' (Where have you gone?).

“Kismā”ti vattate.

“Kismā” (from 'kiṃ') is carried forward.

271. Hiṃhaṃhiñcanaṃ[M 0.0124].

271. 'Hiṃ', 'haṃ', and 'hiñcanaṃ' are added.

Kimiccetasmā hiṃ haṃ hiñcanaṃiccete paccayā honti kvaci sattamyatthe.

From the word 'kiṃ', the suffixes 'hiṃ', 'haṃ', and 'hiñcanaṃ' sometimes occur in the sense of the seventh case.

“Kissā”ti vattate.

“Kissa” (of 'kiṃ') is carried forward.

272. Ku hiṃhaṃsu ca.

272. And 'ku' is substituted when 'hiṃ' and 'haṃ' follow.

Kimiccetassa ku hoti hiṃ haṃ iccetesu. Caggahaṇena hiñcanaṃdācanamiccādīsupi. Kisminti kuhiṃ, kuhaṃ, kuhiñcanaṃ, kahaṃ kādeso.

For the word 'kiṃ', 'ku' is substituted when 'hiṃ' and 'haṃ' follow. By the inclusion of 'ca', this also applies in the case of 'hiñcanaṃ', 'dācanaṃ', and so forth. Examples: In the sense of 'kismiṃ' (in what): 'kuhiṃ', 'kuhaṃ', 'kuhiñcanaṃ'. In 'kahaṃ', there is the substitution of 'ka'.

“Hiṃ ha”nti vattate.

“Hiṃ ha” is carried forward.

273. Tamhā ca.

273. And from 'ta'.

Taiccetasmā ca sabbanāmato hiṃhaṃpaccayā honti kvaci sattamyatthe. Tasminti tahiṃ, tahaṃ.

And from the pronoun 'ta', the suffixes 'hiṃ' and 'haṃ' sometimes occur in the sense of the seventh case. Examples: In the sense of 'tasmiṃ' (in that): 'tahiṃ', 'tahaṃ'.

274. Imasmā hadhā ca.

274. From 'ima', 'ha' and 'dha' are also added.

Imasaddato hadhappaccayā honti kvaci sattamyatthe. “Imassi tha”ntiādinā ikāro. Imasminti iha, idha.

From the word 'ima', the suffixes 'ha' and 'dha' sometimes occur in the sense of the seventh case. By the rule 'Imass-i-thā', etc., 'i' is substituted. Examples: In the sense of 'imasmiṃ' (in this): 'iha', 'idha'.

275. Yato hiṃ.

275. From 'ya', 'hiṃ' is added.

Yaiccetasmā sabbanāmato hiṃpaccayo hoti kvaci sattamyatthe. Yasminti yahiṃ.

From the pronoun 'ya', the suffix 'hiṃ' sometimes occurs in the sense of the seventh case. Example: In the sense of 'yasmiṃ' (in which), 'yahiṃ'.

“Kāle”ti adhikāroyaṃ.

This is the governing rule 'Kāle' (in time).

Kasmiṃ kāleti atthe

In the sense of 'kasmiṃ kāle' (at what time)—

276. Kiṃsabbaññekayakuhi [M 0.0125] dā dācanaṃ.

276. From 'kiṃ', 'sabba', 'añña', 'eka', 'ya', and 'ku', the suffixes 'dā' and 'dācanaṃ' are added.

Kiṃ sabbaaññaekayaiccetehi sabbanāmehi dāpaccayo hoti. Kuiccetasmā dācanañca kāle kvaci sattamyatthe.

From these pronouns—'kiṃ', 'sabba', 'añña', 'eka', and 'ya'—the suffix 'dā' occurs. And from the word 'ku', the suffix 'dācana' occurs, in the sense of time, sometimes in the sense of the seventh case.

“Kissa ka ve cā”ti sutte casaddena kādeso, kadā.

By the word 'ca' in the rule 'Kissa ka ve cā', 'ka' is substituted. Example: 'kadā' (when).

277. Sabbassa so dāmhi vā.

277. For 'sabba', 'sa' is optionally substituted when 'dā' follows.

Sabbaiccetassa saddassa sasaddādeso hoti vā dāpaccaye pare. Sabbasmiṃ kāleti sadā, sabbadā.

For the word 'sabba', the word 'sa' is optionally substituted when the suffix 'dā' follows. Examples: In the sense of 'sabbasmiṃ kāle' (at all times), 'sadā', 'sabbadā'.

Evaṃ aññadā, ekadā, yadā, kasmiṃ kāleti kudācanaṃ, “ku hiṃhaṃsu cā”ti sutte casaddena kuttaṃ, “ku”iti nipātanena vā.

Likewise: 'aññadā' (at another time), 'ekadā' (once), 'yadā' (when). In the sense of 'kasmiṃ kāle' (at what time): 'kudācanaṃ' (at any time). The substitution of 'ku' is by the word 'ca' in the rule 'ku hiṃhaṃsu cā', or by its being an irregular formation.

“Dā”ti vattate.

“Dā” is carried forward.

278. Tamhā dāni ca.

278. And from 'ta', 'dāni' is added.

Taiccetasmā sabbanāmato dānidāpaccayā honti kāle kvaci sattamyatthe. Tasmiṃ kāleti tadāni, tadā.

From the pronoun 'ta', the suffixes 'dāni' and 'dā' are sometimes applied in the sense of time, in the meaning of the seventh case. For example: in the sense of 'tasmiṃ kāle' (at that time), 'tadāni', 'tadā'.

279. Imasmā rahidhunādāni ca.

279. And from 'ima', the suffixes 'rahi', 'dhunā', and 'dāni' are applied.

Imasaddato rahi dhunā dāniiccete paccayā honti kāle kvaci sattamyatthe.

From the word 'ima', these suffixes, 'rahi', 'dhunā', and 'dāni', are sometimes applied in the sense of time, in the meaning of the seventh case.

“Sabbassa, imassā”ti ca vattate.

And the words 'sabbassa' and 'imassa' are carried forward.

280. Eta [M 0.0126] rahimhi.

280. 'Eta' is the substitute when 'rahi' follows.

Sabbassa imasaddassa etādeso hoti rahimhi paccaye pare. Imasmiṃ kāleti etarahi.

For the entire words 'sabba' and 'ima', 'eta' is the substitute when the suffix 'rahi' follows. For example: in the sense of 'imasmiṃ kāle' (at this time), 'etarahi'.

281. A dhunāmhi ca.

281. And 'a' is the substitute when 'dhunā' follows.

Sabbasseva imasaddassa akāro hoti dhunāpaccaye pare. Adhunā, imasaddassa ikāro. Imasmiṃ kāleti idāni.

For the entire words 'sabba' and 'ima', 'a' is the substitute when the suffix 'dhunā' follows, forming 'adhunā'. For 'ima', 'i' is the substitute when 'dāni' follows. For example: in the sense of 'imasmiṃ kāle' (at this time), 'idāni'.

Vibhattippaccayavidhānaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ.

The Section on Case-Endings and Suffixes is concluded.

Opasaggikapada

The Chapter on Prefixes

Athāliṅgasaṅkhyāvibhattibhedā upasagganipātā vuccante.

Now, the prefixes and particles, which are without distinctions of gender, number, and case, are discussed.

Pa parā ni nī u du saṃ vi ava anu pari adhi abhi pati su ā ati api apa upa iti pīsati upasaggā.

'Pa', 'parā', 'ni', 'nī', 'u', 'du', 'saṃ', 'vi', 'ava', 'anu', 'pari', 'adhi', 'abhi', 'pati', 'su', 'ā', 'ati', 'api', 'apa', 'upa'—these twenty are the prefixes.

Tattha pasaddo pakārā’dikamma padhāni’ssariya’ntobhāvaviyoga tappara bhusattha sambhavatitti anāvila patthanādīsu. Paiti ayamupasaggo etesu pakārādīsu atthesu vattati, yathā – pakāre paññā, ādikamme vippakataṃ, padhāne paṇītaṃ, padhānaṃ padhānattaṃ, issariye pabhū ayaṃ desassa, antobhāve pakkhittaṃ, viyoge pavāsī, tappare pācariyo, bhusatthe pavuddhakāyo, sambhave himavatā gaṅgā pabhavati, tittiyaṃ pahūtamannaṃ, anāvile pasannamudakaṃ, patthane paṇihitaṃ.

Among them, the prefix 'pa' is used in the senses of manner, initial action, chiefness, lordship, inclusion, separation, intentness, abundance, origin, satisfaction, clarity, aspiration, and so on. This prefix 'pa' is applied in these senses of manner, etc. For example: in the sense of manner, 'paññā' (wisdom); in initial action, 'vippakataṃ' (unfinished); in chiefness, 'paṇītaṃ' (excellent), 'padhānaṃ' (chief), 'padhānattaṃ' (chiefness); in lordship, 'pabhū ayaṃ desassa' (he is lord of this country); in inclusion, 'pakkhittaṃ' (inserted); in separation, 'pavāsī' (exiled); in intentness, 'pācariyo' (teacher of teachers); in abundance, 'pavuddhakāyo' (large-bodied); in origin, 'himavatā gaṅgā pabhavati' (the Ganges originates from the Himālaya); in satisfaction, 'pahūtamannaṃ' (abundant food); in clarity, 'pasannamudakaṃ' (clear water); in aspiration, 'paṇihitaṃ' (resolved).

Parāiti [M 0.0127] parihāni parājaya gativikkamā’masanādīsu. Yathā – parihāniyaṃ parābhavo, parājaye parājito, gatiyaṃ parāyanaṃ. Vikkame parakkamati, āmasane aṅgassa parāmasanaṃ.

The prefix 'parā' is used in the senses of decline, defeat, movement, exertion, touching, and so on. For example: in the sense of decline, 'parābhavo' (ruin); in defeat, 'parājito' (defeated); in movement, 'parāyanaṃ' (refuge); in exertion, 'parakkamati' (strives); in touching, 'aṅgassa parāmasanaṃ' (touching of a limb).

Niiti nissesa niggata nīharaṇa’ntopavesanā’bhāvanisedha nikkhanta pātubhāvā’vadhāraṇa vibhajana upamū’padhāraṇā’vasānachekādīsu. Nissese nirutti, niravasesaṃ deti, niggate nikkileso, niyyāti, nīharaṇe niddhāraṇaṃ, antopavesane nikhāto, abhāve nimmakkhikaṃ, nisedhe nivāreti, nikkhante nibbāno, nibbānaṃ, pātubhāve nimmitaṃ, avadhāraṇe nicchayo, vibhajane niddeso, upamāyaṃ nidassanaṃ, upadhāraṇe nisāmanaṃ, avasāne niṭṭhitaṃ, cheke nipuṇo.

The prefix 'ni' is used in the senses of entirety, departure, removal, entering inside, absence, prohibition, going out, manifestation, ascertainment, division, comparison, investigation, conclusion, skill, and so on. For example: in the sense of entirety, 'nirutti' (etymology), 'niravasesaṃ deti' (gives without remainder); in departure, 'nikkileso' (free from defilements), 'niyyāti' (goes out); in removal, 'niddhāraṇaṃ' (specification); in entering inside, 'nikhāto' (buried); in absence, 'nimmakkhikaṃ' (free from flies); in prohibition, 'nivāreti' (prevents); in going out, 'nibbāno, nibbānaṃ' (extinguishment); in manifestation, 'nimmitaṃ' (created); in ascertainment, 'nicchayo' (certainty); in division, 'niddeso' (explanation); in comparison, 'nidassanaṃ' (example); in investigation, 'nisāmanaṃ' (attending to); in conclusion, 'niṭṭhitaṃ' (finished); in skill, 'nipuṇo' (skilled).

Nīiti nīharaṇā’varaṇādīsu. Nīharaṇe nīharati, āvaraṇe nīvaraṇaṃ.

The prefix 'nī' is used in the senses of taking out, obstruction, and so on. For example: in the sense of taking out, 'nīharati' (takes out); in obstruction, 'nīvaraṇaṃ' (hindrance).

Uiti uggatu’ddhakamma padhāna viyoga sambhava atthalābhasatti sarūpakathanādīsu. Uggate uggacchati, uddhakamme āsanā uṭṭhito, ukkhepo, padhāne uttamo, lokuttaro, viyoge ubbāsito, sambhave ubbhūto, atthalābhe uppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ, sattiyaṃ ussahati gantuṃ, sarūpakathane uddisati suttaṃ.

The prefix 'u' is used in the senses of rising, upward action, chiefness, separation, origin, attainment of a goal, power, stating the nature of something, and so on. For example: in the sense of rising, 'uggacchati' (rises); in upward action, 'āsanā uṭṭhito' (risen from a seat), 'ukkhepo' (lifting up); in chiefness, 'uttamo' (supreme), 'lokuttaro' (supramundane); in separation, 'ubbāsito' (expelled); in origin, 'ubbhūto' (arisen); in attainment of a goal, 'uppannaṃ ñāṇaṃ' (arisen knowledge); in power, 'ussahati gantuṃ' (is able to go); in stating the nature of something, 'uddisati suttaṃ' (recites a discourse).

Duiti asobhanā’bhāvakucchitā’samiddhi kiccha virūpatādīsu. Asobhane duggandho, abhāve dubbhikkhaṃ, kucchite dukkaṭaṃ, asamiddhiyaṃ dussassaṃ, kicche dukkaraṃ, virūpatāyaṃ dubbaṇṇo, dummukho.

The prefix 'du' is used in the senses of unpleasantness, absence, contemptibility, failure, difficulty, deformity, and so on. For example: in the sense of unpleasantness, 'duggandho' (foul-smelling); in absence, 'dubbhikkhaṃ' (famine); in contemptibility, 'dukkataṃ' (wrongdoing); in failure, 'dussassaṃ' (bad harvest); in difficulty, 'dukkaraṃ' (difficult to do); in deformity, 'dubbaṇṇo' (ill-favored), 'dummukho' (ugly-faced).

Saṃiti samodhāna sammāsama samantabhāvasaṅgata saṅkhepabhusattha sahattha appattha pabhavā’bhimukhabhāva saṅgaha pidhāna punappunakaraṇa samiddhādīsu. Samodhāne sandhi, sammāsamesu samādhi[M 0.0128], sampayutto, samantabhāve saṃkiṇṇā samullapanā, saṅgate saṅgamo, saṅkhepe samāso, bhusatthe sāratto, sahatthe saṃvāso, appatthe samaggho. Pabhave sambhavo, abhimukhabhāve sammukhaṃ, saṅgahe saṅgaṇhāti, pidhāne saṃvutaṃ, punappunakaraṇe sandhāvati, samiddhiyaṃ sampanno.

The prefix 'saṃ' is used in the senses of union, right equality, all-around presence, meeting, abbreviation, intensity, togetherness, smallness, origin, facing, collection, covering, repetition, prosperity, and so on. For example: in the sense of union, 'sandhi' (conjunction); in right equality, 'samādhi' (concentration), 'sampayutto' (associated); in all-around presence, 'saṃkiṇṇā samullapanā' (confused conversation); in meeting, 'saṅgamo' (coming together); in abbreviation, 'samāso' (compounding); in intensity, 'sāratto' (impassioned); in togetherness, 'saṃvāso' (living together); in smallness, 'samaggho' (valuable); in origin, 'sambhavo' (origin); in facing, 'sammukhaṃ' (face to face); in collection, 'saṅgaṇhāti' (collects); in covering, 'saṃvutaṃ' (restrained); in repetition, 'sandhāvati' (runs about); in prosperity, 'sampanno' (endowed with).

Viiti visesa vividha viruddha vigata viyoga virūpatādīsu. Visese vimutti visiṭṭho, vividhe vimati vicitraṃ, viruddhe vivādo, vigate vimalaṃ, viyoge vippayutto, virūpatāyaṃ virūpo.

The prefix 'vi' is used in the senses of distinction, diversity, opposition, absence, separation, deformity, and so on. For example: in the sense of distinction, 'vimutti' (liberation), 'visiṭṭho' (distinguished); in diversity, 'vimati' (doubt), 'vicitraṃ' (variegated); in opposition, 'vivādo' (dispute); in absence, 'vimalaṃ' (stainless); in separation, 'vippayutto' (disassociated); in deformity, 'virūpo' (deformed).

Avaiti adhobhāga viyoga paribhava jānana suddhi nicchayadesa theyyādīsu. Adhobhāge avakkhittacakkhu, viyoge omukkaupāhano avakokilaṃ vanaṃ, paribhave avajānanaṃ avamaññati, jānane avagacchati, suddhiyaṃ vodānaṃ, nicchaye avadhāraṇaṃ, dese avakāso, theyye avahāro.

The prefix 'ava' is used in the senses of downward direction, separation, contempt, knowing, purity, determination, place, theft, and so on. For example: in the sense of downward direction, 'avakkhittacakkhu' (with downcast eyes); in separation, 'omukkaupāhano' (having taken off one's sandals), 'avakokilaṃ vanaṃ' (a forest without cuckoos); in contempt, 'avajānanaṃ' (disregard), 'avamaññati' (despises); in knowing, 'avagacchati' (understands); in purity, 'vodānaṃ' (purification); in determination, 'avadhāraṇaṃ' (ascertainment); in place, 'avakāso' (opportunity, space); in theft, 'avahāro' (theft).

Anuiti anugatā’nupacchinna pacchattha bhusattha sādissa hīnatatiyattha lakkhaṇi’tthambhūtakkhāna bhāga vicchādīsu. Anugate anveti, anupacchinne anusayo, pacchāsaddatthe anurathaṃ, bhusatthe anuratto, sādisse anurūpaṃ. Hīne anusāriputtaṃ paññavanto, tatiyatthe nadimanvavasitā senā, lakkhaṇe rukkhaṃ anu vijjotate vijju, itthambhūtakkhāne sādhu devadatto mātaraṃ anu, bhāge yadettha maṃ anusiyā taṃ dīyatu, vicchāyaṃ rukkhaṃ rukkhaṃ anu vijjotate cando.

The prefix 'anu' is used in the senses of following, uninterruptedness, after, intensity, similarity, inferiority, the meaning of the third case, characteristic, description of a state, share, pervasion, and so on. For example: in the sense of following, 'anveti' (follows); in uninterruptedness, 'anusayo' (latent tendency); in the sense of 'after', 'anurathaṃ' (behind the chariot); in intensity, 'anuratto' (greatly impassioned); in similarity, 'anurūpaṃ' (suitable); in inferiority, 'anusāriputtaṃ paññavanto' (those wise ones who are inferior to Sāriputta); in the meaning of the third case, 'nadimanvavasitā senā' (the army is encamped along the river); in characteristic, 'rukkhaṃ anu vijjotate vijju' (lightning flashes upon the tree); in description of a state, 'sādhu devadatto mātaraṃ anu' (Devadatta is good towards his mother); in share, 'yadettha maṃ anusiyā taṃ dīyatu' (whatever share of this should be mine, let that be given); in pervasion, 'rukkhaṃ rukkhaṃ anu vijjotate cando' (the moon shines on every single tree).

Pariiti samantatobhāva pariccheda vajjanā’liṅgana nivāsanapūjābhojanā’vajānana dosakkhāna lakkhaṇādīsu. Samantatobhāve parivuto, paricchede pariññeyyaṃ, vajjane pariharati[M 0.0129], āliṅgane parissajati, nivāsane vatthaṃ paridhassati, pūjāyaṃ pāricariyā, bhojane bhikkhuṃ parivisati. Avajānane paribhavati, dosakkhāne paribhāsati, lakkhaṇādīsu rukkhaṃ pari vijjotate vijjuiccādi.

The prefix 'pari' is used in the senses of all-around presence, delimitation, avoidance, embracing, dressing, honoring, eating, disdaining, declaring faults, characteristic, and so on. For example: in the sense of all-around presence, 'parivuto' (surrounded); in delimitation, 'pariññeyyaṃ' (to be fully understood); in avoidance, 'pariharati' (avoids); in embracing, 'parissajati' (embraces); in dressing, 'vatthaṃ paridhassati' (will put on a garment); in honoring, 'pāricariyā' (service); in eating, 'bhikkhuṃ parivisati' (serves a monk); in disdaining, 'paribhavati' (despises); in declaring faults, 'paribhāsati' (reviles); in the sense of characteristic, etc., 'rukkhaṃ pari vijjotate vijju' (lightning flashes around the tree), and so on.

Adhiiti adhiki’ssa’rūparibhāvā’dhibhavanajjhāyanā’dhiṭṭhānanicchayapāpuṇanādīsu. Adhike adhisīlaṃ, issare adhipati, adhi brahmadatte pañcālā, uparibhāve adhirohati, pathaviṃ adhisessati, adhibhavane adhibhavati, ajjhāyane byākaraṇamadhīte, adhiṭṭhāne bhūmikampādiṃ adhiṭṭhāti, nicchaye adhimokkho, pāpuṇane bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati.

The prefix 'adhi' is used in the senses of superiority, lordship, being above, overcoming, studying, resolution, decision, attainment, and so on. For example: in the sense of superiority, 'adhisīlaṃ' (higher virtue); in lordship, 'adhipati' (sovereign), 'adhi brahmadatte pañcālā' (the Pañcālas are under Brahmadatta); in being above, 'adhirohati' (ascends), 'pathaviṃ adhisessati' (will lie upon the earth); in overcoming, 'adhibhavati' (overcomes); in studying, 'byākaraṇamadhīte' (studies grammar); in resolution, 'bhūmikampādiṃ adhiṭṭhāti' (determines upon an earthquake, etc.); in decision, 'adhimokkho' (resolve); in attainment, 'bhogakkhandhaṃ adhigacchati' (attains a mass of wealth).

Abhiiti abhimukhabhāva visiṭṭhā’dhi ku’ddhakamma kula sāruppavandana lakkhaṇi’tthambhūtakkhāna vicchādīsu. Abhimukhabhāve abhimukho abhikkamati, visiṭṭhe abhidhammo, adhike abhivassati, uddhakamme abhiruhati, kule abhijāto, sāruppe abhirūpo, vandane abhivādeti, lakkhaṇādīsu purimasamaṃ.

The prefix 'abhi' is used in the senses of facing, excellence, superiority, upward action, lineage, suitability, veneration, characteristic, description of a state, pervasion, and so on. For example: in the sense of facing, 'abhimukho abhikkamati' (advances towards); in excellence, 'abhidhammo' (higher doctrine); in superiority, 'abhivassati' (rains down upon); in upward action, 'abhiruhati' (ascends); in lineage, 'abhijāto' (well-born); in suitability, 'abhirūpo' (handsome); in veneration, 'abhivādeti' (pays homage); in the senses of characteristic, etc., it is the same as the previous.

Patiiti patigata paṭilomapatinidhi patidāna nisedhanivattana sādissa patikaraṇā’dāna patibodha paṭicca lakkhaṇi’tthambhūtakkhāna bhāgavicchādīsu. Patigate paccakkhaṃ, paṭilome patisotaṃ, patinidhimhi ācariyato pati sisso, patidāne telatthikassa ghataṃ pati dadāti, nisedhe paṭisedhanaṃ, nivattane paṭikkamati, sādisse patirūpakaṃ, patikaraṇe patikāro, ādāne patiggaṇhāti, patibodhe paṭivedho, paṭicce paccayo, lakkhaṇādīsu purimasamaṃ.

'Pati' is used in the senses of going towards, opposition, substitution, giving back, prevention, turning back, resemblance, counteracting, receiving, understanding, dependence, characteristic, stating 'it is so', part, covering, and so on. For example: in going towards—'paccakkhaṃ' (direct); in opposition—'patisotaṃ' (against the stream); in substitution—'ācariyato pati sisso' (a pupil in place of a teacher); in giving back—'telatthikassa ghataṃ pati dadāti' (gives ghee in return for oil to one desiring oil); in prevention—'paṭisedhanaṃ' (prevention); in turning back—'paṭikkamati' (retreats); in resemblance—'patirūpakaṃ' (likeness); in counteracting—'patikāro' (requital); in receiving—'patiggaṇhāti' (accepts); in understanding—'paṭivedho' (comprehension); in dependence—'paccayo' (condition); in characteristics and so on—as before.

Suiti sobhana suṭṭhusammā samiddhi sukhatthādīsu. Sobhane sugandho, suṭṭhusammādatthesu suṭṭhu gato sugato, sammā gatotipi sugato, samiddhiyaṃ subhikkhaṃ, sukhatthe sukaro.

'Su' is used in the senses of beauty, 'very well' or 'rightly', prosperity, ease, and so on. For example: in beauty—'sugandho' (fragrant); in the senses of 'very well' and 'rightly'—'suṭṭhu gato' is 'sugato' (well-gone), and 'sammā gato' is also 'sugato' (rightly gone); in prosperity—'subhikkhaṃ' (abundant food); in ease—'sukaro' (easy to do).

Āiti [M 0.0130] abhimukhabhāvu’ddhakamma mariyādā’bhividhi patti’cchāparissajana ādikammaggahaṇa nivāsa samīpa’vhānādīsu. Abhimukhabhāve āgacchati, uddhakamme ārohati, mariyādāyaṃ āpabbatā khettaṃ, abhividhimhi ākumāraṃ yaso kaccāyanassa, pattiyaṃ āpattimāpanno, icchāyaṃ ākaṅkhā, parissajane āliṅganaṃ, ādikamme ārambho, gahaṇe ādīyati ālambati, nivāse āvasatho, samīpe āsannaṃ, avhāne āmantesi.

'Ā' is used in the senses of facing, upward action, boundary, extent, attainment, desire, embracing, initial undertaking, grasping, dwelling, proximity, summoning, and so on. For example: in facing—'āgacchati' (comes); in upward action—'ārohati' (ascends); in boundary—'āpabbatā khettaṃ' (the field up to the mountain); in extent—'ākumāraṃ yaso kaccāyanassa' (Kaccāyana's fame extending to the children); in attainment—'āpattimāpanno' (incurs an offense); in desire—'ākaṅkhā' (longing); in embracing—'āliṅganaṃ' (an embrace); in initial undertaking—'ārambho' (a beginning); in grasping—'ādīyati' (takes hold of), 'ālambati' (clings to); in dwelling—'āvasatho' (a residence); in proximity—'āsannaṃ' (near); in summoning—'āmantesi' (addressed).

Atiiti abhikkamanā’tikkantā’tisaya bhusatthādīsu. Atikkamane atirocati amhehi, atīto, atikkante accantaṃ, atisaye atikusalo, bhusatthe atikkodho ativuddhi.

'Ati' is used in the senses of surpassing, exceeding, excellence, intensity, and so on. For example: in surpassing—'atirocati amhehi' (excels us), 'atīto' (past); in exceeding—'accantaṃ' (completely); in excellence—'atikusalo' (highly skilled); in intensity—'atikkodho' (excessive anger), 'ativuddhi' (great growth).
