Likewise, tecīvarikattaṃ, tecīvarikatā (the state of possessing three robes); odarikattaṃ, odarikatā (the state of being a glutton); manussattaṃ, manussatā (humanity, as a genus); nīlattaṃ, nīlatā (blueness, as a quality); yācakattaṃ, yācakatā (beggary, as an action); daṇḍittaṃ, daṇḍitā (the state of being a staff-bearer, as a substance); saccavāditā (truthfulness); pāramitā (perfection); kataññutā (gratitude); sabbaññutā (omniscience); by the rule 'kvacā' and so on, shortening occurs in the tā affix; appicchatā (fewness of wishes); asaṃsaggatā (unsociability); bhassārāmatā (delight in talk); niddārāmatā (delight in sleep); lahutā (lightness), and so on.

Ttanapaccaye – puthujjanassa bhāvo puthujjanattanaṃ, vedanattanaṃ, jāyattanaṃ.

In the case of the affix -ttana: the state of an ordinary person is puthujjanattanaṃ (ordinariness); vedanattanaṃ (the state of experiencing feeling); jāyattanaṃ (the state of being a wife).

Ṇeyye – sucissa bhāvo soceyyaṃ. Evaṃ ādhipabheyyaṃ, kavissa bhāvokāveyyaṃ, thenassa bhāvo theyyaṃ, mahāvuttinā nakārassa lopo.

In the case of -ṇeyya: the state of being pure is soceyyaṃ (purity). Thus, ādhipateyyaṃ (mastery); the state of being a poet is kāveyyaṃ (poetry); the state of being a thief is theyyaṃ (theft); with the elision of 'na' by the Mahāvutti.

“Ṇyattatā”ti yogavibhāgena kammani, sakatthe ca ṇyādayo, vīrānaṃ bhāvo, kammaṃ vā vīriyaṃ, paribhaṭassa kammaṃ pāribhaṭyaṃ, pāribhaṭyassa bhāvo pāribhaṭyatā. Evaṃ sovacassatā, bhisaggassa kammaṃ bhesajjaṃ, byāvaṭassa kammaṃ veyyāvaccaṃ, saṭhassa bhāvo, kammaṃ vā sāṭheyyaṃ.

By the division of the rule 'ṇyattatā,' affixes like ṇya occur in the sense of action and in their own sense. The state of heroes, or their action, is vīriyaṃ (heroism, energy); the work of a retainer is pāribhaṭyaṃ (retainership); the state of retainership is pāribhaṭyatā. Likewise, sovacassatā (obedience); the work of a physician is bhesajjaṃ (medicine); the work of an engaged person is veyyāvaccaṃ (assistance); the state of a cheat, or their action, is sāṭheyyaṃ (deceit).

Sakatthe pana – yathābhūtameva yathābhuccaṃ, karuṇāyeva kāruññaṃ, pattakālameva pattakallaṃ, ākāsānantameva [M 0.0239] ākāsānañcaṃ, kāyapāguññameva kāyapāguññatā iccādi.

But in its own sense: what is just as it is, is yathābhuccaṃ (truly so); compassion itself is kāruññaṃ; the proper time itself is pattakallaṃ (the opportune time); the infinity of space itself is ākāsānañcaṃ (the sphere of the infinity of space); bodily dexterity itself is kāyapāguññatā (bodily dexterity), and so on.

“Visamassa bhāvo”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, “the state of the uneven”—

“Ttatā, bhāve”ti ca vattate.

And 'tta' and 'tā' continue in the sense of 'bhāva'.

388. Ṇa visamādīhi.

388. The affix -ṇa is used after visama and so on.

Visamaiccevamādīhi chaṭṭhiyantehi ṇappaccayo hoti, tta tā ca “tassa bhāvo” iccetasmiṃ atthe. Ākatigaṇoyaṃ. Vesamaṃ, visamattaṃ, visamatā. Sucissa bhāvo socaṃ, sucittaṃ, sucitā, garuno bhāvo gāravo, ādivuddhi, “o sare cā”ti sutte casaddaggahaṇena ukārassa ca avādeso. Paṭuno bhāvo pāṭavaṃ, paṭuttaṃ, paṭutā.

From words like visama and so on, ending in the sixth case, the affix ṇa occurs, and also tta and tā, in the sense of 'its state.' This is an open group. Vesamaṃ, visamattaṃ, visamatā (unevenness). The state of being pure: socaṃ, sucittaṃ, sucitā. The state of being venerable: gāravo, with initial vowel lengthening; and by the rule "o sare cā," due to the inclusion of 'ca,' 'ava' is the substitute for 'u'. The state of being skilled: pāṭavaṃ, paṭuttaṃ, paṭutā.

Ujuno bhāvo ajjavaṃ, muduno bhāvo maddavaṃ iccatra “āttañcā”ti ṇamhi ikārukārānaṃ āttaṃ, dvibhāvo, saṃyoge ādirassattañca. Ujutā, mudutā. Evaṃ isissa bhāvo ārisyaṃ, āsabhaṃ, kumārassa bhāvokomāraṃ, yuvassa bhāvo yobbanaṃ, mahāvuttinā nakārāgamo, paramānaṃ bhāvo, kammaṃ vā pāramī dānādikriyā, “ṇavaṇikā”disuttena īpaccayo, samaggānaṃ bhāvo sāmaggī.

The state of being straight is ajjavaṃ (uprightness); the state of being gentle is maddavaṃ (mildness). Here, by the rule "āttañcā," when 'ṇa' follows, 'i' and 'u' become 'ā'; doubling, and shortening of the initial vowel in a conjunct also occur. Ujutā (straightness), mudutā (gentleness). Thus, the state of a seer is ārisyaṃ; āsabhaṃ (excellence); the state of a youth is komāraṃ (youthfulness); the state of a young man is yobbanaṃ (youth); by the Mahāvutti, the augment 'na' occurs. The state, or the action, of the supreme is pāramī (perfection), an action such as giving; by the rule beginning "ṇavaṇikā," the suffix 'ī' is applied. The state of the harmonious is sāmaggī (concord).

389. Ramaṇīyādito kaṇa.

389. After ramaṇīya and so on, the affix -kaṇa is used.

Ramaṇīyaiccevamādito kaṇapaccayo hoti, tta tā ca bhāvatthe. Ramaṇīyassa bhāvo rāmaṇīyakaṃ, ramaṇīyattaṃ, ramaṇīyatā[M 0.0240]. Evaṃ mānuññakaṃ, manuññattaṃ, manuññatā, piyarūpakaṃ, piyarūpattaṃ, piyarūpatā, kalyāṇakaṃ, kalyāṇattaṃ, kalyāṇatā, corakaṃ, corikā vā, corattaṃ, coratā, aḍḍhakaṃ, aḍḍhattaṃ, aḍḍhatā iccādi.

From ramaṇīya and so on, the affix kaṇa occurs, and tta and tā also occur, in the sense of 'state'. The state of being pleasant is rāmaṇīyakaṃ, ramaṇīyattaṃ, ramaṇīyatā. Similarly, mānuññakaṃ, manuññattaṃ, manuññatā; piyarūpakaṃ, piyarūpattaṃ, piyarūpatā; kalyāṇakaṃ, kalyāṇattaṃ, kalyāṇatā; corakaṃ, or corikā, corattaṃ, coratā; aḍḍhakaṃ, aḍḍhattaṃ, aḍḍhatā, and so on.

Bhāvataddhitaṃ.

Taddhitas of State

Visesataddhita

Taddhitas of Distinction

“Sabbe ime pāpā ayamimesaṃ visesena pāpo”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, “All these are evil, but this one is especially evil among them”—

390. Visese taratamisikiyiṭṭhā.

390. In the sense of distinction, the suffixes tara, tama, isika, iya, and iṭṭha occur.

Visesatthe tara tama isika iya iṭṭhaiccete paccayā honti. Pāpataro, pāpatarā, pāpataraṃ. Tatopi adhiko pāpatamo, pāpatamā, pāpatamaṃ. Pāpisiko, pāpisikā, pāpisikaṃ. Pāpiyo, pāpiyā, pāpiyaṃ. Pāpiṭṭho, pāpiṭṭhā, pāpiṭṭhaṃ. Atisayena pāpiṭṭho, pāpiṭṭhataro. Evaṃ paṭutaro, paṭutamo, paṭisiko, paṭiyo, paṭiṭṭho. Sabbesaṃ atisayena varo varataro, varatamo, varisiko, variyo, variṭṭho. Evaṃ paṇītataro, paṇītatamo.

In the sense of distinction, these suffixes occur: tara, tama, isika, iya, and iṭṭha. Pāpataro, pāpatarā, pāpataraṃ. Even more so, pāpatamo, pāpatamā, pāpatamaṃ. Pāpisiko, pāpisikā, pāpisikaṃ. Pāpiyo, pāpiyā, pāpiyaṃ. Pāpiṭṭho, pāpiṭṭhā, pāpiṭṭhaṃ. Exceedingly evil is pāpiṭṭho; even more so, pāpiṭṭhataro. Similarly, paṭutaro, paṭutamo, paṭisiko, paṭiyo, paṭiṭṭho. Most excellent of all is varo; then varataro, varatamo, varisiko, variyo, variṭṭho. Similarly, paṇītataro, paṇītatamo.

“Sabbe ime vuḍḍhā ayamimesaṃ visesena vuḍḍho”ti atthe iyaiṭṭhappaccayā honti.

In the sense of 'All these are old, but this one is especially old among them,' the suffixes iya and iṭṭha occur.

391. Vuḍḍhassa [M 0.0241] jo iyiṭṭhesu.

391. For 'vuḍḍha', 'jo' is substituted when the suffixes iya and iṭṭha are present.

Sabbasseva vuḍḍhasaddassa jo hoti iya iṭṭhaiccetesu paccayesu. Jeyyo, jeṭṭho, ettha ca “saralopādi”sutte tuggahaṇena lopamakatvā “sarā sare lopa”nti pubbasare lutte “kvacāsavaṇṇaṃ lutte”ti ekāro.

For the entire word 'vuḍḍha', 'jo' is substituted when these suffixes, iya and iṭṭha, are present. Thus are formed jeyyo and jeṭṭho. And here, in the rule 'saralopādi', elision is not performed due to the inclusion of 'tu'; then, by 'sarā sare lopa', the preceding vowel is elided, and by 'kvacāsavaṇṇaṃ lutte', the vowel 'e' results.

“Iyiṭṭhesū”ti adhikāro, “jo”ti ca vattate.

The term 'iyiṭṭhesu' is the governing rule, and 'jo' also continues.

392. Pasatthassa so ca.

392. And for 'pasattha', 'sa' is substituted.

Sabbasseva pasatthasaddassa sādeso hoti, jo ca iyiṭṭhesu. Ayañca pasattho ayañca pasattho sabbe ime pasatthā ayamimesaṃ visesena pasatthoti seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

For the entire word 'pasattha', 'sa' is substituted, and 'jo' is also substituted, when the suffixes iyiṭṭha are present. Thus, in the sense of 'This one is praised, and that one is praised; all these are praised, but this one is especially praised among them,' the forms are seyyo, seṭṭho, jeyyo, jeṭṭho.

393. Antikassa nedo.

393. For 'antika', 'neda' is substituted.

Sabbasseva antikasaddassa nedādeso hoti iyiṭṭhesu. Visesena antikoti nediyo, nediṭṭho.

For the entire word 'antika', 'neda' is substituted when the suffixes iyiṭṭha are present. Thus, in the sense of 'especially near,' the forms are nediyo, nediṭṭho.

394. Bāḷhassa sādho.

394. For 'bāḷha', 'sādha' is substituted.

Sabbasseva bāḷhasaddassa sādhādeso hoti iyiṭṭhesu. Visesena bāḷhoti sādhiyo, sādhiṭṭho.

For the entire word 'bāḷha', 'sādha' is substituted when the suffixes iyiṭṭha are present. Thus, in the sense of 'especially strong,' the forms are sādhiyo, sādhiṭṭho.

395. Appassa kaṇa.

395. For 'appa', 'kaṇa' is substituted.

Sabbassa appasaddassa kaṇa hoti iyiṭṭhesu. Visesena appoti kaṇiyo, kaṇiṭṭho.

For the entire word 'appa', 'kaṇa' is substituted when the suffixes iyiṭṭha are present. Thus, in the sense of 'especially small,' the forms are kaṇiyo, kaṇiṭṭho.

“Visesena yuvā”ti atthe “kaṇa”iti vattate.

In the sense of 'especially young,' 'kaṇa' continues to be substituted.

396. Yuvānañca[M 0.0242].

396. And of 'yuvan'.

Sabbassa yuvasaddassa kaṇa hoti iyiṭṭhesu. “Tesu vuddhī”tiādinā ṇakārassa nakāro. Kaniyo, kaniṭṭho.

For the entire word 'yuvan', 'kaṇa' is the substitute when the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha' follow. By the rule 'Tesu vuddhī' and so on, the 'ṇ' becomes 'n'. Thus are formed kaniyo, kaniṭṭho.

397. Vantu mantu vīnañca lopo.

397. And elision of the suffixes vantu, mantu, and vī.

Vantumantuvī iccetesaṃ paccayānaṃ lopo hoti iyiṭṭhesu. Sabbe ime guṇavanto ayamimesaṃ visesena guṇavāti guṇiyo, guṇiṭṭho, visesena satimāti satiyo, satiṭṭho, visesena medhāvīti medhiyo, medhiṭṭho iccādi.

Elision of these suffixes, vantu, mantu, and vī, occurs when the suffixes 'iya' and 'iṭṭha' follow. Thus, in the sense of 'All these are endowed with qualities, but this one is especially endowed with qualities,' the forms are guṇiyo, guṇiṭṭho. In the sense of 'especially mindful,' the forms are satiyo, satiṭṭho. In the sense of 'especially wise,' the forms are medhiyo, medhiṭṭho, and so on.

Visesataddhitaṃ.

Taddhita Suffixes Denoting Distinction.

Assatthitaddhita

Taddhita Suffixes Denoting Possession.

“Medhā yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'Wisdom exists for him, or is found in him'—

398. Tadassatthīti vī ca.

398. And the suffix 'vī' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'.

Paṭhamāvibhatyantā “tadassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjati” iccetesvatthesu vīpaccayo hoti. Medhāmāyā saddehi cāyaṃ. Medhāvī, medhāvino. Itthiyaṃ īkārantattā “patibhikkhurājīkārantehi inī”ti inī, medhāvinī, medhāviniyo. Napuṃsake medhāvi kulaṃ. Evaṃ māyāvī, māyāvinī, māyāvi cittaṃ.

After a word ending in the first case-ending, the suffix 'vī' occurs in the senses 'that exists for him' or 'is found in him'. This suffix also occurs after the words 'medhā' and 'māyā'. Thus are formed medhāvī, medhāvino. In the feminine, because the stem ends in 'ī', the suffix 'inī' is added by the rule 'patibhikkhurājīkārantehi inī', forming medhāvinī, medhāviniyo. In the neuter: medhāvi kulaṃ. Similarly: māyāvī, māyāvinī, māyāvi cittaṃ.

Caggahaṇena so i lava ālādippaccayā ca. Yathā – sumedhā yassa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti sumedhaso, rassattaṃ. Evaṃ lomaso. Picchaṃ assa atthi, tasmiṃ [M 0.0243] vā vijjatīti picchilo. Evaṃ phenilo, tuṇḍilo, jaṭilo. Kesā assa atthīti kesavo, vācālo iccādi.

By the inclusion of 'ca', the suffixes 'sa', 'i', 'la', 'va', 'āla', and so on, also occur. For example: from 'good wisdom exists for him, or is found in him' comes sumedhaso, with shortening of the vowel. Similarly, lomaso. From 'feathers exist for him, or are found in him' comes picchilo. Similarly, phenilo, tuṇḍilo, jaṭilo. From 'hair exists for him' comes kesavo, vācālo, and so on.

“Tapo assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'Austerity exists for him, or is found in him'—

“Tadassatthī”ti adhikāro.

The term 'Tadassatthī' is the governing rule.

399. Tapādito sī.

399. From 'tapa' and so on, the suffix 'sī' occurs.

Tapaiccevamādito sīpaccayo hoti “tadassatthi” iccetasmiṃ atthe. Sassa dvibhāvo. Tapassī, tapassino, tapassinī, tapassi. Evaṃ tejassī, yasassī, manassī, payassī.

From 'tapa' and so on, the suffix 'sī' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'. The 'sa' is duplicated. Thus are formed tapassī, tapassino, tapassinī, tapassi. Similarly, tejassī, yasassī, manassī, payassī.

“Daṇḍo assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'A staff exists for him, or is found in him'—

400. Daṇḍādito ikaī.

400. From 'daṇḍa' and so on, the suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' occur.

Ādisaddoyaṃ pakārattho, daṇḍaiccevamādito avaṇṇantā ika ī iccete paccayā honti “tadassatthi” iccetasmiṃ atthe. Daṇḍiko, daṇḍī, daṇḍino, daṇḍinī. Evaṃ māliko, mālī, mālinī, chattiko, chattī, rūpiko, rūpī, kesiko, kesī, saṅghī, ñāṇī, hatthī iccādi.

This word 'ādi' has the meaning of 'kind' or 'type'. From words ending in 'a', such as 'daṇḍa' and so on, the suffixes 'ika' and 'ī' occur in the sense of 'that exists for him'. Thus are formed daṇḍiko, daṇḍī, daṇḍino, daṇḍinī. Similarly, māliko, mālī, mālinī; chattiko, chattī; rūpiko, rūpī; kesiko, kesī; saṅghī, ñāṇī, hatthī, and so on.

401. Madhvādito ro.

401. From 'madhu' and so on, the suffix 'ra' occurs.

Madhuādito rappaccayo hoti “tadassatthī”ti atthe. Madhu assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatīti madhuro guḷo, madhurā sakkharā, madhuraṃ khīraṃ, kuñjā hanū etassa santīti kuñjaro, sabbasmiṃ [M 0.0244] vattabbe mukhamassa atthīti mukharo, susi assa atthīti susiro. Evaṃ ruciro, nagaro.

From 'madhu' and so on, the suffix 'ra' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'. From 'honey exists for it, or is found in it' come madhuro guḷo (sweet molasses), madhurā sakkharā (sweet sugar), and madhuraṃ khīraṃ (sweet milk). From 'he has crooked jaws' comes kuñjaro (elephant). From 'he has a mouth for speaking on every matter' comes mukharo (talkative). From 'it has a hole' comes susiro (hollow). Similarly, ruciro (charming), nagaro (city-dweller).

“Guṇo assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'A quality exists for him, or is found in him'—

402. Guṇāditovantu.

402. From 'guṇa' and so on, the suffix 'vantu' occurs.

Guṇaiccevamādito vantuppaccayo hoti “tadassa atthī”ti atthe. Vibhattilope, nāmabyapadese ca kate syādyuppatti. Guṇavantu si, “savibhattissa, ntussā”ti adhikicca “ā simhī”ti āttaṃ, guṇavā puriso, sesaṃ ñeyyaṃ. Evaṃ gaṇavā, kulavā iccādayo. Itthiyaṃ “ṇava ṇika ṇeyyaṇantūhī”ti īpaccayo, “vā”ti vattamāne “ntussa tamīkāre”ti takāro, guṇavatī, guṇavantī iccādi. Napuṃsake “aṃ napuṃsake”ti savibhattissa ntussa amādeso, guṇavaṃ iccādi.

From 'guṇa' and so on, the suffix 'vantu' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'. After the elision of the case-ending and the designation as a nominal stem, the case-endings beginning with 'si' are generated. For example, from guṇavantu + si, under the governing rule 'savibhattissa, ntussā', the ending becomes 'ā' by the rule 'ā simhī', forming guṇavā puriso. The rest should be understood. Similarly, gaṇavā, kulavā, and so on. In the feminine, the suffix 'ī' is added by 'ṇava ṇika ṇeyyaṇantūhī'; while an optional rule is in effect, 'ntu' becomes 't' before 'ī' by 'ntussa tamīkāre', resulting in guṇavatī or guṇavantī, and so on. In the neuter, by 'aṃ napuṃsake', 'ntu' together with its case-ending is replaced by 'aṃ', resulting in guṇavaṃ, and so on.

“Sati assa atthi, tasmiṃ vā vijjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'Mindfulness exists for him, or is found in him'—

“Tadassatthī”ti vattate.

The term 'Tadassatthī' continues.

493. Satyādīhi mantu.

493. From 'sati' and so on, the suffix 'mantu' occurs.

Satiiccevamādīhi avaṇṇantarahitehi paṭhamāvibhatyantehi liṅgehi mantuppaccayo hoti “tadassatthī”ti atthe. Sesaṃ guṇavantusamaṃ. Satimā, satimatī, satimantī, satimaṃ. Evaṃ dhitimā, gatimā iccādayo.

From nominal stems such as 'sati' and so on, which do not end in 'a' and are declined in the first case, the suffix 'mantu' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'. The remaining process is the same as for 'guṇavantu'. Thus are formed satimā, satimatī, satimantī, satimaṃ. Similarly, dhitimā, gatimā, and so on.

Tathā “āyu assa atthīti āyu mantu”iccatra –

Likewise, in the case of 'life exists for him' from 'āyu mantu'—

404. Āyussukārāsamantumhi[M 0.0245].

404. For the 'u' of 'āyu', 'asa' is the substitute when 'mantu' follows.

Āyussa ukāro asa hoti mantumhīti asādeso. Āyasmā, sesaṃ samaṃ. Gāvo assa santīti gomā, gomanto, gomatī, gomantī, gomaṃ kulaṃ iccādi.

For the 'u' of 'āyu', 'asa' is the substitute when 'mantu' follows; this is the 'asa' substitution. Thus is formed āyasmā. The rest is the same. From 'cows exist for him' come gomā, gomanto, gomatī, gomantī, gomaṃ kulaṃ, and so on.

“Saddhā assa atthī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'Faith exists for him'—

405. Saddhādito ṇa.

405. From 'saddhā' and so on, the suffix 'ṇa' occurs.

Saddhā paññāiccevamādito ṇappaccayo hoti “tadassatthi”iccetasmiṃ atthe. Saddho puriso, saddhā kaññā, saddhaṃ kulaṃ. Evaṃ pañño, amaccharo, tathā buddhaṃ, buddhi assa atthīti buddho iccādi.

From 'saddhā', 'paññā', and so on, the suffix 'ṇa' occurs in the sense of 'that exists for him'. Thus are formed: saddho puriso (a faithful man), saddhā kaññā (a faithful maiden), saddhaṃ kulaṃ (a faithful family). Similarly, pañño (wise), amaccharo (not stingy). Likewise, from 'buddhi assa atthi' ('wisdom exists for him'), 'buddho' is formed, and so on.

Assatthitaddhitaṃ.

Taddhita suffixes denoting possession or existence.

Saṅkhyātaddhita

Saṅkhyātaddhita: The Taddhita Formation of Numerals

“Pañcannaṃ pūraṇo”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'pañcannaṃ pūraṇo' (the one that completes five) –

406. Saṅkhyāpūraṇe mo.

406. The suffix 'ma' is added in the sense of completing a number.

Pūrayati saṅkhyā anenāti pūraṇo, saṅkhyāya pūraṇo saṅkhyāpūraṇo, tasmiṃ saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe chaṭṭhiyantato mappaccayo hoti. Pañcamo, pañcannaṃ pūraṇī pañcamī, “nadādito vā ī”ti īpaccayo. “Itthiyamato āpaccayo”ti āpaccayo, pañcamā vīriyapāramī, pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ. Evaṃ sattamo, sattamī, sattamā, sattamaṃ, aṭṭhamo, aṭṭhamī, aṭṭhamā, aṭṭhamaṃ, navamo[M 0.0246], navamī, navamā, navamaṃ, dasamo, dasamī, dasamā, dasamaṃ iccādi.

That by which a number is completed is a 'pūraṇa'. The 'pūraṇa' of a number is 'saṅkhyāpūraṇa'. In that sense of 'saṅkhyāpūraṇa', the suffix 'ma' is added to a word ending in the sixth case. Thus, 'pañcamo' (fifth). The 'pūraṇī' (feminine completer) of five is 'pañcamī'. By the rule 'nadādito vā ī', the suffix 'ī' is added. By the rule 'itthiyamato āpaccayo', the suffix 'ā' is added. Thus, 'pañcamā vīriyapāramī' (the fifth perfection of energy), 'pañcamaṃ jhānaṃ' (the fifth jhāna). Similarly: 'sattamo' (seventh), 'sattamī' (seventh, fem.), 'sattamā' (seventh, fem.), 'sattamaṃ' (seventh, neut.); 'aṭṭhamo' (eighth), 'aṭṭhamī' (eighth, fem.), 'aṭṭhamā' (eighth, fem.), 'aṭṭhamaṃ' (eighth, neut.); 'navamo' (ninth), 'navamī' (ninth, fem.), 'navamā' (ninth, fem.), 'navamaṃ' (ninth, neut.); 'dasamo' (tenth), 'dasamī' (tenth, fem.), 'dasamā' (tenth, fem.), 'dasamaṃ' (tenth, neut.), and so on.

“Saṅkhyāpūraṇe”ti adhikāro.

The governing principle is 'saṅkhyāpūraṇe' (in the sense of completing a number).

407. Catucchehi thaṭhā.

407. From 'catu' and 'cha', the suffixes 'tha' and 'ṭha' are added.

Catuchaiccetehi thaṭhaiccete paccayā honti saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe. Catunnaṃ pūraṇo catuttho, dvittaṃ, catutthī, catutthā, catutthaṃ, channaṃ pūraṇo chaṭṭho, chaṭṭhī, chaṭṭhā, chaṭṭhaṃ, chaṭṭho eva chaṭṭhamo.

From 'catu' and 'cha', these suffixes 'tha' and 'ṭha' are added in the sense of completing a number. 'Catuttho' (fourth) is the 'pūraṇa' of four. Also: 'catutthī' (fourth, fem.), 'catutthā' (fourth, fem.), 'catutthaṃ' (fourth, neut.). 'Chaṭṭho' (sixth) is the 'pūraṇa' of six. Also: 'chaṭṭhī' (sixth, fem.), 'chaṭṭhā' (sixth, fem.), 'chaṭṭhaṃ' (sixth, neut.). 'Chaṭṭho' is also 'chaṭṭhamo'.

Chāhaṃ, chaḷāyatanaṃ iccatra –

In the case of 'chāhaṃ' and 'chaḷāyatanaṃ' –

408. Sa chassa vā.

408. Optionally, 'sa' is substituted for 'cha'.

Chassa sakārādeso hoti vā saṅkhyāne. Chāhamassa jīvitaṃ sāhaṃ, chāhaṃ vā, saḷāyatanaṃ.

For 'cha', the substitution of the letter 'sa' occurs optionally in the context of numerals. In the phrase 'chāham assa jīvitaṃ' ('his life is of six days'), 'chāhaṃ' becomes 'sāhaṃ', or optionally remains 'chāhaṃ'. Likewise, 'saḷāyatanaṃ' (the six sense bases).

“Dvinnaṃ pūraṇo”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'dvinnaṃ pūraṇo' (the one that completes two) –

409. Dvitīhi tiyo.

409. From 'dvi' and 'ti', the suffix 'tiya' is added.

Dvitiiccetehi tiyappaccayo hoti saṅkhyāpūraṇatthe. Vipariṇāmena “dvi tiṇṇa”nti vattamāne –

From 'dvi' and 'ti', the suffix 'tiya' is added in the sense of completing a number. By modification, when 'dvi' and 'tiṇṇaṃ' are present –

410. Tiye dutāpi ca.

410. When 'tiya' follows, 'du' and 'ta' are also substitutes.

Dvitiiccetesaṃ dutaiccādesā honti tiyappaccaye pare. Dutiyo puriso, dutiyā, dutiyaṃ. Evaṃ tiṇṇaṃ pūraṇo tatiyo, tatiyā, tatiyaṃ. Apiggahaṇena aññatthāpi dvisaddassa duādeso hoti, casaddena di ca. Dve rattiyo durattaṃ, duvidhaṃ, duvaṅgaṃ, dirattaṃ, diguṇaṃ, digu.

For 'dvi' and 'ti', the substitutes 'du' and 'ta' occur when the suffix 'tiya' follows. Thus: 'dutiyo puriso' (the second man), 'dutiyā' (second, fem.), 'dutiyaṃ' (second, neut.). Similarly, 'tatiyo' (third) is the 'pūraṇa' of three; also 'tatiyā' (third, fem.), 'tatiyaṃ' (third, neut.). By the inclusion of 'api', the substitute 'du' also occurs for the word 'dvi' elsewhere, and by the word 'ca', 'di' also occurs. Thus: 'dve rattiyo' (two nights) becomes 'durattaṃ'; also 'duvidhaṃ' (of two kinds), 'duvaṅgaṃ' (having two factors), 'dirattaṃ' (two nights), 'diguṇaṃ' (twofold), 'digu' (two cows).

411. Tesamaḍḍhūpapadena aḍḍhuḍḍhadivaḍḍhadiyaḍḍhaḍḍhatiyā.

411. For them, when 'aḍḍha' is a preceding word, the forms 'aḍḍhuḍḍha', 'divaḍḍha', 'diyaḍḍha', and 'aḍḍhatiya' are formed.

Tesaṃ catutthadutiyatatiyānaṃ aḍḍhūpapadānaṃ aḍḍhūpapadena saha aḍḍhuḍḍhadivaḍḍhadiyaḍḍhaaḍḍhatiyādesā honti.

For those words 'catuttha', 'dutiya', and 'tatiya', when preceded by 'aḍḍha', the substitutes 'aḍḍhuḍḍha', 'divaḍḍha', 'diyaḍḍha', and 'aḍḍhatiya' occur, inclusive of the preceding 'aḍḍha'.

Ettha ca –

And here it is said:

Aḍḍhūpapadapādāna-sāmatthā aḍḍhapubbakā;

Tesaṃsaddena gayhante, catutthadutiyādayo.

By the power of the statement mentioning 'aḍḍha' as a preceding word, the words preceded by 'aḍḍha' are understood; by the word 'tesaṃ' ('of them'), 'catuttha', 'dutiya', and so forth are taken.

Aḍḍhena catuttho aḍḍhuḍḍho, aḍḍhena dutiyo divaḍḍho, diyaḍḍho, aḍḍhena tatiyo aḍḍhatiyo.

'Aḍḍhena catuttho' (fourth with a half) is 'aḍḍhuḍḍho' (three and a half); 'aḍḍhena dutiyo' (second with a half) is 'divaḍḍho' or 'diyaḍḍho' (one and a half); 'aḍḍhena tatiyo' (third with a half) is 'aḍḍhatiyo' (two and a half).

“Ekañca dasa cā”ti atthe dvandasamāse, “ekena adhikā dasā”ti atthe tappurisasamāse vā kate “saṅkhyāne”ti vattamāne “dvekaṭṭhānamākāro vā”ti āttaṃ. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

When a dvandva compound is formed with the meaning 'ekaṃ ca dasa ca' (one and ten), or a tatpurisa compound with the meaning 'ekena adhikā dasā' (ten with one more), while 'saṅkhyāne' (in counting) is current, the substitution of 'ā' occurs according to the rule 'dvekaṭṭhānamākāro vā'. This word 'vā' here has the meaning of 'vavatthitavibhāsā' (a fixed option).

Tena cettha –

Therefore, here it is said:

Dvekaṭṭhānaṃ dase niccaṃ, dvissā’navutiyā navā;

Itaresa’masantañca, āttaṃ dīpeti vāsuti.

The word 'vā' indicates that the substitution to 'ā' is constant for 'dvi' and 'eka' before 'dasa'; it also occurs for 'dvi' up to 'nava' before 'navuti'; and for the others, it is non-existent.

“Ekādito dasara saṅkhyāne”ti rattaṃ.

By the rule 'ekādito dasara saṅkhyāne', 'ra' is substituted.

Rādeso vaṇṇamattattā, vaṇṇamattappasaṅgipi;

Siyā dasassa dasseva, nimittāsannabhāvato.

The 'ra' substitution, being merely a single letter, even if its application is to a single letter, would be for the 'da' of 'dasa', due to proximity to the cause.

Tato bahuvacanaṃ yo, “pañcādīnamakāro”ti savibhattissa antassa attaṃ. Ekārasa, ekādasa, liṅgattayepi samānaṃ.

Then, the plural suffix 'yo' is added. By the rule 'pañcādīnamakāro' ('the 'a' for 'pañca' and so forth'), the final vowel of the inflected word becomes 'a'. Thus: 'ekārasa' (eleven), 'ekādasa' (eleven). It is the same in all three genders.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' (optionally) is current.

412. Ekādito [M 0.0248] dasassī.

412. For `dasa` following `eka` and so forth, the suffix is `ī`.

Ekādito parassa dasassa ante īpaccayo hoti vā pūraṇatthe.

After `eka` and so forth, the suffix `ī` is optionally added at the end of `dasa` when it follows, in the sense of an ordinal number.

Dasassa paccayāyogā, laddhamanteti atthato;

Tadantassa sabhāvena, itthiyaṃyeva sambhavo.

Since the suffix cannot be applied to `dasa` alone, it is understood by the meaning to be at the end of a compound; by its nature, its occurrence is only possible in the feminine gender.

Ekādasannaṃ pūraṇī ekādasī, aññatra ekādasamo, ekādasamaṃ.

The feminine ordinal of eleven is `ekādasī`. Elsewhere it is `ekādasamo` (masculine) and `ekādasamaṃ` (neuter).

Dve ca dasa ca, dvīhi vā adhikā dasāti “dvi dasa”iccatra “vā”ti vattate.

When the meaning is 'two and ten' (`dve ca dasa ca`), or 'ten exceeded by two' (`dvīhi vā adhikā dasā`), in the case of `dvi dasa`, the rule concerning `vā` (optionally) is current.

“Vīsati dasesu bā dvissa tū”ti bādeso, dassa rādeso. Bārasa, aññatra āttaṃ, dvādasa. Dvādasannaṃ pūraṇo bārasamo, dvādasamo, dvādasī.

By the rule 'vīsati dasesu bā dvissa tū', `bā` is substituted, and `ra` is substituted for `dasa`. Thus, `bārasa`. Elsewhere, with lengthening to `ā`, `dvādasa`. The ordinal of twelve is `bārasamo`, `dvādasamo`, `dvādasī`.

Tayo ca dasa ca, tīhi vā adhikā dasāti terasa, “tesu vuddhi lopā”dinā tissa teādaso ānavutiyā, terasamo, terasī.

When the meaning is 'three and ten' (`tayo ca dasa ca`), or 'ten exceeded by three' (`tīhi vā adhikā dasā`), it becomes `terasa`. By the rule 'tesu vuddhi lopā' and so forth, `te` is substituted for `ti` up to ninety. The ordinals are `terasamo` and `terasī`.

Cattāro ca dasa ca, catūhi vā adhikā dasāti catuddasa iccatra “gaṇane dasassā”ti ca vattamāne “catūpapadassa lopo tuttarapadādi cassa cucopi navā”ti tulopo, cuco ca. Cuddasa, coddasa, catuddasa. Cuddasamo, catuddasamo, cakuddasī, cātuddasī vā.

When the meaning is 'four and ten' (`cattāro ca dasa ca`), or 'ten exceeded by four' (`catūhi vā adhikā dasā`), it is `catuddasa`. Here, while the rule 'gaṇane dasassā' is current, by the rule 'catūpapadassa lopo tuttarapadādi cassa cucopi navā', there is elision of `tu`, and also the substitutions `cu` and `co`. The forms are `cuddasa`, `coddasa`, `catuddasa`. The ordinals are `cuddasamo`, `catuddasamo`, `cakuddasī`, or `cātuddasī`.

Pañca ca dasa ca, pañcahi vā adhikā dasāti pañcadasa, “tesu vuddhi lopā”dinā pañcasaddassa dasa vīsesu pannapaṇṇaādesāpi, “aṭṭhādito cā”ti rattaṃ. Pannarasa, pañcadasa. Pannarasamo, pañcadasamo, pannarasī, pañcadasī.

When the meaning is 'five and ten' (`pañca ca dasa ca`), or 'ten exceeded by five' (`pañcahi vā adhikā dasā`), it is `pañcadasa`. By the rule 'tesu vuddhi lopā' and so forth, the substitutes `panna` and `paṇṇa` also occur for the word `pañca` in relation to `dasa` and `vīsa`. And by the rule 'aṭṭhādito ca', `ra` is substituted. Thus, `pannarasa` and `pañcadasa`. The ordinals are `pannarasamo`, `pañcadasamo`, `pannarasī`, `pañcadasī`.

“Cha [M 0.0249] ca dasa ca, chahi vā adhikā dasā”ti samāse kate “chassā”ti vattamāne “dase so niccañcā”ti so, “saṅkhyānaṃ, vā”ti ca vattate, “la darāna”nti lattaṃ, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

When a compound is formed with the meaning 'six and ten' (`cha ca dasa ca`), or 'ten exceeded by six' (`chahi vā adhikā dasā`), while 'chassa' is current, by the rule 'dase so niccañcā', `so` is substituted. And while 'saṅkhyānaṃ, vā' is current, by the rule 'la darāna', `la` is substituted. This word `vā` here has the meaning of a fixed option (`vavatthitavibhāsā`).

Ḷo niccaṃ soḷase dassa, cattālīse ca terase;

Aññatra na ca hotāyaṃ, vavatthitavibhāsato.

`Ḷa` is always substituted for `da` in `soḷasa` (sixteen), and in `cattālīsa` (forty), and in `terasa` (thirteen). Elsewhere, this does not occur, due to the principle of fixed option (`vavatthitavibhāsā`).

Laḷānamaviseso kvaci, soḷasa. Teḷasa, cattālīsaṃ, cattārīsaṃ. Soḷasamo, soḷasī.

Sometimes there is no distinction between `la` and `ḷa`. Thus, `soḷasa`. Also `teḷasa`, `cattālīsaṃ`, `cattārīsaṃ`. The ordinals are `soḷasamo`, `soḷasī`.

“Vā, dasara saṅkhyāne”ti adhikicca “aṭṭhādito cā”ti rattaṃ. Aṭṭhārasa, aṭṭhādasa, āttaṃ. Aṭṭhārasannaṃ pūraṇo aṭṭhārasamo, aṭṭhādasamo. Evaṃ sattarasa, sattadasa. Sattarasamo, sattadasamo.

Referring to the rules 'vā' and 'dasara saṅkhyāne', and by 'aṭṭhādito ca', `ra` is substituted. Thus, `aṭṭhārasa` and `aṭṭhādasa`, with lengthening to `ā`. The ordinal of eighteen is `aṭṭhārasamo`, `aṭṭhādasamo`. Similarly, `sattarasa`, `sattadasa`. The ordinals are `sattarasamo`, `sattadasamo`.

Aṭṭhāditoti kimatthaṃ? Catuddasa.

Why 'from `aṭṭha` onwards'? For the case of `catuddasa`.

Ekena ūnā vīsatīti tappuriso, ekūnavīsati. Ekūnavīsatādayo ānavutiyā ekavacanantā, itthiliṅgā ca daṭṭhabbā, te ca saṅkhyāne, saṅkhyeyye ca vattante, yadā saṅkhyāne vattante, tadā bhikkhūnamekūnavīsati tiṭṭhati, bhoti bhikkhūnamekūnavīsati tiṭṭhatu, bhikkhūnamekūnavīsatiṃ passa, bhikkhūnamekūnavīsatiyā kataṃ iccādi.

The tatpurisa compound `ekūnavīsati` (nineteen) means 'twenty diminished by one' (`ekena ūnā vīsati`). `Ekūnavīsati` and so forth, up to ninety, are to be understood as singular in form and feminine in gender. They are used in counting (`saṅkhyāne`) and in reference to counted objects (`saṅkhyeyye`). When used in counting, for example: `bhikkhūnaṃ ekūnavīsati tiṭṭhati` (a group of nineteen monks stands), `bhoti bhikkhūnamekūnavīsati tiṭṭhatu` (venerable sir, let the group of nineteen monks stand), `bhikkhūnamekūnavīsatiṃ passa` (see the group of nineteen monks), `bhikkhūnamekūnavīsatiyā kataṃ` (done by the group of nineteen monks), and so on.

Saṅkhyeyye pana ekūnavīsati bhikkhavo tiṭṭhanti, bhonto ekūnavīsati bhikkhavo tiṭṭhatha, ekūnavīsatiṃ bhikkhū passa, ekūnavīsatiyā bhikkhūhi kataṃ iccādi. Evaṃ vīsatādīsupi yojetabbaṃ, ekūnavīsatiyā pūraṇo ekūnavīsatimo.

However, when referring to counted objects (`saṅkhyeyye`): `ekūnavīsati bhikkhavo tiṭṭhanti` (nineteen monks stand), `bhonto ekūnavīsati bhikkhavo tiṭṭhatha` (venerable sirs, you nineteen monks, stand), `ekūnavīsatiṃ bhikkhū passa` (see the nineteen monks), `ekūnavīsatiyā bhikkhūhi kataṃ` (done by the nineteen monks), and so on. Similarly, this should be applied to `vīsati` and so forth. The ordinal of `ekūnavīsati` is `ekūnavīsatimo`.

Dasa ca dasa cāti atthe dvandasamāsaṃ katvā “dasadasā”ti vattabbe “sarūpānamekasesvasaki”nti ekasese kate [M 0.0250] dasasaddato paṭhamābahuvacanaṃ yo. “Dasa yo”itīdha –

When a dvandva compound is formed with the meaning 'ten and ten' (`dasa ca dasa ca`), where `dasadasā` should be said, after applying `ekasesa` (retention of a single form) according to the rule 'sarūpānamekasesvasaki', the first case plural suffix `yo` is added to the word `dasa`. Here, in the case of `dasa yo`–

413. Gaṇane dasassa dviti catu pañca cha satta aṭṭhanavakānaṃ vīti cattāra paññā cha sattāsa navā yosu yonañcī samāsaṃ ṭhiri tītuti.

413. In counting, for `dasa` preceded by `dvi`, `ti`, `catu`, `pañca`, `cha`, `satta`, `aṭṭha`, `nava`, the substitutes are `vī`, `ti`, `cattāra`, `paññā`, `cha`, `satta`, `asa`, `nava` when `yo` follows; and for `yo`, the substitutes are `ī`, `saṃ`, `ṭhi`, `ri`, `ti`, `uti` in a compound.

Gaṇane dasassa sambandhīnaṃ dvika tika catukka pañcaka chakkasattaka aṭṭhaka navakānaṃ katekasesānaṃ yathākkamaṃ vīti cattāra paññā cha satta asa nava iccādesā honti yosu paresu, yonañca īsaṃ āsaṃ ṭhi riti īti utiiccete ādesā hontīti dvidasatthavācakassa dasassa vīādeso hoti, yovacanassa īsañca, saralopādi.

In counting, for the words `dvika`, `tika`, `catukka`, `pañcaka`, `chakka`, `sattaka`, `aṭṭhaka`, `navaka`, which are related to `dasa` and have undergone `ekasesa`, the substitutes `vī`, `ti`, `cattāra`, `paññā`, `cha`, `satta`, `asa`, `nava` respectively occur when `yo` follows. And for `yo`, these substitutes `īsaṃ`, `āsaṃ`, `ṭhi`, `riti`, `īti`, `uti` occur. Thus, for `dasa` which expresses the meaning of two tens (i.e., twenty), the substitute `vī` occurs, and for the suffix `yo`, `īsaṃ` occurs, with elision of vowels and so on.

“Saṅkhyānaṃ, vā, ante”ti ca vattate.

And the rules 'saṅkhyānaṃ', 'vā', and 'ante' are current.

414. Ti ca.

414. And `ti`.

Tāsaṃ saṅkhyānamante tikārāgamo hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

For those numbers, the augment `ti` optionally occurs at the end. This word `vā` here has the meaning of a fixed option (`vavatthitavibhāsā`).

Vibhāsā vīsa tiṃsāna-mante hoti tiāgamo;

Aññattha na ca hoteva, vavatthitavibhāsato.

The optional augment `ti` occurs at the end of `vīsa` (twenty) and `tiṃsa` (thirty); elsewhere it does not occur, due to the principle of fixed option (`vavatthitavibhāsā`).

“Byañjane cā”ti niggahītalopo, puna taddhitattā nāmabyapadese syādyuppatti. Bhikkhūnaṃ vīsati, vīsaṃ vā, vīsati bhikkhū, vīsaṃ vā iccādi. Vīsatimo. Tathā ekavīsati kusalacittāni, ekavīsaṃ vā. Ekavīsatimo. Bāvīsati, bāvīsaṃ vā. Bāvīsatimo. Dvāvīsati, dvāvīsaṃ vā. Dvāvīsatimo. Tevīsati, tevīsaṃ vā. Tevīsatimo. Catuvīsati, catuvīsaṃ vā. Catuvīsatimo. Paṇṇavīsati, paṇṇavīsaṃ vā. Paṇṇavīsatimo. Pañcavīsati, pañcavīsaṃ vā. Pañcavīsatimo. Chabbīsati[M 0.0251], chabbīsaṃ vā. Chabbīsatimo. Sattavīsati, sattavīsaṃ vā. Sattavīsatimo. Aṭṭhavīsati, aṭṭhavīsaṃ vā. Aṭṭhavīsatimo. Ekūnatiṃsati, ekūnatiṃsaṃvā. Ekūnatiṃsatimo.

By the rule 'byañjane ca', the elision of the niggahīta occurs. Furthermore, due to its being a taddhita formation, upon its designation as a noun, case endings such as `si` arise. Thus: `bhikkhūnaṃ vīsati` (twenty of the monks), or `vīsaṃ`; `vīsati bhikkhū` (twenty monks), or `vīsaṃ`, and so on. The ordinal is `vīsatimo`. Similarly, `ekavīsati kusalacittāni` (twenty-one wholesome states of mind), or `ekavīsaṃ`. The ordinal is `ekavīsatimo`. `bāvīsati` (twenty-two), or `bāvīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `bāvīsatimo`. `dvāvīsati` (twenty-two), or `dvāvīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `dvāvīsatimo`. `tevīsati` (twenty-three), or `tevīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `tevīsatimo`. `catuvīsati` (twenty-four), or `catuvīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `catuvīsatimo`. `paṇṇavīsati` (twenty-five), or `paṇṇavīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `paṇṇavīsatimo`. `pañcavīsati` (twenty-five), or `pañcavīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `pañcavīsatimo`. `chabbīsati` (twenty-six), or `chabbīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `chabbīsatimo`. `sattavīsati` (twenty-seven), or `sattavīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `sattavīsatimo`. `aṭṭhavīsati` (twenty-eight), or `aṭṭhavīsaṃ`; the ordinal is `aṭṭhavīsatimo`. `ekūnatiṃsati` (twenty-nine), or `ekūnatiṃsaṃ`; the ordinal is `ekūnatiṃsatimo`.

Dasa ca dasa ca dasa cāti “dasa dasa dasā”ti vattabbe ekasese kate “gaṇane dasassā”tiādinā tiīsamādesā, “kvacā”dinā rassattaṃ, niggahītāgamo ca, sesaṃ vīsatisamaṃ. Tiṃsati, tiṃsaṃ, tiṃsa vassāni, niggahītalopo, tiṃsaṃ, tiṃsāya iccādi. Ekatiṃsati, ekatiṃsaṃ vā, bāttiṃsaṃ, dvattiṃsaṃ, tettiṃsaṃ iccādi.

When the meaning is 'ten and ten and ten' (`dasa ca dasa ca dasa ca`), where `dasa dasa dasā` should be said, after applying `ekasesa`, by the rule 'gaṇane dasassā' and so forth, the substitutes `ti` and `īsaṃ` occur; by the rule 'kvaci' and so forth, shortening occurs, and the augment of a niggahīta. The rest is similar to `vīsati`. Thus: `tiṃsati`, `tiṃsaṃ`. For example, `tiṃsa vassāni` (thirty years), with elision of the niggahīta; `tiṃsaṃ`, `tiṃsāya`, and so on. Also: `ekatiṃsati` (thirty-one), or `ekatiṃsaṃ`; `bāttiṃsaṃ` (thirty-two), `dvattiṃsaṃ` (thirty-two), `tettiṃsaṃ` (thirty-three), and so on.

Catudasatthavācakassa katekasesassa dasassa cattāra, yovacanassa īsaṃ, cattālīsaṃ, “la darāna”nti rassa lattaṃ, tālīsaṃ vā. Cattālīsatimo. Ekacattālīsaṃ, dvācattālīsaṃ, dvicattālīsaṃ, tecattālīsaṃ, ticattālīsaṃ iccādi.

For `dasa` which has undergone `ekasesa` and signifies four tens, `cattāra` is substituted, and for the suffix `yo`, `īsaṃ` is substituted, giving `cattālīsaṃ`. By 'la darāna', `la` is substituted for `ra`. An optional form is `tālīsaṃ`. The ordinal is `cattālīsatimo`. `ekacattālīsaṃ`, `dvācattālīsaṃ`, `dvicattālīsaṃ`, `tecattālīsaṃ`, `ticattālīsaṃ`, etc.

Pañcadasatthavācakassa dasassa paññā, yovacanassa āsañca. Paññāsaṃ, “tesu vuddhi lopā”dinā paṇṇādeso, paṇṇāsaṃ vā. Ekapaññāsaṃ, dvepaññāsaṃ, dvipaññāsaṃ.

For `dasa` signifying five tens, `paññā` is substituted, and for the suffix `yo`, `āsaṃ`. Thus, `paññāsaṃ`. By the rule 'tesu vuddhi lopā' and so on, there is the substitution of `paṇṇa`, giving the optional form `paṇṇāsaṃ`. `ekapaññāsaṃ`, `dvepaññāsaṃ`, `dvipaññāsaṃ`.

Chadasatthavācakassa dasassa cha, yovacanassa ṭhiādeso, “sa chassa vā”ti sakārādeso, saṭṭhi, dvāsaṭṭhi, dvesaṭṭhi, dvisaṭṭhi, tesaṭṭhi, tisaṭṭhi.

For `dasa` signifying six tens, the multiplier `cha` is used, and for the suffix `yo`, `ṭhi` is substituted. Also, by the rule 'sa chassa vā', `sa` is substituted for `cha`. Thus, `saṭṭhi`. `dvāsaṭṭhi`, `dvesaṭṭhi`, `dvisaṭṭhi` (sixty-two), `tesaṭṭhi`, `tisaṭṭhi` (sixty-three).

Sattadasatthavācakassa dasassa satta, yovacanassa ri, ti ca. Sattari, sattati, dvāsattari, dvāsattati, dvisattari, disattati, tesattati, tisattati iccādi.

For `dasa` signifying seven tens, the multiplier `satta` is used, and for the suffix `yo`, `ri` and `ti` are substituted. Thus, `sattari`, `sattati`. `dvāsattari`, `dvāsattati`, `dvisattari`, `disattati` (seventy-two), `tesattati`, `tisattati` (seventy-three), and so on.

Aṭṭhadasatthavācakassa dasassa asa, yovacanassa ītiādeso ca. Asīti, ekāsīti, dveasīti, teasīti, caturāsīti, “kvacā”dinā dīgho.

For `dasa` signifying eight tens, `asa` is substituted for the multiplier, and for the suffix `yo`, `īti` is substituted. Thus, `asīti`. `ekāsīti` (eighty-one), `dveasīti` (eighty-two), `teasīti` (eighty-three), `caturāsīti` (eighty-four). Lengthening occurs by the rule 'kvaci' and so on.

Navadasatthavācakassa [M 0.0252] dasassa nava, yovacanassa uti ca, navuti, dvānavuti, dvenavuti, dvinavuti, tenavuti, tinavuti, catunavuti, channavutiyā, channavutīnaṃ pāsaṇḍānaṃ.

For the word denoting ninety, 'nava' is substituted for 'dasa', and 'uti' for the syllable 'yo'. Thus, 'navuti' (ninety). 'Dvānavuti', 'dvenavuti', 'dvinavuti' (ninety-two); 'tenavuti', 'tinavuti' (ninety-three); 'catunavuti' (ninety-four). 'Channavutiyā' (by ninety-six); 'channavutīnaṃ pāsaṇḍānaṃ' (of the ninety-six sects).

“Gaṇane, dasassā”ti ca vattate.

The words 'gaṇane' (in counting) and 'dasassa' (of ten) are also carried forward.

415. Dasadasakaṃ sataṃ dasakānaṃ sataṃ sahassañca yomhi.

415. A group of ten tens is a hundred; a hundred tens is a thousand, in which 'yo' is understood.

Gaṇane pariyāpannassa dasadasakatthavācakassa dasasaddassa sataṃ hoti, satadasakatthavācakassa dasassa sahassaṃ hoti yomhi. Iminā nipātanena yolopo, taddhitattā puna nāmabyapadese syādyuppatti, niggahītassa lopo, “si”nti amādeso, yojanānaṃ sataṃ, sahassaṃ. Sataṃ napuṃsakamekavacanantañca, tathā sahassaṃ, vaggabhede sabbattha bahuvacanampi bhavati. Dve vīsatiyo. Evaṃ tiṃsādīsupi, dve satāni, bahūni satāni, dve sahassāni, bahūni sahassāni.

In counting, for the term expressing ten tens, 'dasa' becomes 'sata' (hundred); for the term expressing a hundred tens, 'dasa' becomes 'sahassa' (thousand), in which 'yo' is understood. By this special rule, there is elision of 'yo'. Being a derivative, case endings (syādi) arise again in nominal designation. There is elision of the niggahīta, and 'si' is substituted by 'am'. For example, 'yojanānaṃ sataṃ' (a hundred yojanas), 'sahassaṃ' (a thousand). 'Sata' is neuter and singular, and so is 'sahassa'. In the distinction of groups, the plural also occurs everywhere. For example, 'dve vīsatiyo' (two twenties). Similarly with thirties and so on: 'dve satāni' (two hundreds), 'bahūni satāni' (many hundreds), 'dve sahassāni' (two thousands), 'bahūni sahassāni' (many thousands).

Satassa dvikanti atthe chaṭṭhītappurisaṃ katvā “sataṃ dvika”nti vattabbe “dvikādīnaṃ taduttarapadānañca nipaccante”ti vuttiyaṃ vacanato iminā nipātanena uttarapadassa pubbanipāto, kakāralopo ca hoti. Dvisataṃ. Evaṃ satassa tikaṃ tisataṃ, tathā catusataṃ, pañcasataṃ, chasataṃ, sattasataṃ, aṭṭhasataṃ, navasataṃ, dasasataṃ sahassaṃ hoti. Atha vā dve satāni dvisatanti digusamāso. Evaṃ tisataṃ, catusataṃ iccādi.

In the sense of 'a pair of a hundred,' having formed a genitive tatpurisa compound, where 'sataṃ dvikaṃ' should be said, according to the statement in the commentary, 'for dvika and similar terms and their subsequent words, there is exceptional treatment,' by this exceptional rule, the subsequent term is preposed, and the letter 'ka' is elided. Thus, 'dvisataṃ' (two hundred). Similarly, 'tisataṃ' (three hundred) for 'a triad of a hundred', and so on: 'catusataṃ' (four hundred), 'pañcasataṃ' (five hundred), 'chasataṃ' (six hundred), 'sattasataṃ' (seven hundred), 'aṭṭhasataṃ' (eight hundred), 'navasataṃ' (nine hundred). 'Dasasataṃ' (ten hundred) is a thousand. Alternatively, 'dve satāni' (two hundreds) becomes 'dvisataṃ' as a digu compound. Similarly, 'tisataṃ', 'catusataṃ', and so on.

416. Yāva taduttari dasaguṇitañca.

416. And beyond that, it is multiplied by ten.

Yāva tāsaṃ saṅkhyānamuttari, tāva dasaguṇitañca kātabbaṃ, ettha dakāro sandhijo. Yathā – dasassa gaṇanassa dasaguṇitaṃ [M 0.0253] sataṃ hoti, satassa dasaguṇitaṃ sahassaṃ, sahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ dasasahassaṃ, idaṃ nahutantipi vuccati, dasasahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ satasahassaṃ, taṃ lakkhantipi vuccati, satasahassassa dasaguṇitaṃ dasasatasahassaṃ.

As far as those numbers are higher, they should be multiplied by ten. Here, the letter 'da' is due to sandhi. For example: ten times ten is a hundred; ten times a hundred is a thousand; ten times a thousand is ten thousand, which is also called 'nahuta'; ten times ten thousand is a hundred thousand, which is also called 'lakkha'; ten times a hundred thousand is ten hundred thousand.

“Yadanupapannā nipātanā sijjhantī”ti vattate.

The rule, 'Whatever is not regularly formed is accomplished by irregular formation,' is carried forward.

417. Sakanāmehi.

417. By their own names.

Yāsaṃ pana saṅkhyānaṃ aniddiṭṭhanāmadheyyānaṃ yāni rūpāni, tāni sakehi nāmehi nipaccante. Satasahassānaṃ sataṃ koṭi, itthiliṅgā, ekavacanantā ca, vaggabhede bahuvacanañca bhavati, koṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ pakoṭi, pakoṭisatasahassānaṃ sataṃ koṭippakoṭi. Evaṃ nahutaṃ, ninnahutaṃ, akkhobhinī, bindu, abbudaṃ, nirabbudaṃ, ahahaṃ, ababaṃ, aṭaṭaṃ, sogandhikaṃ, uppalaṃ, kumudaṃ, puṇḍarīkaṃ, padumaṃ, kathānaṃ, mahākathānaṃ, asaṅkhyeyyanti.

But for those numbers whose names are not specified, their forms are irregularly formed by their own names. A hundred hundred-thousands is a 'koṭi', which is feminine and singular, and in the distinction of groups, the plural also occurs. A hundred hundred-thousands of koṭis is a 'pakoṭi'. A hundred hundred-thousands of pakoṭis is a 'koṭippakoṭi'. Similarly, 'nahuta', 'ninnahuta', 'akkhobhinī', 'bindu', 'abbudaṃ', 'nirabbudaṃ', 'ahahaṃ', 'ababaṃ', 'aṭaṭaṃ', 'sogandhikaṃ', 'uppalaṃ', 'kumudaṃ', 'puṇḍarīkaṃ', 'padumaṃ', 'kathānaṃ', 'mahākathānaṃ', and 'asaṅkhyeyya'.

Iccevaṃ ṭhānato ṭhānaṃ, satalakkhaguṇaṃ mataṃ;

Koṭippabhutinaṃ vīsa-saṅkhyānañca yathākkamaṃ.

Thus, from place to place, it is considered multiplied by ten million; and for the twenty numbers beginning with koṭi, this is so in succession.

“Dve parimāṇāni etassā”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'Two are its measures'—

418. Dvādito konekatthe ca.

418. From 'dvi' onwards, the suffix 'ka' is added in a collective sense.

Dviiccevamādito gaṇanato kappaccayo hoti anekatthe. Dviko rāsi dvikaṃ. Evaṃ tikaṃ, catukkaṃ, pañcakaṃ, chakkaṃ, sattakaṃ, aṭṭhakaṃ, navakaṃ, dasakaṃ, paṇṇāsakaṃ, satakaṃ, sahassakaṃ iccādi.

From the numerals beginning with 'dvi', the suffix 'ka' occurs in a collective sense. A collection of two is 'dvikaṃ'. Similarly, 'tikaṃ' (a triad), 'catukkaṃ' (a tetrad), 'pañcakaṃ' (a pentad), 'chakkaṃ' (a hexad), 'sattakaṃ' (a heptad), 'aṭṭhakaṃ' (an octad), 'navakaṃ' (a nonad), 'dasakaṃ' (a decad), 'paṇṇāsakaṃ' (a group of fifty), 'satakaṃ' (a group of a hundred), 'sahassakaṃ' (a group of a thousand), and so on.

Saṅkhyātaddhitaṃ.

Numerical Derivatives.

Abyayataddhita

Indeclinable Derivatives.

“Ekasmiṃ [M 0.0254] vāre bhuñjati, dvivāre bhuñjatī”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'He eats on one occasion, he eats on two occasions'—

419. Ekādito sakissa kkhattuṃ.

419. From 'eka' onwards, 'kkhattuṃ' is added in place of 'saki'.

Ekadvitiiccevamādito gaṇanato sakissa ṭhāne vāratthe kkhattuṃpaccayo hoti. Ekakkhattuṃ, dvikkhattuṃ bhuñjati, “sabbāsamāvuso”tiādinā silopo. Evaṃ tikkhattuṃ, catukkhattuṃ, pañcakkhattuṃ, chakkhattuṃ, sattakkhattuṃ, aṭṭhakkhattuṃ, navakkhattuṃ, dasakkhattuṃ, satakkhattuṃ, sahassakkhattuṃ, bahukkhattuṃ, katikkhattuṃ.

From the numerals beginning with 'eka', 'dvi', 'ti', and so on, the suffix 'kkhattuṃ' occurs in place of 'saki' in the sense of 'times'. He eats once ('ekakkhattuṃ'), twice ('dvikkhattuṃ'); the elision of 'si' occurs according to the rule beginning 'sabbāsamāvuso'. Likewise, thrice ('tikkhattuṃ'), four times ('catukkhattuṃ'), five times ('pañcakkhattuṃ'), six times ('chakkhattuṃ'), seven times ('sattakkhattuṃ'), eight times ('aṭṭhakkhattuṃ'), nine times ('navakkhattuṃ'), ten times ('dasakkhattuṃ'), a hundred times ('satakkhattuṃ'), a thousand times ('sahassakkhattuṃ'), many times ('bahukkhattuṃ'), how many times ('katikkhattuṃ').

“Ekena vibhāgenā”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, 'By one division'—

Maṇḍūkagatiyā saṅkhyāggahaṇamanuvattate.

The taking of 'number' is carried forward by 'frog's leap'.

420. Vibhāge dhā ca.

420. And 'dhā' in the sense of division.

Vibhāgatthe ekādisaṅkhyāto dhāpaccayo hoti. Casaddena ekadvito jjha ca, suttādito so ca. Ekadhā. Dvīhi vibhāgehi dvidhā, dudhā vā, dvedhā. Tīhi vibhāgehi tidhā, tedhā vā, “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā ikārassekāro. Evaṃ catudhā, pañcadhā, chadhā, sattadhā, aṭṭhadhā, navadhā, dasadhā, satadhā, sahassadhā, katidhā, bahudhā.

In the sense of division, the suffix 'dhā' occurs after numerals beginning with 'eka'. And by the word 'ca', 'jjha' also occurs after 'eka' and 'dvi'; and 'so' after 'sutta' and so on. 'Ekadhā' (in one way). By two divisions, 'dvidhā', or 'dudhā', or 'dvedhā'. By three divisions, 'tidhā', or 'tedhā'; the vowel 'i' becomes 'e' according to the rule beginning 'tesu vuddhī'. Likewise, 'catudhā' (fourfold), 'pañcadhā' (fivefold), 'chadhā' (sixfold), 'sattadhā' (sevenfold), 'aṭṭhadhā' (eightfold), 'navadhā' (ninefold), 'dasadhā' (tenfold), 'satadhā' (hundredfold), 'sahassadhā' (thousandfold), 'katidhā' (how manyfold), 'bahudhā' (manifold).

Jjhappaccaye ekadhā karotīti ekajjhaṃ. Evaṃ dvejjhaṃ.

With the suffix 'jjha', the form is 'ekajjhaṃ' (in one place, together). Likewise, 'dvejjhaṃ' (in two places).

Sopaccaye suttena vibhāgena suttaso. Evaṃ byañjanaso, padaso, atthaso, bahuso, sabbākārena sabbaso[M 0.0255], upāyaso, hetuso, ṭhānaso, yoniso.

With the suffix 'so', from 'suttena vibhāgena' (by division according to the Sutta) comes 'suttaso'. Likewise, 'byañjanaso' (syllable by syllable), 'padaso' (word by word), 'atthaso' (meaning by meaning), 'bahuso' (in many ways), 'sabbaso' (in every way, from 'sabbākārena'), 'upāyaso' (by method, skillfully), 'hetuso' (by cause), 'ṭhānaso' (by place), 'yoniso' (thoroughly, systematically).

421. Sabbanāmehi pakāravacane tu thā.

421. But from pronouns, 'thā' is used in the sense of manner.

Sabbanāmehi pakāravacanatthe thāpaccayo hoti, tusaddena thattāpaccayo ca. Sāmaññassa bhedako viseso pakāro, tassābhidhāneti attho, so pakāro tathā, taṃ pakāraṃ tathā, tena pakārena tathā, yena pakārena yathā. Evaṃ sabbathā, aññathā, itarathā, ubhayathā, thattāpaccaye tena pakārena tathattā. Evaṃ yathattā, aññathattā.

From pronouns, the suffix 'thā' occurs in the sense of expressing manner; and by the word 'tu', the suffix 'tattā' also occurs. Manner ('pakāro') is a specific ('viseso') which distinguishes the general ('sāmaññassa'); the meaning is in the expression of that. 'So pakāro' (that manner) is 'tathā'; 'taṃ pakāraṃ' (in that manner) is 'tathā'; 'tena pakārena' (by that manner) is 'tathā'; 'yena pakārena' (by which manner) is 'yathā'. Thus, 'sabbathā' (in all ways), 'aññathā' (otherwise), 'itarathā' (in another way), 'ubhayathā' (in both ways). With the suffix 'tattā', from 'tena pakārena' comes 'tathattā'. Likewise, 'yathattā', 'aññathattā'.

Ko pakāroti atthe –

In the sense of 'what manner?'—

422. Kimimehi thaṃ.

422. From 'kiṃ' and 'ima', 'thaṃ' is added.

Kiṃimaiccetehi thaṃpaccayo hoti pakāravacanatthe. “Kissa ka ve cā”ti ettha casaddena kissa kādeso. Kathaṃ, kaṃ pakāraṃ kathaṃ, kena pakārena kathaṃ, ayaṃ pakāro itthaṃ, imaṃ pakāraṃ itthaṃ. Anena pakārena itthaṃ, “imassi thaṃ dāniha to dhesu cā”ti imasaddassa ikāro, dvittaṃ. Ettha hi kkhattuṃ ādithaṃpariyosānappaccayantānaṃ abyayataddhitattā nāmabyapadesaṃ katvā vibhattimhi kate “sabbāsamāvuso”tiādinā vibhattilopo, “kvaci to pañcamyatthe”tiādinā vuttatoādippaccayantā ca idheva abyayataddhite saṅgayhanti.

From 'kiṃ' and 'ima', the suffix 'thaṃ' occurs in the sense of expressing manner. In the rule 'kissa ka ve ca', by the word 'ca', 'ka' is substituted for 'kiṃ'. 'Kathaṃ' (how?); 'kaṃ pakāraṃ kathaṃ' (in what manner, how?); 'kena pakārena kathaṃ' (by what manner, how?). 'Ayaṃ pakāro itthaṃ' (this manner is thus); 'imaṃ pakāraṃ itthaṃ' (in this manner, thus); 'anena pakārena itthaṃ' (by this manner, thus). By the rule 'imassi thaṃ dāniha to dhesu ca', the word 'ima' is substituted by 'i', and there is doubling. Indeed, here, because words ending in suffixes beginning with 'kkhattuṃ' and ending with 'thaṃ' are indeclinable derivatives, after the nominal designation is made and a case ending is applied, the case ending is elided according to the rule beginning 'sabbāsamāvuso'. And words ending in suffixes beginning with 'to', mentioned in the rule beginning 'kvaci to pañcamyatthe', are also included here in the indeclinable derivatives.

423. Yadanupapannā [M 0.0256] nipātanā sijjhanti.

423. Those forms which are not derived [by rule] are established by irregular formation (nipātana).

Ye saddā lakkhaṇena anupapannā aniddiṭṭhalakkhaṇā akkharādito, nāmopasagganipātato vā samāsataddhitādito vā, te nipātanā sijjhanti.

Those words which are not derived by rule, not having an indicated rule—whether from letters and so forth, from nouns, prefixes, or particles, or from compounds, derivatives, and so forth—are established by irregular formation (nipātana).

Taddhitato tāva –

From the Taddhita [section], to begin with—

Imasmā jja siyā kāle, samānāparato jju ca;

Imasaddassa’kāro ca, samānassa ca so siyā.

From 'ima', 'jja' may occur in the sense of time; and from 'samāna' and 'apara', 'jju' also [occurs]. And [the stem] 'ima' becomes 'a', and [the stem] 'samāna' becomes 'sa'.

Imasmiṃ kāle, imasmiṃ divase vā ajja, samāne kāle sajju, aparasmiṃdivase aparajju. Nipātehi bhavatthe tanappaccayo. Ajja bhavaṃ ajjatanaṃ, ajja bhavā ajjatanī, sve bhavaṃ svātanaṃ. Evaṃ purātanaṃ, hiyyo bhavaṃ hiyyattanaṃ, hiyyo bhavā hiyyattanī iccādi.

In this time, or on this day, [it becomes] ajja (today); in the same time, sajju (immediately); on a subsequent day, aparajju. From indeclinables, the suffix 'tana' occurs in the sense of 'being' (bhavatthe). That which is of today is ajjatanaṃ; that which is of today (feminine) is ajjatanī. That which is of tomorrow is svātanaṃ. Likewise, purātanaṃ (ancient); that which was of yesterday is hiyyattanaṃ; that which was of yesterday (feminine) is hiyyattanī, and so on.

Abyayataddhitaṃ.

Derivatives from Indeclinables.

Sāmaññavuttibhāvatthā-byayato taddhitaṃ tidhā;

Tatrādi catudhāpaccā-nekatthassatthisaṅkhyāto.

The derivative from indeclinables is threefold: in the sense of generality, usage, and being. Among these, the first is fourfold by way of suffixes in the sense of various meanings, existence, and number.

Iti padarūpasiddhiyaṃ taddhitakaṇḍo

Thus, the section on Taddhita in the Padarūpasiddhi.

Pañcamo.

The Fifth.

6. Ākhyātakaṇḍa

6. The Section on Verbal Inflection

Bhūvādigaṇa

The Bhū Group

Vibhattividhāna

The Rules for Inflections

Atha [M 0.0257] ākhyātavibhattiyo kriyāvācīhi dhātūhi parā vuccante.

Now, verbal inflections are said to occur after roots that express action.

Tattha kriyaṃ ācikkhatīti ākhyātaṃ, kriyāpadaṃ. Vuttañhi “kālakārakapurisaparidīpakaṃ kriyālakkhaṇamākhyātika”nti. Tattha kāloti atītādayo, kārakamiti kammakattubhāvā, purisāti paṭhamamajjhimuttamā, kriyāti gamanapacanādiko dhātvattho, kriyālakkhaṇaṃ saññāṇaṃ etassāti kriyālakkhaṇaṃ, atiliṅgañca.

Here, that which declares an action is called an `ākhyāta`, a verb. For it has been said: 'That which illuminates time, agent, and person, having the characteristic of action, is a verbal form (`ākhyātika`).' Here, 'time' means the past and so on; 'agent' (`kāraka`) means the state of being object, subject, or the action itself; 'person' means the third, second, and first persons; 'action' means the meaning of a root, such as going, cooking, and so on; `kriyālakkhaṇaṃ` means that which has the sign of action; and it is also beyond gender (`atiliṅga`).

Vuttampi cetaṃ –

And this has also been said:

“Yaṃ tikālaṃ tipurisaṃ, kriyāvāci tikārakaṃ;

Atiliṅgaṃ dvivacanaṃ, tadākhyātanti vuccatī”ti.

"That which has three times, three persons, expresses action, has three agents, is beyond gender, and has two numbers—that is called a verb."

Kālādivasena dhātvatthaṃ vibhajantīti vibhattiyo, tyādayo, tā pana vattamānā pañcamī sattamī parokkhāhiyyattanī ajjatanī bhavissantī kālātipatti cāti aṭṭhavidhā bhavanti.

Because they divide the meaning of the root according to time and so on, the endings beginning with 'ti' are called 'inflections' (vibhattiyo). These are of eight kinds: present (vattamānā), imperative (pañcamī), optative (sattamī), perfect (parokkhā), imperfect (hiyyattanī), aorist (ajjatanī), future (bhavissantī), and conditional (kālātipatti).

Kriyaṃ dhārentīti dhātavo, bhūvādayo, khādidhātuppaccayantā ca, te pana atthavasā dvidhā bhavanti sakammakā, akammakā cāti. Tatra sakammakā ye dhātavokammāpekkhaṃ kriyaṃ vadanti, yathā – kaṭaṃ karoti, gāmaṃ gacchati, odanaṃ pacatītiādayo, akammakā ye kammanirapekkhaṃ kriyaṃ vadanti, yathā – acchati, seti, tiṭṭhatītiādayo.

Because they bear action, they are called roots (dhātus), such as the 'bhū' group and those ending with suffixes forming roots like 'khādi'. These, however, are of two kinds based on their meaning: transitive (sakammakā) and intransitive (akammakā). Among them, transitive roots are those that express an action that requires an object, such as 'makes a mat', 'goes to the village', 'cooks rice', and so on. Intransitive roots are those that express an action that does not require an object, such as 'sits', 'lies down', 'stands', and so on.

Te [M 0.0258] pana sattavidhā bhavanti vikaraṇappaccayabhedena, kathaṃ? Avikaraṇā bhūvādayo. Niggahītapubbakaavikaraṇā rudhādayo, yavikaraṇā divādayo, ṇuṇā uṇāvikaraṇā svādayo, nāppaṇhāvikaraṇā kiyādayo, oyiravikaraṇā tanādayo, sakatthe ṇe ṇayantā curādayoti.

These, however, are of seven kinds due to distinctions in the conjugational sign (vikaraṇa) suffixes. How? The 'bhū' group is without a vikaraṇa. The 'rudh' group is without a vikaraṇa but with a preceding nasal. The 'div' group has the 'ya' vikaraṇa. The 'su' group has the 'ṇu' and 'uṇā' vikaraṇas. The 'ki' group has the 'nā' and 'ṇhā' vikaraṇas. The 'tan' group has the 'o' and 'yira' vikaraṇas. The 'cur' group, in their own meaning, has the 'ṇe' and 'ṇaya' vikaraṇas.

Tattha paṭhamaṃ avikaraṇesu bhūvādīsu dhātūsu paṭhamabhūtā akammakā bhūiccetasmā dhātuto tyādayo parā yojīyante.

Here, first, among the roots of the 'bhū' group which are without a conjugational sign, from the root 'bhū', which is primary and intransitive, the suffixes beginning with 'ti' are added after.

Bhūsattāyaṃ, “bhū”iccayaṃ dhātu sattāyamatthe vattate, kriyāsāmaññabhūte bhavane vattateti attho.

'Bhū' is in the sense of 'being' (sattāyaṃ). This root 'bhū' occurs in the sense of 'being'; the meaning is that it occurs in the sense of 'becoming' (bhavana), which is the general nature of action.

“Bhū”iti ṭhite –

When 'bhū' stands thus—

424. Bhūvādayo dhātavo.

424. 'Bhū' and so on are roots.

Bhūiccevamādayo ye kriyāvācino saddagaṇā, te dhātusaññā honti. Bhū ādi yesaṃ te bhūvādayo, atha vā bhūvā ādī pakārā yesaṃ te bhūvādayo.

Those groups of words which express action, such as 'bhū' and so on, are designated as roots. 'Bhūvādayo' means those of which 'bhū' is the beginning. Or alternatively, 'bhūvādayo' means those of which 'bhū' and so forth are the types.

Bhūvādīsu vakāroyaṃ, ñeyyo āgamasandhijo;

Bhūvāppakārā vā dhātū, sakammākammakatthato.

In 'bhūvādīsu', this 'va' is to be understood as arising from an augmentative sandhi. Or, roots of the 'bhū' type are [classified] according to the sense of being transitive or intransitive.

“Kvaci dhātū”tiādito “kvacī”ti vattate.

From the rule beginning 'Kvaci dhātū', the word 'kvaci' carries forward.

425. Dhātussanto loponekassarassa.

425. The final [vowel] of a root consisting of more than one vowel is elided.

Anekassarassa dhātussa anto kvaci lopo hoti.

Sometimes, the final [vowel] of a root consisting of more than one vowel is elided.

Kvaciggahaṇaṃ “mahīyati samatho”tiādīsu nivattanatthaṃ, iti anekassarattābhāvā idha dhātvantalopo na hoti.

The inclusion of 'kvaci' is for the purpose of preventing [the rule's application] in cases like 'mahīyati samatho' and so on. Thus, because there is no polysyllabic root here, the elision of the final [vowel] of the root does not occur.

Tato [M 0.0259] dhātvādhikāravihitānekappaccayappasaṅge “vatticchānupubbikā saddappaṭipattī”ti katvā vattamānavacanicchāyaṃ –

Then, when there is the possibility of applying the many suffixes prescribed under the governing rule for roots, having established that 'the application of words proceeds according to the speaker's intention', when there is a desire to express the present tense—

426. Vattamānā tianti, sitha, mima, teante, sevhe, emhe.

426. The present tense endings are: ti, anti; si, tha; mi, ma; te, ante; se, vhe; e, mhe.

Tyādayo dvādasa vattamānāsaññā hontīti tyādīnaṃ vattamānatthavisayattā vattamānāsaññā.

The twelve endings beginning with 'ti' are designated as 'vattamānā' (present) because they pertain to the meaning of the present tense.

427. Kāle.

427. In time.

Ayamadhikāro.

This is a governing rule.

Ito paraṃ tyādivibhattividhāne sabbattha vattate.

From here onward, this applies everywhere in the rules for the conjugational endings beginning with 'ti'.

428. Vattamānā paccuppanne.

428. The present tense endings occur in the present time.

Paccuppanne kāle gamyamāne vattamānāvibhatti hoti, kāloti cettha kriyā, karaṇaṃ kāro, rakārassa lakāro, kālo.

When the present time is understood, the present tense inflection occurs. And here, 'kālo' is action; the doing ('karaṇaṃ') is 'kāro'; the letter 'ra' becomes the letter 'la', thus 'kālo'.

Tasmā –

Therefore—

Kriyāya gamyamānāya, vibhattīnaṃ vidhānato;

Dhātūheva bhavantīti, siddhaṃ tyādivibhattiyo.

When action is understood, due to the prescription of the conjugational endings, it is established that the inflections beginning with 'ti' occur only after roots.

Idha pana kālassa atītānāgatapaccuppannāṇattiparikappakālābhipattivasena chadhā bhinnattā “paccuppanne”ti viseseti. Taṃ taṃ kāraṇaṃ paṭicca uppanno paccuppanno, paṭiladdhasabhāvo, na tāva atītoti attho.

Here, however, because time is divided sixfold by way of past, future, present, imperative, optative, and conditional, it is specified as 'in the present'. That which has arisen dependent on a particular cause is 'paccuppanna' (present); it has attained its own nature, meaning it is not yet past.

Paccuppannasamīpepi, tabbohārūpacārato;

Vattamānā atītepi, taṃkālavacanicchayāti.

The present tense may be used even in proximity to the present, due to conventional and metaphorical usage; and even in the past, according to the speaker's intention regarding that time.

Tasmiṃ paccuppanne vattamānāvibhattiṃ katvā, tassā ṭhānāniyame “dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā”ti paribhāsato dhātuto [M 0.0260] paraṃ vattamānappaccaye katvā, tesamaniyamappasaṅgesati “vatticchānupubbikā saddappaṭipattī”ti parassapadavacanicchāyaṃ –

Having applied the present tense inflection in that present time, and when there is no fixed rule for its position, having applied the present tense suffix after the root according to the maxim 'suffixes follow roots and nominal stems', and when there is a possibility of their being unregulated, and with the understanding that 'the formation of a word follows the sequence of the speaker's intention', when there is a desire to express the active voice—

429. Atha pubbāni vibhattīnaṃ cha parassapadāni.

429. Now, the first six of the conjugational endings are 'parassapada' (active voice).

Atha taddhitānantaraṃ vuccamānānaṃ sabbāsaṃ vattamānādīnaṃ aṭṭhavidhānaṃ vibhattīnaṃ yāni yāni pubbakāni cha padāni, tāni tāni atthato aṭṭhacattālīsamattāni parassapadasaññāni hontītiādimhi channaṃ parassapadasaññā, parassatthāni padāni parassapadāni, tabbāhullato tabbohāro.

Then, after the Taddhita section, of all the eight kinds of conjugational endings being stated, beginning with the present, the first six forms—amounting to forty-eight in total—are designated as 'parassapada'. Thus, the designation 'parassapada' is for the first six. Forms having the meaning 'for another' are 'parassapada'; this usage is due to their prevalence.

“Dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya”iccādito “dhātūhī”ti vattamāne –

From the rule beginning 'dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya', when 'dhātūhi' (from roots) continues to apply—

430. Kattari parassapadaṃ.

430. The active voice ('parassapada') occurs in the sense of the agent.

Kattarikārake abhidheyye sabbadhātūhi parassapadaṃ hotīti parassapadaṃ katvā, tassāpyaniyamappasaṅge vatticchāvasā –

When the agent-case is to be expressed, the active voice occurs after all roots. Thus, having established the active voice, and when there is a possibility of its being unregulated, according to the speaker's intention—

Vipariṇāmena “parassapadānaṃ, attanopadāna”nti ca vattate.

By modification of the case ending, 'of the active voice forms' and 'of the middle voice forms' also continues to apply.

431. Dve dve paṭhamamajjhimuttamapurisā.

431. Two each are the third, second, and first persons.

Tāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ parassapadāna’mattanopadānañca dve dve vacanāni yathākkamaṃ paṭhamamajjhimuttamapurisasaññāni honti. Taṃ yathā? Ti antiiti paṭhamapurisā, si thaiti majjhimapurisā, mi maiti uttamapurisā. Attanopadesupi te anteiti paṭhamapurisā, se vheiti majjhimapurisā, e mheiti uttamapurisā. Evaṃ sesāsu sattasu vibhattīsupi yojetabbanti[M 0.0261]. Evaṃ aṭṭhavibhattivasena channavutividhe ākhyātapade dvattiṃsa dvattiṃsa paṭhamamajjhimauttamapurisā hontīti vattamānaparassapadādimhi dvinnaṃ paṭhamapurisasaññā.

Of those inflections, for both the active and middle voice forms, the two endings for each number are designated, respectively, as third, second, and first person. How so? 'ti, anti' are the third person; 'si, tha' are the second person; 'mi, ma' are the first person. In the middle voice also: 'te, ante' are the third person; 'se, vhe' are the second person; 'e, mhe' are the first person. This should be applied to the remaining seven inflections as well. Thus, by way of the eight inflections, among the ninety-six kinds of verbal forms, there are thirty-two each for the third, second, and first persons. In this way, in the present active voice and so on, the designation 'third person' is for two endings.

432. Nāmamhi payujjamānepitulyādhikaraṇe paṭhamo.

432. When a noun in apposition is used, the third person is employed.

Tumhāmhasaddavajjite tulyādhikaraṇabhūte sādhakavācake nāmamhi payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi dhātūhi paṭhamapuriso hotīti paṭhamapurisaṃ katvā, tassāpyaniyamappasaṅge kriyāsādhakassa kattuno ekatte vattumicchite “ekamhi vattabbe ekavacana”nti vattamānaparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ ti.

When a noun that indicates the agent, is in apposition, and is other than the words 'tumha' (you) and 'amha' (I), is either used or not used, the third person occurs after the root. Thus, having established the third person, and when there is a possibility of its being unregulated, and when it is desired to express the singularity of the agent that accomplishes the action, according to the rule 'when one is to be expressed, the singular number is used', the result is 'ti', the singular of the third person of the present active voice.

“Paro, paccayo, dhātū”ti ca adhikāro, “yathā kattari cā”ti ito “kattarī”ti vikaraṇappaccayavidhāne sabbattha vattate.

The terms 'after', 'suffix', and 'from a root' are governing rules. And from the rule 'yathā kattari ca', the word 'kattari' (in the agent) applies everywhere in the rules for vikaraṇa suffixes.

433. Bhūvādito a.

433. After the 'bhū' group of roots, 'a'.

Bhūiccevamādito dhātugaṇato paro apaccayo hoti kattari vihitesu vibhattippaccayesu paresu. Sabbadhātukamhiyevāyamissate.

After the group of roots beginning with 'bhū', the suffix 'a' occurs when the inflectional suffixes prescribed for the agent follow. This is desired only when a 'sabbadhātuka' suffix follows.

“Asaṃyogantassa, vuddhī”ti ca vattate.

And 'of that which does not end in a conjunct consonant' and 'vuddhi' also continue to apply.

434. Aññesu ca.

434. And before other suffixes.

Kāritato aññesu paccayesu asaṃyogantānaṃ dhātūnaṃ vuddhi hoti. Caggahaṇena ṇuppaccayassāpi vuddhi hoti. Ettha ca “ghaṭādīnaṃ vā”ti ito vāsaddo anuvattetabbo, so ca vavatthitavibhāsattho. Tena –

Before suffixes other than the causative, 'vuddhi' occurs for roots not ending in a conjunct consonant. By the inclusion of 'ca', 'vuddhi' also occurs for the 'ṇu'-suffix. And here, the word 'vā' from 'ghaṭādīnaṃ vā' should be carried forward, and it has the meaning of a restricted option. Therefore—

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇantānañca, lahūpantāna dhātunaṃ;

Ivaṇṇuvaṇṇānameva, vuddhi hoti parassa na.

For roots ending in the vowels 'i' or 'u', and for roots with a light penultimate vowel, 'vuddhi' occurs only for the 'i' and 'u' vowels themselves, not for that which follows.

Yuvaṇṇānampi [M 0.0262] ya ṇu ṇā-nāniṭṭhādīsu vuddhi na;

Tudādissāvikaraṇe, na chetvādīsu vā siyā.

For the vowels 'i' and 'u', 'vuddhi' also does not occur before suffixes such as 'ya', 'ṇu', 'ṇā', 'nā', and other undesired ones; in the 'a'-vikaraṇa of the 'tud' class, it does not occur; and before 'tvā' and other such suffixes, it is optional.

Tassāpyaniyamappasaṅge – “ayuvaṇṇānañcāyo vuddhī”ti paribhāsato ūkārassokāro vuddhi.

Also, in the case of this being without a specific restriction, according to the technical rule, 'The vuddhi of the vowels a, i, and u are ā, e, and o,' the vuddhi of the vowel 'u' is 'o'.

Vipariṇāmena “dhātūna”nti vattate.

By inversion, 'of roots' is said to apply.

435. O ava sare.

435. The 'o' becomes 'av' when a vowel follows.

Okārassa dhātvantassa sare pare avādeso hoti. “Saralopo mādesa”iccādinā saralopādimhi kate “naye paraṃ yutte”ti paranayanaṃ kātabbaṃ.

For a root ending in the vowel 'o', when a vowel follows, there is the substitution 'av'. When vowel elision and so forth have been performed according to the rule beginning 'Elision of a vowel, substitution of m...', the following consonant should be brought forward according to the principle 'Bring forward the following when joined'.

So puriso sādhu bhavati, sā kaññā sādhu bhavati, taṃ cittaṃ sādhu bhavati.

That man is good, that maiden is good, that mind is good.

Ettha hi –

Here, indeed—

Kattunobhihitattāva, ākhyātena na kattari;

Tatiyā paṭhamā hoti, liṅgatthaṃ panapekkhiya.

Because the agent is indeed expressed by the verbal ending, the instrumental is not used for the agent; the nominative is used, having regard only for the meaning of the gender.

Satipi kriyāyekatte kattūnaṃ bahuttā “bahumhi vattabbe bahuvacana”nti vattamānaparassapadapaṭhamapurisabahuvacanaṃ anti, pure viya appaccayavuddhiavādesā, saralopādi. Te purisā bhavanti, appayujjamānepi bhavati, bhavanti.

Although the action is singular, due to the plurality of agents, according to the rule 'When many are to be expressed, the plural is used,' the present tense, active voice, third person, plural ending is 'anti'. As before, there are the 'a' suffix, vuddhi, the substitution 'av', vowel elision, and so forth. 'Those men become.' Even when the subject is not stated, 'bhavati' and 'bhavanti' occur.

“Payujjamānepi, tulyādhikaraṇe”ti ca vattate.

And 'even when used' and 'in apposition' are said to apply.

436. Tumhe majjhimo.

436. With 'tumha', the middle person.

Tulyādhikaraṇabhūte tumhasadde payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi dhātūhi majjhimapuriso hotīti vattamānaparassapadamajjhimapurisekavacanaṃsi, sesaṃ purimasamaṃ. Tvaṃ bhavasi, tumhe bhavatha, appayujjamānepi bhavasi, bhavatha.

When the word 'tumha' is in apposition, whether stated or not, the middle person is used for roots. Thus, the present tense, active voice, middle person, singular ending is 'si'. The rest is the same as before. 'Tvaṃ bhavasi' (You become), 'tumhe bhavatha' (You all become). Even when the pronoun is not stated, 'bhavasi' and 'bhavatha' occur.

Tulyādhikaraṇeti [M 0.0263] kimatthaṃ? Tayā paccate odano.

What is the purpose of 'in apposition'? 'Rice is cooked by you.'

Tasmiṃyevādhikāre –

In that very governing rule—

437. Amhe uttamo.

437. With 'amha', the highest person.

Tulyādhikaraṇabhūte amhasadde payujjamānepi appayujjamānepi dhātūhi uttamapuriso hotīti vattamānaparassapadauttamapurisekavacanaṃ mi, appaccayavuddhiavādesā.

When the word 'amha' is in apposition, whether stated or not, the highest person is used for roots. Thus, the present tense, active voice, highest person, singular ending is 'mi', and the 'a' suffix, vuddhi, and 'av' substitution occur.

438. Akāro dīghaṃ himimesu.

438. The vowel 'a' is lengthened before the endings 'hi', 'mi', and 'me'.

Akāro dīghamāpajjate himimaiccetāsu vibhattīsu. Ahaṃ bhavāmi, mayaṃ bhavāma. Bhavāmi, bhavāma.

The vowel 'a' becomes long before these endings: 'hi', 'mi', 'ma', and so forth. 'Ahaṃ bhavāmi' (I become), 'mayaṃ bhavāma' (we become). 'Bhavāmi', 'bhavāma'.

“Vibhattīnaṃ, chā”ti ca vattate.

And 'of inflections' and 'six' are said to apply.

439. Parāṇyattanopadāni.

439. The latter are the middle voice endings.

Sabbāsaṃ vattamānānaṃ aṭṭhavidhānaṃ vibhattīnaṃ yāni yāni parāni cha padāni, tāni tāni attanopadasaññāni hontīti teādīnaṃ attanopadasaññā.

Of all the eight kinds of present tense endings, the latter six endings are designated as middle voice. Thus, 'te' and so on are designated as middle voice.

“Dhātūhi, attanopadānī”ti ca vattate.

And 'after roots' and 'middle voice endings' are said to apply.

440. Kattari ca.

440. And in the agent.

Kattari ca kārake abhidheyye dhātūhi attanopadāni honti. Caggahaṇaṃ katthaci nivattanatthaṃ, sesaṃ parassapade vuttanayeneva veditabbaṃ. Bhavate, bhavante, bhavase, bhavavhe, bhave, bhavāmhe.

And when the agent-case is to be expressed, middle voice endings occur after roots. The inclusion of 'ca' is for the purpose of exclusion in certain cases; the rest should be understood by the method stated for the active voice. 'Bhavate', 'bhavante', 'bhavase', 'bhavavhe', 'bhave', 'bhavāmhe'.

Paca pāke, dhātusaññāyaṃ dhātvantalopo, vuttanayeneva tyādyuppatti, ivaṇṇuvaṇṇānamabhāvā vuddhiabhāvovettha viseso. So devadatto odanaṃ pacati, pacanti, pacasi[M 0.0264], pacatha, pacāmi, pacāma, so odanaṃ pacate, te pacante, tvaṃ pacase, tumhe pacavhe, ahaṃ pace, mayaṃ pacāmhe.

'Paca' in the sense of cooking: upon designation as a root, the final vowel of the root is elided, and the derivation of 'ti' and so on occurs by the method stated. Here, the distinction is the absence of the vowels 'i' and 'u', and therefore the absence of vuddhi. 'So devadatto odanaṃ pacati' (That Devadatta cooks rice), 'pacanti' (they cook), 'pacasi' (you cook), 'pacatha' (you all cook), 'pacāmi' (I cook), 'pacāma' (we cook). 'So odanaṃ pacate' (He cooks rice for himself), 'te pacante' (they cook for themselves), 'tvaṃ pacase' (you cook for yourself), 'tumhe pacavhe' (you all cook for yourselves), 'ahaṃ pace' (I cook for myself), 'mayaṃ pacāmhe' (we cook for ourselves).

Paṭhamapurisādīnamekajjhappavattippasaṅge paribhāsamāha –

Regarding the possibility of the simultaneous occurrence of the third person and others, a technical rule is stated—

441. Sabbesamekābhidhāne paro puriso.

441. When all are expressed together, the subsequent person is used.

Sabbesaṃ paṭhamamajjhimānaṃ, paṭhamuttamānaṃ, majjhimuttamānaṃ tiṇṇaṃ vā purisānaṃ ekatobhidhāne kātabbe paro puriso yojetabbo. Ekakālānamevābhidhāne cāyaṃ. So ca pacati, tvañca pacasīti pariyāyappasaṅge tumhe pacathāti bhavati. Evaṃ so ca pacati, ahañca pacāmīti mayaṃ pacāma, tathā tvañca pacasi, ahañca pacāmi, mayaṃ pacāma, so ca pacati, tvañca pacasi, ahañca pacāmi, mayaṃ pacāma. Evaṃ sabbattha yojetabbaṃ.

When a single expression is to be made for all persons—third and second, third and first, second and first, or all three—the subsequent person should be employed. And this applies only when they are expressed in the same tense. When there is the possibility of saying 'he cooks and you cook,' it becomes 'you (pl.) cook.' Likewise, 'he cooks and I cook' becomes 'we cook'; similarly, 'you cook and I cook' becomes 'we cook'; and 'he cooks, you cook, and I cook' becomes 'we cook.' Thus, it should be applied in all cases.

Ekābhidhāneti kimatthaṃ? “So ca pacati, tvañca pacissasi, ahaṃ paciṃ” ettha bhinnakālattā “mayaṃ pacimhā”ti na bhavati.

What is the purpose of 'in a single expression'? In the case of 'He cooks, and you will cook, and I cooked,' the form 'we cooked' does not occur here, due to the different tenses.

Gamu sappa gatimhi, pure viya dhātusaññāyaṃ dhātvantalopo.

The roots 'gamu' and 'sappa' are in the sense of motion. As before, upon designation as a root, the final vowel of the root is elided.

Kattari tyādyuppatti.

In the agent, the formation of 'ti' and so on occurs.

442. Gamissanto ccho vā sabbāsu.

442. Of 'gam', the final consonant optionally becomes 'ccho' in all inflections.

Gamuiccetassa dhātussanto makāro ccho hoti vā sabbāsu vibhattīsu, sabbaggahaṇena mānanta ya kāritappaccayesu ca. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Tenāyaṃ –

The final 'm' of the root 'gamu' optionally becomes 'ccho' in all inflections; and by the inclusion of 'all', also before the suffixes 'māna', 'anta', 'ya', and the causative suffixes. This word 'vā' has the meaning of a regulated option. Therefore—

Vidhiṃ niccañca vāsaddo, māna’ntesu tu kattari;

Dīpetāniccamaññattha, parokkhāyamasantakaṃ.

The word 'vā' denotes a rule and is obligatory; but with the suffixes 'māna' and 'anta', it applies in the active voice; elsewhere it indicates optionality; and in the perfect tense, it is not found.

Appaccayaparanayanāni[M 0.0265], so puriso gāmaṃ gacchati, te gacchanti, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā garupubbarassato parassa paṭhamapurisabahuvacanassa re vā hoti, gacchare. Tvaṃ gacchasi, tumhe gacchatha. Ahaṃ gacchāmi, mayaṃ gacchāma.

The application of the 'a' suffix and subsequent derivations. That man goes to the village; they go. By the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū...', for the third person plural ending following a short vowel preceded by a heavy syllable, 're' optionally occurs, as in 'gacchare'. You go (singular), you go (plural). I go, we go.

Cchādesābhāve “lopañcettamakāro”ti appaccayassa ekāro. Gameti, gamenti, saralopo. Gamesi, gametha. Gamemi, gamema.

In the absence of the 'ccha' substitution, by the rule 'lopañcettamakāro', the 'a' suffix becomes 'e'. Gameti, gamenti, with elision of the vowel. Gamesi, gametha. Gamemi, gamema.

Attanopadepi so gāmaṃ gacchate, gacchante, gacchare. Gacchase, gacchavhe. Gacche, gacchāmhe.

In the middle voice also: he goes to the village, `gacchate`; they go, `gacchante`, `gacchare`. You go, `gacchase`; you all go, `gacchavhe`. I go, `gacche`; we go, `gacchāmhe`.

“Kuto nu tvaṃ āgacchasi, rājagahato āgacchāmī”tiādīsu pana paccuppannasamīpe vattamānavacanaṃ.

However, in examples such as, 'From where do you come? I come from Rājagaha,' the present tense is used to denote the recent past.

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' continues.

443. Gamissa ghammaṃ.

443. For 'gam', 'ghamma' is substituted.

Gamuiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa ghammādeso hoti vā. Ghammati, ghammanti iccādi.

For the entire root 'gamu', the substitution 'ghamma' optionally occurs. For example: `ghammati`, `ghammanti`, etc.

Bhāvakammesu pana –

But in the impersonal and passive voices—

444. Attanopadāni bhāve ca kammani.

444. The middle voice endings are used in the impersonal and passive.

Bhāve ca kammani ca kārake abhidheyye attanopadāni honti, casaddena kammakattaripi. Bhavanaṃ bhāvo, so ca kārakantarena asaṃsaṭṭho kevalo bhavanalavanādiko dhātvattho. Karīyatīti kammaṃ. Akammakāpi dhātavo sopasaggā sakammakāpi bhavanti, tasmā kammani anupubbā bhūdhātuto vattamānattanopadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ te.

When the impersonal and passive constructions are to be expressed, middle voice endings occur; and by the word 'ca', also in the medio-passive construction. 'Bhavana' (being) is the impersonal sense, and that is purely the meaning of the root, such as 'becoming', 'cutting', etc., unconnected with any other case relation. 'What is done' is the passive sense. Even intransitive roots with prefixes become transitive. Therefore, in the passive, from the root 'bhū' preceded by 'anu', the third person singular of the present middle voice is 'te'.

“Dhātūhi [M 0.0266] ṇe ṇaya”iccādito “dhātūhī”ti vattamāne –

From the rule beginning 'Dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya...', when 'dhātūhi' (from roots) continues to apply—

445. Bhāvakammesu yo.

445. In the impersonal and passive voices, 'ya' occurs.

Sabbadhātūhi paro bhāvakammesu yappaccayo hoti. Attanopadavisayevāyamissate, “aññesu cā”ti sutte anuvattitavāggahaṇena yappaccaye vuddhi na bhavati, anubhūyate sukhaṃ devadattena.

After all roots, the suffix 'ya' occurs in the impersonal and passive voices. This is desired only in the domain of the middle voice. By the word 'vā' continuing in the rule 'aññesu cā', vowel strengthening does not occur with the 'ya' suffix. For example: `anubhūyate sukhaṃ devadattena` (Happiness is experienced by Devadatta).

Ākhyātena avuttattā, tatiyā hoti kattari;

Kammassābhihitattā na, dutiyā paṭhamāvidha.

Because the agent is not expressed by the finite verb, the third case ending is used; because the object is expressed, not the second, but the first case ending is the rule here.

Anubhūyante sampattiyo tayā. Anubhūyase tvaṃ devadattena, anubhūyavhe tumhe. Ahaṃ anubhūye tayā, mayaṃ anubhūyāmhe.

Prosperities are experienced by you. You are experienced by Devadatta; you all are experienced. I am experienced by you; we are experienced.

“Kvaci dhātu”iccādito “kvacī”ti vattamāne –

From the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātu...', when 'kvaci' continues to apply—

446. Attanopadāni parassapadattaṃ.

446. Middle voice endings become active voice endings.

Attanopadāni kvaci parassapadattamāpajjante, akattariyevetaṃ. Yakārassa dvittaṃ, anubhūyyati mayā sukhaṃ, anubhūyyate vā, anubhūyyanti. Anubhūyyasi, anubhūyyatha. Anubhūyyāmi, anubhūyyāma. Dvittābhāve – anubhūyati, anubhūyanti.
