Sometimes, middle voice endings take on the active voice form; this is only in the non-active voice. The letter 'ya' is doubled: `anubhūyyati mayā sukhaṃ` (happiness is experienced by me), or `anubhūyyate`; `anubhūyyanti`. `Anubhūyyasi`, `anubhūyyatha`. `Anubhūyyāmi`, `anubhūyyāma`. In the absence of doubling: `anubhūyati`, `anubhūyanti`.

Kvacīti kiṃ? Anubhūyate.

Why 'kvaci' (sometimes)? To allow for `anubhūyate`.

Bhāve adabbavuttino bhāvassekattā ekavacanameva, tañca paṭhamapurisasseva, bhūyate devadattena, devadattena sampati bhavananti attho.

In the impersonal voice, since the action does not express a substance and is singular, only the singular number is used, and that too only of the third person: `bhūyate devadattena`, meaning 'it is now being by Devadatta'.

Pacadhātuto [M 0.0267] kammani attanopade yappaccaye ca kate –

From the root 'pac' (to cook), when in the passive voice the middle voice endings and the 'ya' suffix are applied—

Vipariṇāmena “yassā”ti vattamāne –

By a transformation of the case ending, when 'yassa' continues to apply—

447. Tassa cavaggayakāravakārattaṃ sadhātvantassa.

447. For that (suffix), together with the final consonant of the root, there is a transformation into a letter of the `ca`-group, `ya`, or `va`.

Tassa bhāvakammavisayassa yappaccayassa cavaggayakāravakārattaṃ hoti dhātvantena saha yathāsambhavaṃ. Ettha ca “ivaṇṇāgamo vā”ti ito sīhagatiyā vāsaddo anuvattetabbo, so ca vavatthitavibhāsattho. Tena –

For that 'ya' suffix, in the domain of the impersonal and passive, there is a transformation into a `ca`-group letter, `ya`, or `va`, together with the final consonant of the root, as is possible. Here, the word 'vā' (optionally) from the rule 'ivaṇṇāgamo vā' should be carried forward by the 'lion's gait', and it has the meaning of a regulated option. Hence:

Cavaggo ca ta vaggānaṃ, dhātvantānaṃ yavattanaṃ;

Ravānañca sayappacca-yānaṃ hoti yathākkamanti.

For root-final letters of the `ta`-group, the result is a `ca`-group letter; and for root-final `ra` and `va`, there is a transformation into `ya` and `va` respectively. This occurs in order when they are followed by the `ya` suffix.

Dhātvantassa cavaggādittā cakāre kate “paradvebhāvo ṭhāne”ti cakārassa dvittaṃ. Paccate odano devadattena, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā garupubbarassato parassa paṭhamapurisabahuvacanassa kvaci re hoti. Paccare, paccante. Paccase, paccavhe. Pacce, paccāmhe.

Since the root-final is the first letter of the `ca`-group, when the letter `ca` is formed, it is doubled by the rule 'paradvebhāvo ṭhāne'. `Paccate odano devadattena` (The rice is cooked by Devadatta). By the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū...', the third-person plural ending after a short vowel preceded by a heavy syllable sometimes becomes 're'. `Paccare`, `paccante`. `Paccase`, `paccavhe`. `Pacce`, `paccāmhe`.

Parassapadādese paccati, paccanti. Paccasi, paccatha. Paccāmi, paccāma. Tathā kammakattari paccate odano sayameva, paccante. Paccati, paccanti vā iccādi.

When the active voice endings are substituted: `paccati`, `paccanti`. `Paccasi`, `paccatha`. `Paccāmi`, `paccāma`. Similarly, in the medio-passive voice: `paccate odano sayameva` (the rice cooks by itself), `paccante`. Or `paccati`, `paccanti`, etc.

Gamito kammani attanopade, yappaccaye ca kate –

From the root gam, in the passive voice, in the middle voice, and when the ya suffix is applied—

“Dhātūhi, tasmiṃ, ye”ti ca vattate.

Dhātūhi, tasmiṃ, ye is also carried forward.

448. Ivaṇṇāgamo vā.

448. Or the insertion of the vowel i.

Sabbehi dhātūhi tasmiṃ bhāvakammavisaye yappaccaye pare ivaṇṇāgamo hoti vāti īkārāgamo. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Cchādeso, gacchīyate gāmo devadattena[M 0.0268], gacchīyante. Gacchīyase, gacchīyavhe. Gacchīye, gacchīyāmhe.

After all roots, when the ya suffix follows in the impersonal and passive sense, the insertion of the vowel i occurs, or the insertion of ī. This word vā has the sense of a regulated option. With the substitution of cch: gacchīyate gāmo devadattena (the village is gone to by Devadatta), gacchīyante. Gacchīyase, gacchīyavhe. Gacchīye, gacchīyāmhe.

Cchādesābhāve –

In the absence of the cch substitution—

“Dhātūhi, yo, vā”ti ca vattate.

Dhātūhi, yo, vā is also carried forward.

449. Pubbarūpañca.

449. And the preceding form (assimilation).

Heṭṭhānuttehi parassevedaṃ, tena kaṭapavaggayakāralasanteheva dhātūhi paro yappaccayo pubbarūpamāpajjate vāti makārā parassa yakārassa makāro. Gammate, gamīyate, gammante, gamīyante. Gammase, gamīyase, gammavhe, gamīyavhe. Gamme, gamīye, gammāmhe, gamīyāmhe.

This rule applies only to what follows, not to what is stated below. Therefore, after roots ending in the ka, ṭa, pa groups, and y, r, l, s, the following ya suffix is optionally assimilated to the preceding form; for example, after m, the following y becomes m. Gammate, gamīyate, gammante, gamīyante. Gammase, gamīyase, gammavhe, gamīyavhe. Gamme, gamīye, gammāmhe, gamīyāmhe.

Parassapadatte – gacchīyyati, gacchīyyanti. Gacchīyati, gacchīyanti vā. Gammati, gammanti. Gamīyati, gamīyanti. Ikārāgame gamiyyati, gamiyyanti. Tathā ghammīyati, ghammīyanti iccādi.

In the active voice— gacchīyyati, gacchīyyanti. Or gacchīyati, gacchīyanti. Gammati, gammanti. Gamīyati, gamīyanti. With the insertion of i: gamiyyati, gamiyyanti. Similarly, ghammīyati, ghammīyanti, etc.

Vattamānāvibhatti.

The present tense inflection.

450. Pañcamī tu antu, hi tha, mi ma, taṃ antaṃ, ssuvho, e āmase.

450. The fifth conjugation endings are: tu, antu; hi, tha; mi, ma; taṃ, antaṃ; ssu, vho; e, āmase.

Tvādayo dvādasa pañcamīsaññā honti.

The twelve endings beginning with tu are designated as the fifth conjugation.

451. Āṇatyāsiṭṭhenuttakāle pañcamī.

451. The fifth conjugation is used in the sense of command and wishing, in non-future time.

Āṇatyatthe ca āsīsatthe anuttakāle pañcamīvibhatti hoti.

In the sense of command and in the sense of wishing, the fifth inflection occurs in non-future time.

Satipi kālādhikāre puna kālaggahaṇena vidhinimantanājjhesanānumatipatthanāpattakālādīsu ca pañcamī. Āṇāpanamāṇatti, āsīsanamāsiṭṭho, so ca iṭṭhassa asampattassa [M 0.0269] atthassa patthanaṃ, tasmiṃ āṇatyāsiṭṭhe. Anu samīpe uttakālo anuttakālo, paccuppannakāloti attho, na uttakāloti vā anuttakālo, tasmiṃ anuttakāle, kālamanāmasitvā hotīti attho.

Although time is the governing topic, by the re-mentioning of 'time', the fifth conjugation is also used in injunction, invitation, request, assent, wishing, proper occasion, etc. Commanding is āṇatti; blessing is āsiṭṭha, and that is the wishing for a desired but unattained object; in that sense of command and wishing. Anu means near; uttakālo is future time; thus anuttakālo is near time, meaning the present time. Or, anuttakālo means 'not future time'. In that anuttakāle, the meaning is that it occurs without specifying time.

Tattha āsīsanatthe bhūdhātuto pañcamīparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ tu, appaccayavuddhiavādesā. So sukhī bhavatu, te sukhitā bhavantu.

There, in the sense of wishing, from the root bhū, the fifth conjugation, active voice, third person singular ending tu is used, with the a suffix, vuddhi strengthening, and the av substitution. So sukhī bhavatu (May he be happy), te sukhitā bhavantu (may they be happy).

Vipariṇāmena “akārato”ti vattate.

By modification, akārato (from a) is carried forward.

452. Hilopaṃ vā.

452. Or the elision of hi.

Akārato paro hivibhatti lopamāpajjate vā. Tvaṃ sukhī bhava, bhavāhi vā, himhi dīgho. Tumhe sukhitā bhavatha. Ahaṃ sukhī bhavāmi, mayaṃ sukhino bhavāma.

After the vowel a, the hi inflection is optionally elided. Tvaṃ sukhī bhava (May you be happy), or bhavāhi; when hi is present, there is lengthening of the preceding vowel. Tumhe sukhitā bhavatha (May you all be happy). Ahaṃ sukhī bhavāmi (May I be happy), mayaṃ sukhino bhavāma (may we be happy).

Attanopade so sukhī bhavataṃ, te sukhitā bhavantaṃ. Tvaṃ sukhī bhavassu, tumhe sukhitā bhavavho. Ahaṃ sukhī bhave, mayaṃ sukhitā bhavāmase.

In the middle voice: so sukhī bhavataṃ (May he be happy), te sukhitā bhavantaṃ (may they be happy). Tvaṃ sukhī bhavassu (May you be happy), tumhe sukhitā bhavavho (may you all be happy). Ahaṃ sukhī bhave (May I be happy), mayaṃ sukhitā bhavāmase (may we be happy).

Kammani anubhūyataṃ tayā, anubhūyantaṃ. Anubhūyassu, anubhūyavho. Anubhūye, anubhūyāmase. Parassapadatte anubhūyyatu, anubhūyyantu. Anubhūyatu, anubhūyantu vā, anubhūyyāhi iccādi. Bhāve bhūyataṃ.

In the passive voice: anubhūyataṃ tayā (Let it be experienced by you), anubhūyantaṃ. Anubhūyassu, anubhūyavho. Anubhūye, anubhūyāmase. In the active voice forms: anubhūyyatu, anubhūyyantu. Or anubhūyatu, anubhūyantu; anubhūyyāhi, etc. In the impersonal voice: bhūyataṃ (let there be being).

Āṇattiyaṃ kattari devadatto dāni odanaṃ pacatu, pacantu. Paca, pacāhi, pacatha. Pacāmi, pacāma. Pacataṃ, pacantaṃ. Pacassu, pacavho. Pace, pacāmase.

In the imperative, in the active voice: devadatto dāni odanaṃ pacatu (Let Devadatta now cook the rice), pacantu (let them cook). Paca (Cook! sg.), pacāhi (cook! sg.), pacatha (cook! pl.). Pacāmi (Let me cook), pacāma (let us cook). In the middle voice: pacataṃ (let him cook), pacantaṃ (let them cook). Pacassu (cook! sg.), pacavho (cook! pl.). Pace (let me cook), pacāmase (let us cook).

Kammani yappaccayacavaggādi, paccataṃ odano devadattena, paccantaṃ. Paccassu, paccavho. Pacce, paccāmase. Parassapadatte paccatu, paccantu. Pacca, paccāhi, paccatha. Paccāmi, paccāma.

In the passive voice, with the ya suffix and changes to the ca-group, etc.: paccataṃ odano devadattena (Let the rice be cooked by Devadatta), paccantaṃ. Paccassu, paccavho. Pacce, paccāmase. In the active voice forms: paccatu, paccantu. Pacca, paccāhi, paccatha. Paccāmi, paccāma.

Tathā [M 0.0270] so gāmaṃ gacchatu, gacchantu. Gaccha, gacchāhi, gacchatha. Gacchāmi, gacchāma. Gametu, gamentu. Gama, gamāhi, gametha. Gamemi, gamema. Gacchataṃ, gacchantaṃ. Gacchassu, gacchavho. Gacche, gacchāmase. Ghammādese ghammatu, ghammantu iccādi.

Similarly: so gāmaṃ gacchatu (Let him go to the village), gacchantu. Gaccha, gacchāhi, gacchatha. Gacchāmi, gacchāma. Causative: gametu, gamentu. Simple imperative: gama, gamāhi. Middle imperative: gametha. Causative present: gamemi, gamema. Middle voice: gacchataṃ, gacchantaṃ. Gacchassu, gacchavho. Gacche, gacchāmase. With the substitution of ghamm: ghammatu (let him go), ghammantu, etc.

Kammani gacchīyataṃ, gacchīyatu, gamīyataṃ, gamīyatu, gammataṃ, gammatu iccādi.

In the passive voice: gacchīyataṃ, gacchīyatu, gamīyataṃ, gamīyatu, gammataṃ, gammatu, etc. (all meaning 'let it be gone to').

Vidhimhi idha pabbato hotu, ayaṃ pāsādo suvaṇṇamayo hotūtiādi.

In the sense of injunction: idha pabbato hotu (Let there be a mountain here), ayaṃ pāsādo suvaṇṇamayo hotu (let this palace be made of gold), etc.

Nimantane adhivāsetu me bhante bhagavā bhojanaṃ, idha nisīdatu bhavaṃ.

In invitation: Adhivāsetu me bhante bhagavā bhojanaṃ (Venerable sir, may the Blessed One consent to my invitation for the meal), idha nisīdatu bhavaṃ (may the venerable one be seated here).

Ajjhesane desetu bhante bhagavā dhammaṃ.

In request: Desetu bhante bhagavā dhammaṃ (Venerable sir, may the Blessed One teach the Dhamma).

Anumatiyaṃ pucchatu bhavaṃ pañhaṃ, pavisatu bhavaṃ, ettha nisīdatu.

In permission: Pucchatu bhavaṃ pañhaṃ (May the venerable one ask a question), pavisatu bhavaṃ (may the venerable one enter), ettha nisīdatu (may the venerable one sit here).

Patthanā yācanā, dadāhi me gāmavarāni pañca, ekaṃ me nayanaṃ dehi.

Wishing is requesting: Dadāhi me gāmavarāni pañca (Grant me five excellent villages), ekaṃ me nayanaṃ dehi (give me one of your eyes).

Pattakāle sampatto te kālo kaṭakaraṇe, kaṭaṃ karotu bhavaṃ iccādi.

At the opportune time: “Sampatto te kālo kaṭakaraṇe” (Your time for making a mat has arrived), “kaṭaṃ karotu bhavaṃ” (may the venerable one make a mat), etc.

Pañcamīvibhatti.

The Fifth Inflection.

453. Sattamī eyya eyyuṃ, eyyāsi eyyātha, eyyāmieyyāma, etha eraṃ, etho eyyāvho, eyyaṃeyyāmhe.

453. The seventh conjugation endings are: eyya, eyyuṃ; eyyāsi, eyyātha; eyyāmi, eyyāma; etha, eraṃ; etho, eyyāvho; eyyaṃ, eyyāmhe.

Eyyādayo dvādasa sattamīsaññā honti.

The twelve endings beginning with ‘eyya’ are designated as the seventh conjugation.

“Anuttakāle”ti vattate.

“Anuttakāle” (in unexpressed time) is carried forward.

454. Anumatiparikappatthesu [M 0.0271] sattamī.

454. The seventh conjugation is used in the sense of permission and supposition.

Anumatyatthe ca parikappatthe ca anuttakāle sattamīvibhatti hoti.

The seventh inflection occurs in unexpressed time in the sense of permission and in the sense of supposition.

Atthaggahaṇena vidhinimantanādīsu ca sattamī. Kattumicchato parassa anujānanaṃ anumati, parikappanaṃ parikappo, “yadi nāma bhaveyyā”ti sallakkhaṇaṃ nirūpanaṃ, hetukriyāya sambhave phalakriyāya sambhavaparikappo ca.

By grasping the meaning, the seventh conjugation is also used in injunction, invitation, etc. Permission is allowing another who wishes to act. Supposition is conjecture; it is the discernment and examination expressed as “if it were to be.” It is also the supposition of the possibility of a resultant action when the causal action is possible.

Tattha parikappe sattamīparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ eyya, appaccayavuddhādi purimasamaṃ, “kvaci dhātu vibhattī”tiādinā eyya eyyāsi eyyāmi eyyaṃiccetesaṃ vikappena ekārādeso. So dāni kiṃ nu kho bhave, yadi so paṭhamavaye pabbajeyya, arahā bhaveyya, sace saṅkhārā niccā bhaveyyuṃ, na nirujjheyyuṃ. Yadi tvaṃ bhaveyyāsi, tumhe bhaveyyātha. Kathamahaṃ devo bhaveyyāmi, kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ bhaveyyāma. Tathā bhavetha, bhaveraṃ. Bhavetho, bhaveyyāvho.

Here, in the sense of supposition, the seventh conjugation, active voice, third person singular ending is ‘eyya’; the suffix ‘a’, vowel gradation, etc., are as before. By the rule beginning “kvaci dhātu vibhattī,” for the endings eyya, eyyāsi, eyyāmi, and eyyaṃ, there is optionally a substitution of ‘e’. “So dāni kiṃ nu kho bhave” (What then might he be now)? “Yadi so paṭhamavaye pabbajeyya, arahā bhaveyya” (If he were to go forth in the first stage of life, he would become an arahant). “Sace saṅkhārā niccā bhaveyyuṃ, na nirujjheyyuṃ” (If formations were permanent, they would not cease). “Yadi tvaṃ bhaveyyāsi” (If you were to be), “tumhe bhaveyyātha” (you all would be). “Kathamahaṃ devo bhaveyyāmi” (How would I become a god)? “Kiṃ nu kho mayaṃ bhaveyyāma” (What then would we become)? Similarly, in the middle voice: “bhavetha” (he would be), “bhaveraṃ” (they would be). “Bhavetho” (you two would be), “bhaveyyāvho” (you all would be).

Patthane tu ahaṃ sukhī bhave, buddho bhaveyyaṃ, bhaveyyāmhe.

In the sense of wishing: “ahaṃ sukhī bhave” (May I be happy), “buddho bhaveyyaṃ” (may I become a Buddha), “bhaveyyāmhe” (may we become so).

Kammani sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyetha, anubhūyeraṃ. Anubhūyetho, anubhūyeyyāvho. Anubhūye, anubhūyeyyaṃ, anubhūyeyyāmhe. Parassapadatte anubhūyeyya, anubhūyeyyuṃ. Anubhūyeyyāsi iccādi. Bhāve bhūyetha.

In the passive voice: “sukhaṃ tayā anubhūyetha” (May happiness be experienced by you), “anubhūyeraṃ” (may they be experienced). “Anubhūyetho” (may you two be experienced), “anubhūyeyyāvho” (may you all be experienced). “Anubhūye, anubhūyeyyaṃ” (may I be experienced), “anubhūyeyyāmhe” (may we be experienced). When using active voice endings: “anubhūyeyya” (may it be experienced), “anubhūyeyyuṃ” (may they be experienced). “Anubhūyeyyāsi” (may you be experienced), etc. In the impersonal voice: “bhūyetha” (may there be).

Vidhimhi so odanaṃ pace, paceyya, paceyyuṃ. Tvaṃ pace, paceyyāsi, tumhe paceyyātha. Ahaṃ pace, paceyyāmi, mayaṃ paceyyāma. Pacetha, paceraṃ. Pacetho, paceyyāvho. Pace, paceyyaṃ, paceyyāmhe.

In the sense of injunction: “so odanaṃ pace, paceyya” (He should cook rice), “paceyyuṃ” (they should cook). “Tvaṃ pace, paceyyāsi” (You should cook), “tumhe paceyyātha” (you all should cook). “Ahaṃ pace, paceyyāmi” (I should cook), “mayaṃ paceyyāma” (we should cook). In the middle voice: “Pacetha” (He should cook), “paceraṃ” (they should cook). “Pacetho” (You two should cook), “paceyyāvho” (you all should cook). “Pace, paceyyaṃ” (I should cook), “paceyyāmhe” (we should cook).

Kammani [M 0.0272] paccetha, pacceraṃ. Paccetho, pacceyyāvho. Pacce, pacceyyaṃ, pacceyyāmhe. Parassapadatte pacce, pacceyya, pacceyyuṃ. Pacceyyāsi iccādi.

In the passive voice: “paccetha” (it should be cooked), “pacceraṃ” (they should be cooked). “Paccetho” (you two should be cooked), “pacceyyāvho” (you all should be cooked). “Pacce, pacceyyaṃ” (I should be cooked), “pacceyyāmhe” (we should be cooked). When using active voice endings: “pacce, pacceyya” (it should be cooked), “pacceyyuṃ” (they should be cooked). “Pacceyyāsi” (you should be cooked), etc.

Anumatiyaṃ so gāmaṃ gacche, gaccheyya, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā eyyussa uṃ vā, gacchuṃ, gaccheyyuṃ. Tvaṃ gacche, gaccheyyāsi, gaccheyyātha. Gacche, gaccheyyāmi, gaccheyyāma. Game, gameyya, gamuṃ, gameyyuṃ. Game, gameyyāsi, gameyyātha. Game, gameyyāmi, gameyyāma. Gacchetha, gaccheraṃ. Gacchetho, gaccheyyāvho. Gacche, gaccheyyaṃ, gaccheyyāmhe. Gametha, gameraṃ iccādi.

In the sense of permission: “so gāmaṃ gacche, gaccheyya” (he may go to the village). By the rule beginning “kvaci dhātu,” ‘eyyuṃ’ optionally becomes ‘uṃ’, thus: “gacchuṃ, gaccheyyuṃ” (they may go). “Tvaṃ gacche, gaccheyyāsi” (you may go), “gaccheyyātha” (you all may go). “Gacche, gaccheyyāmi” (I may go), “gaccheyyāma” (we may go). Similarly with the root ‘gam’: “game, gameyya” (he may go), “gamuṃ, gameyyuṃ” (they may go). “Game, gameyyāsi” (you may go), “gameyyātha” (you all may go). “Game, gameyyāmi” (I may go), “gameyyāma” (we may go). In the middle voice: “gacchetha” (he may go), “gaccheraṃ” (they may go). “Gacchetho” (you two may go), “gaccheyyāvho” (you all may go). “Gacche, gaccheyyaṃ” (I may go), “gaccheyyāmhe” (we may go). Similarly: “gametha, gameraṃ” (he may go, they may go), etc.

Kammani gacchīyetha, gamīyetha, gacchīyeraṃ, gamīyeraṃ iccādi. Parassapadatte gacchīyeyya, gamīyeyya, gammeyya, gammeyyuṃ iccādi. Tathā ghamme, ghammeyya, ghammeyyuṃ iccādi.

In the passive voice: “gacchīyetha, gamīyetha” (it may be gone to), “gacchīyeraṃ, gamīyeraṃ” (they may be gone to), etc. When using active voice endings: “gacchīyeyya, gamīyeyya, gammeyya” (it may be gone to), “gammeyyuṃ” (they may be gone to), etc. Similarly: “ghamme, ghammeyya” (there may be heat), “ghammeyyuṃ” (there may be heat), etc.

Sattamīvibhatti.

The Seventh Inflection: The Optative Mood.

Paccuppannāṇattiparikappakālikavibhattinayo.

The System of Verb Inflections for the Present, Imperative, Optative, and Conditional.

455. Hiyyattanī āū, ottha, aṃmhā, tthatthuṃ, sevhaṃ, iṃmhase.

455. The Hiyyattanī endings are: ā, ū; o, ttha; aṃ, mhā; ttha, tthuṃ; se, vhaṃ; iṃ, mhase.

Āādayo dvādasa hiyyattanīsaññā honti.

The twelve endings beginning with ‘ā’ are designated as Hiyyattanī.

“Appaccakkhe, atīte”ti ca vattate.

“Appaccakkhe” (for the unperceived) and “atīte” (in the past) are also carried forward.

456. Hiyyopabhuti paccakkhe hiyyattanī.

456. From yesterday onwards, for the directly perceived past, the Hiyyattanī is used.

Hiyyopabhuti atīte kāle paccakkhe vā appaccakkhe vā hiyyattanīvibhatti hotīti hiyyattanīparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ ā.

From yesterday onwards, in past time, whether directly perceived or not, the Hiyyattanī inflection occurs. Thus, ‘ā’ is the Hiyyattanī, active voice, third person singular ending.

“Kvaci dhātu”iccādito “kvaci, dhātūna”nti ca vattate.

From the rule beginning “kvaci dhātu,” the terms “kvaci” and “dhātūnaṃ” are also carried forward.

457. Akārāgamo [M 0.0273] hiyyattanī ajjatanīkālātipattīsu.

457. The augment ‘a’ occurs in the Hiyyattanī (Imperfect), Ajjatanī (Aorist), and Kālātipatti (Conditional).

Kvaci dhātūnamādimhi akārāgamo hoti hiyyattanīajjatanīkālātipattiiccetāsu tīsu vibhattīsu. Kathamayamakārāgamo dhātvādimhīti ce?

Sometimes, at the beginning of roots, the augment ‘a’ occurs in these three inflections: Hiyyattanī, Ajjatanī, and Kālātipatti. If it is asked, how is this augment ‘a’ placed at the beginning of the root?

Satissarepi dhātvante, punakārāgamassidha;

Niratthattā payogānu rodhā dhātvādito ayaṃ.

Even when there is a vowel at the end of the root, this augment is placed at the beginning of the root; for to place the augment ‘a’ again here would be meaningless, and this is in accordance with usage.

Appaccayavuddhiavādesasaralopādi vuttanayameva.

The suffix ‘a’, vowel gradation, the substitution of ‘av’, vowel elision, etc., are just as stated previously.

Abhavā, abhavū. Abhavo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā okārassa aādeso vā, abhava, abhavattha. Abhavaṃ, abhavamhā. Abhavattha, abhavatthuṃ. Abhavase, abhavavhaṃ. Abhaviṃ, abhavamhase.

“Abhavā” (he was), “abhavū” (they were). “Abhavo” (you were); by the rule beginning “kvaci dhātu,” the ‘o’ optionally becomes ‘a’, thus “abhava” (you were); “abhavattha” (you all were). “Abhavaṃ” (I was), “abhavamhā” (we were). In the middle voice: “Abhavattha” (he was), “abhavatthuṃ” (they were). “Abhavase” (you were), “abhavavhaṃ” (you all were). “Abhaviṃ” (I was), “abhavamhase” (we were).

Kammani yappaccayo, tayā sukhamanvabhūyattha, akārāgamābhāve anubhūyattha, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā tthassa thādeso, anvabhūyatha, anubhūyatha, anvabhūyatthuṃ, anubhūyatthuṃ. Anvabhūyase, anubhūyase, anvabhūyavhaṃ, anubhūyavhaṃ. Anvabhūyiṃ, anubhūyiṃ, anvabhūyamhase, anubhūyamhase. Parassapadatte anvabhūyā, anubhūyā iccādi. Bhāve anvabhūyattha.

In the passive voice, the suffix ‘ya’ is used. “Tayā sukham anvabhūyattha” (Happiness was experienced by you). In the absence of the augment ‘a’: “anubhūyattha” (it was experienced). By the rule beginning “kvaci dhātu,” ‘ttha’ is substituted by ‘tha’, thus: “anvabhūyatha, anubhūyatha” (it was experienced). “Anvabhūyatthuṃ, anubhūyatthuṃ” (they were experienced). “Anvabhūyase, anubhūyase” (you were experienced), “anvabhūyavhaṃ, anubhūyavhaṃ” (you all were experienced). “Anvabhūyiṃ, anubhūyiṃ” (I was experienced), “anvabhūyamhase, anubhūyamhase” (we were experienced). When using active voice endings: “anvabhūyā, anubhūyā” (it was experienced), etc. In the impersonal voice: “anvabhūyattha” (there was an experiencing).

Tathā so odanaṃ apacā, pacā, apacū, pacū. Apaco, paco, apacattha, pacattha. Apacaṃ, pacaṃ, apacamhā, pacamhā. Apacattha, pacattha, apacatthu, pacatthuṃ. Apacase, pacase, apacavhaṃ, pacavhaṃ. Apaciṃ, paciṃ, apacamhase, pacamhase.

Similarly: “so odanaṃ apacā, pacā” (he cooked rice). “Apacū, pacū” (they cooked). “Apaco, paco” (you cooked), “apacattha, pacattha” (you all cooked). “Apacaṃ, pacaṃ” (I cooked), “apacamhā, pacamhā” (we cooked). In the middle voice: “Apacattha, pacattha” (he cooked), “apacatthuṃ, pacatthuṃ” (they cooked). “Apacase, pacase” (you cooked), “apacavhaṃ, pacavhaṃ” (you all cooked). “Apaciṃ, paciṃ” (I cooked), “apacamhase, pacamhase” (we cooked).

Kammani [M 0.0274] apaccatha, apaccattha, apaccatthuṃ. Apaccase, apaccavhaṃ. Apacciṃ, apaccamhase. Apaccā, apaccū iccādi.

In the passive voice: he was cooked, he was cooked, they were cooked. You were cooked, you all were cooked. I was cooked, we were cooked. He was cooked, they were cooked, etc.

Tathā agacchā, agacchū. Agaccho, agaccha, agacchattha. Agacchaṃ, agacchamhā. Agacchattha, agacchatthuṃ. Agacchase, agacchavhaṃ. Agacchiṃ, agacchamhase. Agamā, agamū. Agamo, agama, agamattha. Agamaṃ, agamamhā. Agamattha, agamatthuṃ. Agamase, agamavhaṃ. Agamiṃ, agamamhase.

Similarly: he went, they went. You went, you went, you all went. I went, we went. In the middle voice: he went, they went. You went, you all went. I went, we went. Likewise, with the root form 'gam': he went, they went. You went, you went, you all went. I went, we went. In the middle voice: he went, they went. You went, you all went. I went, we went.

Kammani agacchīyattha, gacchīyattha, agamīyattha, gamīyattha, agacchīyatthuṃ, gacchīyatthuṃ, agamīyatthuṃ, gamīyatthuṃ iccādi. Tathā aghammā, aghammū iccādi.

In the passive voice: it was gone to, it was gone to, it was gone to, it was gone to; they were gone to, they were gone to, they were gone to, they were gone to, etc. Similarly, he sweated, they sweated, etc.

Hiyyattanīvibhatti.

The Hiyyattanī (Imperfect Past) Inflection.

458. Hiyyattanī sattamī pañcamī vattamānā sabbadhātukaṃ.

458. The Hiyyattanī (Imperfect Past), Sattamī (Optative), Pañcamī (Imperative), and Vattamānā (Present) are sabbadhātuka.

Hiyyattanādayo catasso vibhattiyo sabbadhātukasaññā hontīti hiyyattanādīnaṃ sabbadhātukasaññattā “ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhī”ti vutto ikārāgamo na bhavati.

The four inflections beginning with Hiyyattanī are designated as sabbadhātuka. Therefore, because Hiyyattanī and the others are designated as sabbadhātuka, the augment 'i', which is prescribed by the rule 'the augment i occurs when a non-sabbadhātuka follows', does not occur.

Sabbadhātukaṃ.

Sabbadhātuka.

459. Parokkhā a u, e ttha, aṃ mha, ttha re, tho vho, iṃmhe.

459. The Parokkhā endings are: a, u; e, ttha; aṃ, mha; ttha, re; tho, vho; iṃ, mhe.

Aādayo dvādasa parokkhāsaññā honti. Akkhānaṃ indriyānaṃ paraṃ parokkhā, taddīpakattā ayaṃ vibhatti parokkhāti vuccati.

The twelve endings beginning with 'a' are designated as Parokkhā. Parokkhā means 'beyond the senses' (akkhānaṃ paraṃ), and because this inflection indicates that, it is called Parokkhā.

460. Apaccakkhe [M 0.0275] parokkhātīte.

460. The Parokkhā is used for a past time not directly perceived.

Apaccakkhe vattuno indriyāvisayabhūte atīte kāle parokkhāvibhatti hoti. Atikkamma itoti atīto, hutvā atikkantoti attho.

The Parokkhā inflection occurs for a past time that is not directly perceived, being beyond the range of the speaker's senses. 'Atīta' is 'atikkamma iti' (thus gone beyond); the meaning is 'having occurred and passed'.

Heṭṭhā vuttanayena parokkhāparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ a. “Bhū a”itīdha –

According to the method stated above, the third person singular active ending of the Parokkhā is 'a'. Here, in the case of 'Bhū a'—

Vipariṇāmena “dhātūna”nti vattate.

By modification of the case ending, 'of the roots' is carried forward.

461. Kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo.

461. In some cases, the reduplication of the initial monosyllabic part of roots.

Dhātūnamādibhūtānaṃ vaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ kvaci dvebhāvo hoti. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ kvacisaddo, tena –

In some cases, the initial monosyllabic part of roots is doubled. This word 'kvaci' (in some cases) indicates a restricted option, therefore—

Kha cha sesu parokkhāyaṃ, dvebhāvo sabbadhātunaṃ;

Appaccaye juhotyādi-ssapi kiccādike kvaci.

Reduplication of all roots occurs in the Parokkhā, and when suffixes such as 'kha' and 'cha' follow; also for the 'juhoti' class etc. even without a suffix, and sometimes in the case of gerundives ('kicca') etc.

“Bhū bhū a”itīdha –

Here, in the case of 'Bhū bhū a'—

462. Pubbobbhāso.

462. The preceding part is the reduplication.

Dvebhūtassa dhātussa yo pubbo avayavo, so abbhāsasañño hotīti abbhāsasaññā.

The preceding part of a doubled root is termed 'abbhāsa' (reduplication); thus, the designation 'abbhāsa'.

Abbhāsaggahaṇamanuvattate.

The term 'abbhāsa' is carried forward.

463. Antassivaṇṇākāro vā.

463. Optionally, the final vowel of the reduplication becomes 'i' or 'a'.

Abbhāsassa antassa ivaṇṇo hoti vā, akāro ca. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Tena –

The final vowel of the reduplication optionally becomes 'i', and also 'a'. This word 'vā' (or) indicates a restricted option. Therefore—

Kha [M 0.0276] cha sesu avaṇṇassa,

Ikāro sagupussa ī;

Vāssa bhūssa parokkhāyaṃ,

Akāro nāparassimeti.

When 'kha', 'cha', etc. follow, 'i' replaces 'a'; 'ī' replaces a heavy syllable. For 'bhū' in the Parokkhā, 'a' occurs optionally, but not in the second part.

Ūkārassa akāro.

'Ū' becomes 'a'.

464. Dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā.

464. The second and fourth consonants of a class become the first and third, respectively.

Abbhāsagatānaṃ dutiyacatutthānaṃ vaggabyañjanānaṃ yathākkamaṃ paṭhamatatiyā hontīti bhakārassa bakāro.

The second and fourth class consonants within a reduplication become the first and third, respectively; thus, 'bh' becomes 'b'.

465. Brūbhūnamāhabhūvā parokkhāyaṃ.

465. In the Parokkhā, 'āha' and 'bhūva' are substituted for 'brū' and 'bhū'.

Brūbhūiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ āhabhūvaiccete ādesā honti parokkhāvibhattiyanti bhūsaddassa bhūvaādeso, “saralopo mādesappaccayādimhī”tiādinā saralopādi, so kira rājā babhūva, te kira babhūvu. Tvaṃ kira babhūve.

For these roots 'brū' and 'bhū', the substitutes 'āha' and 'bhūva' occur in the Parokkhā inflection. Thus, for the root 'bhū', the substitute is 'bhūva'; vowel elision and other operations occur according to rules such as 'saralopo mādesappaccayādimhi'. For example: 'That king, it is said, was' (so kira rājā babhūva); 'They, it is said, were' (te kira babhūvu); 'You, it is said, were' (Tvaṃ kira babhūve).

“Dhātūhī”ti vattate, sīhagatiyā kvaciggahaṇañca.

The term 'dhātūhi' (from roots) is carried forward, as is the term 'kvaci' by the 'lion's gait' principle.

466. Ikārāgamo asabbadhātukamhi.

466. The augment 'i' occurs before a non-sabbadhātuka suffix.

Sabbasmiṃ asabbadhātukamhi pare kvaci dhātūhi paro ikārāgamo hoti.

In every case, when a non-sabbadhātuka suffix follows, the augment 'i' sometimes occurs after roots.

Asabbadhātuke byañja-nādimhe vāyamāgamo;

Kvacādhikārato byañja-nādopi kvaci no siyā.

In a non-sabbadhātuka suffix beginning with a consonant, this augment 'i' optionally occurs; due to the governing rule 'kvaci' (sometimes), even when beginning with a consonant, it may sometimes not occur.

Ettha ca “na sabbadhātukaṃ asabbadhātuka”miti katvā “hiyyattanī sattamī pañcamī vattamānā sabbadhātuka”nti hiyyattanīādīnaṃ sabbadhātukasaññāya vuttattā tadaññā catasso vibhattiyo asabbadhātukanti vuccati.

And here, having established that 'what is not sabbadhātuka is asabbadhātuka,' and because it has been stated by the designation 'sabbadhātuka' for Hiyyattanī and the others that 'the Hiyyattanī (Imperfect), Sattamī (Optative), Pañcamī (Imperative), and Vattamānā (Present) are sabbadhātuka,' the other four inflections are called asabbadhātuka.

Tumhe [M 0.0277] kira babhūvittha. Ahaṃ kira babhūvaṃ, mayaṃ kira babhūvimha. Attanopade so babhūvittha, babhūvire. Babhūvittho, babhūvivho. Babhūviṃ, babhūvimhe.

Tumhe kira babhūvittha (You all indeed were). Ahaṃ kira babhūvaṃ (I indeed was), mayaṃ kira babhūvimha (we indeed were). In the Attanopada: so babhūvittha (he indeed was), te babhūvire (they indeed were). Tvaṃ babhūvittho (you indeed were), tumhe babhūvivho (you all indeed were). Ahaṃ babhūviṃ (I indeed was), mayaṃ babhūvimhe (we indeed were).

Kammani attanopade īkārāgamayappaccayikārāgamā, anubabhūvīyittha, yappaccayassa asabbadhātukamhi “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā lope kate ivaṇṇāgamo na bhavati, tayā kira anubabhūvittha, anubabhūvire iccādi. Bhāve babhūvīyittha, babhūvittha vā.

In the passive, in the Attanopada, the augment 'ī', the suffix 'ya', and the augment 'i' occur, as in anubabhūvīyittha (it was experienced). When the ya-suffix is elided in a non-sabbadhātuka context by the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., the augment 'i' does not occur, as in: tayā kira anubabhūvittha (it was indeed experienced by you), anubabhūvire (they were experienced), etc. In the impersonal: babhūvīyittha, or babhūvittha.

Tathā papaca, papacū. Papace, papacittha. Papacaṃ, papacimha. Papacittha, papacire. Papacittho, papacivho. Papaciṃ, papacimhe.

Similarly: papaca (he cooked), papacū (they cooked). Papace (you cooked), papacittha (you all cooked). Papacaṃ (I cooked), papacimha (we cooked). [Attanopada:] Papacittha (he cooked), papacire (they cooked). Papacittho (you cooked), papacivho (you all cooked). Papaciṃ (I cooked), papacimhe (we cooked).

Kammani papaccittha, papaccire iccādi. Tathā apacca, apaccū iccādi.

In the passive: papaccittha (it was cooked), papaccire (they were cooked), etc. Similarly, apacca, apaccū (he cooked, they cooked), etc.

Gamimhi “kvacādivaṇṇāna”ntiādinā dvebhāvo, “pubbobbhāso”ti abbhāsasaññā.

In the case of 'gam' (to go), doubling occurs by the rule 'kvaci ādivaṇṇānaṃ' etc., and the designation 'abbhāsa' (reduplication) by 'pubbo'bbhāso' (the first part is the reduplication).

“Abbhāse”ti vattate.

The heading 'abbhāse' (in the reduplication) is carried forward.

467. Kavaggassa cavaggo.

467. The ka-class becomes the ca-class.

Abbhāse vattamānassa kavaggassa cavaggo hotīti vakārassa jakāro, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā anabbhāsassa paṭhamapurisekavacanamhi dīgho. So gāmaṃ jagāma kira, jagama vā, jagamu. Jagame, jagamittha. Jagamaṃ, jagamimha. Jagamittha, jagamire. Jagamittho, jagamivho. Jagamiṃ, jagamimhe.

For a ka-class consonant occurring in the reduplication, the ca-class occurs; thus, 'g' becomes 'j'. By the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., the vowel of the non-reduplicated part is lengthened in the third person singular. So gāmaṃ jagāma kira (he indeed went to the village), or jagama; jagamu (they went). Jagame (you went), jagamittha (you all went). Jagamaṃ (I went), jagamimha (we went). [Attanopada:] Jagamittha (he went), jagamire (they went). Jagamittho (you went), jagamivho (you all went). Jagamiṃ (I went), jagamimhe (we went).

Kammani jagamīyittha, jagamittha vā iccādi.

In the passive: jagamīyittha, or jagamittha (it was gone to), etc.

Parokkhāvibhatti.

The Parokkhā (Perfect) Inflection.

468. Ajjatanī [M 0.0278] ī uṃ, o ttha, iṃ mhā, ā ū, se vhaṃ, amhe.

468. The Ajjatanī (Aorist) endings: ī, uṃ; o, ttha; iṃ, mhā. [Attanopada:] ā, ū; se, vhaṃ; iṃ, amhe.

Īādayo dvādasa ajjatanīsaññā honti. Ajja bhavo ajjatano, taddīpakattā ayaṃ vibhatti ajjatanīti vuccati.

The twelve endings beginning with 'ī' are designated Ajjatanī. 'Ajjatana' means 'of today'; because this inflection indicates that, it is called Ajjatanī.

“Apaccakkhe, atīte, paccakkhe”ti ca vattate.

And the headings 'apaccakkhe' (unperceived), 'atīte' (in the past), and 'paccakkhe' (perceived) are carried forward.

469. Samīpejjatanī.

469. The Ajjatanī in the Near Past.

Samīpe samīpato paṭṭhāya ajjappabhuti atīte kāle paccakkhe ca apaccakkhe ca ajjatanīvibhatti hotīti ajjatanīparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ ī.

The Ajjatanī inflection is used for the near past, that is, for past time beginning from today, in both perceived and unperceived contexts. The Ajjatanī, Parassapada, third person singular ending is 'ī'.

Pure viya akārāgamo, vuddhādi ca, “kvaci dhātuvibhattī”tiādinā īmhādivibhattīnaṃ kvaci rassattaṃ, oāavacanānaṃ itthaamādesā ca, saralopādi, so abhavi, abhavī vā, akārāgamābhāve bhavi.

As before, the augment 'a' occurs, as well as vṛddhi and other changes. By the rule 'kvaci dhātuvibhatti' etc., the inflections such as 'ī' and 'mhā' are sometimes shortened; the endings 'o' and 'ā' are substituted by 'i', 'ttha', and 'aṃ'; and vowel elision, etc., also occurs. Thus: so abhavi, or abhavī; and in the absence of the augment 'a', bhavi (he was).

Maṇḍūkagatiyā “vā”ti vattate.

By the frog-leap principle (maṇḍūkagatiyā), 'vā' (or) is carried forward.

470. Sabbato uṃ iṃ su.

470. After all [roots], uṃ [becomes] iṃ [or] su.

Sabbehi dhātūhi uṃvibhattissa iṃsvādeso hoti vā.

After all roots, the inflection 'uṃ' is optionally substituted by 'iṃsu'.

Te abhaviṃsu, bhaviṃsu vā, abhavuṃ, bhavuṃ vā. Tvaṃ abhavi, bhavi vā, abhavo, bhavo vā, tumhe abhavittha, bhavittha vā, ikārāgamo. Ahaṃ abhaviṃ, bhaviṃ vā, mayaṃ abhavimha, bhavimha vā, abhavimhā, bhavimhā vā. So abhavittha, bhavittha vā, abhavā, bhavā vā, abhavū, bhavū vā. Abhavise, bhavise vā, abhavivhaṃ, bhavivhaṃ vā. Abhavaṃ[M 0.0279], bhavaṃ vā, abhava, bhava vā, abhavimhe, bhavimhe vā.

Te abhaviṃsu, or bhaviṃsu; abhavuṃ, or bhavuṃ (They were). Tvaṃ abhavi, or bhavi; abhavo, or bhavo (You were). Tumhe abhavittha, or bhavittha (You all were), with the augment 'i'. Ahaṃ abhaviṃ, or bhaviṃ (I was). Mayaṃ abhavimha, or bhavimha; abhavimhā, or bhavimhā (We were). [Attanopada:] So abhavittha, or bhavittha; abhavā, or bhavā (He was); te abhavū, or bhavū (They were). Tvaṃ abhavise, or bhavise (You were). Tumhe abhavivhaṃ, or bhavivhaṃ (You all were). Ahaṃ abhavaṃ, or bhavaṃ; abhava, or bhava (I was). Mayaṃ abhavimhe, or bhavimhe (We were).

Kammani yappaccayalope vuddhiavādesādi, sukhaṃ tayā anubhavittha, anvabhūyittha, anubhūyittha vā iccādi. Parassapadatte tayā anvabhūyi, anubhūyi, anvabhūyī, anubhūyī vā, anvabhūyiṃsu, anubhūyiṃsu, anvabhūyuṃ, anubhūyuṃ. Tvaṃ anvabhūyi, anubhūyi, tumhe anvabhūyittha, anubhūyittha. Ahaṃ anvabhūyiṃ, anubhūyiṃ, mayaṃ anvabhūyimha, anubhūyimha, anvabhūyimhā, anubhūyimhā vā. Bhāve abhavittha, abhūyittha tayā.

In the passive, with the elision of the 'ya' suffix, vṛddhi, the 'av' substitute, etc., occur. For example: sukhaṃ tayā anubhavittha (happiness was experienced by you), anvabhūyittha, or anubhūyittha, etc. In the Parassapada (used for the passive): tayā anvabhūyi, or anubhūyi; anvabhūyī, or anubhūyī (it was experienced by you); anvabhūyiṃsu, or anubhūyiṃsu; anvabhūyuṃ, or anubhūyuṃ (they were experienced). Tvaṃ anvabhūyi, or anubhūyi (you were experienced); tumhe anvabhūyittha, or anubhūyittha (you all were experienced). Ahaṃ anvabhūyiṃ, or anubhūyiṃ (I was experienced); mayaṃ anvabhūyimha, or anubhūyimha; anvabhūyimhā, or anubhūyimhā (we were experienced). In the impersonal: abhavittha, or abhūyittha tayā (there was being by you).

So apaci, paci, apacī, pacī vā, te apaciṃsu, paciṃsu, apacuṃ, pacuṃ. Tvaṃ apaci, paci, apaco, paco vā, tumhe apacittha, pacittha. Ahaṃ apaciṃ, paciṃ, mayaṃ apacimha, pacimha, apacimhā, pacimhā vā. So apacittha, pacittha, apacā, pacā vā, apacū, pacū. Apacise, apacivhaṃ. Apacaṃ, pacaṃ, apaca, paca vā, apacimhe, pacimhe.

So apaci, or paci; apacī, or pacī (He cooked). Te apaciṃsu, or paciṃsu; apacuṃ, or pacuṃ (They cooked). Tvaṃ apaci, or paci; apaco, or paco (You cooked). Tumhe apacittha, or pacittha (You all cooked). Ahaṃ apaciṃ, or paciṃ (I cooked). Mayaṃ apacimha, or pacimha; apacimhā, or pacimhā (We cooked). [Attanopada:] So apacittha, or pacittha; apacā, or pacā (He cooked); te apacū, or pacū (They cooked). Tvaṃ apacise (You cooked). Tumhe apacivhaṃ (You all cooked). Ahaṃ apacaṃ, or pacaṃ; apaca, or paca (I cooked). Mayaṃ apacimhe, or pacimhe (We cooked).

Kammani apaccittha, paccittha iccādi. Parassapadatte apacci, pacci, apaccī, paccī vā, apacciṃsu, pacciṃsu, apaccuṃ, paccuṃ. Apacci, pacci, apacco, pacco vā, apaccittha, paccittha. Apacciṃ, pacciṃ, apaccimha, paccimha, apaccimhā, paccimhā vā.

In the passive: apaccittha, paccittha, etc. In the Parassapada (used for the passive): apacci, or pacci; apaccī, or paccī (it was cooked); apacciṃsu, or pacciṃsu; apaccuṃ, or paccuṃ (they were cooked). Apacci, or pacci; apacco, or pacco (you were cooked); apaccittha, or paccittha (you all were cooked). Apacciṃ, or pacciṃ (I was cooked); apaccimha, or pacimha; apaccimhā, or paccimhā (we were cooked).

So gāmaṃ agacchī, gacchī, agacchi, gacchi vā, te agacchiṃsu, gacchiṃsu, agacchuṃ, gacchuṃ. Tvaṃ agacchi, gacchi, agaccho, gaccho vā, tumhe agacchittha, gacchittha. Ahaṃ agacchiṃ, gacchiṃ, mayaṃ agacchimha, gacchimha, agacchimhā, gacchimhā vā.

So gāmaṃ agacchī, or gacchī; agacchi, or gacchi (He went to the village). Te agacchiṃsu, or gacchiṃsu; agacchuṃ, or gacchuṃ (They went). Tvaṃ agacchi, or gacchi; agaccho, or gaccho (You went). Tumhe agacchittha, or gacchittha (You all went). Ahaṃ agacchiṃ, or gacchiṃ (I went). Mayaṃ agacchimha, or gacchimha; agacchimhā, or gacchimhā (We went).

“Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ajjatanimhi gamissa cchassa kvaci ñchādeso, agañchi, gañchi, agañchī, gañchī vā, te agañchiṃsu[M 0.0280], gañchiṃsu, agañchuṃ, gañchuṃ. Tvaṃ agañchi, gañchi, agañcho, gañcho vā, tumhe agañchittha, gañchittha. Ahaṃ agañchiṃ, gañchiṃ, mayaṃ agañchimha, gañchimha, agañchimhā, gañchimhā vā.

By the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., in the Ajjatanī, the 'ccha' from 'gam' is sometimes substituted by 'ñcha'. Thus: agañchi, or gañchi; agañchī, or gañchī (he went). Te agañchiṃsu, or gañchiṃsu; agañchuṃ, or gañchuṃ (they went). Tvaṃ agañchi, or gañchi; agañcho, or gañcho (you went). Tumhe agañchittha, or gañchittha (you all went). Ahaṃ agañchiṃ, or gañchiṃ (I went). Mayaṃ agañchimha, or gañchimha; agañchimhā, or gañchimhā (we went).

Cchādesābhāve so agami, gami, agamī, gamī vā, “karassa kāsattamajjatanimhī”ti ettha bhāvaniddesena, “sattamajjatanimhī”ti yogavibhāgena vā sāgame “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā byañjanato ākārāgamo, agamāsi, uṃvacanassa kvaci aṃsvādeso, ucāgamo tthamhesu kvaci, agamiṃsu, gamiṃsu, agamaṃsu, gamaṃsu, agamuṃ, gamuṃ, tvaṃ agami, gami, agamo, gamo vā, agamittha, gamittha, agamuttha, gamuttha. Ahaṃ agamiṃ, gamiṃ, agamimha, gamimha, agamumha, gamumha, agamimhā, gamimhā vā.

In the absence of the 'ccha' substitution: so agami, or gami; agamī, or gamī (he went). By the indication of the impersonal (bhāvaniddesena) in the rule 'karassa kāsattamajjatanimhī', or by splitting the rule as 'sattamajjatanimhī', the 's' augment occurs; then by 'kvaci dhātu' etc., the preceding vowel is lengthened, resulting in agamāsi. For the ending 'uṃ', 'aṃsu' is sometimes the substitute. The augment 'u' sometimes occurs before the endings 'ttha' and 'mha'. Thus: agamiṃsu, or gamiṃsu; agamaṃsu, or gamaṃsu; agamuṃ, or gamuṃ (they went). Tvaṃ agami, or gami; agamo, or gamo (you went); agamittha, or gamittha; agamuttha, or gamuttha (you all went). Ahaṃ agamiṃ, or gamiṃ (I went); agamimha, or gamimha; agamumha, or gamumha; agamimhā, or gamimhā (we went).

“Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā gamissa ajjatanimhi gādeso ca, so ajjhagā, paralopo, te ajjhaguṃ. Tvaṃ ajjhago, tumhe ajjhaguttha. Ahaṃ ajjhagiṃ, mayaṃ ajjhagumha.

By the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., for 'gam' in the Ajjatanī, there is also the substitute 'gā'. Thus: so ajjhagā (he went/attained), with elision of the following letter. Te ajjhaguṃ (they went/attained). Tvaṃ ajjhago (you went/attained); tumhe ajjhaguttha (you all went/attained). Ahaṃ ajjhagiṃ (I went/attained); mayaṃ ajjhagumha (we went/attained).

Attanopade so agacchittha, gacchittha, agañchittha, gañchittha iccādi. Cchādesābhāve so agamittha, gamittha, agamā, gamā, te agamū, gamū, ajjhagū, agū. Tvaṃ agamise, gamise, agamivhaṃ, gamivhaṃ. Ahaṃ agamaṃ, gamaṃ, agama, gama, ajjhagaṃ vā, agamimhe, gamimhe.

In the middle voice (Attanopada): 'so agacchittha', 'gacchittha', 'agañchittha', 'gañchittha', and so on (he went). In the absence of the 'ccha' substitution: 'so agamittha', 'gamittha', 'agamā', or 'gamā' (he went); 'te agamū', 'gamū', 'ajjhagū', or 'agū' (they went/attained). 'Tvaṃ agamise', 'gamise' (you went); 'agamivhaṃ', or 'gamivhaṃ' (you (pl.) went). 'Ahaṃ agamaṃ', 'gamaṃ', 'agama', or 'gama' (I went); 'ajjhagaṃ vā' (or I attained); 'agamimhe', or 'gamimhe' (we went).

Kamme gāmo agacchīyittha tena, gacchīyittha, agañchiyittha, gañchiyittha, agamīyittha, gamīyittha, agamittha, gamittha iccādi. Parassapadatte agacchīyi, gacchīyi vā, agamīyi, gamīyi [M 0.0281] vā, agacchīyuṃ, agamīyuṃ vā. Tathā aghammīyi, aghammīyiṃsu iccādi.

In the passive voice (Kamma): 'gāmo agacchīyittha tena' (the village was gone to by him), 'gacchīyittha', 'agañchiyittha', 'gañchiyittha', 'agamīyittha', 'gamīyittha', 'agamittha', 'gamittha', and so on. When active endings (Parassapada) are used for the passive: 'agacchīyi', or 'gacchīyi' (it was gone to); 'agamīyi', or 'gamīyi' (it was gone to); 'agacchīyuṃ', or 'agamīyuṃ' (they were gone to). Similarly: 'aghammīyi', 'aghammīyiṃsu', and so on (it was sweated/glowed, they were sweated/glowed).

“Hiyyattanī, ajjatanī”ti ca vattate.

The Hiyyattanī (imperfect) and Ajjatanī (aorist) also apply.

471. Māyoge sabbakāle ca.

471. And in all tenses when 'mā' (the prohibitive particle) is used.

Yadāmāyogo, tadā hiyyattanajjatanīvibhattiyo sabbakālepi honti, casaddena pañcamī ca. Mā bhavati, mā bhavā, mā bhavissatīti vā atthe hiyyattanajjatanīpañcamī vibhattiyo, sesaṃ neyyaṃ, so mā bhavā, mā bhavī, mā te bhavantvantarāyā. Mā pacā, mā pacī, mā pacatu. Mā gacchā, mā gacchī, mā gacchatu. Mā kañci pāpamāgamā, mā agami, mā gamā, mā gamī, mā gametu. Tvaṃ mā gaccho, mā gacchi, mā gacchāhi iccādi.

When 'mā' is used, then the Hiyyattanī (imperfect) and Ajjatanī (aorist) inflections occur in all tenses, and by the word 'ca', the Pañcamī (imperative) as well. For example, in the sense of 'mā bhavati' (let it not be), 'mā bhavā' (let it not be), or 'mā bhavissati' (it will not be), the Hiyyattanī, Ajjatanī, and Pañcamī inflections are used. The rest should be understood. For example: 'so mā bhavā', 'mā bhavī' (may he not be); 'mā te bhavantvantarāyā' (may no obstacles arise for you). 'Mā pacā', 'mā pacī', 'mā pacatu' (let him not cook). 'Mā gacchā', 'mā gacchī', 'mā gacchatu' (let him not go). 'Mā kañci pāpamāgamā' (may you not go to any evil); 'mā agami', 'mā gamā', 'mā gamī', 'mā gametu' (let him not go). 'Tvaṃ mā gaccho', 'mā gacchi', 'mā gacchāhi', and so on (do not you go).

Atītakālikavibhatti.

The Inflections for Past Time.

472. Bhavissantī ssati ssanti, ssasi ssatha, ssāmissāma, ssate ssante, ssase ssavhe, ssaṃssāmhe.

472. The Bhavissantī (future tense) endings are: ssati, ssanti; ssasi, ssatha; ssāmi, ssāma. And for the middle voice: ssate, ssante; ssase, ssavhe; ssaṃ, ssāmhe.

Ssatyādīnaṃ dvādasannaṃ vacanānaṃ bhavissantīsaññā hoti. Bhavissatīti bhavissanto, taṃkāladīpakattā ayaṃ vibhatti bhavissantīti vuccati.

The twelve endings beginning with 'ssati' are designated as Bhavissantī (future). 'Bhavissati' means 'that which will be'; because it indicates that time, this inflection is called 'Bhavissantī'.

473. Anāgate bhavissantī.

473. The Bhavissantī (future tense) is used for the future.

Anāgate kāle bhavissantīvibhatti hoti.

In future time, the Bhavissantī (future tense) inflection occurs.

Atītepi bhavissantī, taṃkālavacanicchayā;

“Anekajātisaṃsāraṃ, sandhāvissa”ntiādisu.

The Bhavissantī (future tense) is also used for the past, by the desire to express that time; as in, 'Anekajātisaṃsāraṃ, sandhāvissaṃ' ('Through the round of many births, I would have to wander'), and so on.

Na [M 0.0282] āgato anāgato, paccayasāmaggiyaṃ sati āyatiṃ uppajjanārahoti attho, ikārāgamo, vuddhiavādesā, saralopādi ca.

'Anāgata' means 'not come'. The meaning is that when the aggregate of conditions exists, it is capable of arising in the future. The grammatical operations include the augment 'i', vuddhi and avādesa substitutions, vowel elision, and so on.

Bhavissati, bhavissanti. Bhavissasi, bhavissatha. Bhavissāmi, bhavissāma. Bhavissate, bhavissante. Bhavissase, bhavissavhe. Bhavissaṃ, bhavissāmhe.

Bhavissati (he will be), bhavissanti (they will be). Bhavissasi (you will be), bhavissatha (you all will be). Bhavissāmi (I will be), bhavissāma (we will be). In the middle voice: Bhavissate (he will be), bhavissante (they will be). Bhavissase (you will be), bhavissavhe (you all will be). Bhavissaṃ (I will be), bhavissāmhe (we will be).

Kamme yappaccayalopo, sukhaṃ tayā anubhavissate, anubhavissante. Anubhavissase, anubhavissavhe. Anubhavissaṃ, anubhavissāmhe. Parassapadatte anubhavissati devadattena, anubhavissanti iccādi. Bhāve bhavissate tena, yappaccayalopābhāve anubhūyissate, anubhūyissante iccādi. Bhāve bhūyissate.

In the passive voice (Kamma), with the elision of the 'ya' suffix: 'sukhaṃ tayā anubhavissate' (happiness will be experienced by you), 'anubhavissante' (they will be experienced). 'Anubhavissase' (you will be experienced), 'anubhavissavhe' (you (pl.) will be experienced). 'Anubhavissaṃ' (I will be experienced), 'anubhavissāmhe' (we will be experienced). When active endings (Parassapada) are used for the passive: 'anubhavissati devadattena' (it will be experienced by Devadatta), 'anubhavissanti' (they will be experienced), and so on. In the impersonal voice (Bhāva): 'bhavissate tena' (it will be by him). In the absence of the 'ya' suffix elision: 'anubhūyissate', 'anubhūyissante', and so on (it will be experienced, they will be experienced). In the impersonal voice: 'bhūyissate' (it will be).

Tathā pacissati, pacissanti. Pacissasi, pacissatha. Pacissāmi, pacissāma. Pacissate, pacissante. Pacissase, pacissavhe. Pacissaṃ, pacissāmhe.

Similarly: Pacissati (he will cook), pacissanti (they will cook). Pacissasi (you will cook), pacissatha (you all will cook). Pacissāmi (I will cook), pacissāma (we will cook). In the middle voice: Pacissate (he will cook), pacissante (they will cook). Pacissase (you will cook), pacissavhe (you all will cook). Pacissaṃ (I will cook), pacissāmhe (we will cook).

Kamme paccissate odano devadattena, paccissante iccādi. Parassapadatte paccissati, paccissanti. Paccissasi, paccissatha. Paccissāmi, paccissāma.

In the passive voice (Kamma): 'odano devadattena paccissate' (the rice will be cooked by Devadatta), 'paccissante' (they will be cooked), and so on. When active endings (Parassapada) are used for the passive: 'paccissati' (it will be cooked), 'paccissanti' (they will be cooked). 'Paccissasi' (you will be cooked), 'paccissatha' (you (pl.) will be cooked). 'Paccissāmi' (I will be cooked), 'paccissāma' (we will be cooked).

Gacchissati, gacchissanti. Gacchissasi, gacchissatha. Gacchissāmi, gacchissāma. Gacchissate, gacchissante. Gacchissase, gacchissavhe. Gacchissaṃ, gacchissāmhe. So saggaṃ gamissati, gamissanti. Gamissasi, gamissatha. Gamissāmi, gamissāma iccādi.

Gacchissati (he will go), gacchissanti (they will go). Gacchissasi (you will go), gacchissatha (you all will go). Gacchissāmi (I will go), gacchissāma (we will go). In the middle voice: Gacchissate (he will go), gacchissante (they will go). Gacchissase (you will go), gacchissavhe (you all will go). Gacchissaṃ (I will go), gacchissāmhe (we will go). 'So saggaṃ gamissati' (He will go to heaven), 'gamissanti' (they will go). 'Gamissasi' (you will go), 'gamissatha' (you (pl.) will go). 'Gamissāmi' (I will go), 'gamissāma' (we will go), and so on.

Kamme gacchīyissate, gacchīyissante. Gacchīyissati, gacchīyissanti vā, gamīyissate, gamīyissante. Gamīyissati, gamīyissanti vā iccādi. Yappaccayalope gamissate[M 0.0283], gamissante. Gamissati, gamissanti vā. Tathā ghammissati, ghammissanti iccādi.

In the passive voice (Kamma): 'gacchīyissate' (it will be gone to), 'gacchīyissante' (they will be gone to). Or, with active endings: 'gacchīyissati', 'gacchīyissanti' (it will be gone to, they will be gone to). 'Gamīyissate', 'gamīyissante' (it will be gone to, they will be gone to). Or, with active endings: 'gamīyissati', 'gamīyissanti' (it will be gone to, they will be gone to), and so on. With the elision of the 'ya' suffix: 'gamissate' (it will be gone to), 'gamissante' (they will be gone to). Or, with active endings: 'gamissati', 'gamissanti' (it will be gone to, they will be gone to). Similarly: 'ghammissati' (it will be hot), 'ghammissanti' (they will be hot), and so on.

Bhavissantīvibhatti.

The Bhavissantī (Future Tense) Inflection.

484. Kālātipatti ssā ssaṃsu, sse ssatha, ssaṃssāmhā, ssatha ssisu, ssase ssavhe, ssiṃssāmhase.

484. The Kālātipatti (conditional) endings are: ssā, ssaṃsu; sse, ssatha; ssaṃ, ssāmhā. And for the middle voice: ssatha, ssisu; ssase, ssavhe; ssiṃ, ssāmhase.

Ssādīnaṃ dvādasannaṃ kālātipattisaññā hoti. Kālassa atipatanaṃ kālātipatti, sā pana viruddhapaccayūpanipātato, kāraṇavekallato vā kriyāya anabhinibbatti, taddīpakattā ayaṃ vibhatti kālātipattīti vuccati.

The twelve endings beginning with 'ssā' are designated as Kālātipatti (conditional). 'Kālassa atipatanaṃ' (the lapsing of time) is 'kālātipatti'. This is the non-occurrence of an action due to the arising of opposing conditions or the deficiency of causes. Because it indicates this, this inflection is called 'Kālātipatti'.

475. Kriyātipannetīte kālātipatti.

475. The Kālātipatti (conditional) is used for the past where the action has lapsed.

Kriyātipannamatte atīte kāle kālātipattivibhatti hoti. Kriyāya atipatanaṃ kriyātipannaṃ, taṃ pana sādhakasattivirahena kriyāya accantānuppatti. Ettha ca kiñcāpi na kriyā atītasaddena voharitabbā, tathāpi takkiriyuppattippaṭibandhakarakriyāya kālabhedena atītavohāro labbhatevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

When an action has failed to occur in past time, the Kālātipatti inflection is used. The failure of an action (kriyātipanna) is its complete non-occurrence due to the absence of the accomplishing power. Here, although the action itself should not be designated by the word 'past,' nevertheless, it should be understood that the designation 'past' is indeed obtained due to the difference in time of the action that obstructs its arising.

Kālātipattiparassapadapaṭhamapurisekavacanaṃ ssā, akārikārāgamā, vuddhiavādesā ca, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ssā ssāmhāvibhattīnaṃ kvaci rassattaṃ, ssevacanassa ca attaṃ.

The Kālātipatti third-person singular active ending is ssā. The augments a and i are added, and the substitutions vuddhi and ava occur. Sometimes, according to the rule 'kvaci dhātū...', the endings ssā and ssāmhā are shortened, and the ending sse is changed to atta.

So ce paṭhamavaye pabbajjaṃ alabhissa, arahā abhavissa, bhavissa, abhavissā, bhavissāvā, te ce taṃ alabhissaṃsu, arahanto abhavissaṃsu, bhavissaṃsu. Evaṃ tvaṃ abhavissa, bhavissa, abhavisse vā, tumhe abhavissatha, bhavissatha. Ahaṃ abhavissaṃ, bhavissaṃ, mayaṃ [M 0.0284] abhavissamha, bhavissamha, abhavissāmhā, bhavissāmhā vā. So abhavissatha, abhavissisu. Abhavissase, abhavissavhe. Abhavissiṃ, abhavissāmhase.

If he had gone forth in the first stage of life, he would have become an arahant; he would have been (abhavissa, bhavissa, abhavissā, or bhavissāvā). If they had obtained that, they would have become arahants; they would have been (abhavissaṃsu, bhavissaṃsu). Similarly, you would have been (abhavissa, bhavissa, or abhavisse); you all would have been (abhavissatha, bhavissatha). I would have been (abhavissaṃ, bhavissaṃ); we would have been (abhavissamha, bhavissamha, abhavissāmhā, or bhavissāmhā). In the middle voice: He would have been (abhavissatha), they would have been (abhavissisu). You would have been (abhavissase), you all would have been (abhavissavhe). I would have been (abhavissiṃ), we would have been (abhavissāmhase).

Kamme anvabhavissatha, anvabhavissisu. Anvabhūyissatha vā iccādi. Parassapadatte anvabhavissa, anvabhavissaṃsu. Anvabhūyissa vā iccādi. Bhāve abhavissatha devadattena, abhūyissatha.

In the passive voice: he would have been experienced (anvabhavissatha), they would have been experienced (anvabhavissisu). Or he would have been experienced (anvabhūyissatha), and so on. When active endings (Parassapada) are used for the passive: it would have been experienced (anvabhavissa), they would have been experienced (anvabhavissaṃsu). Or it would have been experienced (anvabhūyissa), and so on. In the impersonal construction: it would have been by Devadatta (abhavissatha), or it would have been (abhūyissatha).

Tathā so ce taṃ dhanaṃ alabhissa, odanaṃ apacissa, pacissa, apacissā, pacissā vā, apacissaṃsu, pacissaṃsu. Apacissa, pacissa, apacisse, pacisse vā, apacissatha, pacissatha. Apacissaṃ, pacissaṃ, apacissamha, pacissamha, apacissāmhā, pacissāmhā vā. Apacissatha, pacissatha, apacissisu, pacissisu. Apacissase, pacissase, apacissavhe, pacissavhe. Apacissiṃ, pacissiṃ, apacissāmhase, pacissāmhase.

Similarly, if he had obtained that wealth, he would have cooked the rice (apacissa, pacissa, apacissā, or pacissā); they would have cooked (apacissaṃsu, pacissaṃsu). You would have cooked (apacissa, pacissa, apacisse, or pacisse); you all would have cooked (apacissatha, pacissatha). I would have cooked (apacissaṃ, pacissaṃ); we would have cooked (apacissamha, pacissamha, apacissāmhā, or pacissāmhā). In the middle voice: He would have cooked (apacissatha, pacissatha), they would have cooked (apacissisu, pacissisu). You would have cooked (apacissase, pacissase), you all would have cooked (apacissavhe, pacissavhe). I would have cooked (apacissiṃ, pacissiṃ), we would have cooked (apacissāmhase, pacissāmhase).

Kamme apacissatha odano devadattena, apacissisu. Yappaccayalopābhāve apacīyissatha iccādi. Parassapadatte apaccissa tena, paccissa, apaccissā, paccissā vā, apaccissaṃsu, paccissaṃsu iccādi.

In the passive voice: the rice would have been cooked by Devadatta (apacissatha); they would have been cooked (apacissisu). In the absence of the elision of the 'ya' suffix: it would have been cooked (apacīyissatha), and so on. When active endings (Parassapada) are used for the passive: it would have been cooked by him (apaccissa); it would have been cooked (paccissa, apaccissā, or paccissā); they would have been cooked (apaccissaṃsu, paccissaṃsu), and so on.

So agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchissā, gacchissāvā, agacchissaṃsu, gacchissaṃsu. Tvaṃ agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchisse, gacchisse vā, agacchissatha, gacchissatha. Agacchissaṃ, gacchissaṃ, agacchissamha, gacchissamha, agacchissāmhā, gacchissāmhā vā. Agamissa, gamissa, agamissā, gamissā vā, agamissaṃsu, gamissaṃsu. Agamissa, gamissa, agamisse vā, agamissatha, gamissatha. Agamissaṃ[M 0.0285], gamissaṃ, agamissamha, gamissamha, agamissāmhā, gamissāmhā vā. Agacchissatha, gacchissatha vā iccādi.

He would have gone: agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchissā, or gacchissā; they would have gone: agacchissaṃsu, gacchissaṃsu. You would have gone: agacchissa, gacchissa, agacchisse, or gacchisse; you (plural) would have gone: agacchissatha, gacchissatha. I would have gone: agacchissaṃ, gacchissaṃ; we would have gone: agacchissamha, gacchissamha, agacchissāmhā, or gacchissāmhā. He would have gone: agamissa, gamissa, agamissā, or gamissā; they would have gone: agamissaṃsu, gamissaṃsu. You would have gone: agamissa, gamissa, or agamisse; you (plural) would have gone: agamissatha, gamissatha. I would have gone: agamissaṃ, gamissaṃ; we would have gone: agamissamha, gamissamha, agamissāmhā, or gamissāmhā. You (plural) would have gone: agacchissatha or gacchissatha, and so on.

Kamme agacchīyissatha, agamīyissatha, agacchīyissa, agamīyissaiccādi. Tathā aghammissā, aghammissaṃsu iccādi.

In the passive voice: you (plural) would have been gone (agacchīyissatha), you (plural) would have been gone (agamīyissatha), he would have been gone (agacchīyissa), he would have been gone (agamīyissa), and so on. Similarly: he would have struck (aghammissā), they would have struck (aghammissaṃsu), and so on.

Kālātipattivibhatti.

The conditional mood (tense of non-occurrence of action).

Pañcamī sattamī vatta-mānā sampatināgate;

Bhavissantī parokkhādī, catassotītakālikā.

The imperative (fifth) and optative (seventh) moods are for the present and future. The future tense is for the future; the four tenses beginning with the remote past are for past time.

Chakālikavibhattividhānaṃ.

The section on the six tenses and moods.

Vikaraṇavidhāna

The section on stem-forming suffixes (vikaraṇa).

Isu icchākantīsu, pure viya dhātvantalopo, tyādyuppatti, appaccayo ca.

For the root isu in the sense of desiring (icchā) and wishing (kanti), as before, there is elision of the final letter of the root, the arising of tya and so on, and the suffix a.

“Dhātūna”nti vattamāne –

When the rule concerning 'of roots' (dhātūnaṃ) is current:

476. Isuyamūnamanto ccho vā.

476. The final letter of the roots isu, yam, and mu optionally becomes ccha.

Isuyamuiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto ccho hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, “anto ccho vā”ti yogavibhāgena āsassapi. So saggaṃ icchati, icchanti. Icchasi, icchatha. Icchāmi, icchāma. Cchādesābhāve asaṃyogantattā “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi, esati, esanti iccādi.

For these roots, isu, yam, and mu, the final letter optionally becomes ccha. This word 'optionally' (vā) indicates a fixed option; by division of the rule as 'anto ccho vā', it applies also to the root āsa. He desires heaven (so saggaṃ icchati); they desire (icchanti). You desire (icchasi); you (plural) desire (icchatha). I desire (icchāmi); we desire (icchāma). In the absence of the ccha substitution, because the root does not end in a conjunct consonant, there is vowel strengthening by the rule 'aññesu cā', giving: he seeks (esati), they seek (esanti), and so on.

Kamme attanopadassa yebhuyyena parassapadattameva payojīyati, tena cettha attanopade rūpāni saṅkhipissāma. So icchīyati, esīyati, issate, issati, yakārassa [M 0.0286] pubbarūpattaṃ. Tathā icchatu, esatu. Iccheyya, eseyya. Parokkhāhiyyattanīsu pana rūpāni sabbattha payogamanugamma payojetabbāni, icchi, esi. Icchissati, esissati. Icchissā, esissā icchādi.

In the passive voice, the active endings (parassapada) are mostly used instead of the middle endings (attanopada). Therefore, here we will summarize the forms in the middle voice. He is desired (icchīyati), he is sought (esīyati), he is wished (issate), he is wished (issati), with assimilation of the ya to the preceding consonant. Similarly: may he desire (icchatu), may he seek (esatu). He would desire (iccheyya), he would seek (eseyya). However, in the remote past (parokkhā) and the imperfect (hiyyattanī), the forms should be applied following usage everywhere: he desired (icchi), he sought (esi). He will desire (icchissati), he will seek (esissati). He would have desired (icchissā), he would have sought (esissā), and so on.

Yamu uparame, nipubbo, cchādeso ca. Niyacchati, niyacchanti. Niyamati, niyamanti. Saṃpubbo “saye cā”ti ñattaṃ, dvittañca. Saññamati, saññamanti.

The root Yamu means to cease or restrain. With the prefix ni, and the ccha substitution: he restrains (niyacchati), they restrain (niyacchanti). Without the substitution: he restrains (niyamati), they restrain (niyamanti). With the prefix saṃ, by the rule 'saye cā', there is the change to ñ and doubling: he restrains himself (saññamati), they restrain themselves (saññamanti).

Kamme niyacchīyati, niyamīyati, niyammati, saññamīyati vā. Tathā niyacchatu, saññamatu. Niyaccheyya, saññameyya. Niyacchī, saññamī. Niyacchissati, saññamissati. Niyacchissa, saññamissa iccādi.

In the passive voice: one is restrained (niyacchīyati), one is restrained (niyamīyati), one is restrained (niyammati), or one is restrained (saññamīyati). Similarly: let him restrain (niyacchatu), let him restrain himself (saññamatu). He should restrain (niyaccheyya), he should restrain himself (saññameyya). He restrained (niyacchī), he restrained himself (saññamī). He will restrain (niyacchissati), he will restrain himself (saññamissati). He would have restrained (niyacchissa), he would have restrained himself (saññamissa), and so on.

Āsa upavesane, yogavibhāgena cchādeso, rassattaṃ. Acchati, acchanti. Acchasi, acchatha. Acchāmi, acchāma. Aññatra upapubbo upāsati, upāsanti. Acchīyati, upāsīyati. Acchatu, upāsatu. Accheyya, upāseyya. Acchī, upāsī. Acchissati, upāsissati. Acchissa, upāsissa iccādi.

The root Āsa means to sit. By division of the rule, there is ccha substitution and shortening of the root vowel. He sits (acchati), they sit (acchanti). You sit (acchasi), you (plural) sit (acchatha). I sit (acchāmi), we sit (acchāma). In other cases, with the prefix upa: he attends (upāsati), they attend (upāsanti). Passive: it is sat (acchīyati), it is attended (upāsīyati). Imperative: let him sit (acchatu), let him attend (upāsatu). Optative: he should sit (accheyya), he should attend (upāseyya). Aorist: he sat (acchī), he attended (upāsī). Future: he will sit (acchissati), he will attend (upāsissati). Conditional: he would have sat (acchissa), he would have attended (upāsissa), and so on.

Labha lābhe, labhati, labhanti. Labhasi, labhatha. Labhāmi, labhāma. Labhate, labhante. Labhase, labhavhe. Labhe, labhāmhe.

The root Labha means to gain. Active voice: he gains (labhati), they gain (labhanti). You gain (labhasi), you (plural) gain (labhatha). I gain (labhāmi), we gain (labhāma). Middle voice: he obtains (labhate), they obtain (labhante). You obtain (labhase), you (plural) obtain (labhavhe). I obtain (labhe), we obtain (labhāmhe).

Kamme yakārassa pubbarūpatte kate “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā purimabhakārassa bakāro, labbhate, labbhante. Labbhati, labbhanti. Labbhataṃ, labbhatu. Labbhe, labbheyya.

In the passive voice, when the ya is assimilated to the preceding consonant, by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., the preceding bh becomes b. Middle voice: it is obtained (labbhate), they are obtained (labbhante). Active voice: it is obtained (labbhati), they are obtained (labbhanti). Imperative: let it be obtained (labbhataṃ), let it be obtained (labbhatu). Optative: it should be obtained (labbhe), it should be obtained (labbheyya).

Ajjatanimhi “vā, antalopo”ti ca vattamāne –

In the aorist tense, while 'optionally' (vā) and 'elision of the final letter' (antalopo) are current:

477. Labhasmā ī iṃnaṃ tthatthaṃ.

477. After the root Labha, the endings ī and iṃ become ttha and tthaṃ respectively.

Labhaiccetasmā dhātuto paresaṃ īiṃnaṃ vibhattīnaṃ ttha tthaṃiccete ādesā honti vā, dhātvantassa lopo [M 0.0287] ca. Alattha, alabhi, labhi, alabhiṃsu, labhiṃsu. Alabho, labho, alabhi, labhi, alabhittha, labhittha. Alatthaṃ, alabhiṃ, labhiṃ, alabhimha, labhimha iccādi.

After this root Labha, the endings ī and iṃ optionally become ttha and tthaṃ respectively, and there is also elision of the final letter of the root. He obtained (alattha, alabhi, labhi); they obtained (alabhiṃsu, labhiṃsu). You obtained (alabho, labho, alabhi, labhi); you (plural) obtained (alabhittha, labhittha). I obtained (alatthaṃ, alabhiṃ, labhiṃ); we obtained (alabhimha, labhimha), and so on.

Bhavissantimhi “karassa sappaccayassa kāho”ti ettha sappaccayaggahaṇena vaca muca bhujādito ssassakhādeso, vasa chida labhādito chādeso ca vā hotīti ssassa chādeso, “byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu cā”ti dhātvantassa cakāro, lacchati, lacchanti. Lacchasi, lacchatha. Lacchāmi, lacchāma. Chādesābhāve labhissati, labhissanti. Labhissasi, labhissatha. Labhissāmi, labhissāma iccādi. Alabhissa, alabhissaṃsu iccādi.

In the future tense, by the inclusion of the term 'with its suffix' (sappaccaya) in the rule 'karassa sappaccayassa kāho', the future suffix ssa is optionally replaced with kha after roots such as vac, muc, bhuj, and optionally replaced with cha after roots such as vasa, chida, labha; thus ssa is replaced with cha. By the rule 'byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu ca', the final letter of the root becomes ca. Thus: he will obtain (lacchati), they will obtain (lacchanti). You will obtain (lacchasi), you (plural) will obtain (lacchatha). I will obtain (lacchāmi), we will obtain (lacchāma). In the absence of the cha substitution: labhissati, labhissanti. Labhissasi, labhissatha. Labhissāmi, labhissāma, and so on. The conditional forms are: he would have obtained (alabhissa), they would have obtained (alabhissaṃsu), and so on.

Vaca viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vacati, vacanti. Vacasi, vacatha. Vacāmi, vacāma.

The root Vaca means to speak distinctly. He speaks (vacati), they speak (vacanti). You speak (vacasi), you (plural) speak (vacatha). I speak (vacāmi), we speak (vacāma).

Kamme attanopade, yappaccaye ca kate –

In the passive voice, in the middle voice (attanopada), and when the ya suffix is applied:

478. Vaca vasa vahādīnamukāro vassa ye.

478. For roots such as Vaca, Vasa, Vaha, their v becomes u before ya.

Vaca vasa vahaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ vakārassa ukāro hoti yappaccaye pare, ādisaddena vaḍḍhassa ca. “Vassa a va”iti samāsena dutiyañcettha vaggahaṇaṃ icchitabbaṃ, tena akārassapi ukāro hoti, purimapakkhe paralopo. “Tassa cavagga”iccādinā sadhātvantassa yakārassa cakāro, dvittaṃ. Uccate, uccante. Vuccate, vuccante. Vuccati, vuccanti vā iccādi. Tathā vacatu, vuccatu. Vaceyya, vucceyya. Avacā, avaccā, avacū, avaccū. Avaca, avaco, avacuttha. Avaca, avacaṃ, avacamhā. Avacuttha iccādi.

For roots such as Vaca, Vasa, Vaha, and so on, their v becomes u when the ya suffix follows; by the word 'etc.' (ādi), this also applies to vaḍḍha. In the compound 'Vassa a va', a second instance of va should be understood, by which the a also becomes u; in the first case, there is elision of the following vowel. By the rule 'Tassa cavagga' etc., the ya together with the final consonant of the root becomes ca, and is doubled. Thus: it is said (uccate), they are said (uccante); or it is said (vuccate), they are said (vuccante); or it is said (vuccati), they are said (vuccanti), and so on. Similarly: let him speak (vacatu), let it be said (vuccatu). He should speak (vaceyya), it should be said (vucceyya). He spoke (avacā, avaccā, avacū, avaccū). You spoke (avaca, avaco, avacuttha). I spoke (avaca, avacaṃ, avacamhā). You (plural) spoke (avacuttha), and so on.

479. Vacassajjatanimhi [M 0.0288] makāro o.

479. For Vaca in the aorist, the a becomes o.

Vacaiccetassa dhātussa akāro ottamāpajjate ajjatanimhi vibhattimhi. Avoci, avocuṃ. Avoco, avocuttha. Avociṃ, avocumha, ukārāgamo. Avoca, rassattaṃ, avocu iccādi. Avuccittha.

For this root Vaca, the a becomes o in the aorist tense. He spoke (avoci), they spoke (avocuṃ). You spoke (avoco), you (plural) spoke (avocuttha). I spoke (avociṃ), we spoke (avocumha), with the augment u. He spoke (avoca), with shortening; they spoke (avocu), and so on. It was said (avuccittha).

Bhavissantimhi sappaccayaggahaṇena ssassa khādeso, “byañjanantassā”ti vattamāne “ko khe cā”ti dhātvantassa kādeso, vakkhati, vakkhanti. Vakkhasi, vakkhatha. Vakkhāmi, vakkhāma iccādi.

In the future tense, by the inclusion of the term 'with its suffix' (sappaccaya), the future suffix ssa is replaced by kha. While the rule for roots ending in a consonant (byañjanantassa) is current, by the rule 'ko khe ca', the final letter of the root is replaced by ka. Thus: he will speak (vakkhati), they will speak (vakkhanti). You will speak (vakkhasi), you (plural) will speak (vakkhatha). I will speak (vakkhāmi), we will speak (vakkhāma), and so on.

Vasa nivāse, vasati, vasanti.

The root Vasa means to dwell. He dwells (vasati), they dwell (vasanti).

Kamme uttaṃ, pubbarūpattañca vussati, vussanti iccādi. Vasatu. Vaseyya. Avasi, vasi.

In the passive voice, the vowel v becomes u and is assimilated to the following consonant. Thus: it is dwelt (vussati), they are dwelt (vussanti), and so on. Imperative: let him dwell (vasatu). Optative: he should dwell (vaseyya). Aorist: he dwelt (avasi, vasi).

Bhavissantiyaṃ ssassa chādeso, dhātvantassa cakāro ca, vacchati, vacchanti. Vacchasi, vacchatha. Vacchāmi, vacchāma. Vasissati, vasissanti. Avasissa, avasissaṃsu.

In the future tense, cha is the substitute for ssa, and the final letter of the root becomes ca. Thus: he will dwell (vacchati), they will dwell (vacchanti). You will dwell (vacchasi), you (plural) will dwell (vacchatha). I will dwell (vacchāmi), we will dwell (vacchāma). The alternative future forms are: he will dwell (vasissati), they will dwell (vasissanti). The conditional forms are: he would have dwelt (avasissa), they would have dwelt (avasissaṃsu).

Tathā ruda assuvimocane, rodati, rucchati. Rodissati iccādi.

Similarly, the root 'rud' is in the sense of shedding tears. 'Rodati,' 'rucchati.' 'Rodissati,' and so on.

Kusa akkose, āpubbo dvittarassattāni, appaccayavuddhiyo ca. Akkosati. Akkosatu. Akkoseyya.

The root 'kus' is in the sense of reviling. With the prefix 'ā', doubling, shortening, and non-augmentation of the suffix occur. 'Akkosati.' 'Akkosatu.' 'Akkoseyya.'

“Antalopo”ti vattate, maṇḍūkagatiyā “vā”ti ca.

The rule 'antalopo' (elision of the final) is carried forward, and 'vā' (optionally) by frog-leap progression.

480. Kusasmā dī cchi.

480. After 'kus', for the 'ī' [ending], 'cchi' [is substituted].

Kusa iccetasmā dhātuto īvibhattissa cchiādeso hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Akkocchi maṃ, akkosi vā. Akkosissati. Akkosissa iccādi.

From this root 'kus', the substitution of 'cchi' for the 'ī' ending occurs, and the elision of the root's final letter. 'Akkocchi maṃ' (He reviled me), or 'akkosi'. 'Akkosissati.' 'Akkosissa,' and so on.

Vaha [M 0.0289] pāpuṇane, vahati, vahanti.

The root 'vah' is in the sense of reaching. 'Vahati,' 'vahanti.'

Kamme attanopade, yappaccaye ca kate –

In the passive voice, in the attanopada, and when the 'ya' suffix is applied –

“Ye”ti vattate.

'Ye' is carried forward.

481. Ha vipariyayo lo vā.

481. The reversal of 'h' to 'l' occurs optionally.

Hakārassa vipariyayo hoti yappaccaye pare, yappaccayassa ca lakāro hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, tena “gayhatī”tiādīsu lattaṃ na hoti, nimittabhūtassa yakārassevetaṃ lattaṃ, “vacavasa”iccādinā uttaṃ. Vuyhati, vulhati, vuyhanti. Vahatu, vuyhatu. Vaheyya, vuyheyya. Avahī, avuyhittha, avahittha. Avahissati, vuyhissati. Avahissa, avuyhissa iccādi.

The reversal of the letter 'h' occurs when the 'ya' suffix follows, and the 'ya' suffix optionally becomes the letter 'l'. This word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option. Therefore, in forms like 'gayhati' and so on, the change to 'l' does not occur; this change to 'l' applies to the very 'y' which is the cause. The vocalization is by the rule 'vacavasa', etc. 'Vuyhati,' 'vulhati,' 'vuyhanti.' 'Vahatu,' 'vuyhatu.' 'Vaheyya,' 'vuyheyya.' 'Avahī,' 'avuyhittha,' 'avahittha.' 'Avahissati,' 'vuyhissati.' 'Avahissa,' 'avuyhissa,' and so on.

Jara vayohānimhi.

The root 'jar' is in the sense of loss of age.

482. Jaramarānaṃ jīrajīyyamīyyā vā.

482. For 'jar' and 'mar', 'jīra', 'jīyya', and 'mīyya' are the substitutes, optionally.

Jaramara iccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ jīrajīyyamīyyādesā honti vā, saralopādi. Jīrati, jīranti. Jīyyati, jīyyanti. “Kvacā”disuttena ekayakārassa kvaci lopo hoti. Jīyati, jīyanti.

For these roots 'jar' and 'mar', the substitutes 'jīra', 'jīyya', and 'mīyya' occur optionally, along with elision of vowels, etc. 'Jīrati,' 'jīranti.' 'Jīyyati,' 'jīyyanti.' By the rule beginning with 'kvacā', the elision of one 'y' sometimes occurs. 'Jīyati,' 'jīyanti.'

Kamme jīrīyati, jīrīyanti. Jīyiyyati, jīyiyyanti. Jīratu, jīyyatu. Jīreyya, jīyyeyya. Ajīrī, jīrī, jīyyī. Jīrissati, jīyyissati. Ajīrissa, ajīyyissa.

In the passive: 'Jīrīyati,' 'jīrīyanti.' 'Jīyiyyati,' 'jīyiyyanti.' 'Jīratu,' 'jīyyatu.' 'Jīreyya,' 'jīyyeyya.' 'Ajīrī,' 'jīrī,' 'jīyyī.' 'Jīrissati,' 'jīyyissati.' 'Ajīrissa,' 'ajīyyissa.'

Mara pāṇacāge, mīyyādeso, mīyyati, mīyyanti. Mīyati, mīyanti vā. Marati, maranti iccādi.

The root 'mar' is in the sense of abandoning life; the substitute is 'mīyya'. 'Mīyyati,' 'mīyyanti.' Or, 'mīyati,' 'mīyanti.' 'Marati,' 'maranti,' and so on.

Disa pekkhaṇe.

The root 'dis' is in the sense of seeing.

483. Disassa [M 0.0290] passa dissa dakkhā vā.

483. For 'dis', the substitutes are 'passa', 'dissa', and 'dakkha', optionally.

Disaiccetassa dhātussa passa dissa dakkhaiccete ādesā honti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, tena dissādeso kammani sabbadhātuke eva. Passati, passanti. Dakkhati, dakkhanti.

For this root 'dis', the substitutes 'passa', 'dissa', and 'dakkha' occur optionally. This word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option. Therefore, the 'dissa' substitute occurs only in the passive voice with sabbadhātuka endings. 'Passati,' 'passanti.' 'Dakkhati,' 'dakkhanti.'

Kammani yakāralopo, dissate, dissante. Dissati, dissanti. Vipassīyati, dakkhīyati. Passatu, dakkhatu, dissatu. Passeyya, dakkheyya, disseyya.

In the passive, there is elision of the letter 'y': 'dissate,' 'dissante.' 'Dissati,' 'dissanti.' 'Vipassīyati,' 'dakkhīyati.' 'Passatu,' 'dakkhatu,' 'dissatu.' 'Passeyya,' 'dakkheyya,' 'disseyya.'

Hiyyattaniyaṃ “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātuikārassa attaṃ, addasā, addasa. Kammani adissa.

In the aorist tense, by the rule beginning with 'kvaci dhātū', the 'i' of the root becomes 'a': 'addasā,' 'addasa.' In the passive: 'adissa.'

Tathā apassi, passi, apassiṃsu, passiṃsu. Apassi, passi, apassittha, passittha. Apassiṃ, passiṃ, apassimha, passimha. Addasi, dasi, addasaṃsu, dasaṃsu. Kammani adissaṃsu. Addakkhi, addakkhiṃsu.

Similarly: 'apassi,' 'passi,' 'apassiṃsu,' 'passiṃsu.' 'Apassi,' 'passi,' 'apassittha,' 'passittha.' 'Apassiṃ,' 'passiṃ,' 'apassimha,' 'passimha.' 'Addasi,' 'dasi,' 'addasaṃsu,' 'dasaṃsu.' In the passive: 'adissaṃsu.' 'Addakkhi,' 'addakkhiṃsu.'

Passissati, passissanti. “Bhavissantimhi ssassa cā”ti yogavibhāgena ssassa lopo, ikārāgamo ca, dakkhiti, dakkhinti. Lopābhāve dakkhissati, dakkhissanti. Apassissa, adakkhissa iccādi.

'Passissati,' 'passissanti.' By splitting the rule 'bhavissantimhi ssassa cā', there is elision of 'ss' and the insertion of 'i': 'dakkhiti,' 'dakkhinti.' In the absence of elision: 'dakkhissati,' 'dakkhissanti.' 'Apassissa,' 'adakkhissa,' and so on.

Sada visaraṇagatyāvasānesu.

The root 'sad' is in the senses of scattering, going, and ending.

“Sabbatthā”ti vattate, maṇḍūkagatiyā “kvacī”ti ca.

'Sabbatthā' (everywhere) is carried forward, and 'kvacī' (sometimes) by frog-leap progression.

484. Sadassa sīdattaṃ.

484. 'Sad' becomes 'sīd'.

Sadaiccetassa dhātussa sīdādeso hoti sabbattha vibhattippaccayesu kvaci. Sesaṃ neyyaṃ. Nisīdati, nisīdanti. Bhāve nisajjate, idha kvacādhikārena sīdā-deso [M 0.0291] na bhavati. Nisīdatu. Nisīde. Nisīdi. Nisīdissati. Nisīdissa iccādi.

For this root 'sad', the substitute 'sīd' occurs sometimes in all inflections and suffixes. The rest should be inferred. 'Nisīdati,' 'nisīdanti.' In the impersonal, 'nisajjate'; here, by the governing rule 'kvaci', the 'sīd' substitute does not occur. 'Nisīdatu.' 'Nisīde.' 'Nisīdi.' 'Nisīdissati.' 'Nisīdissa,' and so on.

Yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadānesu. Yajati, yajanti.

The root 'yaj' is in the senses of worshipping deities, associating, and giving. 'Yajati,' 'yajanti.'

Kammani “yamhī”ti vattate.

In the passive voice, 'yamhī' is carried forward.

485. Yajassādissi.

485. For 'yaj', the initial part becomes 'i'.

Yajaiccetassa dhātussa ādissa yakārassa ikārādeso hoti yappaccaye pare, saralopo. Ijjate mayā buddho. Tathā yajatu, ijjataṃ. Yaje, ijjetha. Yaji, ijjittha. Yajissati, ijjissate. Yajissa, ijjissatha iccādi.

For this root 'yaj', the substitution of 'i' for the initial letter 'y' occurs when the 'ya' suffix follows, along with elision of the vowel. 'Ijjate mayā buddho' (The Buddha is worshipped by me). Similarly: 'yajatu,' 'ijjataṃ.' 'Yaje,' 'ijjetha.' 'Yaji,' 'ijjittha.' 'Yajissati,' 'ijjissate.' 'Yajissa,' 'ijjissatha,' and so on.

Vada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, tyādyuppatti, appaccayo ca.

The root vad is in the sense of distinct speech. The verbal endings beginning with ti and the a suffix arise.

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' (optionally) is understood.

486. Vadassa vajjaṃ.

486. For 'vad', 'vajja' (is substituted).

Vadaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa vajjādeso hoti vā sabbāsu vibhattīsu. Vibhatyādhikārattā cettha sabbāsūti atthato siddhaṃ.

For the entire root 'vad', the substitute 'vajja' occurs optionally in all inflections. Here, because of the section on inflections, 'in all' is understood in meaning.

“Vā”ti vattate.

'Vā' (optionally) is understood.

487. Lopañcettamakāro.

487. And elision of this 'a' (suffix).

Bhūvādito paro appaccayo ettamāpajjate, lopañca vā. Vikaraṇakāriyavidhippakaraṇato cettha akāroti appaccayo gayhati.

After roots of the bhūvādi class, the a suffix becomes e, and optionally undergoes elision. Here, from the section on the rules for the operations of conjugational signs, by 'the letter a', the a suffix is understood.

Bhūvādito juhotyādi-to ca appaccayo paro;

Lopamāpajjate nāñño, vavatthitavibhāsatoti.

After roots of the bhūvādi class and the juhotyādi class, the a suffix follows; it undergoes elision, and nothing else, because it is a fixed optionality.

Appaccayassa ekāro, saralopādi, vajjeti, vadeti, vadati, antimhi –

The a suffix becomes e, along with elision of vowels, etc.: vajjeti, vadeti, vadati. In the case of the ending anti–

488. Kvaci [M 0.0292] dhātuvibhattippaccayānaṃ dīghaviparītādesalopāgamā ca.

488. Sometimes there are lengthening, reversal, substitution, elision, and augmentation of roots, inflections, and suffixes.

Idha dhātvādhikāre ākhyāte, kitake ca avihitalakkhaṇesu payogesu kvaci dhātūnaṃ, tyādivibhattīnaṃ, dhātuvihitappaccayānañca dīghatabbiparītaādesalopāgamaiccetāni kāriyāni jinavacanānurūpato bhavanti. Tattha –
