Here, in the section on roots, in finite verbs, and in primary derivatives, in usages where the characteristics are not prescribed, sometimes for roots, inflections beginning with ti, and suffixes prescribed for roots, these operations of lengthening, its opposite, substitution, elision, and augmentation occur in accordance with the words of the Conqueror. In this regard–

Nāmhi rasso kiyādīnaṃ, saṃyoge caññadhātunaṃ;

Āyūnaṃ vā vibhattīnaṃ, mhā, ssāntassa ca rassatā.

There is shortening of roots of the kiyādi class before nāmhi, and of other roots before a conjunct consonant; and optional shortening of āyu, of the inflection mhā, and of that which ends in ssa.

Gamito cchassa ñcho vāssa, gamissajjatanimhi gā;

Ucāgamo vā tthamhesu, dhātūnaṃ yamhi dīghatā.

After gam, cch optionally becomes ñch or ss; in the aorist, gam becomes gā; there is an optional augment u before ttha and mhe; and lengthening of roots before ya.

Eyyeyyāseyyāmettañca, vā ssessettañca pāpuṇe;

Okārā attamittañca, ātthā papponti vā tthathe.

And eyya, eyyāsi, and eyyāmi become e; and ssa optionally becomes e; and o becomes atta or itta; and for ttha and the, ātthā is optionally obtained.

Tathā brūtoti antīnaṃ, au vāha ca dhātuyā;

Parokkhāya vibhattimhi, anabbhāsassa dīghatā.

Similarly, for the ending anti, there is ū; and for the root, there is au or āha; in the perfect tense inflection, there is lengthening of the non-reduplicated syllable.

Saṃyoganto akārettha, vibhattippaccayādi tu;

Lopa māpajjate nicca-mekārokārato paroti.

Here, for a root ending in a conjunct consonant, there is the letter a; but the initial vowel of an inflection, suffix, etc., is always elided when following e or o.

Ekārato parassa antiakārassa lopo, vajjenti, vadenti, vadanti. Vajjesi, vadesi, vadasi, vajjetha, vadetha, vadatha. Vajjemi, vajjāmi, vademi, vadāmi, vajjema, vadema, vajjāma, vadāma.

Elision of the 'a' of 'anti' occurs after 'e': 'vajjenti,' 'vadenti,' 'vadanti.' 'Vajjesi,' 'vadesi,' 'vadasi,' 'vajjetha,' 'vadetha,' 'vadatha.' 'Vajjemi,' 'vajjāmi,' 'vademi,' 'vadāmi,' 'vajjema,' 'vadema,' 'vajjāma,' 'vadāma.'

Kammani vajjīyati, vajjīyanti. Vajjati, vajjanti. Vadīyati vā. Vajjetu, vadetu, vadatu. Vajje, vajjeyya, vade, vadeyya, vajjeyyuṃ, vadeyyuṃ. Vajjeyyāsi, vajjesi, vadeyyāsi. Avadi, vadi, vadiṃsu. Vadissati, vadissanti. Avadissa iccādi.

In the passive: vajjīyati, vajjīyanti. (Active:) vajjati, vajjanti. Or optionally, vadīyati. (Imperative:) vajjetu, vadetu, vadatu. (Optative:) vajje, vajjeyya, vade, vadeyya, vajjeyyuṃ, vadeyyuṃ. Vajjeyyāsi, vajjesi, vadeyyāsi. (Aorist:) Avadi, vadi, vadiṃsu. (Future:) Vadissati, vadissanti. (Conditional:) Avadissa, etc.

Kamu [M 0.0293] padavikkhepe, appaccaye kate “kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo”ti dvittaṃ, kavaggassa cavaggo.

The root 'kam' is in the sense of stepping. When the 'a' suffix is applied, by the rule 'sometimes there is doubling of the initial consonant of single-syllable roots,' doubling occurs; the k-group becomes the c-group.

Abbhāsaggahaṇamantaggahaṇaṃ, vāggahaṇañca vattate.

The term 'reduplication', the term 'final', and the term 'vā' are carried forward.

489. Niggahītañca.

489. And the niggahīta.

Abbhāsante niggahītañcāgamo hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, tena kamādīnamevetaṃ. Caṅkamati, caṅkamanti iccādi. Kamati, kamanti iccādi.

The niggahīta augment occurs optionally at the end of the reduplicated syllable. This word 'vā' indicates a fixed optionality; therefore, this applies only to 'kam' and so on. 'Caṅkamati,' 'caṅkamanti,' and so on. 'Kamati,' 'kamanti,' and so on.

Cala kampane, cañcalati, calati.

The root 'cal' is in the sense of shaking. 'Cañcalati,' 'calati.'

Cala dalane, daddallati.

The root 'cal' is in the sense of splitting. 'Daddallati.'

Jhecintāyaṃ, appaccaye “o, sare, e”ti ca adhikicca “te āvāyā”ti yogavibhāgena akāritepi ekārassa āyādeso, jhāyati, jhāyanti iccādi, visesavidhānaṃ.

The root 'jhe' is in the sense of thinking. When the 'a' suffix is applied, by taking into account the rule 'o, sare, e' and by splitting the rule 'te āvāyā', the substitute 'āya' for the letter 'e' occurs even when not in the causative: 'jhāyati,' 'jhāyanti,' and so on. This is a special rule.

Avuddhikabhūvādinayo.

The method of the bhūvādi class without augmentation.

Tuda byathane, tyādyuppatti appaccayo, “aññesu cā”ti etthānuvattita vāggahaṇena tudādīnaṃ vuddhiabhāvova viseso, tudati, tudanti. Tudasi, tudatha. Tudāmi, tudāma.

The root 'tud' is in the sense of piercing. The verbal endings beginning with ti and the a suffix arise. Here, by the term 'vā' (optionally) which is carried forward from 'aññesu ca' (and in others), the absence of augmentation for the 'tudādi' roots is the special feature. 'Tudati,' 'tudanti.' 'Tudasi,' 'tudatha.' 'Tudāmi,' 'tudāma.'

Kamme “tassa cavagga”iccādinā sadakārassa yappaccayassa jakāro dvittaṃ, tujjate, tujjante. Tujjati, tujjanti, tujjare vā. Tathā tudatu, tudantu. Tude, tudeyya, tudeyyuṃ. Atudi, tudiṃsu. Atudi, atudittha. Atudiṃ, atudimha. Atujjittha, atujji. Tudissati. Atudissa iccādi.

In the passive, by the rule 'tassa cavagga', etc., the cluster of the preceding d and the ya suffix becomes a doubled j: tujjate, tujjante. Tujjati, tujjanti, or optionally tujjare. Similarly: tudatu, tudantu. Tude, tudeyya, tudeyyuṃ. Atudi, tudiṃsu. Atudi, atudittha. Atudiṃ, atudimha. Atujjittha, atujji. Tudissati. Atudissa, etc.

Visa pavesane papubbo, so gāmaṃ pavisati, pavisanti. Pavisasi, pavisatha. Pavisāmi, pavisāma.

The root 'vis' is in the sense of entering, with the prefix 'pa'. 'So gāmaṃ pavisati' (He enters the village), 'pavisanti.' 'Pavisasi,' 'pavisatha.' 'Pavisāmi,' 'pavisāma.'

Kamme [M 0.0294] pavisiyyate, pavisiyyante. Pavisiyyati, pavisiyyanti. Pavissate vā. Tathā pavisatu, pavisantu. Paviseyya. Pāvisi, pavisi, pāvekkhi pathaviṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ajjatanimhi visassa vekkhādeso ca. Pāvisiṃsu, pavisiṃsu.

In the passive voice: 'Pavisiyyate,' 'pavisiyyante.' 'Pavisiyyati,' 'pavisiyyanti.' 'Pavissate' optionally. Similarly, 'pavisatu,' 'pavisantu.' 'Paviseyya.' 'Pāvisi,' 'pavisi,' 'pāvekkhi pathaviṃ' (he penetrated the earth); and by the rule 'kvaci dhātū…' etc., the substitute 'vekkha' for 'vis' occurs in the aorist. 'Pāvisiṃsu,' 'pavisiṃsu.'

Kamme pāvisīyittha, pavisīyittha, pāvisīyi, pavisīyi. Pavisissati, pavisissanti. Pavisīyissate, pavisissate. Pāvisissa. Pāvisīyissa iccādi.

In the passive voice: pāvisīyittha, pavisīyittha, pāvisīyi, pavisīyi. Pavisissati, pavisissanti. Pavisīyissate, pavisissate. Pāvisissa. Pāvisīyissa, and so on.

Nuda khepe, nudati, nudanti.

The root nud in the sense of dispelling: nudati, nudanti.

Disa atisajjane, uddisati, uddisanti.

The root dis in the sense of indicating: uddisati, uddisanti.

Likha lekhane, likhati, likhanti.

The root likh in the sense of writing: likhati, likhanti.

Phusa samphasse, phusati, phusanti iccādi.

The root phus in the sense of touching: phusati, phusanti, and so on.

Tudādinayo.

The Tudādi class.

Hū, bhū sattāyaṃ, tyādyuppatti “bhūvādito a”iti appaccayo, “vā”ti adhikicca “lopañcettamakāro”ti bhūvādito parassa appaccayassa lopo, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi. So hoti, te honti, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā parasarassa lopo. Hosi, hotha. Homi, homa. Bhāve hūyate.

The roots hū and bhū are in the sense of existence. The verbal endings beginning with ti arise. The suffix a is applied by the rule 'bhūvādito a'. Governed by 'vā', and by the rule 'lopañcettamakāro', there is elision of the suffix a after a root of the bhūvādi group; and by 'aññesu ca', there is vṛddhi. He is (hoti), they are (honti). By 'kvaci dhātu...' and so on, there is elision of the following vowel. You are (hosi), you are (hotha). I am (homi), we are (homa). In the impersonal voice: hūyate.

Tathā hotu, hontu. Hohi, anakāraparattā hilopo na bhavati, hotha. Homi, homa. Bhāve hūyataṃ.

Similarly: let him be (hotu), let them be (hontu). Be (hohi); the elision of hi does not occur because it is not followed by the letter a. Be (hotha). Let me be (homi), let us be (homa). In the impersonal voice: let it be (hūyataṃ).

Sattamiyaṃ saralopādi, heyya, heyyuṃ. Heyyāsi, heyyātha. Heyyāmi, heyyāma. Heyyaṃ vā. Bhāve hūyetha.

In the optative, with elision of vowels and so on: may he be, may they be. May you be, may you all be. May I be, may we be. Or heyyaṃ. In the impersonal voice, may it be.

Hiyyattaniyaṃ [M 0.0295] appaccayalope “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā hūdhātussa ūkārassa uvādeso. Ahuvā, ahuvu, ahuvū. Ahuva, ahuvo, ahuvattha. Ahuvaṃ, ahuvamha. Ahuvattha, ahuvatthuṃ. Ahuvase, ahuvavhaṃ. Ahuviṃ, ahuvamhase. Bhāve ahūyattha.

In the Hiyyattanī, with the elision of the a-suffix, by 'kvaci dhātu...' and so on, the ū of the root hū undergoes the substitution uva. He was (ahuvā), they were (ahuvu, ahuvū). You were (ahuva, ahuvo), you all were (ahuvattha). I was (ahuvaṃ), we were (ahuvamha). In the middle voice: he was (ahuvattha), they were (ahuvatthuṃ). You were (ahuvase), you all were (ahuvavhaṃ). I was (ahuviṃ), we were (ahuvamhase). In the impersonal voice, it was (ahūyattha).

Ajjatanimhi “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā hūto īvibhattissa lopo rassattaṃ, so ahu, lopābhāve “karassa kāsattamajjatanimhī”ti ettha “sattamajjatanimhī”ti yogavibhāgena sāgamo, vuddhi, ahosi, ahesuṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā okārassekāro. Ahavuṃ vā. Ahosi, ahosittha. Ahosiṃ, ahuṃ, parasarassa lopo, rassattañca, ahosimha, ahumha, rassattaṃ. Bhāve ahūyittha.

In the aorist, by 'kvaci dhātu...' and so on, after hū, the ending ī is elided and shortened, resulting in: he was (ahu). In the absence of elision, by splitting the rule 'karassa kāsattamajjatanimhī' into 'sattamajjatanimhī', the augment sa occurs, and there is vṛddhi, resulting in: ahosi, ahesuṃ. By 'kvaci dhātu...' and so on, o becomes e. Or ahavuṃ. The forms are: ahosi, ahosittha. Ahosiṃ, ahuṃ (with elision of the following vowel and shortening); ahosimha, ahumha (with shortening). In the impersonal voice: ahūyittha.

“Hi lopaṃ vā”ti ito “lopo, vā”ti ca vattate.

From the rule 'hi lopaṃ vā', the terms 'lopo' and 'vā' are carried over.

490. Hotissare’hohe bhavissantimhi ssassa ca.

490. In the future tense, the vowel of the root hū becomes eha or oha, and the ss is also elided.

Hūiccetassa dhātussa saro eha oha ettamāpajjate bhavissantimhi vibhattimhi, ssassa ca lopo hoti vā. Ikārāgamo, saralopādi.

Of this root hū, the vowel becomes eha or oha when a future tense ending follows; and the ss is optionally elided. There is the augment i, elision of vowels, and so on.

Hehiti, hehinti. Hehisi, hehitha. Hehāmi, hehāma. Lopābhāve – hehissati, hehissanti. Hehissasi, hehissatha. Hehissāmi, hehissāma. Ohādese – hohiti, hohinti. Hohisi, hohitha. Hohāmi, hohāma. Tathā hohissati, hohissanti. Hohissasi, hohissatha. Hohissāmi, hohissāma. Ekārādese – heti, henti. Hesi, hetha. Hemi[M 0.0296], hema. Hessati, hessanti. Hessasi, hessatha. Hessāmi, hessāma. Bhāve hūyissate.

He will be, they will be. You will be, you all will be. I will be, we will be. In the absence of elision of ss: hehissati, hehissanti. Hehissasi, hehissatha. Hehissāmi, hehissāma. With the substitution of oha: hohiti, hohinti. Hohisi, hohitha. Hohāmi, hohāma. Similarly, with ss: hohissati, hohissanti. Hohissasi, hohissatha. Hohissāmi, hohissāma. With the substitution of e: he will be, they will be. You will be, you all will be. I will be, we will be. Also with ss: hessati, hessanti. Hessasi, hessatha. Hessāmi, hessāma. In the impersonal voice, it will be.

Kālātipattiyaṃ ahavissa, ahavissaṃsu. Ahuyissatha iccādi.

In the conditional: he would have been, they would have been. You all would have been, and so on.

Hū, bhū sattāyaṃ, bhū itīdha anupubbo, tyādyuppatti appaccayassa lopavuddhiyo, anubhoti, anubhonti. Anubhosi, anubhotha. Anubhomi, anubhoma.

The roots hū and bhū are in the sense of existence. Here, bhū is preceded by the prefix anu. The verbal endings beginning with ti arise, with elision and vṛddhi of the a-suffix. He experiences (anubhoti), they experience (anubhonti). You experience (anubosi), you all experience (anubhotha). I experience (anubhomi), we experience (anubhoma).

Kamme anubhūyati, anubhūyanti. Tathā anubhotu, anubhontu. Anubhohi, anubhotha. Anubhomi, anubhoma. Anubhūyatu, anubhūyantu. Anubhave, anubhaveyya. Anubhūyeyya. Anubhosi, anubhavi. Anubhossati, anubhossanti. Anubhossasi, anubhossatha. Anubhossāmi, anubhossāma. Anubhavissati vā. Anubhossa, anubhavissa vā iccādi.

In the passive, it is experienced, they are experienced. Similarly, let him experience, let them experience. Experience, you all experience. Let me experience, let us experience. Let it be experienced, let them be experienced. He should experience, he might experience. It might be experienced. You experienced, he experienced. He will experience, they will experience. You will experience, you all will experience. I will experience, we will experience. Or anubhavissati. He would experience, or anubhavissa, and so on.

Sī saye appaccayalopo, vuddhi ca, seti, senti. Sesi, setha. Semi, sema. Sete, sente iccādi.

The root sī is in the sense of lying down. There is elision of the a-suffix and vṛddhi. He lies down, they lie down. You lie down, you all lie down. I lie down, we lie down. In the middle voice: he lies down, they lie down, and so on.

Appaccayalopābhāve –

In the absence of the elision of the a-suffix:

“Sare”ti vattate, dhātuggahaṇañca.

The term 'sare' is carried over, and also the term for the root.

491. E aya.

491. E becomes aya.

Ekārassa dhātvantassa sare pare ayādeso hoti, saralopādi. Sayati, sayanti. Sayasi, sayatha. Sayāmi, sayāma.

For an e at the end of a root, when a vowel follows, the substitution aya occurs, with elision of vowels and so on. He lies down, they lie down. You lie down, you all lie down. I lie down, we lie down.

Kamme [M 0.0297] atipubbo, “kvaci dhātvā”dinā yamhi rassasarassa dhātvantassa dīgho, atisīyate, atisīyante. Atisīyati, atisīyanti. Bhāve sīyate.

In the passive, when prefixed with ati, by 'kvaci dhātu...' and so on, when ya follows, a short vowel at the end of a root is lengthened: it is lain upon excessively, they are lain upon excessively. Atisīyati, atisīyanti. In the impersonal voice, it is lain upon.

Tathā setu, sentu. Sehi, setha. Semi, sema. Sayatu, sayantu. Saya, sayāhi, sayatha. Sayāmi, sayāma. Sayataṃ, sayantaṃ. Sayassu, sayavho. Saye, sayāmase. Atisīyataṃ, atisīyantaṃ. Atisīyatu, atisīyantu. Bhāve sīyataṃ.

Similarly, let him lie down, let them lie down. Lie down, you all lie down. Let me lie down, let us lie down. With the aya substitution: let him lie down, let them lie down. Lie down, lie down, you all lie down. Let me lie down, let us lie down. In the middle voice imperative: let him lie down, let them lie down. Lie down, you all lie down. Let me lie down, let us lie down. In the passive imperative with the prefix ati: let it be lain upon excessively, let them be lain upon excessively. Atisīyatu, atisīyantu. In the impersonal voice, let it be lain upon.

Saye, sayeyya, sayeyyuṃ. Atisīyeyya. Bhāve sīyetha.

May I lie down (saye), may he lie down (sayeyya), may they lie down (sayeyyuṃ). May it be excessively lain upon (atisīyeyya). In the impersonal voice, may it be lain upon (sīyetha).

Asayi, sayi, asayiṃsu, sayiṃsu, asayuṃ. Sāgame atisesi, atisesuṃ. Kamme accasīyittha, accasīyi, atisīyi. Bhāve sīyittha.

He lay down, he lay down, they lay down, they lay down, they lay down. With the augment sa: he excessively lay down, they excessively lay down. In the passive, it was excessively lain upon, it was excessively lain upon, it was excessively lain upon. In the impersonal voice, it was lain upon.

Sayissati, sayissanti. Ikārāgamābhāve sessati, sessanti. Kamme atisīyissatha, atisīyissati. Bhāve sīyissate.

He will lie down, they will lie down. In the absence of the i-augment: he will lie down, they will lie down. In the passive, you all will be excessively lain upon, it will be excessively lain upon. In the impersonal voice, it will be lain upon.

Asayissā, asayissaṃsu. Kamme accasīyissatha iccādi.

He would have lain down, they would have lain down. In the passive, you all would have been excessively lain upon, and so on.

Nī pāpuṇane, dvikammakoyaṃ, ajaṃ gāmaṃ neti, nenti. Nesi, netha. Nemi, nema. Lopābhāve nayati, nayanti iccādi. Kamme nīyate gāmaṃ ajo devadattena, nīyare, nīyante. Nīyati, nīyanti.

The root nī is in the sense of reaching or attaining; this is a ditransitive verb. He leads the goat to the village, they lead. You lead, you all lead. I lead, we lead. In the absence of elision: he leads, they lead, and so on. In the passive: the goat is led to the village by Devadatta; they are led, they are led. He is led, they are led.

Tathā netu, nayatu. Nīyataṃ, nīyantaṃ. Naye, nayeyya. Nīyetha, nīyeyya. Anayi, nayi, anayiṃsu, nayiṃsu. Vinesi, vinesuṃ. Anīyittha, nīyittha. Nayissati[M 0.0298], nessati. Nayissate, nīyissate, nīyissati. Anayissa, anīyissa iccādi.

Similarly, let him lead, let him lead. Let it be led, let them be led. He should lead, he might lead. It should be led, it might be led. He led, he led, they led, they led. He removed, they removed. It was led, it was led. He will lead, he will lead. It will be led, it will be led, it will be led. He would lead, it would be led, and so on.

Ṭhā gatinivattimhi, “vā”ti vattate.

The root `ṭhā` is in the sense of stopping movement; the term `vā` is carried over.

492. Ṭhā tiṭṭho.

492. `ṭhā` becomes `tiṭṭha`.

Ṭhāiccetassa dhātussa tiṭṭhādeso hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, appaccayalopo. Tiṭṭhati, tiṭṭhanti. Ṭhāti, ṭhanti. Lopābhāve “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ṭhāto hakārāgamo ca rassattaṃ, saṃpubbo saṇṭhahati, saṇṭhahanti. Ette adhiṭṭheti, adhiṭṭhenti.

For this root `ṭhā`, the substitution `tiṭṭha` occurs optionally. This word `vā` indicates a restricted option, and there is elision of the `a` suffix. He stands, they stand. He stands, they stand. In the absence of elision, by the rule beginning `kvaci dhātu`, for `ṭhā`, the augment `h` occurs and the vowel is shortened; when prefixed with `saṃ`: he remains fixed, they remain fixed. In this context: he determines, they determine.

Kamme –

In the passive voice:

493. Yamhi dādhā mā ṭhā hā pā maha mathādīnamī.

493. When `ya` follows, for the roots `dā`, `dhā`, `mā`, `ṭhā`, `hā`, `pā`, `maha`, `matha`, and so on, there is `ī`.

Bhāvakammavisaye yamhi paccaye pare dā dhā mā ṭhā hāpā maha matha iccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto īkāramāpajjate, niccatthoyamārambho. Upaṭṭhīyati, upaṭṭhīyanti. Hakārāgame rassattaṃ, īkārāgamo ca, patiṭṭhahīyati, patiṭṭhahīyanti. Bhāve ṭhīyate.

In the domain of the impersonal and passive voices, when the suffix `ya` follows, the final vowel of roots such as `dā`, `dhā`, `mā`, `ṭhā`, `hā`, `pā`, `maha`, `matha`, and so on, becomes `ī`; this rule is stated to show it is obligatory. It is served, they are served. With the augment `h`, shortening of the vowel, and the vowel `ī`: it is established, they are established. In the impersonal voice: it is stood.

Tathā tiṭṭhatu, tiṭṭhantu. Ṭhātu, ṭhantu. Saṇṭhahatu, saṇṭhahantu. Tiṭṭhe, tiṭṭheyya. Saṇṭhe, saṇṭheyya, saṇṭheyyuṃ. Saṇṭhahe, saṇṭhaheyyuṃ. Aṭṭhāsi, aṭṭhaṃsu. Saṇṭhahi, saṇṭhahiṃsu. Pakiṭṭhissati, patiṭṭhissanti. Ṭhassati, ṭhassanti. Patiṭṭhahissati, patiṭṭhahissanti. Patiṭṭhissa, patiṭṭhissaṃsu. Patiṭṭhahissa, patiṭṭhahissaṃsu iccādi.

Similarly: let him stand, let them stand. Let him stand, let them stand. Let him remain fixed, let them remain fixed. He should stand, he might stand. He should remain fixed, he might remain fixed, they might remain fixed. He should remain fixed, they might remain fixed. He stood, they stood. He remained fixed, they remained fixed. He will stand firm, they will stand firm. He will stand, they will stand. He will stand firm, they will stand firm. He would stand firm, they would stand firm. He would stand firm, they would stand firm, and so on.

Pā pāne, “vā”ti vattate.

The root `pā` is in the sense of drinking; the term `vā` is carried over.

494. Pā [M 0.0299] pibo.

494. `pā` becomes `piba`.

Pāiccetassa dhātussa pibādeso hoti vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

For this root `pā`, the substitution `piba` occurs optionally. This word `vā` indicates a restricted option.

Pibati. Pibatu. Pibeyya. “Kvaci dhātvā”dinā bakārassa vakāro, pivati, pivanti. Pāti, pānti, panti vā. Pīyate, pīyante. Pīyati, pīyanti. Pivatu. Piveyya. Apāyi, pivi. Pivissati. Apivissa iccādi.

He drinks. Let him drink. He should drink. By the rule beginning `kvaci dhātu`, `b` becomes `v`: he drinks, they drink. He drinks, they drink, or they drink. It is drunk, they are drunk. It is drunk, they are drunk. Let him drink. He should drink. He drank, he drank. He will drink. He would drink, and so on.

Asa bhuvi, vibhattuppatti, appaccayalopo, asa itīdha –

The root `asa` is in the sense of being. With the arising of the verbal ending and the elision of the `a` suffix, here `asa` is discussed:

“Asasmā, antalopo”ti ca vattate.

And the rule `Asasmā, antalopo` is carried over.

495. Tissa tthittaṃ.

495. For `ti`, there is `tthi`.

Asaiccetasmā dhātumhā parassa tissa vibhattissa tthittaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Atthi.

After this root `asa`, for the following `ti` ending, the substitution `tthi` occurs, and there is elision of the final vowel of the root. Thus: `atthi`.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The term `vā` is carried over.

496. Sabbatthāsassādi lopo ca.

496. And everywhere, there is elision of the initial vowel of `asa`.

Sabbattha vibhattippaccayesu ca asaiccetāya dhātuyā ādissa lopo hoti vā, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Santi.

In all endings and suffixes, the initial vowel of this root `asa` is optionally elided; this word `vā` indicates a restricted option. Thus: `santi`.

“Asasmā, antalopo”ti ca adhikāro.

And `Asasmā, antalopo` is the governing rule.

497. Simhi ca.

497. And before `si`.

Asadhātussa antalopo hoti simhi vibhattimhi ca. Tvaṃ asi.

For the root `asa`, elision of the final vowel also occurs before the `si` ending. Thus: `tvaṃ asi`.

498. Thassa [M 0.0300] tthattaṃ.

498. For `tha`, there is `ttha`.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā parassa thassa vibhattissa tthattaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Tumhe attha.

After this root `asa`, for the following `tha` ending, the substitution `ttha` occurs, and there is elision of the final vowel of the root. Thus: `tumhe attha`.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The term `vā` is carried over.

499. Asasmā mimānaṃ mhimhāntalopo ca.

499. After `asa`, for `mi` and `ma`, there are `mhi` and `mha`, and elision of the final vowel.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā parāsaṃ mi maiccetāsaṃ vibhattīnaṃ mhimhaiccete ādesā honti vā, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Amhi, amha. Asmi, asma.

After this root `asa`, for the following `mi` and `ma` endings, the substitutions `mhi` and `mha` optionally occur, and there is elision of the final vowel of the root. Thus: `amhi`, `amha`; `asmi`, `asma`.

500. Tussa tthuttaṃ.

500. For `tu`, there is `tthu`.

Asaiccetāya dhātuyā parassa tussa vibhattissa tthuttaṃ hoti, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Atthu. Asassādilopo ca, santu. Āhi, attha. Asmi, asma.

After this root `asa`, for the following `tu` ending, the substitution `tthu` occurs, and there is elision of the final vowel of the root. Thus: `atthu`. And with elision of the initial vowel of `asa`: `santu`. Also: `āhi`, `attha`, `asmi`, `asma`.

Sattamiyaṃ asassādilopo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā asato eyyaeyyuṃ vibhattīnaṃ iyāiyuñca honti. Siyā, siyuṃ.

In the optative, there is elision of the initial vowel of `asa`; by the rule beginning `kvaci dhātu`, for `asa`, the endings `eyya` and `eyyuṃ` become `iyā` and `iyuṃ`. Thus: `siyā`, `siyuṃ`.

Lopābhāve “kvaci dhātvā”dinā asato eyyādīnaṃ sadhātvantānaṃ ssa ssu ssa ssatha ssaṃ ssāmaādesā honti.

In the absence of elision, by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātu', for the endings of the root 'as' beginning with 'eyya', the substitutions 'ssa', 'ssu', 'ssa', 'ssatha', 'ssaṃ', and 'ssāma' occur.

Evamassa vacanīyo, assu. Assa, assatha. Assaṃ, assāma.

Thus it should be stated: assu. Assa, assatha. Assaṃ, assāma.

Ajjataniyaṃ akārāgamo, dīgho ca, āsi, āsiṃsu, āsuṃ. Āsi, āsittha. Āsiṃ, āsimha.

In the aorist tense, the augment 'a' is added, and there is lengthening: āsi, āsiṃsu, āsuṃ. Āsi, āsittha. Āsiṃ, āsimha.

“Vā[M 0.0301], asassā”ti ca vattate.

And the rule 'Vā, asassā' continues.

501. Asabbadhātuke bhū.

501. Before an asabbadhātuka affix, bhū.

Asasseva dhātussa bhūādeso hoti vā asabbadhātuke. Bhavissati, bhavissanti. Abhavissa, abhavissaṃsu.

For the root 'as' alone, the substitute 'bhū' occurs optionally before an asabbadhātuka affix. Bhavissati, bhavissanti. Abhavissa, abhavissaṃsu.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Āsuṃ.

What is the purpose of 'vā'? To allow for the form āsuṃ.

Brū viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, tyādyuppatti, appaccayalopo ca.

The root 'brū' is used in the sense of articulate speech; the endings beginning with 'ti' are applied, and there is elision of the 'a' suffix.

“Kvacī”ti vattate.

The word 'kvaci' is carried forward.

502. Brūto ī timhi.

502. After 'brū', 'ī' [is the augment] before 'ti'.

Brūiccetāya dhātuyā paro īkārāgamo hoti timhi vibhattimhi kvaci, vuddhiavādesā, saralopādi. Bravīti, brūti, “aññesu cā”ti suttānuvattitavāggahaṇena brūdhātussa byañjane vuddhi na hoti, bahuvacane “jhalānamiyuvā sare vā”ti ūkārassa sare uvādeso, bruvanti. “Kvaci dhātvā”dinā brūto tiantīnaṃ vā a u ādesā brūssa āhādeso ca.

After this root 'brū', the augment 'ī' occurs sometimes before the 'ti' inflection, along with vowel strengthening, the 'av' substitution, vowel elision, and so on. For example: Bravīti, brūti. By the continuation of the word 'vā' from the sutta 'aññesu ca', vowel strengthening of the root 'brū' does not occur before a consonant. In the plural, according to the rule 'jhalānamiyuvā sare vā', for 'ū' before a vowel, the substitute is 'uva'; hence, bruvanti. By the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātu', after 'brū', for the endings 'ti' and 'anti', the substitutes are optionally 'a' and 'u' respectively, and for 'brū' the substitute is 'āha'.

Āha, āhu. Brūsi, brūtha. Brūmi, brūma. Brūte, bruvante. Brūse, bruvavhe. Bruve, brūmhe. Brūtu, bruvantu. Brūhi, brūtha. Brūmi, brūma. Brūtaṃ, bruvantaṃ. Bruve, bruveyya, bruveyyuṃ. Bruveyyāsi, bruveyyātha. Bruveyyāmi, bruveyyāma. Bruvetha, bruveraṃ. Abruvā, abruvū.

Āha, āhu. Brūsi, brūtha. Brūmi, brūma. Brūte, bruvante. Brūse, bruvavhe. Bruve, brūmhe. Brūtu, bruvantu. Brūhi, brūtha. Brūmi, brūma. Brūtaṃ, bruvantaṃ. Bruve, bruveyya, bruveyyuṃ. Bruveyyāsi, bruveyyātha. Bruveyyāmi, bruveyyāma. Bruvetha, bruveraṃ. Abruvā, abruvū.

Parokkhāyaṃ [M 0.0302] “brūbhūnamāhabhūvā parokkhāya”nti brūdhātussa āhaādeso, saralopādi, supine kira māha, tenāhu porāṇā, āhaṃsu vā iccādi.

In the perfect tense, according to the rule 'brūbhūnamāhabhūvā parokkhāya', for the root 'brū' the substitute is 'āha', with vowel elision and so on. For example: supine kira māha (reportedly, I spoke in a dream); for this reason the ancients said āhu, or āhaṃsu, and so on.

Ajjataniyaṃ abravi, abruvi, abravuṃ. Bravissati. Abravissa iccādi.

In the aorist tense: abravi, abruvi, abravuṃ. Future: Bravissati. Conditional: Abravissa, etc.

Hana hiṃsāgatīsu, timhi kvaci appaccayalopo, hanti, hanati, hananti. Hanasi, hanatha. Hanāmi, hanāma.

The root 'hana' is used in the senses of harming and going; before 'ti', there is sometimes elision of the 'a' suffix: hanti, hanati, hananti. Hanasi, hanatha. Hanāmi, hanāma.

Kamme “tassa cavagga”iccādinā ñattaṃ, dvittañca, haññate, haññante, haññare. Haññati, haññanti. Hanatu, hanantu. Haneyya.

In the passive, according to the rule beginning 'tassa cavagga', there is substitution by 'ñ' and doubling: haññate, haññante, haññare. Haññati, haññanti. Hanatu, hanantu. Haneyya.

“Hanassā”ti vattate.

The heading 'hanassā' is carried forward.

503. Vadho vā sabbattha.

503. 'Vadha' is the substitute optionally everywhere.

Hanaiccetassa dhātussa vadhādeso hoti vā sabbattha vibhattippaccayesu, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Vadheti. Vadhīyati. Vadhetu. Vadhīyatu. Vadheyya. Avadhi, avadhiṃsu. Ahani, ahaniṃsu. Vadhissati, hanissati. Khādese paṭihaṅkhāmi, paṭihanissāmi. Avadhissa, ahanissa iccādi.

For this root 'hana', the substitute 'vadha' occurs optionally before all inflections and suffixes; this word 'vā' indicates a specific, established option. Vadheti. Vadhīyati. Vadhetu. Vadhīyatu. Vadheyya. Avadhi, avadhiṃsu. Ahani, ahaniṃsu. Vadhissati, hanissati. With the 'kha' suffix: paṭihaṅkhāmi, paṭihanissāmi. Avadhissa, ahanissa, etc.

Hūvādinayo.

The section on the Huvādi group.

Hu dānādanahabyappadānesu, tyādyuppatti, appaccayo ca, “kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo”ti dvittaṃ, “pubbobbhāso”ti abbhāsasaññā.

The root 'hu' is used in the senses of giving, taking, and offering oblations; the endings beginning with 'ti' are applied, along with the 'a' suffix. By the rule 'kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo', there is doubling; by the rule 'pubbobbhāso', it is designated as 'abbhāsa' (reduplication).

“Abbhāse”ti vattate.

The heading 'abbhāse' is carried forward.

504. Hassa [M 0.0303] jo.

504. For 'ha', 'j' is the substitute.

Hakārassa abbhāse vattamānassa jo hoti. “Lopañcetta makāro”ti appaccayalopo, vuddhi. Juhoti.

For the letter 'ha' occurring in the reduplication, 'j' is the substitute. By the rule 'Lopañcetta makāro', there is elision of the 'a' suffix and vowel strengthening. Juhoti.

Lopābhāve “jhalānaṃ, sare”ti ca vattamāne –

In the absence of elision, and while the rules 'jhalānaṃ' and 'sare' are carried forward –

505. Yavakārā ca.

505. And the letters 'ya' and 'va'.

Jhalasaññānaṃ ivaṇṇuvaṇṇānaṃ yakāravakārādesā honti sare pareti apadantassa ukārassa vakāro.

For the vowels 'i' and 'u' which are designated as 'jhala', the substitutions 'ya' and 'va' respectively occur when a vowel follows; thus, for a non-final 'u', 'va' is the substitute.

Juhvati, juhoti, juhvanti, juhonti. Juhvasi, juhosi, juhvatha, juhotha. Juhvāmi, juhomi, juhvāma, juhoma.

Juhvati, juhoti, juhvanti, juhonti. Juhvasi, juhosi, juhvatha, juhotha. Juhvāmi, juhomi, juhvāma, juhoma.

Kamme “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dīgho, hūyate, hūyante. Hūyati, hūyanti.

In the passive, by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātu', there is lengthening: hūyate, hūyante. Hūyati, hūyanti.

Tathā juhotu, juhontu, juhvantu vā. Juhe, juheyya, juheyyuṃ. Ajuhavi, ajuhavuṃ. Ajuhosi, ajuhosuṃ. Ahūyittha aggi. Juhissati, juhissanti. Juhossati, juhossanti vā. Ajuhissa, ajuhissaṃsu iccādi.

Similarly: juhotu, juhontu, or juhvantu. Juhe, juheyya, juheyyuṃ. Ajuhavi, ajuhavuṃ. Ajuhosi, ajuhosuṃ. Ahūyittha aggi (The fire was offered to). Juhissati, juhissanti; or juhossati, juhossanti. Ajuhissa, ajuhissaṃsu, etc.

Hā cāge, pure viya dvebhāvajādesa appaccayalopā.

The root 'hā' is for abandoning; as before, there is doubling, substitution of 'j', and elision of the 'a' suffix.

“Abbhāse”ti vattate.

The word 'abbhāse' continues.

506. Rasso.

506. Shortening.

Abbhāse vattamānassa sarassa rasso hoti.

A vowel present in the reduplication becomes short.

Jahāti, jahanti. Jahāsi, jahātha. Jahāmi, jahāma.

Jahāti, jahanti. Jahāsi, jahātha. Jahāmi, jahāma.

Kamme [M 0.0304] “yamhi dādhāmāṭhāhāpāmahamathādīnamī”ti dhātvantassa īkāro. Hīyate, hīyante, hīyare. Hīyati, hīyanti.

In the passive, according to the rule 'yamhi dādhāmāṭhāhāpāmahamathādīnamī', the final vowel of the root becomes 'ī'. Hīyate, hīyante, hīyare. Hīyati, hīyanti.

Tathā jahātu, jahantu. Jahe, jaheyya, jaheyyuṃ. Hīyetha, hīyeyya. Ajahāsi, ajahiṃsu, ajahāsuṃ. Pajahi, pajahiṃsu, pajahaṃsu, pajahuṃ. Kamme pajahīyittha, pajahīyi. Pajahissati, pajahissanti. Hīyissati, hīyissanti. Pajahissa, pajahissaṃsu iccādi.

Similarly: 'jahātu,' 'jahantu' (Imperative). 'Jahe,' 'jaheyya,' 'jaheyyuṃ' (Optative). 'Hīyetha,' 'hīyeyya' (Passive Optative). 'Ajahāsi,' 'ajahiṃsu,' 'ajahāsuṃ'; 'Pajahi,' 'pajahiṃsu,' 'pajahaṃsu,' 'pajahuṃ' (Aorist). In the passive: 'pajahīyittha,' 'pajahīyi'. 'Pajahissati,' 'pajahissanti' (Future). 'Hīyissati,' 'hīyissanti' (Passive Future). 'Pajahissa,' 'pajahissaṃsu' (Conditional), and so forth.

Dā dāne, tyādyuppatti, dvebhāvarassattāni, appaccayassa lopo, dadāti, dadanti. Dadāsi, dadātha. Dadāmi, dadāma.

The root 'dā' is for giving; there is the arising of 'ti' and so forth, doubling and shortening, and elision of the 'a' suffix: 'dadāti,' 'dadanti.' 'Dadāsi,' 'dadātha.' 'Dadāmi,' 'dadāma.'

Dvittābhāve maṇḍūkagatiyā “vā”ti vattate.

In the absence of doubling, the word 'vā' continues by the frog-leap method.

507. Dādhātussa dajjaṃ.

507. 'Dajja' for the root 'dā'.

Dāiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa dajjādeso hoti vā, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, appaccayalopo. Dajjati, dajjanti. Dajjasi, dajjatha. Dajjāmi, dajjāma. Dajjādesābhāve “lopañcettamakāro”ti appaccayassa ekāro, dānaṃ deti, denti. Desi, detha.

For this root 'dā,' the substitute 'dajja' occurs optionally for the whole root; this word 'vā' is for an established option; there is elision of the 'a' suffix. 'Dajjati,' 'dajjanti.' 'Dajjasi,' 'dajjatha.' 'Dajjāmi,' 'dajjāma.' In the absence of the 'dajja' substitution, according to the rule 'lopañcettamakāro', the 'a' suffix becomes 'e': 'dānaṃ deti,' 'denti.' 'Desi,' 'detha.'

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' continues.

508. Dādantassaṃ mimesu.

508. The end of 'dā' becomes 'aṃ' before 'mi' and 'ma'.

Dāiccetassa dhātussa antassa aṃ hoti vā mimaiccetesu paresu, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ. Dammi, damma. Demi, dema.

For this root 'dā,' its end becomes 'aṃ' optionally when 'mi' or 'ma' follow; the niggahīta becomes the final consonant of its class. 'Dammi,' 'damma.' 'Demi,' 'dema.'

Kamme “yamhi dādhā”iccādinā īkāro, dīyate, dīyante. Dīyati, dīyanti. Dīyyate, dīyyante. Dīyyati, dīyyanti vā iccādi.

In the passive, according to 'yamhi dādhā' and so forth, there is 'ī': 'dīyate,' 'dīyante.' 'Dīyati,' 'dīyanti.' 'Dīyyate,' 'dīyyante.' 'Dīyyati,' 'dīyyanti,' optionally, and so forth.

Dadātu[M 0.0305], dadantu. Dadāhi, dadātha. Dadāmi, dadāma. Dadataṃ, dadantaṃ. Dadassu, dadavho. Dade, dadāmase. Dajjatu, dajjantu iccādi. Detu, dentu. Dehi, detha. Demi, dema. Kamme dīyataṃ, dīyantaṃ. Dīyatu, dīyantu.

Dadātu, dadantu. Dadāhi, dadātha. Dadāmi, dadāma. Dadataṃ, dadantaṃ. Dadassu, dadavho. Dade, dadāmase. Dajjatu, dajjantu, and so forth. Detu, dentu. Dehi, detha. Demi, dema. In the passive: dīyataṃ, dīyantaṃ. Dīyatu, dīyantu.

Sattamiyaṃ dade, dadeyya, dadeyyuṃ. Dadeyyāsi, dadeyyātha. Dadeyyāmi, dadeyyāma. Dadetha, daderaṃ. Dadetho, dadeyyāvho. Dadeyyaṃ, dadeyyāmhe. Dajje, dajjeyya.

In the optative mood: 'dade,' 'dadeyya,' 'dadeyyuṃ.' 'Dadeyyāsi,' 'dadeyyātha.' 'Dadeyyāmi,' 'dadeyyāma.' 'Dadetha,' 'daderaṃ.' 'Dadetho,' 'dadeyyāvho.' 'Dadeyyaṃ,' 'dadeyyāmhe.'

“Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā eyyassāttañca, dajjā, dajjuṃ, dajjeyyuṃ. Dajjeyyāsi, dajjeyyātha. Dajjaṃ, eyyāmissa amādeso ca, dajjeyyāmi, dajjeyyāma. Dvittābhāve deyya, deyyuṃ. Deyyāsi, deyyātha. Dīyetha, dīyeyya.

According to 'kvaci dhātu' and so forth, 'eyya' also becomes 'ā': 'dajjā,' 'dajjuṃ,' 'dajjeyyuṃ.' 'Dajjeyyāsi,' 'dajjeyyātha.' 'Dajjaṃ,' and for 'eyyāmi' there is also the substitute 'aṃ': 'dajjeyyāmi,' 'dajjeyyāma.' In the absence of doubling: 'deyya,' 'deyyuṃ.' 'Deyyāsi,' 'deyyātha.' 'Dīyetha,' 'dīyeyya.'

Hiyyattaniyaṃ adadā, adadū. Adado, adadattha. Adadaṃ, adadamha. Adadattha, adadamhase. Kamme adīyittha.

In the imperfect tense: 'adadā,' 'adadū.' 'Adado,' 'adadattha.' 'Adadaṃ,' 'adadamha.' 'Adadattha,' 'adadamhase.' In the passive: 'adīyittha.'

Ajjatanimhi adadi, adadiṃsu, adaduṃ. Adajji, adajjiṃsu. Adāsi, adaṃsu. Adāsi, ado, adittha. Adāsiṃ, adāsimha, adamha. Adādānaṃ purindado. Kamme adīyittha, adīyyi.

In the aorist tense: 'adadi,' 'adadiṃsu,' 'adaduṃ.' 'Adajji,' 'adajjiṃsu.' 'Adāsi,' 'adaṃsu.' 'Adāsi,' 'ado,' 'adittha.' 'Adāsiṃ,' 'adāsimha,' 'adamha.' 'Adā dānaṃ purindado' (Purindada gave a gift). In the passive: 'adīyittha,' 'adīyyi.'

Bhavissantiyaṃ ikārāgamo, saralopādi, dadissati, dadissanti. Dajjissati, dajjissanti. Rassattaṃ, dassati, dassanti. Dassasi, dassatha. Dassāmi, dassāma. Dassate. Dīyissate, dīyissati.

In the future tense, there is the augment 'i', vowel elision, and so forth: 'dadissati,' 'dadissanti.' 'Dajjissati,' 'dajjissanti.' With shortening: 'dassati,' 'dassanti.' 'Dassasi,' 'dassatha.' 'Dassāmi,' 'dassāma.' 'Dassate.' 'Dīyissate,' 'dīyissati.'

Kālātipattiyaṃ adadissa, adajjissa, adajjissā, adassa, adassā, adassaṃsu. Adīyissatha, adīyissa iccādi.

In the conditional mood: 'adadissa,' 'adajjissa,' 'adajjissā,' 'adassa,' 'adassā,' 'adassaṃsu.' 'Adīyissatha,' 'adīyissa,' and so forth.

Dhā [M 0.0306] dhāraṇe, pure viya vibhattuppatti, dvittarassattāni, appaccayalopo ca, “dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā”ti dhakārassa dakāro, dadhāti, dadhanti. Apipubbo tassa “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā akāralopo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhakārassa hakāro, rassattañca, dvāraṃ pidahati, pidahanti. Dvebhāvābhāve nidhiṃ nidheti, nidhenti.

The root 'dhā' is for holding; as before, there is the arising of inflections, doubling and shortening, and elision of the 'a' suffix. According to the rule 'dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā', 'dh' becomes 'd': 'dadhāti,' 'dadhanti.' When preceded by 'api', according to 'tesu vuddhī' and so forth, there is elision of 'a'; and according to 'kvaci dhātu' and so forth, 'dh' becomes 'h', and there is shortening: 'dvāraṃ pidahati,' 'pidahanti' (he closes the door, they close the door). In the absence of doubling: 'nidhiṃ nidheti,' 'nidhenti' (he places the treasure, they place the treasure).

Kamme dhīyate, dhīyati, pidhīyate, pidhīyati.

In the passive: 'dhīyate,' 'dhīyati'; 'pidhīyate,' 'pidhīyati'.

Tathā dadhātu, pidahatu, nidhetu, nidhentu. Dadhe, dadheyya, pidahe, pidaheyya, nidhe, nidheyya. Dadhāsi, pidahi. Dhassati, pidahissati, paridahessati. Adhassa, pidahissa iccādi.

Similarly: 'dadhātu,' 'pidahatu,' 'nidhetu,' 'nidhentu' (Imperative). 'Dadhe,' 'dadheyya,' 'pidahe,' 'pidaheyya,' 'nidhe,' 'nidheyya' (Optative). 'Dadhāsi' (Present); 'pidahi' (Imperative). 'Dhassati,' 'pidahissati,' 'paridahessati' (Future). 'Adhassa,' 'pidahissa' (Conditional), and so forth.

Juhotyādinayo.

The method of the Juhotyādi group.

Avuddhikā tudādī ca, hūvādi ca tathāparo;

Juhotyādi catuddhevaṃ, ñeyyā bhūvādayo idha.

The Tudādi group without vowel strengthening, and the Hūvādi group, and the next likewise; the Juhotyādi group—thus these four should be known here as related to the Bhūvādi group.

Bhūvādigaṇo.

The Bhūvādi Group.

Rudhādigaṇa

The Rudhādi Group

Rudha āvaraṇe, pure viya dhātusaññādimhi kate vibhattuppatti.

The root 'rudh' is in the sense of obstructing. As before, after the designation of the root and so forth has been made, the verbal ending arises.

“A”iti vattate.

The 'a' is carried forward.

509. Rudhādito niggahītapubbañca.

509. From the Rudh-ādi group, and with a preceding niggahīta.

Catuppadamidaṃ. Rudhaiccevamādito dhātugaṇato appaccayo hoti kattari vibhattippaccayesu, niggahītañca tato pubbaṃ [M 0.0307] hutvā āgamo hoti, tañca niggahītaṃ pakatiyā sarānugatattā dhātussarato paraṃ hoti. Casaddena iīeopaccayā ca, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ. Idha saṃyogantattā na vuddhi hoti, tadāgamassa taggahaṇena gahaṇato.

This is a four-part rule. From the group of roots beginning with rudh, the a-suffix occurs in the active voice before the verbal endings, and a niggahīta is inserted as an augment after the root's vowel. By the word 'ca,' the suffixes i, ī, e, o also occur, and the niggahīta is assimilated to the nasal of the following consonant's class. Here, because the root ends in a conjunct consonant, there is no vuddhi, as the augment is treated as part of the root.

So maggaṃ rundhati, rundhanti. Rundhasi, rundhatha. Rundhāmi, rundhāma. Rundhate, rundhante iccādi, ikārādippaccayesu pana rundhiti, rundhīti, rundheti, rundhotītipi hoti.

He obstructs the path; they obstruct. You obstruct; you (plural) obstruct. I obstruct; we obstruct. (Middle:) He obstructs; they obstruct, etc. But with suffixes beginning with i, it also becomes rundhiti, rundhīti, rundheti, rundhoti.

Kamme nipubbo yappaccayassa “tassa cavagga”iccādinā sadhātvantassa jhakāre kate “vagge ghosā”tiādinā dvittaṃ, maggo nirujjhate tena, nirujjhante. Parassapadatte nirujjhati, nirujjhanti. Nirujjhasi, nirujjhatha. Nirujjhāmi, nirujjhāma.

In the passive, when preceded by ni, by the rule 'tassa cavagga,' etc., the final of the root together with the ya-suffix becomes jha, and this is doubled by the rule 'vagge ghosā,' etc. The path is obstructed by him (maggo nirujjhate tena); they are obstructed (nirujjhante). With active endings: it is obstructed (nirujjhati); they are obstructed (nirujjhanti). You are obstructed (nirujjhasi); you (plural) are obstructed (nirujjhatha). I am obstructed (nirujjhāmi); we are obstructed (nirujjhāma).

Rundhatu, rundhantu. Rundhāhi, rundhatha. Rundhāmi, rundhāma. Rundhataṃ, rundhantaṃ. Rundhassu, rundhavho. Rundhe, rundhāmase. Nirujjhataṃ, nirujjhantaṃ. Nirujjhatu, nirujjhantu. Rundhe, rundheyya, rundheyyuṃ. Rundhetha, rundheraṃ. Nirujjhetha, nirujjheyya iccādi. Rundhi, rundhiṃsu. Arundhi, nirujjhittha. Nirujjhi, nirujjhiṃsu. Rundhissati, rundhissanti. Nirujjhissate, nirujjhissante. Nirujjhissati, nirujjhissanti. Arundhissa, arundhissaṃsu. Nirujjhissatha, nirujjhissa iccādi.

(Imperative Active:) Rundhatu, rundhantu; Rundhāhi, rundhatha; Rundhāmi, rundhāma. (Imperative Middle:) Rundhataṃ, rundhantaṃ; Rundhassu, rundhavho; Rundhe, rundhāmase. (Imperative Passive:) Nirujjhataṃ, nirujjhantaṃ; Nirujjhatu, nirujjhantu. (Optative Active:) rundheyya, rundheyyuṃ. (Optative Middle:) Rundhe, Rundhetha, rundheraṃ. (Optative Passive:) Nirujjhetha, nirujjheyya, etc. (Aorist Active:) Rundhi, rundhiṃsu; Arundhi. (Aorist Passive:) nirujjhittha; Nirujjhi, nirujjhiṃsu. (Future Active:) Rundhissati, rundhissanti. (Future Passive Middle:) Nirujjhissate, nirujjhissante. (Future Passive Active:) Nirujjhissati, nirujjhissanti. (Conditional Active:) Arundhissa, arundhissaṃsu. (Conditional Passive:) Nirujjhissatha, nirujjhissa, etc.

Chidi dvidhākaraṇe, chindati, chindanti. Kamme chijjate, chijjante. Chijjati, chijjanti. Tathā chindatu, chindantu. Chijjatu, chijjantu. Chinde, chindeyya. Chijjeyya. Achindi, chindi, chindiṃsu. Achijjittha, chijji. Chindissati, chindissanti. Ssassa chādese – checchati, checchanti. Checchiti vā. Kamme chijjissate, chijjissante. Chijjissati, chijjissanti. Achindissa. Achijjissa iccādi.

The root chid in the sense of cutting in two: chindati, chindanti. (Passive:) chijjate, chijjante; chijjati, chijjanti. Similarly (Imperative:) chindatu, chindantu; (Passive:) chijjatu, chijjantu. (Optative:) chinde, chindeyya; (Passive:) chijjeyya. (Aorist:) achindi, chindi, chindiṃsu; (Passive:) achijjittha, chijji. (Future:) chindissati, chindissanti. With the replacement of ssa by cha, it becomes checchati, checchanti; or checchiti. (Passive Future:) chijjissate, chijjissante; chijjissati, chijjissanti. (Conditional:) achindissa; (Passive:) achijjissa, etc.

Bhidi [M 0.0308] vidāraṇe, bhindati, bhindanti iccādi.

The root bhid in the sense of splitting: bhindati, bhindanti, etc.

Yuja yoge, yuñjati, yuñjanti. Yujjate, yujjante. Yujjati, yujjanti. Yuñjatu. Yujjataṃ. Yuñje. Yujjetha. Ayuñji, ayuñjiṃsu. Ayujjittha, ayujji. Yuñjissati, yuñjissanti. Yujjissate, yujjissante. Yujjissati, yujjissanti. Ayuñjissa. Ayujjissatha, ayujjissa iccādi.

The root yuj in the sense of yoking: yuñjati, yuñjanti. (Passive Middle:) yujjate, yujjante. (Passive Active:) yujjati, yujjanti. (Imperative:) yuñjatu; (Passive:) yujjataṃ. (Optative:) yuñje; (Passive:) yujjetha. (Aorist:) ayuñji, ayuñjiṃsu; (Passive:) ayujjittha, ayujji. (Future:) yuñjissati, yuñjissanti. (Passive Middle:) yujjissate, yujjissante. (Passive Active:) yujjissati, yujjissanti. (Conditional:) ayuñjissa; (Passive:) ayujjissatha, ayujjissa, etc.

Bhuja pālanabyavaharaṇesu, bhuñjati, bhuñjanti iccādi.

The root bhuj in the senses of protecting and using: bhuñjati, bhuñjanti, etc.

Bhavissantiyaṃ “karassa sappaccayassa kāho”ti sutte sappaccayaggahaṇena bhujato ssassa khādeso, “ko khe cā”ti dhātvantassa kakāro, vuddhi, bhokkhati, bhokkhanti. Bhokkhasi, bhokkhatha. Bhokkhāmi, bhokkhāma. Khādesābhāve bhuñjissati, bhuñjissanti iccādi.

In the future tense, by the inclusion of 'sappaccaya' in the rule 'karassa sappaccayassa kāho,' for the root bhuj, ssa is replaced by kha; by 'ko khe ca,' the final of the root becomes ka; and there is vuddhi: bhokkhati, bhokkhanti. Bhokkhasi, bhokkhatha. Bhokkhāmi, bhokkhāma. In the absence of the substitution of kha: bhuñjissati, bhuñjissanti, etc.

Muca mocane, muñcati, muñcanti. Muccate, muccante. Muñcatu, muñcantu. Muccataṃ, muccantaṃ. Muñce, muñceyya, muñceyyuṃ. Muccetha, mucceraṃ. Amuñci, amuñciṃsu. Amuccittha. Mokkhati, mokkhanti. Muñcissati, muñcissanti. Muccissate, muccissante. Amuñcissa, amuccissatha iccādi.

The root muc in the sense of releasing: muñcati, muñcanti. (Passive:) muccate, muccante. (Imperative:) muñcatu, muñcantu; (Passive:) muccataṃ, muccantaṃ. (Optative:) muñce, muñceyya, muñceyyuṃ; (Passive:) muccetha, mucceraṃ. (Aorist:) amuñci, amuñciṃsu; (Passive:) amuccittha. (Future:) mokkhati, mokkhanti; muñcissati, muñcissanti. (Passive Future:) muccissate, muccissante. (Conditional:) amuñcissa; (Passive:) amuccissatha, etc.

Rudhādigaṇo.

The Rudh-ādi Group.

Divādigaṇa

The Div-ādi Group

Divu kīḷāvijigīsābyavahārajutithutikantigatīsu. Pure viya dhātvantalopavibhattuppattiyo.

The root div in the senses of playing, desiring victory, transacting, shining, praising, loving, and going. As before, there is elision of the final of the root and generation of the verbal ending.

510. Divādito [M 0.0309] yo.

510. From the Div-ādi group, the ya-suffix.

Divādito dhātugaṇato yappaccayo hoti kattari vihitesu vibhattippaccayesu.

From the group of roots beginning with div, the ya-suffix occurs in the active voice before the prescribed verbal endings.

“Yaggahaṇaṃ, cavagga yakāra vakārattaṃ sadhātvantassa, pubbarūpa”nti ca vattate.

The rules concerning the taking of ya, the change of the final of the root together with it into a palatal, y, or v, and assimilation to the preceding are carried forward.

511. Tathā kattari ca.

511. And similarly in the active voice.

Yathā bhāvakammesu yappaccayassādeso hoti, tathā kattaripi yappaccayassa sadhātvantassa cavagga yakāravakārādeso, pubbarūpañca kātabbānīti dhātvantassa vakārattā saha tena yakārassa vakāre kate dvibhāvo, “do dhassa cā”ti ettha caggahaṇena “bo vassā”ti vuttattā vakāradvayassa bakāradvayaṃ, dibbati, dibbanti. Dibbasi, dibbatha. Dibbāmi, dibbāma.

Just as in the impersonal and passive voices there are substitutions for the ya-suffix, so too in the active voice, the substitutions of a palatal, y, or v for the final of the root together with the ya-suffix, and assimilation to the preceding, are to be performed. Thus, since the final of the root (div) is v, when the ya-suffix together with it becomes v, there is doubling (vv). Because it is stated 'ba for va' by the inclusion of 'ca' in the rule 'do dhassa ca,' the doubled v becomes a doubled b. Hence: dibbati, dibbanti. Dibbasi, dibbatha. Dibbāmi, dibbāma.

Kamme dibbate, dibbante. Dibbati, dibbanti. Dibbatu. Dibbataṃ. Dibbe. Dibbetha. Adibbi. Adibbittha. Dibbissati. Dibbissate. Adibbissa iccādi.

(Passive:) dibbate, dibbante. (Active forms are also used for the passive:) dibbati, dibbanti. (Imperative:) dibbatu; (Passive:) dibbataṃ. (Optative Middle:) dibbe; (Passive:) dibbetha. (Aorist:) adibbi; (Passive:) adibbittha. (Future:) dibbissati; (Passive:) dibbissate. (Conditional:) adibbissa, etc.

Sivu tantasantāne, sibbati, sibbanti. Sibbatu. Sibbeyya. Asibbi, sibbi. Sibbissati. Asibbissa iccādi.

The root siv in the sense of sewing: sibbati, sibbanti. (Imperative:) Sibbatu. (Optative:) Sibbeyya. (Aorist:) Asibbi, sibbi. (Future:) Sibbissati. (Conditional:) Asibbissa, etc.

Pada gatimhi, upubbo dvittaṃ, “tathā kattari cā”ti sadhātvantassa yakārassa jakāro, dvittañca.

The root pad in the sense of going. When preceded by the prefix ud, there is doubling. By the rule 'and similarly in the active voice,' the final of the root together with the ya-suffix becomes ja, and this is doubled.

Uppajjati, uppajjanti. Uppajjate, uppajjante, uppajjare.

Uppajjati, uppajjanti. (Middle:) Uppajjate, uppajjante, uppajjare.

Kamme paṭipajjate, paṭipajjante. Paṭipajjati, paṭipajjanti. Bhāve uppajjate tayā.

In the passive: paṭipajjate, paṭipajjante; paṭipajjati, paṭipajjanti. In the impersonal: uppajjate tayā (there is an arising by you).

Tathā [M 0.0310] uppajjatu. Uppajjeyya. Udapajjā. Udapajjatha. Udapādi, uppajjī. Uppajjittha. Uppajjissati. Uppajjissa, uppajjissā iccādi.

Similarly (Imperative:) uppajjatu. (Optative:) uppajjeyya. (Aorist:) udapajjā, udapajjatha, udapādi, uppajjī; (Passive:) uppajjittha. (Future:) uppajjissati. (Conditional:) uppajjissa, uppajjissā, etc.

Budha avagamane, yappaccayaparattā na vuddhi, jhakārādesova viseso, dhammaṃ bujjhati, bujjhanti. Bujjhate, bujjhante, bujjhare vā.

The root budh in the sense of understanding. Because the ya-suffix follows, there is no vuddhi; the substitution of jha is the special feature. He understands the Dhamma (dhammaṃ bujjhati); they understand (bujjhanti). (Middle:) bujjhate, bujjhante, or bujjhare.

Kamme bujjhate mayā dhammo, bujjhante. Bujjhati, bujjhanti. Bujjhatu. Bujjheyya. Abujjhi. Abujjhittha. Bujjhissati. Abujjhissa.

In the passive: The Dhamma is understood by me (bujjhate mayā dhammo); they are understood (bujjhante). (Active forms for passive:) bujjhati, bujjhanti. (Imperative:) bujjhatu. (Optative:) bujjheyya. (Aorist:) abujjhi; (Passive:) abujjhittha. (Future:) bujjhissati. (Conditional:) abujjhissa.

Yudha sampahāre, yujjhati, yujjhanti.

The root yudh in the sense of fighting: yujjhati, yujjhanti.

Kudha kope, kujjhati, kujjhanti.

The root kudh in the sense of anger: kujjhati, kujjhanti.

Vidha tāḷane, vijjhati, vijjhanti iccādi.

The root vidha in the sense of piercing: vijjhati, vijjhanti, etc.

Naha bandhane, “ha vipariyayo”ti yogavibhāgena vipariyayo. Sannayhati, sannayhanti iccādi.

The root nah in the sense of binding. By splitting the rule 'ha vipariyayo,' metathesis occurs. Sannayhati, sannayhanti, etc.

Mana ñāṇe, ñādesova viseso, maññati, maññanti iccādi.

The root man in the sense of knowing. The special feature is the assimilation that results in ññ. Maññati, maññanti, etc.

Dā ādāne, saṃāpubbo “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā yamhi dhātvantassa ikāro, sīlaṃ samādiyati, samādiyanti iccādi.

The root dā in the sense of taking. When preceded by saṃ and ā, by the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., the final vowel of the root becomes i before the ya-suffix. He undertakes the precepts (sīlaṃ samādiyati); they undertake (samādiyanti), etc.

Tusa pītimhi, yappaccayassa pubbarūpattaṃ, tussati, tussanti iccādi.

The root tus in the sense of joy. The ya-suffix is assimilated to the preceding consonant: tussati, tussanti, etc.

Tathā samu upasame, sammati, sammanti.

Similarly, the root sam in the sense of being calm: sammati, sammanti.

Kupa kope, kuppati, kuppanti.

The root kup in the sense of anger: kuppati, kuppanti.

Janajanane, “janādīnamā timhi cā”ti ettha “janādīnamā”ti yogavibhāgena yamhi dhātvantassa ākāro. Jāyati, jāyanti. Jāyate, jāyante.

The root jan in the sense of being born. Here, by splitting the rule 'janādīnamā timhi ca' into 'janādīnamā,' the final vowel of the root becomes ā before the ya-suffix. Jāyati, jāyanti. Jāyate, jāyante.

Kamme [M 0.0311] janīyati, janīyanti. Jāyatu. Jāyeyya. Ajāyi, ajani. Jāyissati, janissati. Ajāyissa, ajanissa iccādi.

In the passive: janīyati, janīyanti. Imperative: jāyatu. Optative: jāyeyya. Aorist: ajāyi, ajani. Future: jāyissati, janissati. Conditional: ajāyissa, ajanissa, etc.

Divādigaṇo.

The Divādi Group.

Svādigaṇa

The Svādi Group

Su savaṇe, pure viya vibhattuppatti.

The root su in the sense of hearing. As before, the inflectional endings are applied.

512. Svādito ṇuṇāuṇā ca.

512. After the roots of the Svādi group, the affixes are ṇu, ṇā, and uṇā.

Suiccevamādito dhātugaṇato ṇu ṇāuṇāiccete paccayā honti kattari vihitesu vibhattippaccayesu. “Aññesu cā”ti ettha caggahaṇena ṇuppaccayassa vuddhi. Tatthevānuvattitavāggahaṇena svādīnaṃ ṇuṇādīsu na vuddhi.

From the group of roots beginning with su, these affixes—ṇu, ṇā, and uṇā—are applied when the inflectional endings are prescribed for the agent. In the rule 'aññesu ca', by the inclusion of 'ca', there is vowel strengthening (vuddhi) of the root before the ṇu-affix. By the inclusion of 'vā', which is carried over into that same rule, there is no vowel strengthening for the roots of the Svādi group before ṇu, ṇā, and so on.

Dhammaṃ suṇoti, saralopādi, suṇanti. Suṇosi, suṇotha. Suṇomi, suṇoma. Ṇāpaccaye suṇāti, suṇanti. Suṇāsi, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā rassattaṃ, suṇasi, suṇātha, suṇatha. Suṇāmi, suṇāma.

He hears the Dhamma (dhammaṃ suṇoti); by vowel elision and so on, they hear (suṇanti). You hear (suṇosi), you all hear (suṇotha). I hear (suṇomi), we hear (suṇoma). With the ṇā-affix: he hears (suṇāti), they hear (suṇanti). You hear (suṇāsi); by the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., there is shortening, thus you hear (suṇasi), you all hear (suṇātha, suṇatha). I hear (suṇāmi), we hear (suṇāma).

Kamme yappaccaye “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dīgho, sūyate, sūyante. Sūyati, sūyanti. Dvitte rassattaṃ, suyyati, suyyanti. Sūyyati, sūyyanti vā.

In the passive, with the ya-affix, by the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., there is lengthening: sūyate, sūyante. Sūyati, sūyanti. With doubling of the consonant, there is shortening: suyyati, suyyanti. Or, sūyyati, sūyyanti.

Suṇotu, suṇantu. Suṇohi, suṇotha. Suṇomi, suṇoma. Suṇātu, suṇantu. Suṇa, suṇāhi, suṇātha. Suṇāmi, suṇāma. Suṇataṃ, suṇantaṃ[M 0.0312]. Suṇassu, suṇavho. Suṇe, suṇāmase. Kamme sūyataṃ, sūyantaṃ. Sūyatu, sūyantu.

Let him hear (suṇotu), let them hear (suṇantu). Hear (suṇohi), you all hear (suṇotha). Let me hear (suṇomi), let us hear (suṇoma). Let him hear (suṇātu), let them hear (suṇantu). Hear (suṇa, suṇāhi), you all hear (suṇātha). Let me hear (suṇāmi), let us hear (suṇāma). Middle: Let him hear (suṇataṃ), let them hear (suṇantaṃ). Hear (suṇassu), you all hear (suṇavho). Let me hear (suṇe), let us hear (suṇāmase). In the passive: let it be heard (sūyataṃ), let them be heard (sūyantaṃ). Let it be heard (sūyatu), let them be heard (sūyantu).

Suṇe, suṇeyya, suṇeyyuṃ. Suṇeyyāsi, suṇeyyātha. Suṇeyyāmi, suṇeyyāma. Suṇetha, suṇeraṃ. Suṇetho, suṇeyyāvho. Suṇeyyaṃ, suṇeyyāmhe. Sūyetha, sūyeyya.

He might hear (suṇe, suṇeyya), they might hear (suṇeyyuṃ). You might hear (suṇeyyāsi), you all might hear (suṇeyyātha). I might hear (suṇeyyāmi), we might hear (suṇeyyāma). Middle: You all might hear (suṇetha), they might hear (suṇeraṃ). You might hear (suṇetho), you all might hear (suṇeyyāvho). I might hear (suṇeyyaṃ), we might hear (suṇeyyāmhe). Passive: It might be heard (sūyetha, sūyeyya).

Asuṇi, suṇi, asuṇiṃsu, suṇiṃsu. Asuṇi, asuṇittha. Asuṇiṃ, suṇiṃ, asuṇimha, suṇimha. Asuṇittha, suṇittha. Ṇāpaccayalopo, vuddhi, sassa dvibhāvo, sāgamo, assosi, assosiṃsu, paccassosuṃ. Assosi, assosittha. Assosiṃ, assosimha, assosimhā vā, assosittha. Asūyittha, assūyi.

He heard (asuṇi, suṇi), they heard (asuṇiṃsu, suṇiṃsu). You heard (asuṇi), you all heard (asuṇittha). I heard (asuṇiṃ, suṇiṃ), we heard (asuṇimha, suṇimha). You all heard (asuṇittha, suṇittha). With elision of the ṇā-affix, vowel strengthening, doubling of s, and the s-augment: he heard (assosi), they heard (assosiṃsu), they replied (paccassosuṃ). You heard (assosi), you all heard (assosittha). I heard (assosiṃ), we heard (assosimha or assosimhā). You all heard (assosittha). Passive: they were heard (asūyittha), it was heard (assūyi).

Saralopādi, suṇissati, suṇissanti. Suṇissasi, suṇissatha. Suṇissāmi, suṇissāma. Suṇissate, suṇissante. Suṇissase, suṇissavhe. Suṇissaṃ, suṇissāmhe. Ṇāpaccayalopo, vuddhi, sossati, sossanti. Sossasi, sossatha. Sossāmi, sossāma. Sossate. Sūyissate, sūyissati. Asuṇissa. Asūyissa iccādi.

By vowel elision and so on: he will hear (suṇissati), they will hear (suṇissanti). You will hear (suṇissasi), you all will hear (suṇissatha). I will hear (suṇissāmi), we will hear (suṇissāma). Middle: suṇissate, suṇissante. Suṇissase, suṇissavhe. Suṇissaṃ, suṇissāmhe. With elision of the ṇā-affix and vowel strengthening: he will hear (sossati), they will hear (sossanti). You will hear (sossasi), you all will hear (sossatha). I will hear (sossāmi), we will hear (sossāma). Middle: sossate. Passive: sūyissate, sūyissati. Conditional: he would have heard (asuṇissa). Passive conditional: it would have been heard (asūyissa), etc.

Hi gatimhi, papubbo ṇāpaccayo, pahiṇāti, pahiṇati vā, pahiṇanti. Pahiṇātu, pahiṇantu. Pahiṇeyya. Pahiṇi, dūtaṃ pāhesi. Pahiṇissati. Pahiṇissa iccādi.

The root hi in the sense of going. With the prefix pa- and the ṇā-affix: he sends (pahiṇāti or pahiṇati), they send (pahiṇanti). Imperative: pahiṇātu, pahiṇantu. Optative: pahiṇeyya. Aorist: pahiṇi; for example, he dispatched a messenger (dūtaṃ pāhesi). Future: pahiṇissati. Conditional: pahiṇissa, etc.

Vu saṃvaraṇe, āvuṇāti, āvuṇanti iccādi.

The root vu in the sense of covering: he covers (āvuṇāti), they cover (āvuṇanti), etc.

Mi pakkhepe, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ṇassa nattaṃ, minoti, minanti iccādi.

The root mi in the sense of measuring. By the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., ṇ becomes n: he measures (minoti), they measure (minanti), etc.

Apa [M 0.0313] pāpuṇane, papubbo saralope “dīgha”nti dīgho, uṇāpaccayo, sampattiṃ pāpuṇāti, pāpuṇanti. Pāpuṇāsi, pāpuṇātha. Pāpuṇāmi, pāpuṇāma.

The root ap in the sense of reaching. With the prefix pa-, vowel elision, and lengthening by the rule 'dīghaṃ', the uṇā-affix is applied: he attains success (sampattiṃ pāpuṇāti), they attain (pāpuṇanti). You attain (pāpuṇāsi), you all attain (pāpuṇātha). I attain (pāpuṇāmi), we attain (pāpuṇāma).

Kamme pāpīyati, pāpīyanti. Tathā pāpuṇātu. Pāpīyatu. Pāpuṇe, pāpuṇeyya. Pāpīyeyya. Pāpuṇi, pāpuṇiṃsu. Pāpīyi. Pāpuṇissati. Pāpīyissati. Pāpuṇissa. Pāpīyissa iccādi.

In the passive: it is attained (pāpīyati), they are attained (pāpīyanti). Similarly, for other tenses: Imperative: pāpuṇātu (active), pāpīyatu (passive). Optative: pāpuṇe, pāpuṇeyya (active), pāpīyeyya (passive). Aorist: pāpuṇi, pāpuṇiṃsu (active), pāpīyi (passive). Future: pāpuṇissati (active), pāpīyissati (passive). Conditional: pāpuṇissa (active), pāpīyissa (passive), etc.

Saka sattimhi, dvibhāvo, sakkuṇāti, sakkuṇanti. Bhāve “pubbarūpañcā”ti pubbarūpattaṃ, sakkate tayā, sakkati vā, sakkuṇātu. Sakkuṇeyya. “Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā sakantassa khādeso ajjatanādimhi, asakkhi, sakkhi, asakkhiṃsu, sakkhiṃsu. Sakkhissati, sakkhissanti. Asakkhissa, asakkhissaṃsu iccādi.

The root sak in the sense of ability. With doubling of the consonant (dvibhāvo): he is able (sakkuṇāti), they are able (sakkuṇanti). In the impersonal voice (bhāve), by the rule 'pubbarūpañca', there is assimilation: it is possible for you (sakkate tayā), or it is possible (sakkati). Imperative: sakkuṇātu. Optative: sakkuṇeyya. By the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., the final k of sak is replaced by kh in the aorist and other tenses: he was able (asakkhi, sakkhi), they were able (asakkhiṃsu, sakkhiṃsu). Future: he will be able (sakkhissati), they will be able (sakkhissanti). Conditional: he would have been able (asakkhissa), they would have been able (asakkhissaṃsu), etc.

Svādigaṇo.

The Svādi Group.

Kiyādigaṇa

The Kiyādi Group.

Kī dabbavinimaye, vipubbo dvittaṃ, pure viya vibhattuppatti.

The root kī in the sense of exchanging goods. With the prefix vi-, there is doubling of the consonant. As before, the inflectional endings are applied.

513. Kiyādito nā.

513. After the roots of the Kiyādi group, the affix is nā.

Kīicceva mādito dhātugaṇato nāpaccayo hoti kattari. Nāparattā na vuddhi, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā kiyādīnaṃ nāmhi rassattaṃ, kīto nāpaccayanakārassa ṇattañca.

From the root group beginning with 'kī' itself, the nā affix is applied in the agentive sense. Due to not being followed by a vowel, there is no vuddhi-strengthening. By the rule 'kvaci dhātūnaṃ…' and so on, there is shortening for the Kiyādi roots when the nā affix is present, and the 'n' of the nā affix becomes 'ṇ' after the root 'kī'.

Bhaṇḍaṃ vikkiṇāti, vikkiṇanti. Vikkīyati, vikkīyanti. Vikkiṇātu, vikkiṇantu. Vikkīyatu, vikkīyantu. Vikkiṇe, vikkiṇeyya[M 0.0314]. Vikkīyeyya, vikkīyeyyuṃ. Avikkiṇi, vikkiṇi. Vikkīyittha, vikkīyi. Vikkiṇissati, vikkiṇissanti. Vikkīyissati, vikkīyissanti. Avikkiṇissa, avikkiṇissaṃsu. Vikkīyissa, vikkīyissaṃsu iccādi.

He sells goods (bhaṇḍaṃ vikkiṇāti), they sell goods (vikkiṇanti). It is sold (vikkīyati), they are sold (vikkīyanti). Let him sell (vikkiṇātu), let them sell (vikkiṇantu). Let it be sold (vikkīyatu), let them be sold (vikkīyantu). He should sell (vikkiṇe), he might sell (vikkiṇeyya). It might be sold (vikkīyeyya), they might be sold (vikkīyeyyuṃ). He sold (avikkiṇi), he sold (vikkiṇi). It was sold (vikkīyittha), it was sold (vikkīyi). He will sell (vikkiṇissati), they will sell (vikkiṇissanti). It will be sold (vikkīyissati), they will be sold (vikkīyissanti). He would have sold (avikkiṇissa), they would have sold (avikkiṇissaṃsu). It would have been sold (vikkīyissa), they would have been sold (vikkīyissaṃsu), and so on.

Ji jaye, kilese jināti, jinanti. Jīyati, jīyanti. Evaṃ jinātu. Jīyatu. Jineyya. Jīyeyya. Ajini, jini, ajiniṃsu, jiniṃsu. Ajesi, ajesuṃ. Ajinittha. Ajīyittha, ajīyi. Jinissati, jinissanti. Vijessati, vijessanti. Jīyissati, jīyissanti. Ajinissa. Ajīyissa iccādi.

The root 'ji' is in the sense of conquering (jaye): he conquers the defilements (kilese jināti), they conquer (jinanti). He is conquered (jīyati), they are conquered (jīyanti). Thus: let him conquer (jinātu). Let it be conquered (jīyatu). He might conquer (jineyya). It might be conquered (jīyeyya). He conquered (ajini, jini), they conquered (ajiniṃsu, jiniṃsu). He conquered (ajesi), they conquered (ajesuṃ). You all conquered (ajinittha). It was conquered (ajīyittha, ajīyi). He will conquer (jinissati), they will conquer (jinissanti). He will conquer (vijessati), they will conquer (vijessanti). It will be conquered (jīyissati), they will be conquered (jīyissanti). He would have conquered (ajinissa). It would have been conquered (ajīyissa), and so on.

Tathā ci caye, cināti, cinanti iccādi.

Similarly, the root 'ci' is in the sense of accumulating (caye): he accumulates (cināti), they accumulate (cinanti), and so on.

Ñā avabodhane nāpaccayo.

For the root 'ñā' in the sense of understanding (avabodhane), the nā affix is applied.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' (or) is carried over.

514. Ñāssa jā jaṃ nā.

514. For 'ñā', the substitutes are 'jā', 'jaṃ', and 'nā'.

Ñāiccetassa dhātussa jā jaṃ nāiccete ādesā honti vā.

For the root 'ñā', these substitutes—'jā', 'jaṃ', and 'nā'—optionally occur.

Jādeso nāmhi jaṃ ñāmhi, nābhāvo timhi evidha;

Vavatthitavibhāsattha-vāsaddassānuvattanā;

Dhammaṃ vijānāti, vināyati vā, vijānanti.

The substitute 'jā' occurs when the `nā` affix is present; 'jaṃ' when `ñā` is present; the substitute 'nā' is absent before the 'ti' ending here. By the continuation of the word 'vā', which signifies a fixed option: one understands the Dhamma (dhammaṃ vijānāti), or one disciplines (vināyati); they understand (vijānanti).

Kamme viññāyati, viññāyanti. Ivaṇṇāgame pubbalopo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ekāro, dvittañca, ñeyyati, ñeyyanti. Vijānātu, vijānantu, rassattaṃ. Vijāna, vijānāhi, vijānātha. Vijānāmi, vijānāma. Vijānataṃ, vijānantaṃ. Vijānassu. Viññāyatu, viññāyantu.

In the passive: it is known (viññāyati), they are known (viññāyanti). With the insertion of 'i' and elision of the preceding vowel, by the rule 'kvaci dhātū…' and so on, there is the vowel 'e' and also doubling: it is to be known (ñeyyati), they are to be known (ñeyyanti). Let him understand (vijānātu), let them understand (vijānantu); with shortening: understand (vijāna, vijānāhi), you all understand (vijānātha). I understand (vijānāmi), we understand (vijānāma). Let them two understand (vijānataṃ), let them understand (vijānantaṃ). Understand (vijānassu). Let it be known (viññāyatu), let them be known (viññāyantu).

515. Eyyassa [M 0.0315] ñāto iyā ñā vā.

515. After 'ñā', 'eyya' is optionally substituted by 'iyā' or 'ñā'.

Eyyassa vibhattissa ñāiccetāya dhātuyā parassa iyā ñāiccete ādesā honti vā, saralopādi. Vijāniyā.

For the 'eyya' inflection following the root 'ñā', the substitutes 'iyā' and 'ñā' optionally occur, with vowel elision and so on. For example, vijāniyā.

Ñādese ñāssa jaṃādeso.

When 'ñā' is the substitute, 'jaṃ' is substituted for the root 'ñā'.

“Ñāto, vā”ti ca vattate.

The words 'ñāto' (after 'ñā') and 'vā' (or) are carried over.

516. Nāssa lopo yakārattaṃ.

516. For 'nā', there is elision or it becomes 'ya'.

Ñāiccetāya dhātuyā parassa nāpaccayassa lopo hoti vā, yakārattañca, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Tena –

For the nā affix following the root 'ñā', there is optional elision and also the change to 'ya'. This word 'vā' (or) is for a fixed option. Therefore:

Ñāmhi niccañca nālopo,

Vibhāsājjatanādisu;

Aññattha na ca hotāyaṃ,

Nāto timhi yakāratā.

When `ñā` is present, elision of `nā` is constant; in the aorist and so on, it is optional. Elsewhere, this does not occur. After `nā`, before `ti`, there is no change to `ya`.

Niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ, vijaññā, vijāneyya, vijāneyyuṃ. Vijāneyyāsi, vijāneyyātha. Vijāneyyāmi, vijāneyyāma, vijānemu vā. Vijānetha. Viññāyeyya, viññāyeyyuṃ.

The niggahīta becomes a class-final consonant. One should know (vijaññā), he should know (vijāneyya), they should know (vijāneyyuṃ). You should know (vijāneyyāsi), you all should know (vijāneyyātha). I should know (vijāneyyāmi), we should know (vijāneyyāma), or we should know (vijānemu). You all should know (vijānetha). It might be known (viññāyeyya), they might be known (viññāyeyyuṃ).

Samajāni, sañjāni, sañjāniṃsu. Nālope aññāsi, aññāsuṃ. Vijānittha. Viññāyittha. Paññāyi, paññāyiṃsu. Vijānissati, vijānissanti. Ñassati, ñassanti. Viññāyissate, viññāyissante. Paññāyissati, paññāyissanti. “Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ssassa [M 0.0316] hi ca, paññāyihiti, paññāyihinti. Ajānissa. Ajānissatha. Aññāyissatha, aññāyissa iccādi.

He knew fully (samajāni, sañjāni), they knew fully (sañjāniṃsu). With the elision of nā: he knew (aññāsi), they knew (aññāsuṃ). You all understood (vijānittha). It was known (viññāyittha). It was perceived (paññāyi), they were perceived (paññāyiṃsu). He will understand (vijānissati), they will understand (vijānissanti). He will know (ñassati), they will know (ñassanti). It will be known (viññāyissate), they will be known (viññāyissante). It will be perceived (paññāyissati), they will be perceived (paññāyissanti). By the rule 'kvaci dhātū…' and so on, 'ss' becomes 'h' and 'i': it will be perceived (paññāyihiti), they will be perceived (paññāyihinti). He would have known (ajānissa). You all would have known (ajānissatha). You all would have been known (aññāyissatha), it would have been known (aññāyissa), and so on.

Mā māne, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā māntassa ikāro, mināti, minanti. Kamme mīyati, mīyanti iccādi.

The root 'mā' is in the sense of measuring (māne). By the rule 'kvaci dhātū…' and so on, the final vowel of 'mā' becomes 'i': he measures (mināti), they measure (minanti). In the passive: it is measured (mīyati), they are measured (mīyanti), and so on.

Lū chedane, nāmhi rassattaṃ, lunāti, lunanti. Lūyati, lūyanti iccādi.

The root 'lū' is in the sense of cutting (chedane). When the nā affix is present, there is shortening: he cuts (lunāti), they cut (lunanti). It is cut (lūyati), they are cut (lūyanti), and so on.

Dhū kampane, dhunāti, dhunanti. Dhūyati, dhūyanti iccādi.

The root 'dhū' is in the sense of shaking (kampane): he shakes (dhunāti), they shake (dhunanti). It is shaken (dhūyati), they are shaken (dhūyanti), and so on.

Gaha upādāne, nāmhi sampatte –

The root 'gaha' is in the sense of taking (upādāne). When the nā affix is to be applied:

517. Gahāditoppaṇhā.

517. From 'gaha' and so on, 'ppa' and 'ṇhā'.

Gahaiccevamādito dhātuto ppa ṇhāiccete paccayā honti kattari. Ādisaddoyaṃ pakāro.

From the root 'gaha' and so on, these affixes—'ppa' and 'ṇhā'—are applied in the agentive sense. The word 'ādi' here indicates a class.

“Gahassā”ti vattate.

The word 'gahassa' (for 'gaha') is carried over.

518. Halopo ṇhāmhi.

518. Elision of 'h' when 'ṇhā' is present.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa hakārassa lopo hoti ṇhāmhi paccaye pare. Sīlaṃ gaṇhāti, rassatte gaṇhati vā, gaṇhanti. Gaṇhāsi, gaṇhātha. Gaṇhāmi, gaṇhāma.

For the root 'gaha', the 'h' is elided when the ṇhā affix follows. He takes virtue (sīlaṃ gaṇhāti), or with shortening, he takes (gaṇhati). They take (gaṇhanti). You take (gaṇhāsi), you all take (gaṇhātha). I take (gaṇhāmi), we take (gaṇhāma).

Kamme “ye”ti vattamāne “havipariyayo lo vā”ti hakārassa yakārena vipariyayo hoti. Gayhati, gayhanti.

In the passive, when 'ye' is current, by the rule 'havipariyayo lo vā' (the 'h' is changed or optionally elided), the 'h' is changed to 'y'. For example, it is taken (gayhati), they are taken (gayhanti).

Gaṇhātu, gaṇhantu. Gaṇha, gaṇhāhi, gaṇhātha. Gaṇhāmi, gaṇhāma. Gaṇhataṃ, gaṇhantaṃ. Gayhataṃ, gayhantaṃ. Gayhatu, gayhantu. Gaṇhe, gaṇheyya, gaṇheyyuṃ. Gayheyya, gayheyyuṃ. Aggaṇhi, gaṇhi, aggaṇhiṃsu, gaṇhiṃsu.

Let him take (gaṇhātu), let them take (gaṇhantu). Take (gaṇha, gaṇhāhi), you all take (gaṇhātha). Let me take (gaṇhāmi), let us take (gaṇhāma). Let them two take (gaṇhataṃ), let them take (gaṇhantaṃ). Let them two be taken (gayhataṃ), let them be taken (gayhantaṃ). Let it be taken (gayhatu), let them be taken (gayhantu). He should take (gaṇhe), he might take (gaṇheyya), they might take (gaṇheyyuṃ). It might be taken (gayheyya), they might be taken (gayheyyuṃ). He took (aggaṇhi, gaṇhi), they took (aggaṇhiṃsu, gaṇhiṃsu).

Yadā [M 0.0317] “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā asabbadhātuke vikaraṇapaccayassa lopo, ikārāgamassa ekāro ca, tadā sāgamo.

When, by the rule 'kvaci dhātu' and so on, there is elision of the vikaraṇa affix before a non-sabbadhātuka ending, and the augment 'i' becomes 'e', then there is the augment 's'.

Aggahesi, aggahesuṃ. Aggahi, aggahiṃsu, aggahuṃ. Aggayhittha, aggayhi. Gaṇhissati, gaṇhissanti. Gahessati, gahessanti. Gahīyissate, gahīyissante. Gayhissati, gayhissanti. Aggaṇhissa, aggahissa. Aggaṇhissatha, aggahissatha. Aggayhissatha, aggayhissa iccādi.

He took, they took. He took, they took, they took. It was taken, it was taken. He will take, they will take. He will take, they will take. It will be taken, they will be taken. It will be taken, they will be taken. He would take, he would take. You all would take, you all would take. You all would be taken, it would be taken, and so on.

Ppappaccaye –

When the ppa affix is present—

519. Gahassa ghe ppe.

519. For 'gaha', 'ghe' is substituted when 'ppa' is present.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa gheādeso hoti ppappaccaye pare. Gheppati iccādi.

For the entire root 'gaha', the substitute 'ghe' occurs when the ppa affix follows. For example: gheppati, and so on.

Kiyādigaṇo.

The Kiyādi Group.

Tanādigaṇa

The Tanādi Group

Tanu vitthāre, pure viya dhātvantalopavibhattuppattiyo.

The root 'tanu' is in the sense of 'to spread'. As before, there is elision of the final element of the root and the application of inflections.

520. Tanādito oyirā.

520. From the Tanādi group of roots, the affixes 'o' and 'yira' are applied.

Tanuiccevamādito dhātugaṇato oyiraiccete paccayā honti kattari. Karatovāyaṃ yirappaccayo.

From this group of roots, beginning with 'tanu', these affixes 'o' and 'yira' occur in the active voice. This 'yira' affix is from the root 'kar'.

Dhammaṃ tanoti, tanonti. Tanosi, tanotha. Tanomi, tanoma.

He spreads the Dhamma; they spread. You spread; you all spread. I spread; we spread.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' (or) is carried forward.

521. Uttamokāro[M 0.0318].

521. The 'o' is for the first person.

Tanādito okārappaccayo uttamāpajjate vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo. Ettha ca vikaraṇakāriyavidhippakaraṇato “okāro”ti ovikaraṇaṃ gayhati. Tanute, bahuvacane “yavakārā cā”ti vattaṃ, tanvante. Tanuse, tanuvhe. Tanve, tanumhe.

From the Tanādi group, the 'o' affix optionally applies to the first person. This word 'vā' signifies a fixed option. Here, due to the section on rules concerning the function of vikaraṇas, 'okāro' is understood as the vikaraṇa 'o'. He spreads (tanute); in the plural, according to the rule 'yavakārā ca', it is 'tanvante' (they spread). You spread (tanuse); you all spread (tanuvhe). I spread (tanve); we spread (tanumhe).

Kamme “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā tanudhātvantassa yamhi ākāro, patāyate, patāyante. Patāyati, patāyanti. Ākārābhāve pataññati, pataññanti. Tanotu, tanontu. Taneyya, taneyyuṃ. Atani, ataniṃsu. Atāyittha, patāyi. Tanissati, tanissanti. Patāyissati, patāyissanti. Atanissa. Patāyissa iccādi.

In the passive voice, by the rule 'kvaci dhātu' and so on, 'ā' is substituted for the final vowel of the root 'tanu' when 'ya' follows: it is spread (patāyate), they are spread (patāyante). It is spread (patāyati), they are spread (patāyanti). In the absence of 'ā': it is spread (pataññati), they are spread (pataññanti). Let him spread (tanotu), let them spread (tanontu). He might spread (taneyya), they might spread (taneyyuṃ). He spread (atani), they spread (ataniṃsu). It was spread (atāyittha, patāyi). He will spread (tanissati), they will spread (tanissanti). It will be spread (patāyissati), they will be spread (patāyissanti). He would spread (atanissa). It would be spread (patāyissa), and so on.

Kara karaṇe, puññaṃ karoti.

The root 'kara' is in the sense of 'doing'. He does merit.

Bahuvacane “vā”ti vattamāne, “uttamokāro”ti utte kate –

In the plural, when 'vā' is carried forward, and 'uttamokāro' is stated—

“Vā, utta”nti ca vattate.

And 'vā' (or) and 'utta' (first person) are also carried forward.

522. Karassākāro ca.

522. And the 'a' of 'kara' becomes 'u'.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa akāro uttamāpajjate vā. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, “yavakārā cā”ti apadantassa paraukārassa vakāro, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhāturakārassa vakārasmiṃ lopo, vakārassa dvitte tassa “bbo vvassā”ti bakāradvayaṃ, kubbanti, karonti. Karosi, karotha. Karomi, karoma. Tathā kurute, kubbante. Kuruse, kuruvhe. Kubbe, kurumhe. Yirappaccaye rakāralopo, kayirati, kayiranti iccādi.

For this root 'kara', its 'a' optionally becomes 'u'. This word 'vā' signifies a fixed option. According to the rule 'yavakārā ca', a following 'u' not at the end of a word becomes 'v'; and according to 'kvaci dhātu' and so on, the 'a' of the root is elided when 'v' follows; when 'v' is doubled, it becomes a double 'b' according to 'bbo vvassā'. Thus: they do (kubbanti), they do (karonti). You do (karosi), you all do (karotha). I do (karomi), we do (karoma). Similarly: he does (kurute), they do (kubbante). You do (kuruse), you all do (kuruvhe). I do (kubbe), we do (kurumhe). When the 'yira' affix is applied, the 'r' is elided: it is done (kayirati), they are done (kayiranti), and so on.

Kamme [M 0.0319] yappaccaye “ivaṇṇāgamo vā”ti īkārāgamo, yakārassa dvittaṃ, karīyyate kaṭo tena, karīyyati, karīyyanti. Karīyati, karīyanti vā. Īkārābhāve “tassa cavagga”iccādinā sadhātvantassa yakārattaṃ, dvittañca. Kayyati, kayyanti. Ikārāgame “kvaci dhātu”iccādisutte caggahaṇena rayānaṃ vipariyayo, kayirati kaṭo tena, kayiranti iccādi.

In the passive voice, when the 'ya' affix is applied, the vowel 'ī' is optionally augmented according to 'ivaṇṇāgamo vā', and the 'y' is doubled. Thus: a mat is made by him (karīyyate kaṭo tena), it is made (karīyyati), they are made (karīyyanti). Or, karīyati, karīyanti. In the absence of the 'ī' augment, according to 'tassa cavagga' and so on, the final consonant of the root together with the 'y' becomes 'yy'. Thus: it is made (kayyati), they are made (kayyanti). When the 'i' vowel is augmented, by the inclusion of 'ca' in the rule 'kvaci dhātu' and so on, there is a metathesis of 'r' and 'y', resulting in: a mat is made by him (kayirati kaṭo tena), they are made (kayiranti), and so on.

Tathā kusalaṃ karotu, kurutu vā, kubbantu, karontu. Karohi, karotha. Karomi, karoma. Kurutaṃ, kubbantaṃ. Kurussu, kurassu vā, kuruvho. Kubbe, kubbāmase.

Similarly: Let him do good (kusalaṃ karotu), or let him do (kurutu); let them do (kubbantu), let them do (karontu). Do (karohi); do (you all) (karotha). Let me do (karomi); let us do (karoma). Let him do (kurutaṃ); let them do (kubbantaṃ). Do (kurussu), or do (kurassu); do (you all) (kuruvho). Let me do (kubbe); let us do (kubbāmase).

Kamme karīyatu, karīyantu, kayyataṃ, kayirataṃ, kayiratu.

In the passive voice: Let it be done (karīyatu), let them be done (karīyantu), let it be done (kayyataṃ), let it be done (kayirataṃ), let it be done (kayiratu).

Sattamiyaṃ kare, kareyya, kareyyuṃ. Kareyyāsi, kareyyātha. Kareyyāmi, kareyyāma. Utte kubbe, kubbeyya.

In the Optative: he might do (kare, kareyya), they might do (kareyyuṃ). You might do (kareyyāsi), you all might do (kareyyātha). I might do (kareyyāmi), we might do (kareyyāma). With the 'u' substitution: I might do (kubbe), he might do (kubbeyya).

Yirappaccaye –

When the 'yira' affix is applied—

Yirato āttameyyassa, ethādisseyyumādisu;

Eyyasaddassa lopo ca, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā.

After 'yira', 'eyya' becomes 'ā', and in endings such as 'eyyum', the 'eyya' is elided, according to the rule 'kvaci dhātu' and so on.

Saralopādi, kayirā, kayiruṃ. Kayirāsi, kayirātha. Kayirāmi, kayirāma. Attanopade kayirātha dhīro, kubbetha, karetha vā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā kussa kru ca, krubbetha, krubberaṃ. Krubbetho, krubbeyyāvho. Krubbeyyaṃ, krubbeyyāmhe. Kamme karīyeyya, karīyeyyuṃ.

With elision of vowels and so on: he might do (kayirā), they might do (kayiruṃ). You might do (kayirāsi), you all might do (kayirātha). I might do (kayirāmi), we might do (kayirāma). In the middle voice: a wise person might do (kayirātha dhīro); or he might do (kubbetha), or he might do (karetha). According to 'kvaci dhātu' and so on, 'ku' also becomes 'kru'. Thus: he might do (krubbetha), they might do (krubberaṃ). You might do (krubbetho), you all might do (krubbeyyāvho). I might do (krubbeyyaṃ), we might do (krubbeyyāmhe). In the passive voice: it might be done (karīyeyya), they might be done (karīyeyyuṃ).

Hiyyattaniyaṃ [M 0.0320] “karassa kā”ti yogavibhāgena kā hoti, saralopādi.

In the Imperfect tense, by splitting the rule 'karassa kā', 'kā' is substituted for the root, followed by elision of vowels and so on.

Akā, akarā, akarū. Akaro, akattha, akarottha. Akaṃ, akaraṃ, akamha, akaramha. Akattha. Akariṃ, akaramhase.

He did (akā, akarā); they did (akarū). You did (akaro); you all did (akattha, akarottha). I did (akaṃ, akaraṃ); we did (akamha, akaramha). You all did (akattha). I did (akariṃ); we did (akaramhase).

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' (or) is carried forward.

523. Karassa kāsattamajjatanimhi.

523. For the root kara, the substitution kā and the augment sa in the Aorist.

Kara iccetassa dhātussa sabbasseva kāsattaṃ hoti vā ajjatanimhi vibhattimhi pare. “Kāsatta”miti bhāvaniddesena aññasmāpi dhātuto sāgamo. Atha vā yadā karassa kā hoti, sattañcāgamo ajjatanimhi vāti attho, tadā “sattamajjatanimhī”ti yogavibhāgena aññasmāpi dhātuto sāgamopi sijjhati, “yogavibhāgato iṭṭhappasiddhī”ti yebhuyyena dīghatova hoti, “karassa kā”ti yogavibhāgena kābhāvo ca hiyyattaniyaṃ siddho hoti.

For this entire root kara, the substitution to kā and the augment sa optionally occurs when an Aorist tense inflection follows. By the abstract designation 'kāsatta', the augment sa also occurs after other roots. Alternatively, the meaning is that when kara becomes kā, the augment sa also optionally occurs in the Aorist. Then, by splitting the rule as 'sattamajjatanimhi', the augment sa is also accomplished for other roots, for 'the desired result is achieved by splitting the rule'. Generally, only the long vowel occurs. And by splitting the rule as 'karassa kā', the non-occurrence of the substitution kā is established in the Hiyyattanī (Imperfect).
