Akāsi, akāsuṃ. Akāsi, akāsittha. Akāsiṃ, akāsimha. Akāsittha. Kāsattābhāve akari, kari, akariṃsu, kariṃsu, akaṃsu, akaruṃ. Akari, akarittha. Akariṃ, kariṃ, akarimha, karimha. Akarittha. Akarīyittha, akarīyi vā.

Akāsi (he did), akāsuṃ (they did). Akāsi (you did), akāsittha (you all did). Akāsiṃ (I did), akāsimha (we did). Akāsittha (you all did). In the absence of the kāsa substitution: akari, kari (he did); akariṃsu, kariṃsu, akaṃsu, akaruṃ (they did). Akari (you did), akarittha (you all did). Akariṃ, kariṃ (I did); akarimha, karimha (we did). Akarittha (you all did). Akarīyittha, or akarīyi (it was done).

“Vā, lopo, bhavissantimhi ssassa cā”ti ca vattate.

And 'vā' (optionally), 'lopo' (elision), and 'for ssa in the future tense (bhavissantimhi)' are also carried forward.

524. Karassa sappaccayassa kāho.

524. For the root kara with the suffix sa, the substitution is kāha.

Karaiccetassa [M 0.0321] dhātussa sappaccayassa kāhādeso hoti vā bhavissantimhi, ssassa ca lopo hoti. Adhikabhūtasappaccayaggahaṇena vacamucabhujādito ssassa khādeso, vasa chidi labhādito chādeso ca hoti.

For this root kara with the suffix sa, the substitution kāha optionally occurs in the future tense, and the ssa is also elided. By the inclusion of the suffix sa which has become additional, for ssa after roots like vac, muc, bhuj, etc., there is the substitution khā, and for ssa after roots like vas, chid, labh, etc., there is the substitution chā.

Kāhati, kāhanti. Kāhasi, kāhatha. Kāhāmi, kāhāma. Ikārāgame kāhiti, kāhinti iccādi. Kāhābhāve karissati, karissanti. Karissasi, karissatha. Karissāmi, karissāma. Karissate, karissante. Karissase, karissavhe. Karissaṃ, karissāmhe. Karīyissati, karīyissanti. Akarissa. Akarīyissā iccādi.

Kāhati (he will do), kāhanti (they will do). Kāhasi (you will do), kāhatha (you all will do). Kāhāmi (I will do), kāhāma (we will do). With the augment i: kāhiti, kāhinti, and so forth. In the absence of kāha: karissati (he will do), karissanti (they will do). Karissasi (you will do), karissatha (you all will do). Karissāmi (I will do), karissāma (we will do). Karissate (he will do, middle voice), karissante (they will do, middle voice). Karissase (you will do, middle voice), karissavhe (you all will do, middle voice). Karissaṃ (I will do, middle voice), karissāmhe (we will do, middle voice). Karīyissati (it will be done), karīyissanti (they will be done). Akarissa (he would have done). Akarīyissā (it would have been done), and so forth.

Yadā saṃpubbo, tadā “purasamupaparīhi karotissa kha kharā vā”ti yogavibhāgena tyādivibhattīsupi saṃpubbakarotissa kharādeso.

When preceded by saṃ, then by splitting the rule 'purasamupaparīhi karotissa kha kharā vā', the substitution khara occurs for karoti preceded by saṃ, even with the ti, etc., inflections.

Abhisaṅkharoti, abhisaṅkharonti. Abhisaṅkharīyati, abhisaṅkharīyanti. Abhisaṅkharotu. Abhisaṅkhareyya. Abhisaṅkhari, khādese abhisaṅkhāsi vā. Abhisaṅkharissati. Abhisaṅkharissa iccādi.

Abhisaṅkharoti (he fabricates), abhisaṅkharonti (they fabricate). Abhisaṅkharīyati (it is fabricated), abhisaṅkharīyanti (they are fabricated). Abhisaṅkharotu (let him fabricate). Abhisaṅkhareyya (he might fabricate). Abhisaṅkhari (he fabricated), or with the substitution khā, abhisaṅkhāsi (he fabricated). Abhisaṅkharissati (he will fabricate). Abhisaṅkharissa (he would have fabricated), and so forth.

Saka sattimhi, opaccayo, sakkoti, sakkonti. Sakkosi, sakkotha. Sakkomi, sakkoma iccādi.

The root sak in the sense of 'ability'; the suffix is o. Sakkoti (he is able), sakkonti (they are able). Sakkosi (you are able), sakkotha (you all are able). Sakkomi (I am able), sakkoma (we are able), and so forth.

Apa pāpuṇane, papubbo, pappoti, papponti. Papposi, pappotha. Pappomi, pappoma. Pappotu, pappontu iccādi.

The root āp in the sense of 'reaching'. When preceded by pa: pappoti (he reaches), papponti (they reach). Papposi (you reach), pappotha (you all reach). Pappomi (I reach), pappoma (we reach). Pappotu (let him reach), pappontu (let them reach), and so forth.

Tanādigaṇo.

The Tanādi Group.

Curādigaṇa

The Curādi Group.

Dhura [M 0.0322] theyye, pure viya dhātvantalopo, vibhattuppatti.

The root dhur in the sense of 'stealing'. As before, there is elision of the final vowel of the root, and the inflection is produced.

“Tathā kattari cā”ti ito “kattarī”ti ca sīhavilokanena bhāvakammaggahaṇāni ca vattante, maṇḍūkagatiyā kāritaggahaṇañca.

From 'Tathā kattari cā' ('Similarly, and in the agent'), the term 'kattari' (agent) is carried forward by the 'lion's glance' (sīhavilokana), and the terms for the abstract (bhāva) and passive (kamma) senses are also carried forward; and by the 'frog's leap' (maṇḍūkagati), the term for the causative (kārita) is also included.

525. Curādito ṇeṇayā.

525. After the Curādi group, ṇe and ṇaya.

Curaiccevamādito dhātugaṇato ṇe ṇayaiccete paccayā honti kattari, bhāve ca kammani, vibhattippaccayesu. “Kāritaṃ viya ṇānubandho”ti ṇe ṇayānaṃ kāritabyapadeso.

From the group of roots beginning with cur, etc., these suffixes ṇe and ṇaya occur in the active, abstract, and passive senses, before the verbal inflections. Because 'the anubandha ṇ is like a causative', ṇe and ṇaya have the designation 'causative'.

526. Kāritānaṃ ṇo lopaṃ.

526. There is elision of the ṇ of causative suffixes.

Kāritappaccayānaṃ ṇakāro lopamāpajjate.

The letter ṇ of causative suffixes undergoes elision.

527. Asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite.

527. For a root not ending in a conjunct consonant, there is vṛddhi when a causative suffix follows.

Asaṃyogantassa dhātussa kārite pare vuddhi hotīti ukārassokāro vuddhi.

For a root not ending in a conjunct consonant, there is vṛddhi when a causative suffix follows; thus, for the vowel u, the vṛddhi is o.

Dhanaṃ coreti, corenti. Coresi, coretha. Coremi, corema. Ṇayappaccaye – corayati, corayanti. Corayasi, corayatha. Corayāmi, corayāma. Corayate, corayante. Corayase, corayavhe. Coraye, corayāmhe.

Dhanaṃ coreti (he steals wealth), corenti (they steal). Coresi (you steal), coretha (you all steal). Coremi (I steal), corema (we steal). With the ṇaya suffix: corayati (he steals), corayanti (they steal). Corayasi (you steal), corayatha (you all steal). Corayāmi (I steal), corayāma (we steal). Middle voice: corayate (he steals), corayante (they steal). Corayase (you steal), corayavhe (you all steal). Coraye (I steal), corayāmhe (we steal).

Kamme yappaccaye īkārāgamo, saralopādi ca, corīyate devadattena, corīyati, corīyanti iccādi.

In the passive, with the suffix ya, there is the augment ī, and elision of vowels, etc. For example: corīyate devadattena (it is stolen by Devadatta), corīyati (it is stolen), corīyanti (they are stolen), and so forth.

Coretu[M 0.0323], corentu. Corehi. Corayatu, corayantu. Coraya, corayāhi.

Coretu (let him steal), corentu (let them steal). Corehi (steal!). Corayatu (let him steal), corayantu (let them steal). Coraya, corayāhi (steal!).

Coreyya, coreyyuṃ. Coraye, corayeyyuṃ. Acoresi, coresi, acoresuṃ, coresuṃ. Acorayi, corayi, acorayiṃsu, corayiṃsu, acorayuṃ, corayuṃ. Acoresi, acoresittha. Tvaṃ acorayi, acorayittha. Acoresiṃ, acoresimha. Acorayiṃ, acorayimha. Acorayittha. Acorīyittha, acorīyi.

Coreyya (he would steal), coreyyuṃ (they would steal). Coraye (he would steal), corayeyyuṃ (they would steal). Aorist: acoresi, coresi (he stole); acoresuṃ, coresuṃ (they stole). Acorayi, corayi (he stole); acorayiṃsu, corayiṃsu, acorayuṃ, corayuṃ (they stole). Acoresi (you stole), acoresittha (you all stole). Tvaṃ acorayi (you stole), acorayittha (you all stole). Acoresiṃ (I stole), acoresimha (we stole). Acorayiṃ (I stole), acorayimha (we stole). Acorayittha (you all stole). Acorīyittha, acorīyi (it was stolen).

Corissati, corissanti. Corayissati, corayissanti. Corīyissate, corīyissante. Corīyissati, corīyissanti. Acorissa, acorayissa. Acorīyissatha, acorīyissa iccādi.

Corissati (he will steal), corissanti (they will steal). Corayissati (he will steal), corayissanti (they will steal). Middle Passive Future: corīyissate (it will be stolen), corīyissante (they will be stolen). Active Passive Future: corīyissati (it will be stolen), corīyissanti (they will be stolen). Conditional: acorissa (he would have stolen), acorayissa (he would have stolen). Passive Conditional: acorīyissatha (it would have been stolen), acorīyissa (it would have been stolen), and so forth.

Tathā cinta cintāyaṃ, saṃyogantattā vuddhiabhāvova viseso.

Similarly, for the root cint in the sense of 'thinking', the special feature is only the absence of vṛddhi because it ends in a conjunct consonant.

Cinteti, cintayati, cintenti, cintayanti. Cintetu, cintayatu. Cinteyya, cintayeyya. Acintesi, cintesi, acintayi, cintayi. Cintessati, cintayissati. Acintissa, acintayissa iccādi.

Cinteti, cintayati (he thinks); cintenti, cintayanti (they think). Cintetu, cintayatu (let him think). Cinteyya, cintayeyya (he would think). Acintesi, cintesi, acintayi, cintayi (he thought). Cintessati, cintayissati (he will think). Acintissa, acintayissa (he would have thought), and so forth.

Manta guttabhāsane, manteti, mantayati iccādi purimasamaṃ.

The root mant in the sense of 'secret speech' or 'counsel': manteti (he advises), mantayati (he counsels), etc., are formed as before.

Pāla rakkhaṇe, dhammaṃ pāleti, pālayati. Pālīyati. Pāletu, pālayatu iccādi.

The root pāl in the sense of 'protecting': dhammaṃ pāleti (he protects the Dhamma), pālayati (he protects). Pālīyati (it is protected). Pāletu (let him protect), pālayatu (let him protect), and so forth.

Ghaṭa ghaṭane, ghāṭeti, ghāṭayati, ghaṭeti, ghaṭayati, ghaṭādittā vikappena vuddhi.

'Ghaṭa' in the sense of 'striving' or 'joining' (ghaṭane): 'ghāṭeti' (he strives/joins), 'ghāṭayati' (he strives/joins), 'ghaṭeti' (he strives/joins), 'ghaṭayati' (he strives/joins). Augmentation (vuddhi) occurs optionally due to its being in the Ghaṭādi group.

Vida ñāṇe, vedeti, vedayati.

'Vida' in the sense of 'knowing' (ñāṇe): 'vedeti' (he knows/feels), 'vedayati' (he knows/feels).

Gaṇa [M 0.0324] saṅkhyāne, “ghaṭādīnaṃ vā”ti na vuddhi, gaṇeti, gaṇayati iccādi, sabbattha subodhaṃ.

'Gaṇa' in the sense of 'counting' (saṅkhyāne): by 'ghaṭādīnaṃ vā', there is no augmentation (vuddhi), thus 'gaṇeti' (he counts), 'gaṇayati' (he counts), and so forth. All this is easily understood.

Curādigaṇo.

The Curādi Group.

Bhūvādī ca rudhādī ca, divādī svādayo gaṇā;

Kiyādī ca tanādī ca, curādī cidha sattadhā.

The Bhūvādi and Rudhādi, and the Divādi and Svādi groups; the Kiyādi and Tanādi, and the Curādi groups—here they are sevenfold.

Vikaraṇavidhānaṃ samattaṃ.

The section on Vikaraṇa (conjugational signs) is complete.

Dhātuppaccayantanaya

The Method of Stems with Root-Suffixes

Atha dhātuppaccayantā vuccante.

Now, stems ending in root-suffixes are explained.

Tattha dhātvatthe niddiṭṭhā khādikāritantā paccayā dhātuppaccayā nāma.

Therein, suffixes such as `kha`, and those ending in `kārita`, which are prescribed in the sense of a root, are called root-suffixes.

Tija nisāna bandhanakhamāsu, dhātusaññādi.

'Tija' in the senses of 'sharpening' (nisāna), 'binding' (bandhana), and 'enduring' (khamāsu); the designation as a root, and so forth, applies.

“Dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā”ti ito dhātuggahaṇaṃ anuvattate, “parā, paccayā”ti ca adhikāro.

From 'Dhātuliṅgehi parā paccayā' ('Suffixes follow roots and nominal stems'), the term 'dhātu' (root) is carried forward, and 'parā' (following) and 'paccayā' (suffixes) are governing rules.

528. Tija gupa kita mānehi kha cha sā vā.

528. From 'tij', 'gup', 'kit', and 'mān', the suffixes `kha`, `cha`, and `sa` optionally occur.

Tija gupa kita māna iccetehi dhātūhi kha cha sa iccete paccayā parā honti vā.

From these roots, 'tij', 'gup', 'kit', and 'mān', these suffixes, `kha`, `cha`, and `sa`, optionally follow.

Tijato khantiyaṃ khova, nindāyaṃ gupato tu cho;

Kitā cho sova mānamhā, vavatthitavibhāsato.

From 'tij', the suffix `kha` indeed applies in the sense of 'endurance' (khantiyaṃ); from 'gup', the suffix `cha` indeed applies in the sense of 'censure' (nindāyaṃ); from 'kit', `cha`, and from 'mān', `sa` indeed apply, due to this being a fixed option (vavatthitavibhāsā).

“Kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo”ti dhātvādissa dvibhāvo.

By 'Kvacādivaṇṇānamekassarānaṃ dvebhāvo' ('Doubling of single-vowel initial sounds of roots beginning with kva, etc.'), the initial part of the root is doubled.

“Byañjanantassā”ti vattamāne –

When 'Byañjanantassa' ('of that which ends in a consonant') is current—

529. Ko khe ca.

529. And the final consonant becomes `ka` before `kha`.

Dhātvantassa [M 0.0325] byañjanassa kakārādeso hoti khappaccaye pare.

The consonant at the end of a root is substituted by `ka` when the `kha` suffix follows.

Titikkha iti ṭhite –

When the form is 'titikkha'—

Dhātuvihitānaṃ tyādivibhattīnaṃ adhātuto appavattiyamāha.

It is stated that inflections such as `ti`, which are prescribed for roots, do not apply after that which is not a root.

530. Dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo.

530. Inflections follow root-suffixes.

Dhātvatthe niddiṭṭhehi khādikāritantehi paccayehi tyādayo vibhattiyo hontīti pure viya vattamānādayo yojetabbā.

After suffixes such as `kha` and those ending in `kārita`, which are prescribed in the sense of a root, the inflections beginning with `ti` occur. Thus, the present tense and so forth should be applied as before.

Ativākyaṃ titikkhati, titikkhanti. Kamme titikkhīyati. Tathā titikkhatu, titikkhantu. Titikkheyya, titikkheyyuṃ. Atitikkhi, atitikkhiṃsu. Titikkhissati. Atitikkhissa iccādi.

'He endures excessive speech' (ativākyaṃ titikkhati), 'they endure' (titikkhanti). In the passive: 'it is endured' (titikkhīyati). Similarly: 'let him endure' (titikkhatu), 'let them endure' (titikkhantu); 'he would endure' (titikkheyya), 'they would endure' (titikkheyyuṃ); 'he endured' (atitikkhi), 'they endured' (atitikkhiṃsu); 'he will endure' (titikkhissati); 'he would have endured' (atitikkhissa), and so forth.

Khappaccayābhāve appaccayassa ekāro, tejeti, tejati vā, tejanti iccādi.

In the absence of the `kha` suffix, the `a` suffix becomes `e`: 'tejeti' (he sharpens), or 'tejati' (he sharpens), 'tejanti' (they sharpen), and so forth.

Gupa gopane, chappaccaye dvibhāvo, “pubbobbhāso”ti abbhāsasaññā, “abbhāsassā”ti vattamāne “antassivaṇṇākāro vā”ti abbhāsantassikāro, “kavaggassa cavaggo”ti abbhāsagakārassa jakāro ca.

'Gup' in the sense of 'protecting' (gopane): when the `cha` suffix follows, doubling occurs. By 'pubbobbhāso', the reduplicated syllable is designated 'abbhāsa'. When 'abbhāsassa' ('of the reduplicated syllable') is current, by 'antassivaṇṇākāro vā', the final vowel of the reduplicated syllable becomes `i`. And by 'kavaggassa cavaggo', the `g` of the reduplicated syllable becomes `j`.

531. Byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu ca.

531. And the final consonant of a root becomes `ca` when the `cha` suffixes follow.

Dhātvanthassa byañjanassa cakārādeso hoti chappaccayesu paresu. Tato vibhattiyo, kāyaṃ jigucchati, jigucchanti. Sesaṃ purimasamaṃ. Chābhāve gopeti, gopenti iccādi.

The consonant at the end of a root is substituted by `ca` when the `cha` suffixes follow. Then the inflections are added: 'he abhors the body' (kāyaṃ jigucchati), 'they abhor' (jigucchanti). The rest is the same as before. In the absence of `cha`: 'gopeti' (he protects), 'gopenti' (they protect), and so forth.

Kita rogāpanayane, chappaccayo, dvittañca.

'Kit' in the sense of 'removing illness' (rogāpanayane): the `cha` suffix is added, and doubling occurs.

Abbhāsaggahaṇamanuvattate[M 0.0326].

The term 'abbhāsa' (reduplicated syllable) is carried forward.

532. Mānakitānaṃ vatattaṃ vā.

532. For `māna` and `kita`, the substitution of `t` optionally occurs.

Abbhāsagatānaṃ māna kitaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ vakāratakārattaṃ hoti vā yathākkamanti takāro, dhātvantassa cakāro, sesaṃ samaṃ. Rogaṃ tikicchati, tikicchanti iccādi. Takārābhāve “kavaggassa cavaggo”ti cakāro, vicikicchati, vicikicchanti iccādi.

For these roots 'māna' and 'kita' which have undergone reduplication, the substitutions 'va' and 'ta' optionally occur respectively. The substitution of 'ta' occurs, and for the end of the root, the substitution of 'ca' occurs. The rest is the same. For example, 'he treats illness' (rogaṃ tikicchati), 'they treat' (tikicchanti), and so forth. In the absence of the 'ta' substitution, by the rule 'kavaggassa cavaggo' ('the ka-group becomes the ca-group'), the substitution of 'ca' occurs, as in 'he doubts' (vicikicchati), 'they doubt' (vicikicchanti), and so forth.

Māna vīmaṃsapūjāsu, sappaccayadvibhāvaīkāravakārā.

For the root 'māna' in the senses of 'investigation' (vīmaṃsa) and 'veneration' (pūjā): the 'sa' suffix, reduplication, and the substitutions 'ī' and 'va' occur.

533. Tato pāmānānaṃ vā maṃ sesu.

533. Then, 'vā' and 'maṃ' are substituted for 'pā' and 'māna' respectively when 'sa' follows.

Tato abbhāsato parāsaṃ pāmānānaṃ dhātūnaṃ vāmaṃiccete ādesā honti yathākkamaṃ sappaccaye pare. Sesūti bahuvacananiddeso payogepi vacanavipallāsañāpanatthaṃ. Atthaṃ vīmaṃsati, vīmaṃsanti iccādi.

Then, after the reduplicated syllable, for the roots 'pā' and 'māna', these substitutions 'vā' and 'maṃ' occur respectively when the 'sa' suffix follows. The plural designation 'sesu' is to indicate the change of number even in usage. For example, 'he investigates the meaning' (atthaṃ vīmaṃsati), 'they investigate' (vīmaṃsanti), and so forth.

Aññattha “lopañcettamakāro”ti appaccayassekāro, māneti, mānenti.

Elsewhere, by the rule 'lopañcettamakāro', the 'a' suffix becomes 'e', as in 'māneti' (he honors), 'mānenti' (they honor).

Bhuja pālanabyavaharaṇesu, bhottumicchatīti atthe –

For the root 'bhuja' in the senses of 'protecting' (pālana) and 'using' or 'eating' (byavaharaṇa); and in the sense of 'desiring to eat' (bhottumicchatīti atthe) –

“Kha cha sā, vā”ti ca vattate.

And the rule 'kha, cha, sā, vā' (the suffixes kha, cha, sa occur optionally) is carried forward.

534. Bhuja ghasa hara su pādīhi tumicchatthesu.

534. From the roots 'bhuja', 'ghasa', 'hara', 'su', 'pā', and so forth, in the desiderative sense.

Bhuja ghasa hara su pā iccevamādīhi dhātūhi tumicchatthesu ca kha cha saiccete paccayā honti vā. Tumicchānaṃ, tumantayuttaicchāya vā atthā tumicchatthā, tena tumantarahitesu “bhojanamicchatī”tiādīsu na honti, “vuttatthānamappayogo”ti vākyassa appayogo, dhātvādissa dvebhāve kate [M 0.0327] “dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā”ti abbhāsabhakārassa bakāro, dhātvantassa “ko khe cā”ti kakāro, bubhukkhati, bubhukkhanti iccādi.

From these roots 'bhuja', 'ghasa', 'hara', 'su', 'pā', and so forth, these suffixes 'kha', 'cha', and 'sa' optionally occur in the desiderative sense. The desiderative senses are those of wishing connected with 'tum', or wishing associated with the affix 'tum'. Therefore, they do not occur in contexts lacking 'tum', such as 'bhojanam icchati' ('he wishes for food'), etc.; or, because 'what has been stated is not repeated' (vuttatthānamappayogo), the full phrase is not used. When doubling of the root initial occurs, by the rule 'dutiyacatutthānaṃ paṭhamatatiyā' ('the first and third for the second and fourth'), the 'bha' of the reduplicated syllable becomes 'ba'. For the root-ending, by the rule 'ko khe cā', 'ka' is substituted, as in 'he desires to eat' (bubhukkhati), 'they desire to eat' (bubhukkhanti), and so forth.

Vāti kimatthaṃ? Bhottumicchati, icchatthesūti kimatthaṃ? Bhottuṃ gacchati.

What is the purpose of 'vā' (optionally)? For the form 'bhottum icchati' (he desires to eat). What is the purpose of 'in the desiderative sense' (icchatthesu)? To exclude cases like 'bhottuṃ gacchati' (he goes to eat).

Ghasa adane, ghasitumicchatīti atthe chappaccayo, dvittaṃ, tatiya cavagga ikāra cakārādesā, jighacchati, jighacchanti.

For the root 'ghasa' in the sense of 'eating' (adane): in the sense of 'desiring to eat' (ghasitumicchatīti atthe), the 'cha' suffix occurs, along with reduplication, and the substitutions of the third consonant of the ca-group, 'i', and 'ca', as in 'he is hungry' (jighacchati), 'they are hungry' (jighacchanti).

Hara haraṇe, haritumicchatīti atthe sappaccayo.

For the root 'hara' in the sense of 'carrying' (haraṇe): in the sense of 'desiring to carry' (haritumicchatīti atthe), the 'sa' suffix occurs.

535. Harassa gī se.

535. For 'hara', 'gī' is substituted when 'sa' follows.

Haraiccetassa dhātussa sabbassa gī hoti se paccaye pare. “Gīse”ti yogavibhāgena jissapi, ṭhānūpacārenādesassāpi dhātuvohārattā dvittaṃ, bhikkhaṃ jigīsati, jigīsanti.

For this entire root 'hara', 'gī' is substituted when the 'sa' suffix follows. By splitting the rule ('yogavibhāga') 'Gīse', this also applies to the root 'ji'. Doubling occurs because the substitute is also treated as a root by metaphorical extension. For example, 'he desires to obtain alms' (bhikkhaṃ jigīsati), 'they desire to obtain' (jigīsanti).

Su savaṇe, sotumicchati sussūsati, sussūsanti, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dīgho.

For the root 'su' in the sense of 'hearing' (savaṇe): 'sotum icchati' (he desires to hear) becomes 'sussūsati', 'sussūsanti'. By the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., lengthening occurs.

Pā pāne, pātumicchatīti atthe sappaccayadvittarassattaikārādesā, “tato pāmānānaṃ vāmaṃ sesū”ti vādeso, pivāsati, pivāsanti iccādi.

For the root 'pā' in the sense of 'drinking' (pāne): in the sense of 'desiring to drink' (pātumicchatīti atthe), the 'sa' suffix, reduplication, shortening, and the substitution of 'i' occur. By the rule 'tato pāmānānaṃ vāmaṃ sesū' ('then for pā and māna, vā and maṃ when sa follows'), the substitution of 'vā' occurs, as in 'he desires to drink' (pivāsati), 'they desire to drink' (pivāsanti), and so forth.

Ji jaye, vijetumicchati vijigīsati iccādi.

For the root 'ji' in the sense of 'conquering' (jaye): 'vijetum icchati' (he desires to conquer) becomes 'vijigīsati', and so forth.

Saṅgho pabbatamiva attānamācarati, pabbato iva ācaratīti vā atthe –

In the sense that 'the Saṅgha behaves like a mountain' (saṅgho pabbatamiva attānamācarati), or 'he behaves like a mountain' (pabbato iva ācarati) –

536. Āya nāmato kattupamānādācāre.

536. The suffix 'āya' occurs after a noun that is a standard of comparison for the agent, in the sense of 'behaving like'.

Ācaraṇakriyāya kattuno upamānabhūtamhā nāmato āyappaccayo hoti ācāratthe. Upamīyati etenāti [M 0.0328] upamānaṃ, kattuno upamānaṃ kattupamānaṃ, “vuttatthānamappayogo”ti ivasaddanivatti, dhātuppaccayantattā “tesaṃ vibhattiyo lopā cā”ti sutte tesaṃgahaṇena vibhattilopo, “pakati cassa sarantassā”ti pakatibhāvo, saralopādi, “dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo”ti vibhattuppatti, pabbatāyati saṅgho, evaṃ samuddamiva attānamācarati samuddāyati, cicciṭamiva attānamācarati cicciṭāyati saddo. Evaṃ dhūmāyati.

The suffix 'āya' occurs after a noun that is a standard of comparison for the agent of the action of behaving, in the sense of 'behaving like'. 'Upamāna' (standard of comparison) is that by which something is compared. 'Kattupamāna' is a standard of comparison for the agent. The word 'iva' (like) is omitted by the principle 'vuttatthānamappayogo' ('what has been stated is not repeated'). Because it ends with a root-suffix, the case inflection is elided by the term 'tesaṃ' in the rule 'tesaṃ vibhattiyo lopā cā'. By 'pakati cassa sarantassā', it remains in its natural state, and vowel elision, etc., occur. By 'dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo', a verbal inflection is added. For example, 'the Saṅgha behaves like a mountain' (pabbatāyati saṅgho). Similarly, from 'samuddamiva attānamācarati', 'he behaves like the ocean' (samuddāyati). From 'cicciṭamiva attānamācarati', 'the sound crackles' (cicciṭāyati saddo). Likewise, 'it smokes' (dhūmāyati).

“Nāmato, ācāre”ti ca vattate.

And the words 'nāmato' (from a noun) and 'ācāre' (in the sense of behaving like) are carried forward.

537. Īyūpamānā ca.

537. And the suffix 'īya' occurs after a standard of comparison.

Upamānabhūtā nāmato īyappaccayo hoti ācāratthe. Puna upamānaggahaṇaṃ kattuggahaṇanivattanatthaṃ, tena kammatopi sijjhati, sesaṃ samaṃ. Achattaṃ chattamivācarati chattīyati, aputtaṃ puttamivācarati puttīyati sissamācariyo.

The suffix 'īya' occurs after a noun that is a standard of comparison, in the sense of 'acting like'. The repeated mention of 'upamāna' is to exclude the agent; therefore, it is also formed from the object. The rest is the same. He treats a non-umbrella like an umbrella: 'chattīyati'. A teacher treats a pupil, who is not his son, like a son: 'puttīyati'.

Upamānāti kiṃ? Dhammamācarati, ācāreti kiṃ? Achattaṃ chattamiva rakkhati.

Why is 'standard of comparison' stated? To prevent application in cases like 'dhammam ācarati' (he practices the Dhamma). Why is 'in the sense of behaving like' stated? To prevent application in cases like 'achattaṃ chattamiva rakkhati' (he protects a non-umbrella as if it were an umbrella).

“Īyo”ti vattate.

The suffix 'īya' is carried forward.

538. Nāmamhātticchatthe.

538. After a noun, in the sense of desiring for oneself.

Nāmamhā attano icchatthe īyappaccayo hoti. Attano pattamicchati pattīyati, evaṃ vatthīyati, parikkhārīyati, cīvarīyati, paṭīyati, dhanīyati, puttīyati.

After a noun, the suffix 'īya' occurs in the sense of desiring for oneself. 'He desires a bowl for himself' becomes 'pattīyati'; similarly, 'vatthīyati' (he desires cloth), 'parikkhārīyati' (he desires requisites), 'cīvarīyati' (he desires a robe), 'paṭīyati' (he desires a cloth), 'dhanīyati' (he desires wealth), 'puttīyati' (he desires a son).

Atticchattheti kimatthaṃ? Aññassa pattamicchati.

Why is 'in the sense of desiring for oneself' stated? To prevent application in a case like 'aññassa pattam icchati' (he desires another's bowl).

Daḷhaṃ karoti vīriyanti atthe –

In the sense of 'he makes effort firm' (daḷhaṃ karoti vīriyaṃ) –

Kāritaggahaṇamanuvattate.

The mention of 'kārita' (causative) is carried forward.

539. Dhāturūpe [M 0.0329] nāmasmā ṇayoca.

539. From a noun, the suffix ṇaya is also applied to form a verbal root.

Dhātuyā rūpe nipphādetabbe, “taṃ karoti, tena atikkamati”iccādike payujjitabbe vā sati nāmamhā ṇayappaccayo hoti, kāritasaññā ca. Ṇalope, vibhattilopasaralopādīsu katesu vibhattuppatti, daḷhayati vīriyaṃ, evaṃ pamāṇayati, amissayati, tathā hatthinā atikkamati atihatthayati, vīṇāya upagāyati upavīṇayati, visuddhā hoti ratti visuddhayati, kusalaṃ pucchati kusalayati iccādi.

When a form of a verbal root is to be produced, or when expressions such as 'he does it,' 'he surpasses with it,' and so on, are to be used, the suffix ṇaya occurs after a noun, and it also has the causative designation. After the elision of ṇa, the elision of case endings, the elision of vowels, and so on, have been performed, the verbal inflections are applied. For example: `daḷhayati vīriyaṃ` (he makes effort firm); likewise, `pamāṇayati` (he measures), `amissayati` (he mixes). Similarly, from `hatthinā atikkamati` (he surpasses with an elephant) comes `atihatthayati`; from `vīṇāya upagāyati` (he sings along with a lute) comes `upavīṇayati`; from `visuddhā hoti ratti` (the night becomes pure) comes `visuddhayati`; from `kusalaṃ pucchati` (he asks about what is skillful) comes `kusalayati`, and so on.

540. Dhātūhi ṇe ṇaya ṇāpe ṇāpayā kāritāni hetvatthe.

540. From roots, the suffixes ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, and ṇāpaya are causative in the sense of cause.

Sabbehi dhātūhi hetvatthe abhidheyye ṇe ṇayaṇāpe ṇāpaya iccete paccayā parā honti, te kāritasaññā ca honti. Hetuyeva attho hetvattho, so ca “yo kāreti sa hetū”ti laddhahetusañño suddhakattuno payojako hetukattā, atthato pesanajjhesanādiko payojakabyāpāro idha hetu nāma.

From all roots, when the sense of cause (hetvattha) is to be expressed, these suffixes—ṇe, ṇaya, ṇāpe, and ṇāpaya—are appended, and they also have the causative (kārita) designation. The sense of cause (hetvattha) is simply the meaning of 'hetu' (cause). And that 'hetu' is the instigator (payojaka) of the agent (kattu), which has received the designation 'hetu' from the statement, 'He who causes is the cause.' In essence, the activity of the instigator, such as sending or urging, is here called 'hetu'.

Ettha ca –

And here:

Ṇe ṇayāva uvaṇṇantā, āto dve pacchimā siyuṃ;

Sesato caturo dve vā, vāsaddassānuvattito.

After roots ending in `u` or `ū`, only `ṇe` and `ṇaya` occur. After roots ending in `ā`, the last two (`ṇāpe`, `ṇāpaya`) may occur. After the remaining roots, either all four or the first two may occur, due to the continuation of the word `vā` (optionally).

Akammā dhātavo honti, kārite tu sakammakā;

Sakammakā dvikammāssu, dvikammā tu tikammakā.

Intransitive roots become transitive in the causative; transitive roots become ditransitive, and ditransitive roots become tritransitive.

Tasmā kattari kamme ca, kāritākhyātasambhavo;

Na bhāve suddhakattā ca, kārite kammasaññito.

Therefore, a causative finite verb may occur in the active (kattari) and passive (kamme) voices, but not in the impersonal (bhāve) voice. And in the causative, the original agent (kattu) is designated as the object (kamma).

Niyādīnaṃ [M 0.0330] padhānañca, appadhānaṃ duhādinaṃ;

Kārite suddhakattā ca, kammamākhyātagocaranti.

For roots like `nī` (to lead), the primary object is retained, and for roots like `duh` (to milk), the secondary object is retained. In the causative, the agent and the object are within the scope of the finite verb.

Tattha yo koci bhavati, tamañño “bhavāhi bhavāhi” iccevaṃ bravīti, atha vā bhavantaṃ bhavituṃ samatthaṃ payojayati, bhavituṃ payojetīti vā atthe iminā ṇeṇayappaccayā, kāritasaññā ca, “vuttatthānamappayogo”ti vākyassa appayogo, “kāritānaṃ ṇo lopa”nti ṇalopo, “asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite”ti ūkārassokāro vuddhi.

In this case, someone exists, and another tells him, 'Be! Be!' thus he speaks; or he employs one who is capable of being; or in the sense of 'he causes to be', by this rule the suffixes ṇe and ṇaya are applied, and they also have the causative designation. The original phrase is not used, according to the principle 'what is already expressed is not used'. The elision of `ṇ` occurs by the rule '`kāritānaṃ ṇo lopa`'. The strengthening (`vuddhi`) of the vowel `u` to `o` occurs by the rule '`asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite`'.

“O, e”ti ca vattate, dhātuggahaṇañca.

And the terms 'o' and 'e' are carried forward, as is the specification 'of a root'.

541. Te āvāyā kārite.

541. Those vowels, 'o' and 'e', become 'āva' and 'āya' respectively when a causative suffix follows.

Te dhātvantabhūtā okārekārā āvaāyādese pāpuṇanti kārite pare. “Te āvāyā”ti yogavibhāgena jheādīnaṃ akāritepi hontīti okārassa āvādeso, saralopādi, “dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo”ti tyādayo.

Those vowels `o` and `e` which are at the end of a root are replaced by `āva` and `āya` respectively when a causative suffix follows. By splitting the rule `Te āvāyā`, for roots like `jhe`, etc., these substitutions also occur even when a non-causative suffix follows; thus, the vowel `o` is replaced by `āva`, followed by vowel elision, etc. Then, inflections such as `ti` are applied by the rule `dhātuppaccayehi vibhattiyo`.

So samādhiṃ bhāveti, bhāvayati, bhāventi, bhāvayanti. Bhāvesi, bhāvayasi, bhāvetha, bhāvayatha. Bhāvemi, bhāvayāmi, bhāvema, bhāvayāma. Bhāvayate, bhāvayante.

`So samādhiṃ bhāveti` (He develops concentration), `bhāvayati`. `Bhāventi`, `bhāvayanti`. `Bhāvesi`, `bhāvayasi`. `Bhāvetha`, `bhāvayatha`. `Bhāvemi`, `bhāvayāmi`. `Bhāvema`, `bhāvayāma`. (Middle voice:) `Bhāvayate`, `bhāvayante`.

Kamme attanopadayappaccayaīkārāgamā, saralopādi ca, tena bhāvīyate samādhi, bhāvīyante. Bhāvīyati, bhāvīyanti.

In the passive (`kamme`), the middle voice (`attanopada`) suffixes, the suffix `ya`, and the augment `ī` are applied, along with vowel elision, etc. By this process: `bhāvīyate samādhi` (concentration is developed), `bhāvīyante` (they are developed). Also: `bhāvīyati` (it is developed), `bhāvīyanti` (they are developed).

Tathā bhāvetu, bhāvayatu, bhāventu, bhāvayantu. Bhāvehi, bhāvaya, bhāvayāhi, bhāvetha, bhāvayatha[M 0.0331]. Bhāvemi, bhāvayāmi, bhāvema, bhāvayāma. Bhāvayataṃ, bhāvayantaṃ.

Similarly (in the imperative): `bhāvetu`, `bhāvayatu`; `bhāventu`, `bhāvayantu`. `Bhāvehi`, `bhāvaya`, `bhāvayāhi`. `Bhāvetha`, `bhāvayatha`. `Bhāvemi`, `bhāvayāmi`. `Bhāvema`, `bhāvayāma`. (Middle voice:) `Bhāvayataṃ`, `bhāvayantaṃ`.

Kamme bhāvīyataṃ, bhāvīyatu, bhāvīyantu.

In the passive: `bhāvīyataṃ`, `bhāvīyatu`, `bhāvīyantu`.

Bhāveyya, bhāvaye, bhāvayeyya, bhāveyyuṃ, bhāvayeyyuṃ. Bhāveyyāsi, bhāvayeyyāsi, bhāveyyātha, bhāvayeyyātha. Bhāveyyāmi, bhāvayeyyāmi, bhāveyyāma, bhāvayeyyāma. Bhāvetha, bhāvayetha, bhāveraṃ, bhāvayeraṃ.

(Optative:) `Bhāveyya`, `bhāvaye`, `bhāvayeyya`; `bhāveyyuṃ`, `bhāvayeyyuṃ`. `Bhāveyyāsi`, `bhāvayeyyāsi`; `bhāveyyātha`, `bhāvayeyyātha`. `Bhāveyyāmi`, `bhāvayeyyāmi`; `bhāveyyāma`, `bhāvayeyyāma`. (Middle voice:) `Bhāvetha`, `bhāvayetha`; `bhāveraṃ`, `bhāvayeraṃ`.

Kamme bhāvīyeyya, bhāvīyeyyuṃ.

In the passive: `bhāvīyeyya`, `bhāvīyeyyuṃ`.

Ajjataniyaṃ “sattamajjatanimhī”ti yogavibhāgena kāritantāpi dīghato sakārāgamo.

In the Aorist, by splitting the rule '`sattamajjatanimhī`', the augment `s` also occurs after a long vowel of a causative stem.

Abhāvesi, bhāvesi, abhāvayi, bhāvayi, abhāvesuṃ, bhāvesuṃ, abhāvayiṃsu, bhāvayiṃsu, abhāvayuṃ, bhāvayuṃ. Abhāvesi, abhāvayasi, abhāvittha, abhāvayittha. Abhāvesiṃ, bhāvesiṃ, abhāvayiṃ, bhāvayiṃ, abhāvimha, abhāvayimha.

(Aorist:) `Abhāvesi`, `bhāvesi`, `abhāvayi`, `bhāvayi`. `Abhāvesuṃ`, `bhāvesuṃ`, `abhāvayiṃsu`, `bhāvayiṃsu`, `abhāvayuṃ`, `bhāvayuṃ`. `Abhāvesi`, `abhāvayasi`. `Abhāvittha`, `abhāvayittha`. `Abhāvesiṃ`, `bhāvesiṃ`, `abhāvayiṃ`, `bhāvayiṃ`. `Abhāvimha`, `abhāvayimha`.

Kamme abhāvīyittha, abhāvīyi.

In the passive: `abhāvīyittha` (you all were developed), `abhāvīyi` (it was developed).

Bhāvessati, bhāvayissati, bhāvessanti, bhāvayissanti. Bhāvessasi, bhāvayissasi, bhāvissatha, bhāvayissatha. Bhāvessāmi, bhāvayissāmi, bhāvessāma, bhāvayissāma.

(Future:) `Bhāvessati`, `bhāvayissati`; `bhāvessanti`, `bhāvayissanti`. `Bhāvessasi`, `bhāvayissasi`; `bhāvissatha`, `bhāvayissatha`. `Bhāvessāmi`, `bhāvayissāmi`; `bhāvessāma`, `bhāvayissāma`.

Kamme bhāvīyissate, bhāvīyissante. Bhāvīyissati, bhāvīyissanti.

In the passive: `bhāvīyissate` (middle), `bhāvīyissante` (middle). `Bhāvīyissati` (active), `bhāvīyissanti` (active).

Abhāvissa, abhāvayissa, abhāvissaṃsu, abhāvayissaṃsu. Kamme abhāvīyissatha, abhāvīyissa iccādi.

(Conditional:) `Abhāvissa`, `abhāvayissa`; `abhāvissaṃsu`, `abhāvayissaṃsu`. In the passive: `abhāvīyissatha`, `abhāvīyissa`, and so on.

Tathā [M 0.0332] yo koci pacati, tamañño “pacāhi pacāhi” iccevaṃ bravīti, atha vā pacantaṃ payojeti, pacituṃ vā payojetīti atthe vuttanayena ṇe ṇayādayo, akārassākāro vuddhi, sesaṃ neyyaṃ.

Similarly, someone cooks, and another tells him, 'Cook! Cook!' thus he speaks; or he employs one who is cooking, or in the sense of 'he causes to cook', by the method stated, the suffixes ṇe, ṇaya, etc., are applied; the strengthening (`vuddhi`) of the vowel `a` is `ā`; the rest is to be understood.

So devadattaṃ odanaṃ pāceti, pācenti. Pācesi, pācetha. Pācemi, pācema. Pācayati, pācayanti. Pācayasi, pācayatha. Pācayāmi, pācayāma. Ṇāpeṇāpayesu pana so puriso taṃ purisaṃ odanaṃ pācāpeti, pācāpenti. Pācāpayati, pācāpayanti.

`So devadattaṃ odanaṃ pāceti` (He makes Devadatta cook rice). `Pācenti`. `Pācesi`, `pācetha`. `Pācemi`, `pācema`. (With `ṇaya`:) `Pācayati`, `pācayanti`. `Pācayasi`, `pācayatha`. `Pācayāmi`, `pācayāma`. With `ṇāpe` and `ṇāpaya`, however: `so puriso taṃ purisaṃ odanaṃ pācāpeti` (that man makes that man cook rice), `pācāpenti`. `Pācāpayati`, `pācāpayanti`.

Kamme so odanaṃ pācīyati tena, pācayīyati, pācāpīyati, pācāpayīyati.

In the passive: `so odanaṃ pācīyati tena` (that rice is caused to be cooked by him). Alternative forms are `pācayīyati`, `pācāpīyati`, and `pācāpayīyati`.

Tathā pācetu, pācayatu, pācāpetu, pācāpayatu. Pācīyataṃ, pācīyatu, pācayīyataṃ, pācayīyatu, pācāpīyataṃ, pācāpīyatu, pācāpayīyataṃ, pācāpayīyatu. Pāceyya, pācayeyya, pācāpeyya, pācāpayeyya. Pācīyeyya, pācīyeyyuṃ. Apācesi, apācayi, apācāpesi, apācāpayi. Pācessati, pācayissati, pācāpessati, pācāpayissati. Apācissa, apācayissa, apācāpissa, apācāpayissa iccādi.

Similarly (the other tense-mood forms are): (Imperative:) `pācetu`, `pācayatu`, `pācāpetu`, `pācāpayatu`. (Passive Imperative:) `pācīyataṃ`, `pācīyatu`; `pācayīyataṃ`, `pācayīyatu`; `pācāpīyataṃ`, `pācāpīyatu`; `pācāpayīyataṃ`, `pācāpayīyatu`. (Optative:) `pāceyya`, `pācayeyya`, `pācāpeyya`, `pācāpayeyya`. (Passive Optative:) `pācīyeyya`, `pācīyeyyuṃ`. (Aorist:) `apācesi`, `apācayi`, `apācāpesi`, `apācāpayi`. (Future:) `pācessati`, `pācayissati`, `pācāpessati`, `pācāpayissati`. (Conditional:) `apācissa`, `apācayissa`, `apācāpissa`, `apācāpayissa`, and so on.

Gacchantaṃ, gantuṃ vā payojetīti atthe ṇe ṇayādayo, vuddhiyaṃ sampattāyaṃ –

In the sense of 'he employs one who is going' (`gacchantaṃ payojeti`) or 'he employs someone to go' (`gantuṃ payojeti`), the suffixes ṇe, ṇaya, etc., are applied; when strengthening (`vuddhi`) is to be applied –

“Asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite”ti vattate.

The rule 'asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite' (strengthening of the final vowel of a root not ending in a conjunct consonant when a causative suffix follows) is understood to apply.

542. Ghaṭādīnaṃ vā.

542. Or for the `ghaṭa` group of roots.

Ghaṭādīnaṃ dhātūnaṃ asaṃyogantānaṃ vuddhi hoti vā kāriteti ettha vāggahaṇena vuddhi na hoti, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

For roots of the `ghaṭa` group, which do not end in a conjunct consonant, strengthening (vuddhi) occurs optionally (vā) when a causative suffix follows. Here, by the inclusion of the word 'vā' (optionally), strengthening does not occur in some cases; this word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option (vavatthitavibhāsā).

So [M 0.0333] taṃ purisaṃ gāmaṃ gameti, gamayati, gacchāpeti, gacchāpayati. So gāmaṃ gamīyati tena, gamayīyati, gacchāpīyati, gacchāpayīyati iccādi. Sabbattha yojetabbaṃ. Evaṃ uparipi.

He makes that man go to the village: `gameti`, `gamayati`, `gacchāpeti`, `gacchāpayati`. The village is caused to be gone to by him: `gamīyati tena`, `gamayīyati`, `gacchāpīyati`, `gacchāpayīyati`, and so on. This should be applied in all cases, including the preceding examples.

Ghaṭa īhāyaṃ, ghaṭantaṃ payojayati, ghaṭeti, ghaṭādīnaṃ vāti na vuddhi, ghaṭayati, ghaṭāpeti, ghaṭāpayati.

The root `ghaṭa` is in the sense of striving. He employs one who strives: `ghaṭeti`. By the rule 'optionally for the `ghaṭa` group', there is no strengthening, hence `ghaṭayati`. Other forms are `ghaṭāpeti` and `ghaṭāpayati`.

“Kārite”ti vattate.

The term 'kārite' (when a causative suffix follows) is understood to apply.

543. Guha dusānaṃ dīghaṃ.

543. For the roots `guha` and `dusa`, the vowel becomes long.

Guhadusaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ saro dīghamāpajjate kārite pare, vuddhāpavādoyaṃ.

For these roots, `guha` and `dusa`, the vowel becomes long when a causative suffix follows. This is an exception to the strengthening (vuddhi) rule.

Guha saṃvaraṇe, guhituṃ payojayati gūhayati, gūhayanti. Dusa appītimhi, dussantaṃ payojayati dūsayati, dūsayanti iccādi.

The root `guha` is in the sense of concealing. He employs someone to conceal: `gūhayati` (he causes to conceal), `gūhayanti` (they cause to conceal). The root `dusa` is in the sense of displeasure. He employs one who is displeased: `dūsayati` (he causes displeasure), `dūsayanti` (they cause displeasure), and so on.

Tathā icchantaṃ payojayati icchāpeti, icchāpayati, eseti, esayati. Niyacchantaṃ payojayati niyāmeti, niyāmayati. Āsantaṃ payojayati āseti, āsayati, acchāpeti, acchāpayati. Labhantaṃ payojayati lābheti, lābhayati. Vacantaṃ payojayati vāceti, vācayati, vācāpeti, vācāpayati. Evaṃ vāseti, vāsayati, vāsāpeti, vāsāpayati. Vāheti, vāhayati, vāhāpeti, vāhāpayati. Jīreti, jīrayati, jīrāpeti, jīrāpayati. Māreti, mārayati, mārāpeti, mārāpayati. Dasseti, dassayati iccādi.

Likewise, he employs one who desires: `icchāpeti`, `icchāpayati` (he causes to desire); `eseti`, `esayati` (he causes to seek). He employs one who restrains: `niyāmeti`, `niyāmayati` (he causes to restrain). He employs one who sits: `āseti`, `āsayati`, `acchāpeti`, `acchāpayati` (he causes to sit). He employs one who obtains: `lābheti`, `lābhayati` (he causes to obtain). He employs one who speaks: `vāceti`, `vācayati`, `vācāpeti`, `vācāpayati` (he causes to speak). Similarly: `vāseti`, `vāsayati`, `vāsāpeti`, `vāsāpayati` (he causes to dwell); `vāheti`, `vāhayati`, `vāhāpeti`, `vāhāpayati` (he causes to carry); `jīreti`, `jīrayati`, `jīrāpeti`, `jīrāpayati` (he causes to grow old); `māreti`, `mārayati`, `mārāpeti`, `mārāpayati` (he causes to die); `dasseti`, `dassayati` (he shows), and so on.

Tathā tudantaṃ payojayati todeti, todayati, todāpeti, todāpayati. Pavisantaṃ payojayati, pavisituṃ vā paveseti, pavesayati, pavesāpeti[M 0.0334], pavesāpayati. Uddisantaṃ payojayati uddisāpeti, uddisāpayati. Pahontaṃ payojayati pahāveti, pahāvayati. Sayantaṃ payojayati sāyeti, sāyayati, sāyāpeti, sāyāpayati. Ettha ekārassa āyādeso, sayāpeti, sayāpayati, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ṇāpeṇāpayesu āyādesassa rassattaṃ. Nayantaṃ payojayati nayāpeti, nayāpayati. Patiṭṭhantaṃ payojayati patiṭṭhāpeti, patiṭṭhāpayati, patiṭṭhapeti vā.

Likewise, he employs one who pierces: `todeti`, `todayati`, `todāpeti`, `todāpayati`. He employs one who enters, or employs someone to enter: `paveseti`, `pavesayati`, `pavesāpeti`, `pavesāpayati`. He employs one who points out: `uddisāpeti`, `uddisāpayati`. He employs one who abandons: `pahāveti`, `pahāvayati`. He employs one who lies down: `sāyeti`, `sāyayati`, `sāyāpeti`, `sāyāpayati`. Here, for the `e` there is the substitution `āya`. In `sayāpeti` and `sayāpayati`, by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', there is shortening of the `āya` substitution before `ṇāpe` and `ṇāpaye`. He employs one who leads: `nayāpeti`, `nayāpayati`. He employs one who establishes: `patiṭṭhāpeti`, `patiṭṭhāpayati`, or `patiṭṭhapeti`.

Hanantaṃ payojayatīti atthe ṇeṇayādayo.

In the sense 'he employs one who kills', the causative suffixes `ṇe`, `ṇaya`, and so on, are applied.

“Ṇamhī”ti vattate.

The condition 'when a suffix with `ṇ` follows' (`ṇamhi`) is understood to apply.

544. Hanassa ghāto.

544. For `han`, there is the substitution `ghāta`.

Hanaiccetassa dhātussa ghātādeso hoti ṇakāravati kāritappaccaye pare. Ghāteti, ghātayati, ghātāpeti, ghātāpayati, “vadho vā sabbatthā”ti vadhādese vadheti, vadhāpeti.

For this root `han`, the substitution `ghāta` occurs when a causative suffix containing the letter `ṇ` follows. Thus: `ghāteti`, `ghātayati`, `ghātāpeti`, `ghātāpayati`. Alternatively, by the rule 'vadho vā sabbatthā' (or `vadha` everywhere), the substitution `vadha` occurs, giving: `vadheti`, `vadhāpeti`.

Juhontaṃ payojayati juhāveti, juhāvayati. Jahantaṃ payojayati jahāpeti, jahāpayati, hāpeti, hāpayati. Dadantaṃ payojayati dāpeti, dāpayati. Pidahantaṃ payojayati pidhāpeti, pidhāpayati, pidahāpeti, pidahāpayati.

He employs one who sacrifices: `juhāveti`, `juhāvayati`. He employs one who abandons: `jahāpeti`, `jahāpayati`, `hāpeti`, `hāpayati`. He employs one who gives: `dāpeti`, `dāpayati`. He employs one who covers: `pidhāpeti`, `pidhāpayati`, `pidahāpeti`, `pidahāpayati`.

Rundhantaṃ payojayati rodheti, rodhayati, rodhāpeti, rodhāpayati. Chindantaṃ payojayati chedeti, chedayati, chedāpeti, chedāpayati. Yuñjantaṃ payojayati [M 0.0335] yojeti, yojayati, yojāpeti, yojāpayati. Bhuñjantaṃ payojayati bhojeti, bhojayati, bhojāpeti, bhojāpayati. Muñcantaṃ payojayati moceti, mocayati, mocāpeti, mocāpayati.

He employs one who obstructs: `rodheti`, `rodhayati`, `rodhāpeti`, `rodhāpayati`. He employs one who cuts: `chedeti`, `chedayati`, `chedāpeti`, `chedāpayati`. He employs one who joins: `yojeti`, `yojayati`, `yojāpeti`, `yojāpayati`. He employs one who eats: `bhojeti`, `bhojayati`, `bhojāpeti`, `bhojāpayati`. He employs one who releases: `moceti`, `mocayati`, `mocāpeti`, `mocāpayati`.

Dibbantaṃ payojayati deveti, devayati. Uppajjantaṃ payojayati uppādeti, uppādayati. Bujjhantaṃ payojayati bodheti, bodhayati. “Dādhāntato yo kvacī”ti yakārāgamo, bujjhāpeti, bujjhāpayati. Tussantaṃ payojayati toseti, tosayati, tosāpeti, tosāpayati. Sammantaṃ payojayati sameti, samayati, ghaṭādittā na vuddhi. Kuppantaṃ payojayati kopeti, kopayati. Jāyantaṃ payojayati janeti, janayati, ghaṭādittā na vuddhi.

He employs one who plays: `deveti`, `devayati`. He employs one who arises: `uppādeti`, `uppādayati`. He employs one who awakens: `bodheti`, `bodhayati`. By the rule 'Dādhāntato yo kvaci', there is the insertion of the letter `ya`, giving `bujjhāpeti`, `bujjhāpayati`. He employs one who is satisfied: `toseti`, `tosayati`, `tosāpeti`, `tosāpayati`. He employs one who is calmed: `sameti`, `samayati`; because it belongs to the `ghaṭa` group, there is no strengthening. He employs one who is angry: `kopeti`, `kopayati`. He employs one who is born: `janeti`, `janayati`; because it belongs to the `ghaṭa` group, there is no strengthening.

Suṇantaṃ payojayati dhammaṃ sāveti, sāvayati. Pāpuṇantaṃ payojayati pāpeti, pāpayati.

He employs one who listens to the Dhamma: `sāveti`, `sāvayati` (he causes to hear). He employs one who reaches: `pāpeti`, `pāpayati` (he causes to reach).

Vikkiṇantaṃ payojayati vikkāyāpeti, vikkāyāpayati. Jinantaṃ payojayati jayāpeti, jayāpayati. Jānantaṃ payojayati ñāpeti, ñāpayati. Gaṇhantaṃ payojayati gāheti, gāhayati, gāhāpeti, gāhāpayati, gaṇhāpeti, gaṇhāpayati.

He employs one who sells: `vikkāyāpeti`, `vikkāyāpayati`. He employs one who conquers: `jayāpeti`, `jayāpayati`. He employs one who knows: `ñāpeti`, `ñāpayati` (he informs). He employs one who takes: `gāheti`, `gāhayati`, `gāhāpeti`, `gāhāpayati`, `gaṇhāpeti`, `gaṇhāpayati` (he causes to take).

Vitanantaṃ payojayati vitāneti, vitānayati. Yo koci karoti, tamañño “karohi karohi”iccevaṃ bravīti, karontaṃ payojayati, kātuṃ vā kāreti, kārayati, kārāpeti, kārāpayati iccādi.

He employs one who spreads: `vitāneti`, `vitānayati`. When someone is doing something, and another says to him, 'Do it! Do it!', in this way he employs the one who is doing, or employs someone to do. Thus: `kāreti`, `kārayati`, `kārāpeti`, `kārāpayati` (he causes to do), and so on.

Corentaṃ payojayati corāpeti, corāpayati. Cintentaṃ payojayati cintāpeti, cintāpayati[M 0.0336], pūjentaṃ payojayati pūjāpeti, pūjāpayati iccādi. Sabbattha subodhaṃ.

He employs one who steals: `corāpeti`, `corāpayati`. He employs one who thinks: `cintāpeti`, `cintāpayati`. He employs one who honors: `pūjāpeti`, `pūjāpayati`, and so on. This is easily understood in all cases.

Dhātuppaccayato cāpi, kāritappaccayā siyuṃ;

Sakāritehi yuṇvūnaṃ, dassanañcettha ñāpakaṃ.

Causative suffixes may also be applied to stems formed with verbal suffixes; the appearance of the suffixes `yu` and `ṇvu` with such causatives is an indicator of this.

Tena titikkhantaṃ payojayati titikkheti, titikkhāpeti. Tikicchantaṃ payojayati tikiccheti, tikicchayati, tikicchāpeti, tikicchāpayati. Evaṃ bubhukkheti, bubhukkhayati, bubhukkhāpeti, bubhukkhāpayati, pabbatāyantaṃ payojayati pabbatāyayati. Puttīyayati iccādipi siddhaṃ bhavati.

Therefore, he employs one who endures: `titikkheti`, `titikkhāpeti`. He employs one who treats or heals: `tikiccheti`, `tikicchayati`, `tikicchāpeti`, `tikicchāpayati`. Similarly, `bubhukkheti`, `bubhukkhayati`, `bubhukkhāpeti`, `bubhukkhāpayati` (he causes to be hungry). He employs one who acts like a mountain: `pabbatāyayati`. Forms such as `puttīyayati` (he causes someone to be treated as a son) are also established in this way.

Dhātuppaccayantanayo.

End of the section on stems ending in verbal suffixes.

Sāsanatthaṃ samuddiṭṭhaṃ, ākhyātaṃ sakabuddhiyā;

Bāhusaccabalenīdaṃ, cintayantu vicakkhaṇā.

The purpose of the teaching has been pointed out, explained according to my own understanding; let the discerning reflect upon this with the power of their great learning.

Bhavati tiṭṭhati seti, ahosi evamādayo;

Akammakāti viññeyyā, kammalakkhaṇaviññunā.

Verbs such as `bhavati` (he is), `tiṭṭhati` (he stands), `seti` (he lies down), `ahosi` (he was), and so on, should be known as intransitive by one who understands the characteristics of the grammatical object.

Akammakāpi hetvattha-ppaccayantā sakammakā;

Taṃ yathā bhikkhu bhāveti, maggaṃ rāgādidūsakanti.

Even intransitive verbs become transitive when they take a causative suffix. For example: 'A monk develops the path, the destroyer of lust and other defilements.'

Iti padarūpasiddhiyaṃ ākhyātakaṇḍo

Thus ends the Chapter on Verbs in the Padarūpasiddhi.

Chaṭṭho.

The Sixth.

7. Kibbidhānakaṇḍa

7. The Chapter on Kibbidhāna

Tekālika

Pertaining to the Three Times

Kiccappaccayantanaya

The Method of Kicca Suffixes

Atha dhātūhiyeva bhāvakammakattukaraṇādisādhanasahitaṃ kibbidhānamārabhīyate.

Then, the formation of kibbidhāna, together with its derivations such as state, object, agent, and instrument, is begun from the roots themselves.

Tattha kiccakitakavasena duvidhā hi paccayā, tesu kiccasaññāya paṭhamaṃ vuttattā, kiccānamappakattā ca kiccappaccayā tāva vuccante.

Herein, suffixes are indeed twofold by way of kicca and kitaka. Among them, because the designation 'kicca' is stated first, and because kicca suffixes are few, the kicca suffixes are spoken of first.

Bhū sattāyaṃ, “bhūyate, abhavittha, bhavissate vā devadattenā”ti viggahe –

Bhū in the sense of 'to be/exist,' with the analysis: 'He is being, he was, or he will be, by Devadatta.'

“Dhātuyā kammādimhi ṇo”ti ito “dhātuyā”ti sabbattha paccayādividhāne vattate, “parā, paccayā”ti ca adhikāro.

From the rule 'The suffix ṇa comes after a root in the sense of object, etc.,' the term 'after a root' applies everywhere in the formulation of suffixes and so on, and 'after' and 'suffixes' are also the governing rule.

545. Bhāvakammesu tabbānīyā.

545. The suffixes tabba and anīya are used in the sense of state and object.

Bhāvakammaiccetesvatthesu sabbadhātūhi tabba anīyaiccete paccayā parā honti. Yogavibhāgena aññatthāpi.

In these meanings, namely state (bhāva) and object (kamma), these suffixes, tabba and anīya, come after all roots. By division of the rule, they apply also elsewhere.

Tattha –

Therein –

Akammakehi dhātūhi, bhāve kiccā bhavanti te;

Sakammakehi kammatthe, arahasakkatthadīpakā.

From intransitive roots, those kicca suffixes occur in the sense of state (bhāva); from transitive roots, in the sense of object (kamma), indicating the meanings of 'worthy' and 'able'.

Te ca –

And they –

546. Ṇādayo [M 0.0338] tekālikā.

546. The ṇa-group of suffixes pertains to the three times.

Tikāle niyuttā tekālikā, ye idha tatiye dhātvādhikāre vihitā aniddiṭṭhakālā ṇādayo paccayā, te tekālikā hontīti paribhāsato kālattayepi honti.

Those assigned to the three times are 'tekālika'. Those suffixes of the ṇa-group which are prescribed here in the third section on roots and whose time is not specified, by definition, they are 'tekālika', thus they apply to all three times.

Sīhagatiyā “kvacī”ti vattate.

By the lion's gait analogy, 'sometimes' (kvaci) applies.

547. Yathāgamamikāro.

547. The augment 'i' occurs according to tradition.

Yathāgamaṃ yathāpayogaṃ jinavacanānuparodhena dhātūhi paro ikārāgamo hoti kvaci byañjanādikesu kiccakitakappaccayesu, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi, “o ava sare”ti avādeso, “naye paraṃ yutte”ti paraṃ netabbaṃ.

According to tradition, according to usage, without contradicting the words of the Conqueror, the augment 'i' sometimes occurs after roots in kicca and kitaka suffixes beginning with a consonant. By 'and in others,' there is lengthening (vuddhi). By 'o becomes ava before a vowel,' there is the substitution of ava. By 'when what follows is joined to the ṇaya,' what follows should be carried forward.

548. Te kiccā.

548. Those suffixes are kicca.

Ye idha vuttā tabbānīyaṇya teyya riccappaccayā, te kiccasaññā hontīti veditabbā. Tato “aññe kiti”ti vacanato kiccappaccayānamakitakattā nāmabyapadese asampatte “taddhitasamāsakitakā nāmaṃvātavetunādīsu cā”ti ettha caggahaṇena nāmabyapadeso, tato syādyuppatti. Bhāve bhāvassekattā ekavacanameva, “si”nti amādeso. Bhavitabbaṃ bhavatā paññena, bhavanīyaṃ.

Those suffixes stated here, namely tabba, anīya, ṇya, teyya, and ricca, should be understood as having the designation 'kicca'. Then, because kicca suffixes are not 'kita' according to the statement 'others are kita,' the designation 'nāma' (noun) is not attained. But here, by the inclusion of 'ca' in 'taddhita, compound, and kita are nouns, and in vātavetunādi etc.', the designation 'nāma' (noun) occurs. Thence, the origination of syādi inflections. In the sense of bhāva, due to the oneness of the bhāva, only the singular number is used. The 'si' ending is replaced by 'am'. Examples: 'It is to be by you, the wise' (bhavitabbaṃ bhavatā paññena), 'it is to be/become' (bhavanīyaṃ).

Idha byañjanādittābhāvā anuvattitakvaciggahaṇena ikārāgamābhāvo. Bhāve kiccappaccayantā napuṃsakā. Kamme tiliṅgā.

Here, due to the absence of a suffix beginning with a consonant, by the application of the 'kvaci' (sometimes) rule that is carried forward, there is no augment 'i'. In the sense of bhāva, those ending in kicca suffixes are neuter. In the sense of kamma, they are of all three genders.

Kammani abhipubbo, abhibhūyate, abhibhūyittha, abhibhūyissateti abhibhavitabbo kodho paṇḍitena, abhibhavitabbā [M 0.0339] taṇhā, abhibhavitabbaṃ dukkhaṃ, evaṃ abhibhavanīyo, abhibhavanīyā, abhibhavanīyaṃ, purisa kaññā cittasaddanayena netabbaṃ, evaṃ sabbattha.

In the sense of kamma, with 'abhi' as a prefix: 'is overcome' (abhibhūyate), 'was overcome' (abhibhūyittha), 'will be overcome' (abhibhūyissate). Thus, 'anger is to be overcome by the wise' (abhibhavitabbo kodho paṇḍitena), 'craving is to be overcome' (abhibhavitabbā taṇhā), 'suffering is to be overcome' (abhibhavitabbaṃ dukkhaṃ). Similarly, abhibhavanīyo, abhibhavanīyā, abhibhavanīyaṃ, following the pattern of the words purisa, kaññā, and citta. Thus everywhere.

Ettha hi –

Herein, indeed, –

Tabbādīheva kammassa, vuttattāva punattanā;

Vattabbassa abhāvā na, dutiyā paṭhamā tato.

Because the object (kamma) is already expressed by the tabba-group of suffixes, there is no repetition. Because there is no need to express it again, the accusative (dutiyā) is not used, but the nominative (paṭhamā) instead.

Āsa upavesane, āsīyittha, āsīyate, āsīyissateti āsitabbaṃ tayā, āsanīyaṃ. Kamme upāsitabbo garu, upāsanīyo.

Āsa in the sense of 'sitting/approaching': 'was sat upon' (āsīyittha), 'is sat upon' (āsīyate), 'will be sat upon' (āsīyissate). Thus, 'it is to be sat upon by you' (āsitabbaṃ tayā), 'to be sat upon' (āsanīyaṃ). In the sense of kamma: 'the teacher is to be attended upon' (upāsitabbo garu), 'worthy of attendance' (upāsanīyo).

Sī saye, asīyittha, sīyate, sīyissateti sayitabbaṃ bhavatā, sayanīyaṃ, “e ayā”ti ayādeso, atisayitabbo paro, atisayanīyo.

Sī in the sense of 'lying down/sleeping': 'was slept upon' (asīyittha), 'is slept upon' (sīyate), 'will be slept upon' (sīyissate). Thus, 'it is to be slept upon by you' (sayitabbaṃ bhavatā), 'to be slept upon' (sayanīyaṃ). By the rule 'e becomes aya,' there is the substitution of aya. 'Another is to be surpassed' (atisayitabbo paro), 'to be surpassed' (atisayanīyo).

Pada gatimhi, uppajjittha, uppajjate, uppajjissateti uppajjitabbaṃ tena, uppajjanīyaṃ, ettha ca “kattarī”ti adhikāraṃ vinā “divādito yo”ti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena yappaccayo, “tassa cavaggayakāra”iccādinā cavaggo, “paradvebhāvo ṭhāne”ti dvibhāvo, paṭipajjitabbo maggo, paṭipajjanīyo.

Pada in the sense of 'going/moving': 'arose' (uppajjittha), 'arises' (uppajjate), 'will arise' (uppajjissate). Thus, 'it is to be arisen by him' (uppajjitabbaṃ tena), 'to be arisen' (uppajjanīyaṃ). And here, without the governing rule 'in the sense of agent' (kattarī), by the division of the rule 'the suffix ya comes from the divādi group' without a governing rule, the suffix ya is applied. By the rule 'tassa cavaggayakāra' etc., the palatal consonant (cavagga) is substituted. By the rule 'doubling of the subsequent consonant in place,' there is doubling. Examples: 'The path is to be followed' (paṭipajjitabbo maggo), 'to be followed' (paṭipajjanīyo).

Budha avagamane, abujjhittha, bujjhate, bujjhissateti bujjhitabbo dhammo, bujjhanīyo.

Budha in the sense of 'understanding': 'was understood' (abujjhittha), 'is understood' (bujjhate), 'will be understood' (bujjhissate). Thus, 'the Dhamma is to be understood' (bujjhitabbo dhammo), 'to be understood' (bujjhanīyo).

Su savaṇe, asūyittha, sūyate, sūyissateti sotabbo dhammo, idha yathāgamaggahaṇena ikārāgamābhāvo, suṇitabbo, “svādito ṇu ṇā uṇā cā”ti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena ṇāpaccayo, savaṇīyo.

Su in the sense of 'hearing': 'was heard' (asūyittha), 'is heard' (sūyate), 'will be heard' (sūyissate). Thus, 'the Dhamma is to be heard' (sotabbo dhammo). Here, by the acceptance of tradition, there is no augment 'i'. 'To be heard' (suṇitabbo). By the rule 'from svādi roots, ṇu, ṇā, uṇā, and ca,' by division of the rule without a governing rule, the suffix ṇā is applied. 'To be heard' (savaṇīyo).

Kara karaṇe, karīyittha, karīyati, karīyissatīti atthe tabbā’nīyā.

Kara in the sense of 'doing': 'was done' (karīyittha), 'is done' (karīyati), 'will be done' (karīyissati). In this sense, the suffixes tabba and anīya are used.

“Antassa, karassa, ca, tatta”nti ca vattate.

And the rule 'of the end, of kara, and, the change to ta' applies.

549. Tuṃ [M 0.0340] tu na tabbesu vā.

549. Optionally, before the suffixes tuṃ, tu, na, and tabba.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa antabhūtassa rakārassa takārattaṃ hoti vā tuṃ tu na tabbaiccetesu paccayesu paresu. Kattabbo bhavatā dhammo, kattabbā pūjā, kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ, tattābhāve “karotissā”ti vattamāne “tavetunādīsu kā”ti ettha ādisaddena tabbepi kādeso, kātabbaṃ hitaṃ.

Of the root 'kara', the final 'ra' optionally becomes 'ta' when these suffixes—tuṃ, tu, na, and tabba—follow. For example: kattabbo bhavatā dhammo (the Dhamma is to be done by you), kattabbā pūjā (worship is to be done), kattabbaṃ kusalaṃ (a wholesome deed is to be done). In the absence of the change to 'ta', while the rule 'karotissa ā' is current, by the word 'ādi' in the rule 'tavetunādīsu kā', the substitution of 'kā' also occurs for tabba. For example: kātabbaṃ hitaṃ (welfare is to be done).

550. Rahādito ṇa.

550. After the rahādi group of roots, na becomes ṇa.

Rakāra hahārādyantehi dhātūhi parassa anānīyādinakārassa ṇakāro hoti. Ādisaddena ramu apañātāditopi.

After roots ending in 'ra', 'ha', and so forth, the 'na' of a following suffix such as anīya becomes 'ṇa'. By the word 'ādi', this also applies after roots such as ramu, apa, and ñā.

Rahādito parassettha, nakārassa asambhavā;

Anānīyādinasseva, sāmathyāyaṃ ṇakāratā.

Here, since the suffix 'na' is not possible after the rahādi group of roots, this change to 'ṇa' occurs by the force of the rule for suffixes such as anīya.

Karaṇīyo dhammo, karaṇārahoti attho, karaṇīyā, karaṇīyaṃ.

Karaṇīyo dhammo (the Dhamma is to be done); the meaning is 'worthy of being done' (karaṇa-araho). Also, the feminine karaṇīyā and the neuter karaṇīyaṃ.

Bhara bharaṇe, bharīyatīti bharitabbo, bharaṇīyo.

The root bhara in the sense of 'bearing'. From bharīyati (it is borne), come bharitabbo (to be borne) and bharaṇīyo (to be borne).

Gaha upādāne, agayhittha, gayhati, gayhissatīti gahetabbo, “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā ikārassekāro, saṅgaṇhitabbo, “gahādito ppaṇhā”ti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena ṇhāpaccayo, halopasaralopādi, saṅgaṇhaṇīyo, gahaṇīyo.

The root gaha in the sense of 'taking'. From agayhittha (it was taken), gayhati (it is taken), and gayhissati (it will be taken), comes gheyyo (to be taken). By the rule 'tesu vuddhi' etc., the 'i' becomes 'e'. Also, saṅgaṇhitabbo (to be grasped). By the rule 'gahādito ppaṇhā', through a splitting of the rule without a governing principle, the suffix ṇhā is applied. There is elision of 'ha', elision of 'sa', etc. Also, saṅgaṇhaṇīyo (to be grasped), and gahaṇīyo (to be taken).

Ādiggahaṇena ramu kīḷāyaṃ, ramīyittha, ramīyati, ramīyissatīti ramitabbo, ramaṇīyo vihāro.

By the inclusion of 'ādi': the root ramu in the sense of 'enjoying'. From ramīyittha (it was enjoyed), ramīyati (it is enjoyed), and ramīyissati (it will be enjoyed), come ramitabbo vihāro (a monastery to be enjoyed) and ramaṇīyo vihāro (an enjoyable monastery).

Apa [M 0.0341] pāpuṇane, uṇāpaccayo, pāpīyatīti pāpuṇitabbo, “gupādīnañcā”ti dhātvantassa lopo, dvittañca, pattabbo, patteyyo, pāpuṇaṇīyo, pāpaṇīyo.

The root apa in the sense of 'attaining'; the suffix uṇā is applied. From pāpīyati (it is being attained), comes pāpuṇitabbo (to be attained). By the rule 'gupādīnañca', there is elision of the end of the root and also doubling, giving pattabbo (to be attained) and patteyyo (attainable). Also, pāpuṇaṇīyo (to be attained) and pāpaṇīyo (to be attained).

“Antassa, vā”ti ca vattate.

And the rules 'antassa' and 'vā' are also current.

551. Gama khana hanādīnaṃ tuṃtabbādīsu na.

551. Of roots such as gama, khana, and hana, the final consonant becomes na before suffixes such as tuṃ and tabba.

Gama khana hanaiccevamādīnaṃ makāra nakārantānaṃ dhātūnamantassa nakāro hoti vā tuṃ tabba tave tuna tvānatvāiccevamādīsu takārādippaccayesu paresu. Agacchīyittha, gacchīyati, gacchīyissatīti gantabbo maggo, gamitabbaṃ, gamanīyaṃ.

Of roots ending in 'm' or 'n', such as gama, khana, and hana, the final consonant optionally becomes 'na' when suffixes beginning with 'ta', such as tuṃ, tabba, tave, tuna, tvā, and tvāna, follow. From the passive forms agacchīyittha (it was gone), gacchīyati (it is gone), and gacchīyissati (it will be gone), come the examples: gantabbo maggo (the path is to be traversed), gamitabbaṃ (to be gone), and gamanīyaṃ (to be gone).

Khanu avadāraṇe, akhaññittha, khaññati, khaññissatīti khantabbaṃ āvāṭaṃ, khanitabbaṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā khanantassa ṇattañca, khaṇitabbaṃ, khaṇaṇīyaṃ, khananīyaṃ vā.

The root khanu in the sense of 'digging'. From akhaññittha (it was dug), khaññati (it is dug), and khaññissati (it will be dug), come khantabbaṃ āvāṭaṃ (the pit is to be dug) and khanitabbaṃ (to be dug). And by the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., the 'na' of 'khana' becomes 'ṇa', giving khaṇitabbaṃ (to be dug), and khaṇaṇīyaṃ or khananīyaṃ (to be dug).

Hana hiṃsā gatīsu, ahaññittha, haññate, haññissateti hantabbaṃ, hanitabbaṃ, hananīyaṃ.

The root hana in the senses of 'harming' and 'going'. From ahaññittha (it was harmed), haññate (it is harmed), and haññissate (it will be harmed), come hantabbaṃ (to be harmed), hanitabbaṃ (to be harmed), and hananīyaṃ (to be harmed).

Mana ñāṇe, amaññittha, maññate, maññissateti mantabbo, manitabbo, yappaccaye cavaggādi, maññitabbaṃ, maññanīyaṃ.

The root mana in the sense of 'knowing'. From amaññittha (it was thought), maññate (it is thought), and maññissate (it will be thought), come mantabbo (to be thought) and manitabbo (to be thought). (The passive stem is formed with the ya suffix, causing palatalization, etc.). Also, maññitabbaṃ (to be thought) and maññanīyaṃ (to be thought).

Pūja pūjāyaṃ, apūjīyittha, pūjīyati, pūjīyissatīti atthe tabbānīyā. “Curādito ṇe ṇayā”ti akattaripi ṇeṇayā, ikārāgamānīyesu “saralopo”tiādinā kāritasarassa lopo, pūjetabbo, pūjayitabbo, pūjanīyo bhagavā.

The root pūja in the sense of 'worship'. From apūjīyittha (he was worshipped), pūjīyati (he is worshipped), and pūjīyissatīti (he will be worshipped); in this sense, the suffixes tabba and anīya are used. By the rule 'Curādito ṇe ṇayā', the suffixes ṇe and ṇaya are applied even in a non-agentive sense. In cases with the augment 'i' and the suffix anīya, by the rule 'saralopo' etc., there is elision of the causative vowel. For example: pūjetabbo, pūjayitabbo, pūjanīyo bhagavā (the Blessed One is to be worshipped).

“Tabbānīyā”ti yogavibhāgena kattukaraṇesupi, yā pāpuṇane, niyyātīti niyyānīko maggo. Gacchantīti gamanīyā [M 0.0342] bhogā. Naha soce, nahāyati etenāti nahānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ.

By splitting the rule 'Tabbānīyā', these suffixes are also applied in the sense of agent and instrument. The root yā in the sense of 'going': niyyātīti niyyānīko maggo (the path is 'leading forth' because it leads forth). Gacchantīti gamanīyā bhogā (possessions are 'transient' because they go away). The root naha in the sense of 'bathing': nahāyati etenāti nahānīyaṃ cuṇṇaṃ (the powder is 'for bathing' because one bathes with it).

“Bhāvakammesū”ti adhikāro.

The governing rule is 'Bhāvakammesu' (in the sense of state and object).

552. Ṇyo ca.

552. And the suffix ṇya.

Bhāvakammesu sabbadhātūhi ṇyappaccayo hoti, caggahaṇena “ñāteyya”ntiādīsu teyyappaccayo ca.

In the sense of state and object, the suffix ṇya occurs after all roots; and by the inclusion of 'ca', the suffix teyya also occurs in examples such as 'ñāteyya'.

553. Kāritaṃ viya ṇānubandho.

553. A suffix with the indicatory letter ṇa is treated like a causative.

Anubandho appayogī, ṇakārānubandho paccayo kāritaṃ viya daṭṭhabboti kāritabyapadeso, “kāritānaṃ ṇo lopa”nti ṇalopo, “asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite”ti vuddhi, ikārāgamo, kattabbaṃ kāriyaṃ.

An indicatory letter is not used in the final form. A suffix with the indicatory letter 'ṇa' should be regarded as a causative, hence it receives the designation 'causative'. By the rule 'kāritānaṃ ṇo lopa', there is elision of 'ṇa'. By the rule 'asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite', there is vuddhi strengthening. There is also the augment 'i'. For example: kattabbaṃ (to be done), kāriyaṃ (to be done).

Hara haraṇe, aharīyittha, harīyati, harīyissatīti vā haritabbaṃ hāriyaṃ.

The root hara in the sense of 'carrying'. From aharīyittha (it was carried), harīyati (it is carried), and harīyissatīti (it will be carried), come haritabbaṃ (to be carried) and hāriyaṃ (to be carried).

Bhara bharaṇe, bharitabbaṃ bhāriyaṃ.

The root bhara in the sense of 'bearing': bharitabbaṃ (to be borne), bhāriyaṃ (to be borne).

Labha lābhe, labhitabbaṃ labbhaṃ, “yavataṃ talana”iccādisutte kāraggahaṇena yavato bhakārassa bhakāro, dvittaṃ.

The root labha in the sense of 'obtaining': labhitabbaṃ (to be obtained), labbhaṃ (to be obtained). By the inclusion of 'kāra' in the rule 'yavataṃ talana' etc., the 'bha' of 'yavato' becomes 'bha', and there is doubling.

Sāsa anusiṭṭhimhi, sāsitabbo sisso, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ākārassikāro.

The root sāsa in the sense of 'instructing'. Sāsitabbo sisso (the pupil is to be instructed). By the rule 'kvaci dhātu' etc., the 'ā' becomes 'i'.

Vaca viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, ṇyappaccayādimhi kate “antānaṃ, ṇānubandhe”ti ca vattate.

The root vaca in the sense of 'clear speech'. When the suffix ṇya or a similar suffix is applied, the rule 'antānaṃ... ṇānubandhe' (of the final consonants... when a ṇa-indicatory suffix follows) is also current.

554. Kagā [M 0.0343] cajānaṃ.

554. Ka and ga are substituted for ca and ja.

Cajaiccetesaṃ dhātvantānaṃ kakāra gakārādesā honti ṇakārānubandhe paccaye pareti cassa kādeso. Vacanīyaṃ vākyaṃ.

For these root-endings, ca and ja, the substitutions ka and ga respectively occur when a suffix with the indicatory letter 'ṇa' follows. Thus, for 'ca' there is the substitution 'ka'. For example: vacanīyaṃ vākyaṃ (that which is to be spoken is a sentence).

Bhaja sevāyaṃ, bhajanīyaṃ bhāgyaṃ, jassa gādeso.

The root bhaj is in the sense of serving. For example: bhajanīyaṃ bhāgyaṃ ('fortune is to be associated with'); for the j of the root, there is the substitution of g.

Ci caye, acīyittha, cīyati, cīyissatīti cetabbaṃ ceyyaṃ, ikārassekāro vuddhi, yakārassa dvittaṃ, vinipubbo “do dhassa cā”ti sutte caggahaṇena cakārassa chakāro, viniccheyyaṃ, vinicchitabbaṃ, vinicchanīyaṃ. “Kiyādito nā”ti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena tabbānīya tuṃ tunā dīsu ca nāpaccayo, vinicchinitabbaṃ, vinicchinanīyaṃ.

The root ci is in the sense of accumulating: (Passive Aorist:) acīyittha; (Passive Present:) cīyati; (Passive Future:) cīyissati. The gerundive is cetabbaṃ or ceyyaṃ. For ceyyaṃ, the i of the root becomes e by vuddhi, and the y is doubled. When preceded by vi and ni, by the inclusion of ca in the rule 'do dhassa ca', c becomes ch, yielding viniccheyyaṃ, vinicchitabbaṃ, vinicchanīyaṃ. By splitting the rule 'kiyādito nā' without its governing context, the nā-suffix also occurs with suffixes such as tabba and anīya, yielding vinicchinitabbaṃ and vinicchinanīyaṃ.

Nī pāpuṇane, anīyittha, nīyati, nīyissatīti neyyo, neyyā, neyyaṃ. Netabbaṃ.

The root nī is in the sense of leading: (Passive Aorist:) anīyittha; (Passive Present:) nīyati; (Passive Future:) nīyissati. The gerundive is neyyo, neyyā, neyyaṃ, or netabbaṃ.

Ṇyaggahaṇaṃ chaṭṭhīyantavasenānuvattate, maṇḍūkagatiyā antaggahaṇañca tatiyantavasena.

The term 'ṇyassa' is carried forward as a genitive, and the term 'antena' is carried forward as an instrumental by the frog-leap principle.

555. Bhūtobba.

555. From bhū, the suffix is bba.

Bhū iccetasmā parassa ṇyappaccayassa saha dhātvantena abbādeso hoti. Bhavitabbo bhabbo, bhabbā, bhabbaṃ.

After the root bhū, for the ṇya-suffix together with the final of the root, there is the substitution of abba. Meaning bhavitabbo, the form is bhabbo, bhabbā, bhabbaṃ.

“Ṇyassa, antenā”ti ca vattate.

And the terms 'ṇyassa' and 'antena' are carried forward.

556. Vada mada gamu yuja garahākārādīhi jjammaggayheyyāgāro vā.

556. From vad, mad, gam, yuj, garah, and roots ending in ā, there are optionally the substitutions jja, mma, gga, yha, eyya, and āgāra.

Vada mada gamu yuja garahaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi, ākārantehi ca parassa ṇyappaccayassa dhātvantena saha yathākkamaṃ [M 0.0344] jja mma gga yha e yyaiccete ādesā honti vā, garassa ca gārādeso, garahassa garassevāyaṃ gāro. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo.

From roots such as vad, mad, gam, yuj, garah, and those ending in ā, for the following ṇya-suffix together with the final of the root, there are optionally the respective substitutions jja, mma, gga, yha, e, yya. And for gara, the substitution is gāra; this gāra is for the root garah itself. The word vā (optionally) here indicates a fixed option.

Vada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, avajjittha, vajjati, vajjissatīti vā vajjaṃ vadanīyaṃ, rassattaṃ. Vajjaṃ doso.

The root vad is in the sense of clear speech: (Passive Aorist:) avajjittha; (Passive Present:) vajjati; (Passive Future:) vajjissati. The gerundive is optionally vajjaṃ or vadanīyaṃ, with shortening. Vajjaṃ also means 'fault'.

Mada ummāde, amajjittha, majjate, majjissati etenāti majjaṃ madanīyaṃ. Madaggahaṇena karaṇepi ṇyappaccayo. Gamu sappa gatimhi, gantabbaṃ gammaṃ.

The root mad is in the sense of intoxication. 'One was intoxicated, is intoxicated, or will be intoxicated by this'; hence, majjaṃ (an intoxicant), madanīyaṃ (intoxicating). By the inclusion of the root mad, the suffix ṇya is also used in the instrumental sense. The roots gam and sapp are in the sense of going; hence gantabbaṃ (to be gone to), gammaṃ (accessible).

Yuja yoge, ayujjittha, yujjate, yujjissatīti yoggaṃ, niyojjo vā.

The root yuj is in the sense of joining. 'It was joined, is joined, or will be joined'; hence yoggaṃ (fit to be yoked), or niyojjo (to be appointed).

Garaha nindāyaṃ, agarayhittha, garahīyati, garahīyissatīti atthe ṇyappaccayo, tassiminā dhātvantena saha yhādeso, garassa gārādeso ca, gārayho, gārayhā, gārayhaṃ, garahaṇīyaṃ.

The root garah is in the sense of blame. In the sense 'it was blamed, is blamed, or will be blamed,' the suffix ṇya is added. For this suffix, together with the final of the root, there is the substitution of yha, and for gara, there is the substitution of gāra. Hence: gārayho, gārayhā, gārayhaṃ (blameworthy); garahaṇīyaṃ (blameworthy).

Ādisaddena aññepi damajahantā gayhante. Gada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, gajjate, gadanīyaṃ vā gajjaṃ. Pada gatimhi, pajjanīyaṃ pajjaṃ gāthā. Khāda bhakkhaṇe, khajjateti khajjaṃ khādanīyaṃ. Damu damane, adammittha, dammate, damīyissatīti dammo damanīyo. Bhuja pālanabyavaharaṇesu, abhujjittha, bhujjati, bhujjissatīti bhoggaṃ, bhojjaṃ vā, kāraggahaṇena yassa jakāro. Gahetabbaṃ gayhamiccādi.

By the word ādi (etc.), other roots ending in da, ma, ja, and ha are also included. The root gad is in the sense of articulate speech; hence gajjate (is spoken), gadanīyaṃ or gajjaṃ (to be spoken). The root pad is in the sense of going; hence pajjanīyaṃ, pajjaṃ (a verse), a gāthā. The root khād is in the sense of eating; 'it is eaten,' hence khajjaṃ, khādanīyaṃ (food, edible). The root dam is in the sense of taming; 'it was tamed, is tamed, or will be tamed,' hence dammo, damanīyo (to be tamed). The root bhuj is in the senses of protecting and using; 'it was used, is used, or will be used,' hence bhoggaṃ, or bhojjaṃ; its j becomes g by inclusion with the gutturals (ka-group). Gahetabbaṃ (to be taken), gayhaṃ (to be grasped), and so on.

Ākārantato pana dā dāne, adīyittha, dīyati, dīyissatīti atthe ṇyappaccayo, tassiminā dhātvantena ākārena saha eyyādeso, deyyaṃ, dātabbaṃ. Anīye “saralopo”tiādinā pubbasarassa lope sampatte tattheva [M 0.0345] tuggahaṇena nisedhetvā “sarā sare lopa”nti ākāre lutte parasarassa dīgho, dānīyaṃ.

Now, from roots ending in ā, such as dā in the sense of giving: in the sense 'it was given, is given, or will be given,' the suffix ṇya is added. For this suffix, together with the root-final ā, there is the substitution of eyya; hence deyyaṃ (to be given), dātabbaṃ (to be given). With the suffix anīya, when the elision of the preceding vowel is occasioned by the rule beginning 'saralopo', it is prohibited by the inclusion of tu in that very rule. Then, by the rule 'sarā sare lopaṃ', the ā is elided and the following vowel is lengthened, resulting in dānīyaṃ.

Pā pāne, apīyittha, pīyati, pīyissatīti peyyaṃ, pātabbaṃ, pānīyaṃ. Hā cāge, ahīyittha, hīyati, hīyissatīti heyyaṃ, hātabbaṃ, hānīyaṃ. Mā māne, amīyittha, mīyati, mīyissatīti meyyaṃ, mātabbaṃ, minitabbaṃ, metabbaṃ vā. Ñā avabodhane, aññāyittha, ñāyati, ñāyissatīti ñeyyaṃ, ñātabbaṃ, ñāteyyaṃ. “Ñāssa jā jaṃ nā”ti jādese “kiyādito nā”ti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena nāpaccayo, ikārāgamo ca, jānitabbaṃ, vijānanīyaṃ. Khyāpakathane, saṅkhyātabbaṃ, saṅkhyeyyaṃ iccādi.

The root pā is in the sense of drinking: 'it was drunk, is drunk, or will be drunk'; hence peyyaṃ (drinkable), pātabbaṃ (to be drunk), pānīyaṃ (potable). The root hā is in the sense of abandoning: 'it was abandoned, is abandoned, or will be abandoned'; hence heyyaṃ (to be abandoned), hātabbaṃ (to be abandoned), hānīyaṃ (to be abandoned). The root mā is in the sense of measuring: 'it was measured, is measured, or will be measured'; hence meyyaṃ (measurable), mātabbaṃ (to be measured), minitabbaṃ (to be measured), or metabbaṃ (to be measured). The root ñā is in the sense of understanding: 'it was known, is known, or will be known'; hence ñeyyaṃ (knowable), ñātabbaṃ (to be known), ñāteyyaṃ (to be known). By the rule 'ñāssa jā jaṃ nā', there is the substitution of jā. By splitting the rule 'kiyādito nā' without its governing context, the suffix nā and the augment i are added; hence jānitabbaṃ (to be known), vijānanīyaṃ (discernible). The root khyā is in the sense of telling; hence saṅkhyātabbaṃ (to be enumerated), saṅkhyeyyaṃ (to be reckoned), and so on.

557. Karamhā ricca.

557. After kar, ricca.

Karadhātuto riccappaccayo hoti bhāvakammesu.

After the root kar, the suffix ricca occurs in the impersonal and passive senses.

558. Ramhi ranto rādi no.

558. When ra follows, the final of a root and the initial ra do not remain.

Rakārānubandhe paccaye pare sabbo dhātvanto rādi paccayarakāramariyādo no hoti, lopamāpajjateti attho. Rantoti ettha rakāro sandhijo, kattabbaṃ kiccaṃ. “Riccā”ti yogavibhāgena bharāditopi riccappaccayo, yathā, bharīyatīti bhacco, saralopo. I gatimhi, pati etabbo paṭicco.

When a suffix with the anubandha ra follows, the entire root-final, along with the initial ra of the suffix, is elided. Here in the rule, the ra in ranto is euphonic. For example: kattabbaṃ, kiccaṃ. By splitting the rule 'riccā', the suffix ricca also follows roots of the bhar-group and others. For example: from bharīyati (is carried) comes bhacco (a servant), with elision of the vowel. From the root i in the sense of going, pati etabbo (to be gone towards) becomes paṭicco.

559. Pesātisaggapattakālesu kiccā.

559. In the senses of command, permission, and opportune time, the kicca suffixes.

Pesa atisagga pattakālaiccetesvatthesu kiccappaccayā honti. Pesanaṃ nāma “kattabbamidaṃ bhavatā”ti āṇāpanaṃ, ajjhesanañca. Atisaggonāma “kimidaṃ mayā kattabba”nti puṭṭhassa vā [M 0.0346] “pāṇo na hantabbo”tiādinā paṭipattidassanamukhena vā kattabbassa anuññā. Pattakālo nāma sampattasamayo yo attano kiccakaraṇasamayamanupaparikkhitvā na karoti, tassa samayārocanaṃ, na tattha ajjhesanamatthīti. Te ca “bhāvakammesu kiccattakkhatthā”ti vuttattā bhāvakammesveva bhavanti.

The kicca suffixes occur in these senses: command (pesa), permission (atisagga), and opportune time (pattakāla). Command is ordering, 'This should be done by you,' and also requesting. Permission is the granting of what should be done, either to one who has asked, 'What should be done by me?' or by way of showing the practice, as in, 'A living being should not be killed.' Opportune time is the announcement of the arrived time to one who, though aware of the time for performing his duty, does not act; in this, there is no request. And since it is stated, 'The kicca, ta, and khattha suffixes are in the impersonal and passive senses,' they occur only in the impersonal and passive senses.

Pesane tāva – karīyatu bhavatā kammanti atthe iminā tabbānīyā, sesaṃ vuttanayameva, kattabbaṃ kammaṃ bhavatā, karaṇīyaṃ kiccaṃ bhavatā.

First, in the sense of command: in the sense 'Let the work be done by you,' the suffixes tabba and anīya are used by this rule; the rest is as already explained. Kattabbaṃ kammaṃ bhavatā (The work is to be done by you); karaṇīyaṃ kiccaṃ bhavatā (The duty is to be done by you).

Atisagge bhujjatu bhavatāti atthe tabbādi, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi.

In the sense of permission: in the sense 'May you eat,' the suffixes tabba, etc., are used. By the rule 'aññesu ca', there is vowel strengthening.

“Tassā”ti vattate.

The word 'tassa' is carried forward.

560. Bhujādīnamanto no dvi ca.

560. Of bhuj and other roots, the final is elided, and there is doubling.

Bhujaiccevamādīnaṃ jakārādiantānaṃ dhātūnamanto no hoti, parassa kiccakitakappaccayatakārassa ca dvebhāvo hoti. Bhottabbaṃ bhojanaṃ bhavatā, bhojanīyaṃ bhojjaṃ bhavatā.

Of roots such as bhuj and others ending in ja, the final consonant is elided, and the ta of a following kicca or kita suffix is doubled. For example: Bhottabbaṃ bhojanaṃ bhavatā (Food is to be eaten by you); bhojanīyaṃ bhojjaṃ bhavatā (Food is to be eaten by you).

Ikārāgamayuttatakāre pana – “namakarānamantānaṃ niyuttatamhī”ti ettha “antānaṃ niyuttatamhī”ti yogavibhāgena dhātvantalopādinisedho, “rudhādito niggahītapubba”nti vinādhikārayogavibhāgena, “niggahītañcā”ti vā niggahītāgamo, bhuñjitabbaṃ tayā, yuñjitabbaṃ.

However, when the suffix ta is joined with the augment i, the elision of the root-final is prohibited by splitting the rule 'namakarānamantānaṃ niyuttatamhī' into 'antānaṃ niyuttatamhī'. Then, by splitting the rule 'rudhādito niggahītapubba' without its governing context, or by the rule 'niggahītañca', there is the augment of a nasal. For example: bhuñjitabbaṃ tayā (to be eaten by you), yuñjitabbaṃ (to be yoked).

Samayārocane pana – i ajjhayane adhipubbo, adhīyataṃ bhavatāti atthe tabbānīyādi, ikārāgamavuddhiayādesaajjhādesā ca, ṇyappaccaye tu vuddhi, yakārassa dvittañca, ajjhayitabbaṃ, ajjheyyaṃ bhavatā, ajjhayanīyaṃ bhavatā, avassaṃ [M 0.0347] kattabbanti vākye pana “kiccā”ti adhikicca “avassakādhamiṇesu ṇī cā”ti avassakādhamiṇatthe ca tabbādayo, kattabbaṃ me bhavatā gehaṃ, karaṇīyaṃ, kāriyaṃ. Evaṃ dātabbaṃ me bhavatā sataṃ, dānīyaṃ, deyyaṃ.

Now, in the sense of announcing the time: the root i is preceded by adhi in the sense of studying.
