In the sense 'May it be studied by you,' the suffixes tabba, anīya, etc., are used, with the augment i, vowel strengthening, the substitution of ay, and the substitution of ajjha. With the suffix ṇya, however, there is vowel strengthening and doubling of the ya. Hence: ajjhayitabbaṃ (to be studied), ajjheyyaṃ bhavatā (to be studied by you), ajjhayanīyaṃ bhavatā (to be studied by you). Further, in a sentence expressing 'must be done,' governing the rule for kicca suffixes, by the rule 'avassakādhamiṇesu ṇī ca', the suffixes tabba, etc., are also used in the senses of necessity and indebtedness. For example: kattabbaṃ me bhavatā gehaṃ (A house must be built for me by you), karaṇīyaṃ, kāriyaṃ. Similarly, dātabbaṃ me bhavatā sataṃ (A hundred must be given to me by you), dānīyaṃ, deyyaṃ.

Dhara dhāraṇe, curādittā ṇeṇayā, vuddhi, ikārāgamo ca, dhāretabbaṃ, dhārayitabbaṃ iccādi.

The root dhar is in the sense of holding. Because it belongs to the curādi group, the suffixes ṇe and ṇaya are used, along with vowel strengthening and the augment i. Hence: dhāretabbaṃ (to be held), dhārayitabbaṃ (to be held), and so on.

“Nudādīhi yuṇvūnamanānanākānanakā sakāritehi cā”ti sakāritehipi yuṇvūnamādesavidhānatoyeva dhātuppaccayantatopi kiccakitakappaccayā bhavantīti daṭṭhabbo. Tena titikkhāpīyatīti titikkhāpetabbo. Evaṃ tikicchāpetabbo tikicchāpanīyo. Abhāvīyittha, bhāvīyati, bhāvīyissatīti bhāvetabbo maggo. Bhāvayitabbo, bhāvanīyo, bhāvanīyaṃ, bhāvanīyā, akārīyittha, kārīyati, kārīyissatīti kāretabbaṃ, kārayitabbaṃ, kārāpetabbaṃ, kārāpayitabbaṃ, kārāpanīyamiccādi ca siddhaṃ bhavati.

It should be understood that because the substitutions yu, ṇvu, ana, anāka, and anaka are prescribed even for causative verbs by the rule 'Nudādīhi...cā', the kicca and kita suffixes can also follow a root that ends in a verbal suffix. Thus, from titikkhāpīyati (is caused to be endured) comes titikkhāpetabbo (to be caused to be endured). Similarly, tikicchāpetabbo (to be caused to be treated), tikicchāpanīyo (to be caused to be treated). From 'It was developed, is developed, or will be developed', there is bhāvetabbo maggo (the path is to be developed), bhāvayitabbo, bhāvanīyo, bhāvanīyaṃ, bhāvanīyā. From 'It was caused to be done, is caused to be done, or will be caused to be done', there are kāretabbaṃ, kārayitabbaṃ, kārāpetabbaṃ, kārāpayitabbaṃ, kārāpanīyaṃ, and so on, which are also established.

Kattabbaṃ karaṇīyañca, kāriyaṃ kiccamiccapi;

Kāretabbaṃ tathā kārā-petabbaṃ kiccasaṅgaho.

Kattabbaṃ and karaṇīyaṃ, kāriyaṃ and also kiccaṃ; likewise kāretabbaṃ and kārāpetabbaṃ—this is the summary of kicca forms.

Kiccappaccayantanayo.

The Section on Words Ending in Kicca Suffixes.

Tekālika

Pertaining to the Three Tenses

Kitakappaccayantanaya

The Section on Words Ending in Kita Suffixes

Idāni kitakappaccayā vuccante.

Now, the kita suffixes are explained.

Kara karaṇe, pure viya dhātusaññādi.

The root 'kara' in the sense of 'doing'; the designation as a root, etc., is as before.

Kumbhaiccupapadaṃ, tato dutiyā.

The word 'kumbha' is an upapada; from that, the second case ending.

“Kumbhaṃ karoti, akāsi, karissatī”ti vā viggahe –

In the analysis, 'kumbhaṃ karoti' (he makes a pot), 'akāsi' (he made a pot), or 'karissatī' (he will make a pot)—

“Parā, paccayā”ti ca vattate.

And 'parā, paccayā' (after, suffixes) is understood to apply.

561. Dhātuyā [M 0.0348] kammādimhi ṇo.

561. The suffix ṇo follows a root when there is an object, etc., [as an upapada].

Kammasmiṃ ādimhi sati dhātuyā paro ṇappaccayo hoti.

When an object, etc., is present at the beginning [as an upapada], the suffix ṇa follows the root.

So ca –

And that [suffix] –

562. Aññe kita.

562. Other [suffixes] are kita.

Tatiye dhātvādhikāre vihitā kiccehi aññe paccayā kiticceva saññā hontīti kitasaññā katā.

In the third section, the one concerning roots, suffixes prescribed therein, other than the kicca suffixes, are designated as 'kita'; thus the designation 'kita' is made.

563. Kattari kita.

563. Kita [suffixes] occur in the agentive sense.

Kattari kārake kitapaccayo hotīti niyamato kattari bhavati, so ca “ṇādayo tekālikā”ti vuttattā kālattaye ca hoti. Pure viya kāritabyapadesaṇalopavuddhiyo, paccayantassāliṅgattā syādimhi asampatte “taddhitasamāsakitakā nāmaṃvātavetunādīsu cā”ti kitakantattā nāmaṃva kate syādyuppatti, tato kumbhaṃ karotīti atthe “amādayo parapadebhī”ti dutiyātappurisasamāso, “nāmāna”ntiādinā samāsasaññā, “tesaṃ vibhattiyo lopā cā”ti vibhattilopo, “pakati cassa sarantassā”ti pakatibhāvo, puna samāsattā nāmamiva kate syādyuppatti.

By rule, the kita suffix occurs in the agentive case, and thus it occurs in the agentive sense. And since it is stated, 'ṇādayo tekālikā' (the suffixes beginning with ṇa, etc., pertain to the three tenses), it occurs in all three tenses. As before, the designation as kārita, the elision of ṇ, and vuddhi strengthening occur. Since that which ends in the suffix is without gender, before the syādi affixes are applied, because it ends in a kita suffix, by the rule 'taddhitasamāsakitakā nāmaṃvātavetunādīsu ca', it is treated as a noun, and the syādi affixes arise. Then, in the sense of 'kumbhaṃ karoti' (he makes a pot), by 'amādayo parapadebhī', a second-case tatpuruṣa compound is formed. By 'nāmāna...', etc., it is designated as a compound. By 'tesaṃ vibhattiyo lopā ca', the case ending is elided. By 'pakati cassa sarantassā', it remains in its natural form. Again, because it is a compound, it is treated like a noun, and the syādi affixes arise.

So kumbhakāro, te kumbhakārā iccādi. Itthiyaṃ kumbhakārī, kumbhakāriyo iccādi, tathā kammaṃ karotīti kammakāro. Evaṃ mālākāro, kaṭṭhakāro, rathakāro, suvaṇṇakāro, suttakāro, vuttikāro, ṭīkākāro.

Thus, 'kumbhakāro' (a potter), 'te kumbhakārā' (those potters), and so on. In the feminine, 'kumbhakārī' (a female potter), 'kumbhakāriyo' (female potters), and so on. Likewise, 'kammakāro' (a workman) is one who does work. Similarly, 'mālākāro' (a garland maker), 'kaṭṭhakāro' (a woodworker), 'rathakāro' (a chariot maker), 'suvaṇṇakāro' (a goldsmith), 'suttakāro' (an author of suttas), 'vuttikāro' (a commentator), 'ṭīkākāro' (a sub-commentator).

Gaha upādāne, pattaṃ agaṇhi, gaṇhāti, gaṇhissatīti vā pattaggāho. Evaṃ rasmiggāho, rajjuggāho.

The root 'gaha' in the sense of 'grasping'. 'Pattaggāho' (one who grasps a bowl) is formed from 'pattaṃ agaṇhi' (he grasped a bowl), 'gaṇhāti' (he grasps), or 'gaṇhissati' (he will grasp). Similarly, 'rasmiggāho' (one who grasps the reins), 'rajjuggāho' (one who grasps a rope).

Ve [M 0.0349] tantasantāne, tantaṃ avāyi, vāyati, vāyissatīti vā tantavāyo, “te āvāyā kārite”ti āyādeso, vākye panettha “te āvāyā”ti yogavibhāgena āyādeso. Evaṃ tunnavāyo.

The root 've' in the sense of 'weaving' (lit. continuing a thread). 'Tantavāyo' (a weaver) is formed from 'tantaṃ avāyi' (he wove a thread), 'vāyati' (he weaves), or 'vāyissati' (he will weave). The substitution 'āya' occurs by the rule 'te āvāyā kārite'. Here in the sentence [analysis], the substitution 'āya' occurs by splitting the rule 'te āvāyā'. Similarly, 'tunnavāyo' (a tailor).

Mā parimāṇe, dhaññaṃ amini, mināti, minissatīti vā atthe ṇappaccaye kate –

The root 'mā' in the sense of 'measuring'. When the suffix ṇa is applied in the sense of 'dhaññaṃ amini' (he measured grain), 'mināti' (he measures), or 'minissati' (he will measure) –

“Ṇamhī”ti vattate.

'Ṇamhī' (when ṇa follows) is understood to apply.

564. Ākārantānamāyo.

564. For [roots] ending in 'ā', there is the substitution 'āya'.

Ākārantānaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa āyādeso hoti ṇakārānubandhe paccaye pare, saralopādi. Dhaññamāyo. Evaṃ dānaṃ dadātīti dānadāyo.

For roots ending in 'ā', the final [vowel] is replaced by 'āya' when a suffix with 'ṇ' as an indicatory letter follows; vowel elision, etc., [also apply]. Dhaññamāyo (one who measures grain). Similarly, 'dānadāyo' (a giver of gifts) is from 'dānaṃ dadāti' (he gives a gift).

Kamu kantimhi, dhammaṃ akāmayi, kāmayati, kāmayissatīti vā dhammakāmo puriso, dhammakāmā kaññā, dhammakāmaṃ cittaṃ. Evaṃ atthakāmo, hitakāmo, sukhakāmo, dhammaṃ pāletīti dhammapālo iccādi.

The root 'kamu' in the sense of 'desiring'. 'Dhammakāmo puriso' (a man who desires the Dhamma) is from 'dhammaṃ akāmayi' (he desired the Dhamma), 'kāmayati' (he desires), or 'kāmayissati' (he will desire). Similarly, 'dhammakāmā kaññā' (a woman who desires the Dhamma), 'dhammakāmaṃ cittaṃ' (a mind that desires the Dhamma). In this way, 'atthakāmo' (one who desires benefit), 'hitakāmo' (one who desires welfare), 'sukhakāmo' (one who desires happiness). 'Dhammapālo' (a protector of the Dhamma) is one who protects the Dhamma, and so on.

Damu damane, “ariṃ adami, dameti, damissatī”ti viggahe “dhātuyā”ti adhikāro, “kammādimhī”ti ca vattate.

The root 'damu' in the sense of 'taming'. In the analysis 'ariṃ adami' (he tamed the enemy), 'dameti' (he tames), or 'damissati' (he will tame), the governing rule 'dhātuyā' (after a root) and 'kammādimhi' (when there is an object, etc.) are understood to apply.

565. Saññāyamanu.

565. When it is a specific designation, [the suffix] a and [the augment] nu [are added].

Kammūpapade ādimhi sati saññāyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ dhātuyā appaccayo hoti, upapadante nukārāgamo ca. Ettha ca “nu niggahītaṃ padante”ti sutte “padante”ti vacanato upapadanteyeva nukārāgamo hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Tesu vuddhī”tiādinā ukāralopo. Ayaṃ pana nvāgamo samāsaṃ [M 0.0350] katvā upapadavibhattilope kateyeva hotīti veditabbaṃ.

When an upapada that is an object is present at the beginning, and a specific designation is understood, the suffix 'a' follows the root, and the augment 'nu' is added to the end of the upapada. Here, it should be understood that the augment 'nu' occurs only at the end of the upapada, on the strength of the word 'padante' (at the end of a word) in the rule 'nu niggahītaṃ padante'. The elision of the vowel 'u' occurs by rules such as 'Tesu vuddhī'. This augment 'nu', however, should be understood to occur only after the compound has been formed and the case ending of the upapada has been elided.

566. Nu niggahītaṃ padante.

566. The augment 'nu' becomes a niggahīta at the end of a pada.

Upapadabhūtanāmapadante vattamāno nukārāgamo niggahītamāpajjate, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ, sesaṃ samaṃ, vuddhābhāvova viseso, arindamo rājā.

The augment 'nu', occurring at the end of a nominal pada that is an upapada, becomes a niggahīta. The niggahīta becomes the nasal of the appropriate class. The rest is the same; the only difference is the absence of vuddhi, as in 'arindamo rājā' (the king who tames enemies).

Tathā tara taraṇe, vessaṃ taratīti vessantaro, taṇhaṃ karoti hiṃsatīti taṇhaṅkaro bhagavā. Evaṃ medhaṅkaro, saraṇaṅkaro, dīpaṅkaro.

Similarly, the root 'tara' is in the sense of 'crossing.' 'Vessantaro' is from 'vessaṃ tarati' (he crosses the merchant class). The Blessed One 'Taṇhaṅkaro' is from 'taṇhaṃ karoti hiṃsati' (he destroys craving). Likewise are 'Medhaṅkaro', 'Saraṇaṅkaro', and 'Dīpaṅkaro'.

“Ādimhi, a”iti ca vattate.

And 'ādimhi, a' (at the beginning, the suffix 'a') is carried forward.

567. Pure dadā ca iṃ.

567. And for 'pura' before 'dada', there is 'iṃ'.

Purasadde ādimhi sati “dada dāne”iccetāya dhātuyā appaccayo hoti, purasadde akārassa iñca hoti. Ettha ca “tadanuparodhenā”ti paribhāsato purasaddantasseva iṃ hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Ṇādīnaṃ tekālikattepi upapadatthavisesena atīteyevāyamappaccayo hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Pure dānaṃ adadīti purindado sakko. Idhāpi vibhattilope kateyeva iṃādeso.

When the word 'pura' is at the beginning, the suffix 'a' is applied to the root 'dada' (to give), and the 'a' of the word 'pura' becomes 'iṃ'. Here, it should be noted that according to the maxim 'tadanuparodhena' (without obstructing that), 'iṃ' is substituted only for the final vowel of 'pura'. Although suffixes beginning with 'ṇ' apply in all three times, it should be noted that this suffix 'a' occurs only in the past tense due to the specific meaning of the pre-verb. For example, 'purindado sakko' (Sakka, the former giver) is formed from 'pure dānaṃ adadīti' (he formerly gave gifts). Here too, the 'iṃ' substitution occurs only after the elision of the case ending.

“Kammādimhi, a”iti ca vattate.

And 'kammādimhi, a' (when there is an object, etc., the suffix 'a') is carried forward.

568. Sabbato ṇvu tvāvī vā.

568. From all roots, 'ṇvu', 'tu', and 'āvī' optionally.

Sabbato dhātuto kammādimhi vā akammādimhi vā sati a ṇvu tu āvī iccete cattāro paccayā honti. Vāggahaṇaṃ “akammādimhi vā”ti vikappanatthaṃ.

From all roots, whether there is an object, etc., or not, these four suffixes – 'a', 'ṇvu', 'tu', and 'āvī' – occur. The word 'vā' (or) is for the purpose of making an option, as in 'or when there is not an object, etc.'

Appaccaye [M 0.0351] tāva – dhara dhāraṇe, dhammaṃ adhari, dharati, dharissatīti vā dhammadharo. Evaṃ vinayadharo. Tathā taṃ karotīti takkaro, dvittaṃ. Evaṃ hitakaro, divasakaro, dinakaro, divākaro, nisākaro, dhanuṃ gaṇhātīti dhanuggaho. Evaṃ kaṭaggaho, sabbakāmaṃ dadātīti sabbakāmadado, sabbadado.

First, regarding the suffix 'a': from the root 'dhara' in the sense of 'holding.' 'Dhammadharo' (one who upholds the Dhamma) is from 'dhammaṃ adhari' (he upheld the Dhamma), 'dharati' (he upholds), or 'dharissati' (he will uphold). Likewise, 'vinayadharo' (one who upholds the Vinaya). Similarly, from 'taṃ karoti' (he does that) comes 'takkaro' (that doer), with duplication. Likewise, 'hitakaro' (one who does good), 'divasakaro' (day-maker, i.e., the sun), 'dinakaro' (day-maker, i.e., the sun), 'divākaro' (day-maker, i.e., the sun), 'nisākaro' (night-maker, i.e., the moon). From 'dhanuṃ gaṇhāti' (he takes a bow) comes 'dhanuggaho' (an archer). Likewise, 'kaṭaggaho' (one who grasps a mat). From 'sabbakāmaṃ dadāti' (he gives all desires) comes 'sabbakāmadado' (one who gives all desires), and 'sabbadado' (one who gives all).

Āto pana – annaṃ adāsi, dadāti, dadissatīti annado. Evaṃ dhanado, saccaṃ sandahatīti saccasandho. Pā pāne, majjaṃ pivatīti majjapo. Tā pālane, gavaṃ saddaṃ tāyatīti gottaṃ. Evaṃ kattari.

Now, from roots ending in 'ā': from 'annaṃ adāsi' (he gave food), 'dadāti' (he gives), or 'dadissati' (he will give) comes 'annado' (a giver of food). Likewise, 'dhanado' (a giver of wealth). From 'saccaṃ sandahati' (he binds to truth) comes 'saccasandho' (one who binds to truth). From the root 'pā' in the sense of 'drinking': from 'majjaṃ pivati' (he drinks liquor) comes 'majjapo' (a drinker of liquor). From the root 'tā' in the sense of 'protecting': from 'gavaṃ saddaṃ tāyati' (he protects the sound of cows) comes 'gottaṃ' (a lineage). Likewise, in the agentive sense.

Akammādimhi pana “yasmā dapetī”ti sutte bhayaggahaṇena sesasādhanepi appaccayo.

However, when there is no object, etc., the suffix 'a' also occurs for the remaining grammatical roles, due to the inclusion of 'bhaya' (fear) in the rule 'yasmā dapetī'.

Nī pāpuṇane vipubbo, vinesi, vineti, vinessati etena, etthāti vā vinayo, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi, ayādeso ca, nayanaṃ nayo. Si sevāyaṃ nipubbo, nissīyittha, nissīyati, nissīyissatīti vā nissayo. Si saye, anusayi, anuseti, anusessatīti vā anusayo.

From the root 'nī' in the sense of 'reaching,' with the prefix 'vi.' 'Vinayo' (discipline) is from 'vinesi' (he disciplined), 'vineti' (he disciplines), or 'vinessati' (he will discipline) by means of this or in this. By the rule 'aññesu ca,' there is vowel strengthening (vuddhi) and the substitution 'aya.' 'Nayo' (method) is from 'nayanaṃ' (leading). From the root 'si' in the sense of 'serving,' with the prefix 'ni.' 'Nissayo' (dependence) is from 'nissīyittha' (he depended), 'nissīyati' (he depends), or 'nissīyissati' (he will depend). From the root 'si' in the sense of 'lying,' with the prefix 'anu.' 'Anusayo' (latent tendency) is from 'anusayi' (he lay latent), 'anuseti' (he lies latent), or 'anusessati' (he will lie latent).

I gatimhi patipubbo, paṭicca ekasmā phalametīti paccayo, samudayo. Ci caye, vinicchīyate anena, vinicchayanaṃ vā vinicchayo, uccayanaṃ uccayo, sañcayo, dhammaṃ vicinātīti dhammavicayo. Khī khaye, khayanaṃ khayo. Ji jaye, vijayanaṃ vijayo, jayo. Kī dabbavinimaye, vikkayanaṃ vikkayo, kayo. Lī silesane, allīyati etthāti ālayo, layo. Evaṃ ivaṇṇantato.

From the root 'i' in the sense of 'going,' with the prefix 'paṭi.' 'Paccayo' (condition) is from 'paṭicca ekasmā phalaṃ eti' (dependent on one, the result comes). 'Samudayo' (origin). From the root 'ci' in the sense of 'accumulating.' 'Vinicchayo' (discernment) is from 'vinicchīyate anena' (it is discerned by this) or 'vinicchayanaṃ' (the act of discerning). 'Uccayo' (accumulation) is from 'uccayanaṃ' (the act of accumulating). 'Sañcayo' (collection). 'Dhammavicayo' (investigation of the Dhamma) is from 'dhammaṃ vicināti' (he investigates the Dhamma). From the root 'khī' in the sense of 'destroying.' 'Khayo' (destruction) is from 'khayanaṃ' (the act of destroying). From the root 'ji' in the sense of 'conquering.' 'Vijayo' (victory) is from 'vijayanaṃ' (the act of conquering). 'Jayo' (victory). From the root 'kī' in the sense of 'exchange of goods.' 'Vikkayo' (selling) is from 'vikkayanaṃ' (the act of selling). 'Kayo' (buying). From the root 'lī' in the sense of 'clinging.' 'Ālayo' (attachment) is from 'allīyati ettha' (one clings here). 'Layo' (clinging). Thus from roots ending in 'i'.

Āsuṇantīti [M 0.0352] assavā, avādeso, paṭissavanaṃ paṭissavo. Su gatimhi, ābhavaggā savantīti āsavā. Ru sadde, ravatīti ravo. Bhavatīti bhavo. Pabhavati etasmāti pabhavo. Lū chedane, lavanaṃ lavo. Evaṃ uvaṇṇantato.

From 'āsuṇanti' (they hear) comes 'assavā' (obedient ones); there is the substitution 'ava'. 'Paṭissavo' (response) is from 'paṭissavanaṃ' (the act of responding). From the root 'su' in the sense of 'flowing.' 'Āsavā' (influxes) is from 'ābhavaggā savanti' (they flow up to the highest becoming). From the root 'ru' in the sense of 'sounding.' 'Ravo' (sound) is from 'ravati' (it sounds). 'Bhavo' (existence) is from 'bhavati' (it exists). 'Pabhavo' (origin) is from 'pabhavati etasmā' (it arises from this). From the root 'lū' in the sense of 'cutting.' 'Lavo' (a cut) is from 'lavanaṃ' (the act of cutting). Thus from roots ending in 'u'.

Niggaṇhāti, niggahaṇaṃ vā niggaho, paggaho, saṅgaṇhāti tena, saṅgahaṇaṃ vā saṅgaho. Vara varaṇe, saṃvaraṇaṃ saṃvaro. Dara ādare, ādaraṇaṃ ādaro. Āgacchati, āgamananti vā āgamo, āgamīyanti ettha, etena vā atthāti āgamo pariyatti. Sappatīti sappo. Dibbatīti devo. Kamu padavikkhepe, pakkamanaṃ, pakkamatīti vā pakkamo. Evaṃ vikkamo.

'Niggaho' (restraint) is from 'niggaṇhāti' (he restrains) or 'niggahaṇaṃ' (the act of restraining). 'Paggaho' (exertion). 'Saṅgaho' (collection) is from 'saṅgaṇhāti tena' (he collects by that) or 'saṅgahaṇaṃ' (the act of collecting). From the root 'vara' in the sense of 'choosing.' 'Saṃvaro' (restraint) is from 'saṃvaraṇaṃ' (the act of restraining). From the root 'dara' in the sense of 'respecting.' 'Ādaro' (respect) is from 'ādaraṇaṃ' (the act of respecting). 'Āgamo' (arrival) is from 'āgacchati' (he comes) or 'āgamanaṃ' (the act of coming). 'Āgamo' (scripture) is that in which or by which meanings are approached. 'Sappo' (a snake) is from 'sappati' (it creeps). 'Devo' (a god) is from 'dibbati' (he shines). From the root 'kamu' in the sense of 'stepping.' 'Pakkamo' (departure) is from 'pakkamanaṃ' (the act of departing) or 'pakkamati' (he departs). Likewise, 'vikkamo' (valor).

Cara caraṇe, vane caratīti vanacaro, kāmo avacarati etthāti kāmāvacaro loko, kāmāvacarā saññā, kāmāvacaraṃ cittaṃ. Gāvo caranti etthāti gocaro, chaṭṭhītappuriso.

From the root 'cara' in the sense of 'walking.' 'Vanacaro' (a forest-dweller) is from 'vane carati' (he wanders in the forest). 'Kāmāvacaro loko' (the world of the sensual sphere) is that in which desire frequents. Likewise, 'kāmāvacarā saññā' (perceptions pertaining to the sensual sphere), 'kāmāvacaraṃ cittaṃ' (consciousness pertaining to the sensual sphere). 'Gocaro' (pasture) is from 'gāvo caranti ettha' (cows graze here); it is a sixth-case tatpuruṣa compound.

Pādena pivatīti pādapo. Evaṃ kacchapo, tatiyātappuriso.

'Pādapo' (a tree) is from 'pādena pivati' (it drinks with its foot). Likewise, 'kacchapo' (a tortoise). This is a third-case tatpuruṣa compound.

Ruha janane, sirasmiṃ ruhatīti siroruho, guhāyaṃ sayatīti guhāsayaṃ cittaṃ. Evaṃ kucchisayā vātā. Ṭhā gatinivattimhi, pabbate aṭṭhāsi, tiṭṭhati, ṭhassatīti vā pabbataṭṭho puriso, pabbataṭṭhā nadī, pabbataṭṭhaṃ osadhaṃ. Evaṃ thalaṭṭhaṃ, jalaṭṭhaṃ, sattamītappuriso.

From the root 'ruha' in the sense of 'growing.' 'Siroruho' (hair) is from 'sirasmiṃ ruhati' (it grows on the head). 'Guhāsayaṃ cittaṃ' (consciousness dwelling in a cave) is from 'guhāyaṃ sayati' (it lies in a cave). Likewise, 'kucchisayā vātā' (winds dwelling in the belly). From the root 'ṭhā' in the sense of 'stopping movement.' 'Pabbataṭṭho puriso' (a man standing on a mountain) is from 'pabbate aṭṭhāsi' (he stood on a mountain), 'tiṭṭhati' (he stands), or 'ṭhassati' (he will stand). Likewise, 'pabbataṭṭhā nadī' (a river on a mountain), 'pabbataṭṭhaṃ osadhaṃ' (medicine on a mountain). Likewise, 'thalaṭṭhaṃ' (standing on land), 'jalaṭṭhaṃ' (standing in water). This is a seventh-case tatpuruṣa compound.

569. Gahassupadhasse vā.

569. The penultimate vowel of 'gaha' optionally becomes 'e'.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa upadhassa ettaṃ hoti vā, upadhāti antakkharato pubbakkharassa parasamaññā, gayhatīti gehaṃ, gahaṃ vā.

The penultimate vowel of the root 'gaha' optionally becomes 'e'. 'Upadhā' is another name for the letter before the final letter. 'Gehaṃ' (a house) or 'gahaṃ' (a house) is from 'gayhati' (it is grasped).

Ṇvuppaccaye [M 0.0353] rathaṃ karotīti atthe ṇvuppaccayo, so ca “aññe kita”ti kitasaññattā “kattari kita”ti kattariyeva bhavati, tato kāritabyapadesa ṇalopavuddhiyo.

Regarding the suffix 'ṇvu': the suffix 'ṇvu' is applied in the sense of 'rathaṃ karoti' (he makes a chariot). And since it is designated as a 'kita' suffix by the rule 'aññe kita' (other suffixes are 'kita'), it occurs only in the agentive sense by the rule 'kattari kita' ('kita' suffixes are used in the agentive sense). Then there are the designation as causative, the elision of 'ṇ', and vowel strengthening (vuddhi).

570. Anakā yuṇvūnaṃ.

570. 'Ana' and 'aka' are substituted for 'yu' and 'ṇvu'.

Yuṇvuiccetesaṃ paccayānaṃ ana akaiccete ādesā hontīti akādeso. Sesaṃ kumbhakārasaddasamaṃ, rathakārako. Tathā annaṃ dadātīti annadāyako, “ākārantānamāyo”ti āyādeso, “itthiyamato āpaccayo”ti āpaccayo, “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā akārassa ikāro, annadāyikā kaññā, annadāyakaṃ kulaṃ. Lokaṃ netīti lokanāyako, vineti satteti vināyako, “te āvāyā kārite”ti āyādeso.

For the suffixes 'yu' and 'ṇvu', the substitutions 'ana' and 'aka' occur; thus, there is the substitution 'aka'. The rest is similar to the word 'kumbhakāra' (potter). For example, 'rathakārako' (a chariot-maker). Similarly, 'annadāyako' (a giver of food) is from 'annaṃ dadāti' (he gives food). The substitution 'āya' occurs by the rule 'ākārantānamāyo'. The suffix 'ā' occurs in the feminine by the rule 'itthiyamato āpaccayo'. By rules beginning with 'tesu vuddhī,' the 'a' of 'aka' becomes 'i', resulting in 'annadāyikā kaññā' (a girl who gives food) and 'annadāyakaṃ kulaṃ' (a family that gives food). 'Lokanāyako' (a world-leader) is from 'lokaṃ neti' (he leads the world). 'Vināyako' (a guide) is from 'vineti satte' (he guides beings). The substitution 'āya' occurs by the rule 'te āvāyā kārite'.

Akammūpapade karotīti kārako, kārikā, kārakaṃ. Dadātīti dāyako, dāyikā, dāyakaṃ. Netīti nāyako, nāyikā, nāyakaṃ. Bhagavato ovādānusāsaniṃ asuṇi, suṇāti, suṇissatīti vā sāvako, sāvikā, āvādeso. Lunātīti lāvako. Pu pavane, punātīti pāvako, bhavatīti bhāvako, upāsatīti upāsako, upāsikā. Gaṇhātīti gāhako.

When there is no object as a pre-verb: from 'karoti' (he does) come 'kārako' (a doer, masc.), 'kārikā' (fem.), 'kārakaṃ' (neut.). From 'dadāti' (he gives) come 'dāyako' (a giver, masc.), 'dāyikā' (fem.), 'dāyakaṃ' (neut.). From 'neti' (he leads) come 'nāyako' (a leader, masc.), 'nāyikā' (fem.), 'nāyakaṃ' (neut.). From 'Bhagavato ovādānusāsaniṃ asuṇi, suṇāti, suṇissatīti' (he heard, hears, or will hear the Blessed One’s advice and instruction) come 'sāvako' (a disciple, masc.) and 'sāvikā' (fem.); the substitution 'āva' occurs. From 'lunāti' (he reaps) comes 'lāvako' (a reaper). From the root 'pu' in the sense of 'purifying'; from 'punāti' (he purifies) comes 'pāvako' (a purifier). From 'bhavati' (he exists) comes 'bhāvako' (a developer). From 'upāsati' (he attends) come 'upāsako' (a male lay disciple) and 'upāsikā' (a female lay disciple). From 'gaṇhāti' (he grasps) comes 'gāhako' (a grasper).

Pacatīti pācako. Ayaji, yajati, yajissatīti vā yājako. Ettha hi “kagā cajāna”nti cajānaṃ kagatte sampatte –

From 'pacati' (he cooks) comes 'pācako' (a cook). From 'ayaji' (he sacrificed), 'yajati' (he sacrifices), or 'yajissati' (he will sacrifice) comes 'yājako' (a sacrificer). Here, indeed, when 'ca' and 'ja' would become 'ka' and 'ga' by the rule 'kagā cajāna'—

571. Na [M 0.0354] kagattaṃ cajā ṇvumhi.

571. 'Ca' and 'ja' do not become 'ka' and 'ga' when 'ṇvu' follows.

Dhātvantabhūtā cakārajakārā kakāra gakārattaṃ nāpajjante ṇvuppaccaye pareti paṭisiddhattā na bhavati.

The letters 'ca' and 'ja' at the end of a root do not become 'ka' and 'ga', because it is prohibited when the 'ṇvu' suffix follows; thus, it does not occur.

Jana janane, janetīti janako, janikā, “ghaṭādīnaṃ vā”ti ettha vāggahaṇena vuddhi na hoti. Evaṃ khanatīti khanako, sametīti samako, gametīti gamako, dametīti damako, ahani, hanti, hanissatīti vā vadhako, “vadho vā sabbatthā”ti hanassa vadhādeso, hantīti yātako, “hanassa ghāto”ti ṇvumhi ghātādeso, gāvo hanatīti goghātako, rundhatīti rundhako, niggahītāgamo, saṃyogantattā na vuddhi hoti. Evaṃ bhuñjatīti bhuñjako, kiṇātīti kāyako, pāletīti pālako, pūjetīti pūjako.

From the root 'jana' in the sense of 'generating'; from 'janeti' (he generates) come 'janako' (a generator, masc.) and 'janikā' (fem.). Here, by the inclusion of 'vā' in 'ghaṭādīnaṃ vā', vowel strengthening (vuddhi) does not occur. Likewise, from 'khanati' (he digs) comes 'khanako' (a digger); from 'sameti' (he pacifies) comes 'samako' (a pacifier); from 'gameti' (he causes to go) comes 'gamako' (one who causes to go); from 'dameti' (he tames) comes 'damako' (a tamer). From 'ahani' (he struck), 'hanti' (he strikes), or 'hanissati' (he will strike) comes 'vadhako' (a killer); by the rule 'vadho vā sabbatthā', there is the substitution 'vadha' for 'han'. From 'hanti' (he strikes) comes 'yātako' (a tormentor). By the rule 'hanassa ghāto', there is the substitution 'ghāta' for 'han' when 'ṇvu' follows; from 'gāvo hanati' (he strikes cows) comes 'goghātako' (a cow-killer). From 'rundhati' (he obstructs) comes 'rundhako' (an obstructer); there is the augment 'niggahīta', and because the root ends in a conjunct consonant, vowel strengthening (vuddhi) does not occur. Likewise, from 'bhuñjati' (he enjoys) comes 'bhuñjako' (an enjoyer); from 'kiṇāti' (he buys) comes 'kāyako' (a buyer); from 'pāleti' (he protects) comes 'pālako' (a protector); from 'pūjeti' (he reveres) comes 'pūjako' (a reverer).

572. Nudādīhi yuṇvūnamanānanākānanakā sakāritehi ca.

572. For the suffixes 'yu' and 'ṇvu' after the 'nud'-group roots and after causative roots, the substitutions are 'ana', 'ānana', 'aka', and 'ānanaka'.

Nudādīhi dhātūhi, sakāritehi ca dhātūhi paresaṃ yuṇvuppaccayānaṃ yathākkamaṃ ana ānana aka ānanakaiccete ādesā honti.

For the suffixes 'yu' and 'ṇvu' that follow the 'nud'-group roots and causative roots, these substitutions 'ana', 'ānana', 'aka', and 'ānanaka' occur respectively.

Ettha hi –

Here, indeed—

Sakāritehi yuṇvūnaṃ, kāriyassa vidhānato;

Kiccakitthambhavo dhātu-ppaccayehipi vediyo.

For the suffixes `yu` and `ṇvu` with causative roots, the nature of the derivative as a `kicca` (gerundive) or `kittha` (primary derivative) is to be known from the prescription of the action, and also from the root and suffixes.

Nuda khepe papubbo, panudi, panudati, panudissatīti vā atthe ṇvuppaccayo, tassiminā akādeso, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā nudissa dīgho, panūdako.

`Nud` in the sense of 'throwing away', prefixed with 'pa'; in the sense of 'has thrown away', 'throws away', or 'will throw away', the `ṇvu` suffix is applied. By this rule, the `aka` substitution occurs for the suffix, and by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' and so on, there is lengthening of `nud`, resulting in `panūdako` (one who throws away).

Sūda [M 0.0355] paggharaṇe, sūdatīti sūdako. Ñā avabodhane, aññāsi, jānāti, jānissatīti vā atthe ṇvuppaccayo, tassānena ānanakādeso, “ñāssa jājaṃnā”ti jādeso, saralopādi, jānanako.

`Sūda` in the sense of 'flowing forth'; one who flows forth is `sūdako`. `Ñā` in the sense of 'understanding'; in the sense of 'has understood', 'understands', or 'will understand', the `ṇvu` suffix is applied. By this rule, the `ānanaka` substitution occurs for the suffix, and by the rule 'ñāssa jājaṃnā', the `jā` substitution occurs for the root, with vowel elision and so on, resulting in `jānanako`.

Sakāritehi pana āṇa pesane, āṇāpesi, āṇāpeti, āṇāpessatīti vā atthe “sabbato ṇvutvāvī vā”ti ṇvuppaccayo, tassiminā akādeso, saralopādi, āṇāpako, saññāpetīti saññāpako, sañjānanako, ettha ānanakādeso, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā kāritalopo. Tathā dāpetīti dāpako, “anakā yuṇvūna”nti akādeso, patiṭṭhāpetīti patiṭṭhāpako, nibbānaṃ sampāpetīti nibbānasampāpako, kārāpetīti kārāpako, kārāpikā iccādi.

However, from causative roots: `āṇa` in the sense of 'commanding'; in the sense of 'has commanded', 'commands', or 'will command', the `ṇvu` suffix is applied according to "sabbato ṇvutvāvī vā". By this rule, the `aka` substitution occurs for the suffix, with vowel elision and so on, resulting in `āṇāpako`. Similarly, from `saññāpeti` comes `saññāpako`, and also `sañjānanako`, where the `ānanaka` substitution occurs, and by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' and so on, there is elision of the causative marker. Likewise, from `dāpeti` comes `dāpako`, with the `aka` substitution occurring for the suffix according to "anakā yuṇvūnaṃ". From `patiṭṭhāpeti` comes `patiṭṭhāpako`; from `nibbānaṃ sampāpeti` comes `nibbānasampāpako`; from `kārāpeti` comes `kārāpako`, `kārāpikā`, and so on.

Tuppaccaye akāsi, karoti, karissatīti vā atthe “sabbato ṇvutvāvī vā”ti tuppaccayo, so ca kitasaññattā ṇvuppaccayo viya sabbattha kattariyeva bhavati.

Regarding the `tu` suffix: in the sense of 'did', 'does', or 'will do', the `tu` suffix is applied according to "sabbato ṇvutvāvī vā". And since it has the designation `kita`, like the `ṇvu` suffix, it occurs everywhere only in the agent sense.

“Antassā”ti vattate.

The word `antassa` (of the final) is carried forward.

573. Karassa ca tattaṃ tusmiṃ.

573. And for `kar`, its final becomes `ta` when `tu` follows.

Karaiccetassa dhātussa antassa rakārassa takārattaṃ hoti tuppaccaye pare. Casaddena bharādīnañca, tato nāmamiva kate syādyuppatti, “satthupitādīnamā sismiṃ silopo cā”ti āttaṃ, silopo, tassa kattā takkattā, chaṭṭhīsamāso. Tathā bharatīti bhattā.

For the root `kar`, its final `ra` becomes `ta` when the `tu` suffix follows. And by the word `ca`, this also applies to `bhara` and other roots. Thereafter, it being treated like a noun stem, the case endings `si`, etc., arise. By the rule 'satthupitādīnamā sismiṃ silopo cā', there is lengthening to `ā` and elision of `si`. The phrase `tassa kattā` (the doer of that) forms `takkattā`, a genitive compound. Likewise, one who bears is `bhattā`.

Hara haraṇe, haratīti hattā, bhindatīti bhettā, bheditā vā, chindatīti chettā, dadātīti dātā, bhojanassa dābhā bhojanadātā, sandahatīti sandhātā, avaci, vacati[M 0.0356], vakkhatīti vā vattā, “bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā”ti dhātvantalopo, dvittañca, bhuñjatīti bhottā, abujjhi, bujjhati, bujjhissatīti vā bujjhitā, yakārikārāgamā, jānātīti ñātā, jinātīti jetā, suṇātīti sotā, gaṇhātīti gahetā, bhavatīti bhavitā, saratīti saritā, gacchatīti gantā. “Gama khana hanādīnaṃ tuṃ tabbādīsu na”iti dhātvantassa nattaṃ. Evaṃ khanatīti khantā, hanatīti hantā, maññatīti mantā, pāletīti pāletā, pālayitā.

`Hara` in the sense of 'taking'; one who takes is `hattā`. One who breaks is `bhettā` or `bheditā`. One who cuts is `chettā`. One who gives is `dātā`. One who gives food is `bhojanadātā`. One who connects is `sandhātā`. One who spoke, speaks, or will speak is `vattā`. By the rule "bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā," there is elision of the final of the root and doubling; one who eats is `bhottā`. One who understood, understands, or will understand is `bujjhitā`, with the augment `i` and the `ya` of the stem. One who knows is `ñātā`. One who conquers is `jetā`. One who hears is `sotā`. One who takes is `gahetā`. One who becomes is `bhavitā`. One who remembers is `saritā`. One who goes is `gantā`. By the rule "gama khana hanādīnaṃ tuṃ tabbādīsu na," there is elision of the final of the root. Thus, one who digs is `khantā`. One who strikes is `hantā`. One who thinks is `mantā`. One who protects is `pāletā` or `pālayitā`.

Kārite bhāvetīti bhāvetā, bhāvayitā. Evaṃ sāretā, sārayitā, dāpetā, dāpayitā, hāpetā, hāpayitā, nirodhetā, nirodhayitā, bodhetā, bodhayitā, ñāpetā, ñāpayitā, sāvetā, sāvayitā, gāhebhā, gāhayitā, kāretā, kārayitā, kārāpetā, kārāpayitā iccādi.

In the causative: from `bhāveti` comes `bhāvetā` or `bhāvayitā` (one who causes to be). Likewise: `sāretā`, `sārayitā` (one who causes to proceed); `dāpetā`, `dāpayitā` (one who causes to give); `hāpetā`, `hāpayitā` (one who causes to diminish); `nirodhetā`, `nirodhayitā` (one who causes to cease); `bodhetā`, `bodhayitā` (one who causes to awaken); `ñāpetā`, `ñāpayitā` (one who causes to know); `sāvetā`, `sāvayitā` (one who causes to hear); `gāhetā`, `gāhayitā` (one who causes to seize); `kāretā`, `kārayitā` (one who causes to do); `kārāpetā`, `kārāpayitā` (one who causes to be done), and so on.

Āvīpaccaye disa pekkhane, bhayaṃ apassi, passati, passissatīti vā atthe āvīpaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā disassa dassādeso, bhayadassāvī, bhayadassāvino iccādi daṇḍīva neyyaṃ. Itthiyaṃ bhayadassāvinī. Napuṃsake bhayadassāvi cittaṃ.

Regarding the `āvī` suffix: from `dis` in the sense of 'seeing'; in the sense of 'saw danger', 'sees danger', or 'will see danger', the `āvī` suffix is applied. By the rule 'kvaci dhātū' and so on, the substitution `dassa` occurs for `dis`, resulting in `bhayadassāvī` (one who sees danger), `bhayadassāvino`, and so on. Its declension should be understood to be like `daṇḍī`. In the feminine, it is `bhayadassāvinī`. In the neuter, it is `bhayadassāvi cittaṃ` (a mind that sees danger).

Sāsa anusiṭṭhimhi, sadevakaṃ lokaṃ diṭṭhadhammikādivasena sāsatīti atthe –

`Sāsa` in the sense of 'instructing'; in the sense of 'one who instructs the world with its deities by means of what pertains to this life and so on'—

574. Sāsādīhi ratthu.

574. From `sāsa` and other roots, the `ratthu` suffix occurs.

Sāsaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi ratthuppaccayo hoti.

From the roots `sāsa` and so on, the `ratthu` suffix occurs.

“Ramhi ranto rādi no”ti rādilopo, saralopādi, nāmabyapadeso, syādyuppatti, āttaṃ, silopo. Satthā, satthāro.

By the rule 'Ramhi ranto rādi no', there is elision of the initial `ra`. Then, with vowel elision and so on, there is the designation as a noun stem, the arising of case endings, lengthening to `ā`, and elision of `si`. Thus are formed `Satthā` (teacher) and `satthāro` (teachers).

Pā rakkhaṇe, puttaṃ pātīti atthe –

`Pā` in the sense of 'protecting'; in the sense of 'one who protects an offspring'—

575. Pādito [M 0.0357] ritu.

575. From `pā` and other roots, the `ritu` suffix occurs.

Pāiccevamādito dhātuggaṇato rituppaccayo hoti, rādilopo saralopādi. Pitā. Dhara dhāraṇe, mātāpitūhi dharīyatīti dhītā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ikārassa dīgho.

From the group of roots beginning with `pā`, the `ritu` suffix occurs, with elision of the initial `ra`, vowel elision, and so on. Thus is formed `Pitā` (father). From `dhara` in the sense of 'holding': one who is held by mother and father is `dhītā` (daughter); by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' and so on, there is lengthening of the `i` vowel.

Māna pūjāyaṃ, dhammena puttaṃ mānetīti atthe –

`Māna` in the sense of 'honoring'; in the sense of 'one who honors a son with the Dhamma'—

576. Mānādīhi rātu.

576. From `māna` and other roots, the `rātu` suffix occurs.

Māna bhāsaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rātuppaccayo hoti, rādilopo, mātā. Bhāsa viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, pubbe bhāsatīti bhātā iccādi.

From the roots `māna`, `bhāsa`, and so on, the `rātu` suffix occurs, with elision of the initial `ra`, resulting in `mātā` (mother). `Bhāsa` in the sense of 'clear speech'; one who speaks first is `bhātā` (brother), and so on.

Visa pavesane papubbo, pāvisi, pavisati, pavisissatīti vā atthe –

`Vis` in the sense of 'entering', prefixed with 'pa'; in the sense of 'has entered', 'enters', or 'will enter'—

577. Visa ruja padādito ṇa.

577. From `vis`, `ruj`, `pad`, and other roots, the `ṇa` suffix occurs.

Visa ruja padaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi paro ṇappaccayo hotīti ṇappaccayo. So ca kitasaññattā kattari bhavati, kāritabyapadesaṇalopa vuddhiyo, paveso.

The `ṇa` suffix occurs after the roots `vis`, `ruj`, `pad`, and so on. And since it has the designation `kita`, it occurs in the agent sense. Due to its designation as a `kārita` suffix, there is elision of `ṇ` and `vuddhi` (strengthening) of the vowel, resulting in `paveso`.

Tathā ruja roge, aruji, rujati, rujissatīti vā rogo, “kagācajāna”nti jakārassa gakāro, uppajjatīti uppādo. Phusa phusane, aphusi, phusati, phusissati, phusanti vā tena sampayuttāti phasso, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā phusassa phasso, saṃyogantattā na vuddhi. Bhavatīti bhāvo. Uca samavāye, ucatīti oko, cakārassa kakāro. Aya gatimhi, ayi, ayati, ayissati, ayati vā itoti āyo. Budha avagamane, sammā bujjhatīti sambodho, āharatīti [M 0.0358] āhāro, upahanatīti upaghāto, “hanassa ghāto”ti ghātādeso.

Likewise, from `ruja` in the sense of 'sickness': the act of being sick (was sick, is sick, or will be sick) is `rogo` (sickness). By 'kagācajānaṃ', `ja` becomes `ga`. The act of arising is `uppādo` (arising). From `phusa` in the sense of 'touching': the act of touching (touched, touches, will touch), or that by which one is connected, is `phasso` (contact). By the rule 'kvaci dhātū' and so on, `phus` becomes `phassa`; due to ending in a conjunct consonant, there is no `vuddhi`. The act of becoming is `bhāvo` (existence/state). From `uca` in the sense of 'combination': the act of combining is `oko` (abode), and `ca` becomes `ka`. From `aya` in the sense of 'going': the act of going (went, goes, will go), or that from which one goes, is `āyo` (income). From `budha` in the sense of 'understanding': the act of understanding rightly is `sambodho` (perfect enlightenment). The act of bringing is `āhāro` (food). The act of striking down is `upaghāto` (destruction); by 'hanassa ghāto', the substitution `ghāta` occurs.

Ranja rāge, ranjatīti atthe ṇappaccayo.

`Ranja` in the sense of 'passion' or 'coloring'; in the sense of 'being impassioned' or 'being colored', the `ṇa` suffix is applied.

578. Niggahīta saṃyogādi no.

578. An initial `na` of a conjunct becomes niggahīta.

Saṃyogasmiṃ ādibhūto nakāro niggahītamāpajjate. Niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ, jakārassa gattaṃ, raṅgo.

In a conjunct, an initial `na` becomes `niggahīta`. The `niggahīta` becomes the nasal of the same class as the following consonant, and `ja` becomes `ga`, resulting in `raṅgo` (coloring/passion).

579. Ṇamhi ranjassa jo bhāvakaraṇesu.

579. For `ranj`, its final becomes `ja` when the `ṇa` suffix follows, in the senses of state/action and instrument.

Ranjaiccetassa dhātussa antabhūtassa njassa jakārādeso hoti bhāvakaraṇaiccetesvatthesu vihite ṇakāravatippaccaye pare.

For the root `ranj`, its final `ñj` has the `ja` substitution when a suffix containing the letter `ṇ`, which has been prescribed in the senses of state/action and instrument, follows.

Ettha hi –

Here, indeed –

Ṇamhi ranjassa karaṇe, jādesassa vidhānato;

Akattaripi viññeyyo, kārake ṇassa sambhavoti.

When the `ṇa` suffix follows, for the root `rañj` in the sense of instrument, due to the prescription of the `ja` substitution, it should be understood to occur even in a non-agentive sense, despite its [usual] occurrence in the agentive sense.

Ranjanti anenāti rāgo, rañjīyati anenāti vā rāgo, sayaṃ rañjatītipi rāgo. “Ṇamhi ranjassa jo”ti yogavibhāgena jakāro. Pajjate anenāti pādo, patujjate anenāti patodo, jarīyati anenāti jāro. Evaṃ dāro. Tathā kammādīsu, bhujjatīti bhogo. Evaṃ bhāgo, bhāro, labbhatīti lābho, voharīyatīti vohāro, dīyatīti dāyo, vihaññati etasmāti vighāto, viharanti etthāti vihāro, āramanti etasminti ārāmo. Evaṃ papāto iccādi.

One is impassioned by this, therefore it is `rāgo` (passion); or one is made impassioned by this, therefore it is `rāgo`; or it is impassioned of itself, therefore it is `rāgo`. By splitting the rule 'Ṇamhi ranjassa jo', the letter `ja` is substituted. One goes by this, therefore it is `pādo` (foot). One is goaded by this, therefore it is `patodo` (goad). One is worn out by this, therefore it is `jāro` (paramour). Likewise `dāro` (wife). Similarly, in the sense of object and so on: it is enjoyed, therefore it is `bhogo` (enjoyment). Likewise `bhāgo` (share), `bhāro` (burden). It is obtained, therefore it is `lābho` (gain). It is transacted, therefore it is `vohāro` (transaction). It is given, therefore it is `dāyo` (inheritance). One is struck down by this, therefore it is `vighāto` (destruction). They dwell in this, therefore it is `vihāro` (dwelling). They delight in this, therefore it is `ārāmo` (pleasure ground). Likewise `papāto` (precipice), and so on.

“Ṇa”iti vattate.

The word 'Ṇa' is understood to continue.

580. Bhāve ca.

580. And in the sense of state.

Bhāvatthe bhāvābhidheyye dhātūhi ṇappaccayo hoti. Bhūyate, bhavanaṃ vā bhāvo, paccate, pacanaṃ vā pāko, “kagā cajāna”nti kādeso.

When the meaning of state is to be expressed, the `ṇa` suffix occurs after roots. For example, `bhūyate` (it is), or `bhavanaṃ` (becoming) is `bhāvo`; `paccate` (it is cooked), or `pacanaṃ` (cooking) is `pāko`; by 'kagā cajānaṃ', the `ka` substitution occurs.

Sica paggharaṇe, secanaṃ seko. Suca soke, socanaṃ soko. Caja hānimhi, acajjittha, cajjate, cajjissate, cajanaṃ vā cāgo. Yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadānesu, ijjittha, ijjate, ijjissate, yajanaṃ vā yāgo, yuñjanaṃ yogo. Bhaja sevāyaṃ, abhajjittha, bhajjate, bhajjissate, bhajanaṃ vā bhāgo, arajjittha, rajjate, rajjissate, rajanaṃ vā rāgo, jassa gakāro.

The root `sic` in the sense of 'sprinkling'; `secanaṃ` is `seko`. The root `suc` in the sense of 'grieving'; `socanaṃ` is `soko`. The root `caj` in the sense of 'abandoning'; `acajjittha` (was abandoned), `cajjate` (is abandoned), `cajjissate` (will be abandoned), or `cajanaṃ` is `cāgo`. The root `yaj` in the senses of 'worshipping deities, associating, making, and giving'; `ijjittha` (was sacrificed), `ijjate` (is sacrificed), `ijjissate` (will be sacrificed), or `yajanaṃ` is `yāgo`. `yuñjanaṃ` is `yogo`. The root `bhaj` in the sense of 'serving'; `abhajjittha` (was served), `bhajjate` (is served), `bhajjissate` (will be served), or `bhajanaṃ` is `bhāgo`. [From the root `rañj`:] `arajitṭha` (was colored), `rajjate` (is colored), `rajjissate` (will be colored), or `rajanaṃ` is `rāgo`. For `j` there is `g`.

Daha bhasmīkaraṇe, pariḍayhittha, pariḍayhati, pariḍayhissati, pariḍayhanaṃ vāti atthe ṇappaccayo.

The root `dah` is in the sense of 'reducing to ashes'; the suffix `ṇa` occurs in the sense of 'burning' (`pariḍayhanaṃ`), as in `pariḍayhittha` (was burnt), `pariḍayhati` (is burnt), or `pariḍayhissati` (will be burnt).

“Ṇamhi, vā”ti ca vattate.

The terms 'ṇamhi' and 'vā' are understood to continue.

581. Dahassa do laṃ.

581. For `dah`, the `d` becomes `ḷ`.

Dahaiccetassa dhātussa dakāro lattamāpajjate ṇappaccaye pare vā. Pariḷāho, paridāho. Bhanja avamaddane, bhañjanaṃ bhaṅgo. Sanja saṅge, sañjanaṃ saṅgo, nassa niggahītaṃ.

The `d` of this root `dah` optionally becomes `ḷ` when the suffix `ṇa` follows. Examples: `pariḷāho`, `paridāho`. The root `bhañj` is in the sense of 'crushing'; `bhañjanaṃ` is `bhaṅgo`. The root `sañj` is in the sense of 'attachment'; `sañjanaṃ` is `saṅgo`. The `n` becomes a `niggahīta`.

Paccayehi saṅgamma karīyati, saṅkharīyati tena vāti atthe visarujapadādinā, saṅkharaṇanti atthe “bhāve cā”ti vā ṇappaccayo.

In the sense 'it is made by assembling conditions' or 'it is fabricated by them', the `ṇa` suffix is added by the rule beginning with `visarujapada`, etc.; or, the `ṇa` suffix is added in the sense of 'fabricating' by the rule 'bhāve ca'.

“Ṇamhī”ti vattate.

The term 'ṇamhi' is understood to continue.

582. Purasamupaparīhi [M 0.0360] karotissa khakharā vā tappaccayesu ca.

582. After `pura`, `saṃ`, `upa`, and `pari`, for the root `kar`, the substitutes `kha` and `khara` optionally occur when suffixes beginning with `t` follow.

Pura saṃ upa pariiccetehi parassa karotissa dhātussa kha kharaiccete ādesā honti vā tappaccaye, ṇappaccaye ca pare. “Tappaccayesū”ti bahuvacananiddesena tuṃ tvādīsupi. Dhātvādesassāpi ṭhānopacārena dhātuvohārato “asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite”ti vuddhi, saṅkhāro. Evaṃ parikkhāro, purekkhāro.

For the root `kar` that follows `pura`, `saṃ`, `upa`, and `pari`, the substitutes `kha` and `khara` optionally occur when a suffix beginning with `t` or the suffix `ṇa` follows. By the plural designation 'tappaccayesu', this also applies to `tuṃ`, `tvā`, etc. Since the substitute for the root is also treated as a root by metaphorical extension of place, there is `vuddhi` by the rule 'asaṃyogantassa vuddhi kārite', resulting in `saṅkhāro`. Similarly, `parikkhāro` and `purekkhāro`.

Vāti kiṃ? Upakāro.

Why 'vā' (optionally)? For `upakāro`.

Lubha giddhimhi, lubbhanti tena, sayaṃ vā lubbhati, lubbhanamattameva vā tanti lobho. Dusa appītimhi, dussanti tena, sayaṃ vā dussati, dussanamattameva vā tanti doso. Muha vecitte, muyhanti tena, sayaṃ vā muyhati, muyhanamattameva vā tanti moho iccādi kattukaraṇabhāvesu yathārahaṃ yojetabbaṃ.

The root `lubh` is in the sense of 'greed'; they are greedy because of it, or they themselves are greedy, or just the mere act of being greedy—this is `lobho` (greed). The root `dus` is in the sense of 'displeasure'; they are averse because of it, or they themselves are averse, or just the mere act of being averse—this is `doso` (aversion). The root `muh` is in the sense of 'bewilderment'; they are bewildered because of it, or they themselves are bewildered, or just the mere act of being bewildered—this is `moho` (delusion). And so on, these should be connected appropriately in the senses of agent, instrument, and state.

Gaha upādāne, gayhatīti atthe visarujapadādinā kammani ṇappaccayo.

The root `gah` is in the sense of 'grasping'; in the sense of 'is grasped', the suffix `ṇa` is used in the object sense (kammani) by the rule beginning with `visarujapada`, etc.

583. Gahassa ghara ṇe vā.

583. For `gah`, `ghara` is the optional substitute when `ṇa` follows.

Gahaiccetassa dhātussa gharādeso hoti vā ṇappaccaye pare, saralopādi, gharaṃ, gharāni.

For this root `gah`, `ghara` is the optional substitute when the suffix `ṇa` follows, with elision of the vowel, etc. Examples: `gharaṃ`, `gharāni`.

Vāti kiṃ? Gaṇhāti, gahaṇaṃ vā gāho.

Why 'vā' (optionally)? For `gaṇhāti` (he takes), or `gahaṇaṃ` or `gāho` (taking).

Sambhavatīti atthe –

In the sense of 'it comes into being' –

584. Kvi [M 0.0361] ca.

584. And the suffix `kvi`.

Sabbadhātūhi kvipaccayo hoti, so ca kitasaññattā kattari bhavati.

The suffix `kvi` occurs after all roots, and because it has the designation `kit`, it occurs in the sense of the agent.

585. Kvilopo ca.

585. And elision of `kvi`.

Kvino sabbassa lopo hoti. Kitantattā nāmamiva katvā syādyuppatti, silopo, sambhū. Evaṃ vibhavatīti vibhū, abhibhū, sayambhū.

There is elision of the entire `kvi` suffix. Because it ends in a `kit` suffix, after treating it like a noun, nominal inflections (`si`, etc.) are generated, and `si` is elided, resulting in `sambhū`. Thus, from `vibhavati` (is powerful) comes `vibhū` (powerful one); `abhibhū` (overcomer); `sayambhū` (self-existent).

Tathā dhū kampane, sandhunātīti sandhū. Bhā dittimhi, vibhātīti vibhā, pabhātīti pabhā, saha, saṅgamma vā bhanti, bhāsanti vā etthāti sabhā, sahassa sādeso, niggahītalopo ca.

Similarly, the root `dhū` is in the sense of 'shaking'; from `sandhunāti` (shakes thoroughly) comes `sandhū`. The root `bhā` is in the sense of 'shining'; from `vibhāti` (shines forth) comes `vibhā` (splendor); from `pabhāti` (dawns) comes `pabhā` (light). Where they shine (`bhanti`) together (`saha`), or having gathered (`saṅgamma`) shine, or speak (`bhāsanti`), hence `sabhā` (assembly). For `saha` there is the substitution of `sā`, and elision of the `niggahīta`.

Bhujena gacchatīti atthe kvippaccayo.

In the sense of 'it goes with its coil' (`bhujena gacchati`), the suffix `kvi` is used.

586. Dhātvantassa lopo kvimhi.

586. There is elision of the final letter of the root when `kvi` follows.

Dhātvantassa byañjanassa lopo hoti kvippaccaye pare. Kvilopo, bhujago. Evaṃ urasā gacchatīti urago, turaṃ sīghaṃ turitaturito gacchatīti turago, khe gacchatīti khago, vihāyase gacchatīti vihago, vihādeso, na gacchatīti ago, nago.

There is elision of the final consonant of the root when the suffix `kvi` follows. With elision of `kvi`, we get `bhujago` (snake). Similarly, `urago` (serpent) means one who moves with the chest; `turago` (horse) means one who moves swiftly and fast; `khago` (bird) means one who moves in the sky; `vihago` (bird) means one who moves in the atmosphere, with the substitution of `vihā`; `ago` (mountain) means one who does not move; `nago` (mountain).

Khanu avadhāraṇe saṃpubbo, saṅkhani, saṅkhanati, saṅkhanissatīti vā saṅkho. Ramu kīḷāyaṃ, kuñje ramatīti kuñjaro. Jana janane, kammato jātoti atthe kvippaccayo, dhātvantassa lopādi purimasamaṃ, pañcamītappurisova viseso. Kammajo vipāko, kammajā paṭisandhi, kammajaṃ rūpaṃ[M 0.0362]. Evaṃ cittajaṃ, utujaṃ, āhārajaṃ, attajo putto. Vārimhi jāto vārijo. Evaṃ thalajo, paṅkajaṃ, jalajaṃ, aṇḍajaṃ, sirajaṃ, sattamīsamāso. Dvikkhattuṃ jāto dvijo, pacchā jāto anujo iccādi.

The root khanu is in the sense of 'determining', when preceded by saṃ; from saṅkhani (he determined), saṅkhanati (he determines), or saṅkhanissati (he will determine), thus saṅkho (conch-shell, number). The root ramu is in the sense of 'playing'; he delights in the thicket, thus kuñjaro (elephant). The root jana is in the sense of 'generating'; the suffix kvi is in the sense of 'born from action'; the elision of the final of the root and so on is as before; the only difference is that this is a fifth-case tatpurisa compound. Examples: kammajo vipāko (result born of action), kammajā paṭisandhi (rebirth-linking born of action), kammajaṃ rūpaṃ (form born of action). Similarly, cittajaṃ (mind-born), utujaṃ (temperature-born), āhārajaṃ (nutriment-born), attajo putto (self-born son). Born in water is vārijo (water-born). Similarly, thalajo (land-born), paṅkajaṃ (mud-born), jalajaṃ (water-born), aṇḍajaṃ (egg-born), sirajaṃ (head-born)—these are seventh-case compounds. Born twice is dvijo (twice-born); born after is anujo (later-born), and so on.

Vida ñāṇe, lokaṃ avedīti atthe kvippaccayo.

The root vida is in the sense of 'knowing'; the suffix kvi is in the sense of 'he knew the world'.

“Kvimhī”ti vattate.

The rule concerning kvimhi continues.

587. Vidante ū.

587. To the end of vida, ū.

Vidadhātuno ante ūkārāgamo hoti kvimhi, kvilopo. Lokavidū.

The augment ū is added at the end of the root vida when the suffix kvi follows, and kvi is elided. The result is Lokavidū.

Disa pekkhaṇe, imamiva naṃ apassi, passati, passissatīti, ayamiva dissatīti vā atthe kvippaccayo.

The root disa is in the sense of 'seeing'; the suffix kvi is in the sense of 'he saw him like this', 'he sees him like this', 'he will see him like this', or 'he appears like this'.

“Dhātvantassa lopo kvimhī”ti dhātvantalope sampatte –

When the elision of the final of the root is applicable according to the rule, Dhātvantassa lopo kvimhi—

588. Iyatamakiesānamantassaro dīghaṃ kvaci disassa guṇaṃ do raṃ sakkhī ca.

588. The final vowel of ima, ya, ta, amha, kiṃ, eta, and samāna is sometimes lengthened; of the subordinate root disa, its da becomes ra, and sa, kkha, and ī are also substitutes for its final.

Ima ya ta amha kiṃ eta samānaiccetesaṃ sabbanāmānaṃ upamānupapadabhāvena disassa dhātussa guṇabhūtānaṃ anto saro dīghamāpajjate, disaiccetassa dhātussa antassa sa kkha īiccete ādesā ca honti. Disassa dakāro rakāramāpajjateti kvimhi dhātvantassa sasaddādesaṃ katvā kvilopādimhi ca kate iiti nipātanena imasaddassikāre, tassiminā dīghe ca kate syādyuppatti.

Of these pronouns—ima, ya, ta, amha, kiṃ, eta, and samāna—which are subordinate to the root disa by being a comparison and a preceding word, the final vowel becomes long; and for the end of this root disa, these substitutes sa, kkha, and ī occur. The da of disa becomes ra. When kvi follows, after substituting the sound sa for the final of the root and performing the elision of kvi and so on, and after the word ima is irregularly formed as ī and lengthened, the nominal inflections are generated.

Īdiso [M 0.0363] puriso, īdisā kaññā, īdisī vā, īdisaṃ cittaṃ. Tathā yamiva naṃ passati, yo viya dissatīti vā yādiso, yādisā, yādisī, yādisaṃ. Tamiva naṃ passati, so viya dissatīti vā tādiso, tādisā, tādisī, tādisaṃ. Mamiva naṃ passati, ahaṃ viya so dissatīti vā mādiso, mādisā, mādisī, mādisaṃ, maiti nipātanena amhasaddassa masaddādeso. Kimiva naṃ passati, ko viya dissatīti vā kīdiso, kīdisā, kīdisī, kīdisaṃ. Etamiva naṃ passati, eso viya dissatīti vā ediso, etādiso vā, edisā, edisī, edisaṃ, eiti nipātanena etasaddassa ekāro. Samānaṃ katvā naṃ passati, samāno viya dissatīti sādiso, sadiso, saiti nipātanena samānassa sādeso, tadantassa vā dīgho, sādisā, sādisī, sadisā, sadisī, sādisaṃ, sadisaṃ.

Examples: īdiso puriso (a man of such a kind), īdisā kaññā (a maiden of such a kind), or īdisī, īdisaṃ cittaṃ (a mind of such a kind). Similarly, in the sense of 'he sees him like whom', or 'he appears like whom', we have yādiso, yādisā, yādisī, yādisaṃ. In the sense of 'he sees him like that', or 'he appears like that', we have tādiso, tādisā, tādisī, tādisaṃ. In the sense of 'he sees him like me', or 'he appears like me', we have mādiso, mādisā, mādisī, mādisaṃ; by the irregular formation of mā, the word amha is substituted by mā. In the sense of 'he sees him like what', or 'he appears like what', we have kīdiso, kīdisā, kīdisī, kīdisaṃ. In the sense of 'he sees him like this', or 'he appears like this', we have ediso, or etādiso, edisā, edisī, edisaṃ; by the irregular formation of e, the word eta becomes e. In the sense of 'he sees him as equal', or 'he appears as equal', we have sādiso, sadiso; by the irregular formation of sa, samāna is substituted by sā, or its final vowel is lengthened, resulting in sādisā, sādisī, sadisā, sadisī, sādisaṃ, sadisaṃ.

Dakārassa rakārādese pana īriso, yāriso, tāriso, māriso, kīriso, eriso, sāriso, sariso. Kkhādese īdikkho, yādikkho, tādikkho, mādikkho, kīdikkho, edikkho, sādikkho, sadikkho. Rakārādese sārikkho, sarikkho, īkārādese īdī, yādī, tādī, mādī, kīdī, edī, sādī.

However, when the sound da is substituted by the sound ra, we have īriso, yāriso, tāriso, māriso, kīriso, eriso, sāriso, sariso. When kkha is substituted, we have īdikkho, yādikkho, tādikkho, mādikkho, kīdikkho, edikkho, sādikkho, sadikkho. When the sound ra is substituted, we have sārikkho, sarikkho. When the sound ī is substituted, we have īdī, yādī, tādī, mādī, kīdī, edī, sādī.

Casaddena tumhādiupapadepi tumhe viya dissatīti tumhādiso, tumhādisī, khandhā viya dissantīti khandhādisā iccādi.

By the word ca (and), the rule also applies when tumha and other words are the preceding word. For example, in the sense of 'he appears like you', we have tumhādiso, tumhādisī. In the sense of 'they appear like the aggregates', we have khandhādisā, and so on.

Dhara dhāraṇe, apāyesvapatamāne adhigatamaggādike satte dhāreti, dharanti tenāti vā, salakkhaṇaṃ dhāreti vā, paccayehi dharīyati vāti atthe –

The root dhara is in the sense of 'holding'; in the sense that it holds beings who have attained the path and so on from falling into the lower realms; or that they hold by means of it; or that it holds its own characteristic; or that it is held by conditions—

589. Dharādīhi [M 0.0364] rammo.

589. After dhara and other roots, the suffix ramma.

Dharaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rammappaccayo hoti.

The suffix ramma occurs after the root dhara and similar roots.

So ca –

And it—

Kammaggahaṇabho bhāva- kammesūtettha vediyo;

Akattaripi hotīti, kārake rammappaccayo.

It is to be known here that this suffix is used in the senses of state (bhāva) and object (kamma); since it also occurs in a non-agentive sense, the suffix ramma is used for a case-role (kāraka).

Rādilopo, dhammo, evaṃ karīyatīti kammaṃ. Vara varaṇe, vammaṃ.

With elision of ra and so on, we get dhammo (Dhamma, nature). Similarly, 'that which is done' is kammaṃ (action). The root vara is in the sense of 'choosing'; hence vammaṃ (armor).

Saṃsa pasaṃsane papubbo, piyaiccupapadaṃ, piyaṃ pasaṃsituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā piyaṃ pasaṃsanasīlo, piyaṃ pasaṃsanadhammo, piyaṃ pasaṃsane sādhukārīti vā atthe –

The root saṃsa is in the sense of 'praising', when preceded by pa, and when piya is the preceding word; in the sense of 'one whose nature it is to praise what is dear', or 'one who is by nature a praiser of what is dear', 'one whose practice is to praise what is dear', or 'one who acts well in praising what is dear'—

590. Tassīlādīsu ṇītvāvī ca.

590. In the senses of tassīla and so on, the suffixes ṇī, tu, and āvī also occur.

Sīlaṃ pakati, tassīla taddhamma tassādhukārīsvatthesu gamyamānesu sabbadhātūhi ṇī tu āvīiccete paccayā hontīti kattari ṇīpaccayo, saṃyogantattāna vuddhi. Sesaṃ neyyaṃ.

Sīla is nature. When the senses of tassīla (having that as one's nature), taddhamma (having that as one's practice), and tassādhukārī (acting well in that) are understood, these suffixes ṇī, tu, and āvī occur after all roots. Thus, the suffix ṇī is in the agentive sense. There is no vuddhi because the root ends in a conjunct consonant. The rest is to be inferred.

Piyapasaṃsī rājā. Atha vā piyaṃ pasaṃsi, pasaṃsati, pasaṃsissati vā sīlena vā dhammena vā sādhu vāti piyapasaṃsī, piyapasaṃsinī, piyapasaṃsi kulaṃ. Brahmaṃ carituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā brahmaṃ carati sīlena, dhammena, sādhu vāti brahmacārī, brahmacārinī, brahmacāri. Evaṃ saccavādī, dhammavādī, sīghayāyī, pāpakārī, mālākārī iccādi.

Example: Piyapasaṃsī rājā (a king who is wont to praise what is pleasing). Or, in the sense of 'he praised, praises, or will praise what is pleasing by nature, by practice, or well', we have piyapasaṃsī (masculine), piyapasaṃsinī (feminine), piyapasaṃsi kulaṃ (neuter, a family that is wont to praise what is pleasing). Or, in the sense of 'one whose nature it is to live the holy life', or 'one who lives the holy life by nature, by practice, or well', we have brahmacārī (masculine), brahmacārinī (feminine), brahmacāri (neuter). Similarly, saccavādī (one who is wont to speak truth), dhammavādī (one who is wont to speak Dhamma), sīghayāyī (one who is wont to go swiftly), pāpakārī (one who is wont to do evil), mālākārī (one who is wont to make garlands), and so on.

Casaddena attamānepi ṇī, paṇḍitaṃ attānaṃ maññatīti paṇḍitamānī bālo, bahussutamānī iccādi.

By the word ca, the suffix ṇī is also used in the sense of 'thinking oneself to be'. For example, 'a fool who thinks himself wise' is paṇḍitamānī bālo. Similarly, bahussutamānī (one who thinks himself learned), and so on.

Vatu [M 0.0365] vattane papubbo, pasayha pavattituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti atthe iminā tuppaccayo, pasayhapavattā. Atha vā vaca viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, pasayha pavattituṃ sīlamassāti pasayhapavattā, pasayhapavattāro, bhujādittā dhātvantalopadvittāni, sesaṃ kattusamaṃ.

The root vatu is in the sense of 'occurring', when preceded by pa; in the sense of 'one whose nature it is to proceed forcefully', by this rule the suffix tu is added, resulting in pasayhapavattā (one who proceeds forcefully). Alternatively, the root vaca is in the sense of 'clear speech'; in the sense of 'one whose nature it is to proceed forcefully', we have pasayhapavattā (singular), pasayhapavattāro (plural). Because it belongs to the bhuj-group, there is elision of the final of the root and doubling; the rest is like the agent noun kattu.

Bhayaṃ passituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā bhayaṃ dassanasīlo, bhayaṃ dassanadhammo, bhayaṃ dassane sādhukārīti vā bhayadassāvī, bhayadassāvinī, bhayadassāvi cittaṃ. Evaṃ ādīnavadassāvī.

In the sense of 'one whose nature it is to see danger', or 'one who is by nature a seer of danger', 'one whose practice is to see danger', or 'one who acts well in seeing danger', we have bhayadassāvī (a seer of danger), bhayadassāvinī (a female seer of danger), bhayadassāvi cittaṃ (a mind that sees danger). Similarly, ādīnavadassāvī (a seer of drawbacks).

“Tassīlādīsū”ti adhikāro.

The governing rule is Tassīlādīsu.

591. Sadda ku dha ca la ma ṇḍa ttha rucādīhi yu.

591. After the roots sadda, ku, dha, cala, maṇḍa, ttha, and the ruc-group, the suffix yu.

Sadda ku dha ca la maṇḍatthehi dhātūhi, rucādīhi ca yuppaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu.

After the roots sadda, ku, dha, cala, maṇḍa, ttha, and after the ruc-group, the suffix yu occurs in the senses of tassīla and so on.

Ghusa sadde, ghosituṃ sīlaṃ assāti vā ghosanasīloti vā aghosayi, ghosayati, ghosayissati sīlena, dhammena, sādhu vāti atthe iminā yuppaccayo, tassa “anakā yuṇvūna”nti anādeso, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi, so ghosano, sā ghosanā. Bhāsa viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, bhāsituṃ sīlamassāti vā bhāsanasīlo, bhāsanadhammo, bhāsane sādhukārīti vā bhāsano.

The root ghusa is in the sense of 'sound'. In the sense of 'one whose nature it is to proclaim', or 'one who is by nature a proclaimer', or 'one who proclaimed, proclaims, or will proclaim by nature, by practice, or well', the suffix yu is applied by this rule. For this suffix, there is the substitute ana by the rule Anakā yuṇvūnaṃ, and there is vuddhi by Aññesu ca. Thus we have ghosano (masculine) and ghosanā (feminine). The root bhāsa is in the sense of 'clear speech'. In the sense of 'one whose nature it is to speak', or 'one who is by nature a speaker', 'one whose practice is to speak', or 'one who acts well in speaking', we have bhāsano.

Kudha kope, kujjhituṃ sīlamassāti vā kujjhanasīloti vā kodhano, kodhanā, kodhanaṃ.

The root kudha is in the sense of 'anger'. In the sense of 'one whose nature it is to be angry', or 'one who is by nature angry', we have kodhano (masculine), kodhanā (feminine), kodhanaṃ (neuter).

Rusa rose, rosituṃ sīlamassāti vā rosanasīloti vā rosano.

The root rusa is in the sense of 'anger'. One whose characteristic is to be angry, or one whose nature is to be angry—thus, rosano.

Cala kampane, calituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā calati sīlenāti vā calano. Kapicalane, kampituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā [M 0.0366] akampi, kampati, kampissati sīlenāti vā kampano, ikārānubandhidhātusarato “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā, “niggahītañcā”ti vā niggahītāgamo. Phadi kiñcicalane, phandituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā phandati sīlenāti vā phandano.

The root cala is in the sense of 'shaking'. One whose characteristic is to shake, or one who shakes by characteristic—thus, calano. The root kapi is in the sense of 'shaking'. One whose characteristic is to tremble, or one who trembled, trembles, or will tremble by characteristic—thus, kampano. The nasal augment is due to the root having the indicatory letter 'i', by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., or by 'niggahītañca'. The root phadi is in the sense of 'slight shaking'. One whose characteristic is to quiver, or one who quivers by characteristic—thus, phandano.

Maḍi bhūsāyaṃ, maṇḍayituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā maṇḍayati sīlenāti vā maṇḍano. Bhūsa alaṅkāre, bhūsanasīloti vā abhūsayi, bhūsayati, bhūyayissati sīlenāti vā bhūsano, bhūsanā, bhūsanaṃ.

The root maḍi is in the sense of 'adornment'. One whose characteristic is to adorn, or one who adorns by characteristic—thus, maṇḍano. The root bhūsa is in the sense of 'decoration'. One whose nature is to adorn, or one who adorned, adorns, or will adorn by characteristic—thus, bhūsano (masculine), bhūsanā (feminine), bhūsanaṃ (neuter).

Ruca dittimhi, arucci, ruccati, ruccissati sīlenāti vā rocano. Juta dittimhi, ajoti, jotati, jotissati sīlenāti vā jotano. Vaḍḍha vaḍḍhane, vaḍḍhituṃ sīlamassāti vaḍḍhano iccādi.

The root ruca is in the sense of 'shining'. One who shone, shines, or will shine by characteristic—thus, rocano. The root juta is in the sense of 'shining'. One who shone, shines, or will shine by characteristic—thus, jotano. The root vaḍḍha is in the sense of 'growth'. One whose characteristic is to grow—thus, vaḍḍhano, and so on.

592. Pārādigamimhā rū.

592. From the root gami preceded by pāra and so on, the suffix rū is applied.

Pārādiupapadehi parasmā gamiiccetasmā dhātumhā paro rūpaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu kattariyeva. Pāro ādi yesaṃ te pārādayo, pārādīhi gami pārādigami. Rādilopo, bhavapāraṃ gantuṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā bhavapāraṃ gamanasīlo, bhavapāraṃ gamanadhammo, bhavapāraṃ gamane sādhukārīti vā bhavapāragū, bhavapāraguno. Antaṃ gamanasīlo antagū. Evaṃ vedagū, addhagū.

After the root gami, when preceded by pāra and so on, the suffix rū occurs in the senses of 'having that characteristic' and others, only in the agentive case. 'Pārādayo' are those which begin with 'pāra'; 'pārādigami' is the root gami preceded by 'pārādi'. There is elision of the 'r' and so on. One whose characteristic is to go to the far shore of existence, or one whose nature is to go to the far shore of existence, or one who does well in going to the far shore of existence—thus, bhavapāragū or bhavapāraguno. One whose characteristic is to go to the end is antagū. Similarly, vedagū (one who has gone to the end of the Vedas or knowledge), and addhagū (one who has gone to the end of the path).

“Rū”ti vattate.

The suffix 'rū' is continued.

593. Bhikkhādito ca.

593. And also from bhikkha and so on.

Bhikkhaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi rūpaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu. Bhikkha yācane, bhikkhituṃ sīlaṃ yassāti vā abhikkhi, bhikkhati, bhikkhissati sīlenāti vā bhikkhanadhammoti [M 0.0367] vā bhikkhane sādhukārīti vā bhikkhu, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā rassattaṃ. Ikkha dassanaṅkesu, saṃsāre bhayaṃ ikkhatītipi bhikkhu, vijānituṃ sīlaṃ yassa, vijānanasīloti vā viññū, sabbaṃ jānātīti sabbaññū. Evaṃ mattaññū, dhammaññū, atthaññū, kālaññū, kataññū iccādayo.

From the roots bhikkha and so on, the suffix rū occurs in the senses of 'having that characteristic' and others. The root bhikkha is in the sense of 'begging'. One whose characteristic is to beg, or one who begged, begs, or will beg by characteristic, or one whose nature is to beg, or one who does well in begging—thus, bhikkhu. By the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., there is shortening of the vowel. The root ikkha is in the sense of 'seeing' or 'marking'. Or one who sees danger in saṃsāra—thus, bhikkhu. One whose characteristic is to know, or one whose nature is to know—thus, viññū (the wise one). One who knows all—thus, sabbaññū (the all-knowing one). Similarly, mattaññū (one who knows moderation), dhammaññū (one who knows the Dhamma), atthaññū (one who knows the meaning), kālaññū (one who knows the proper time), kataññū (one who knows what has been done), and so on.

594. Hanatyādīnaṃ ṇuko.

594. For hanati and so on, the suffix ṇuka is applied.

Hanatyādīnaṃ dhātūnamante ṇukappaccayo hoti tassīlādīsvatthesu kattari, antāpekkhāyaṃ chaṭṭhī, ṇakāro vuddhattho. Āhananasīlo āghātuko, ghātādeso, saralopādi, karaṇasīlo kāruko sippi. Bhī bhaye, bhāyanasīlo bhīruko, rakārāgamo. Ava rakkhaṇe, āvuko pitā.

At the end of roots like hanati and so on, the suffix ṇuka occurs in the senses of 'having that characteristic' and others, in the agentive case. The genitive case is used with reference to the end. The letter 'ṇ' is for the purpose of vuddhi (strengthening). One whose characteristic is striking is āghātuko, with ghāta as the substitute, and elision of vowels, etc. One whose characteristic is making is kāruko, a craftsman. The root bhī is in the sense of 'fear'. One whose characteristic is fearing is bhīruko, with the augment 'ra'. The root ava is in the sense of 'protecting'. Āvuko means father.

595. Saṃhanaññāya vā ro gho.

595. After the root han preceded by saṃ, and after another root, the suffix ra is optionally applied, and gha is substituted for han.

Saṃpubbāya hanaiccetāya dhātuyā, aññāya ca dhātuyā paro rappaccayo hoti, hanassa gho ca. Vāggahaṇaṃ sampiṇḍanatthaṃ, vikappanatthaṃ vā, tena saṅghātotipi siddhaṃ hoti.

From the root hana preceded by saṃ, and from another root, the suffix ra occurs, and gha is substituted for han. The inclusion of 'vā' (or) is for the purpose of combining, or for the purpose of providing an alternative; therefore, saṅghāta is also established.

Hanassevāyaṃ gho hoti, abhidhānānurūpato;

Asaṃpubbā ca ro tena, paṭighotipi sijjhati.

This gha is substituted only for han, according to usage; and by that, the suffix ra is also applied when the root is not preceded by saṃ, thus paṭigha is also established.

Hana hiṃsāgatīsu saṃ pubbo, saṃhanati samaggaṃ kammaṃ samupagacchati, sammadeva kilesadarathe hanatīti vā saṅgho, rādilopo[M 0.0368], samantato nagarassa bāhiye khaññatīti parikhā, itthiyaṃ āpaccayo, antaṃ karotīti antako maccu.

The root hana is in the sense of 'harming' or 'going', when preceded by saṃ. It brings together, it approaches collective action, or it rightly destroys the defilements and anxieties—thus, saṅgha. There is elision of 'r' and so on. That which is dug all around outside the city—thus, parikhā (moat). The suffix ā is applied in the feminine. One who makes an end—thus, antako (Death).

“Bhāvakammesū”ti vattate.

The senses of 'state/action' and 'object' are continued.

596. Nandādīhi yu.

596. From nanda and so on, the suffix yu is applied.

Nandaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi paro yuppaccayo hoti bhāvakammesu. “Anakā yuṇvūna”nti yuppaccayassa anādeso, nanda samiddhimhi, nanda nandane vā. Bhāve – nandīyate nandanaṃ. Kamme – anandīyittha, nandīyati, nandīyissati, nanditabbanti vā nandanaṃ vanaṃ, gayhati, gahaṇīyaṃ vā gahaṇaṃ, gaṇhanaṃ vā, caritabbaṃ caraṇaṃ, bhūyate bhavanaṃ, hūyate havanaṃ. Rundhitabbaṃ rundhanaṃ, rodhanaṃ vā, bhuñjitabbaṃ bhuñjanaṃ, bhojanaṃ vā. Bujjhitabbaṃ bujjhanaṃ, bodhanaṃ vā. Sūyati, suti vā savaṇaṃ, pāpīyatīti pāpuṇanaṃ, pāpanaṃ vā, pālīyatīti pālanaṃ iccādi.

From the roots nanda and so on, the suffix yu occurs in the senses of 'state/action' and 'object'. By the rule 'Anakā yuṇvūna', 'ana' is substituted for the suffix yu. The root nanda is in the sense of 'prosperity', or 'delighting'. In the sense of state/action: there is delighting (nandīyate), which is nandanaṃ (delighting). In the sense of object: it was delighted (anandīyittha), is delighted (nandīyati), will be delighted (nandīyissati), or ought to be delighted (nanditabbaṃ)—thus, nandanaṃ, as in 'a delightful forest' (nandanaṃ vanaṃ). That which is taken (gayhati), or ought to be taken (gahaṇīyaṃ), is gahaṇaṃ (taking), or gaṇhanaṃ (grasping). That which ought to be practiced (caritabbaṃ) is caraṇaṃ (practice). There is becoming (bhūyate), which is bhavanaṃ (becoming). There is sacrificing (hūyate), which is havanaṃ (sacrifice). That which ought to be obstructed (rundhitabbaṃ) is rundhanaṃ (obstruction), or rodhanaṃ. That which ought to be enjoyed (bhuñjitabbaṃ) is bhuñjanaṃ (enjoying), or bhojanaṃ (food). That which ought to be understood (bujjhitabbaṃ) is bujjhanaṃ (understanding), or bodhanaṃ. That which is heard (sūyati), or hearing (suti), is savaṇaṃ (hearing). That which is reached (pāpīyati) is pāpuṇanaṃ (reaching), or pāpanaṃ. That which is protected (pālīyati) is pālanaṃ (protection), and so on.

“Yū”ti vattate.

The suffix 'yu' is continued.

597. Kattukaraṇapadesesu ca.

597. And also in the senses of agent, instrument, and locative.

Kattukaraṇapadesaiccetesvatthesu ca sabbadhātūhi yuppaccayo hoti. Ettha ca padesoti adhikaraṇakārakaṃ vuccati. Kattari tāva – rajaṃ haratīti rajoharaṇaṃ toyaṃ. Āramaṇaṃ vijānātīti viññāṇaṃ, vijānanaṃ vā, ānanajādesā. Ghā gandhopādāne, ghāyatīti ghānaṃ, jhe cintāyaṃ, jhāyatīti jhānaṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā āttaṃ.

In all roots, the suffix yu occurs in these senses of agent, instrument, and locative. Here, padesa refers to the locative case. First, in the agentive case: 'one who removes dust'—thus, rajoharaṇaṃ (dust-remover), as in toyaṃ (water). 'One who knows the object'—thus, viññāṇaṃ (consciousness), or vijānanaṃ (knowing); and so on, by the substitution of āna and ja. The root ghā is in the sense of 'taking fragrance'. 'One who smells'—thus, ghānaṃ (nose). The root jhe is in the sense of 'thinking'. 'One who meditates'—thus, jhānaṃ (meditation); by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., there is lengthening to ā.

Karaṇe [M 0.0369] – kara karaṇe, karoti tenāti karaṇaṃ, yathāsarūpaṃ saddā byākarīyanti etenāti byākaraṇaṃ. Pūra pūraṇe, pūrayati tenāti pūraṇaṃ. Dīyati anenāti dānaṃ, pamīyati anenāti pamānaṃ, vuccati anenāti vacanaṃ, panudati, panujjate anenāti vā panūdano. Sūda paggharaṇe, sūdati, sujjate anenāti vā sūdano, suṇāti, sūyati etenāti vā savaṇaṃ. Lū chedane, lunāti, lūyati anenāti vā lavanaṃ, lavaṇaṃ, loṇaṃ vā. Nayati, nīyati etenāti vā nayanaṃ. Pū pavane, punāti, pūyate anenāti vā pavano, sameti, samīyati vā pāpaṃ anenāti samaṇo, samaṇaṃ vā. Tathā bhāveti, bhāvīyati ekāyāti vā bhāvanā. Evaṃ pācanaṃ, pācāpanaṃ iccādi.

In the instrumental case: The root kara is in the sense of 'doing'. That by which one does—thus, karaṇaṃ (instrument). That by which sounds are explained according to their nature—thus, byākaraṇaṃ (grammar/explanation). The root pūra is in the sense of 'filling'. That by which one fills—thus, pūraṇaṃ (filling instrument). That by which it is given—thus, dānaṃ (giving). That by which it is measured—thus, pamānaṃ (measure). That by which it is spoken—thus, vacanaṃ (speech/word). That by which one repels, or is repelled—thus, panūdano (repeller/instrument of repulsion). The root sūda is in the sense of 'flowing'. That by which one flows, or is purified—thus, sūdano (flowing/purifier). That by which one hears, or is heard—thus, savaṇaṃ (ear/hearing). The root lū is in the sense of 'cutting'. That by which one cuts, or is cut—thus, lavanaṃ (cutting instrument), lavaṇaṃ (salt), or loṇaṃ (salt). That by which one leads, or is led—thus, nayanaṃ (leading/eye). The root pū is in the sense of 'purifying'. That by which one purifies, or is purified—thus, pavano (purifier/wind). That by which one calms evil, or by which evil is calmed—thus, samaṇo (an ascetic), or samaṇaṃ (calming). Similarly, that by which one develops, or is developed, with one-pointedness—thus, bhāvanā (development/meditation). Thus, pācanaṃ (cooking), pācāpanaṃ (causing to cook), and so on.

Adhikaraṇe – ṭhā gatinivattimhi, tiṭṭhati tasminti ṭhānaṃ. Evaṃ sayanaṃ, senaṃ vā, āsanaṃ, adhikarīyati etthāti adhikaraṇaṃ.

In the locative case: The root ṭhā is in the sense of 'stopping movement'. That in which one stands—thus, ṭhānaṃ (place). Similarly, sayanaṃ (lying down/bed), or senaṃ (bed), āsanaṃ (sitting/seat). That in which something is undertaken—thus, adhikaraṇaṃ (locative case/base).

Casaddena sampadānāpādānesupi – sammā pakārena dadāti assāti sampadānaṃ, apecca etasmā ādadātīti apādānaṃ.

By the word 'ca', also in the senses of dative (recipient) and ablative: One gives to this in a proper manner—thus, sampadānaṃ (dative case/recipient). One takes from this, having gone away—thus, apādānaṃ (ablative case/source).

598. Saññāyaṃ dādhāto i.

598. In the sense of a proper noun or designation, from the roots dā and dhā, the suffix i is applied.

Saññāyaṃ gamyamānāyaṃ dādhāiccetehi dhātūhi ippaccayo hoti, bhāvakammādiadhikārevāyaṃ, saralopādi. Dā dāne āpubbo, ādīyatītiādi. Evaṃ upādi. Dhā dhāraṇe[M 0.0370], udakaṃ dadhātīti udadhi, tesu vuddhilopādinā saññāyaṃ udakassa udādeso. Jalaṃ dhīyate asminti jaladhi, vālāni dadhāti tasminti vāladhi, sandhīyati, sandadhātīti vā sandhi, nidhīyatīti nidhi. Evaṃ vidhīyati, vidadhāti, vidhānaṃ vā vidhi, sammā, samaṃ vā cittaṃ ādadhātīti samādhi.

When a proper noun or designation is intended, the suffix i occurs after the roots dā and dhā. This is only in the governing rules of state/action, object, etc., with elision of vowels, etc. The root dā is in the sense of 'giving', when preceded by ā. 'It is taken'—thus, ādi (beginning). Similarly, upādi (substratum of existence). The root dhā is in the sense of 'holding'. That which holds water—thus, udadhi (ocean). In these formations, by operations of strengthening, elision, etc., in a proper noun or designation, uda is substituted for udaka. That in which water is held—thus, jaladhi (ocean). That which holds hairs—thus, vāladhi (tail). It is joined, or it joins—thus, sandhi (junction). It is deposited—thus, nidhi (treasure). Similarly, it is arranged, or arranges, or arrangement—thus, vidhi (method). One properly, or evenly, places the mind—thus, samādhi (concentration).

599. Itthiyamatiyavo vā.

599. In the feminine, the suffixes a, ti, and yu are applied optionally.

Itthiyaṃ abhidheyyāyaṃ sabbadhātūhi akāratiyuiccete paccayā honti vā bhāvakammādīsu. Appaccaye tāva jara vayohānimhi, jīrati, jīraṇanti vā jarā, “itthiyamato āpaccayo”ti āpaccayo, paṭisambhijjatīti paṭisambhidā. Paṭipajjati etāyāti paṭipadā. Evaṃ sampadā, āpadā. Upādīyatīti upādā. Sañjānātīti saññā, pajānātīti paññā. Upekkhatīti upekkhā. Cintanaṃ cintā. Patiṭṭhānaṃ patiṭṭhā. Sikkha vijjopādāne, sikkhanaṃ, sikkhīyatīti vā sikkhā. Evaṃ bhikkhā. Jhe cintāyaṃ, parasampattiṃ abhimukhaṃ jhāyatīti abhijjhā, hitesitaṃ upaṭṭhapetvā jhāyatīti upajjhā, upajjhāyo, sammā jhāyati etthāti sajjhā.

When the meaning is feminine, from all roots the suffixes a, ti, yu, and so on, optionally occur in the senses of state, object, and others. First, with the a suffix: The root jara is in the sense of 'loss of youth'. 'It decays', or 'the act of decaying', is jarā (old age). By the rule 'from a stem ending in a, the suffix ā in the feminine', the suffix ā is applied. 'It is analytically known' is paṭisambhidā (analytical knowledge). 'One proceeds by means of this' is paṭipadā (path). Similarly, sampadā (accomplishment) and āpadā (misfortune). 'It is clung to' is upādā (clinging). 'One perceives' is saññā (perception). 'One understands' is paññā (wisdom). 'One looks on with equanimity' is upekkhā (equanimity). 'The act of thinking' is cintā (thought). 'The act of establishing' is patiṭṭhā (foundation). The root sikkha is in the sense of 'acquiring knowledge'. 'The act of training', or 'it is trained in', is sikkhā (training). Similarly, bhikkhā (alms). The root jhe is in the sense of 'thinking'. 'One thinks intently upon another's success' is abhijjhā (covetousness). 'Having presented what is beneficial, one thinks' is upajjhā (female preceptor) or upajjhāyo (male preceptor). 'One recites correctly in this' is sajjhā (recitation).

Isu [M 0.0371] icchāyaṃ, esananti atthe appaccayo, “isu yamūnamanto ccho vā”ti cchādeso, icchā. Puccha pucchane, pucchanaṃ pucchā, tikicchanaṃ tikicchā, ghasitumicchā jighacchā, titikkhā, bubhukkhā, pātumicchā pipāsā, maṇḍūkagatiyā vādhikārato vādesābhāvo. Byāpitumicchā vicchā iccādi.

The root isu is in the sense of 'desiring'. In the sense of 'seeking', the suffix a is applied. By the rule 'isu yamūnamanto ccho vā', there is the substitution of ccha, forming icchā (desire). The root puccha is in the sense of 'asking'; 'the act of asking' is pucchā. 'The act of treating' is tikicchā. 'The desire to eat' is jighacchā.
