Titikkhā (patience), bubhukkhā (hunger), 'the desire to drink' is pipāsā. Or, due to the 'frog's leap' principle or a governing rule, there is an absence of substitution. 'The desire to pervade' is vicchā, and so on.

Tippaccaye sambhavanaṃ sambhūti. Vādhikārato tippaccayamhi na vuddhi, savaṇaṃ suti, nayanaṃ, nīyati etāyāti vā nīti. Mana ñāṇe, maññatīti mati.

With the ti suffix, 'arising' (sambhavanaṃ) becomes sambhūti. Due to the governing rule of 'optionally' (vā), there is no vuddhi strengthening with the ti suffix. 'The act of hearing' (savaṇaṃ) is suti. 'The act of leading' (nayanaṃ), or 'that by which one is led', is nīti. The root mana is in the sense of 'knowing'; 'one thinks' is mati.

“Te, no, timhī”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'te', 'no', and 'timhi' also continue.

600. Gamakhanahanaramādīnamanto.

600. The final of gama, khana, hana, rama, and so on.

Gama khana hana ramaiccevamādīnaṃ makāranakārantānaṃ dhātūnaṃ anto byañjano no hoti tappaccaye, timhi cāti dhātvantalopo. Gamanaṃ, gantabbāti vā gati, upahananaṃ upahati, ramanti tāya, ramaṇaṃ vā rati. Tanu vitthāre, tananaṃ tati. Yamu uparame, niyamanaṃ niyati. “Ramato, ramatī”tiādīsu pana akārabyavahitattā na dhātvantalopo, bhuñjanaṃ bhutti, yuñjanaṃ yutti, “bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā”ti dhātvantalopo, dvittañca. Samāpajjanaṃ, samāpajjateti vā samāpatti, sampatti, “gupādīnañcā”ti dhātvantalopadvittāni. “Kvaci dhātū”tiādinā hādito tissa ni hoti. Hāni, jāni iccādi.

Of roots such as gama, khana, hana, rama, and so on, which end in the consonants m and n, the final consonant is elided before the ta suffix and also before the ti suffix; this is elision of the root's final. Gati is 'the act of going' (gamanaṃ), or 'that which should be gone to' (gantabbā). Upahati is 'the act of striking'. Rati is 'that by which one delights', or 'the act of delighting'. The root tanu is in the sense of 'spreading'; tati is 'the act of spreading'. The root yamu is in the sense of 'restraining'; niyati is 'the act of restraining'. However, in forms such as ramato and ramatī, because of the separation by the vowel a, there is no elision of the root's final. Bhutti is 'the act of eating'; yutti is 'the act of joining'. By the rule 'bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā', there is elision of the root's final and also doubling. Samāpatti is 'the act of attaining', or 'one attains'; sampatti (accomplishment). And by 'gupādīnañca', there is elision of the root's final and doubling. By the rule beginning with 'Kvaci dhātu', after roots beginning with hā, ti becomes ni. For example, hāni (decline), jāni (birth), and so on.

Yuppaccaye cita sañcetane, cetayatīti atthe yuppaccayo, anādesavuddhī, āpaccayo, cetanā. Vida anubhavane[M 0.0372], vedayatīti vedanā. Disī uccāraṇe, desīyatīti desanā, bhāvīyatīti bhāvanā iccādi.

With the yu suffix: the root cita is in the sense of 'intending'. In the sense of 'one intends' (cetayati), the yu suffix is applied; with the substitution of ana for yu, vuddhi strengthening, and the suffix ā, it becomes cetanā. The root vida is in the sense of 'experiencing'; 'one experiences' (vedayati) becomes vedanā. The root disī is in the sense of 'preaching'; 'it is preached' (desīyati) becomes desanā. 'It is developed' (bhāvīyati) becomes bhāvanā, and so on.

“Itthiyaṃ, vā”ti ca vattate.

The rules 'itthiyaṃ' (in the feminine) and 'vā' (optionally) also continue.

601. Karato ririya.

601. From the root kara, the suffix ririya.

Karadhātuto itthiyamanitthiyaṃ vā abhidheyyāyaṃ ririyappaccayo hoti, rādilopo. Kattabbā kiriyā. Karaṇīyaṃ kiriyaṃ.

From the root kara, the suffix ririya occurs when the meaning to be expressed is either feminine or non-feminine, with elision of the initial ra. Kiriyā (feminine) is 'that which should be done'. Kiriyaṃ (neuter) is 'that which is to be done'.

“Kattarī”ti vattate.

The rule 'kattari' (in the agentive sense) continues.

602. Jito ina sabbattha.

602. From the root ji, the suffix ina in all cases.

Jiiccetāya dhātuyā paro inappaccayo hoti sabbakāle kattari. Ji jaye, pāpake akusale dhamme ajini, jināti, jinissatīti vā jino.

After this root ji, the suffix ina occurs in all tenses in the agentive sense. The root ji is in the sense of 'conquering'. One who conquered (ajini), conquers (jināti), or will conquer (jinissati) evil, unwholesome states is a jino.

“Inā”ti vattate.

The rule 'ina' continues.

603. Supato ca.

603. And from the root supa.

Supaiccetāya dhātuyā ca paro inappaccayo hoti. Supa saye, supati, supananti vā supino, supinaṃ.

And after this root supa, the suffix ina occurs. The root supa is in the sense of 'sleeping'. 'One who sleeps' (supati), or 'the act of sleeping' (supanaṃ), is supino or supinaṃ.

Sī saye, “īsaṃ”iti upapadaṃ, īsaṃ sīyati bhavatāti atthe –

The root sī is in the sense of 'lying down'. Īsaṃ is a pre-verb. In the sense 'it is easily lain down' (īsaṃ sīyati) –

604. Īsaṃdusūhi kha.

604. From īsaṃ, du, and su, the suffix kha.

Īsaṃdusuiccetehi upapadehi parehi dhātūhi khappaccayo hoti.

After roots preceded by the pre-verbs īsaṃ, du, and su, the suffix kha occurs.

So ca –

And that suffix –

605. Bhāvakammesu [M 0.0373] kiccaktakkhatthā.

605. The suffixes kicca, kta, kha, and ttha occur in the senses of state (bhāva) and object (kamma).

Bhāvakammaiccetesvatthesu kiccaktakkhatthaiccete paccayā hontīti niyamato bhāvakammesveva hoti. “Kvaci dhātū”ti kkhakārānubandhassa lopo, vuddhi, ayādesadvittāni, īsassayo bhavatā, dukkhena sīyati dussayo, sukhena sīyati sussayo.

In these senses of state (bhāva) and object (kamma), the suffixes kicca, kta, kha, and ttha occur; thus, by rule, they occur only in the senses of state and object. By the rule 'Kvaci dhātu', there is elision of the indicatory letter kh. For example, īsassayo (easily lain down). 'It is lain down with difficulty' (dukkhena sīyati) is dussayo. 'It is lain down with ease' (sukhena sīyati) is sussayo.

Kamme – īsaṃ karīyatīti īsakkaraṃ kammaṃ bhavatā. Evaṃ dukkhena karīyatīti dukkaraṃ hitaṃ bhavatā, sukaraṃ pāpaṃ bālena, dukkhena bharīyatīti dubbharo mahiccho. Sukhena bharīyatīti subharo appiccho. Dukkhena rakkhitabbanti durakkhaṃ cittaṃ. Dukkhena passitabboti duddaso dhammo. Sukhena passitabbanti sudassaṃ paravajjaṃ. Dukkhena anubujjhitabboti duranubodho dhammo. Sukhena bujjhitabbanti subodhamiccādi.

In the sense of object (kamma): 'An action easily done' (īsaṃ karīyati) is īsakkaraṃ. Similarly, 'a benefit done with difficulty' (dukkhena karīyati) is dukkaraṃ. 'Evil is easily done by a fool' (sukaraṃ pāpaṃ bālena). 'One with great desire is supported with difficulty' (dukkhena bharīyati) is dubbharo. 'One with few desires is supported with ease' (sukhena bharīyati) is subharo. 'The mind, which should be guarded with difficulty' (dukkhena rakkhitabbaṃ), is durakkhaṃ. 'The Dhamma, which should be seen with difficulty' (dukkhena passitabbo), is duddaso. 'The fault of others, which is seen with ease' (sukhena passitabbaṃ), is sudassaṃ. 'The Dhamma, which should be understood with difficulty' (dukkhena anubujjhitabbo), is duranubodho. 'That which should be understood with ease' (sukhena bujjhitabbaṃ) is subodhaṃ, and so on.

Budha avagamane, sabbe saṅkhatāsaṅkhatasammutibhede dhamme abujjhi, bujjhati, bujjhissatīti vā atthe –

The root budha is in the sense of 'understanding'. In the sense that one understood (abujjhi), understands (bujjhati), or will understand (bujjhissati) all phenomena in their distinctions as conditioned, unconditioned, and conventional –

“Ta”iti vattate.

The rule 'ta' continues.

606. Budhagamāditthe kattari.

606. For budha, gama, and so on, in the specified sense, in the agentive.

Budhagamuiccegamādīhi dhātūhi tadatthe gamyamāne kattari tappaccayo hoti sabbakāle.

From roots such as budha, gama, and so on, when that specific meaning is understood, the suffix ta occurs in the agentive sense in all tenses.

“Tassā”ti vattate.

The rule 'of ta' continues.

607. Dhaḍhabhahehi dha ḍhā ca.

607. After dh, ḍh, and bh, dha and ḍha respectively.

Dhaḍhanta bhahantehi dhātūhi parassa paccayatakārassa yathākkamaṃ dhakāraḍhakārādesā hontīti dhabhato takārassa [M 0.0374] dhakāro, “hacatutthāna”nti ettha hakāraggahaṇato hakāratopi kvaci dhattaṃ, abyavadhāne cāyaṃ, tena “rundhati, ārādhito, vaḍḍhito, labhitvā, gahito”tiādīsu paccayāgamabyavahitattā na bhavati.

After roots ending in dh, ḍh, and bh, the t of a following suffix is replaced by dh and ḍha respectively. Thus, after dh and bh, the t becomes dh. In the rule 'hacatutthāna', due to the inclusion of h, sometimes after h also there is the substitution of dh. And this rule applies only without separation; therefore, in examples like rundhati, ārādhito, vaḍḍhito, labhitvā, and gahito, it does not apply because of the separation by a suffix or an augment.

608. Hacatutthānamantānaṃ do dhe.

608. For roots ending in 'ha' and the fourth consonants of the vargas, `d` is the substitute when `dh` follows.

Hakāravaggacatutthānaṃ dhātvantabhūtānaṃ dakārādeso hoti dhakāre pare. Buddho bhagavā. Saraṇaṃ agacchi, gacchati, gacchissatīti vā saraṇaṅgato upāsako, “gamakhanahanaramādīnamanto”ti dhātvantalopo. Evaṃ jānātīti ñāto. I gatimhi, upetīti upeto. Cinta cintāyaṃ, cintetīti cittaṃ, “gupādīnañcā”ti dhātvantalopadvittāni. Sanja saṅge, rūpādīsu asajji, sajjati, sajjissatīti vā satto, “bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā”ti dhātvantalopo, dvittañca.

For root-finals that are `h` or the fourth consonants of the vargas, the substitution of `d` occurs when `dh` follows. For example: The Buddha, the Blessed One. A lay follower who has gone for refuge (saraṇaṅgato upāsako) is one who went for refuge (saraṇaṃ agacchi), goes (gacchati), or will go (gacchissatīti) for refuge. By the rule `gamakhanahanaramādīnamanto`, the final of the root is elided. Similarly, `ñāto` is one who knows (jānāti). The root `i` is in the sense of going; `upeto` is one who approaches (upeti). The root `cinta` is in the sense of thinking; `cittaṃ` is that which thinks (cinteti). By `gupādīnañcā`, elision of the root-final and doubling occur. The root `sanja` is in the sense of clinging; `satto` is one who clung (asajji) to forms etc., clings (sajjati), or will cling (sajjissatīti). By `bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā`, elision of the root-final and doubling occur.

“Saññāya”miti vattate.

The rule `saññāyaṃ` (in the sense of a name) continues.

609. Tikiccāsiṭṭhe.

609. In the sense of a desiderative and a wish.

Saññāyamabhidheyyāyaṃ āsiṭṭhe gamyamāne dhātūhi tippaccayo hoti, kitapaccayo ca. Jino enaṃ bujjhatūti jinabuddhi, dhakāradakārādesā, dhanamassa bhavatūti dhanabhūti.

When a name is the meaning or a wish is understood, the suffix `ti` and the `kita` suffixes occur after roots. `Jinabuddhi` is derived from 'may the Victor understand him' (jino enaṃ bujjhatū); substitutions of `dh` and `d` occur. `Dhanabhūti` is derived from 'may there be wealth for him' (dhanaṃ assa bhavatū).

Kitapaccaye bhavatūti bhūto, dhammo enaṃ dadātūti dhammadinno, “bhidādito inna anna īṇā vā”ti tappaccayassa innādeso. Vaḍḍhatūti vaḍḍhamāno, “bhūvādito a”iti mānantesu appaccayo, nandatūti nandako, jīvatūti jīvako iccādi.

With a `kita` suffix: `bhūto` is from 'may it be' (bhavatū). `Dhammadinno` is from 'may the Dhamma give this to him' (dhammo enaṃ dadātū); by the rule `bhidādito inna anna īṇā vā`, `inna` is the substitute for the suffix `ta`. `Vaḍḍhamāno` is from 'may he grow' (vaḍḍhatū). By `bhūvādito a`, the suffix `a` occurs in forms ending in `māna`. `Nandako` is from 'may he rejoice' (nandatū); `jīvako` is from 'may he live' (jīvatū), and so on.

610. Āgamā [M 0.0375] tuko.

610. From `ā-gam`, the suffix `tuka`.

Āpubbā gamito tukappaccayo hoti, kitakattā kattari. Āgacchatīti āgantuko.

From the root `gam` preceded by `ā`, the suffix `tuka` occurs in the agentive sense because it is a `kita` affix. `Āgantuko` is one who comes (āgacchati).

“Gamā”ti vattate.

The rule `gamā` (from the root `gam`) continues.

611. Bhabbe ika.

611. The suffix `ika` occurs in the sense of capability (bhabba).

Gamito ikappaccayo hoti bhabbatthe. Gantuṃ bhabboti gamiko bhikkhu.

From the root `gam`, the suffix `ika` occurs in the sense of capability (bhabbatthe). `Gamiko bhikkhu` is a monk who is capable of going (gantuṃ bhabbo).

Tekālikappaccayantanayo.

The section on words ending in suffixes related to the three times.

Atītappaccayantanaya

The section on words ending in past tense suffixes.

612. Atīte ta tavantu tāvī.

612. In the past tense: `ta`, `tavantu`, and `tāvī`.

Atīte kāle sabbehi dhātūhi ta tavantu tāvī iccete paccayā honti. Ete eva parasamaññāya niṭṭhasaññakāpi, te ca kitasaññattā kattari bhavanti. Abhavīti bhūto, bhūtā, bhūtaṃ, “aññesu cā”ti etthānuvattitavāggahaṇena ta tavantutāvīsu vuddhi na hoti. Hu dānādanahabyappadānesu, ahavīti huto aggiṃ.

In past time, from all roots these suffixes `ta`, `tavantu`, and `tāvī` occur. These are also designated `niṭṭha` by another terminology. And because they are designated `kita`, they occur in the agentive sense. `Bhūto`, `bhūtā`, `bhūtaṃ` is from `abhavī` (he/she/it was). Because of the word `vā` being carried forward here in the rule `aññesu cā`, `vuddhi` does not occur with `ta`, `tavantu`, or `tāvī`. The root `hu` is in the senses of giving, taking, and offering oblations. `Huto aggiṃ` (he offered the fire) is from `ahavī` (he offered).

Tavantuppaccaye – “ā simhī”ti ākāro, aggiṃ hutavā, hutavanto iccādi guṇavantusamaṃ. Tāvīmhi – aggiṃ hutāvī, aggiṃ hutāvino iccādi daṇḍīsamaṃ. Itthiyaṃ inīpaccayo – hutāvinī, napuṃsake – rassattaṃ hutāvi.

With the suffix `tavantu`—by the rule `ā simhī`, `ā` is the substitute, as in `aggiṃ hutavā`, `hutavanto`, etc., similar to `guṇavantu`. With `tāvī`—`aggiṃ hutāvī`, `aggiṃ hutāvino`, etc., similar to `daṇḍī`. In the feminine, the suffix `inī` is used, forming `hutāvinī`; in the neuter, shortening occurs, forming `hutāvi`.

Vasa nivāse, vassaṃ avasīti atthe tappaccayo, sakārantattā “sādisanta”iccādinā ṭhādese sampatte –

The root `vasa` is in the sense of 'dwelling.' In the sense 'he dwelt for a year' (`vassaṃ avasī`), the suffix `ta` is applied. Because the root ends in `s`, when the substitution of `ṭh` would be obtained by the rule `sādisanta` and so forth—

“Tassā”ti adhikāro, “sādī”ti ca.

The governing rules are `Tassa` and `sādī`.

613. Vasato [M 0.0376] uttha.

613. After `vasa`, `uttha` is the substitute for `ta`.

Vasaiccetasmā dhātumhā parassa takārassa sahādibyañjanena utthādeso hoti, saralopādi. Vassaṃ vuttho, vutthā sā, “saralopo”tiādisutte tuggahaṇato pubbalopābhāve “adhivatthā devatā, vatthabba”ntiādīsu paralopo.

For the `t` that follows the root `vasa`, the substitution `uttha` occurs, with elision of the root's vowel. For example: `vassaṃ vuttho` (he dwelt for a year), `vutthā sā` (she dwelt). In the rule `saralopo...`, due to the inclusion of `tu`, the preceding vowel is not elided; but in examples like `adhivatthā devatā` (the deity who dwelt there) and `vatthabba` (to be dwelt in), the following vowel is elided.

“Vasassā”ti vipariṇāmena vattate.

`Vasassa` continues by modification of its case ending.

614. Vassa vā vu.

614. For `vasa`, `vu` is substituted for `va`, optionally.

Vasaiccetassa dhātussa vakārassa takāre pare ukāro hoti, tattha vakārāgamo ca vā hoti. Niṭṭhatakāre evāyaṃ. Atha vā “vū”ti ettha vakāro sandhijo, tantañāyena dutiyañcettha vāggahaṇamicchitabbaṃ, tena akārassapi ukāro siddho bhavati, usito brahmacariyaṃ, vusito, tathā vusitavā, vusitāvī, ikārāgamena byavahitattā utthādeso na bhavati.

For the `va` of this root `vasa`, `u` is the substitute when `t` follows, and an optional augment `v` is also inserted. This rule applies only when `t` is a `niṭṭha` suffix. Alternatively, in `vū`, the `v` arises from sandhi, and by the tantric method, a second `vā` (optionally) should be understood here; by this, the substitution of `u` for `a` is also established, as in `usito brahmacariyaṃ` (he has lived the holy life), and `vusito` (he has dwelt), and similarly `vusitavā`, `vusitāvī`. Because of the separation by the augment `i`, the substitution `uttha` does not occur.

Bhuja pālanabyavaharaṇesu, odanaṃ abhuñjīti atthe tatavantutāvī, “bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā”ti dhātvantalopo, takārassa dvittañca, bhutto, bhuttavā, bhuttāvī. Tathā ranja rāge, arañjīti ratto, rattā, rattaṃ. Yuja yoge, ayuñjīti yutto, yuttā, yuttaṃ. Vica vivecane vipubbo, viviccīti vivitto, vivittā, vivittaṃ. Muca mocane, amuccīti bandhanā mutto. Tathā tippaccayepi iminā dhātvantalopadvittāni, āsajjanaṃ āsatti, vimuccanaṃ, vimuccati etāyāti vā vimutti.

The root `bhuja` is in the senses of 'protecting' and 'using.' In the sense 'he ate rice' (`odanaṃ abhuñjī`), the suffixes `ta`, `tavantu`, `tāvī` are applied. By the rule `bhujādīnamanto no dvi cā`, the final of the root is elided, and the `t` is doubled, resulting in `bhutto`, `bhuttavā`, `bhuttāvī`. Likewise, the root `ranja` is in the sense of 'coloring.' `Ratto`, `rattā`, `rattaṃ` is from `arañjī` (he was impassioned). The root `yuja` is in the sense of 'joining.' `Yutto`, `yuttā`, `yuttaṃ` is from `ayuñjī` (he joined). The root `vica` is in the sense of 'discerning,' with the prefix `vi-`. `Vivitto`, `vivittā`, `vivittaṃ` is from `viviccī` (he was secluded). The root `muca` is in the sense of 'releasing.' `Mutto` (released) from bondage is from `amuccī` (he was released). Similarly, even with the `ti` suffix, by this rule elision of the root-final and doubling occur: `āsajjanaṃ` (clinging) becomes `āsatti`; `vimuccanaṃ` (release), or that by which one is released, is `vimutti` (liberation).

Kudha [M 0.0377] kope, akujjhīti atthe tappaccayo, tassa “dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā cā”ti dhattaṃ, “hacatutthānamantānaṃ dodhe”ti dhakārassa dakāro, kuddho. Yudha sampahāre, ayujjhīti yuddho, yuddhaṃ. Sidha saṃsiddhimhi, asijjhīti siddho. Āpubbo rabha rābhasse, ārabhīti āraddho gantuṃ. Naha bandhane saṃpubbo, sannayhīti sannaddho, “dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā cā”ti nahādito takārassa dhakāro.

The root `kudha` is in the sense of 'anger.' In the sense 'he was angry' (`akujjhī`), the suffix `ta` is applied. For that `ta`, by the rule `dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā cā`, it becomes `dha`; by `hacatutthānamantānaṃ do dhe`, the `dh` of the root becomes `d`, resulting in `kuddho`. The root `yudha` is in the sense of 'fighting.' `Yuddho`, `yuddhaṃ` is from `ayujjhī` (he fought). The root `sidha` is in the sense of 'accomplishment.' `Siddho` is from `asijjhī` (he accomplished). The root `rabha` in the sense of 'impetuosity' with the prefix `ā-`. `Āraddho gantuṃ` (he began to go) is from `ārabhī`. The root `naha` in the sense of 'binding' with the prefix `saṃ-`. `Sannaddho` is from `sannayhī` (he bound himself); by `dhaḍhabhahehi dhaḍhā cā`, the `t` after `nah` becomes `dh`.

Vaḍḍha vaḍḍhane, avaḍḍhīti atthe tappaccayo, tassa ḍhattaṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātvākārassuttaṃ, ḍalopo ca.

The root `vaḍḍha` is in the sense of 'growth.' In the sense 'it grew' (`avaḍḍhī`), the suffix `ta` is applied. For that `ta`, it becomes `ḍha`. By the rule `kvaci dhātū...` etc., the `a` of the root becomes `u`, and there is elision of `ḍa`.

“Hacatutthānamantāna”nti vattate.

The rule `Hacatutthānamantānaṃ` continues.

615. Ḍo ḍhakāre.

615. `Ḍ` is the substitute when `ḍh` follows.

Hacatutthānaṃ dhātvantānaṃ ḍakārādeso hoti ḍhakāre pare. Vuḍḍho, vuḍḍhā, “bo vassā”ti batte buḍḍho. Tippaccaye – bujjhanaṃ, bujjhati vā etāyāti buddhi. Evaṃ siddhi, vaḍḍhi. Tabbappaccaye – boddhabbamiccādi.

For root-finals that are `h` or the fourth consonants, the substitution `ḍ` occurs when `ḍh` follows. For example: `vuḍḍho` (aged), `vuḍḍhā`. When `bo vassā` is said, `buḍḍho` is formed. With the `ti` suffix: `bujjhanaṃ` (awakening), or that by which one awakens, is `buddhi` (wisdom). Similarly, `siddhi` (accomplishment), `vaḍḍhi` (growth). With the `tabba` suffix: `boddhabbaṃ` (to be understood), and so on.

“Anto, no”ti ca adhikāro.

The governing rules are also `Anto` (final) and `na`.

616. Tarādīhi iṇṇo.

616. After tara, etc., iṇṇa [is substituted for the suffix ta].

Taraiccevamādīhi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa iṇṇādeso hoti, dhātvanto ca no hoti, saralopādi. Tara taraṇe, saṃsāraṇṇavaṃ atarīti tiṇṇo tāreyyaṃ. Evaṃ uttiṇṇo, tiṇṇaṃ vā. Pūra pūraṇe, saṃpūrīti saṃpuṇṇo, “saralopo”tiādisutte tuggahaṇato pubbalopābhāve uvaṇṇato parassa “vā paro asarūpā”ti lopo, saṃyoge rassattaṃ. Tura vege, aturīti tuṇṇaṃ[M 0.0378], turitaṃ vā. Jara vayohānimhi, parijīrīti parijiṇṇo. Kira vikiraṇe, ākirīti ākiṇṇo iccādi.

After roots such as tara, for the following suffix ta, there is the substitution iṇṇa, and the final of the root becomes na; vowel elision, etc., also apply. The root tara is in the sense of 'crossing.' From saṃsāraṇṇavaṃ atari (he crossed the ocean of saṃsāra), comes tiṇṇo (crossed). Tāreyyaṃ (one should cross). Similarly, uttiṇṇo (crossed over), or tiṇṇaṃ (of those who have crossed). The root pūra is in the sense of 'filling.' From saṃpūri (he filled) comes saṃpuṇṇo (filled). In the rule saralopo, etc., due to the inclusion of tu, there is no elision of the preceding vowel; after the vowel u, elision occurs by the rule vā paro asarūpā; and in a conjunct consonant, shortening occurs. The root tura is in the sense of 'speed.' From aturi (he hurried) comes tuṇṇaṃ (hurried), or turitaṃ (hurried). The root jara is in the sense of 'decay due to age.' From parijīri (it decayed thoroughly) comes parijiṇṇo (thoroughly decayed). The root kira is in the sense of 'scattering.' From ākiri (he scattered) comes ākiṇṇo (scattered), etc.

617. Susa paca sakato kkhakkā ca.

617. After susa, paca, and saka, kkha and kka [are substituted for the suffix ta], and also...

Susa paca sakaiccetehi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa kkhakkādesā honti, anto ca byañjano no hoti. Casaddena mucādito kkādeso. Susa sosane, asussīti sukkho rukkho. Apaccīti pakkaṃ phalaṃ. Saka sāmatthe, asakkhīti sakko assa, omuccīti omukkā upāhanā. “Pacituṃ, pacitabba”ntiādīsu pana na bhavati, ikārena byavahitattā. Evaṃ sabbattha byavadhāne na bhavati.

For the suffix ta following these roots, susa, paca, and saka, the substitutions kkha and kka occur, and the final consonant of the root is elided. By the word ca, the substitution kka also applies after muca, etc. The root susa is in the sense of 'drying.' From asussi (it dried) comes sukkho rukkho (a dry tree). From apacci (it ripened/cooked) comes pakkaṃ phalaṃ (a ripe/cooked fruit). The root saka is in the sense of 'ability.' From asakkhi (he was able) comes sakko assa (he is able). From omucci (he took off) comes omukkā upāhanā (sandals taken off). However, in cases like pacituṃ and pacitabbaṃ, this does not occur, because of the intervention by the vowel i. Thus, it does not occur in any case of intervention.

Sīhagatiyā tiggahaṇamanuvattate.

The inclusion of ti is carried forward by the 'lion's gait' (sīhagati).

618. Pakkamādīhi nto ca.

618. After pakkama, etc., nta [is substituted for the suffix ta], and also...

Pakkamaiccevamādīhi makārantehi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa ntādeso hoti, dhātvanto ca no hoti. Casaddena tippaccayassa nti ca hoti. Kamu padavikkhepe, pakkamīti pakkanto. Evaṃ saṅkanto, nikkhanto, “do dhassa cā”ti sutte caggahaṇena kassa khattaṃ. Bhamu anavaṭṭhāne, vibbhamīti vibbhanto, bhanto. Khamu sahane, akkhamīti khanto. Samu upasame, asamīti santo. Damu damane, adamīti danto.

After roots ending in m, such as those in the list beginning with pakkama, for the following suffix ta, there is the substitution nta, and the final of the root is elided. By the word ca, for the suffix ti, there is also the substitution nti. The root kamu is in the sense of 'stepping.' From pakkami (he departed) comes pakkanto (departed). Similarly, saṅkanto (gone together), nikkhanto (gone out). In the rule do dhassa cā, by the inclusion of ca, ka becomes kha. The root bhamu is in the sense of 'instability.' From vibbhami (he wandered) comes vibbhanto (wandered), bhanto (wandering). The root khamu is in the sense of 'endurance.' From akkhami (he endured) comes khanto (endured). The root samu is in the sense of 'calming.' From asami (he calmed) comes santo (calmed). The root damu is in the sense of 'taming.' From adami (he tamed) comes danto (tamed).

Timhi – saṅkamanaṃ saṅkanti. Evaṃ okkanti, vibbhanti, khanti, santi danti iccādi.

With the ti suffix: saṅkamanaṃ (the act of transitioning) becomes saṅkanti (transition). Similarly, okkanti (descent), vibbhanti (wandering), khanti (forbearance), santi (serenity), danti (self-control), etc.

619. Janādīnamā [M 0.0379] timhi ca.

619. For jana, etc., the final [consonant] becomes ā with the suffix ti, and also [with the suffix ta].

Janaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnamantassa byañjanassa āttaṃ hoti tappaccaye, timhi ca. Yogavibhāgena aññatthāpi. Jana janane, ajanīti jāto, vijāyīti puttaṃ vijātā, jananaṃ jāti. Tappaccaye satipi takāre puna tiggahaṇakaraṇaṃ paccayantaratakāre āttanivattanatthaṃ, yathā – jantu. “Janitvā, janitu”ntiādīsu pana ikārena byavahitattā na bhavati.

For roots such as jana, etc., the final consonant becomes long ā with the suffix ta, and also with ti. By separation of the rule, this can apply elsewhere also. The root jana is in the sense of 'producing.' From ajani (he was born) comes jāto (born). From vijāyi (she gave birth) comes puttaṃ vijātā (she who gave birth to a son). The verbal noun jananaṃ (producing) becomes jāti (birth). Although the suffix ta is present, the mentioning of ti again is for the purpose of preventing this lengthening to ā with other suffixes containing ta, for example, jantu. However, in cases like janitvā and janituṃ, it does not occur, because of the intervention by the vowel i.

“Ā, timhi, cā”ti ca vattate.

The rules ā, timhi, and ca are also carried forward.

620. Ṭhāpānamiī ca.

620. For ṭhā and pā, i and ī [are substituted for the final vowel] respectively, and ca [also applies].

Ṭhā pāiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ antassa ākārassa yathākkamaṃ ikāraīkārādesā honti tappaccaye, timhi ca. Casaddena aññatrāpi kvaci. Ṭhā gatinivattimhi, aṭṭhāsīti ṭhito, upaṭṭhito garuṃ, ṭhitavā, adhiṭṭhitvā, ṭhānaṃ ṭhiti. Pā pāne, apāyīti pītā, yāguṃ pītavā, pānaṃ pīti, pītvā.

For the final vowel ā of these roots, ṭhā and pā, the substitutions i and ī occur respectively with the suffix ta, and also with ti. By the word ca, this occurs sometimes elsewhere too. The root ṭhā is in the sense of 'ceasing movement.' From aṭṭhāsi (he stood) comes ṭhito (stood), as in upaṭṭhito garuṃ (he attended upon the teacher); also ṭhitavā (having stood), adhiṭṭhitvā (having resolved). The verbal noun ṭhānaṃ (standing) becomes ṭhiti with the ti suffix. The root pā is in the sense of 'drinking.' From apāyi (he drank) comes pītā (drunk), as in yāguṃ pītavā (he drank gruel); also pītvā (having drunk). The verbal noun pānaṃ (drinking) becomes pīti with the ti suffix.

621. Hantehi ho hassa lo vā adahanahānaṃ.

621. After roots ending in h, ha [is substituted for ta and ti], and la is optionally substituted for the h of the root, except for daha and naha.

Hakārantehi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa, tissa ca hakārādeso hoti, hassa ca dhātvantassa lakāro hoti vā dahanahe vajjetvā, ḍhattāpavādoyaṃ. Ruha janane, aruhīti āruḷho rukkhaṃ. Laḷānamaviseso, ārulho vā, ruhanaṃ ruḷhī. Gāhu viloḷane, agāhīti gāḷho, ajjhogāḷho mahaṇṇavaṃ. Baha vuddhimhi, abahīti bāḷho, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dīgho. Muha vecitte, amuyhīti mūḷho. Guha saṃvaraṇe, aguhīti gūḷhaṃ. Vaha pāpuṇane[M 0.0380], upavahīti upavuḷho, “vaca vasa vahādīnamukāro vassā”ti yogavibhāgena uttaṃ.

For the suffix ta following roots ending in h, and also for ti, the substitution ha occurs; and for the final h of the root, la optionally occurs, excepting the roots daha and naha. This is an exception to the ḍha rule. The root ruha is in the sense of 'growing.' From aruhi (he climbed) comes āruḷho rukkhaṃ (he climbed the tree). There is no distinction between la and ḷa. Or, alternatively, ārulho. The verbal noun ruhanaṃ (climbing) becomes ruḷhī. The root gāhu is in the sense of 'stirring.' From agāhi (he stirred) comes gāḷho (stirred), as in ajjhogāḷho mahaṇṇavaṃ (he plunged into the great ocean). The root baha is in the sense of 'increase.' From abahi (it increased) comes bāḷho (increased); the lengthening is by the rule kvaci dhātu..., etc. The root muha is in the sense of 'bewilderment.' From amuyhi (he was bewildered) comes mūḷho (bewildered). The root guha is in the sense of 'concealing.' From aguhi (he concealed) comes gūḷhaṃ (concealed). The root vaha is in the sense of 'attaining.' From upavahi (he approached) comes upavuḷho (approached). By separation of the rule vaca vasa vahādīnam ukāro vassa, the substitution of u for va is stated.

Adahanahānanti kimatthaṃ? Daḍḍho, sannaddho. Vāti kiṃ? Duddho, siniddho. “Gahitaṃ, mahita”ntiādīsu pana ikārāgamena byavahitattā na bhavati.

Why state 'except for daha and naha'? For the forms daḍḍho (burned) and sannaddho (bound). Why state 'optionally' (vā)? For the forms duddho (milked) and siniddho (smooth/oily). However, in cases like gahitaṃ and mahitaṃ, it does not occur because of the intervention by the augment i.

Dhātuppaccayantatopi “atīte ta tavantutāvī”ti tappaccayo, abubhukkhīti bubhukkhito. Evaṃ jighacchito, pipāsito iccādi.

Even after a root ending in a suffix, the ta suffix is applied by the rule atīte ta tavantutāvī. From abubhukkhi (he was hungry) comes bubhukkhito (hungry). Similarly, jighacchito (hungry), pipāsito (thirsty), etc.

Evaṃ kattari niṭṭhanayo.

Thus is the method for niṭṭha in the active voice.

“Atīte”ti vattate.

The rule Atīte (in the past) is carried forward.

622. Bhāvakammesu ta.

622. In the impersonal and passive senses, the suffix ta [is applied].

Atīte kāle gamyamāne sabbadhātūhi tappaccayo hoti bhāvakammaiccetesvatthesu.

When past time is understood, the suffix ta occurs after all roots in these senses: impersonal (bhāva) and passive (kamma).

Bhāve tāva –

First, in the impersonal sense:

Ge sadde, gāyanaṃ, agāyitthāti vā atthe tappaccayo.

The root ge is in the sense of 'sound.' In the sense of gāyanaṃ (singing), or agāyittha (he sang), the suffix ta is applied.

623. Sabbattha ge gī.

623. Everywhere, ge becomes gī.

Geiccetassa dhātussa gīādeso hoti sabbattha, tappaccayatipaccayesvevāyaṃ. Tassa gītaṃ, gāyanaṃ, gāyitabbāti vā gīti.

For this root ge, the substitution gī occurs everywhere; this applies only with the suffixes ta and ti. Therefore, the form is gītaṃ (sung). The verbal noun gāyanaṃ (singing), or gāyitabbaṃ (to be sung), becomes gīti (singing/song).

Bhāve – tappaccayantā napuṃsakā. Kammani – tiliṅgā.

In the impersonal sense, words ending with the suffix ta are neuter. In the passive sense, they are of all three genders.

Nata gattavināme, naccanaṃ, anaccitthāti vā atthe tappaccayo.

The root nata is in the sense of 'bending the limbs.' In the sense of naccanaṃ (dancing), or anaccittha (he danced), the suffix ta is applied.

624. Paccayā daniṭṭhā nipātanā sijjhanti.

624. Unfinished forms with suffixes are accomplished by irregular derivation.

Ye idha sappaccayā saddā paccayehi na niṭṭhaṃ gatā, te nipātanato sijjhantīti dhātvantena saha tappaccayassa cca ṭṭādesā. Naccaṃ, naṭṭaṃ. Hasa hasane, hasanaṃ hasitaṃ, ikārāgamo. Gamanaṃ gataṃ. Evaṃ ṭhitaṃ, sayitaṃ, vādhikārassa vavatthitavibhāsattā vuddhi. Ruda assuvimocane, arujjhitthāti roditaṃ, ruṇṇaṃ vā iccādi.

Those words here with suffixes which have not reached completion through the regular application of suffixes are accomplished by irregular derivation. Thus, together with the end of the root, for the suffix ta, the substitutions cca and ṭṭa occur, yielding naccaṃ (dancing) and naṭṭaṃ (danced). The root hasa is in the sense of 'laughing': hasanaṃ (laughing) becomes hasitaṃ (laughed), with the augment i. Gamanaṃ (going) becomes gataṃ (gone). Similarly, ṭhitaṃ (stood), sayitaṃ (lain down); because the governing rule of option is a regulated option, vuddhi occurs. The root ruda is in the sense of 'shedding tears': from arujjittha (he wept) comes roditaṃ (wept), or ruṇṇaṃ (wept), etc.

Kammani –

In the passive sense:

Abhibhūyitthāti abhibhūto kodho bhavatā, abhibhūtā, abhibhūtaṃ. Bhāsa byattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, abhāsittha tenāti bhāsito dhammo, bhāsitā gāthā, bhāsitaṃ suttaṃ. Disī uccāraṇe, curādittā ṇe. Adesīyitthāti desito dhammo bhagavatā, ikārāgame kāritasaralopo. Ji jaye, ajīyitthāti jito māro. Nī pāpuṇane, anīyiṃsūti nītā gāmamajā, suto tayā dhammo, ñāto.

'Abhibhūyittha' (it was overcome) becomes abhibhūto (overcome), as in 'kodho bhavatā' (anger by you), abhibhūtā (feminine), and abhibhūtaṃ (neuter). From 'Bhāsa' in the sense of clear speech: 'abhāsittha tena' (he spoke) becomes bhāsito dhammo (the Dhamma was spoken), bhāsitā gāthā (the verse was spoken), bhāsitaṃ suttaṃ (the discourse was spoken). From 'Disī' in the sense of uttering, which is in the curādi class and takes the 'ṇe' suffix: 'Adesīyittha' (it was taught) becomes desito dhammo bhagavatā (the Dhamma was taught by the Blessed One), with the insertion of 'i' and the elision of the causative vowel. From 'Ji' in the sense of victory: 'ajīyittha' (it was conquered) becomes jito māro (Māra was conquered). From 'Nī' in the sense of leading: 'anīyiṃsu' (they led) becomes nītā gāmamajā (the goats were led to the village); suto tayā dhammo (the Dhamma was heard by you); ñāto (known).

Sāsa anusiṭṭhimhi, anusāsīyitthāti atthe tappaccayo.

From 'Sāsa' in the sense of instruction: the suffix 'ta' is used in the sense of 'anusāsīyittha' (it was instructed).

625. Sāsadisato tassa riṭṭho ca.

625. And for the suffix 'ta' after 'Sāsa' and similar roots, 'riṭṭha' is the substitute.

Sāsadisaiccetehi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa riṭṭhādeso hoti, casaddena tissa riṭṭhi ca, disato kiccatakāratuṃtvādīnañca raṭṭha raṭṭhuṃ raṭṭhādesā ca honti, rādilopo, anusiṭṭho so mayā, anusiṭṭhā sā, anusiṭṭhaṃ. Disa pekkhaṇe, adissitthāti diṭṭhaṃ me rūpaṃ.

For the suffix 'ta' following these roots, namely 'Sāsa' and similar, the substitution 'riṭṭha' occurs. And by the word 'ca', for the suffix 'ti', 'riṭṭhi' also occurs. And from the root 'disa', for the kicca suffixes, 'ta', 'tuṃ', 'tvā', and so on, the substitutions 'raṭṭha', 'raṭṭhuṃ', 'raṭṭhā' also occur, with elision of the initial 'ra'. Thus: 'anusiṭṭho so mayā' (he was instructed by me), 'anusiṭṭhā sā' (she was instructed), 'anusiṭṭhaṃ' (it was instructed). From 'Disa' in the sense of seeing: 'adissittha' (it was seen) becomes 'diṭṭhaṃ me rūpaṃ' (the form was seen by me).

Timhi – anusāsanaṃ anusiṭṭhi, dassanaṃ diṭṭhi.

With the suffix 'ti': anusāsanaṃ (instructing) becomes anusiṭṭhi (instruction); dassanaṃ (seeing) becomes diṭṭhi (view).

Kiccādīsu [M 0.0382] – dassanīyaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ, daṭṭheyyaṃ, passitunti daṭṭhuṃ gacchati, passitvāti nekkhamaṃ daṭṭhuṃ, daṭṭhā, ikārāgamena antarikassa na bhavati, yathā – anusāsitaṃ, anusāsitabbaṃ, anusāsituṃ, anusāsitvā, dassitaṃ iccādi.

In the case of the kicca suffixes and others: 'dassanīyaṃ', 'daṭṭhabbaṃ', 'daṭṭheyyaṃ' (all meaning 'to be seen'). For 'passituṃ' (to see), the form is 'daṭṭhuṃ', as in 'daṭṭhuṃ gacchati' (he goes to see). For 'passitvā' (having seen), the form is 'daṭṭhā'. When the connecting vowel 'i' is inserted, the special substitution for the suffix does not occur, for example: 'anusāsitaṃ' (instructed), 'anusāsitabbaṃ' (to be instructed), 'anusāsituṃ' (to instruct), 'anusāsitvā' (having instructed), 'dassitaṃ' (shown), and so on.

Tusa pītimhi, atussīti atthe kattari tappaccayo.

From 'Tusa' in the sense of delight: the suffix 'ta' is used in the active voice in the sense of 'atussī' (he was delighted).

“Tassā”ti adhikāro.

The governing rule is 'Tassa'.

626. Sādi, santapucchabhanjahansādīhi ṭṭho.

626. After roots beginning with 'sa', and after 'puccha', 'bhanja', 'hansa', and so on, 'ṭṭha' is the substitute.

Ādinā saha vattatīti sādi. Sakārantehi, puccha bhanjahansaiccevamādīhi ca dhātūhi parassa anantarikassa takārassa sahādibyañjanena dhātvantenaṭṭhādeso hoti. Hansassa satipi santatte punaggabhaṇaṃ kvaci ṭṭhādesassa aniccatādīpanatthaṃ, tena “viddhasto utrasto”tiādīsu na hoti. Tuṭṭho, santusito. Bhasa bhassane, abhassīti bhaṭṭho, bhassito. Nasa adassane, nassīti naṭṭho. Daṃsa daṃsane, adaṃsīyitthāti daṭṭho sappena, ḍaṃsito vā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dassa ḍattaṃ. Phusa phassane, aphusīyitthāti phuṭṭho rogena, phussito vā. Isu icchāyaṃ, esīyitthāti iṭṭho, icchito, esito. Masa āmasane, āmasīyitthāti āmaṭho. Vasasecane, avassīti vuṭṭho devo, pavisīyitthāti paviṭṭho, uddisīyitthāti uddiṭṭho. Puccha pucchane, apucchīyitthāti puṭṭho pañhaṃ, pucchito. Bhanja avamaddane, abhañjīyitthāti bhaṭṭhaṃ dhaññaṃ. Hansa pītimhi, ahaṃsīti haṭṭho, pahaṭṭho, pahaṃsito.

'Sādi' means that which occurs together with the initial (consonant of the part being replaced). For the suffix 'ta' immediately following roots ending in 'sa', and roots such as 'puccha', 'bhanja', 'hansa', and so on, the substitution 'ṭṭha' occurs, replacing the final consonant of the root. Although 'hansa' is a root ending in 'sa', its separate mention is to indicate that the 'ṭṭha' substitution is sometimes optional; therefore, it does not occur in forms like 'viddhasto' (destroyed) and 'utrasto' (frightened). Examples: Tuṭṭho (pleased), santusito (satisfied). From 'Bhasa' in the sense of falling down: 'abhassī' becomes bhaṭṭho (fallen), or bhassito. From 'Nasa' in the sense of disappearing: 'nassī' becomes naṭṭho (perished). From 'Daṃsa' in the sense of biting: 'adaṃsīyittha' becomes daṭṭho (bitten) by a snake, or ḍaṃsito; by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', the 'da' of 'daṃs' becomes 'ḍa'. From 'Phusa' in the sense of touching: 'aphusīyittha' becomes phuṭṭho (touched) by disease, or phussito. From 'Isu' in the sense of desiring: 'esīyittha' becomes iṭṭho (desired), or icchito, esito. From 'Masa' in the sense of touching: 'āmasīyittha' becomes āmaṭṭho (touched). From 'Vasa' in the sense of raining: 'avassī' becomes vuṭṭho devo (the deva rained); from 'vis': 'pavisīyittha' becomes paviṭṭho (entered); from 'dis': 'uddisīyittha' becomes uddiṭṭho (pointed out). From 'Puccha' in the sense of asking: 'apucchīyittha' becomes puṭṭho pañhaṃ (a question was asked), or pucchito. From 'Bhanja' in the sense of crushing: 'abhañjīyittha' becomes bhaṭṭhaṃ dhaññaṃ (the grain was parched). From 'Hansa' in the sense of delighting: 'ahaṃsī' becomes haṭṭho (delighted), pahaṭṭho (very delighted), or pahaṃsito.

Ādisaddena [M 0.0383] yaja devapūjāsaṅgatikaraṇadānesu, ijjitthāti atthe tappaccayo, tassa ṭṭhādeso.

By the word 'ādi': from 'yaja' in the senses of worshipping deities, associating, and giving, the suffix 'ta' is used in the sense of 'ijjittha' (it was sacrificed/worshipped), and 'ṭṭha' is its substitute.

627. Yajassa sarassi ṭṭhe.

627. For the vowel of 'yaja', 'i' is the substitute when 'ṭṭha' follows.

Yajaiccetassa dhātussa sarassa ikārādeso hoti ṭṭhe pare. Yiṭṭho mayā jino. Saja vissagge saṃpubbo, saṃsajjitthāti saṃsaṭṭho tena, vissaṭṭho. Maja suddhimhi, amajjīti maṭṭho iccādi.

For the vowel of the root 'yaja', the substitution 'i' occurs when 'ṭṭha' follows. Example: 'Yiṭṭho mayā jino' (The Conqueror was worshipped by me). From 'Saja' in the sense of releasing, preceded by 'saṃ': 'saṃsajjittha' (it was associated) becomes saṃsaṭṭho tena (associated with that); vissaṭṭho (released). From 'Maja' in the sense of cleansing: 'amajjī' (he cleansed) becomes maṭṭho (polished), and so on.

Kiccatakārādīsu tussitabbaṃ toṭṭhabbaṃ, phusitabbaṃ phoṭṭhabbaṃ, pucchituṃ puṭṭhuṃ, yajituṃ yiṭṭhuṃ, abhiharituṃ abhihaṭṭhuṃ, tosanaṃ tuṭṭhi, esanaṃ eṭṭhi, vassanaṃ vuṭṭhi, vissajjanaṃ vissaṭṭhi iccādi.

In the case of the kicca, 'ta', and other suffixes: tussitabbaṃ (should be pleased) or toṭṭhabbaṃ (should be gladdened); phusitabbaṃ (should be touched) or phoṭṭhabbaṃ (should be touched); pucchituṃ (to ask) or puṭṭhuṃ (to ask); yajituṃ (to sacrifice) or yiṭṭhuṃ (to sacrifice); abhiharituṃ (to offer) or abhihaṭṭhuṃ (to offer); tosanaṃ (satisfaction) becomes tuṭṭhi (satisfaction); esanaṃ (seeking) becomes eṭṭhi (seeking); vassanaṃ (raining) becomes vuṭṭhi (rain); vissajjanaṃ (releasing) becomes vissaṭṭhi (releasing), and so on.

“Tassa, sādī”ti ca vattate.

The governing rules 'Tassa' and 'Sādi' are continued.

628. Bhanjato ggo ca.

628. And from 'bhanja', 'gga' is the substitute.

Bhanjato dhātumhā tappaccayassa sahādibyañjanena ggo ādeso hoti. Bhaggo rāgo anena. Vasanivāse, parivasīyitthāti parivuṭṭho parivāso, vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ, uṭṭha uādesā. Vasa acchādane, nivasīyitthāti nivatthaṃ vatthaṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā stakārasaṃyogassa tthattaṃ, evaṃ nivatthabbaṃ. Saṃsa pasaṃsane, pasaṃsīyitthāti pasattho pasaṃsito, pasaṃsanaṃ pasatthi. Badha bandhane, abajjhitthāti baddho raññā, alabhīyitthāti laddhaṃ me dhanaṃ, dhattadattāni. Rabha rābhasse, ārabhīyitthāti āraddhaṃ vīriyaṃ. Daha bhasmīkaraṇe[M 0.0384], adayhittāti daḍḍhaṃ vanaṃ, abhujjitthāti bhutto odano, bhujādittā dhātvantalopo, dvittañca. Caja hānimhi, pariccajīyitthāti pariccattaṃ dhanaṃ, amuccitthāti mutto saro.

From the root 'bhanj', for the suffix 'ta', 'gga' is the substitution, replacing the final consonant of the root. Example: 'Bhaggo rāgo anena' (passion is broken by this). From 'Vasa' in the sense of dwelling: 'parivasīyittha' (he dwelt) becomes parivuṭṭho parivāso (one who has completed the probationary period); vusitaṃ brahmacariyaṃ (the holy life has been lived); the vowel 'a' is substituted by 'u'. From 'Vasa' in the sense of clothing: 'nivasīyittha' (it was worn) becomes nivatthaṃ vatthaṃ (the cloth is worn); by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', the consonant cluster 'sta' becomes 'ttha'; thus also nivatthabbaṃ (to be worn). From 'Saṃsa' in the sense of praising: 'pasaṃsīyittha' (it was praised) becomes pasattho (praised), or pasaṃsito; pasaṃsanaṃ (praising) becomes pasatthi (praise). From 'Badha' in the sense of binding: 'abajjhitthāti' (it was bound) becomes baddho raññā (bound by the king). From 'labh': 'alabhīyittha' (it was obtained) becomes laddhaṃ me dhanaṃ (my wealth is obtained); dhattadattāni (placed and given). From 'Rabha' in the sense of exertion: 'ārabhīyittha' (it was begun) becomes āraddhaṃ vīriyaṃ (energy is aroused). From 'Daha' in the sense of burning: 'adayhitthāti' (it was burned) becomes daḍḍhaṃ vanaṃ (the forest is burned). From 'bhuj': 'abhujjittha' (it was eaten) becomes bhutto odano (the rice is eaten); because it belongs to the 'bhuj' group, there is elision of the root-final and doubling of the consonant. From 'Caja' in the sense of abandoning: 'pariccajīyittha' (it was abandoned) becomes pariccattaṃ dhanaṃ (wealth is abandoned). From 'muc': 'amuccittha' (it was released) becomes mutto saro (the arrow is released).

Vaca viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, avacīyitthāti atthe tappaccayo.

From 'Vaca' in the sense of distinct speech: the suffix 'ta' is used in the sense of 'avacīyittha' (it was spoken).

“Anto, no, dvi, cā”ti ca adhikāro.

The governing rule is 'Anto, no, dvi, ca'.

629. Vaca vā vu.

629. For 'Vaca', 'vu' is optionally the substitute.

Catuppadamidaṃ. Vacaiccetassa dhātussa vakārassa ukārādeso hoti vā, dhātvanto ca cakāro no hoti, tappaccayassa ca dvibhāvo hoti. Vāggahaṇamavadhāraṇatthaṃ, dhātvādimhi vakārāgamo. Vuttamidaṃ bhagavatā, uttaṃ vā.

This is a four-part rule. For the root 'vaca', the 'va' is optionally substituted by 'u', the final 'ca' of the root is elided, and the suffix 'ta' is doubled. The inclusion of 'vā' is for determination; a 'va' is prefixed to the root. Example: 'Vuttamidaṃ bhagavatā' (this was spoken by the Blessed One), or 'uttaṃ' (spoken).

630. Gupādīnañca.

630. And for 'gupa' and other such roots.

Gupaiccevamādīnaṃ dhātūnamanto ca byañjano no hoti, parassa takārassa ca dvibhāvo hoti. Gupa gopane, sugopīyitthāti sugutto, sugopito, ikārena byavahitattā na dhātvantalopo, “aññesu cā”ti sutte vādhikārassa vavatthitavibhāsattā niṭṭhatakārepi kvaci vuddhi. Gopanaṃ gutti.

For roots such as 'gupa', the final consonant is elided, and the following suffix 'ta' is doubled. From 'Gupa' in the sense of protecting: 'sugopīyittha' (it was well-protected) becomes sugutto (well-guarded), or sugopito; because of the intervention of 'i', there is no elision of the root-final. And in the rule 'aññesu ca', because the governing word 'vā' indicates a regulated option, there is sometimes vṛddhi strengthening even before the 'niṭṭha' suffix 'ta'. 'Gopanaṃ' (protecting) becomes 'gutti' (protection).

Lipa limpane, alimpīyitthāti litto sugandhena. Tapa santāpe, santapīyitthāti santatto tejena. Dīpa dittimhi, ādīpīyitthātiāditto agginā, rassattaṃ, dīpanaṃ ditti. Apa pāpuṇane, pāpīyitthāti patto gāmo, pāpuṇīti patto sukhaṃ, pāpuṇanaṃ patti, pattabbaṃ. Mada ummāde, pamajjīti pamatto. Supa sayane, asupīti sutto iccādi.

From 'Lipa' in the sense of smearing: 'alimpīyittha' (it was smeared) becomes litto sugandhena (smeared with fragrance). From 'Tapa' in the sense of heating: 'santapīyittha' (it was heated) becomes santatto tejena (heated by heat). From 'Dīpa' in the sense of shining: 'ādīpīyittha' (it was kindled) becomes āditto agginā (kindled by fire); shortening occurs; dīpanaṃ (illuminating) becomes ditti (light). From 'Āpa' in the sense of reaching: 'pāpīyittha' (it was reached) becomes patto gāmo (the village was reached); 'pāpuṇī' (he reaches) becomes patto sukhaṃ (happiness is obtained); pāpuṇanaṃ (reaching) becomes patti (attainment); pattabbaṃ (to be reached). From 'Mada' in the sense of intoxication: 'pamajjī' (he was negligent) becomes pamatto (negligent). From 'Supa' in the sense of sleeping: 'asupī' (he slept) becomes sutto (asleep), and so on.

Cara [M 0.0385] caraṇe, acarīyitthāti ciṇṇo dhammo, iṇṇādeso, carito vā. Evaṃ puṇṇo, pūrito.

From 'Cara' in the sense of practicing: 'acarīyittha' (it was practiced) becomes ciṇṇo dhammo (the Dhamma was practiced); 'iṇṇa' is the substitution; or carito (practiced). Similarly, puṇṇo (full), pūrito (filled).

Nuda khepe, panujjitthāti paṇunno, nassa ṇattaṃ, panudito. Dā dāne, ādīyitthātiādinno, atto vā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dāsaddassa takāro, rassattaṃ.

From 'Nuda' in the sense of dispelling: 'panujjittha' (it was dispelled) becomes paṇunno; 'na' becomes 'ṇa'; or panudito. From 'Dā' in the sense of giving: 'ādīyittha' (it was given) becomes ādinno, or atto; by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', for the word 'dāsa', 'ta' is the substitute, and shortening occurs.

631. Bhidādito innaannaīṇā vā.

631. After 'bhida' and other such roots, 'inna', 'anna', or 'īṇa' are optionally substituted.

Bhidaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi parassa tappaccayassa inna annaīṇaiccete ādesā honti vā, anto ca no hoti. Vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, saralopādi.

For the suffix 'ta' following roots such as 'bhida', the substitutions 'inna', 'anna', or 'īṇa' occur optionally, and the final consonant of the root is elided. This word 'vā' (optionally) indicates a regulated option (vavatthitavibhāsā), as in cases of vowel elision and so on.

Bhidi vidāraṇe, abhijjitthāti bhinno ghaṭo bhavatā, bhijjīti vā bhinno devadatto. Chidi dvidhākaraṇe, achijjitthāti chinno rukkho, acchinnaṃ cīvaraṃ, ucchijjīti ucchinno. Adīyitthābhi dinno suṅko. Sada visaraṇagatyāvasānesu, nisīdīti nisinno. Khida uttāsane, khida dīnabhāve vā, akhijjīti khinno.

From 'Bhidi' in the sense of breaking: 'abhijjittha' (it was broken) becomes bhinno, as in 'ghaṭo bhavatā' (the pot by you); or 'bhijjī' (it breaks) becomes bhinno, as in 'devadatto' (Devadatta). From 'Chidi' in the sense of splitting in two: 'achijjittha' (it was split) becomes chinno rukkho (the tree was cut); acchinnaṃ cīvaraṃ (the robe was uncut); 'ucchijjī' (it is cut off) becomes ucchinno. From 'dā': 'Adīyittha' (it was given) becomes dinno, as in 'suṅko' (tax). From 'Sada' in the senses of scattering, moving, and ceasing: 'nisīdī' (he sits down) becomes nisinno (seated). From 'Khida' in the sense of weariness, or in the sense of dejection: 'akhijjī' (he was dejected) becomes khinno (dejected).

Annādese chada apavāraṇe, acchādīyitthāti channo, paṭicchannaṃ gehaṃ, pasīdīti pasanno. Pada gatimhi, uppajjīti uppanno, jhānaṃ samāpanno. Rudi assuvimocane, ruṇṇo, paralopo.

In the case of the 'anna' substitution: from 'chada' in the sense of covering: 'acchādīyittha' (it was covered) becomes channo; paṭicchannaṃ gehaṃ (a covered house). From 'sad' with 'pa-': 'pasīdī' (he becomes clear/pleased) becomes pasanno (pleased). From 'Pada' in the sense of going: 'uppajjī' (it arises) becomes uppanno (arisen); jhānaṃ samāpanno (one who has attained meditation). From 'Rudi' in the sense of shedding tears: ruṇṇo (wept); there is elision of the following consonant.

Khī khaye īṇādeso, akhīyīti khīṇo doso, khīṇā jāti, khīṇaṃ dhanaṃ. Hā cāge, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā hādito īṇādese ṇakārassa nattaṃ, pahīyitthāti pahīno kileso, parihāyīti parihīno. Āsa upavesane[M 0.0386], acchīti āsīno. Lī silesane, līyīti līno, nilīno. Ji jaye, jiyīti jīno vittamanusocati, jito vā. Dī khaye, dīno. Pī tappane, pīno. Lū chedane, lūyitthāti lūno iccādi.

The root khī in the sense of destruction: īṇa is the substitution; from akhīyī (it was destroyed) comes khīṇo doso (hatred is destroyed), khīṇā jāti (birth is destroyed), khīṇaṃ dhanaṃ (wealth is destroyed). The root hā in the sense of abandoning: by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', for the root hā and others, when īṇa is substituted, ṇ becomes n; from pahīyittha (it was abandoned) comes pahīno kileso (defilement is abandoned); from parihāyī (it diminishes) comes parihīno (diminished). The root āsa in the sense of sitting: from acchī (he sat) comes āsīno (seated). The root lī in the sense of clinging: from līyī (he clings) comes līno (clung), nilīno (hidden). The root ji in the sense of conquering: from jiyī (he conquers) comes jīno, as in vittamanusocati (the conquered one grieves for his wealth); or jito (conquered). The root dī in the sense of destruction: dīno (wasted away). The root pī in the sense of satisfying: pīno (satisfied, plump). The root lū in the sense of cutting: from lūyittha (it was cut) comes lūno (cut), and so on.

Vamu uggiraṇe, vamīyitthāti vantaṃ, vamitaṃ, “pakkamādīhi nto”ti ntādeso. Agacchīyitthāti gato gāmo tayā, gāmaṃ gato vā, “gamakhanahanaramādīnamanto”ti dhātvantalopo. Akhaññitthāti khato kūpo, upahaññitthāti upahataṃ cittaṃ, aramīti rato, abhirato. Mana ñāṇe, amaññitthāti mato, sammato. Tanu vitthāre, atanitthāti tataṃ, vitataṃ. Yamu uparame, niyacchīti niyato.

The root vamu in the sense of vomiting: from vamīyittha (it was vomited) comes vantaṃ or vamitaṃ; nta is the substitution by the rule 'pakkamādīhi nto'. From agacchīyittha (it was gone to) comes gato, as in gāmo tayā gato (the village was gone to by you), or gāmaṃ gato (gone to the village); by the rule 'gamakhanahanaramādīnamanto', elision of the root-final occurs. From akhaññittha (it was dug) comes khato kūpo (a dug well); from upahaññittha (it was afflicted) comes upahataṃ cittaṃ (the mind is afflicted); from aramī (he delighted) comes rato (delighted), abhirato (greatly delighted). The root mana in the sense of knowing: from amaññittha (it was thought) comes mato (thought), sammato (agreed upon, esteemed). The root tanu in the sense of spreading: from atanittha (it was spread) comes tataṃ (spread), vitataṃ (widely spread). The root yamu in the sense of ceasing or restraining: from niyacchī (he restrains) comes niyato (restrained, controlled).

“No, tamhi, timhī”ti ca vattate.

And 'no, tamhi, timhī' also applies.

632. Rakāro ca.

632. And the letter 'ra'.

Rakāro ca dhātūnamantabhūto no hoti tappaccaye, tippaccaye ca pare. Pakarīyitthāti pakato kaṭo bhavatā, katā me rakkhā, kataṃ me puññaṃ. “Do dhassa cā”ti etta casaddena ṭo tassa, yathā – sukaṭaṃ, dukkaṭaṃ, pure akarīyitthāti purakkhato, “purasamupaparīhi karotissa khakharā vā tappaccayesu cā”ti khakāro, paccayehi saṅgamma karīyitthāti saṅkhato, abhisaṅkhato, upakarīyitthāti upakkhato, upakkhaṭo, parikarīyitthāti parikkhato.

And the final letter 'ra' of roots is not elided when the suffix 'ta' or 'ti' follows. From pakarīyittha comes pakato, as in kaṭo bhavatā (a mat made by you); katā me rakkhā (my protection was made), kataṃ me puññaṃ (my merit was made). In the rule 'Do dhassa ca', by the word 'ca', 'ṭo' replaces 'ta', as in: sukaṭaṃ (well-done), dukkaṭaṃ (ill-done). From pure akarīyittha comes purakkhato (placed before). By the rule 'purasamupaparīhi karotissa khakharā vā tappaccayesu ca', 'kha' is substituted. From paccayehi saṅgamma karīyittha comes saṅkhato (conditioned), abhisaṅkhato (fully conditioned). From upakarīyittha comes upakkhato or upakkhaṭo (prepared, furnished). From parikarīyittha comes parikkhato (investigated, surrounded).

Tippaccaye pakaraṇa pakati. Sara gaticintāyaṃ, asarīti sato, visarīti visaṭo, saraṇaṃ, sarati etāyāti vā sati, nīharīyitthāti nīhaṭo. Dhara dhāraṇe, uddharīyitthāti [M 0.0387] uddhaṭo, abharīyitthāti bhato, bharaṇaṃ, bharati etāyāti vā bhati.

When the suffix 'ti' follows, from pakaraṇa (making) comes pakati (nature). The root sara in the sense of going and thinking: from asarī (he remembered) comes sato (mindful); from visarī (it spread) comes visaṭo (scattered). Saraṇaṃ (refuge). Or, sati (mindfulness), because one remembers by means of it. From nīharīyittha (it was drawn out) comes nīhaṭo (drawn out). The root dhara in the sense of holding: from uddharīyittha (it was lifted up) comes uddhaṭo (lifted up). From abharīyittha (it was carried) comes bhato (carried). Bharaṇaṃ (bearing). Or, bhati (wages), because one is supported by it.

Ikārāgamayuttesu “gamito”tiādīsu dhātvantalope sampatte –

In cases such as 'gamito', which are joined with the augment 'i', when the elision of the final letter of the root is applicable—

“Lopo”ti vattate.

The rule 'lopo' (elision) is carried forward.

633. Namakarānamantānaṃ niyuttatamhi.

633. Of roots ending in 'na, ma, ka, ra', when 'ta' joined with the augment 'i' follows.

Nakāra makāra kakāra rakārānaṃ dhātvantānaṃ lopo na hoti ikārāgamayutte takāre pareti lopābhāvo. Agacchī, gamīyitthāti vā gamito, ramitthāti ramito. Evaṃ vamito, namito. Saki saṅkāyaṃ, saṅkito, sarito, bharito. Tathā khanitabbaṃ, hanitabbaṃ, gamitabbaṃ, ramitabbaṃ iccādi.

The elision of the final 'na, ma, ka,' and 'ra' of roots does not occur when the letter 'ta' with the augment 'i' follows; thus, there is non-elision. From agacchī or gamīyittha (it was gone to) comes gamito; from ramittha (he delighted) comes ramito. Similarly, vamito, namito. The root saki in the sense of doubting: saṅkito. Also sarito, bharito. Likewise, khanitabbaṃ (to be dug), hanitabbaṃ (to be struck), gamitabbaṃ (to be gone to), ramitabbaṃ (to be delighted in), and so on.

Nidhīyitthāti nihito, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhissa hi tappaccaye. Evaṃ vihito.

From nidhīyittha (it was placed) comes nihito (placed, hidden). By the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', for the root dhā, 'hi' is the substitution when the suffix 'ta' follows. Similarly, vihito (arranged, prescribed).

Kārite abhāvīyitthāti atthe “bhāvakammesu ta”iti tappaccayo, “yathāgamamikāro”ti ikārāgamo, saralopādi, bhāvito maggo tena, bhāvayito, apācīyitthāti pācito odanaṃ yaññadatto devadattena, pācayito, pācāpito, pācāpayito, kammaṃ kārīyitthāti kārito, kārayito, kārāpito, kārāpayito iccādi.

In the causative, in the sense of abhāvīyittha (it was caused to be), the suffix 'ta' is applied by the rule 'bhāvakammesu ta'; the augment 'i' is added by the rule 'yathāgamamikāro', and there is vowel elision and so on. For example, bhāvito maggo tena (the path was developed by him); also bhāvayito. From apācīyittha (it was caused to be cooked) comes pācito, as in odanaṃ yaññadatto devadattena (rice was caused to be cooked by Devadatta at the instigation of Yaññadatta); also pācayito, pācāpito, pācāpayito. From kammaṃ kārīyittha (the action was caused to be done) comes kārito; also kārayito, kārāpito, kārāpayito, and so on.

“Bhāvakammesu ta”iti ettha “ta”iti yogavibhāgena acalana gati bhojanatthādīhi adhikaraṇepi tappaccayo, yathā – āsa upavesane, adhikaraṇe acchiṃsu ettha teti idaṃ tesaṃ āsitaṃ ṭhānaṃ. Bhāve idha tehi āsitaṃ. Kammani ayaṃ tehi ajjhāsito gāmo. Kattari [M 0.0388] idha te āsitā. Tathā aṭṭhaṃsu etthāti idaṃ tesaṃ ṭhitaṃ ṭhānaṃ, idha tehi ṭhitaṃ, ayaṃ tehi adhiṭṭhito okāso, idha te ṭhitā. Nisīdiṃsu etthāti idaṃ tesaṃ nisinnaṃ ṭhānaṃ, ayaṃ tesaṃ nisinnakālo, te idha nisinnā. Nipajjiṃsu etthāti idaṃ tesaṃ nipannaṃ ṭhānaṃ, idha te nipannā.

In the rule 'bhāvakammesu ta', by splitting the rule at 'ta', the suffix 'ta' is also applied in the sense of locus (adhikaraṇa) for roots with meanings such as motionlessness, motion, eating, and so on. For example, the root āsa in the sense of sitting: in the sense of locus, from acchiṃsu ettha (they sat here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ āsitaṃ ṭhānaṃ (this is their sitting place). In the sense of state (bhāva), idha tehi āsitaṃ (here it was sat by them). In the sense of action (kamma), ayaṃ tehi ajjhāsito gāmo (this village was inhabited by them). In the sense of agent (kattā), idha te āsitā (here they sat). Similarly, from aṭṭhaṃsu ettha (they stood here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ ṭhitaṃ ṭhānaṃ (this is their standing place); idha tehi ṭhitaṃ (here it was stood by them); ayaṃ tehi adhiṭṭhito okāso (this space was stood upon by them); idha te ṭhitā (here they stood). From nisīdiṃsu ettha (they sat down here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ nisinnaṃ ṭhānaṃ (this is their sitting place); ayaṃ tesaṃ nisinnakālo (this is their time of sitting); te idha nisinnā (here they sat down). From nipajjiṃsu ettha (they lay down here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ nipannaṃ ṭhānaṃ (this is their lying place); idha te nipannā (here they lay down).

Yā gatipāpuṇane. Ayāsuṃ te etthāti ayaṃ tesaṃ yāto maggo, idha tehi yātaṃ, ayaṃ tehi yāto, maggo, idha te yātā. Tathā idaṃ tesaṃ gataṭṭhānaṃ, ayaṃ tesaṃ gatakālo, idha tehi gataṃ, ayaṃ tehi gato gāmo, idha te gatā.

The root yā in the sense of going and reaching. From ayāsuṃ te ettha (they went here) comes ayaṃ tesaṃ yāto maggo (this is the path they went on); idha tehi yātaṃ (here it was gone by them); ayaṃ tehi yāto maggo (this is the path gone by them); idha te yātā (here they went). Similarly, for the root gam: idaṃ tesaṃ gataṭṭhānaṃ (this is the place they went to); ayaṃ tesaṃ gatakālo (this is their time of going); idha tehi gataṃ (here it was gone by them); ayaṃ tehi gato gāmo (this is the village gone to by them); idha te gatā (here they went).

Bhuñjiṃsu etasminti idaṃ tesaṃ bhuttaṭṭhānaṃ, ayaṃ tesaṃ bhuttakālo, idha tehi bhutto odano, idha te bhuttā. Piviṃsu te etthāti idaṃ tesaṃ pītaṃ ṭhānaṃ, idha tehi pītā yāgu, idha te pītā. Dissanti etthāti idaṃ tesaṃ diṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ iccādi.

From bhuñjiṃsu etasmiṃ (they ate in this) comes idaṃ tesaṃ bhuttaṭṭhānaṃ (this is their eating place); ayaṃ tesaṃ bhuttakālo (this is their eating time); idha tehi bhutto odano (here rice was eaten by them); idha te bhuttā (here they have eaten). From piviṃsu te ettha (they drank here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ pītaṃ ṭhānaṃ (this is their drinking place); idha tehi pītā yāgu (here gruel was drunk by them); idha te pītā (here they have drunk). From dissanti ettha (they are seen here) comes idaṃ tesaṃ diṭṭhaṭṭhānaṃ (this is their seeing place), and so on.

“Kattari kiti”ti ito maṇḍūkagatiyā “kattarī”ti vattate.

From the rule 'Kattari kiti', by the frog-leap method, the word 'kattari' (in the agent) is carried forward.

634. Kammani dutiyāyaṃ kto.

634. When there is an accusative case in the sense of the object, the suffix 'kta' is used.

Kammatthe dutiyāyaṃ vibhattiyaṃ vijjamānāyaṃ dhātūhi kattari ktappaccayo hoti. Idameva vacanaṃ ñāpakaṃ abhihite kammādimhi dutiyādīnamabhāvassa. Dānaṃ adāsīti atthe ktappaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā paccayakakārassa lopo, tassa innādeso, dānaṃ dinno devadatto. Rakkha pālane, sīlaṃ arakkhīti sīlaṃ rakkhito, bhattaṃ abhuñjīti bhattaṃ bhutto, garuṃ upāsīti garumupāsito iccādi.

When the accusative case ending is present in the sense of the object, the suffix 'kta' occurs after roots in the sense of the agent. This very rule indicates the absence of the accusative and other cases when the object and so on are expressed by the verbal ending. In the sense of dānaṃ adāsi (he gave a gift), the suffix 'kta' is applied; by the rule beginning 'kvaci dhātū', the 'ka' of the suffix is elided, and 'inna' is substituted for the root, yielding dānaṃ dinno devadatto (Devadatta has given a gift). The root rakkha in the sense of guarding: from sīlaṃ arakkhī (he guarded virtue) comes sīlaṃ rakkhito (he has guarded virtue). From bhattaṃ abhuñjī (he ate food) comes bhattaṃ bhutto (he has eaten food). From garuṃ upāsi (he attended upon the teacher) comes garumupāsito (he has attended upon the teacher), and so on.

635. Bhyādīhi matibudhipūjādīhi ca kto.

635. The suffix 'kta' is also used with roots beginning with 'bhī', and with roots having the meaning of thinking, knowing, honoring, and so on.

Bhīiccevamādīhi dhātūhi, mati budhi pūjādīhi ca ktappaccayo hoti. So ca “bhāvakammesu kiccattakkhatthā”ti vuttattā bhāvakammesveva bhavati.

The suffix 'kta' occurs with roots beginning with 'bhī' and so on, and with roots having the meaning of thinking, knowing, honoring, and so on. And since it is stated by the rule 'bhāvakammesu kiccattakkhatthā', it occurs only in the sense of state (bhāva) and action (kamma).

Bhī bhaye, abhāyitthāti bhītaṃ bhavatā. Supa saye, asupīyitthāti suttaṃ bhavatā. Evaṃ sayitaṃ bhavatā. Asa bhojane, asitaṃ bhavatā, pacito odano bhavatā.

The root bhī in the sense of fear: from abhāyittha (he was afraid) comes bhītaṃ bhavatā (it was feared by you). The root supa in the sense of sleep: from asupīyittha (he slept) comes suttaṃ bhavatā (it was slept by you). Similarly, sayitaṃ bhavatā (it was lain down by you). The root asa in the sense of eating: asitaṃ bhavatā (it was eaten by you); pacito odano bhavatā (rice was cooked by you).

Idha matyādayo icchatthā, budhiādayo ñāṇatthā.

Here, roots with the meaning of thinking (mati) and so on have the meaning of desiring, and roots with the meaning of knowing (budhi) and so on have the meaning of knowing.

Mana ñāṇe saṃpubbo, “budhagamāditthe kattarī”ti tappaccaye sampatte iminā kammani ktappaccayo, “gama khanā”tiādinā dhātvantalopo, raññā sammato. Kappa takkane, saṅkappito. Dhara dhāraṇe, curādittā ṇe, vuddhi, ikārāgamo, saralopādi, avadhārito.

The root mana in the sense of knowing, when prefixed with 'saṃ': although the suffix 'ta' in the agent sense is applicable by the rule 'budhagamāditthe kattari', by the present rule the suffix 'kta' is applied in the object sense; by the rule beginning 'gama khanā', there is elision of the final letter of the root, yielding raññā sammato (esteemed by the king). The root kappa in the sense of thinking: saṅkappito (planned). The root dhara in the sense of holding: because it is in the curādi group, the suffix 'ṇe' is added, causing vowel gradation, the augment 'i', vowel elision, and so on, yielding avadhārito (determined).

Budha avagamane, avabujjhitthāti buddho bhagavā mahesakkhehi devamanussehi. I ajjhayane, adhīyitthāti adhīto.

The root budha in the sense of understanding: from avabujjhittha (he understood) comes buddho, as in bhagavā mahesakkhehi devamanussehi buddho (the Blessed One was understood by powerful devas and humans). The root i in the sense of studying: from adhīyittha (it was studied) comes adhīto (studied).

I gatimhi, abhisamito. Vida ñāṇe, avedīyitthāti vidito. Ñā avabodhane, aññāyitthāti ñāto. Vidha vedhane, paṭivijjhitthāti paṭividdho dhammo. Takka vitakke, takkito.

The root i in the sense of going: abhisamito (realized, attained). The root vida in the sense of knowing: from avedīyittha (it was known) comes vidito (known). The root ñā in the sense of understanding: from aññāyittha (it was understood) comes ñāto (known). The root vidha in the sense of piercing: from paṭivijjhittha (he penetrated) comes paṭividdho dhammo (the Dhamma was penetrated). The root takka in the sense of thinking: takkito (thought).

Pūjanatthesu –

For roots with the meaning of honoring—

Pūja pūjāyaṃ, apūjīyitthāti pūjito bhagavā. Cāya santānapūjanesu apapubbo, apacāyito. Māna pūjāyaṃ, mānito. Ci caye, apacito. Vanda abhivandane, vandito. Kara karaṇe, sakkato. Sakkāra pūjāyaṃ, sakkārito iccādi.

The root pūja in the sense of worship: from apūjīyittha (he was worshipped) comes pūjito bhagavā (the Blessed One was worshipped). The root cāya in the senses of continuing and worshipping, when prefixed with 'apa': apacāyito (revered). The root māna in the sense of worship: mānito (honored). The root ci in the sense of gathering, when prefixed with 'apa': apacito (honored). The root vanda in the sense of paying homage: vandito (venerated). The root kara in the sense of doing: sakkato (respected). The root sakkāra in the sense of worship: sakkārito (honored), and so on.

Huto [M 0.0390] hutāvī hutavā, vuṭṭho vusita jiṇṇako;

Pakkaṃ pakkantako jāto, ṭhito ruḷho bubhukkhito.

Offered, one who has offered, one who has offered; risen, dwelt, an aged one; ripened, one who has departed, born; stood, grown, hungry.

Gītaṃ naccaṃ jito diṭṭho, tuṭṭho yiṭṭho ca bhaggavā;

Vuttañca gutto acchinno, pahīno gamito gato.

Sung, danced, conquered, seen; delighted, sacrificed, and one who has broken; and spoken, guarded, unbroken; abandoned, caused to go, gone.

Katobhisaṅkhato bhuttaṃ, ṭhānaṃ garumupāsito;

Bhītañca sammato buddho, pūjitotītakālikā.

Done, prepared, eaten; a place, attended upon a teacher; and feared, esteemed, known, honored—these are of past time.

Atītappaccayantanayo.

The section on past participles.

Tavetunādippaccayantanaya

The section on suffixes beginning with 'tave', 'tuṃ', and so forth.

“Puññāni kātumicchi, icchati, icchissati vā”ti viggahe –

In the analysis, as in: 'He wished to do meritorious deeds, he wishes, or he will wish to do them.'

636. Icchatthesu samāna kattu kesu ta ve tuṃ vā.

636. When the agent is the same, in the meanings of wishing, the suffixes 'tave' and 'tuṃ' are optionally used.

Icchā attho yesaṃ te icchatthā, tesu icchatthesu dhātūsu samānakattukesu santesu sabbadhātūhi tavetuṃiccete paccayā honti vā, “tavetuṃ vā”ti yogavibhāgena tadatthakriyāyañca, te ca kitakattā kattari honti.

Those whose meaning is 'wishing' are 'icchatthā.' When those roots having the meaning of wishing have the same agent, these suffixes, 'tave' and 'tuṃ', optionally occur after all roots. And by the separation of the rule 'tave tuṃ vā', they also occur for an action having that meaning. And these, being 'kita' suffixes, are in the active voice.

“Karotissa, vā”ti ca vattate.

The words 'karotissa' and 'vā' are carried over.

637. Tavetunādīsu kā.

637. When the suffixes 'tave', 'tuṃ', and so forth follow, 'kā' is the substitute.

Tavetunaiccevamādīsu paccayesu paresu karotissa dhātussa kādeso hoti vā, ādisaddena tuṃtvāna tvā tabbesu ca.

When suffixes such as 'tave', 'tuna', and so forth follow, the substitution 'kā' for the root 'karoti' optionally occurs. And by the word 'ādi', this also applies to the suffixes 'tuṃ', 'tvāna', 'tvā', and 'tabba'.

“Taddhitasamāsakitakā nāmaṃvātavetunādīsu cā”ti ettha “atave tunādīsū”ti nāmabyapadesassa nisedhanato tadantānaṃ nipātattaṃ siddhaṃ bhavati, tato nipātattā tavetunamantato “sabbāsamāvuso”tiādinā vibhattilopo. So puññāni kātave icchati, kātumicchati.

Here, in the rule 'Derivatives, compounds, and primary derivatives are optionally names, but not those ending in `tave`, `tun`, and so forth,' by the prohibition of the designation 'name' for those ending in `tave`, `tun`, etc., their status as indeclinables (`nipāta`) is established. Therefore, due to being indeclinables, the case ending is elided after words ending in `tave`, `tuna`, etc., by the rule `sabbāsamāvuso` and so forth. For example: `So puññāni kātave icchati` (He wishes to do meritorious deeds), `kātumicchati` (he wishes to do).

Kādesābhāve [M 0.0391] “tuṃtunatabbesu vā”ti rakārassa tattaṃ. Kattuṃ kāmetīti kattukāmo, abhisaṅkharitumākaṅkhati. Tathā saddhammaṃ sotave, sotuṃ, suṇituṃ vā pattheti. Evaṃ anubhavituṃ, pacituṃ, gantuṃ, gamituṃ, khantuṃ, khanituṃ, hantuṃ, hanituṃ, mantuṃ, manituṃ, harituṃ, anussaritumicchati, ettha ikārayuttatamhi “namakarāna”miccādinā paṭisiddhattā na dhātvantalopo.

In the absence of the 'kā' substitution, the 'ra' becomes 'ta' according to the rule '`tuṃtunatabbesu vā`'. '`Kattuṃ kāmeti`' (he desires to do) forms '`kattukāmo`' (desirous of doing); `abhisaṅkharitumākaṅkhati` (he longs to prepare). Similarly, `saddhammaṃ sotave, sotuṃ, suṇituṃ vā pattheti` (he yearns to hear the true Dhamma). Thus, `anubhavituṃ` (to experience), `pacituṃ` (to cook), `gantuṃ` (to go), `gamituṃ` (to go), `khantuṃ` (to endure), `khanituṃ` (to dig), `hantuṃ` (to kill), `hanituṃ` (to kill), `mantuṃ` (to think), `manituṃ` (to think), `harituṃ` (to carry), `anussaritumicchati` (he desires to recollect). Here, when connected with the letter 'i', because it is prohibited by the rule `namakarānaṃ` and so forth, there is no elision of the final vowel of the root.

Tathā tudabyathane, tudituṃ, pavisituṃ, uddisibhuṃ, hotuṃ, sayibhuṃ, netuṃ, juhotuṃ, pajahituṃ, pahātuṃ, dātuṃ. Roddhuṃ, rundhituṃ, tuṃtunādīsupi yogavibhāgena kattari vikaraṇappaccayā, saralopādi ca. Bhottuṃ, bhuñjituṃ, chettuṃ, chindituṃ. Sibbituṃ, boddhuṃ, bujjhituṃ. Jāyituṃ, janituṃ. Pattuṃ, pāpuṇituṃ. Jetuṃ, jinituṃ, ketuṃ, kiṇituṃ, vinicchetuṃ, vinicchinituṃ, ñātuṃ, jānituṃ, gahetuṃ, gaṇhituṃ. Coretuṃ, corayituṃ, pāletuṃ, pālayituṃ.

Similarly, from the root `tud` (to strike): `tudituṃ` (to strike), `pavisituṃ` (to enter), `uddisituṃ` (to point out), `hotuṃ` (to be), `sayituṃ` (to lie down), `netuṃ` (to lead), `juhotuṃ` (to sacrifice), `pajahituṃ` (to abandon), `pahātuṃ` (to forsake), `dātuṃ` (to give). `Roddhuṃ`, `rundhituṃ` (to obstruct). Also, for the suffixes `tuṃ`, `tuna`, and so forth, by separation of the rule, the conjugational sign suffixes occur in the active voice, and there is elision of vowels and so forth. `Bhottuṃ`, `bhuñjituṃ` (to eat); `chettuṃ`, `chindituṃ` (to cut). `Sibbituṃ` (to sew); `boddhuṃ`, `bujjituṃ` (to know). `Jāyituṃ`, `janituṃ` (to be born). `Pattuṃ`, `pāpuṇituṃ` (to attain). `Jetuṃ`, `jinituṃ` (to conquer); `ketuṃ`, `kiṇituṃ` (to buy); `vinicchetuṃ`, `vinicchinituṃ` (to decide); `ñātuṃ`, `jānituṃ` (to know); `gahetuṃ`, `gaṇhituṃ` (to take). `Coretuṃ`, `corayituṃ` (to steal); `pāletuṃ`, `pālayituṃ` (to protect).

Kārite bhāvetuṃ, bhāvayituṃ, kāretuṃ, kārayituṃ, kārāpetuṃ, kārāpayitumicchati iccādi.

In the causative: `bhāvetuṃ`, `bhāvayituṃ` (to cause to be); `kāretuṃ`, `kārayituṃ` (to cause to do); `kārāpetuṃ`, `kārāpayitumicchati` (one wishes to cause to make), and so forth.

“Tavetuṃ vā”ti yogavibhāgena kriyatthakriyāyañca gammamānāyaṃ tuṃpaccayo. Yathā – subuddhuṃ vakkhāmi, bhottuṃ vajati, bhojanāya vajatīti attho. Evaṃ daṭṭhuṃ gacchati, gantumārabhati, gantuṃ payojayati, dassetumāha iccādi.

By the separation of the rule '`tave tuṃ vā`', the suffix 'tuṃ' also occurs when an action for the purpose of another action is understood. For example: `subuddhuṃ vakkhāmi` (I will speak so as to understand well); `bhottuṃ vajati` (he goes to eat), which means 'he goes for the purpose of eating' (`bhojanāya vajatīti attho`). Similarly: `daṭṭhuṃ gacchati` (he goes to see), `gantumārabhati` (he begins to go), `gantuṃ payojayati` (he causes to go), `dassetumāha` (he says to show), and so forth.

“Tu”miti vattate.

The word 'tuṃ' is carried over.

638. Arahasakkādīsu ca.

638. And in conjunction with 'araha,' 'sakkā,' and so forth.

Arahasakkabhabbānucchavikānurūpaiccevamādīsvatthesu payujjamānesu sabbadhātūhi tuṃpaccayo hoti, casaddena kālasamayavelādīsupi. Ninda garahāyaṃ, ko taṃ ninditumarahati[M 0.0392], rājā arahasi bhavituṃ, araho bhavaṃ vattuṃ. Sakkā jetuṃ dhanena vā, sakkā laddhuṃ, kātuṃ sakkhissati. Bhabbo niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ, abhabbo kātuṃ. Anucchaviko bhavaṃ dānaṃ paṭiggahetuṃ. Idaṃ kātuṃ anurūpaṃ. Dānaṃ dātuṃ yuttaṃ, dātuṃ vattuñca labhati, evaṃ vaṭṭati bhāsituṃ, chindituṃ na ca kappati iccādi. Tathā kālo bhuñjituṃ, samayo bhuñjituṃ, velā bhuñjituṃ.

When used in meanings such as 'worthy' (`araha`), 'able' (`sakkā`), 'capable' (`bhabba`), 'suitable' (`anucchavika`), 'fitting' (`anurūpa`), and so forth, the suffix 'tuṃ' is applied to all verbal roots; and with the particle 'ca,' also in senses of time (`kāla`), occasion (`samaya`), or hour (`velā`). From `nind` (to blame): `ko taṃ ninditumarahati` (Who is worthy to blame him?). `Rājā arahasi bhavituṃ` (You are worthy to be king). `Araho bhavaṃ vattuṃ` (You are fit to speak). `Sakkā jetuṃ dhanena vā` (It is possible to conquer with wealth). `Sakkā laddhuṃ` (It is possible to obtain). `Kātuṃ sakkhissati` (He will be able to do). `Bhabbo niyāmaṃ okkamituṃ` (He is capable of entering the fixed path). `Abhabbo kātuṃ` (He is unable to do). `Anucchaviko bhavaṃ dānaṃ paṭiggahetuṃ` (You are suitable to receive a gift). `Idaṃ kātuṃ anurūpaṃ` (This is fitting to do). `Dānaṃ dātuṃ yuttaṃ` (It is proper to give a gift). `Dātuṃ vattuñca labhati` (He gets to give and to speak). `Evaṃ vaṭṭati bhāsituṃ` (Thus it is proper to speak). `Chindituṃ na ca kappati` (It is not right to cut), and so forth. Likewise: `kālo bhuñjituṃ` (It is time to eat), `samayo bhuñjituṃ` (it is the occasion to eat), `velā bhuñjituṃ` (it is the hour to eat).

“Tu”miti vattate.

The word 'tuṃ' is carried over.

639. Pattavacane alamatthesu ca.

639. And in the meanings of 'alam' when the word 'patta' is used.

Alamatthesu pattavacane sati sabbadhātūhi tuṃpaccayo hoti, alaṃsaddassa atthā alamatthā bhūsanapariyattinivāraṇā, tesu alamatthesu. Pattassa vacanaṃ pattavacanaṃ, alameva dānāni dātuṃ, alameva puññāni kātuṃ, sampattameva pariyattamevāti attho.

When the word 'patta' is used in the meanings of 'alam,' the suffix 'tuṃ' occurs after all roots. The meanings of the word 'alam' are adornment, sufficiency, and prohibition; in those meanings of 'alam.' The use of 'patta' is 'pattavacanaṃ.' `Alameva dānāni dātuṃ` (It is indeed sufficient to give gifts), `alameva puññāni kātuṃ` (it is indeed sufficient to perform meritorious deeds) – this means 'it is accomplished, it is sufficient.'

Katvā kammaṃ agacchi, gacchati, gacchissatīti vā atthe –

In the meaning, as in: 'Having done the deed, he went, goes, or will go' –

640. Pubbakālekakattukānaṃ tuna tvāna tvā vā.

640. For actions with a prior time and a single agent, the suffixes 'tuna,' 'tvāna,' or 'tvā' are optionally used.

Pubbakāloti pubbakriyā, eko kattā yesaṃ te ekakattukā, tesaṃ ekakattukānaṃ samānakattukānaṃ dhātūnamantare pubbakāle vattamānadhātumhā tuna tvāna tvāiccete paccayā honti vā.

'Pubbakāla' means a prior action. Those whose agent is one are 'ekakattukā.' From a root that expresses the prior action among roots that have a single agent (or the same agent), these suffixes 'tuna,' 'tvāna,' and 'tvā' optionally occur.

Vāsaddassa vavatthitavibhāsattā tunappaccayo katthaciyeva bhavati. Te ca kitasaññattā, “ekakattukāna”nti vuttattā ca kattariyeva bhavanti. Tune “tavetunādīsu kā”ti kādeso, nipātattā silopo. So kātuna kammaṃ gacchati, akātuna puññaṃ kilamissanti sattā.

Because the word 'vā' implies a restricted option, the suffix 'tuna' occurs only in some instances. And these, being designated as 'kita', and because it is stated 'for those with a single agent,' occur only in the active voice. When 'tuna' follows, the 'kā' substitution occurs by the rule '`kā` in `tavetunādi` and so forth,' and due to being an indeclinable, there is elision of the case ending. `So kātuna kammaṃ gacchati` (He goes, having done the deed); `akātuna puññaṃ kilamissanti sattā` (Not having done merit, beings become weary).

Tvānatvāsu [M 0.0393] “rakāro cā”ti dhātvantalopo, kammaṃ katvāna bhadrakaṃ, dānādīni puññāni katvā saggaṃ gacchati, abhisaṅkharitvā, karitvā. Tathā sibbitvā, jāyitvā, janitvā, dhammaṃ sutvā, sutvāna dhammaṃ modati, suṇitvā, patvā, pāpuṇitvā. Kiṇitvā, jetvā, jinitvā, jitvā. Coretvā, corayitvā, pūjetvā, pūjayitvā. Tathā mettaṃ bhāvetvā, bhāvayitvā, vihāraṃ kāretvā, kārayitvā, kārāpetvā, kārāpayitvā saggaṃ gamissanti iccādi.

When 'tvāna' and 'tvā' follow, there is elision of the final vowel of the root by the rule '`rakāro ca`'. For example: `kammaṃ katvāna bhadrakaṃ` (having done a good deed); `dānādīni puññāni katvā saggaṃ gacchati` (having done meritorious deeds like giving and so forth, he goes to heaven); `abhisaṅkharitvā` (having prepared), `karitvā` (having done). Similarly: `sibbitvā` (having sewn), `jāyitvā` (having been born), `janitvā` (having begotten), `dhammaṃ sutvā` (having heard the Dhamma), `sutvāna dhammaṃ modati` (having heard the Dhamma, one rejoices), `suṇitvā` (having listened), `patvā` (having attained), `pāpuṇitvā` (having reached). `Kiṇitvā` (having bought), `jetvā` (having conquered), `jinitvā` (having won), `jitvā` (having conquered). `Coretvā`, `corayitvā` (having stolen); `pūjetvā`, `pūjayitvā` (having honored). Likewise: `mettaṃ bhāvetvā`, `bhāvayitvā` (having developed loving-kindness); `vihāraṃ kāretvā`, `kārayitvā` (having caused a dwelling to be built), `kārāpetvā`, `kārāpayitvā saggaṃ gamissanti` (having caused it to be made, they will go to heaven), and so forth.

Pubbakāleti kimatthaṃ? Paṭhati, pacati. Ekakattukānanti kiṃ? Bhutte devadatte yaññadatto vajati.

Why is the word 'pubbakāle' used? For cases like: 'He recites, he cooks.' Why is the word 'ekakattukānaṃ' used? For cases like: 'When Devadatta has eaten, Yaññadatta goes.'

“Apatvāna nadiṃ pabbato, atikkamma pabbataṃ nadī”tiādīsu pana sabbattha “bhavatī”ti sambandhato ekakattukatā, pubbakālatā ca gamyate.

However, in phrases like '`apatvāna nadiṃ pabbato`' (the mountain, not having reached the river) and '`atikkamma pabbataṃ nadī`' (the river, having crossed the mountain), in all such cases, due to the connection with an implied '`bhavati`' (is), a single agent and a prior action are understood.

“Vā”ti vattate.

The word 'vā' is carried over.

641. Sabbehi tunādīnaṃ yo.

641. After all roots, 'ya' is substituted for the suffixes beginning with 'tuna'.

Sabbehi sopasaggānupasaggehi dhātūhi paresaṃ tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ yasaddādeso hoti vā. Vanda abhivandane abhipubbo, tvāpaccayassa yo, ikārāgamo ca, abhivandiya bhāsissaṃ, abhivanditvā, vandiya, vanditvā. Tathā abhibhuyya, dvittarassattāni, abhibhavitvā, abhibhotvā.

After all roots, whether with or without prefixes, the substitution of 'ya' for the following suffixes beginning with 'tuna' optionally occurs. The root 'vand' is in the sense of veneration, with 'abhi' as a prefix; 'ya' is substituted for the 'tvā' suffix, and the 'i' augment is added: as in `abhivandiya bhāsissaṃ` (having venerated, I will speak), `abhivanditvā` (having venerated), `vandiya` (having venerated), `vanditvā` (having venerated). Similarly: `abhibhuyya` (having overcome), with doubling and shortening; `abhibhavitvā` (having overcome), `abhibhotvā` (having overcome).

Si sevāyaṃ, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ikārassa āttaṃ, nissāya, nissitvā.

'Si' is in the meaning of serving; by [the rule] 'kvaci dhātu' and so forth, the 'i' becomes 'ā': as in 'nissāya' (having relied on), 'nissitvā' (having relied on).

Bhaja sevāyaṃ, “tathā kattari cā”ti pubbarūpattaṃ, vibhajja, vibhajiya, vibhajitvā.

'Bhaja' is in the meaning of serving; by [the rule] 'tathā kattari ca,' there is assimilation to the preceding form: as in 'vibhajja' (having divided), 'vibhajiya' (having divided), 'vibhajitvā' (having divided).

Disa [M 0.0394] atisajjane, uddissa, uddisiya, uddisitvā. Pavissa, pavisiya, pavisitvā.

'Disa' is in the meaning of pointing out: as in 'uddissa' (having pointed out), 'uddisiya' (having pointed out), 'uddisitvā' (having pointed out). 'Pavissa' (having entered), 'pavisiya' (having entered), 'pavisitvā' (having entered).

Nī pāpuṇane, upanīya, upanetvā. Atiseyya, atisayitvā. Ohāya, ohitvā, jahitvā, hitvā. Ādāya, ādiyitvā, “divādito yo”ti yappaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātvantassikāro ca, datvā, datvāna. Pidhāya, pidahitvā. Bhuñjiya, bhuñjitvā, bhotvā. Viceyya, vicinitvā. Viññāya, vijānitvā, ñatvā.
