'Nī' is in the meaning of reaching: [as in] 'having approached' (upanīya), 'having approached' (upanetvā). 'Having surpassed' (atiseyya), 'having surpassed' (atisayitvā). 'Having abandoned' (ohāya), 'having abandoned' (ohitvā), 'having abandoned' (jahitvā), 'having left' (hitvā). 'Having taken' (ādāya), 'having taken' (ādiyitvā); by [the rule] 'divādito yo,' the 'ya' suffix is added, and by [the rule] 'kvaci dhātu' and so forth, the end of the root becomes 'i'. 'Having given' (datvā), 'having given' (datvāna). 'Having covered' (pidhāya), 'having covered' (pidahitvā). 'Having eaten' (bhuñjiya), 'having eaten' (bhuñjitvā), 'having eaten' (bhotvā). 'Having examined' (viceyya), 'having examined' (vicinitvā). 'Having known' (viññāya), 'having known' (vijānitvā), 'having known' (ñatvā).

“Yathāgamaṃ, tunādīsū”ti ca vattate.

[The words] 'yathāgamaṃ' and 'tunādīsu' are carried over.

642. Dadhantato yo kvaci.

642. From roots ending in 'da' or 'dha,' 'ya' is sometimes added.

Dakāradhakārantehi dhātūhi yathāgamaṃ yakārāgamo hoti kvaci tunādīsu paccayesu. Yavato dakārassa jakāro, samāpajjitvā, uppajjitvā, bhijjitvā, chijjitvā gato. Budha avagamane, “tathā kattari cā”ti sakhātvantassa yakārassa cavaggo, bujjhiya, bujjhitvā. Virajjhiya, virajjhitvā. Rundhiya, rundhitvā.

From roots ending in 'da' or 'dha,' the 'ya' augment is sometimes added according to tradition when the 'tuna' and so forth suffixes follow. When 'ya' follows, 'da' becomes 'ja': as in 'samāpajjitvā' (having attained), 'uppajjitvā' (having arisen), 'bhijjitvā' (having split), 'chijjitvā' (having broken), 'gato' (gone). 'Budha' is in the meaning of understanding; by [the rule] 'tathā kattari ca', the final consonant and the following 'ya' are assimilated into a palatal consonant: as in 'bujjhiya' (having understood), 'bujjhitvā' (having understood); 'virajjhiya' (having become dispassionate), 'virajjhitvā' (having become dispassionate); 'rundhiya' (having obstructed), 'rundhitvā' (having obstructed).

“Tunādīna”nti adhikāro, “vā”ti ca.

The word 'tunādīnaṃ' is the governing rule, and 'vā' is also carried over.

643. Canantehi raccaṃ.

643. From roots ending in 'ca' or 'na,' 'racca' is substituted.

Cakāranakārantehi dhātūhi paresaṃ tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ raccādeso hoti vā, “racca”nti yogavibhāgena aññasmāpi, vavatthitavibhāsatthoyaṃ vāsaddo, rādilopo. Vica vivecane vipubbo, vivicca, viviccitvā, “yo kvacī”ti yogavibhāgena yakārāgamo.

For the 'tuna' and so forth suffixes following roots ending in 'ca' or 'na,' the 'racca' substitution optionally occurs. By splitting the rule as 'racca,' it also applies to other roots. This word 'vā' has the meaning of a restricted option, and there is elision of the initial 'ra.' 'Vica' is in the meaning of separation, with 'vi' as a prefix: as in 'vivicca' (having separated), 'viviccitvā' (having separated). By splitting the rule 'yo kvaci,' the 'ya' augment is added.

Pava pāke, pacca, pacciya, paccitvā. Vimucca, vimuccitvā.

'Paca' is in the meaning of cooking: as in 'pacca' (having cooked), 'pacciya' (having cooked), 'paccitvā' (having cooked). 'Vimucca' (having been released), 'vimuccitvā' (having been released).

Hana [M 0.0395] hiṃsāgatīsu, āhacca, upahacca, āhantvā, upahantvā.

'Hana' is in the meanings of harming and going: as in 'āhacca' (having struck), 'upahacca' (having struck), 'āhantvā' (having struck), 'upahantvā' (having struck).

Vāti kiṃ? Avamañña, avamaññitvā, mantvā, nyassañakāro.

Why is the word 'vā' used? For cases such as: 'avamañña' (having disdained), 'avamaññitvā' (having disdained), 'mantvā' (having thought); this involves the 'ñ' from 'nya'.

I gatimhi, yogavibhāgena raccādeso, paṭicca, avecca, upecca upetvā. Kara karaṇe, sakkacca, adhikicca, ikārāgamo, kariya.

'I' is in the meaning of going; by splitting the rule, the 'racca' substitution occurs: as in 'paṭicca' (having relied on), 'avecca' (having known), 'upecca' (having approached), 'upetvā' (having approached). 'Kara' is in the meaning of doing: as in 'sakkacca' (having done well), 'adhikicca' (having aimed at); with the 'i' augment: 'kariya' (having done).

Disa pekkhaṇe –

'Disa' is in the meaning of seeing—

644. Disā svānasvāntalopo ca.

644. For 'disa,' the substitutions are 'svāna' and 'svā,' and there is elision of the end of the root.

Disaiccetāya dhātuyā paresaṃ tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ svāna svāiccādesā honti vā, dhātvantassa lopo ca. Disvānassa etadahosi, cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā.

For this root 'disa,' the substitutions 'svāna' and 'svā' optionally occur for the following 'tuna' and so forth suffixes, and the end of the root is elided. As in: 'disvānassa etadahosi' (this occurred to him, having seen); 'cakkhunā rūpaṃ disvā' (having seen a form with the eye).

Vāti kiṃ? Nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhuṃ, daṭṭhā. Passiya, passituna, passitvā.

Why is the word 'vā' used? For cases such as: 'nekkhammaṃ daṭṭhuṃ' (to see renunciation), 'daṭṭhā' (having seen). Also: 'passiya' (having seen), 'passituna' (to see), 'passitvā' (having seen).

Antaggahaṇaṃ antalopaggahaṇañcānuvattate.

The mention of the final letter and the mention of the elision of the final letter are carried over.

645. Ma ha da bhehi mma yha jja bbha ddhā ca.

645. From roots ending in 'ma,' 'ha,' 'da,' or 'bha,' the substitutions 'mma,' 'yha,' 'jja,' 'bbha,' and 'ddhā' occur.

Ma ha da bhaiccevamantehi dhātūhi paresaṃ tunādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ yathākkamaṃ mma yha jja bbha ddhāiccete ādesā honti vā, dhātvantalopo ca. Makārantehi tāva āgamma, āgantvā. Kamu padavikkhepe, okkamma, okkamitvā, nikkhamma, nikkhamitvā, abhiramma, abhiramitvā.

For the 'tuna' and so forth suffixes following roots ending in 'ma,' 'ha,' 'da,' and 'bha,' these substitutions 'mma,' 'yha,' 'jja,' 'bbha,' and 'ddhā' occur respectively and optionally, and the final letter of the root is elided. First, for those ending in 'ma': 'āgamma,' 'āgantvā.' 'Kamu' is in the meaning of stepping: 'okkamma,' 'okkamitvā,' 'nikkhamma,' 'nikkhamitvā,' 'abhiramma,' 'abhiramitvā.'

Hakārantehi paggayha, paggaṇhitvā, paggahetvā. Muha vecitte, sammuyha, sammuyhitvā, yakārāgamo, āruyha, āruhitvā, ogayha, ogahetvā.

For those ending in 'ha': 'paggayha,' 'paggaṇhitvā,' 'paggahetvā.' 'Muha' is in the meaning of confusion: 'sammuyha,' 'sammuyhitvā.' With the 'ya' augment: 'āruyha,' 'āruhitvā,' 'ogayha,' 'ogahetvā.'

Dakārantehi [M 0.0396] uppajja, uppajjitvā, pamajja, pamajjitvā, upasampajja, upasampajjitvā. Chidi dvidhākaraṇe, acchijja, chijja, chijjitvā, chindiya, chinditvā, chetvā.

For those ending in 'da': 'uppajja,' 'uppajjitvā,' 'pamajja,' 'pamajjitvā,' 'upasampajja,' 'upasampajjitvā.' 'Chidi' is in the meaning of dividing into two: 'acchijja,' 'chijja,' 'chijjitvā,' 'chindiya,' 'chinditvā,' 'chetvā.'

Bhakārantehi rabha rābhasse, ārabbha kathesi, āraddhā, ārabhitvā. Labha lābhe, upalabbha, upaladdhā, saddhaṃ paṭilabhitvā puññāni karonti iccādi.

For those ending in 'bha': 'rabha' is in the meaning of violence or haste: 'ārabbha kathesi,' 'āraddhā,' 'ārabhitvā.' 'Labha' is in the meaning of gain: 'upalabbha,' 'upaladdhā,' 'saddhaṃ paṭilabhitvā puññāni karonti,' and so forth.

Tavetunādippaccayantanayo.

The Section on Suffixes such as '-tave' and '-tuṃ'.

Vattamānakālikamānantappaccayantanaya

The Section on the Present Tense Suffixes '-māna' and '-anta'.

646. Vattamāne mānantā.

646. In the present tense, the suffixes are '-māna' and '-anta'.

Āraddho aparisamatto attho vattamāno, tasmiṃ vattamāne kāle gammamāne sabbadhātūhi mānaantaiccete paccayā honti. Te ca kitasaññattā “kattari kita”ti kattari bhavanti.

An action that has begun but is not yet completed is called 'present'. When that present time is indicated, from all roots these suffixes, namely '-māna' and '-anta', occur. And being designated as 'kita', they occur in the agent sense according to the rule 'kattari kita'.

Antamānappaccayānañcettha “parasamaññāpayoge”ti parasamaññāvasena parassapadattanopadasaññattā tyādīsu viya antamānesu ca vikaraṇappaccayā bhavanti.

And here, for the suffixes '-anta' and '-māna', due to their designation as 'parassapada' and 'attanopada' by means of another's convention, according to the rule 'parasamaññāpayoge', the conjugational sign suffixes also occur with '-anta' and '-māna', just as they do with suffixes like '-ti' and so forth.

Teneva mānappaccayo “attanopadāni bhāve ca kammanī”ti bhāvakammesupi hoti, tassa ca “attanopadāni parassapadatta”nti kvaci antappaccayādeso ca.

For that reason, the suffix '-māna' also occurs in the impersonal and passive senses, according to the rule 'attanopadāni bhāve ca kammanī'. And sometimes, the suffix '-anta' is substituted for it, according to the rule 'attanopadāni parassapadatta'.

Gamu, sappa gatimhi, gacchatīti atthe antappaccayo, “bhūvādito a”iti appaccayo, “gamissanto ccho vā sabbāsū”ti dhātvantassa cchādeso, saralopādi, nāmabyapadese syādyuppatti. Gacchanta si itīdha “vā”ti vattamāne “simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo aṃ” iti ntassa amādeso.

For the roots Gamu and Sappa, in the sense of motion: in the sense of 'gacchati' (he goes), the suffix -anta occurs. The suffix -a occurs according to the rule 'bhūvādito a'. The substitution of -ccha for the final consonant of the root occurs according to the rule 'gamissanto ccho vā sabbāsū'. There is elision of vowels, etc., and in nominal designation, the arising of case endings such as -si. Here, in 'gacchanta si', when 'vā' is operative from a previous rule, the substitution of -aṃ for -nta occurs according to the rule 'simhi gacchantādīnaṃ ntasaddo aṃ'.

Vāsaddassa [M 0.0397] vavatthibhavibhāsattā ekārokāraparassa na bhavati, saralopādi, so puriso gacchaṃ, gacchanto gaṇhāti, sesaṃ guṇavantusamaṃ.

Because the word 'vā' indicates an option, a certain operation does not occur when followed by the vowel 'e' or 'o'. There is elision of vowels, etc. That man, going (gacchaṃ), or going (gacchanto), takes. The remainder is similar to the word guṇavantu.

Itthiyaṃ “nadādito vā ī”ti īpaccayo, “sesesu ntuvā”ti ntubyapadese “vā”ti adhikicca “ntussa tamīkāre”ti takāre saralopasilopā, sā kaññā gacchatī, gacchantī iccādi itthisamaṃ.

In the feminine, the suffix -ī is optionally added according to the rule 'nadādito vā ī'. When designated as 'ntu' by 'sesesu ntuvā', with 'vā' being carried forward, a 't' is substituted according to the rule 'ntussa tamīkāre', with elision of a vowel and the case ending 'si'. That maiden (is) going (gacchatī), or going (gacchantī), etc., similar to feminine forms.

Napuṃsake pure viya ntassa amādeso, taṃ cittaṃ gacchaṃ, gacchantaṃ, gacchantāni iccādi pulliṅgasamaṃ.

In the neuter, as before, the substitution of -aṃ for -nta occurs. That mind (is) going (gacchaṃ), or going (gacchantaṃ), or going (gacchantāni), etc., similar to masculine forms.

Tathā gacchatīti atthe mānappaccayo, cchādesādi ca, so gacchamāno gaṇhāti, te gacchamānā iccādi purisasaddasamaṃ. Sā gacchamānā, tā gacchamānāyo iccādi kaññāsaddasamaṃ. Taṃ gacchamānaṃ, tāni gacchamānāni iccādi cittasaddasamaṃ.

Similarly, in the sense of 'gacchati' (he goes), the suffix -māna occurs, as well as the substitution of -ccha, etc. He, going (gacchamāno), takes; they, going (gacchamānā), etc., is similar to the word 'purisa'. She, going (gacchamānā); they, going (gacchamānāyo), etc., is similar to the word 'kaññā'. That, going (gacchamānaṃ); those, going (gacchamānāni), etc., is similar to the word 'citta'.

Gacchīyatīti atthe “attanopadāni bhāve ca kammanī”ti kammani mānappaccayo, “bhāvakammesu yo”ti yappaccayo, “ivaṇṇāgamo vā”ti ikārāgamo, cchādeso, so tena gacchiyamāno, sā gacchiyamānā, taṃ gacchiyamānaṃ.

In the sense of 'gacchīyati' (it is gone to), the suffix -māna is used in the passive voice according to the rule 'attanopadāni bhāve ca kammanī'. According to the rule 'bhāvakammesu yo', the suffix -ya is applied. According to the rule 'ivaṇṇāgamo vā', the vowel 'i' is inserted, and there is the substitution of -ccha. He, being gone to by him (so tena gacchiyamāno); she, being gone to (sā gacchiyamānā); that, being gone to (taṃ gacchiyamānaṃ).

Cchādesābhāve “pubbarūpañcā”ti yakārassa makāro, dhammo adhigammamāno hitāya bhavati, adhigammamānā, adhigammamānaṃ.

In the absence of the -ccha substitution, the 'ya' becomes 'ma' according to the rule 'pubbarūpañcā'. The Dhamma, being realized, leads to welfare; she, being realized; that, being realized.

Tathā maha pūjāyaṃ, mahatīti mahaṃ, mahanto, mahatī, mahantī, mahaṃ, mahantaṃ, mahamāno, mahamānā, mahamānaṃ. Kammani “yamhi dādhāmāṭhāhāpā maha mathādīnamī”iti dhātvantassa akārassa īkāro, mahīyamāno, mahīyamānā, mahīyamānaṃ.

Similarly, for the root 'maha' in the sense of worship: in the sense of 'mahati' (he worships/honors), the forms are mahaṃ, mahanto, mahatī, mahantī, mahaṃ, mahantaṃ, mahamāno, mahamānā, mahamānaṃ. In the passive, the final 'a' of the root becomes 'ī' according to the rule 'yamhi dādhāmāṭhāhāpā maha mathādīnamī', hence mahīyamāno, mahīyamānā, mahīyamānaṃ.

Evaṃ [M 0.0398] caratīti caraṃ, caratī, carantī, carantaṃ, caramāno, cariyamāno, pacatīti pacaṃ, pacatī, pacantī, pacantaṃ, pacamāno, paccamāno, “tassa cavagga”iccādinā cavaggattaṃ, dvittañca.

Thus, in the sense of 'carati' (he walks), the forms are caraṃ, caratī, carantī, carantaṃ, caramāno, cariyamāno. In the sense of 'pacati' (he cooks), the forms are pacaṃ, pacatī, pacantī, pacantaṃ, pacamāno, paccamāno. By the rule 'tassa cavagga', etc., there is transformation into a palatal and also gemination.

Bhū sattāyaṃ, bhavatīti atthe antappaccayo, appaccayavuddhiavādesādi, so bhavaṃ, bhavanto. Itthiyaṃ īpaccayo, “bhavato bhoto”ti bhotādeso, bhotī, bhotī, bhotiyo. Napuṃsake bhavaṃ, bhavantaṃ, bhavantāni, abhibhavamāno. Bhāve bhūyamānaṃ. Kammani abhibhūyamāno.

For the root Bhū, in the sense of existence: in the sense of 'bhavati' (he is/becomes), the suffix -anta occurs, along with the suffix -a, vowel strengthening, the substitution of -ava, etc. Hence, he, being (bhavaṃ), or being (bhavanto). In the feminine, the suffix -ī occurs, and the substitution of 'bhoto' for 'bhavato' according to the rule 'bhavato bhoto', hence bhotī, bhotī, bhotiyo. In the neuter, bhavaṃ, bhavantaṃ, bhavantāni, and abhibhavamāno. In the impersonal sense, bhūyamānaṃ. In the passive sense, abhibhūyamāno.

Jara vayohānimhi, “jara marāna”ntiādinā jīra jīyyādesā, jīratīti jīraṃ, jīrantī, jīrantaṃ, jīramāno, jīrīyamāno, jīyaṃ, jīyantī, jīyantaṃ, jīyamāno, jīyyamāno.

For the root Jara, in the sense of the decline of life: by the rule 'jara marāna', etc., the substitutions 'jīra' and 'jīyya' occur. In the sense of 'jīrati' (it ages), the forms are jīraṃ, jīrantī, jīrantaṃ, jīramāno, jīrīyamāno, and jīyaṃ, jīyantī, jīyantaṃ, jīyamāno, jīyyamāno.

Mara pāṇacāge, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ekassa yakārassa lopo, maratīti mīyaṃ, mīyantī, mīyantaṃ, mīyamāno, mīyyamāno, maraṃ, marantī, marantaṃ, maramāno, marīyamāno. Labhaṃ, labhantī, labhantaṃ, labhamāno, labbhamāno. Vahaṃ, vahantī, vahantaṃ, vahamāno, vuyhamāno. “Isuyamūnamanto ccho vā”ti cchādeso, icchatīti icchaṃ, icchantī, icchantaṃ, icchamāno, icchīyamāno, issamāno.

For the root Mara, in the sense of relinquishing life: by the rule 'kvaci dhātū', etc., the elision of one 'ya' occurs. In the sense of 'marati' (he dies), the forms are mīyaṃ, mīyantī, mīyantaṃ, mīyamāno, mīyyamāno, and maraṃ, marantī, marantaṃ, maramāno, marīyamāno. For 'labhati' (he obtains): labhaṃ, labhantī, labhantaṃ, labhamāno, labbhamāno. For 'vahati' (he carries): vahaṃ, vahantī, vahantaṃ, vahamāno, vuyhamāno. By the rule 'Isuyamūnamanto ccho vā', the substitution of -ccha occurs. In the sense of 'icchati' (he desires), the forms are icchaṃ, icchantī, icchantaṃ, icchamāno, icchīyamāno, issamāno.

“Disassa passadissadakkhā vā”ti passa dissa dakkhādesā, passatīti passaṃ, passantī, passantaṃ, passamāno, vipassīyamāno, dissamāno, dissanto, mānassa antādeso, dissaṃ, dissantī, dissantaṃ, dakkhaṃ, dakkhantī, dakkhantaṃ, dakkhamāno dakkhiyamāno iccādi.

By the rule 'Disassa passadissadakkhā vā', the substitutions 'passa', 'dissa', and 'dakkha' occur for the root 'dis'. In the sense of 'passati' (he sees), the forms are passaṃ, passantī, passantaṃ, passamāno, vipassīyamāno. Also dissamāno, dissanto; with the substitution of -anta for -māna, the forms are dissaṃ, dissantī, dissantaṃ. Also dakkhaṃ, dakkhantī, dakkhantaṃ, dakkhamāno, dakkhiyamāno, etc.

Tuda byathane, tudatīti tudaṃ, tudantī, tudantaṃ, tudamāno, tujjamāno. Pavisatīti pavisaṃ, pavisantī, pavisantaṃ, pavisamāno, pavisīyamāno iccādi.

For the root Tuda, in the sense of piercing or afflicting: in the sense of 'tudati' (he pierces), the forms are tudaṃ, tudantī, tudantaṃ, tudamāno, tujjamāno. In the sense of 'pavisati' (he enters), the forms are pavisaṃ, pavisantī, pavisantaṃ, pavisamāno, pavisīyamāno, etc.

Hū, [M 0.0399] bhū sattāyaṃ, appaccayalopo, pahotīti pahonto, pahontī, pahontaṃ, pahūyamānaṃ tena. Setīti sento, sentī, sentaṃ, semāno, sayaṃ, sayantī, sayantaṃ, sayamāno, sayāno vā, mānassa ānādeso, atisīyamāno.

For the roots Hū and Bhū, in the sense of existence: with elision of the suffix -a, in the sense of 'pahoti' (he is able), the forms are pahonto, pahontī, pahontaṃ, and pahūyamānaṃ by that. In the sense of 'seti' (he sleeps), the forms are sento, sentī, sentaṃ, semāno, and sayaṃ, sayantī, sayantaṃ, sayamāno, or sayāno (with the substitution of -āna for -māna), and atisīyamāno.

Asa sabbhāve, “sabbatthāsassādilopo cā”ti akārassa lopo, atthīti saṃ, santo, satī, santī, santaṃ, samāno, samānā, samānaṃ.

For the root Asa, in the sense of existence: by the rule 'sabbatthāsassādilopo cā', the initial 'a' of 'asa' is elided. In the sense of 'atthi' (it is), the forms are saṃ, santo, satī, santī, santaṃ, samāno, samānā, samānaṃ.

Ṭhā gatinivattimhi, “vā”ti vattamāne “ṭhā tiṭṭho”ti tiṭṭhādeso, tiṭṭhaṃ, tiṭṭhantī, tiṭṭhantaṃ, tiṭṭhamāno. Tiṭṭhābhāve “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ṭhāto hakārāgamo, rassattañca, upaṭṭhahaṃ, upaṭṭhahantī, upaṭṭhahantaṃ, upaṭṭhahamāno. Ṭhīyamānaṃ tena, upaṭṭhīyamāno, upaṭṭhahīyamāno.

For the root Ṭhā, in the sense of the cessation of movement: when 'vā' is operative from a previous rule, the substitution 'tiṭṭha' occurs for 'ṭhā' according to the rule 'ṭhā tiṭṭho', hence tiṭṭhaṃ, tiṭṭhantī, tiṭṭhantaṃ, tiṭṭhamāno. In the absence of the 'tiṭṭha' substitution, by the rule 'kvaci dhātū', etc., the insertion of 'ha' after 'ṭhā' occurs, as well as shortening of the vowel, hence upaṭṭhahaṃ, upaṭṭhahantī, upaṭṭhahantaṃ, upaṭṭhahamāno. Being stood upon by that: Ṭhīyamānaṃ, and upaṭṭhīyamāno, upaṭṭhahīyamāno.

Pā pāne, “pā pibo”ti pibādeso, pibatīti pibaṃ, pibantī, pibantaṃ, pibamāno, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā bakārassa vattaṃ, pivaṃ, pivantī, pivantaṃ, pivamāno, pīyamāno, pīyamānā, pīyamānaṃ iccādi.

For the root Pā, in the sense of drinking: the substitution 'piba' occurs for 'pā' according to the rule 'pā pibo'. In the sense of 'pibati' (he drinks), the forms are pibaṃ, pibantī, pibantaṃ, pibamāno. By the rule 'kvaci dhātū', etc., the change of 'ba' to 'va' occurs, hence pivaṃ, pivantī, pivantaṃ, pivamāno, pīyamāno, pīyamānā, pīyamānaṃ, etc.

Hu dānādanahabyappadānesu, appaccaye pure viya dvibhāvādi, juhotīti juhaṃ, juhantī, juhantaṃ, juhamāno, hūyamāno. Evaṃ jahaṃ, jahantī, jahantaṃ, jahamāno, jahīyamāno. Dadātīti dadaṃ, dadantī, dadantaṃ, dadamāno, dvittābhāve dānaṃ dento, dentī, dentaṃ, dīyamāno.

For the root Hu, in the senses of giving, taking, and offering sacrifices: when the suffix -a is used, as before, there is reduplication, etc. In the sense of 'juhoti' (he offers), the forms are juhaṃ, juhantī, juhantaṃ, juhamāno, hūyamāno. Similarly, for 'jahati' (he abandons), the forms are jahaṃ, jahantī, jahantaṃ, jahamāno, jahīyamāno. In the sense of 'dadāti' (he gives), the forms are dadaṃ, dadantī, dadantaṃ, dadamāno. In the absence of reduplication, as in 'dānaṃ dento' (giving a gift), the forms are dento, dentī, dentaṃ, and dīyamāno.

Rudhi āvaraṇe, “rudhādito niggahītapubbañcā”ti appaccayaniggahītāgamā, rundhatīti rundhaṃ, rundhantī, rundhantaṃ, rundhamāno, rujjhamāno. Bhuñjatīti bhuñjaṃ, bhuñjantī, bhuñjantaṃ, bhuñjamāno, bhujjamāno iccādi.

For the root Rudhi, in the sense of obstructing: by the rule 'rudhādito niggahītapubbañcā', the suffix -a and a preceding niggahīta are inserted. In the sense of 'rundhati' (he obstructs), the forms are rundhaṃ, rundhantī, rundhantaṃ, rundhamāno, rujjhamāno. In the sense of 'bhuñjati' (he enjoys), the forms are bhuñjaṃ, bhuñjantī, bhuñjantaṃ, bhuñjamāno, bhujjamāno, etc.

Divu [M 0.0400] kīḷāyaṃ, “divādito yo”ti yappaccayo, “tathā kattari cā”ti pubbarūpattaṃ, battañca, dibbatīti dibbaṃ, dibbantī, dibbantaṃ, dibbamāno. Evaṃ bujjhatīti bujjhaṃ, bujjhanto, bujjhamāno, cavaggādeso. Janī pātubhāve, “janādīnamā”ti yogavibhāgena āttaṃ, jāyatīti jāyaṃ, jāyamāno, jaññamāno.

For the root Divu, in the sense of playing: by the rule 'divādito yo', the suffix -ya occurs, and by the rule 'tathā kattari cā', there is assimilation to the preceding form and also transformation into 'ba'. In the sense of 'dibbati' (he plays), the forms are dibbaṃ, dibbantī, dibbantaṃ, dibbamāno. Similarly, in the sense of 'bujjhati' (he awakens), the forms are bujjhaṃ, bujjhanto, bujjhamāno, with substitution of a palatal. For the root Janī, in the sense of manifestation: by the rule 'janādīnamā', through separation of the rule, there is lengthening to 'ā'. In the sense of 'jāyati' (he is born/arises), the forms are jāyaṃ, jāyamāno, jaññamāno.

Su savaṇe, “svādito”tiādinā ṇu ṇā uṇā ca, suṇātīti suṇaṃ, suṇanto, suṇamāno, sūyamāno, suyyamāno. Pāpuṇātīti pāpuṇaṃ, pāpuṇamāno, pāpīyamāno.

For the root Su, in the sense of hearing: by the rule 'svādito', etc., the suffixes ṇu, ṇā, and uṇā occur. In the sense of 'suṇāti' (he hears), the forms are suṇaṃ, suṇanto, suṇamāno, sūyamāno, suyyamāno. In the sense of 'pāpuṇāti' (he reaches), the forms are pāpuṇaṃ, pāpuṇamāno, pāpīyamāno.

“Kiyādito nā”ti nā, rassattaṃ, kiṇātīti kiṇaṃ, kīṇamāno, kīyamāno. Vinicchinātīti vinicchinaṃ, vinicchinamāno, vinicchīyamāno, cinaṃ, cīyamāno. Jānātīti jānaṃ, jānamāno, jādeso, ñāyamāno. Gaṇhātīti gaṇhaṃ, gaṇhamāno, gayhamāno.

By the rule ‘Kiyādito nā’, the suffix is ‘nā,’ with shortening. ‘Kiṇāti’ (he buys) becomes ‘kiṇaṃ’ (buying), ‘kīṇamāno’ (buying), ‘kīyamāno’ (being bought). ‘Vinicchināti’ (he discriminates) becomes ‘vinicchinaṃ’ (discriminating), ‘vinicchinamāno’ (discriminating), ‘vinicchīyamāno’ (being discriminated); ‘cinaṃ’ (collecting), ‘cīyamāno’ (being collected). ‘Jānāti’ (he knows) becomes ‘jānaṃ’ (knowing), ‘jānamāno’ (knowing); there is a substitution of 'jā', and the passive form is ‘ñāyamāno’ (being known). ‘Gaṇhāti’ (he takes) becomes ‘gaṇhaṃ’ (taking), ‘gaṇhamāno’ (taking), ‘gayhamāno’ (being taken).

Kara karaṇe, karotīti atthe “vattamāne mānantā”ti antappaccayo, “tanādito oyirā”ti o, “tassa vā”ti adhikicca “uttamokāro”ti uttaṃ, “karassākāro cā”ti akārassukāro. “Yavakārā cā”ti sare ukārassa vattaṃ, dvittaṃ, “bo vassā”ti bakāradvayañca, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ralopo, so kubbaṃ, kubbanto, kubbatī, kubbantī, kubbantaṃ. Uttābhāve – kammaṃ karonto, karontī, karontaṃ. Māne – uttadvayaṃ, kurumāno, kurumānā, kurumānaṃ, kubbāno vā. Kammani kayiramāno, karīyamāno vā iccādi.

The root ‘kara’ in the sense of doing: in the meaning of ‘he does,’ the suffix ‘anta’ is applied by the rule ‘vattamāne mānantā’. By ‘tanādito oyirā’, the infix ‘o’ is applied. Governed by ‘tassa vā’, by the rule ‘uttamokāro’, ‘o’ becomes ‘u’ (`uttaṃ`). By ‘karassākāro ca’, the ‘a’ of ‘kara’ also becomes ‘u’. By ‘Yavakārā ca’, when a vowel follows, ‘u’ becomes ‘va’, and there is doubling. And by ‘bo vassā’, ‘v’ becomes ‘b’, and there is doubling of ‘b’. By ‘kvaci dhātū’ etc., the ‘ra’ is elided. Thus, the forms are ‘kubbaṃ,’ ‘kubbanto,’ ‘kubbatī,’ ‘kubbantī,’ ‘kubbantaṃ’. In the absence of the change to ‘u’ (`utta`): ‘kammaṃ karonto,’ ‘karontī,’ ‘karontaṃ’. With the `māna` suffix, the two changes to ‘u’ apply, resulting in ‘kurumāno,’ ‘kurumānā,’ ‘kurumānaṃ,’ or alternatively ‘kubbāno’. In the passive: ‘kayiramāno,’ or ‘karīyamāno,’ etc.

Cura theyye, “curādito”tiādinā ṇe ṇayā, coretīti corento, corentī, corentaṃ, corayaṃ, corayatī, corayantaṃ, corayamāno, corīyamāno. Pāletīti pālento, pālentī, pālentaṃ, pālayaṃ, pālayantī, pālayantaṃ, pālayamāno, pālīyamāno iccādi.

The root ‘cura’ in the sense of stealing: by ‘curādito’ etc., the suffixes ‘ṇe’ and ‘ṇaya’ are applied. From ‘coreti’ are derived the forms ‘corento,’ ‘corentī,’ ‘corentaṃ,’ ‘corayaṃ,’ ‘corayatī,’ ‘corayantaṃ,’ ‘corayamāno,’ ‘corīyamāno’. From ‘pāleti’ are derived ‘pālento,’ ‘pālentī,’ ‘pālentaṃ,’ ‘pālayaṃ,’ ‘pālayantī,’ ‘pālayantaṃ,’ ‘pālayamāno,’ ‘pālīyamāno,’ etc.

Kārite [M 0.0401] bhāvetīti bhāvento, bhāventī, bhāventaṃ, bhāvayaṃ, bhāvayantī, bhāvayantaṃ, bhāvayamāno, bhāvīyamāno. Kāretīti kāronto, kārentī, kārentaṃ, kārayaṃ, kārayantī, kārayantaṃ, kārayamāno, kārīyamāno, kārāpento, kārāpentī, kārāpentaṃ, kārāpayaṃ, kārāpayantī, kārāpayantaṃ, kārāpayamāno, kārāpīyamāno iccādi.

In the causative: from ‘bhāveti’ are derived ‘bhāvento,’ ‘bhāventī,’ ‘bhāventaṃ,’ ‘bhāvayaṃ,’ ‘bhāvayantī,’ ‘bhāvayantaṃ,’ ‘bhāvayamāno,’ ‘bhāvīyamāno’. From ‘kāreti’ are derived ‘kāronto,’ ‘kārentī,’ ‘kārentaṃ,’ ‘kārayaṃ,’ ‘kārayantī,’ ‘kārayantaṃ,’ ‘kārayamāno,’ ‘kārīyamāno,’ ‘kārāpento,’ ‘kārāpentī,’ ‘kārāpentaṃ,’ ‘kārāpayaṃ,’ ‘kārāpayantī,’ ‘kārāpayantaṃ,’ ‘kārāpayamāno,’ ‘kārāpīyamāno,’ etc.

Vattamānakālikamānantappaccayantanayo.

The section on words ending in the suffixes ‘māna’ and ‘anta’ in the present tense.

Anāgatakālikappaccayantanaya

The section on words ending in suffixes for the future tense.

“Kāle”ti adhikāro.

‘Kāle’ (in the tense) is the governing rule.

647. Bhavissati gamādīhi ṇī ghiṇa.

647. In the future tense, the suffixes ‘ṇī’ and ‘ghiṇa’ are applied to roots such as ‘gam’.

Bhavissati kāle gammamāne gamādīhi dhātūhi ṇī ghiṇaiccete paccayā honti. Ṇakārā vuddhatthā. Āyati gamanaṃ sīlamassāti atthe ṇī, vuddhiṇalopā. Gāmī, gāmino, āgāmī kālo. Ghiṇapaccaye – “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ghalopo, gāmaṃ gāmi, gāmī, gāmayo.

When the future tense is understood, these suffixes ‘ṇī’ and ‘ghiṇa’ occur after roots such as ‘gam’. The letter ‘ṇ’ indicates vowel gradation (`vuddhi`). In the sense of ‘one whose nature is to go in the future,’ the suffix ‘ṇī’ is applied, with vowel gradation and elision of ‘ṇ’. The forms are ‘gāmī,’ ‘gāmino,’ ‘āgāmī kālo’ (the coming time). With the ‘ghiṇa’ suffix, by ‘kvaci dhātū’ etc., there is elision of ‘gh’, resulting in forms like ‘gāmaṃ gāmi,’ ‘gāmī,’ ‘gāmayo’.

Bhaja sevāyaṃ, āyati bhajituṃ sīlamassāti bhājī, bhāji, “na kagattaṃ cajā”ti yogavibhāgena nisedhanato “sacajānaṃ kagā ṇānubandhe”ti gattaṃ na bhavati.

The root ‘bhaja’ in the sense of serving: in the sense of ‘one whose nature is to serve in the future,’ the forms are ‘bhājī,’ ‘bhāji’. Due to the prohibition by splitting the rule `na kagattaṃ cajā`, the change to ‘ga’ prescribed by the rule ‘sacajānaṃ kagā ṇānubandhe’ does not occur.

Su gatimhi, kārite vuddhiāvādesā ca, āyati passavituṃ sīlamassāti passāvī, passāvi. Āyati paṭṭhānaṃ sīlamassāti paṭṭhāyī, paṭṭhāyi, “ākārantānamāyo”ti āyādeso.

The root ‘su’ in the sense of going: in the causative, there is vowel gradation (`vuddhi`) and the substitution of ‘āv’. In the sense of ‘one whose nature is to flow in the future,’ the forms are ‘passāvī,’ ‘passāvi’. In the sense of ‘one whose nature is to establish in the future,’ the forms are ‘paṭṭhāyī,’ ‘paṭṭhāyi’; by the rule ‘ākārantānamāyo’, there is the substitution of ‘āy’.

“Bhavissatī”ti adhikāro.

‘Bhavissati’ (in the future tense) is the governing rule.

648. Kiriyāyaṃ [M 0.0402] ṇvutavo.

648. In the sense of action, the suffixes are ‘ṇvu’ and ‘tu’.

Kiriyāyaṃ kiriyatthāyaṃ gammamānāyaṃ dhātūhi ṇvutuiccete paccayā honti bhavissati kāle. Ṇvumhi – ṇalopavuddhiakādesā, karissaṃ vajatīti kārako vajati.

When an action is understood for the purpose of another action, these suffixes ‘ṇvu’ and ‘tu’ occur after roots in the future tense. With ‘ṇvu’, there is elision of ‘ṇ’, vowel gradation (`vuddhi`), and substitution of ‘aka’. For example, ‘karissaṃ vajati’ (he goes in order to do) becomes ‘kārako vajati’ (the doer goes).

Tumhi – “karassa ca tattaṃ tusmi”nti takāro, sesaṃ kattusamaṃ, kattā vajati, kattuṃ vajatīti attho. Evaṃ pacissaṃ vajatīti pācako vajati, pacitā vajati. Bhuñjissaṃ vajatīti bhuñjako vajati, bhottā vajati iccādi.

With the suffix ‘tu’: by the rule ‘karassa ca tattaṃ tusmi’, the root ‘kara’ becomes ‘kat’. The rest is declined like ‘kattu’. ‘Kattā vajati’ has the meaning ‘kattuṃ vajati’ (he goes to do). Similarly, ‘pacissaṃ vajati’ (he goes to cook) becomes ‘pācako vajati’ or ‘pacitā vajati’. ‘Bhuñjissaṃ vajati’ (he goes to eat) becomes ‘bhuñjako vajati’ or ‘bhottā vajati,’ etc.

649. Kammani ṇo.

649. When an object is a preceding word, the suffix is ‘ṇa’.

Kammasmiṃ upapade dhātūhi ṇappaccayo hoti bhavissati kāle ṇalopavuddhī. Nagaraṃ karissatīti nagarakāro vajati. Lū chedane, sāliṃ lavissatīti sālilāvo vajati. Vapa bījasantāne, dhaññaṃ vapissatīti dhaññavāpo vajati. Bhogaṃ dadissatīti bhogadāyo vajati, sindhuṃ pivissatīti sindhupāyo vajati iccādi.

When the object is a preceding word, the suffix ‘ṇa’ occurs after roots in the future tense, with elision of ‘ṇ’ and vowel gradation (`vuddhi`). For example, ‘Nagaraṃ karissati’ (he will make a city) becomes ‘nagarakāro vajati’ (the city-maker goes). The root ‘lū’ in the sense of cutting: ‘sāliṃ lavissati’ (he will cut rice) becomes ‘sālilāvo vajati’ (the rice-cutter goes). The root ‘vapa’ in the sense of sowing seeds: ‘dhaññaṃ vapissati’ (he will sow grain) becomes ‘dhaññavāpo vajati’ (the grain-sower goes). ‘Bhogaṃ dadissati’ (he will give wealth) becomes ‘bhogadāyo vajati’ (the wealth-giver goes). ‘Sindhuṃ pivissati’ (he will drink the river) becomes ‘sindhupāyo vajati,’ etc.

“Kammanī”ti vattate.

The rule ‘Kammani’ continues.

650. Sese ssaṃ ntu mānānā.

650. In the remaining cases, the suffixes are ‘ssaṃ,’ ‘ntu,’ ‘māna,’ and ‘āna’.

Kammasmiṃ upapade sese aparisamattatthe dhātūhi ssaṃntu māna ānaiccete paccayā honti bhavissati kāle gammamāne, te ca kitakattā kattari bhavanti. Kammaṃ karissatīti atthe ssaṃpaccayo, ikārāgamo, silopo, kammaṃ karissaṃ vajati, sāpekkhattā na samāso. Ntupaccaye “tanādito oyirā”ti o, “simhi vā”ti ntva’ntassa attaṃ, kammaṃ karissatīti kammaṃ karonto vajati iccādi guṇavantusamaṃ.

When the object is a preceding word, in the remaining cases, in the sense of an incomplete action, these suffixes ‘ssaṃ,’ ‘ntu,’ ‘māna,’ and ‘āna’ occur after roots when the future tense is understood. And they, being primary suffixes (`kitaka`), occur in the active voice (`kattari`). In the sense of ‘he will do the action,’ the suffix ‘ssaṃ’ is applied, with the augment ‘i’ and elision of ‘si’. For example, ‘kammaṃ karissaṃ vajati’ (he goes to do the work); because it is dependent, it is not compounded. With the ‘ntu’ suffix, by ‘tanādito oyirā,’ the infix ‘o’ is applied; by ‘simhi vā,’ the ending of the stem in `-ntu` becomes `-o`. ‘Kammaṃ karissati’ becomes ‘kammaṃ karonto vajati’ (doing the work, he goes), etc., declined like ‘guṇavantu’.

Atha [M 0.0403] vā “bhavissati gamādīhi ṇī ghiṇa”ti ettha “bhavissatī”ti vacanato “ssantu”iti ekova paccayo daṭṭhabbo, tato “simhi vā”ti attaṃ, “ntasaddo a”mitiyogavibhāgena amādeso, silopo, karissaṃ karissanto, karissantā, karissantaṃ, karissante, karissatā karissantena, karissantehi, karissato karissantassa, karissataṃ karissantānaṃ, karissatā, karissantehi, karissato karissantassa, karissataṃ karissantānaṃ, karissati karissante, karissantesūtiādi guṇavantusadisaṃ neyyaṃ.

Alternatively, in the rule ‘bhavissati gamādīhi ṇī ghiṇa,’ from the word ‘bhavissati’ itself, ‘ssantu’ should be understood as a single suffix. Then, by ‘simhi vā,’ the nominative singular ending is formed. By splitting the rule ‘ntasaddo aṃ’, there is the substitution of ‘aṃ’, and elision of ‘si’, resulting in ‘karissaṃ’. The declension, similar to ‘guṇavantu’, should be understood as: ‘karissanto,’ ‘karissantā,’ ‘karissantaṃ,’ ‘karissante,’ ‘karissatā/karissantena,’ ‘karissantehi,’ ‘karissato/karissantassa,’ ‘karissataṃ/karissantānaṃ,’ ‘karissatā,’ ‘karissantehi,’ ‘karissato/karissantassa,’ ‘karissataṃ/karissantānaṃ,’ ‘karissati/karissante,’ ‘karissantesu,’ etc.

Mānamhi – okārākārānaṃ uttaṃ, kammaṃ karissatīti kammaṃ kurumāno, kammaṃ karāno vajati. Evaṃ bhojanaṃ bhuñjissaṃ vajati, bhojanaṃ bhuñjanto, bhuñjamāno, bhuñjāno vajati.

With the ‘māna’ suffix: the vowels ‘o’ and ‘a’ of the root are changed to ‘u’. ‘Kammaṃ karissati’ (he will do the work) becomes ‘kammaṃ kurumāno vajati’ or ‘kammaṃ karāno vajati’. Similarly, ‘bhojanaṃ bhuñjissaṃ vajati’ (he goes to eat food) becomes ‘bhojanaṃ bhuñjanto vajati,’ ‘bhojanaṃ bhuñjamāno vajati,’ or ‘bhojanaṃ bhuñjāno vajati’.

Sabbattha kattari ntumānesu sakasakavikaraṇappaccayo kātabbo.

Everywhere in the active voice, with the suffixes ‘ntu’ and ‘māna’, their respective conjugational signs (`vikaraṇappaccayo`) should be applied.

Khādanaṃ khādissatīti khādanaṃ khādissaṃ vajati, khādanaṃ khādanto, khādanaṃ khādamāno, khādanaṃ khādāno vajati. Maggaṃ carissatīti maggaṃ carissaṃ, maggaṃ caranto, maggaṃ caramāno, maggaṃ carāno vajati. Bhikkha āyācane, bhikkhaṃ bhikkhissatīti bhikkhaṃ bhikkhissaṃ carati, bhikkhaṃ bhikkhanto, bhikkhaṃ bhikkhamāno, bhikkhaṃ bhikkhāno carati iccādi.

‘Khādanaṃ khādissati’ (he will eat food) becomes ‘khādanaṃ khādissaṃ vajati,’ ‘khādanaṃ khādanto vajati,’ ‘khādanaṃ khādamāno vajati,’ or ‘khādanaṃ khādāno vajati’. ‘Maggaṃ carissati’ (he will walk the path) becomes ‘maggaṃ carissaṃ vajati,’ ‘maggaṃ caranto vajati,’ ‘maggaṃ caramāno vajati,’ or ‘maggaṃ carāno vajati’. The root ‘bhikkha’ in the sense of begging: ‘bhikkhaṃ bhikkhissati’ (he will beg for alms) becomes ‘bhikkhaṃ bhikkhissaṃ carati,’ ‘bhikkhaṃ bhikkhanto carati,’ ‘bhikkhaṃ bhikkhamāno carati,’ or ‘bhikkhaṃ bhikkhāno carati,’ etc.

Anāgatakālikappaccayantanayo.

End of the section on words ending in suffixes for the future tense.

Uṇādippaccayantanaya

The section on words ending in Uṇādi suffixes.

Atha uṇādayo vuccante.

Now, the Uṇādi suffixes are explained.

“Dhātuyā”ti adhikāro.

‘Dhātuyā’ (from a root) is the governing rule.

651. [M 0.0404] Kāle vattamānātīte ṇvādayo.

651. In the present and past tenses, the `ṇvu`-ādi suffixes apply.

Atīte kāle, vattamāne ca gammamāne dhātūhi ṇuppaccayo hoti. Ādisaddena yu kta miiccādayo ca honti.

When the past tense, and also the present, is understood, the suffix ‘ṇu’ occurs after roots. And by the word ‘ādi’ in the previous rule, suffixes such as ‘yu,’ ‘kta,’ ‘mi,’ etc., also occur.

Kara karaṇe, akāsi, karotīti vā atthe ṇuppaccayo, ṇalopo, vuddhi, kāru sippī, kārū kāravo. Vā gatigandhanesu, avāyi, vāyatīti vā vāyu, āyādeso. Sada assādane, assādīyatīti sādu. Rādha, sādha saṃsiddhimhi, sādhīyati anena hitanti sādhu. Bandha bandhane, attani paraṃ bandhatīti bandhu. Cakkha viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, cakkhatīti cakkhu. I gatimhi, enti gacchanti pavattanti sattā etenāti āyu. Dara vidāraṇe, darīyatīti dāru kaṭṭhaṃ. Sanu dāne. Sanotīti sānu pabbatekadeso. Janīyatīti jānu jaṅghāsandhi. Carīyatīti cāru dassanīyo. Raha cāge, rahīyatīti rāhu asurindo. Tara taraṇe, tālu, lo rassa.

The root ‘kara’ in the sense of doing: in the meaning of ‘akāsi’ (he did) or ‘karoti’ (he does), the suffix ‘ṇu’ is applied, with elision of ‘ṇ’ and vowel gradation, resulting in ‘kāru’ (a craftsman), plural ‘kārū’ or ‘kāravo’. The root ‘vā’ in the sense of going and smelling: from ‘avāyi’ (it blew) or ‘vāyati’ (it blows) comes ‘vāyu’ (wind), with the substitution of ‘āya’. The root ‘sada’ in the sense of savoring: from ‘assādīyati’ (it is savored) comes ‘sādu’ (tasty). The roots ‘rādha’ and ‘sādha’ in the sense of accomplishment: from ‘sādhīyati anena hitanti’ (by this, benefit is accomplished) comes ‘sādhu’ (good). The root ‘bandha’ in the sense of binding: from ‘attani paraṃ bandhatīti’ (one who binds another to oneself) comes ‘bandhu’ (a relative). The root ‘cakkha’ in the sense of clear expression of speech: from ‘cakkhati’ (he expresses) comes ‘cakkhu’ (the eye). The root ‘i’ in the sense of going: from ‘enti gacchanti pavattanti sattā etena’ (beings go, move, and continue by this) comes ‘āyu’ (life-span). The root ‘dara’ in the sense of splitting: from ‘darīyati’ (it is split) comes ‘dāru’ (wood). The root ‘sanu’ in the sense of giving: from ‘sanoti’ (he gives) comes ‘sānu’ (a mountain slope). From ‘janīyati’ (it is produced) comes ‘jānu’ (the knee, the joint of the lower leg). From ‘carīyati’ (it is frequented) comes ‘cāru’ (lovely, pleasing to see). The root ‘raha’ in the sense of abandoning: from ‘rahīyati’ (it is abandoned) comes ‘rāhu’ (Rāhu, the lord of the asuras). The root ‘tara’ in the sense of crossing: gives ‘tālu’ (palate), with ‘l’ substituting for ‘r’.

Marādīnaṃ panettha ṇumhi “ghaṭādīnaṃ vā”ti ettha vāsaddena na vuddhi, maru, taru, tanu, dhanu, hanu, manu, asu, vasu, vaṭu, garu iccādi.

Here, for roots such as 'mara', when the ṇu affix is applied, by the word 'vā' in the rule 'ghaṭādīnaṃ vā', there is no vuddhi-strengthening, as in 'maru' (wind), 'taru' (tree), 'tanu' (slender), 'dhanu' (bow), 'hanu' (jaw), 'manu' (man), 'asu' (life), 'vasu' (wealth), 'vaṭu' (student), 'garu' (heavy), etc.

Cadi hilādane, yuppaccayo, “nudādīhi yuṇvūnamanānanākānanakā sakāritehi cā”ti anādeso, niggahītāgamo ca, candanaṃ. Bhavati etthāti bhuvanaṃ, “jhalānamiyuvāsare vā”ti uvādeso. Kira vikkhepe, kiraṇo. Vicakkhaṇo, kampanaṃ karotīti karuṇā, akārassuttaṃ.

For 'cadi' in the sense of 'rejoicing', the yu affix is applied. By the rule 'nudādīhi yuṇvūnamanānanākānanakā sakāritehi cā', there is the substitution of 'ana' and the insertion of a nasal, resulting in 'candanaṃ' (sandalwood). 'Bhavati etthāti' (it exists here), thus 'bhuvanaṃ' (world). By the rule 'jhalānamiyuvāsare vā', there is the substitution of 'uva'. For 'kira' in the sense of 'scattering', 'kiraṇo' (ray). 'Vicakkhaṇo' (wise). 'Kampanaṃ karotīti' (it causes trembling), thus 'karuṇā' (compassion); the vowel 'a' becomes 'u'.

Ktappaccaye [M 0.0405] – kalopo, abhavi, bhavatīti vā bhūtaṃ yakkhādi, bhūtāni. Vāyatīti vāto, tāyatīti tāto. Mimhi – bhavanti etthāti bhūmi, netīti nemi iccādi.

With the kta affix: there is elision of 'ka'. 'Abhavi' (it was), or 'bhavatīti' (it becomes), thus 'bhūtaṃ' (a being, such as a yakkha, etc.), 'bhūtāni' (beings). 'Vāyatīti' (it blows), thus 'vāto' (wind). 'Tāyatīti' (it protects), thus 'tāto' (father). With the mi affix: 'bhavanti etthāti' (they exist here), thus 'bhūmi' (earth). 'Netīti' (it leads), thus 'nemi' (rim), etc.

652. Khyādīhi mana ma ca to vā.

652. From roots such as 'khyā', the affix 'mana' is applied, and its 'ma' optionally becomes 'ta'.

Khī bhī su ru hu vā dhū hi lūpī adaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi manapaccayo hoti, massa ca to hoti vā.

From roots such as khī, bhī, su, ru, hu, vā, dhū, hi, lū, pī, ada, etc., the affix 'mana' is applied, and its 'ma' optionally becomes 'ta'.

Adadhātuparasseva, makārassa takāratā;

Tadaññato na hotāyaṃ, vavatthitavibhāsato.

Only after the root 'ada' does the 'ma' become 'ta'. This does not occur after other roots, due to restricted optionality.

Khī khaye, khīyanti ettha upaddavupasaggādayoti atthe manapaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā nalopo, “aññesu cā”ti vuddhi, khemo. Tathā bhī bhaye, bhāyanti etasmāti bhīmo, vādhikārato na vuddhi. Su abhisave, savatīti somo. Ru gatimhi, romo. Hu dānādanahabyappadānesu, hūyatīti homo. Vā gatigandhanesu, vāmo. Dhū kampane, dhunātīti dhūmo. Hi gatimhi, hinotīti hemo. Lū chedane, lūyatīti lomo. Pī tappane, pīṇanaṃ pemo. Ada bhakkhaṇe, adatīti atthe mana, massa ca vā takāro, “to dassā”ti takāro, attā, ātumā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā adassa dīgho, ukārāgamo ca. Yā pāpaṇe, yāmo.

For 'khī' in the sense of 'destruction', in the meaning 'afflictions and dangers are destroyed here', the 'mana' affix is applied. By the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., there is elision of 'na', and by 'aññesu cā', there is vuddhi-strengthening, resulting in 'khemo' (safe). Similarly, for 'bhī' in the sense of 'fear', 'bhāyanti etasmāti' (they fear from this), thus 'bhīmo' (terrible). Due to the governing rule of 'vā', there is no vuddhi-strengthening. For 'su' in the sense of 'pressing out', 'savati' (it flows), thus 'somo' (Soma). For 'ru' in the sense of 'going', 'romo' (hair). For 'hu' in the sense of 'giving, taking, offering oblations', 'hūyati' (it is offered), thus 'homo' (oblation). For 'vā' in the sense of 'going' and 'smelling', 'vāmo' (left/beautiful). For 'dhū' in the sense of 'shaking', 'dhunāti' (it shakes), thus 'dhūmo' (smoke). For 'hi' in the sense of 'going', 'hinoti' (it goes), thus 'hemo' (winter/gold). For 'lū' in the sense of 'cutting', 'lūyati' (it is cut), thus 'lomo' (hair). For 'pī' in the sense of 'satisfying', 'pīṇanaṃ' (satisfaction), thus 'pemo' (love). For 'ada' in the sense of 'eating', in the meaning 'he eats', the 'mana' affix is applied, and its 'ma' optionally becomes 'ta'. By the rule 'to dassā', the 'd' becomes 't', resulting in 'attā' (self) and 'ātumā' (self). By the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., the 'a' of 'ada' is lengthened, and 'u' is inserted. For 'yā' in the sense of 'obtaining', 'yāmo' (watch of the night).

“Vā”ti vattamāne –

When 'vā' is current—

653. Samādihi thamā.

653. From roots such as 'sam', the affixes 'tha' and 'ma' occur.

Samadamadara raha lapa vasa yu du hi si dā sā ṭhā bhasa bahausuiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tha maiccete paccayā honti vā.

The affixes 'tha' and 'ma' optionally occur after roots such as sam, dam, dara, raha, lapa, vasa, yu, du, hi, si, dā, sā, ṭhā, bhasa, baha, usu, etc.

Sama [M 0.0406] upasame, kvaciggahaṇādhikārā na dhātvantalopo, kilese sametīti samatho samādhi. Evaṃ damanaṃ damatho. Dara dāhe, daraṇaṃ daratho paridāho. Raha upādāne, rahīyatīti ratho, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā halopo. Sapa akkose, sapanaṃ sapatho. Vasa nivāse, āvasanti etasminti āvasatho. Yu missane, yūtho, dīgho. Du gativuddhimhi, davati vaḍḍhatīti dumo. Hinotīti himo ussāvo. Si bandhane, sīyatīti sīmā, dīgho. Dā avakhaṇḍane, dāmo. Sā sāmatthe, sāmo. Ṭhā gatinivattimhi, thāmo, ṭhassa thattaṃ. Bhasa bhasmīkaraṇe, bhasmā, brahmādittā “syā cā”ti āttaṃ. Baha vuddhimhi, brahmā, nipātanato bro bassa. Usu dāhe, usmā iccādi.

For 'sama' in the sense of 'calming', due to the governing rule of 'kvaciggahaṇa' (taking 'sometimes'), there is no elision of the root-final vowel. 'Kilese sametīti' (it calms defilements), thus 'samatho' (tranquility), which is 'samādhi' (concentration). Similarly, 'damana' (taming) is 'damatho' (restraint). For 'dara' in the sense of 'burning', 'daraṇaṃ' (burning) is 'daratho' (anguish), torment. For 'raha' in the sense of 'taking', 'rahīyatīti' (it is taken), thus 'ratho' (chariot); by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc., there is elision of 'ha'. For 'sapa' in the sense of 'cursing', 'sapanaṃ' (cursing) is 'sapatho' (oath). For 'vasa' in the sense of 'dwelling', 'āvasanti etasmin' (they dwell in this), thus 'āvasatho' (lodging). For 'yu' in the sense of 'mixing', 'yūtho' (herd), with lengthening. For 'du' in the sense of 'going' and 'increasing', 'davati vaḍḍhatīti' (it goes, it increases), thus 'dumo' (tree). 'Hinotīti' (it goes), thus 'himo' (cold), dew. For 'si' in the sense of 'binding', 'sīyatīti' (it is bound), thus 'sīmā' (boundary), with lengthening. For 'dā' in the sense of 'cutting', 'dāmo' (bond). For 'sā' in the sense of 'ability', 'sāmo' (strength). For 'ṭhā' in the sense of 'standing' and 'ceasing', 'thāmo' (strength), with 'ṭh' becoming 'th'. For 'bhasa' in the sense of 'reducing to ashes', 'bhasmā' (ashes); due to being in the brahma-group, 'ā' is added by 'syā ca'. For 'baha' in the sense of 'increasing', 'brahmā' (Brahma); by irregular formation, 'bro' of 'bassa' occurs. For 'usu' in the sense of 'burning', 'usmā' (heat), etc.

654. Masussa sussa ccha ra ccherā.

654. For 'masu', its 'su' becomes 'cchara' and 'cchera'.

Masuiccetassa dhātussa sussa ccharaccheraiccete ādesā honti. Masu macchere, kvippaccayo, ccharaccherādesā, maccharo, macchero.

For the root 'masu', its 'su' becomes 'cchara' and 'cchera'. For 'masu' in the sense of 'miserliness', the kvi affix is applied, and the substitutions 'cchara' and 'cchera' occur, resulting in 'maccharo' and 'macchero'.

“Cchara ccherā”ti vattate.

The rule 'cchara ccherā' is current.

655. Āpubbacarassa ca.

655. And for 'cara' preceded by 'ā'.

Āpubbassa caraiccetassa dhātussa ccharaccherādesā honti, casaddena cchariyādeso ca. Bhuso caraṇanti atthe kvippaccayo, cchariyādiādeso, rassattañca. Acchariyaṃ[M 0.0407], accharaṃ, accheraṃ. Accharaṃ paharituṃ yuttantipi acchariyaṃ.

For the root 'cara' preceded by 'ā', the substitutions 'cchara' and 'cchera' occur, and by the word 'ca', the substitution 'cchariya' also occurs. In the meaning 'bhuso caraṇaṃ' (frequent movement), the kvi affix is applied, the substitution 'cchariya', etc., occurs, and shortening. Thus, 'acchariyaṃ', 'accharaṃ', 'accheraṃ'. Also, 'acchariyaṃ' (wonder) is what is suitable for a finger-snap ('accharaṃ paharituṃ').

656. Ala kala salehi layā.

656. From 'ala', 'kala', and 'sala', the affixes 'la' and 'ya' occur.

Ala kala sala iccetehi dhātūhi la yaiccete paccayā honti. Ala parisamattimhi, allaṃ, alyaṃ. Kala saṅkhyāne, kallaṃ, kalyaṃ. Sala, hula, pada gatimhi, sallaṃ, salyaṃ.

From these roots 'ala', 'kala', and 'sala', the affixes 'la' and 'ya' occur. For 'ala' in the sense of 'completion', 'allaṃ' and 'alyaṃ' are formed. For 'kala' in the sense of 'counting', 'kallaṃ' and 'kalyaṃ' are formed. For 'sala', 'hula', and 'pada' in the sense of 'going', 'sallaṃ' and 'salyaṃ' are formed.

“Kala salehī”ti vattate.

The rule 'kala salehi' is current.

657. Yāṇa lāṇā.

657. The affixes 'yāṇa' and 'lāṇa'.

Tehi kala salaiccetehi dhātūhi yāṇa lāṇappaccayā honti. Kalyāṇaṃ, paṭisalyāṇaṃ, kallāṇo, paṭisallāṇo. Yadā pana lī silesaneti dhātu, tadā “paṭisallayanaṃ, paṭisallāṇa”nti yuppaccayena siddhaṃ, upasaggantassa niggahītassa lattaṃ, rahādiparattā nassa ṇattaṃ, ekārassa “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā attañca.

From those roots 'kala' and 'sala', the affixes 'yāṇa' and 'lāṇa' occur. Thus, 'kalyāṇaṃ', 'paṭisalyāṇaṃ', 'kallāṇo', 'paṭisallāṇo'. However, when the root is 'lī' in the sense of 'adhering', then 'paṭisallayanaṃ' and 'paṭisallāṇa' are formed by the yu affix, with the nasal at the end of the prefix becoming 'la', the 'na' becoming 'ṇa' due to being after 'ra' etc., and the 'e' vowel becoming 'a' by the rule 'kvaci dhātū' etc.

658. Mathissa thassa lo ca.

658. For 'matha', its 'tha' becomes 'la', and also 'la'.

Mathaiccetassa dhātussa thassa lādeso hoti, casaddena lappaccayo, matha viloḷane, mallo, so eva mallako, yathā hīnako.

For the root 'matha', its 'tha' is substituted by 'la', and by the word 'ca', the 'la' affix also occurs. For 'matha' in the sense of 'agitation', 'mallo' (wrestler) is formed, and that itself is 'mallako', just like 'hīnako'.

“Kiccā”ti vattate.

The rule 'kiccā' is current.

659. Avassakādhamiṇesu ṇī ca.

659. And in the meanings of 'necessary' and 'debtor', the affix 'ṇī' occurs.

Avassaka adhamiṇaiccetesvatthesu, ṇīpaccayo hoti, kiccā cāti ṇīpaccayo, ṇalopa vuddhisilopā, avassaṃ [M 0.0408] me kammaṃ kātuṃ yuttosīti kārīsi me kammaṃ avassaṃ, kārino me kammaṃ avassaṃ, hārīsi me bhāraṃ avassaṃ.

In the meanings of 'necessary' and 'debtor', the ṇī affix occurs, and the ṇī affix is a 'kicca' affix. There is elision of ṇa, vuddhi-strengthening, and elision of 'si'. In the meaning 'you are obliged to do my work', it becomes 'kārīsi me kammaṃ avassaṃ' (you are necessarily a doer of my work), 'kārino me kammaṃ avassaṃ' (you are necessarily a doer of my work), 'hārīsi me bhāraṃ avassaṃ' (you are necessarily a carrier of my burden).

Adhamiṇe – sataṃ me iṇaṃ dātuṃ yuttosīti dāyīsi me sataṃ iṇaṃ, dhārīsi me sahassaṃ iṇaṃ iccādi, kiccappaccayā pana heṭṭhāyeva dassitā.

In the meaning 'debtor': 'sataṃ me iṇaṃ dātuṃ yuttosīti' (you are obliged to give me the hundred owed), thus 'dāyīsi me sataṃ iṇaṃ' (you are a giver of a hundred owed to me), 'dhārīsi me sahassaṃ iṇaṃ' (you are a holder of a thousand owed to me), etc. The kicca affixes, however, have already been shown below.

660. Vajādīhi pabbajjādayo nipaccante.

660. From roots such as 'vaja', words such as 'pabbajjā' are irregularly formed.

Ākatigaṇoyaṃ. Vajaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi paccayādesalopāgamanisedhaliṅgādividhinā yathābhidhānaṃ pabbajjādayo saddā nipaccante.

This is an open class of roots (ākatigaṇa). From roots such as 'vaja', words like 'pabbajjā' are irregularly formed by means of affixes, substitutions, elisions, augmentations, prohibitions, gender rules, and other methods, according to usage.

Vaja gatimhi papubbo, paṭhamameva vajitabbanti atthe “bhāvakammesū”ti adhikicca “ṇyocā”ti ṇyappaccayo, ṇalopādi. “Pavvajya”nti rūpe sampatte iminā jjhassa jjādeso, vakāradvayassa bakāradvayaṃ, vuddhinisedho, itthiliṅgattañca nipaccante, pabbajjā.

For 'vaja' in the sense of 'going', when preceded by 'pa'. In the meaning 'paṭhamameva vajitabbaṃ' (it is to be gone forth first), by the governing rule 'bhāvakammesu' and the rule 'ṇyocā', the ṇya affix occurs, with elision of ṇa, etc. When the form 'pavajya' is reached, by this rule, 'jjha' is substituted by 'jjā', the two 'va's become two 'ba's, vuddhi-strengthening is prohibited, and the feminine gender is irregularly formed, resulting in 'pabbajjā'.

Tathā iñja kampane, iñjanaṃ ijjā. Yaja devapūjāyaṃ, yajanaṃ ijjā, “yajassādissī”ti ittaṃ. Añja byattigatīsu saṃpubbo, samañjanaṃ samajjā, ñjhassa jjādeso. Sada visaraṇagatyāvasānesu, nisīdanaṃ nisajjā. Vida ñāṇe, vijānanaṃ, vidatīti vā vijjā. Saja vissagge, vissajjanaṃ vissajjā. Pada gatimhi, nipajjanaṃ nipajjā.

Similarly, from the root 'iñja' in the sense of 'shaking', 'iñjanaṃ' becomes 'ijjā'. From the root 'yaja' in the sense of 'worship of deities', 'yajanaṃ' becomes 'ijjā'; the 'i' is by the rule 'yajassādissī'. From the root 'añja' in the senses of 'manifestation' and 'movement', when preceded by 'saṃ', 'samañjanaṃ' becomes 'samajjā', with 'ñjh' being substituted by 'jjā'. From the root 'sada' in the senses of 'scattering', 'movement', and 'cessation', 'nisīdanaṃ' becomes 'nisajjā'. From the root 'vida' in the sense of 'knowledge', 'vijānanaṃ' (knowing), or 'vidati' (it knows), becomes 'vijjā'. From the root 'saja' in the sense of 'release', 'vissajjanaṃ' becomes 'vissajjā'. From the root 'pada' in the sense of 'movement', 'nipajjanaṃ' becomes 'nipajjā'.

Hana hiṃsāgatīsu, hantabbanti atthe ṇyamhi kate “vadho vā sabbatthā”ti hanassa vadhādeso, jhassiminā jjhādeso ca, so vajjho, sā vajjhā. Sī saye, sayanaṃ, sayanti etthāti vā seyyā, vuddhi, yakārassa dvittañca[M 0.0409]. Dhā dhāraṇe saṃpubbo, sammā cittaṃ nidheti etāya, sayaṃ vā saddahatīti atthe “itthiyamatiyavo vā”ti appaccayo, “sandhā”ti rūpe sampatte iminā nakārassa dakāro, saddhā. Cara caraṇe, caraṇanti atthe ṇyappaccaye, ikārāgame ca kate iminā vuddhinisedho, cariyā.

From the root 'hana' in the senses of 'harming' and 'going'. When the ṇya affix is applied in the meaning 'is to be killed', then by the rule 'vadho vā sabbatthā', 'hana' is substituted by 'vadha', and by this rule, 'dhy' is substituted by 'jjh'. Thus, 'vajjho' (he who is to be killed) and 'vajjhā' (she who is to be killed). From the root 'sī' in the sense of 'lying down', 'sayanaṃ' (lying down), or 'sayanti ettha' (they lie down here), becomes 'seyyā' (bed), with vuddhi and doubling of 'ya'. From the root 'dhā' in the sense of 'holding', when preceded by 'saṃ'. In the meaning 'by this, one places the mind well', or 'one believes by oneself', by the rule 'itthiyamatiyavo vā', the 'a' affix occurs. When the form 'sandhā' is reached, by this rule, 'na' becomes 'da', resulting in 'saddhā' (faith). From the root 'cara' in the sense of 'walking'. When the ṇya affix and the 'i' augment are applied in the meaning 'walking', by this rule, vuddhi is prohibited, resulting in 'cariyā' (conduct).

Ruja roge, rujananti atthe iminā chappaccayo, “byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu cā”ti dhātvantassa cakāro, rucchā, rujāti appaccayena siddhaṃ. Tathā kuca saṅkocane, chappaccayo, kocanaṃ kucchā. Labha lābhe, chamhi cādeso, lacchā. Rada vilekhane, racchā. Muha vecitte, muyhanaṃ mucchā, mucchanaṃ vā mucchā. Vasa nivāse, vacchā. Kaca dittimhi, kacchā. Katha kathane saṃpubbo, saddhiṃ kathananti atthe ṇyappaccayo, iminā thyassa cchādeso, saṃsaddassa sādeso ca, sākacchā. Tuda byathane, tucchā. Pada gatimhi, byāpajjananti atthe ṇyamhi kate “byāpādyā”ti rūpe sampatte iminā nipātanena dyassa jjādeso, rassattañca, byāpajjā.

From the root 'ruja' in the sense of 'disease', in the meaning 'they injure', by this rule the 'cha' suffix is applied. By the rule 'byañjanantassa co chappaccayesu cā', the final consonant of the root becomes 'ca', resulting in 'rucchā'. 'Rujā' is formed with the 'a' suffix. Similarly, from 'kuca' in the sense of 'shrinking', the 'cha' suffix is applied; 'kocanaṃ' becomes 'kucchā'. From 'labha' in the sense of 'gaining', when 'cha' follows, 'c' is the substitute for the final consonant, resulting in 'lacchā'. From 'rada' in the sense of 'scraping', 'racchā'. From 'muha' in the sense of 'confusion', 'muyhanaṃ' or 'mucchanaṃ' becomes 'mucchā'. From 'vasa' in the sense of 'dwelling', 'vacchā'. From 'kaca' in the sense of 'shining', 'kacchā'. From 'katha' in the sense of 'speaking', when preceded by 'saṃ', in the meaning 'speaking together', the 'ṇya' affix is applied; by this rule, 'thy' is substituted by 'cch', and 'saṃ' is substituted by 'sā', resulting in 'sākacchā'. From 'tuda' in the sense of 'hurting', 'tucchā'. From 'pada' in the sense of 'movement', in the meaning 'destroying', when the 'ṇya' affix is applied, and when the form 'byāpādyā' is reached, by this irregular formation, 'dy' is substituted by 'jjā', and there is shortening, resulting in 'byāpajjā'.

Mara pāṇacāge, marati maraṇanti ca atthe iminā tyatyuppaccayā, dhātvantalopoca, tato “yavata”miccādinā cakāro, macco, maccu. Sata sātacce, iminā yappaccayo, tyassa cakāro, saccaṃ. Tathā nata gattavināme, naccaṃ. Niti nicce, niccaṃ. Mā māne, māyā. Jana janane, jāyā, kana dittikantīsu, nyassa ñattaṃ, dvittañca, kaññā. Dhana dhaññe, dhaññaṃ. Punātīti puññaṃ, nakārāgamo iccādi.

From the root 'mara' in the sense of 'abandoning life', and in the meanings 'he dies' or 'death', by this rule the suffixes 'tya' and 'tyu' are applied, and there is elision of the final of the root; then, by the rule 'yavata...' etc., 'ty' is substituted by 'c', resulting in 'macco' and 'maccu'. From 'sata' in the sense of 'continuity', by this rule the 'ya' suffix is applied, and 'ty' becomes 'c', resulting in 'saccaṃ'. Similarly, from 'nata' in the sense of 'bending the limbs', 'naccaṃ'. From 'niti' in the sense of 'constant', 'niccaṃ'. From 'mā' in the sense of 'measuring', 'māyā'. From 'jana' in the sense of 'generating', 'jāyā'. From 'kana' in the senses of 'shining' and 'beauty', 'ny' is substituted by 'ññ', resulting in 'kaññā'. From 'dhana' in the sense of 'grain', 'dhaññaṃ'. 'That which purifies' is 'puññaṃ', with the augment 'na', etc.

661. Ve [M 0.0410] pu sī davava mu ku dā bhūhvādīhi thuttima ṇimā nibbatte.

661. From the roots ve, pu, sī, dava, vamu, ku, dā, bhū, and those beginning with hvā, the suffixes thu, tti, ma, ṇi, and mā are applied in the sense of 'produced from'.

Vepusīdavavamuiccevamādīhi dhātūhi, ku dā bhūādito, hvādito ca yathākkamaṃ thuttimaṇimaiccete paccayā honti nibbattatthe. Vepu kampane, thuppaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā akārāgamo, atha vā “athū”ti vattabbe saralopaṃ katvā “thū”ti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ, vepena nibbatto vepathu. Sī saye, sayanena nibbatto sayathu. Dava davane, davena nibbatto davathu. Vamu uggiraṇe, vamena nibbatto vamathu.

From roots such as vepu, sī, dava, vamu, etc., and from ku, dā, bhū, etc., and hvā, etc., the suffixes thu, tti, ma, ṇi, and mā occur in order, in the sense of 'produced from'. From the root 'vepu' in the sense of 'trembling'; the 'thu' suffix is applied. By the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., there is the augment 'a', or alternatively, it should be understood that 'thu' is stated after eliding the vowel when 'athu' should have been said. 'Vepathu' is that which is produced from trembling. From 'sī' in the sense of 'lying down'; 'sayathu' is that which is produced from lying down. From 'dava' in the sense of 'running'; 'davathu' is that which is produced from running. From 'vamu' in the sense of 'vomiting'; 'vamathu' is that which is produced from vomiting.

Kutti karaṇaṃ, tena nibbattaṃ kuttimaṃ, “ku”iti nipātanato karassa kuttaṃ. Dā dāne, dāti dānaṃ, tena nibbattaṃ dattimaṃ, rassattaṃ. Bhūti bhavanaṃ, tena nibbattaṃ bhottimaṃ. Avahuti avahanaṃ, tena nibbattaṃ ohāvimaṃ, ṇalopavuddhiāvādesā.

'Kutti' is 'making'; 'produced from that' is 'kuttimaṃ'. From the irregular formation of 'ku', 'kara' becomes 'kutta'. From 'dā' in the sense of 'giving'; 'dāti' is 'giving'; 'produced from that' is 'dattimaṃ', with shortening. 'Bhūti' is 'being'; 'produced from that' is 'bhottimaṃ'. 'Avahuti' is 'carrying away'; 'produced from that' is 'ohāvimaṃ', with elision of 'ṇ', vuddhi, and the substitution of 'av'.

662. Akkose namhāni.

662. In the sense of reviling, the suffix 'āni' is applied when the particle 'naṃ' is present.

Akkose gammamāne namhi nipāte upapade sati dhātuto ānippaccayo hoti. Na gamitabbo te jamma desoti atthe ānippaccayo, kitakattā nāmamiva katvā simhi kate na gamānīti atthe kammadhārayasamāso, nassa attaṃ, puna samāsattā nāmamiva kate syādyuppatti, agamāni te jamma deso. Na kattabbaṃ te jamma kammanti akarāni te jamma kammaṃ.

When reviling is understood, and when the particle 'naṃ' is present as a pre-verb, the suffix 'āni' is applied to the root. The suffix 'āni' is used in the sense of 'That wretched land should not be gone to by you'. Because it is a primary derivative, it is treated like a noun, and when the 'si' case ending is applied, it forms a kammadhāraya compound in the sense of 'not to be gone to'. 'Na' becomes 'a'. Again, because it is a compound, it is treated like a noun, and case endings etc. are produced, resulting in 'agamāni te jamma deso' (that wretched land is not to be gone to by you). 'That wretched deed should not be done by you' becomes 'akarāni te jamma kammaṃ' (that wretched deed is not to be done by you).

Namhīti kiṃ? Vipatti te. Akkoseti kiṃ? Agati te.

Why is 'namhi' stated? For the counter-example: 'Vipatti te' (Ruin to you). Why is 'akkose' stated? For the counter-example: 'Agati te' (No-going for you).

663. Sunassunassoṇavānuvānununakhuṇānā[M 0.0411].

663. For the stem 'suna', its part 'una' is substituted by 'oṇa', 'vāna', 'uvāna', 'una', 'unakha', 'uṇa', 'ā', and 'āna'.

Sunaiccetassa pāṭipadikassa sambandhino unasaddassa oṇa vāna uvāna una unakha uṇa ā ānaiccete ādesā honti. Sunassunassa oṇādiādese, paranayane ca kate syādyuppatti, soṇo, soṇā, svāno, svānā, suvāno, suvānā, suno, sunā, sunakho, sunakhā, suṇo, suṇā, sā sāno, sānā iccādi.

For the nominal stem 'suna', for its related part 'una', these substitutes occur: 'oṇa', 'vāna', 'uvāna', 'una', 'unakha', 'uṇa', 'ā', and 'āna'. When the substitutes 'oṇa' etc. are applied to the 'una' of 'suna', and after assimilation is done, case endings etc. are produced, resulting in forms such as: soṇo, soṇā, svāno, svānā, suvāno, suvānā, suno, sunā, sunakho, sunakhā, suṇo, suṇā, sā, sāno, sānā, etc.

664. Taruṇassa susu ca.

664. For 'taruṇa', 'susu' is the substitute, and this is optional.

Taruṇaiccetassa saddassa susuiccādeso hoti. Casaddo aniyamattho, susu, taruṇo vā.

For the word 'taruṇa', the substitute 'susu' occurs. The word 'ca' has the meaning of optionality; thus, 'susu' or 'taruṇo'.

665. Yuvassuvassuvuvānunūnā.

665. For 'yuva', the substitutes for its part 'uva' are 'uva', 'uvāna', 'una', and 'ūna'.

Yuvaiccetassa pāṭipadikassa uvasaddassa uvauvānaunaūnaiccete ādesā honti. Yuvā tiṭṭhati, yuvāno tiṭṭhati, yuno tiṭṭhati, yūno tiṭṭhati.

For the nominal stem 'yuva', these substitutes occur for its part 'uva': 'uva', 'uvāna', 'una', and 'ūna'. Examples: Yuvā tiṭṭhati, yuvāno tiṭṭhati, yuno tiṭṭhati, yūno tiṭṭhati.

666. Chadādīhi tatraṇa.

666. From the roots 'chada' and so on, the suffixes 'tta', 'tra', and 'ṇa' are applied.

Chadaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi tatraṇaiccete paccayā honti. Chada apavāraṇe, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātvantassa takāro. Ātapaṃ chādetīti chattaṃ, chatraṃ, byañjanattaye sarūpānamekassa lopo.

From the roots 'chada' and so on, these suffixes occur: 'tta', 'tra', and 'ṇa'. From the root 'chada' in the sense of 'covering'; by the rule 'kvaci dhātu...' etc., the final of the root becomes 'ta'. 'It covers from the heat', therefore 'chattaṃ' or 'chatraṃ'. When there are three identical consonants, one is elided.

Cinta cintāyaṃ, cintetīti cittaṃ, nakārassa saṃyogādittā niggahītaṃ, tassa “byañjane cā”ti lopo, citraṃ, “ghaṭādīnaṃ vā”ti na vuddhi.

From the root 'cinta' in the sense of 'thinking'; 'it thinks', therefore 'cittaṃ'. The letter 'na', because it is at the beginning of a conjunct, becomes a niggahīta; of that, there is elision by the rule 'byañjane ca', resulting in 'citraṃ'. By the rule 'ghaṭādīnaṃ vā', there is no vuddhi.

Su [M 0.0412] abhisave, “paradvebhāvo ṭhāne”ti tassa dvittaṃ, atthe abhisavetīti suttaṃ, sutraṃ.

From the root 'su' in the sense of 'pressing out'; by the rule 'paradvebhāvo ṭhāne', there is doubling of that consonant. In the meaning 'it presses out', it is 'suttaṃ' or 'sutraṃ'.

Sūda paggharaṇe, atthe sūdetīti suttaṃ, rassattaṃ, bhujādittā dalopo, dvittañca. Su savane, suṇātīti sotaṃ, sotraṃ, vuddhi.

From the root 'sūda' in the sense of 'flowing'; in the meaning 'it flows', it is 'suttaṃ', with shortening, and because it belongs to the bhujādi group, there is elision of 'da' and doubling. From the root 'su' in the sense of 'hearing'; 'he hears', therefore 'sotaṃ' or 'sotraṃ', with vuddhi.

Ni pāpaṇe, netīti nettaṃ, netraṃ. Vida maṅgalle, to dassa, pavittaṃ, pavitraṃ. Pū pavane, punātīti pavittaṃ, pavitraṃ, ikārāgamo, vuddhiavādesā ca.

From the root 'ni' in the sense of 'leading'; 'it leads', therefore 'nettaṃ' or 'netraṃ'. From the root 'vida' in the sense of 'auspiciousness'; 't' is the substitute for 'd'; hence 'pavittaṃ' or 'pavitraṃ'. From the root 'pū' in the sense of 'purifying'; 'it purifies', therefore 'pavittaṃ' or 'pavitraṃ', with the augment 'i', and with vuddhi and the substitution of 'av'.

Pata gatimhi, patatīti pattaṃ, patraṃ, patato tāyatīti patto, patro. Tanu vitthāre, taññatīti tantaṃ, tantraṃ. Yata yatane, yattaṃ, yatraṃ. Yā pāpaṇe, yāpanā yatrā. Yamu uparame, yantaṃ, yantraṃ. Ada bhakkhaṇe, adatīti attaṃ, atraṃ. Yuja yoge, yujjatīti yottaṃ, yotraṃ, bhujādittā dhātvantalopadvittāni.

From the root 'pata' in the sense of 'going'; 'it falls', therefore 'pattaṃ' or 'patraṃ'. 'It protects from falling', therefore 'patto' or 'patro'. From 'tanu' in the sense of 'spreading'; 'it is stretched', therefore 'tantaṃ' or 'tantraṃ'. From 'yata' in the sense of 'striving', 'yattaṃ' or 'yatraṃ'. From 'yā' in the sense of 'reaching'; 'yāpanā' (maintenance) becomes 'yatrā'. From 'yamu' in the sense of 'restraining', 'yantaṃ' or 'yantraṃ'. From 'ada' in the sense of 'eating'; 'it eats', therefore 'attaṃ' or 'atraṃ'. From 'yuja' in the sense of 'joining'; 'it is joined', therefore 'yottaṃ' or 'yotraṃ', with elision of the final of the root and doubling because it belongs to the bhujādi group.

Vatu vattane, vattaṃ, vatraṃ. Mida sinehane, mijjatīti mittaṃ, mitraṃ. Mā parimāṇe, mattā parimāṇaṃ, dvittarassattāni. Evaṃ punātīti putto, putro. Kala saṅkhyāne, kalattaṃ, kalatraṃ bhariyā. Vara saṃvaraṇe, varattaṃ, varatraṃ cammamayayottaṃ. Vepu kampane, vepatīti vettaṃ, vetraṃ.

From the root 'vatu' in the sense of 'existing'; 'vattaṃ' or 'vatraṃ'. From 'mida' in the sense of 'affection'; 'it is affectionate', therefore 'mittaṃ' or 'mitraṃ'. From 'mā' in the sense of 'measuring'; 'mattā' is a measure, with doubling and shortening. Similarly, 'he purifies', therefore 'putto' or 'putro'. From 'kala' in the sense of 'counting'; 'kalattaṃ' or 'kalatraṃ' is a wife. From 'vara' in the sense of 'enclosing'; 'varattaṃ' or 'varatraṃ' is a leather strap. From 'vepu' in the sense of 'trembling'; 'it trembles', therefore 'vettaṃ' or 'vetraṃ'.

Gupa saṃvaraṇe, gottaṃ, gotraṃ, “gupādīnañcā”ti dhātvantalopo, dvittañca, gattaṃ vā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā ukārassa akāro. Dā avakhaṇḍane, dāttaṃ, dātraṃ. Hu havane, aggihuttaṃ. Vaha pāpaṇe, vahittaṃ, vahitraṃ. Cara caraṇe, carittaṃ, caritraṃ. Muca mocane, muttaṃ passāvo. Bhāsa dittimhi, bhastrā iccādi.

Gupa, in the sense of guarding or covering (saṃvaraṇe); it becomes gottaṃ or gotraṃ. By the rule 'gupādīnañcā,' there is elision of the root-final and doubling; or alternatively gattaṃ, with the change of 'u' to 'a' by 'kvaci dhātū,' etc. Dā, in the sense of cutting (avakhaṇḍane); it becomes dāttaṃ or dātraṃ. Hu, in the sense of offering (havane); it becomes aggihuttaṃ. Vaha, in the sense of carrying (pāpaṇe); it becomes vahittaṃ or vahitraṃ. Cara, in the sense of moving (caraṇe); it becomes carittaṃ or caritraṃ. Muca, in the sense of releasing (mocane); muttaṃ is urine (passāvo). Bhāsa, in the sense of shining (dittimhi); it becomes bhastrā, etc.

667. Vadādīhi [M 0.0413] ṇitto gaṇe.

667. From vada and so on, the suffix ṇitta is applied in the sense of a group.

Vada cara varaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi ṇittappaccayo hoti gaṇe gammamāne. Vada viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vaditānaṃ gaṇo vādittaṃ. Cara caraṇe, caritānaṃ gaṇo cārittaṃ. Vara varaṇe, varitānaṃ gaṇo vārittaṃ. Atha vā caranti tasmiṃ paripūrakāritāyāti cārittaṃ. Vāritaṃ tāyanti ettha, etenāti vā vārittaṃ.

From roots such as vada, cara, vara, etc., the suffix ṇitta is applied when a group is to be expressed. Vada, in the sense of distinct speech (viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ); a group of those who have spoken is vādittaṃ. Cara, in the sense of moving (caraṇe); a group of those who have moved is cārittaṃ. Vara, in the sense of choosing (varaṇe); a group of those who have chosen is vārittaṃ. Alternatively, cārittaṃ is so called because they move in it due to its fulfilling nature. Vārittaṃ is so called because they protect what is enclosed in it, or by it.

668. Midādīhi ttitiyo.

668. From mida and so on, the suffixes tti and ti are applied.

Mida pada ranja tanu dhāiccevamādīhi dhātūhi yathābhidhānaṃ tti tiiccete paccayā honti. Mijjati siniyhatīti metti, dhātvantalopo. Pajjatīti patti. Ranja rāge, ranjati etthāti ratti. Vitthārīyatīti tanti. Dhāretīti dhāti. Pā rakkhaṇe, pāti. Vasa nivāse, vasati.

From roots such as mida, pada, ranja, tanu, dhā, etc., the suffixes tti and ti occur according to their respective meanings. Because it is affectionate (mijjati siniyhati), it is metti, with elision of the root-final. Because it is attained (pajjati), it is patti. Ranja, in the sense of passion (rāge); because one is passionate in it (ranjati ettha), it is ratti. Because it is extended (vitthārīyati), it is tanti. Because it holds (dhāreti), it is dhāti. Pā, in the sense of protecting (rakkhaṇe); because it protects, it is pāti. Vasa, in the sense of dwelling (nivāse); because it dwells, it is vasati.

669. Usuranjadaṃsānaṃ daṃsassa daḍḍho ḍha ṭhā ca.

669. For usu, ranja, and daṃsa, daṃsa becomes daḍḍha, and the suffixes ḍha and ṭha are applied.

Usu ranja daṃsaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ antare daṃsassa daḍḍhādeso hoti, sesehi dhātūhi ḍha ṭhaiccete paccayā honti. Usu dāhe, ranja rāge, ḍha ṭhappaccayā, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātvantalopo, dvittaṃ, uḍḍho, raṭṭhaṃ. Daṃsa daṃsane, kvippaccayo, kvilopo, daṃsassa daḍḍhādeso ca, daḍḍhaṃ.

Among these roots—usu, ranja, and daṃsa—the substitute daḍḍha occurs for daṃsa, while the remaining roots take the suffixes ḍha and ṭha. Usu, in the sense of burning (dāhe), and ranja, in the sense of passion (rāge), take the suffixes ḍha and ṭha. By 'kvaci dhātū,' etc., there is elision of the root-final and doubling, resulting in uḍḍho and raṭṭhaṃ. Daṃsa, in the sense of biting (daṃsane), takes the suffix kvi; there is elision of kvi, and daṃsa becomes daḍḍha, hence daḍḍhaṃ.

670. Sūvusānamūvusānamato tho ca.

670. For sū, vu, and asa, their respective ū, u, and as become ata, and the suffix tha is applied.

Sū vu asaiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ ū u asānaṃ ataiccādeso hoti, ante thappaccayo ca.

For these roots—sū, vu, and asa—their ū, u, and as become the substitute ata, and the suffix tha is applied at the end.

Sū [M 0.0414] hiṃsāyaṃ, satthaṃ. Vu saṃvaraṇe, vatthaṃ. Asa bhuvi, attho. Yadā pana sasu hiṃsāyaṃ, vasa acchādane, ara gatimhīti ca dhātu, tadā “samādīhi tha mā”ti thappaccayo, “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā dhātvantalopo, “vagge ghosā”tiādinā dvittaṃ, sasatīti satthaṃ, vasīyatīti vatthaṃ, arīyatīti attho.

Sū, in the sense of harming (hiṃsāyaṃ), becomes satthaṃ. Vu, in the sense of covering (saṃvaraṇe), becomes vatthaṃ. Asa, in the sense of being (bhuvi), becomes attho. However, when the roots are sasu in the sense of harming (hiṃsāyaṃ), vasa in the sense of covering (acchādane), and ara in the sense of going (gatimhi), then the suffix tha is applied by 'samādīhi tha mā'; by 'kvaci dhātū,' etc., there is elision of the root-final; by 'vagge ghosā,' etc., there is doubling. Because it harms (sasati), it is satthaṃ; because it is covered (vasīyati), it is vatthaṃ; because it is gone to (arīyati), it is attho.

671. Ranjudādīhi dhadiddakirā kvaci ja da lopo ca.

671. From ranja, udi, and so on, the suffixes dha, da, idda, ka, and ira are sometimes applied, and there is elision of ja and da.

Ranja udiiccevamādīhi dhātūhi dha da idda ka iraiccete paccayā honti kvaci, dhātvantānaṃ jadānaṃ lopo ca hoti.

From roots such as ranja, udi, etc., the suffixes dha, da, idda, ka, and ira sometimes occur, and there is also elision of the final ja and da of the roots.

Ranja rāge, dhappaccayo, jalopo ca, randhaṃ. Udi pasavanakledanesu saṃpubbo, dappaccayo, samuddo, uddo. Khuda pipāsāyaṃ, khuddo. Chidi dvidhākaraṇe, chiddo. Rudi hiṃsāyaṃ, ruddo, luddo, lo rassa. Bhadi kalyāṇe, bhaddo. Nidi kucchāyaṃ, niddā. Muda hāse, muddā. Dala duggatimhi, iddappaccayo, daliddo.

Ranja, in the sense of passion (rāge); the suffix dha is applied, and there is elision of ja, hence randhaṃ. Udi, in the sense of flowing and moistening (pasavanakledanesu), when prefixed with saṃ; the suffix da is applied, hence samuddo and uddo. Khuda, in the sense of thirst (pipāsāyaṃ), becomes khuddo. Chidi, in the sense of splitting in two (dvidhākaraṇe), becomes chiddo. Rudi, in the sense of harming (hiṃsāyaṃ), becomes ruddo or luddo, with l for r. Bhadi, in the sense of auspiciousness (kalyāṇe), becomes bhaddo. Nidi, in the sense of contempt (kucchāyaṃ), becomes niddā. Muda, in the sense of laughter (hāse), becomes muddā. Dala, in the sense of misfortune (duggatimhi); the suffix idda is applied, hence daliddo.

Susa sosane, suca soke vā, kappaccayo, dhātvantassa kakāro, sukkaṃ. Vaca viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ, vaka ādāne vā, vakkaṃ. Saka sattimhi, sakko. Usu dāhe, ukkā.

Susa, in the sense of drying up (sosane), or suca in the sense of grieving (soke); with the suffix ka and the final of the root becoming ka, it is sukkaṃ. Vaca, in the sense of distinct speech (viyattiyaṃ vācāyaṃ), or vaka in the sense of taking (ādāne), it is vakkaṃ. Saka, in the sense of power (sattimhi), it is sakko. Usu, in the sense of burning (dāhe), it is ukkā.

Vaja gatimhi, irappaccayo, appaṭihataṃ vajatīti vajiraṃ. Mada ummāde, madirā. Evaṃ mandiraṃ, rudhiraṃ, ruhiraṃ, ruciraṃ. Badha bandhane, badhiro, badhirā, badhiraṃ, timiro, timiraṃ, siro. Sara hiṃsāyaṃ, sariraṃ. “Kalilaṃ, salila”ntiādīsu lo rassa. Kuṭilo, kokilo iccādayo.

Vaja, in the sense of motion (gatimhi); with the suffix ira, because it goes unhindered (appaṭihataṃ vajati), it is vajiraṃ. Mada, in the sense of intoxication (ummāde), it is madirā. Similarly, mandiraṃ, rudhiraṃ, ruhiraṃ, ruciraṃ. Badha, in the sense of binding (bandhane), it is badhiro, badhirā, badhiraṃ; also timiro, timiraṃ, siro. Sara, in the sense of harming (hiṃsāyaṃ), it is sariraṃ. In words like kalilaṃ and salilaṃ, l is for r. Kuṭilo, kokilo, and so on.

672. Paṭito [M 0.0415] hissa heraṇa hīraṇa.

672. After paṭi, for the root hi, the substitutes heraṇa and hīraṇa occur.

Paṭito parassa hiiccetassa dhātussa heraṇa hīraṇaiccete ādesā honti. Hi gatimhi paṭipubbo, paṭipakkhe madditvā gacchatīti atthe “kvi cā”ti kvippaccayo, kvilopo, iminā heraṇa hīraṇaādesā, ṇalopo, “tesu vuddhī”tiādinā paṭisaddādissa vuddhi, pāṭiheraṃ, pāṭihīraṃ, yadā pana hara haraṇeti dhātu, tadā paṭipakkhe haratīti “pāṭihāriya”miti ṇyenapi siddhaṃ.

For the root hi, when it follows paṭi, the substitutes heraṇa and hīraṇa occur. The root hi is in the sense of motion (gatimhi); when preceded by paṭi, in the sense of 'going having crushed the opponent,' the suffix kvi is applied by 'kvi cā,' followed by the elision of kvi. By this rule, the substitutes heraṇa and hīraṇa occur, with the elision of ṇ. By the rule 'tesu vuddhī,' etc., there is vuddhi of the initial syllable of the word paṭi, forming pāṭiheraṃ and pāṭihīraṃ. However, when the root is hara in the sense of carrying (haraṇe), then in the sense of 'carrying away the opponent,' pāṭihāriya is also established with the suffix ṇya.

673. Kaḍyādīhi ko.

673. From kaḍi and so on, the suffix ka is applied.

Kaḍiiccevamādīhi dhātūhi kappaccayo hoti.

From the roots beginning with kaḍi and so on, the suffix ka is applied.

Kaḍi chedane, kappaccaye kate “kvaci dhātū”tiādinā, “niggahītañcā”ti vā ikārānubandhassa dhātussa niggahītāgamo, kalopo ca, niggahītassa vaggantattaṃ, kaṇḍo usu, parimāṇañca. Evaṃ ghaṭi ghaṭṭane, ghaṇṭo, ghaṇṭā vā. Vaṭi āvattane, vaṭi dhāraṇabandhanasaṅghātesu vā, vaṇṭo. Karaḍi bhājanatthe, karaṇḍo. Maḍi maṇḍanatthe, maṇḍo. Saḍi gumbatthe, saṇḍo. Bhaḍi bhaṇḍatthe, bhaṇḍaṃ. Paḍi liṅgavekallatthe, paṇḍo, so eva paṇḍako. Daḍi āṇāyaṃ, daṇḍo. Raḍi hiṃ sāyaṃ, raṇḍo. Taḍi calanatthe, vitaṇḍo. Caḍi caṇḍatthe, caṇḍo. Gaḍi sanniccaye, gaṇḍo. Aḍi aṇḍatthe, aṇḍo. Laḍi jigucchāyaṃ, laṇḍaṃ. Meḍi kuṭilatthe, meṇḍo, meṇḍako vā. Eraḍi hiṃsāyaṃ, eraṇḍo. Khaḍi chedanatthe, khaṇḍo. Madi hāse, mando. Idi paramissariye, indo. Cadi icchākantīsu, cando. Khura chedane, khuro iccādi.

Kaḍi, in the sense of cutting (chedane); when the suffix ka is applied, by 'kvaci dhātū,' etc., or by 'niggahītañcā,' a niggahīta is inserted into the root having an indicatory i, and there is elision of ka. The niggahīta becomes a class-final consonant, forming kaṇḍo (an arrow, and a measure). Similarly, ghaṭi, in the sense of striking (ghaṭṭane), forms ghaṇṭo or ghaṇṭā. Vaṭi, in the sense of turning (āvattane), or in the senses of holding, binding, and collecting, forms vaṇṭo. Karaḍi, in the sense of a vessel (bhājanatthe), forms karaṇḍo. Maḍi, in the sense of adorning (maṇḍanatthe), forms maṇḍo. Saḍi, in the sense of a thicket (gumbatthe), forms saṇḍo. Bhaḍi, in the sense of merchandise (bhaṇḍatthe), forms bhaṇḍaṃ. Paḍi, in the sense of lacking virility (liṅgavekallatthe), forms paṇḍo, which is the same as paṇḍako. Daḍi, in the sense of command (āṇāyaṃ), forms daṇḍo. Raḍi, in the sense of injuring (hiṃsāyaṃ), forms raṇḍo. Taḍi, in the sense of moving (calanatthe), forms vitaṇḍo. Caḍi, in the sense of fierceness (caṇḍatthe), forms caṇḍo. Gaḍi, in the sense of accumulation (sanniccaye), forms gaṇḍo. Aḍi, in the sense of an egg (aṇḍatthe), forms aṇḍo. Laḍi, in the sense of disgust (jigucchāyaṃ), forms laṇḍaṃ. Meḍi, in the sense of crookedness (kuṭilatthe), forms meṇḍo or meṇḍako. Eraḍi, in the sense of injuring (hiṃsāyaṃ), forms eraṇḍo. Khaḍi, in the sense of cutting (chedanatthe), forms khaṇḍo. Madi, in the sense of laughter (hāse), forms mando. Idi, in the sense of supremacy (paramissariye), forms indo. Cadi, in the sense of desire and loveliness (icchākantīsu), forms cando. Khura, in the sense of cutting (chedane), forms khuro, etc.

“Ko”ti vattate.

The suffix 'ka' is carried forward.

674. Khādāmagamānaṃ [M 0.0416] khandhandhagandhā.

674. For khāda, ama, and gamu, the substitutes are khandha, andha, and gandha.

Khāda ama gamuiccetesaṃ dhātūnaṃ khandha andha gandhaiccete ādesā honti, kappaccayo ca hoti. Khāda bhakkhane, jātijarāmaraṇādīhi saṃsāradukkhehi khajjatīti khandho. Ama roge, andho. Gamu, sappa gatimhi, gandho. Kvaciggahaṇena kalopābhāve khandhako, andhako, gandhako. Atha vā rāsaṭṭhena khandho. Gandha sūcane, attano nissayassa gandhanato sūcanato gandho.

For these roots—khāda, ama, and gamu—the substitutes khandha, andha, and gandha occur, and the suffix ka is applied. Khāda is in the sense of eating (bhakkhane); it is khandho because it is devoured by the sufferings of saṃsāra, such as birth, aging, and death. Ama is in the sense of disease (roge), forming andho. Gamu and sappa are in the sense of motion (gatimhi), forming gandho. Through the inclusion of 'kvaci' (sometimes), when there is no elision of ka, the forms are khandhako, andhako, and gandhako. Alternatively, khandho is in the sense of a heap (rāsaṭṭhena). Gandha is in the sense of indicating (sūcane); it is gandho from indicating or making known (gandhanato sūcanato) its own basis (attano nissayassa).

675. Paṭādīhyalaṃ.

675. From paṭa and so on, the suffix ala is applied.

Paṭaiccevamādīhi dhātūhi, pāṭipadikehi ca alappaccayo hoti. Aṭa, paṭa gatimhi, paṭe alaṃ samatthanti atthe iminā alappaccayo, “si”nti amādeso, paṭalaṃ, paṭalāni. Tathā kala kalale, kalalaṃ. Kusa chedanabhūta dāna sañcayesu, kusalaṃ, yadā pana sala lū lāiti dhātu, tadā kucchitānaṃ salanato, kusānaṃ lavanato, kuso viya lavanato vā kusena lātabbattā kusalanti appaccayena kappaccayena vā rūpasiddhi veditabbā.

From the roots beginning with paṭa and so on, and also from nominal stems, the suffix ala is applied. The roots aṭa and paṭa are in the sense of motion (gatimhi). In the sense of 'being capable for the purpose' (paṭe alaṃ samatthaṃ), the suffix ala is applied by this rule; with aṃ as the substitute for the nominative ending si, paṭalaṃ and paṭalāni are formed. Similarly, the root kal, in the sense of an embryo (kalale), forms kalalaṃ. The root kus, in the senses of cutting, being, giving, and collecting, forms kusalaṃ. However, when the roots are sal, lū, or lā, the formation of kusala with the suffix a or ka should be understood as follows: because it shakes off what is contemptible (kucchitānaṃ salanato), because it cuts off what is bad (kusānaṃ lavanato), because it is cut like kusa grass, or because it is to be taken with kusa grass.

Kada made, kadalaṃ. Bhaganda secane, bhagandalaṃ. Mekha kaṭivicitte, mekhalaṃ, mekhalā vā. Vakka rukkhatace, vakkalaṃ. Takka rukkhasilese, takkalaṃ. Palla ninnaṭṭhāne, pallalaṃ. Sadda harite, saddalaṃ, paralopo. Mūla patiṭṭhāyaṃ, mulālaṃ, rassattaṃ. Bila nissaye, bilālaṃ. Vida sattāyaṃ, vidālaṃ. Caḍi caṇḍikke, caṇḍālo, dīghattaṃ. Vā gatigandhanesu, vālaṃ. Vasa acchādane, vasalo. Paci vitthāre, pacalo, pañcālo[M 0.0417], pañcannaṃ rājūnaṃ alantipi pañcālo. Maca core, macalo. Musa theyye, musalo.

The root `kad` is in the sense of 'intoxication', forming `kadalaṃ`. The root `bhagand` is in the sense of 'oozing', forming `bhagandalaṃ`. The root `mekh` is in the sense of 'waist adornment', forming `mekhalaṃ` or `mekhalā`. The root `vakk` is in the sense of 'tree bark', forming `vakkalaṃ`. The root `takk` is in the sense of 'tree resin', forming `takkalaṃ`. The root `pall` is in the sense of a 'low-lying place', forming `pallalaṃ`. The root `sadd` is in the sense of 'green', forming `saddalaṃ`, with elision of the following vowel. The root `mūl` is in the sense of 'foundation', forming `mulālaṃ`, with shortening. The root `bil` is in the sense of 'support', forming `bilālaṃ`. The root `vid` is in the sense of 'existence', forming `vidālaṃ`. The root `caḍi` is in the sense of 'fierceness', forming `caṇḍālo`, with lengthening. The root `vā` is in the sense of 'motion' or 'smell', forming `vālaṃ`. The root `vas` is in the sense of 'covering', forming `vasalo`. The root `pac` is in the sense of 'spreading', forming `pacalo` or `pañcālo`; `pañcālo` is also formed because it is sufficient for five kings. The root `mac` is in the sense of 'concealing', forming `macalo`. The root `mus` is in the sense of 'stealing', forming `musalo`.
